families.title: Milne’s rationality conjecture and algebraic specialization
families.summary: Proves Milne's rationality conjecture for abelian varieties over $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ with good reduction: specialized Hodge classes pair rationally with complementary divisor products, independently of cohomology theory. Together with result 032, every specialized Hodge class is represented by a single rational algebraic cycle simultaneously in all prime-to-p and crystalline realizations, for every residue characteristic p.
families.subject: Number theory
families.overviewTitle: Milne's rationality conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Proves Milne's rationality conjecture for abelian varieties over $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ with good reduction: specialized Hodge classes pair rationally with complementary divisor products, independently of cohomology theory. Together with result 032, every specialized Hodge class is represented by a single rational algebraic cycle simultaneously in all prime-to-$p$ and crystalline realizations, for every residue characteristic $p$.

families.title: The full BSD formula from low Selmer corank
families.summary: Proves the full Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer leading-term formula for every elliptic curve over ℚ whose full q-power Selmer group has corank zero or one for some prime q, including finiteness of the Tate–Shafarevich group. With result 006, this gives full BSD for a density-one set of quadratic twists of every elliptic curve over ℚ.
families.subject: Number theory
families.overviewTitle: The full Birch--Swinnerton-Dyer formula in Selmer coranks zero and one
families.overviewSummary: Proves the full Birch--Swinnerton-Dyer leading-term formula for every elliptic curve over $\mathbb Q$ whose full $q$-power Selmer group has corank zero or one for some prime $q$, including finiteness of the Tate--Shafarevich group. With result 006, this gives full BSD for a density-one set of quadratic twists of every elliptic curve over $\mathbb Q$.

families.title: The quasi-Riemann hypothesis
families.summary: Proves that every Dirichlet L-function, including $\zeta(s)$, is zero-free in $\Re s\gt 7/8$, resolving the quasi-Riemann hypothesis. The same half-plane is zero-free for every finite-order Hecke L-function over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$. A companion gives a different proof of the zero-free half-plane $\Re s\gt 11/12$.
families.subject: Number theory
families.overviewTitle: The quasi-Riemann hypothesis
families.overviewSummary: Proves that every Dirichlet $L$-function, including $\zeta(s)$, is zero-free in $\Re s>7/8$, resolving the quasi-Riemann hypothesis. The same half-plane is zero-free for every finite-order Hecke $L$-function over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$. A companion gives a different proof of the zero-free half-plane $\Re s>11/12$.

families.title: Hilbert’s tenth problem over ℚ
families.summary: Proves that no algorithm decides whether an integer-coefficient polynomial in an arbitrary number of variables has a rational zero, resolving Hilbert's tenth problem over ℚ negatively.
families.subject: Number theory
families.overviewTitle: Hilbert's tenth problem over $\mathbb Q$
families.overviewSummary: Proves that no algorithm decides whether an integer-coefficient polynomial in an arbitrary number of variables has a rational zero, resolving Hilbert's tenth problem over $\mathbb Q$ negatively.

families.title: Irrationality of Catalan’s constant
families.summary: Proves that Catalan's constant $G=\sum_{j\ge0}(-1)^j/(2j+1)^2$ is irrational.
families.subject: Number theory
families.overviewTitle: Irrationality of Catalan's constant
families.overviewSummary: Proves that Catalan's constant $G=\sum_{j\ge0}(-1)^j/(2j+1)^2$ is irrational.

families.title: Goldfeld’s conjecture: densities and mean analytic rank
families.summary: Proves Goldfeld's conjecture for quadratic twists of every elliptic curve over ℚ: analytic ranks zero and one each have density 1/2, and the mean analytic rank tends to 1/2. Both statements order signed squarefree twist parameters by absolute value.
families.subject: Number theory
families.overviewTitle: Goldfeld's conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Proves Goldfeld's conjecture for quadratic twists of every elliptic curve over $\mathbb Q$: analytic ranks zero and one each have density $1/2$, and the mean analytic rank tends to $1/2$. Both statements order signed squarefree twist parameters by absolute value.

families.title: Ordinary two-point correlations and the corrected Elliott conjecture
families.summary: Proves the ordinary two-point Chowla conjecture, with a bound $O(X/(\log X)^c)$ for Liouville correlation sums along fixed nonproportional affine forms, where c > 0 is absolute. More generally, proves the binary corrected Elliott conjecture for complex multiplicative functions bounded by one when one factor is uniformly nonpretentious against each fixed Dirichlet character times $n^{it}$ for $|t|\le X$.
families.subject: Number theory
families.overviewTitle: Two-point Chowla and the corrected binary Elliott conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Proves the ordinary two-point Chowla conjecture, with a bound $O(X/(\log X)^c)$ for Liouville correlation sums along fixed nonproportional affine forms, where $c>0$ is absolute. More generally, proves the binary corrected Elliott conjecture for complex multiplicative functions bounded by one when one factor is uniformly nonpretentious against each fixed Dirichlet character times $n^{it}$ for $|t|\le X$.

families.title: The Deligne–Drinfeld conjecture
families.summary: Proves that the rational Grothendieck–Teichmüller Lie algebra, with the Ihara bracket, is freely generated by one element in each odd weight 3, 5, 7, …, resolving the Deligne–Drinfeld conjecture.
families.subject: Number theory
families.overviewTitle: The Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Proves that the rational Grothendieck--Teichm\"uller Lie algebra, with the Ihara bracket, is freely generated by one element in each odd weight $3,5,7,\ldots$, resolving the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture.

families.title: Function-field reconstruction from Milnor K-theory and Galois data
families.summary: Reconstructs function fields of transcendence degree at least two over algebraically closed constants from $K^{\mathrm M}_1/\ell$, $K^{\mathrm M}_2/\ell$, and their product. These data recover the perfect closure and constants when ℓ differs from the characteristic, and the original field and its named base in equal characteristic. Also proves Bogomolov–Pop reconstruction from abelian-by-central pro-ℓ Galois data away from the characteristic.
families.subject: Number theory
families.overviewTitle: Bogomolov--Pop and Milnor $K$-theoretic reconstruction
families.overviewSummary: Reconstructs function fields of transcendence degree at least two over algebraically closed constants from $K^{\mathrm M}_1/\ell$, $K^{\mathrm M}_2/\ell$, and their product. These data recover the perfect closure and constants when $\ell$ differs from the characteristic, and the original field and its named base in equal characteristic. Also proves Bogomolov--Pop reconstruction from abelian-by-central pro-$\ell$ Galois data away from the characteristic.

families.title: Unrestricted pro-modularity at the prime two
families.summary: Every continuous odd absolutely irreducible two-dimensional 2-adic representation of $G_{\mathbb Q}$ unramified outside finitely many primes occurs in a completed Hecke algebra at some odd tame level. Also proves classical modularity up to Tate twist for irreducible odd representations with these finiteness conditions that are de Rham at 2 with distinct Hodge–Tate weights, resolving the dyadic Fontaine–Mazur case without residual restrictions.
families.subject: Number theory
families.overviewTitle: Fontaine--Mazur modularity at the prime $2$ and $2$-adic pro-modularity
families.overviewSummary: Every continuous odd absolutely irreducible two-dimensional $2$-adic representation of $G_{\mathbb Q}$ unramified outside finitely many primes occurs in a completed Hecke algebra at some odd tame level. Also proves classical modularity up to Tate twist for irreducible odd representations with these finiteness conditions that are de Rham at $2$ with distinct Hodge--Tate weights, resolving the dyadic Fontaine--Mazur case without residual restrictions.

families.title: Prime-factor statistics of $p-1$
families.summary: Proves that the normalized ordered logarithms of the prime factors of $p-1$, counted with multiplicity, converge jointly to the Poisson–Dirichlet law $\mathrm{PD}(1)$ as p ranges uniformly over primes up to x and $x\to\infty$. This resolves the Ford–Konyagin–Luca conjecture. It also proves that infinitely many integers n have more than $n^{1-\varepsilon}$ totient preimages, for every ε > 0.
families.subject: Number theory
families.overviewTitle: The Ford--Konyagin--Luca conjecture on prime predecessors
families.overviewSummary: Proves that the normalized ordered logarithms of the prime factors of $p-1$, counted with multiplicity, converge jointly to the Poisson--Dirichlet law $\mathrm{PD}(1)$ as $p$ ranges uniformly over primes up to $x$ and $x\to\infty$. This resolves the Ford--Konyagin--Luca conjecture. It also proves that infinitely many integers $n$ have more than $n^{1-\varepsilon}$ totient preimages, for every $\varepsilon>0$.

families.title: Independent largest prime factors of consecutive integers
families.summary: Resolves the Erdős–Pomerance joint Dickman conjecture: the logarithmic sizes of the largest prime factors of n and $n+1$ are asymptotically independent in ordinary natural density. In particular, the integers satisfying $P^+(n)\lt P^+(n+1)$ have density 1/2.
families.subject: Number theory
families.overviewTitle: Independent largest prime factors of consecutive integers
families.overviewSummary: Resolves the Erd\H{o}s--Pomerance joint Dickman conjecture: the logarithmic sizes of the largest prime factors of $n$ and $n+1$ are asymptotically independent in ordinary natural density. In particular, the integers satisfying $P^+(n)<P^+(n+1)$ have density $1/2$.

families.title: Ostmann’s inverse Goldbach conjecture
families.summary: Proves that no finite modification of the primes can be written as $A+B$ with $A,B\subseteq\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ each containing at least two elements. This resolves Ostmann's inverse Goldbach conjecture on additive indecomposability.
families.subject: Number theory
families.overviewTitle: Ostmann's inverse Goldbach conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Proves that no finite modification of the primes can be written as $A+B$ with $A,B\subseteq\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ each containing at least two elements. This resolves Ostmann's inverse Goldbach conjecture on additive indecomposability.

families.title: Restricted geometric Langlands, global Arthur enhancements, and generic Ramanujan
families.summary: Proves the restricted geometric Langlands equivalence for connected reductive groups on smooth projective connected curves over $\overline{\mathbb F}_q$ under the four stated Lie-theoretic characteristic hypotheses. Over arbitrary algebraically closed fields of characteristic p > 0, the same conclusion holds assuming additionally that p is very good for the group and $p\nmid |W_G|$. Over global function fields, proves Ramanujan at every place for globally generic cuspidal representations of split adjoint absolutely simple exceptional groups, without characteristic or ramification-depth restrictions, and at every unramified place for cuspidal representations of split adjoint absolutely simple groups with a generic unramified component. Assuming the finite-level Ramanujan–Arthur decomposition, constructs global Arthur enhancements of occurring cuspidal excursion parameters for split connected semisimple groups at full finite level, recovering the given parameters by diagonal specialization on the entire Weil group, including inertia.
families.subject: Number theory
families.overviewTitle: Restricted geometric Langlands, generic Ramanujan and Arthur parameters
families.overviewSummary: Proves the restricted geometric Langlands equivalence for connected reductive groups on smooth projective connected curves over $\overline{\mathbb F}_q$ under the four stated Lie-theoretic characteristic hypotheses. Over arbitrary algebraically closed fields of characteristic $p>0$, the same conclusion holds assuming additionally that $p$ is very good for the group and $p\nmid |W_G|$. Over global function fields, proves Ramanujan at every place for globally generic cuspidal representations of split adjoint absolutely simple exceptional groups, without characteristic or ramification-depth restrictions, and at every unramified place for cuspidal representations of split adjoint absolutely simple groups with a generic unramified component. Assuming the finite-level Ramanujan--Arthur decomposition, constructs global Arthur enhancements of occurring cuspidal excursion parameters for split connected semisimple groups at full finite level, recovering the given parameters by diagonal specialization on the entire Weil group, including inertia.

families.title: Torus-packet equidistribution in prime, quartic, and sextic degrees
families.summary: Proves Haar equidistribution without escape of mass for complete volume-weighted torus packets from totally real fields: arbitrary lattices and prescribed local types in fixed prime degree at least five, arbitrary-order Picard packets in primitive quartic fields, and maximal-order ideal-class packets in primitive sextic fields. Here primitive means having no proper intermediate field; the relevant order or field discriminant tends to infinity.
families.subject: Number theory
families.overviewTitle: Torus-packet equidistribution in prime, quartic, and sextic degrees
families.overviewSummary: Proves Haar equidistribution without escape of mass for complete volume-weighted torus packets from totally real fields: arbitrary lattices and prescribed local types in fixed prime degree at least five, arbitrary-order Picard packets in primitive quartic fields, and maximal-order ideal-class packets in primitive sextic fields. Here primitive means having no proper intermediate field; the relevant order or field discriminant tends to infinity.

families.title: Zilber–Pink in abelian varieties and the Siegel threefold
families.summary: Proves the abelian Zilber–Pink conjecture over $\overline{\mathbb Q}$: every irreducible subvariety has finitely many maximal atypical subvarieties relative to its smallest containing torsion coset. It also proves the full curve case in the Siegel threefold $\mathcal A_2$ for Hodge-generic curves defined over $\overline{\mathbb Q}$, without boundary or reduction assumptions.
families.subject: Number theory
families.overviewTitle: Zilber--Pink in abelian varieties and the Siegel threefold
families.overviewSummary: Proves the abelian Zilber--Pink conjecture over $\overline{\mathbb Q}$: every irreducible subvariety has finitely many maximal atypical subvarieties relative to its smallest containing torsion coset. It also proves the full curve case in the Siegel threefold $\mathcal A_2$ for Hodge-generic curves defined over $\overline{\mathbb Q}$, without boundary or reduction assumptions.

families.title: The irrationality exponent of π is 2
families.summary: Proves that the irrationality exponent of π is exactly 2: for every ε > 0 and all sufficiently large denominators q, every rational $p/q$ satisfies $|\pi-p/q|\ge q^{-2-\varepsilon}$. This also proves convergence of the Flint–Hills series $\sum_{n\ge1}1/(n^3\sin^2 n)$, with angles in radians.
families.subject: Number theory
families.overviewTitle: The irrationality exponent of $\pi$ is $2$
families.overviewSummary: Proves that the irrationality exponent of $\pi$ is exactly $2$: for every $\varepsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large denominators $q$, every rational $p/q$ satisfies $|\pi-p/q|\ge q^{-2-\varepsilon}$. This also proves convergence of the Flint--Hills series $\sum_{n\ge1}1/(n^3\sin^2 n)$, with angles in radians.

families.title: The Margulis–Platonov conjecture over global fields
families.summary: Proves the Margulis–Platonov conjecture over every global field, including function fields of characteristic two. For an absolutely almost simple simply connected algebraic group G over k, every noncentral abstract normal subgroup of $G(k)$ is the inverse image of an open normal subgroup in the finite product of its anisotropic nonarchimedean local groups.
families.subject: Number theory
families.overviewTitle: The Margulis--Platonov conjecture over global fields
families.overviewSummary: Proves the Margulis--Platonov conjecture over every global field, including function fields of characteristic two. For an absolutely almost simple simply connected algebraic group $G$ over $k$, every noncentral abstract normal subgroup of $G(k)$ is the inverse image of an open normal subgroup in the finite product of its anisotropic nonarchimedean local groups.

families.title: The local p-adic section conjecture and global consequences
families.summary: Proves that rational points on every smooth proper geometrically connected curve of genus at least two over a finite extension of ℚp correspond bijectively to conjugacy classes of sections of its full arithmetic étale fundamental group. It also proves Grothendieck's section conjecture over ℚ for the modular curves $X_0(N)$ and $X_1(N)$ of genus at least two.
families.subject: Number theory
families.overviewTitle: The $p$-adic section conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Proves that rational points on every smooth proper geometrically connected curve of genus at least two over a finite extension of $\mathbb Q_p$ correspond bijectively to conjugacy classes of sections of its full arithmetic \'etale fundamental group. It also proves Grothendieck's section conjecture over $\mathbb Q$ for the modular curves $X_0(N)$ and $X_1(N)$ of genus at least two.

families.title: Squarefree quartics and power-free polynomial values
families.summary: Proves the squarefree-values conjecture for irreducible integer quartics with no fixed prime-square divisor: squarefree values on positive integers have the predicted positive Euler-product density. More generally, establishes the $(d-2)$-power-free density for irreducible integer polynomials of degrees four through eight under the necessary local condition; together with Browning's higher-degree theorem, this covers every d ≥ 4.
families.subject: Number theory
families.overviewTitle: Squarefree quartics and power-free polynomial values
families.overviewSummary: Proves the squarefree-values conjecture for irreducible integer quartics with no fixed prime-square divisor: squarefree values on positive integers have the predicted positive Euler-product density. More generally, establishes the $(d-2)$-power-free density for irreducible integer polynomials of degrees four through eight under the necessary local condition; together with Browning's higher-degree theorem, this covers every $d\ge4$.

families.title: A quadratic bound for Jacobsthal’s function
families.summary: Answers Jacobsthal's quadratic-bound question: every interval of $Ck^2$ consecutive integers contains an integer coprime to any prescribed positive integer with at most k distinct prime divisors, for an absolute constant C. The bound is uniform over prime sets and interval positions and removes the classical logarithmic loss.
families.subject: Number theory
families.overviewTitle: A quadratic bound for Jacobsthal's function
families.overviewSummary: Answers Jacobsthal's quadratic-bound question: every interval of $Ck^2$ consecutive integers contains an integer coprime to any prescribed positive integer with at most $k$ distinct prime divisors, for an absolute constant $C$. The bound is uniform over prime sets and interval positions and removes the classical logarithmic loss.

families.title: The weak inhomogeneous Duffin–Schaeffer conjecture
families.summary: Proves that for every real shift γ and finite-valued $\psi:\mathbb N\to[0,\infty)$, divergence of $\sum_q\phi(q)\psi(q)/q$ implies $\|qx-\gamma\|\lt \psi(q)$ for infinitely many q, for almost every x. Here ϕ is Euler's totient and the norm is distance to the nearest integer. Numerators are unrestricted; no monotonicity or Diophantine condition on γ is needed.
families.subject: Number theory
families.overviewTitle: The weak inhomogeneous Duffin--Schaeffer conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Proves that for every real shift $\gamma$ and finite-valued $\psi:\mathbb N\to[0,\infty)$, divergence of $\sum_q\phi(q)\psi(q)/q$ implies $\|qx-\gamma\|<\psi(q)$ for infinitely many $q$, for almost every $x$. Here $\phi$ is Euler's totient and the norm is distance to the nearest integer. Numerators are unrestricted; no monotonicity or Diophantine condition on $\gamma$ is needed.

families.title: Patterson's first moment for cubic Gauss sums
families.summary: Proves unconditionally the all-primary-prime form of Patterson’s first-moment asymptotic: normalized cubic Gauss sums over primary Eisenstein primes of norm at most X, including both conjugates, have an explicit positive main term of order $X^{5/6}/\log X$. Every fixed nonzero prime-angle Fourier mode has smaller order.
families.subject: Number theory
families.overviewTitle: Patterson’s first moment for cubic Gauss sums
families.overviewSummary: Proves unconditionally the all-primary-prime form of Patterson’s first-moment asymptotic: normalized cubic Gauss sums over primary Eisenstein primes of norm at most $X$, including both conjugates, have an explicit positive main term of order $X^{5/6}/\log X$. Every fixed nonzero prime-angle Fourier mode has smaller order.

families.title: An asymptotic formula for the number of totients
families.summary: Gives an asymptotic equivalent for the number $V(x)$ of distinct totient values up to x, with a positive bounded phase-dependent factor determined by convergent arithmetic approximations. In particular, $V(cx)/V(x)\to c$ for every fixed c > 0, answering Erdős and Hall’s scaling question.
families.subject: Number theory
families.overviewTitle: An asymptotic formula for the number of totients
families.overviewSummary: Gives an asymptotic equivalent for the number $V(x)$ of distinct totient values up to $x$, with a positive bounded phase-dependent factor determined by convergent arithmetic approximations. In particular, $V(cx)/V(x)\to c$ for every fixed $c>0$, answering Erd\H{o}s and Hall’s scaling question.

families.title: Short Egyptian fractions
families.summary: Every rational $a/b$ with $1\le a\lt b$ is a sum of $O(\log\log b)$ distinct positive unit fractions. The worst-case minimum number of terms has the same order, resolving Erdős’s conjecture on short Egyptian fractions.
families.subject: Number theory
families.overviewTitle: Erd\H{o}s’s short Egyptian-fraction conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Every rational $a/b$ with $1\le a<b$ is a sum of $O(\log\log b)$ distinct positive unit fractions. The worst-case minimum number of terms has the same order, resolving Erd\H{o}s’s conjecture on short Egyptian fractions.

families.title: Positive lower density of large prime gaps
families.summary: For every fixed C > 0, a positive proportion of consecutive prime gaps exceed $C\log p_n$, throughout every sufficiently large initial segment of the primes. The proportion may depend on C. Consequently, the indices where $p_n/n$ increases have positive lower density, answering Erdős and Prachar.
families.subject: Number theory
families.overviewTitle: Positive lower density of large prime gaps
families.overviewSummary: For every fixed $C>0$, a positive proportion of consecutive prime gaps exceed $C\log p_n$, throughout every sufficiently large initial segment of the primes. The proportion may depend on $C$. Consequently, the indices where $p_n/n$ increases have positive lower density, answering Erd\H{o}s and Prachar.

families.title: Potential integral density on curve character varieties
families.summary: Resolves the determinant-one curve case of Litt's integral-density question. For every smooth connected complex algebraic curve and every rank, integral points become Zariski dense in every component of its SLr character variety over the full ring of integers of one number field. Prescribed quasi-unipotent boundary conjugacy classes are allowed, including nonsemisimple classes.
families.subject: Number theory
families.overviewTitle: Integral density on curve character varieties
families.overviewSummary: Resolves the determinant-one curve case of Litt's integral-density question. For every smooth connected complex algebraic curve and every rank, integral points become Zariski dense in every component of its $\mathrm{SL}_r$ character variety over the full ring of integers of one number field. Prescribed quasi-unipotent boundary conjugacy classes are allowed, including nonsemisimple classes.

families.title: Uniformly bounded components of Gaussian-prime graphs
families.summary: Proves the Gaussian moat conjecture: no infinite walk through distinct Gaussian primes can have uniformly bounded steps. More strongly, for every distance bound D, the graph joining Gaussian primes at distance at most D has uniformly bounded finite component sizes, depending only on D, including primes on the coordinate axes.
families.subject: Number theory
families.overviewTitle: The Gaussian moat conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Proves the Gaussian moat conjecture: no infinite walk through distinct Gaussian primes can have uniformly bounded steps. More strongly, for every distance bound $D$, the graph joining Gaussian primes at distance at most $D$ has uniformly bounded finite component sizes, depending only on $D$, including primes on the coordinate axes.

families.title: Primitive roots for every admissible integer base
families.summary: Proves the infinitude assertion in Artin's primitive root conjecture for every integer a that is neither −1 nor a square. For each such base, at least $c_a x/(\log x)^2$ primes in every sufficiently large interval $(x,2x)$ have primitive root a, with $c_a\gt 0$.
families.subject: Number theory
families.overviewTitle: Artin's primitive root conjecture: infinitude for every base
families.overviewSummary: Proves the infinitude assertion in Artin's primitive root conjecture for every integer $a$ that is neither $-1$ nor a square. For each such base, at least $c_a x/(\log x)^2$ primes in every sufficiently large interval $(x,2x)$ have primitive root $a$, with $c_a>0$.

families.title: Modularity of elliptic curves over imaginary quadratic fields
families.summary: Proves the modularity conjecture for elliptic curves over imaginary quadratic fields: every elliptic curve over every imaginary quadratic field is modular, with matching local parameters at every place.
families.subject: Number theory
families.overviewTitle: Modularity over imaginary quadratic fields
families.overviewSummary: Proves the modularity conjecture for elliptic curves over imaginary quadratic fields: every elliptic curve over every imaginary quadratic field is modular, with matching local parameters at every place.

families.title: Uchida’s conjecture for open homomorphisms of Galois groups
families.summary: Proves Uchida's conjecture: every continuous open homomorphism between Galois groups of possibly infinite solvably closed Galois extensions of number fields comes from a unique equivariant field embedding in the opposite direction. No restriction on the kernel or separate cyclotomic-compatibility assumption is needed.
families.subject: Number theory
families.overviewTitle: Uchida's conjecture for open Galois homomorphisms
families.overviewSummary: Proves Uchida's conjecture: every continuous open homomorphism between Galois groups of possibly infinite solvably closed Galois extensions of number fields comes from a unique equivariant field embedding in the opposite direction. No restriction on the kernel or separate cyclotomic-compatibility assumption is needed.

families.title: The rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties
families.summary: Proves the rational Hodge conjecture for every complex CM abelian variety, in every dimension and codimension. Through Milne's theorems, this also gives the Tate conjecture for all abelian varieties over finite fields and the Hodge standard conjecture for abelian varieties in every characteristic.
families.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
families.overviewTitle: The rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties
families.overviewSummary: Proves the rational Hodge conjecture for every complex CM abelian variety, in every dimension and codimension. Through Milne's theorems, this also gives the Tate conjecture for all abelian varieties over finite fields and the Hodge standard conjecture for abelian varieties in every characteristic.

families.title: Iitaka subadditivity, variation, and logarithmic additivity
families.summary: Proves Campana's orbifold Iitaka subadditivity conjecture for smooth Fujiki-class-$\mathcal C$ manifolds with rational simple-normal-crossing boundaries. For projective fibrations $f:U\to V$ of smooth complex quasi-projective varieties with connected fibers, general fiber F, and $\bar\kappa(V)\ge0$, proves Popa's inequality $\bar\kappa(U)\ge\kappa(F)+\max\{\bar\kappa(V),\mathop{\mathrm{Var}}\nolimits (f)\}$, where variation measures the whole geometric generic fiber.
families.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
families.overviewTitle: Campana's orbifold Iitaka conjecture and logarithmic subadditivity
families.overviewSummary: Proves Campana's orbifold Iitaka subadditivity conjecture for smooth Fujiki-class-$\mathcal C$ manifolds with rational simple-normal-crossing boundaries. For projective fibrations $f:U\to V$ of smooth complex quasi-projective varieties with connected fibers, general fiber $F$, and $\bar\kappa(V)\ge0$, proves Popa's inequality $\bar\kappa(U)\ge\kappa(F)+\max\{\bar\kappa(V),\operatorname{Var}(f)\}$, where variation measures the whole geometric generic fiber.

families.title: Log abundance for compact Kähler spaces under logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity
families.summary: Using logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity, proves log abundance in every dimension for normal compact Kähler log canonical pairs with effective rational boundary: an analytically nef ℚ-Cartier adjoint is semiample. It also proves projective log abundance over every algebraically closed field of characteristic zero and the effective Iitaka fibration conjecture for smooth projective varieties of nonnegative Kodaira dimension in that setting. A further result resolves the finite-rational-coefficient index conjecture for connected projective semi-log-canonical log Calabi–Yau pairs over such fields in each fixed dimension and for each fixed finite set of rational boundary coefficients, with a uniform index independent of the number of components.
families.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
families.overviewTitle: Log abundance and effective Iitaka fibrations
families.overviewSummary: Using logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity, proves log abundance in every dimension for normal compact K\"ahler log canonical pairs with effective rational boundary: an analytically nef $\mathbb Q$-Cartier adjoint is semiample. It also proves projective log abundance over every algebraically closed field of characteristic zero and the effective Iitaka fibration conjecture for smooth projective varieties of nonnegative Kodaira dimension in that setting. A further result resolves the finite-rational-coefficient index conjecture for connected projective semi-log-canonical log Calabi--Yau pairs over such fields in each fixed dimension and for each fixed finite set of rational boundary coefficients, with a uniform index independent of the number of components.

families.title: Log-canonical threefold abundance in numerical dimension one
families.summary: Proves log abundance for projective log canonical threefold pairs over algebraically closed fields of characteristic p > 3 when the effective boundary is rational and the ℚ-Cartier adjoint is nef of numerical dimension one. The adjoint is semiample, without requiring the original variety to be terminal or ℚ-factorial.
families.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
families.overviewTitle: Threefold log abundance in numerical dimension one in characteristic $p>3$
families.overviewSummary: Proves log abundance for projective log canonical threefold pairs over algebraically closed fields of characteristic $p>3$ when the effective boundary is rational and the $\mathbb Q$-Cartier adjoint is nef of numerical dimension one. The adjoint is semiample, without requiring the original variety to be terminal or $\mathbb Q$-factorial.

families.title: Numerical semiampleness and generalized minimal models
families.summary: Proves numerical semiampleness for nef adjoints $K_X+B+M$ with $K_X+B$ pseudo-effective and M nef rational, for projective klt rational pairs over algebraically closed characteristic-zero fields and smooth compact Kähler rational klt simple-normal-crossing pairs, using Bott–Chern cohomology in the latter case. Separately, projective generalized log canonical rational pairs over such fields admit minimal models for pseudo-effective adjoints and Mori fiber spaces otherwise, with nef b-data fixed.
families.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
families.overviewTitle: Numerical semiampleness and generalized minimal models
families.overviewSummary: Proves numerical semiampleness for nef adjoints $K_X+B+M$ with $K_X+B$ pseudo-effective and $M$ nef rational, for projective klt rational pairs over algebraically closed characteristic-zero fields and smooth compact K\"ahler rational klt simple-normal-crossing pairs, using Bott--Chern cohomology in the latter case. Separately, projective generalized log canonical rational pairs over such fields admit minimal models for pseudo-effective adjoints and Mori fiber spaces otherwise, with nef b-data fixed.

families.title: The ordinary-double-point volume gap
families.summary: Proves the ordinary-double-point volume-gap conjecture: every singular complex algebraic klt germ of dimension n ≥ 2, with zero boundary, has normalized volume at most $2(n-1)^n$. Equality holds precisely for an analytic ordinary double point.
families.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
families.overviewTitle: The sharp ordinary-double-point volume gap
families.overviewSummary: Proves the ordinary-double-point volume-gap conjecture: every singular complex algebraic klt germ of dimension $n\ge2$, with zero boundary, has normalized volume at most $2(n-1)^n$. Equality holds precisely for an analytic ordinary double point.

families.title: Fujita’s freeness conjecture
families.summary: Proves Fujita's freeness conjecture at its sharp bound in every dimension: for a smooth projective complex variety X of dimension n and an ample line bundle L, the adjoint $K_X+mL$ is globally generated for every integer $m\ge n+1$.
families.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
families.overviewTitle: Fujita's freeness conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Proves Fujita's freeness conjecture at its sharp bound in every dimension: for a smooth projective complex variety $X$ of dimension $n$ and an ample line bundle $L$, the adjoint $K_X+mL$ is globally generated for every integer $m\ge n+1$.

families.title: Nagata’s conjecture and maximal Seshadri constants
families.summary: Proves Nagata's strict inequality $\sum_i m_i\lt d\sqrt r$ for every nonzero effective plane curve of degree d through r ≥ 10 very general complex points, with arbitrary multiplicities mi. It also proves maximal multipoint Seshadri constants $(L^n/r)^{1/n}$ for every smooth polarized projective variety of dimension n ≥ 2 and all sufficiently large r: at very general points over ℂ, and at the geometric generic tuple over any algebraically closed field of positive characteristic.
families.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
families.overviewTitle: Nagata's conjecture and maximal Seshadri constants
families.overviewSummary: Proves Nagata's strict inequality $\sum_i m_i<d\sqrt r$ for every nonzero effective plane curve of degree $d$ through $r\ge10$ very general complex points, with arbitrary multiplicities $m_i$. It also proves maximal multipoint Seshadri constants $(L^n/r)^{1/n}$ for every smooth polarized projective variety of dimension $n\ge2$ and all sufficiently large $r$: at very general points over $\mathbb C$, and at the geometric generic tuple over any algebraically closed field of positive characteristic.

families.title: Bloch’s conjecture for complex surfaces
families.summary: Proves Bloch's conjecture: for every smooth connected projective complex surface S with $p_g(S)=0$, the Albanese map $\mathrm{CH}_0(S)^0\to\mathrm{Alb}(S)(\mathbb C)$ on integral degree-zero zero-cycles is an isomorphism. This combines the new $p_g=q=0$ theorem with the classical theorem of Bloch, Kas, and Lieberman.
families.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
families.overviewTitle: Bloch's conjecture for complex surfaces
families.overviewSummary: Proves Bloch's conjecture: for every smooth connected projective complex surface $S$ with $p_g(S)=0$, the Albanese map $\mathrm{CH}_0(S)^0\to\mathrm{Alb}(S)(\mathbb C)$ on integral degree-zero zero-cycles is an isomorphism. This combines the new $p_g=q=0$ theorem with the classical theorem of Bloch, Kas, and Lieberman.

families.title: Hyperkähler SYZ and projective-space bases
families.summary: Proves the strong hyperkähler SYZ conjecture: every holomorphic line bundle with nonzero nef isotropic first Chern class on a compact irreducible holomorphic symplectic Kähler manifold is semiample. It also proves that every projective Lagrangian fibration with normal projective base has projective space as its base, in every dimension and deformation type.
families.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
families.overviewTitle: Hyperk\"ahler SYZ and projective-space bases
families.overviewSummary: Proves the strong hyperk\"ahler SYZ conjecture: every holomorphic line bundle with nonzero nef isotropic first Chern class on a compact irreducible holomorphic symplectic K\"ahler manifold is semiample. It also proves that every projective Lagrangian fibration with normal projective base has projective space as its base, in every dimension and deformation type.

families.title: Oka classification for minimal compact complex surfaces: Kodaira dimension zero and class VII
families.summary: Proves that every complex K3 surface is Oka, including nonprojective surfaces. More generally, every connected minimal compact complex surface of Kodaira dimension zero is Oka; a connected minimal compact complex surface of class VII is Oka exactly when it is a Hopf or Enoki surface.
families.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
families.overviewTitle: Oka classification for K3 surfaces and other compact complex surfaces
families.overviewSummary: Proves that every complex K3 surface is Oka, including nonprojective surfaces. More generally, every connected minimal compact complex surface of Kodaira dimension zero is Oka; a connected minimal compact complex surface of class VII is Oka exactly when it is a Hopf or Enoki surface.

families.title: P = W for fixed-determinant SLn moduli spaces
families.summary: Proves $P_k=W_{2k}=W_{2k+1}$ on the full rational cohomology of smooth coprime fixed-determinant, trace-free Higgs moduli spaces and their character varieties for composite ranks over smooth projective complex curves of genus at least two. This includes variant cohomology and, together with the known prime-rank theorems, establishes the fixed-determinant P = W conjecture in every coprime rank.
families.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
families.overviewTitle: $P=W$ for fixed-determinant moduli spaces
families.overviewSummary: Proves $P_k=W_{2k}=W_{2k+1}$ on the full rational cohomology of smooth coprime fixed-determinant, trace-free Higgs moduli spaces and their character varieties for composite ranks over smooth projective complex curves of genus at least two. This includes variant cohomology and, together with the known prime-rank theorems, establishes the fixed-determinant $P=W$ conjecture in every coprime rank.

families.title: The equivariant cohomological Hikita conjecture
families.summary: Proves the equivariant cohomological Hikita correspondence for every finite quiver, including loops and multiple arrows, with arbitrary dimension and framing vectors and commuting flavor torus. When every semistable point is stable and the gauge action is free, the equivariant cohomology of the Nakajima variety is canonically the coordinate ring of the scheme-theoretic cocharacter-fixed locus of its flavor-deformed Coulomb branch.
families.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
families.overviewTitle: The equivariant cohomological Hikita conjecture for quivers
families.overviewSummary: Proves the equivariant cohomological Hikita correspondence for every finite quiver, including loops and multiple arrows, with arbitrary dimension and framing vectors and commuting flavor torus. When every semistable point is stable and the gauge action is free, the equivariant cohomology of the Nakajima variety is canonically the coordinate ring of the scheme-theoretic cocharacter-fixed locus of its flavor-deformed Coulomb branch.

families.title: Shafarevich counterexamples in dimension two and with large fundamental group
families.summary: Constructs a smooth projective complex fourfold with large fundamental group whose universal cover contains no positive-dimensional compact analytic subvariety but is neither Stein nor holomorphically convex. A separate smooth projective complex surface already disproves unrestricted Shafarevich holomorphic convexity in dimension two.
families.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
families.overviewTitle: Counterexamples to Shafarevich holomorphic convexity
families.overviewSummary: Constructs a smooth projective complex fourfold with large fundamental group whose universal cover contains no positive-dimensional compact analytic subvariety but is neither Stein nor holomorphically convex. A separate smooth projective complex surface already disproves unrestricted Shafarevich holomorphic convexity in dimension two.

families.title: Zariski cancellation and affine fibrations over the complex numbers
families.summary: Constructs an integral complex affine fourfold $X\not\cong\mathbb A^4$ with $X\times\mathbb A^1\cong\mathbb A^5$, disproving affine-space cancellation over ℂ in dimension four. It also disproves the Dolgachev–Weisfeiler affine-fibration conjecture: smooth surjections $X\to\mathbb A^1$ and $\mathbb A^5\to\mathbb A^2$ have every residue-field fiber isomorphic to affine three-space but are not Zariski-locally trivial.
families.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
families.overviewTitle: Complex counterexamples to cancellation and affine fibrations
families.overviewSummary: Constructs an integral complex affine fourfold $X\not\cong\mathbb A^4$ with $X\times\mathbb A^1\cong\mathbb A^5$, disproving affine-space cancellation over $\mathbb C$ in dimension four. It also disproves the Dolgachev--Weisfeiler affine-fibration conjecture: smooth surjections $X\to\mathbb A^1$ and $\mathbb A^5\to\mathbb A^2$ have every residue-field fiber isomorphic to affine three-space but are not Zariski-locally trivial.

families.title: A characteristic-zero counterexample to Lipman–Zariski
families.summary: Constructs a singular normal affine complex surface with free rank-two tangent sheaf, disproving the characteristic-zero Lipman–Zariski conjecture.
families.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
families.overviewTitle: A characteristic-zero counterexample to Lipman--Zariski
families.overviewSummary: Constructs a singular normal affine complex surface with free rank-two tangent sheaf, disproving the characteristic-zero Lipman--Zariski conjecture.

families.title: A stable-coordinate counterexample in four variables
families.summary: Constructs a polynomial in four complex variables that is not a coordinate but becomes one after adjoining a single variable, disproving the Stable Coordinate conjecture in four variables. Every fiber is affine three-space, yet none of its embeddings is rectifiable, also disproving the Abhyankar–Sathaye conjecture even when all fibers are affine spaces.
families.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
families.overviewTitle: A stable-coordinate counterexample in four variables
families.overviewSummary: Constructs a polynomial in four complex variables that is not a coordinate but becomes one after adjoining a single variable, disproving the Stable Coordinate conjecture in four variables. Every fiber is affine three-space, yet none of its embeddings is rectifiable, also disproving the Abhyankar--Sathaye conjecture even when all fibers are affine spaces.

families.title: A counterexample to Griffiths’ positivity conjecture
families.summary: Constructs ample rank-two bundles on $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$ with no smooth Hermitian metric of strictly Griffiths-positive curvature, disproving Griffiths' positivity conjecture already on the quadric surface.
families.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
families.overviewTitle: A counterexample to Griffiths' positivity conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Constructs ample rank-two bundles on $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$ with no smooth Hermitian metric of strictly Griffiths-positive curvature, disproving Griffiths' positivity conjecture already on the quadric surface.

families.title: Kobayashi’s canonical-ampleness conjecture
families.summary: Every compact connected Kähler manifold of positive complex dimension with no nonconstant entire curve has ample canonical bundle and is therefore projective. This proves Kobayashi's canonical-ampleness conjecture in the smooth compact Kähler setting.
families.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
families.overviewTitle: Kobayashi's canonical-ampleness conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Every compact connected K\"ahler manifold of positive complex dimension with no nonconstant entire curve has ample canonical bundle and is therefore projective. This proves Kobayashi's canonical-ampleness conjecture in the smooth compact K\"ahler setting.

families.title: Tangent splittings and product decompositions
families.summary: A splitting of the tangent bundle of a compact Kähler manifold into two integrable holomorphic subbundles induces a compatible product decomposition of its universal cover, proving the two-summand form of Beauville's splitting conjecture. On smooth rationally connected projective manifolds, both summands are automatically integrable, establishing Höring's conjecture and the corresponding product decomposition.
families.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
families.overviewTitle: Tangent-bundle splittings and universal covers
families.overviewSummary: A splitting of the tangent bundle of a compact K\"ahler manifold into two integrable holomorphic subbundles induces a compatible product decomposition of its universal cover, proving the two-summand form of Beauville's splitting conjecture. On smooth rationally connected projective manifolds, both summands are automatically integrable, establishing H\"oring's conjecture and the corresponding product decomposition.

families.title: A counterexample to Pixton completeness in Chow
families.summary: Constructs a tautological relation on a moduli space of stable pointed curves that vanishes in rational Chow, hence in rational cohomology, but lies outside Pixton's original relation span. This disproves the Chow and rational-cohomological forms of his original completeness conjecture.
families.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
families.overviewTitle: A counterexample to Pixton's original completeness conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Constructs a tautological relation on a moduli space of stable pointed curves that vanishes in rational Chow, hence in rational cohomology, but lies outside Pixton's original relation span. This disproves the Chow and rational-cohomological forms of his original completeness conjecture.

families.title: Irrational cubic fourfolds with Hodge-theoretic and categorical K3 associations
families.summary: For every sufficiently large admissible Hassett discriminant, a very general smooth complex cubic fourfold is irrational despite having both an untwisted geometric K3 category and an integral Hodge-theoretic K3 association. This disproves Kuznetsov's rationality conjecture and the sufficiency of the associated-K3 criterion for rationality; the discriminant threshold is ineffective.
families.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
families.overviewTitle: Counterexamples to Kuznetsov's rationality conjecture
families.overviewSummary: For every sufficiently large admissible Hassett discriminant, a very general smooth complex cubic fourfold is irrational despite having both an untwisted geometric K3 category and an integral Hodge-theoretic K3 association. This disproves Kuznetsov's rationality conjecture and the sufficiency of the associated-K3 criterion for rationality; the discriminant threshold is ineffective.

families.title: Gepner symmetry and large-volume stability on threefolds
families.summary: Proves Toda's Gepner conjecture for every smooth complex quintic threefold, constructing a numerical Bridgeland stability condition with the prescribed phase shift 2/5. Also constructs numerical Bridgeland stability conditions at every sufficiently large volume on all smooth projective complex threefolds with trivial canonical bundle, with the exact ordinary and square-root-Todd central charges.
families.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
families.overviewTitle: Toda's Gepner conjecture and large-volume stability
families.overviewSummary: Proves Toda's Gepner conjecture for every smooth complex quintic threefold, constructing a numerical Bridgeland stability condition with the prescribed phase shift $2/5$. Also constructs numerical Bridgeland stability conditions at every sufficiently large volume on all smooth projective complex threefolds with trivial canonical bundle, with the exact ordinary and square-root-Todd central charges.

families.title: Termination of projective and Kähler fourfold minimal model programs
families.summary: Proves termination of every existing generalized log canonical flip sequence on globally Weil ℚ-factorial compact Kähler fourfolds, with rational boundary, fixed rational analytically nef b-data, and projective small flip diagrams with the prescribed ample signs. Also proves termination of arbitrary permitted minimal model programs for projective log canonical fourfolds with rational boundary in characteristic zero.
families.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
families.overviewTitle: Termination of fourfold minimal model programs
families.overviewSummary: Proves termination of every existing generalized log canonical flip sequence on globally Weil $\mathbb Q$-factorial compact K\"ahler fourfolds, with rational boundary, fixed rational analytically nef b-data, and projective small flip diagrams with the prescribed ample signs. Also proves termination of arbitrary permitted minimal model programs for projective log canonical fourfolds with rational boundary in characteristic zero.

families.title: Fundamental groups of special complex varieties and root orbifolds
families.summary: Proves Campana's abelianity conjecture: special compact Kähler manifolds have virtually abelian fundamental groups. Using this theorem, establishes the same conclusion for order-two root orbifolds of smooth projective complex fourfolds along one nonempty smooth connected divisor, when special in the stated differential-line sense. For smooth special complex quasi-projective varieties, proves that every finite-dimensional complex linear representation of the fundamental group has virtually nilpotent image of class at most two.
families.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
families.overviewTitle: Campana's abelianity conjecture and special varieties
families.overviewSummary: Proves Campana's abelianity conjecture: special compact K\"ahler manifolds have virtually abelian fundamental groups. Using this theorem, establishes the same conclusion for order-two root orbifolds of smooth projective complex fourfolds along one nonempty smooth connected divisor, when special in the stated differential-line sense. For smooth special complex quasi-projective varieties, proves that every finite-dimensional complex linear representation of the fundamental group has virtually nilpotent image of class at most two.

families.title: Semialgebraic universal covers and bounded domains
families.summary: Proves the Kollár–Pardon conjecture: the semialgebraic universal covers of connected normal projective complex varieties are exactly products $D\times\mathbb C^m\times F$, with D bounded symmetric and F simply connected, normal, and projective. A universal cover is quasi-projective exactly when the bounded symmetric factor is absent. In particular, a smooth projective variety covered by ℂn has a finite étale cover by an abelian variety.
families.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
families.overviewTitle: The Koll\'ar--Pardon universal-cover conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Proves the Koll\'ar--Pardon conjecture: the semialgebraic universal covers of connected normal projective complex varieties are exactly products $D\times\mathbb C^m\times F$, with $D$ bounded symmetric and $F$ simply connected, normal, and projective. A universal cover is quasi-projective exactly when the bounded symmetric factor is absent. In particular, a smooth projective variety covered by $\mathbb C^n$ has a finite étale cover by an abelian variety.

families.title: Counterexamples to Zariski’s multiplicity conjecture
families.summary: Disproves Zariski's multiplicity conjecture by constructing reduced holomorphic hypersurface germs that are ambiently homeomorphic but have different multiplicities. The examples include hypersurfaces in ℂ4 with isolated critical points and multiplicities four and five.
families.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
families.overviewTitle: Counterexamples to Zariski's multiplicity conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Disproves Zariski's multiplicity conjecture by constructing reduced holomorphic hypersurface germs that are ambiently homeomorphic but have different multiplicities. The examples include hypersurfaces in $\mathbb C^4$ with isolated critical points and multiplicities four and five.

families.title: The Global Spherical Shell conjecture
families.summary: Every connected minimal compact complex surface of class VII with $b_2\gt 0$ contains a global spherical shell, proving the positive-b2 Global Spherical Shell conjecture. Such a shell is a holomorphically embedded neighborhood of the standard three-sphere in $\mathbb C^2\setminus\{0\}$ whose complement is connected.
families.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
families.overviewTitle: The Global Spherical Shell conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Every connected minimal compact complex surface of class VII with $b_2>0$ contains a global spherical shell, proving the positive-$b_2$ Global Spherical Shell conjecture. Such a shell is a holomorphically embedded neighborhood of the standard three-sphere in $\mathbb C^2\setminus\{0\}$ whose complement is connected.

families.title: Projective contact classification and the LeBrun–Salamon conjecture
families.summary: Proves the LeBrun–Salamon conjecture: every closed connected positive quaternionic-Kähler manifold of real dimension at least eight is homothetic to a compact symmetric Wolf space. It also proves contact-Fano homogeneity and classifies smooth connected complex projective contact manifolds of complex dimension at least three: those with $b_2=1$ are adjoint varieties with their canonical contact structures, while those with $b_2\ge2$ have underlying manifold $\mathbb P(T^*Z)$ for a smooth projective variety Z.
families.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
families.overviewTitle: The LeBrun--Salamon conjecture and projective contact classification
families.overviewSummary: Proves the LeBrun--Salamon conjecture: every closed connected positive quaternionic-K\"ahler manifold of real dimension at least eight is homothetic to a compact symmetric Wolf space. It also proves contact-Fano homogeneity and classifies smooth connected complex projective contact manifolds of complex dimension at least three: those with $b_2=1$ are adjoint varieties with their canonical contact structures, while those with $b_2\ge2$ have underlying manifold $\mathbb P(T^*Z)$ for a smooth projective variety $Z$.

families.title: The generalized Mukai conjecture
families.summary: Proves the generalized Mukai conjecture: every positive-dimensional smooth complex projective Fano manifold of dimension n, Picard number ρ and pseudoindex ι satisfies $\rho(\iota-1)\le n$, with equality exactly for $(\mathbb P^{\iota-1})^\rho$. Here the pseudoindex is the least anticanonical degree of a rational curve.
families.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
families.overviewTitle: The generalized Mukai conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Proves the generalized Mukai conjecture: every positive-dimensional smooth complex projective Fano manifold of dimension $n$, Picard number $\rho$ and pseudoindex $\iota$ satisfies $\rho(\iota-1)\le n$, with equality exactly for $(\mathbb P^{\iota-1})^\rho$. Here the pseudoindex is the least anticanonical degree of a rational curve.

families.title: Topological triviality of μ-constant surface singularities
families.summary: Proves topological right-triviality for every holomorphic one-parameter family of isolated hypersurface singularities in ℂ3 with constant Milnor number, resolving the surface case of the μ-constant problem. After shrinking the parameter disk and representatives, ambient homeomorphisms vary jointly continuously, fix the origin section and preserve the defining functions.
families.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
families.overviewTitle: The $\mu$-constant problem for surface singularities
families.overviewSummary: Proves topological right-triviality for every holomorphic one-parameter family of isolated hypersurface singularities in $\mathbb C^3$ with constant Milnor number, resolving the surface case of the $\mu$-constant problem. After shrinking the parameter disk and representatives, ambient homeomorphisms vary jointly continuously, fix the origin section and preserve the defining functions.

families.title: Virasoro constraints for complete intersections and projective-bundle towers
families.summary: Proves the full ordinary unreduced descendant Virasoro conjecture for smooth complete intersections in complex projective space, in every genus and curve class with arbitrary cohomology insertions. The constraints also pass from any smooth projective complex base satisfying them to the projectivization of every algebraic vector bundle of rank at least two, and hence to projective-bundle towers.
families.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
families.overviewTitle: Virasoro constraints for complete intersections and projective bundles
families.overviewSummary: Proves the full ordinary unreduced descendant Virasoro conjecture for smooth complete intersections in complex projective space, in every genus and curve class with arbitrary cohomology insertions. The constraints also pass from any smooth projective complex base satisfying them to the projectivization of every algebraic vector bundle of rank at least two, and hence to projective-bundle towers.

families.title: Bounded klt complements for Fano contractions
families.summary: Proves the finite-rational-coefficient form of Shokurov’s bounded-klt-complement conjecture for ϵ-lc complex Fano-type pairs with nef anti-log-canonical divisor. For ϵ-lc Fano contractions over any algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, it gives klt complements near every base point, with index bounded only by dimension and positive rational ϵ.
families.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
families.overviewTitle: Bounded klt complements for Fano contractions
families.overviewSummary: Proves the finite-rational-coefficient form of Shokurov’s bounded-klt-complement conjecture for $\epsilon$-lc complex Fano-type pairs with nef anti-log-canonical divisor. For $\epsilon$-lc Fano contractions over any algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, it gives klt complements near every base point, with index bounded only by dimension and positive rational $\epsilon$.

families.title: The Campana–Peternell conjecture in dimension six
families.summary: Proves the Campana–Peternell conjecture in complex dimension six: every smooth connected complex projective Fano sixfold with nef tangent bundle is rational homogeneous.
families.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
families.overviewTitle: The Campana--Peternell conjecture in dimension six
families.overviewSummary: Proves the Campana--Peternell conjecture in complex dimension six: every smooth connected complex projective Fano sixfold with nef tangent bundle is rational homogeneous.

families.title: Anticanonical nonvanishing in every dimension
families.summary: If X is a smooth connected complex projective variety and $-K_X$ admits a smooth Hermitian metric with nonnegative curvature, then $H^0(X,-mK_X)\ne0$ for some m > 0. Thus smooth semipositivity forces a nonzero section of a positive tensor power of the anticanonical bundle in every dimension.
families.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
families.overviewTitle: Anticanonical nonvanishing under smooth semipositivity
families.overviewSummary: If $X$ is a smooth connected complex projective variety and $-K_X$ admits a smooth Hermitian metric with nonnegative curvature, then $H^0(X,-mK_X)\ne0$ for some $m>0$. Thus smooth semipositivity forces a nonzero section of a positive tensor power of the anticanonical bundle in every dimension.

families.title: Global quantum geometric Langlands at irrational level
families.summary: Proves the unramified de Rham quantum geometric Langlands equivalence for every connected simple complex algebraic group on every smooth projective connected complex curve, at every shifted level $c\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb Q$. It identifies the full derived categories of twisted D-modules for the group and its Langlands dual, retaining all global forms and connected components.
families.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
families.overviewTitle: Quantum geometric Langlands at irrational level
families.overviewSummary: Proves the unramified de Rham quantum geometric Langlands equivalence for every connected simple complex algebraic group on every smooth projective connected complex curve, at every shifted level $c\in\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb Q$. It identifies the full derived categories of twisted $D$-modules for the group and its Langlands dual, retaining all global forms and connected components.

families.title: Koebe’s circle-domain conjecture
families.summary: Resolves the existence part of Koebe's circle-domain conjecture: every domain in the Riemann sphere is conformally equivalent to a domain whose complementary components are round disks or points. It also proves that circle domains with conformally removable boundary are rigid, meaning every conformal equivalence to another circle domain is Möbius, establishing this direction of the He–Schramm conjecture.
families.subject: Real and complex analysis
families.overviewTitle: Koebe's circle-domain conjecture and circle-domain rigidity
families.overviewSummary: Resolves the existence part of Koebe's circle-domain conjecture: every domain in the Riemann sphere is conformally equivalent to a domain whose complementary components are round disks or points. It also proves that circle domains with conformally removable boundary are rigid, meaning every conformal equivalence to another circle domain is M\"obius, establishing this direction of the He--Schramm conjecture.

families.title: Brennan's conjecture and the integral-means spectrum
families.summary: Proves Brennan's conjecture: for every conformal bijection ϕ from a simply connected plane domain onto the disk, $|\phi'|^s$ is area-integrable for $4/3\lt s\lt 4$. The sharp universal integral-means identity is $B_{\mathcal S}(t)=|t|-1$ for t ≤ −2. A strict bound $B_b(-1)\lt 1/4$ for bounded univalent functions disproves Kraetzer's prediction at that parameter.
families.subject: Real and complex analysis
families.overviewTitle: Brennan's conjecture and a counterexample to Kraetzer's prediction
families.overviewSummary: Proves Brennan's conjecture: for every conformal bijection $\phi$ from a simply connected plane domain onto the disk, $|\phi'|^s$ is area-integrable for $4/3<s<4$. The sharp universal integral-means identity is $B_{\mathcal S}(t)=|t|-1$ for $t\le-2$. A strict bound $B_b(-1)<1/4$ for bounded univalent functions disproves Kraetzer's prediction at that parameter.

families.title: The Falconer distance conjecture
families.summary: Resolves the Falconer distance conjecture in every dimension d ≥ 2: every compact set $E\subset\mathbb R^d$ with Hausdorff dimension greater than $d/2$ determines a set of Euclidean distances of positive Lebesgue measure.
families.subject: Real and complex analysis
families.overviewTitle: The Falconer distance conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Resolves the Falconer distance conjecture in every dimension $d\ge2$: every compact set $E\subset\mathbb R^d$ with Hausdorff dimension greater than $d/2$ determines a set of Euclidean distances of positive Lebesgue measure.

families.title: Kakeya in three and four dimensions
families.summary: Resolves the Kakeya maximal conjecture in three dimensions and the Hausdorff-dimension conjecture in four. In three dimensions, the radius-δ tube maximal operator maps $L^3(\mathbb R^3)$ to $L^3(S^2)$ with norm $O_\varepsilon(\delta^{-\varepsilon})$ for every ε > 0. In four dimensions, every set containing a unit segment in every direction has Hausdorff dimension four.
families.subject: Real and complex analysis
families.overviewTitle: Kakeya in three and four dimensions
families.overviewSummary: Resolves the Kakeya maximal conjecture in three dimensions and the Hausdorff-dimension conjecture in four. In three dimensions, the radius-$\delta$ tube maximal operator maps $L^3(\mathbb R^3)$ to $L^3(S^2)$ with norm $O_\varepsilon(\delta^{-\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$. In four dimensions, every set containing a unit segment in every direction has Hausdorff dimension four.

families.title: The $L\log L$ Fourier-convergence conjecture
families.summary: Proves that the ordinary symmetric Fourier partial sums of every complex-valued function in $L\log L(\mathbb T)$ converge almost everywhere along the full sequence. This resolves the classical sufficiency conjecture at the $L\log L$ scale.
families.subject: Real and complex analysis
families.overviewTitle: The $L\log L$ Fourier-convergence conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Proves that the ordinary symmetric Fourier partial sums of every complex-valued function in $L\log L(\mathbb T)$ converge almost everywhere along the full sequence. This resolves the classical sufficiency conjecture at the $L\log L$ scale.

families.title: Real ultraflat Littlewood polynomials and unbounded binary merit factors
families.summary: Constructs polynomials with N consecutive coefficients in $\{-1,1\}$ whose modulus is $(1+o(1))\sqrt N$ uniformly on the entire unit circle, for every sufficiently large integer length N. Thus real Littlewood polynomials are ultraflat, including at the real endpoints. Their binary merit factors tend to infinity, disproving Turyn's bounded-merit-factor conjecture.
families.subject: Real and complex analysis
families.overviewTitle: Ultraflat real Littlewood polynomials
families.overviewSummary: Constructs polynomials with $N$ consecutive coefficients in $\{-1,1\}$ whose modulus is $(1+o(1))\sqrt N$ uniformly on the entire unit circle, for every sufficiently large integer length $N$. Thus real Littlewood polynomials are ultraflat, including at the real endpoints. Their binary merit factors tend to infinity, disproving Turyn's bounded-merit-factor conjecture.

families.title: Fourier restriction for positively curved surfaces
families.summary: Proves the diagonal Fourier extension conjecture for positively curved surfaces in three dimensions. For every compact smooth positively curved surface $\Sigma\subset\mathbb R^3$, including surfaces with boundary, the extension operator is bounded from $L^p(\Sigma)$ to $L^p(\mathbb R^3)$ for every p > 3.
families.subject: Real and complex analysis
families.overviewTitle: Fourier restriction for positively curved surfaces
families.overviewSummary: Proves the diagonal Fourier extension conjecture for positively curved surfaces in three dimensions. For every compact smooth positively curved surface $\Sigma\subset\mathbb R^3$, including surfaces with boundary, the extension operator is bounded from $L^p(\Sigma)$ to $L^p(\mathbb R^3)$ for every $p>3$.

families.title: The three-dimensional Bochner–Riesz conjecture
families.summary: Resolves the three-dimensional Bochner–Riesz conjecture in its strict range: the Bochner–Riesz multipliers of order δ are bounded on $L^p(\mathbb R^3)$ for every $1\le p\le\infty$ whenever $\delta\gt \max\{3|1/p-1/2|-1/2,0\}$.
families.subject: Real and complex analysis
families.overviewTitle: The three-dimensional Bochner--Riesz conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Resolves the three-dimensional Bochner--Riesz conjecture in its strict range: the Bochner--Riesz multipliers of order $\delta$ are bounded on $L^p(\mathbb R^3)$ for every $1\le p\le\infty$ whenever $\delta>\max\{3|1/p-1/2|-1/2,0\}$.

families.title: Local smoothing in three dimensions
families.summary: Resolves Sogge's local smoothing conjecture for the Euclidean wave equation in three spatial dimensions. The estimate holds throughout the full strict range $2\lt p\lt \infty$, with Sobolev regularity above $\max\{0,1-3/p\}$. In particular, the critical L3 estimate holds with every positive Sobolev loss.
families.subject: Real and complex analysis
families.overviewTitle: Sogge's local smoothing conjecture in dimension three
families.overviewSummary: Resolves Sogge's local smoothing conjecture for the Euclidean wave equation in three spatial dimensions. The estimate holds throughout the full strict range $2<p<\infty$, with Sobolev regularity above $\max\{0,1-3/p\}$. In particular, the critical $L^3$ estimate holds with every positive Sobolev loss.

families.title: The exact Sobolev endpoint for Schrödinger convergence
families.summary: Proves almost-everywhere convergence $e^{it\Delta}f\to f$ as $t\downarrow0$ for every $f\in H^{n/(2(n+1))}(\mathbb R^n)$ and every dimension n ≥ 2. This attains the sharp Sobolev equality case of Carleson's Schrödinger convergence problem, including the planar endpoint H1/3.
families.subject: Real and complex analysis
families.overviewTitle: The Sobolev endpoint in Carleson's Schr\"odinger convergence problem
families.overviewSummary: Proves almost-everywhere convergence $e^{it\Delta}f\to f$ as $t\downarrow0$ for every $f\in H^{n/(2(n+1))}(\mathbb R^n)$ and every dimension $n\ge2$. This attains the sharp Sobolev equality case of Carleson's Schr\"odinger convergence problem, including the planar endpoint $H^{1/3}$.

families.title: Riesz transforms and rectifiability in higher codimension
families.summary: Resolves the remaining higher-codimension Riesz-transform rectifiability problem: for d ≥ 4 and $2\le n\le d-2$, an n-Ahlfors–David regular Radon measure on ℝd is uniformly n-rectifiable whenever its n-dimensional Riesz transform is uniformly L2-bounded over all positive hard truncations. The rectifiability bounds depend only on dimension, regularity and operator bounds.
families.subject: Real and complex analysis
families.overviewTitle: The David--Semmes Riesz-transform problem in higher codimension
families.overviewSummary: Resolves the remaining higher-codimension Riesz-transform rectifiability problem: for $d\ge4$ and $2\le n\le d-2$, an $n$-Ahlfors--David regular Radon measure on $\mathbb R^d$ is uniformly $n$-rectifiable whenever its $n$-dimensional Riesz transform is uniformly $L^2$-bounded over all positive hard truncations. The rectifiability bounds depend only on dimension, regularity and operator bounds.

families.title: Annular variation and dyadic absolute bounds for the triangular Hilbert transform
families.summary: Proves maximal and annular r-variation bounds, for every r > 2, from complex $L^3(\mathbb R^2)\times L^3(\mathbb R^2)$ to $L^{3/2}(\mathbb R^2)$. The maximal estimate controls both hard truncation endpoints and gives almost-everywhere and norm convergence. Pairing with a third input settles the triangular Hilbert transform estimate at the symmetric $L^3\times L^3\times L^3$ point.
families.subject: Real and complex analysis
families.overviewTitle: Maximal and variational bounds for the triangular Hilbert transform
families.overviewSummary: Proves maximal and annular $r$-variation bounds, for every $r>2$, from complex $L^3(\mathbb R^2)\times L^3(\mathbb R^2)$ to $L^{3/2}(\mathbb R^2)$. The maximal estimate controls both hard truncation endpoints and gives almost-everywhere and norm convergence. Pairing with a third input settles the triangular Hilbert transform estimate at the symmetric $L^3\times L^3\times L^3$ point.

families.title: Hilbert transforms along Lipschitz directions
families.summary: Proves a uniform strong L2 bound for the planar Hilbert transform along any Lipschitz unit vector field, at integration lengths bounded by an absolute multiple of its reciprocal Lipschitz constant. The estimate is uniform over inner truncations and yields an L2-bounded principal-value operator, establishing Stein's weak-type conjecture at this short scale.
families.subject: Real and complex analysis
families.overviewTitle: Stein's conjecture for Hilbert transforms along Lipschitz directions
families.overviewSummary: Proves a uniform strong $L^2$ bound for the planar Hilbert transform along any Lipschitz unit vector field, at integration lengths bounded by an absolute multiple of its reciprocal Lipschitz constant. The estimate is uniform over inner truncations and yields an $L^2$-bounded principal-value operator, establishing Stein's weak-type conjecture at this short scale.

families.title: The geometric case of the Erdős similarity conjecture
families.summary: For every fixed $q\in(0,1)$, constructs compact subsets of $[0,1]$ with measure arbitrarily close to one containing no translated and nontrivially dilated copy of $\{q^n:n\ge1\}$, with dilations of either sign. This resolves the geometric-progression case of the Erdős similarity conjecture for every ratio.
families.subject: Real and complex analysis
families.overviewTitle: The geometric case of the Erd\H{o}s similarity conjecture
families.overviewSummary: For every fixed $q\in(0,1)$, constructs compact subsets of $[0,1]$ with measure arbitrarily close to one containing no translated and nontrivially dilated copy of $\{q^n:n\ge1\}$, with dilations of either sign. This resolves the geometric-progression case of the Erd\H{o}s similarity conjecture for every ratio.

families.title: Endpoint Sobolev regularity of centered disk averages
families.summary: Resolves the planar centered-disk case of the Hajłasz–Onninen maximal-function regularity problem. For every real $f\in W^{1,1}(\mathbb R^2)$, the centered disk maximal function satisfies $\|\nabla Mf\|_1\le C\|\nabla f\|_1$ with an absolute constant. It belongs locally to $W^{1,1}$ and has a globally integrable weak gradient.
families.subject: Real and complex analysis
families.overviewTitle: Endpoint regularity of the planar centered maximal function
families.overviewSummary: Resolves the planar centered-disk case of the Haj{\l}asz--Onninen maximal-function regularity problem. For every real $f\in W^{1,1}(\mathbb R^2)$, the centered disk maximal function satisfies $\|\nabla Mf\|_1\le C\|\nabla f\|_1$ with an absolute constant. It belongs locally to $W^{1,1}$ and has a globally integrable weak gradient.

families.title: An L3 bound for the trilinear Hilbert transform
families.summary: Proves that the principal-value trilinear Hilbert transform with shifts $x-t$, $x-2t$, $x-3t$ is bounded from $L^3(\mathbb R)^3$ to $L^1(\mathbb R)$. This resolves the L3 exponent case of the standard conjecture for slopes 1, 2, 3.
families.subject: Real and complex analysis
families.overviewTitle: An $L^3$ bound for the trilinear Hilbert transform
families.overviewSummary: Proves that the principal-value trilinear Hilbert transform with shifts $x-t$, $x-2t$, $x-3t$ is bounded from $L^3(\mathbb R)^3$ to $L^1(\mathbb R)$. This resolves the $L^3$ exponent case of the standard conjecture for slopes $1,2,3$.

families.title: The Mahler conjectures, functional inequalities and polar-product symplectic width
families.summary: Resolves the symmetric and nonsymmetric geometric Mahler conjectures in every dimension, with Hanner polytopes and simplices as the respective volume-product minimizers and all equality cases classified. The corresponding sharp functional Mahler inequalities also hold. For n ≥ 2, every symmetric polar product $K\times K^\circ$ in dimension $2n$ has Gromov width 4.
families.subject: Convex and metric geometry
families.overviewTitle: The Mahler conjectures and symplectic width
families.overviewSummary: Resolves the symmetric and nonsymmetric geometric Mahler conjectures in every dimension, with Hanner polytopes and simplices as the respective volume-product minimizers and all equality cases classified. The corresponding sharp functional Mahler inequalities also hold. For $n\ge2$, every symmetric polar product $K\times K^\circ$ in dimension $2n$ has Gromov width $4$.

families.title: Sharp projection-body inequalities and a counterexample to simplex maximization
families.summary: Proves Petty's projection-volume conjecture in the remaining dimensions n ≥ 4: ellipsoids uniquely minimize projection-body volume at fixed body volume. Also establishes the full Lutwak–Petty projection inequalities. In contrast, products of simplices exceed Brannen's proposed simplex maximum for normalized projection-body volume by an exponential factor in every sufficiently large dimension.
families.subject: Convex and metric geometry
families.overviewTitle: Petty's projection-volume conjecture and simplex counterexamples
families.overviewSummary: Proves Petty's projection-volume conjecture in the remaining dimensions $n\ge4$: ellipsoids uniquely minimize projection-body volume at fixed body volume. Also establishes the full Lutwak--Petty projection inequalities. In contrast, products of simplices exceed Brannen's proposed simplex maximum for normalized projection-body volume by an exponential factor in every sufficiently large dimension.

families.title: Bounded-distortion L1 embeddings of planar and bounded-treewidth graphs
families.summary: Resolves the planar and bounded-treewidth cases of the Gupta–Newman–Rabinovich–Sinclair conjecture. Shortest-path metrics of finite connected graphs with arbitrary positive edge lengths embed into real L1 with universal distortion for planar graphs, and distortion depending only on treewidth for bounded-treewidth graphs. The corresponding multicommodity flow–cut gaps are uniformly bounded.
families.subject: Convex and metric geometry
families.overviewTitle: Bounded-distortion $L_1$ embeddings of planar and bounded-treewidth graphs
families.overviewSummary: Resolves the planar and bounded-treewidth cases of the Gupta--Newman--Rabinovich--Sinclair conjecture.
