Shortest-path metrics of finite connected graphs with arbitrary positive edge lengths embed into real $L_1$ with universal distortion for planar graphs, and distortion depending only on treewidth for bounded-treewidth graphs. The corresponding multicommodity flow--cut gaps are uniformly bounded.

families.title: Triangular-lattice optimality, long-range Riesz and Coulomb energies, and spherical logarithmic energy
families.summary: Proves that the triangular lattice minimizes the lower limit of energy per particle for every nonnegative completely monotone potential of squared distance among locally finite planar configurations of centered-disk density one. It also minimizes unit-background renormalized Riesz energies for $0\lt s\lt 2$ and Coulomb energy, resolving Sandier–Serfaty and the two-dimensional Brauchart–Hardin–Saff conjecture on the linear term of optimal spherical logarithmic energy.
families.subject: Convex and metric geometry
families.overviewTitle: Universal optimality of the triangular lattice
families.overviewSummary: Proves that the triangular lattice minimizes the lower limit of energy per particle for every nonnegative completely monotone potential of squared distance among locally finite planar configurations of centered-disk density one. It also minimizes unit-background renormalized Riesz energies for $0<s<2$ and Coulomb energy, resolving Sandier--Serfaty and the two-dimensional Brauchart--Hardin--Saff conjecture on the linear term of optimal spherical logarithmic energy.

families.title: Logarithmic and Lp Brunn–Minkowski inequalities and the B-conjecture
families.summary: Proves the logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski inequality for origin-symmetric convex bodies in every dimension, and the scalar-dilation B-conjecture for all even log-concave Radon measures. For Lebesgue volume it also proves the additive Lp Brunn–Minkowski inequality for full-dimensional origin-symmetric convex bodies throughout $0\lt p\lt 1$.
families.subject: Convex and metric geometry
families.overviewTitle: The logarithmic Brunn--Minkowski conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Proves the logarithmic Brunn--Minkowski inequality for origin-symmetric convex bodies in every dimension, and the scalar-dilation B-conjecture for all even log-concave Radon measures. For Lebesgue volume it also proves the additive $L_p$ Brunn--Minkowski inequality for full-dimensional origin-symmetric convex bodies throughout $0<p<1$.

families.title: The optimal order of convex-body covering density
families.summary: Determines the optimal worst-case covering density as $\Theta(n\log n)$, for both lattice and unrestricted translative coverings. Every convex body in ℝn, n ≥ 2, admits a lattice covering of density at most $Cn\log n$; centrally symmetric examples in every sufficiently large dimension require at least $cn\log n$ even without the lattice restriction, for absolute $c,C\gt 0$.
families.subject: Convex and metric geometry
families.overviewTitle: The optimal order of convex-body covering density
families.overviewSummary: Determines the optimal worst-case covering density as $\Theta(n\log n)$, for both lattice and unrestricted translative coverings. Every convex body in $\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, admits a lattice covering of density at most $Cn\log n$; centrally symmetric examples in every sufficiently large dimension require at least $cn\log n$ even without the lattice restriction, for absolute $c,C>0$.

families.title: Dimension-free logarithmic Sobolev inequality for subgaussian log-concave measures
families.summary: Proves a dimension-free logarithmic Sobolev inequality for centered log-concave densities with uniformly subgaussian linear marginals, with constant bounded by a universal multiple of the squared linear subgaussian parameter.
families.subject: Convex and metric geometry
families.overviewTitle: Dimension-free logarithmic Sobolev inequality for subgaussian log-concave measures
families.overviewSummary: Proves a dimension-free logarithmic Sobolev inequality for centered log-concave densities with uniformly subgaussian linear marginals, with constant bounded by a universal multiple of the squared linear subgaussian parameter.

families.title: Subpolynomial dimension reduction in Lp
families.summary: For every fixed $1\lt p\lt \infty$ and distortion D > 1, every n-point subset of real Lp embeds into $\ell_p^d$ with distortion at most D and dimension $d=n^{o(1)}$, answering Naor's sublinear-dimension question for p ≠ 2. In contrast, exact embeddings require worst-case dimension $\Theta(n^2)$ when p ≠ 2.
families.subject: Convex and metric geometry
families.overviewTitle: Subpolynomial dimension reduction in $L_p$
families.overviewSummary: For every fixed $1<p<\infty$ and distortion $D>1$, every $n$-point subset of real $L_p$ embeds into $\ell_p^d$ with distortion at most $D$ and dimension $d=n^{o(1)}$, answering Naor's sublinear-dimension question for $p\ne2$. In contrast, exact embeddings require worst-case dimension $\Theta(n^2)$ when $p\ne2$.

families.title: Hyperbolicity cones without semidefinite lifts
families.summary: Disproves the Projected Lax conjecture: some hyperbolicity cones are not spectrahedral shadows. The examples admit no exact finite affine semidefinite lift, regardless of the number of auxiliary variables or the real coefficients used. This also disproves the generalized Lax conjecture that every hyperbolicity cone is spectrahedral.
families.subject: Convex and metric geometry
families.overviewTitle: Hyperbolicity cones without semidefinite lifts
families.overviewSummary: Disproves the Projected Lax conjecture: some hyperbolicity cones are not spectrahedral shadows. The examples admit no exact finite affine semidefinite lift, regardless of the number of auxiliary variables or the real coefficients used. This also disproves the generalized Lax conjecture that every hyperbolicity cone is spectrahedral.

families.title: The Gaussian propeller conjecture in every dimension
families.summary: Proves that the sum of squared Gaussian first moments of any finite measurable partition is at most $9/(8\pi)$. In dimension at least two, three planar sectors of angle $2\pi/3$, extended orthogonally, attain the bound. Combined with the separate Unique Games theorem, this proves NP-hardness of improving the loss factor $(8\pi/9)(1-1/k)$ for identity-target kernel clustering with fixed k ≥ 3 on rational centered positive semidefinite inputs.
families.subject: Convex and metric geometry
families.overviewTitle: The Gaussian propeller conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Proves that the sum of squared Gaussian first moments of any finite measurable partition is at most $9/(8\pi)$. In dimension at least two, three planar sectors of angle $2\pi/3$, extended orthogonally, attain the bound. Combined with the separate Unique Games theorem, this proves NP-hardness of improving the loss factor $(8\pi/9)(1-1/k)$ for identity-target kernel clustering with fixed $k\ge3$ on rational centered positive semidefinite inputs.

families.title: The Euclidean Steinitz–Bergström bound
families.summary: Proves that any finite sequence in the Euclidean unit ball of ℝd admits signs keeping every partial sum within $C\sqrt d$, independently of length. Consequently every zero-sum family can be reordered with the same bound on unsigned partial sums. A matching lower bound gives the optimal order $S_2(d)=\Theta(\sqrt d)$.
families.subject: Convex and metric geometry
families.overviewTitle: The Euclidean Steinitz--Bergstr\"om conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Proves that any finite sequence in the Euclidean unit ball of $\mathbb R^d$ admits signs keeping every partial sum within $C\sqrt d$, independently of length. Consequently every zero-sum family can be reordered with the same bound on unsigned partial sums. A matching lower bound gives the optimal order $S_2(d)=\Theta(\sqrt d)$.

families.title: Compact counterexamples to bi-Lipschitz dimension reduction
families.summary: Every infinite-dimensional real Banach space contains a compact doubling set that admits no bi-Lipschitz embedding into any finite-dimensional normed space. The doubling constant is universal. This answers the Lang–Plaut problem negatively, even for compact subsets of Hilbert space.
families.subject: Convex and metric geometry
families.overviewTitle: A negative answer to the Lang--Plaut problem
families.overviewSummary: Every infinite-dimensional real Banach space contains a compact doubling set that admits no bi-Lipschitz embedding into any finite-dimensional normed space. The doubling constant is universal. This answers the Lang--Plaut problem negatively, even for compact subsets of Hilbert space.

families.title: The sharp exponential scale of edit-distance distortion
families.summary: Determines the least distortion of embedding edit distance on words of length at most d into real ℓ1: it is $\exp(\Theta(\sqrt{\log d\,\log\log d}))$. Insertions, deletions and substitutions have unit cost. The constants are uniform over all finite alphabets with at least two symbols, even when the alphabet grows with d; binary words already force the lower bound.
families.subject: Convex and metric geometry
families.overviewTitle: The sharp distortion of edit distance into $\ell_1$
families.overviewSummary: Determines the least distortion of embedding edit distance on words of length at most $d$ into real $\ell_1$: it is $\exp(\Theta(\sqrt{\log d\,\log\log d}))$. Insertions, deletions and substitutions have unit cost. The constants are uniform over all finite alphabets with at least two symbols, even when the alphabet grows with $d$; binary words already force the lower bound.

families.title: Cylinder coverings below the half-area bound
families.summary: Covers the entire closed regular tetrahedron by finitely many cylinders with compact triangular perpendicular bases whose total area is less than half its smallest orthogonal projection area. This disproves Bang's half-area cylinder-covering bound and the stronger directionwise normalized conjecture in dimension three.
families.subject: Convex and metric geometry
families.overviewTitle: A counterexample to Bang's cylinder-covering bound
families.overviewSummary: Covers the entire closed regular tetrahedron by finitely many cylinders with compact triangular perpendicular bases whose total area is less than half its smallest orthogonal projection area. This disproves Bang's half-area cylinder-covering bound and the stronger directionwise normalized conjecture in dimension three.

families.title: The sharp simplex conjecture for isotropic constants
families.summary: Proves that simplices uniquely maximize the isotropic constant among convex bodies in every dimension, resolving the strong isotropic constant conjecture. Also establishes the sharp entropy lower bound for log-concave probability densities, with equality precisely for invertible affine images of products of one-sided exponential laws.
families.subject: Convex and metric geometry
families.overviewTitle: The sharp simplex conjecture for isotropic constants
families.overviewSummary: Proves that simplices uniquely maximize the isotropic constant among convex bodies in every dimension, resolving the strong isotropic constant conjecture. Also establishes the sharp entropy lower bound for log-concave probability densities, with equality precisely for invertible affine images of products of one-sided exponential laws.

families.title: The Unique Games Conjecture and optimal approximation thresholds
families.summary: Proves Khot's Unique Games Conjecture. Independent direct reductions also establish NP-hardness, on unweighted graphs, of approximation beyond the Goemans–Williamson ratio for Max-Cut, below factor two for Vertex Cover, and within any fixed constant factor for Min-UnCut and directed feedback vertex set. These direct proofs use established PCP and Label Cover hardness results.
families.subject: Theoretical computer science
families.overviewTitle: The Unique Games Conjecture and optimal approximation thresholds
families.overviewSummary: Proves Khot's Unique Games Conjecture. Independent direct reductions also establish NP-hardness, on unweighted graphs, of approximation beyond the Goemans--Williamson ratio for Max-Cut, below factor two for Vertex Cover, and within any fixed constant factor for Min-UnCut and directed feedback vertex set. These direct proofs use established PCP and Label Cover hardness results.

families.title: Exact derandomization of logarithmic space: $\mathsf L=\mathsf{RL}=\mathsf{BPL}$
families.summary: Proves $\mathsf L=\mathsf{RL}=\mathsf{BPL}$, resolving derandomization for bounded-error logarithmic-space computation. An effective compiler converts each randomized polynomial-time logarithmic-space machine deciding a language with one-sided or two-sided error into a deterministic logarithmic-space decider with explicit polynomial running-time bounds.
families.subject: Theoretical computer science
families.overviewTitle: Derandomization of logarithmic space: $\mathsf L=\mathsf{RL}=\mathsf{BPL}$
families.overviewSummary: Proves $\mathsf L=\mathsf{RL}=\mathsf{BPL}$, resolving derandomization for bounded-error logarithmic-space computation. An effective compiler converts each randomized polynomial-time logarithmic-space machine deciding a language with one-sided or two-sided error into a deterministic logarithmic-space decider with explicit polynomial running-time bounds.

families.title: Quasipolynomial algorithms for mean-payoff, stochastic and parity games
families.summary: Gives deterministic algorithms using $2^{O((\log(L+2))^2)}$ bit operations, for complete binary input length L, for ordinary mean-payoff games and two separate extensions. They compute exact values and optimal positional strategies in ordinary games, the nonnegative expectation-of-liminf value set in turn-based stochastic games, and the winning set for nonnegative liminf mean payoff conjoined with parity. Signed rewards, rational chance probabilities, and parity priorities are unrestricted and binary-encoded.
families.subject: Theoretical computer science
families.overviewTitle: Quasipolynomial algorithms for mean-payoff, stochastic and parity games
families.overviewSummary: Gives deterministic algorithms using $2^{O((\log(L+2))^2)}$ bit operations, for complete binary input length $L$, for ordinary mean-payoff games and two separate extensions. They compute exact values and optimal positional strategies in ordinary games, the nonnegative expectation-of-liminf value set in turn-based stochastic games, and the winning set for nonnegative liminf mean payoff conjoined with parity. Signed rewards, rational chance probabilities, and parity priorities are unrestricted and binary-encoded.

families.title: Perfect completeness for 2-to-1 games
families.summary: Proves Khot's 2-to-1 Games Conjecture with perfect completeness: for every fixed rational $\delta\in(0,1)$, it is NP-hard to distinguish satisfiable games from games whose optimum is at most δ, on explicit unweighted instances. The alphabet depends only on δ, and every right-hand label has exactly two preimages under each constraint map.
families.subject: Theoretical computer science
families.overviewTitle: The 2-to-1 Games Conjecture with perfect completeness
families.overviewSummary: Proves Khot's 2-to-1 Games Conjecture with perfect completeness: for every fixed rational $\delta\in(0,1)$, it is NP-hard to distinguish satisfiable games from games whose optimum is at most $\delta$, on explicit unweighted instances. The alphabet depends only on $\delta$, and every right-hand label has exactly two preimages under each constraint map.

families.title: Hardness of coloring three-colorable graphs
families.summary: It is NP-hard to color a three-colorable graph using any fixed number c ≥ 3 of colors. More strongly, for every fixed $0\lt \delta\lt 1/3$, a deterministic polynomial-time reduction from 3SAT produces simple unweighted graphs that are three-colorable in the satisfiable case and have no independent set of size $\delta n$ otherwise, where n is the number of vertices.
families.subject: Theoretical computer science
families.overviewTitle: Hardness of coloring three-colorable graphs
families.overviewSummary: It is NP-hard to color a three-colorable graph using any fixed number $c\ge3$ of colors. More strongly, for every fixed $0<\delta<1/3$, a deterministic polynomial-time reduction from $3$SAT produces simple unweighted graphs that are three-colorable in the satisfiable case and have no independent set of size $\delta n$ otherwise, where $n$ is the number of vertices.

families.title: Matrix multiplication with exponent at most 9/4
families.summary: Proves $\omega\le9/4$ over ℂ, giving $O_\varepsilon(n^{9/4+\varepsilon})$ arithmetic operations for square matrix multiplication. In characteristic zero, some inner dimension na with a > 0.465 permits $n^{2+o(1)}$ rectangular multiplication. Further square bounds give ω < 2.258 outside finitely many positive characteristics and ω < 2.371054886006746 over every fixed field.
families.subject: Theoretical computer science
families.overviewTitle: Matrix multiplication with exponent at most $9/4$
families.overviewSummary: Proves $\omega\le9/4$ over $\mathbb C$, giving $O_\varepsilon(n^{9/4+\varepsilon})$ arithmetic operations for square matrix multiplication. In characteristic zero, some inner dimension $n^a$ with $a>0.465$ permits $n^{2+o(1)}$ rectangular multiplication. Further square bounds give $\omega<2.258$ outside finitely many positive characteristics and $\omega<2.371054886006746$ over every fixed field.

families.title: A cubic permanent–determinant lower bound
families.summary: Proves an $\Omega(n^3)$ lower bound for the border determinantal complexity of the $n\times n$ permanent over ℂ. Even coefficientwise limits of determinants of affine-linear matrices require matrix size at least $cn^3$, for an absolute c > 0 and all sufficiently large n; the same bound therefore holds for exact representations.
families.subject: Theoretical computer science
families.overviewTitle: A cubic permanent--determinant lower bound
families.overviewSummary: Proves an $\Omega(n^3)$ lower bound for the border determinantal complexity of the $n\times n$ permanent over $\mathbb C$. Even coefficientwise limits of determinants of affine-linear matrices require matrix size at least $cn^3$, for an absolute $c>0$ and all sufficiently large $n$; the same bound therefore holds for exact representations.

families.title: Integer multiplication below $n\log n$
families.summary: Multiplies two n-bit integers exactly at every input length in deterministic worst-case time $O(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa})$, with $\kappa=2^{-182}$, on one fixed finite-alphabet Turing machine with finitely many one-dimensional tapes. This disproves the Schönhage–Strassen $n\log n$ optimality conjecture in the ordinary multitape bit model.
families.subject: Theoretical computer science
families.overviewTitle: Integer multiplication below $n\log n$
families.overviewSummary: Multiplies two $n$-bit integers exactly at every input length in deterministic worst-case time $O(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa})$, with $\kappa=2^{-182}$, on one fixed finite-alphabet Turing machine with finitely many one-dimensional tapes. This disproves the Sch\"onhage--Strassen $n\log n$ optimality conjecture in the ordinary multitape bit model.

families.title: Optimal-order randomized k-server on arbitrary metrics
families.summary: Establishes a randomized competitive ratio $O(\log^2(k+1))$ for k-server on every metric space, matching the worst-case lower-bound order. One policy serves every finite oblivious request sequence, including on infinite unbounded metrics. On finite rational metrics, a uniform implementation has polynomial preprocessing and per-request bit cost in the input length and $\log(t+1)$ at request t, with a finite instance-dependent additive movement constant.
families.subject: Theoretical computer science
families.overviewTitle: Optimal-order randomized $k$-server on arbitrary metrics
families.overviewSummary: Establishes a randomized competitive ratio $O(\log^2(k+1))$ for $k$-server on every metric space, matching the worst-case lower-bound order. One policy serves every finite oblivious request sequence, including on infinite unbounded metrics. On finite rational metrics, a uniform implementation has polynomial preprocessing and per-request bit cost in the input length and $\log(t+1)$ at request $t$, with a finite instance-dependent additive movement constant.

families.title: One-sample matroid prophet inequalities against an almighty adversary
families.summary: For every finite matroid known in advance, gives a distribution-independent online rule using one independent sample per element and earning a universal constant fraction of the expected offline optimum. Values are independent and nonnegative, with finite expected optimum. The guarantee holds even when the arrival-order adversary sees all samples, values, and the rule's entire random seed; no polynomial-time implementation is asserted.

families.title: Beyond the square-root exponent for depth-three circuits
families.summary: Constructs a single language in deterministic polynomial time whose n-bit membership function requires $2^{\omega(\sqrt n)}$ total gates in unbounded-fan-in OR–AND–OR circuits, at every sufficiently large input length. This crosses the square-root-exponent threshold for explicit depth-three Boolean circuit lower bounds.
families.subject: Theoretical computer science
families.overviewTitle: Beyond the square-root exponent for depth-three circuits

families.title: Approximate counting and entropy of perfect matchings
families.summary: Gives a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for counting perfect matchings in arbitrary finite simple graphs, with exact detection of zero counts. Also proves the perfect-matching entropy conjecture of Anari, Oveis Gharan, and Vinzant, bounding the maximum entropy of a matching law at every feasible edge-marginal vector in a loopless labelled multigraph, including boundary points.

families.overviewTitle: Approximate counting and the perfect-matching entropy conjecture

families.title: Approximate counting of common integer polymatroid bases
families.summary: Gives a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for counting common integer bases of two integral polymatroids of equal total rank, supplied by exact rank-value oracles. Capacities are binary-encoded, each integer vector counts once, and oracle calls and bit operations outside the oracles are polynomial on every execution. For matroids presented by independence oracles, the results also cover common independent sets of prescribed, unrestricted, or maximum cardinality, even when the ranks differ.

families.title: Sampling and counting contingency tables with arbitrary margins
families.summary: For nonnegative integer matrices with prescribed row and column sums, gives exact uniform sampling in expected polynomial bit time and almost-uniform sampling in worst-case polynomial bit time. The dimensions and binary-encoded margins are unrestricted. Also gives a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for counting such tables with arbitrary individual cell bounds, including structural zeros, with polynomial cost on every execution.

families.overviewSummary: For nonnegative integer matrices with prescribed row and column sums, gives exact uniform sampling in expected polynomial bit time and almost-uniform sampling in worst-case polynomial bit time. The dimensions and binary-encoded margins are unrestricted. Also gives a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for counting such tables with arbitrary individual cell bounds, including structural zeros, with polynomial cost on every execution.

families.title: Uniform black-box noncommutative identity testing across characteristics
families.summary: For each characteristic, constructs in deterministic polynomial bit time a polynomial-dimensional matrix tuple detecting every nonzero division-free noncommutative formula of bounded size over any field of that characteristic. Rational formulas over ℚ also admit polynomial-size hitting lists whenever they have a defined rational-matrix evaluation.
families.subject: Theoretical computer science
families.overviewTitle: Uniform identity testing for noncommutative formulas
families.overviewSummary: For each characteristic, constructs in deterministic polynomial bit time a polynomial-dimensional matrix tuple detecting every nonzero division-free noncommutative formula of bounded size over any field of that characteristic. Rational formulas over $\mathbb Q$ also admit polynomial-size hitting lists whenever they have a defined rational-matrix evaluation.

families.title: Uniform sparsest cut: hardness and semidefinite gaps
families.summary: Proves that approximating Uniform Sparsest Cut within any fixed constant factor is NP-hard, even with nonnegative rational capacities and unit demands. The Goemans–Linial semidefinite relaxation also has integrality gaps of order at least $\sqrt{\log n}/(\log\log n)^3$, approaching the square-root-logarithmic upper bound.
families.subject: Theoretical computer science
families.overviewTitle: Uniform sparsest cut: hardness and semidefinite gaps
families.overviewSummary: Proves that approximating Uniform Sparsest Cut within any fixed constant factor is NP-hard, even with nonnegative rational capacities and unit demands. The Goemans--Linial semidefinite relaxation also has integrality gaps of order at least $\sqrt{\log n}/(\log\log n)^3$, approaching the square-root-logarithmic upper bound.

families.title: Bin packing and unbounded configuration-LP gaps
families.summary: Disproves the modified integer round-up conjecture of Scheithauer and Terno: the integral bin-packing optimum can exceed its configuration linear-programming value by an arbitrarily large additive constant. Approximating the optimum within any fixed additive constant is also NP-hard, even when every item exceeds 1/6 and each bin holds at most five items.
families.subject: Theoretical computer science
families.overviewTitle: Unbounded bin-packing gaps and the modified integer round-up conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Disproves the modified integer round-up conjecture of Scheithauer and Terno: the integral bin-packing optimum can exceed its configuration linear-programming value by an arbitrarily large additive constant. Approximating the optimum within any fixed additive constant is also NP-hard, even when every item exceeds $1/6$ and each bin holds at most five items.

families.title: The Courtade–Kumar and Hellinger conjectures
families.summary: Proves the Courtade–Kumar conjecture: among Boolean functions of independent uniform bits, a single coordinate retains the most mutual information after independent bit-flip noise. A stronger theorem treats randomized binary summaries at fixed initial information. The Hellinger conjecture is also proved for every Boolean output bias and noise correlation.
families.subject: Theoretical computer science
families.overviewTitle: The Courtade--Kumar and Hellinger conjectures

A stronger theorem treats randomized binary summaries at fixed initial information. The Hellinger conjecture is also proved for every Boolean output bias and noise correlation.

families.title: Almost-linear-time exact matching and prescribed-degree factors in general graphs
families.summary: Gives a randomized algorithm finding an exact maximum-cardinality matching in any simple undirected graph in $(n+m)^{1+o(1)}$ word time, with success probability at least 2/3. The time bound holds on every computation path. The same guarantees apply to finding a spanning subgraph with prescribed admissible vertex degrees, or deciding that none exists.
families.subject: Theoretical computer science

The time bound holds on every computation path. The same guarantees apply to finding a spanning subgraph with prescribed admissible vertex degrees, or deciding that none exists.

families.title: Almost-linear approximation of edit distance
families.summary: For every fixed rational $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, gives a randomized $(1+\varepsilon)$ approximation to unit-cost edit distance in worst-case expected time $N^{1+o(1)}$, with success probability at least 2/3. The strings have total length N and polynomially bounded integer symbols. This is an asymptotic guarantee at fixed accuracy.
families.subject: Theoretical computer science
families.overviewTitle: Almost-linear expected-time approximation of edit distance
families.overviewSummary: For every fixed rational $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, gives a randomized $(1+\varepsilon)$ approximation to unit-cost edit distance in worst-case expected time $N^{1+o(1)}$, with success probability at least $2/3$. The strings have total length $N$ and polynomially bounded integer symbols. This is an asymptotic guarantee at fixed accuracy.

families.title: Quantitative trace-reconstruction bounds with a uniform decoder
families.summary: At every fixed deletion probability in $(0,1)$, reconstructing an arbitrary length-n binary string requires $n^{\Omega(\log\log n)}$ independent traces, ruling out polynomial-sample reconstruction. A uniform decoder achieves quasipolynomial sample and running-time bounds for known fixed rational retention probabilities. When the deletion probability is at most $n^{-\varepsilon}$ for fixed ε > 0, both bounds become polynomial in the input and parameter encoding.
families.subject: Theoretical computer science
families.overviewTitle: Superpolynomial lower bounds and quasipolynomial reconstruction from deletion traces
families.overviewSummary: At every fixed deletion probability in $(0,1)$, reconstructing an arbitrary length-$n$ binary string requires $n^{\Omega(\log\log n)}$ independent traces, ruling out polynomial-sample reconstruction. A uniform decoder achieves quasipolynomial sample and running-time bounds for known fixed rational retention probabilities. When the deletion probability is at most $n^{-\varepsilon}$ for fixed $\varepsilon>0$, both bounds become polynomial in the input and parameter encoding.

families.title: Polynomial-time scheduling on three identical machines
families.summary: Resolves the three-processor unit-job scheduling problem of Garey and Johnson: a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm minimizes makespan for nonpreemptive unit-length jobs with arbitrary precedence constraints on three identical parallel machines. For an explicitly given precedence graph, it decides deadline feasibility exactly and constructs a feasible schedule.

families.title: The metric k-median approximation threshold and recovery
families.summary: Gives a deterministic polynomial-time $(1+2/e+\varepsilon)$-approximation for finite rational metric k-median with specified candidate facilities, for every fixed ε > 0. Assuming $P\ne NP$, the optimal infimum approximation factor is $1+2/e$.
families.subject: Theoretical computer science
families.overviewTitle: The approximation threshold for metric $k$-median
families.overviewSummary: Gives a deterministic polynomial-time $(1+2/e+\varepsilon)$-approximation for finite rational metric $k$-median with specified candidate facilities, for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$. Assuming $P\ne NP$, the optimal infimum approximation factor is $1+2/e$.

families.title: Exponential semidefinite complexity of perfect matching
families.summary: Proves that every exact semidefinite lift of the perfect matching polytope has exponential size, answering Rothvoss's polynomial-size lift question negatively. The bound holds even for the positive semidefinite rank of its odd-cut slack matrix after any fixed shift $0\lt \rho\lt 1$, allowing arbitrary real positive semidefinite factors.
families.subject: Theoretical computer science
families.overviewTitle: Exponential semidefinite complexity of perfect matching

families.title: Average sensitivity of polynomial threshold functions
families.summary: Proves that a degree-at-most-d polynomial threshold function on the uniform n-dimensional Boolean cube has average sensitivity at most $8d\sqrt n$, uniformly for $1\le d\le n$. Average sensitivity counts expected output changes under single-bit flips. This establishes the asymptotic Gotsman–Linial conjecture, allowing polynomial zeros with $\mathop{\mathrm{sign}}\nolimits (0)=1$.
families.subject: Theoretical computer science
families.overviewTitle: The asymptotic Gotsman--Linial conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Proves that a degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial threshold function on the uniform $n$-dimensional Boolean cube has average sensitivity at most $8d\sqrt n$, uniformly for $1\le d\le n$. Average sensitivity counts expected output changes under single-bit flips. This establishes the asymptotic Gotsman--Linial conjecture, allowing polynomial zeros with $\operatorname{sign}(0)=1$.

families.title: A factor-two approximation for shortest common superstring
families.summary: Gives a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm constructing a common superstring of length at most twice the optimum for every finite family of explicitly represented strings. The running time is polynomial in the full encoded input length, including symbol labels.
families.subject: Theoretical computer science
families.overviewTitle: A factor-two approximation for shortest common superstring

families.title: Exponential state costs for two-way automata
families.summary: Proves exponential lower bounds both for complementing two-way nondeterministic finite automata and for simulating one-way nondeterministic automata by two-way deterministic ones. The latter resolves the Sakoda–Sipser state-succinctness conjecture over growing finite alphabets; both results rule out polynomial state bounds independent of alphabet size.
families.subject: Theoretical computer science
families.overviewTitle: Exponential state costs for two-way automata

families.title: Exact Fourier transforms below $n\log n$
families.summary: Gives a deterministic length-n discrete Fourier transform algorithm using $O(n(\log n)^{1-\delta})$ operations for every n, with explicit $\delta=10^{-13}$. The model uses exact complex arithmetic, unrestricted coefficients and a supplied root of unity, and counts scalar preparation and logarithmic-word indexing.
families.subject: Theoretical computer science
families.overviewTitle: Fourier transforms below $n\log n$

families.title: Rapid mixing of graph switches for every degree sequence
families.summary: Resolves the simple-undirected Kannan–Tetali–Vempala conjecture: the lazy edge-switch chain mixes in $O(n^8)$ time for every graphical labeled degree sequence. The same degree-constrained graphs can also be sampled exactly uniformly by an almost-surely terminating algorithm with expected polynomial bit running time.

families.overviewTitle: Polynomial mixing of graph switches with prescribed degrees

families.title: A superquadratic separation of sensitivity and block sensitivity
families.summary: Constructs total Boolean functions with block sensitivity $\mathop{\mathrm{bs}}\nolimits (f)\ge s(f)^\alpha$ for a fixed α > 2, disproving the quadratic strengthening of the Sensitivity Conjecture. Here $s(f)$ counts influential individual-bit flips, while block sensitivity allows disjoint groups of bits to change together.
families.subject: Theoretical computer science
families.overviewTitle: A counterexample to the quadratic sensitivity conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Constructs total Boolean functions with block sensitivity $\operatorname{bs}(f)\ge s(f)^\alpha$ for a fixed $\alpha>2$, disproving the quadratic strengthening of the Sensitivity Conjecture. families.title: The computational complexity of Weisfeiler–Leman refinement
families.summary: Proves unconditional $n^{\Omega(k)}$ deterministic time lower bounds for joint and separate k-dimensional Weisfeiler–Leman equivalence, for sufficiently large fixed k in the specified sequential adjacency-matrix models. With dimension as input, joint equivalence is EXPTIME-complete even on subcubic graphs; deciding whether refinement identifies a graph is also EXPTIME-complete.
families.subject: Theoretical computer science
families.overviewTitle: The complexity of Weisfeiler--Leman refinement

families.title: Generalized star height at most three
families.summary: Every regular language over a finite alphabet has a generalized regular expression with at most three nested Kleene stars, allowing union, concatenation and complement over the same alphabet. This establishes an absolute bound independent of automaton size, resolving the uniform-boundedness version of the generalized star-height problem.

families.title: Homogeneous depth-five lower bounds for iterated matrix multiplication
families.summary: Over every characteristic-zero field, the $(1,1)$ entry of a product of n independent $n\times n$ variable matrices requires $n^{\Theta(\sqrt n)}$ gates in homogeneous depth-five sum–product circuits. This sharp bound allows shared gates and bottom linear forms involving all variables.
families.subject: Theoretical computer science
families.overviewTitle: Sharp homogeneous depth-five complexity of matrix products
families.overviewSummary: Over every characteristic-zero field, the $(1,1)$ entry of a product of $n$ independent $n\times n$ variable matrices requires $n^{\Theta(\sqrt n)}$ gates in homogeneous depth-five sum--product circuits. families.title: A quasilinear PCP theorem for PPAD
families.summary: Resolves the quasilinear PCP-for-PPAD conjecture. An End-of-Line instance of length N reduces to numerical circuit constraints of total length $N(\log N)^{O(1)}$ such that any polynomially encoded rational assignment satisfying all but a fixed fraction to fixed accuracy yields an endpoint solution. Such assignments always exist, giving robust local verification with only quasilinear size overhead.
families.subject: Theoretical computer science

families.title: One-tape time simulation in two-fifths-power space
families.summary: Determines the halting and finite-control outcome of a fixed deterministic one-writable-tape machine up to time T using $O(T^{2/5}\log^C(T+2))$ space, improving the square-root exponent. Heads move at most one cell per step; finitely many read-only input heads are allowed. Initial contents are independent of T, and contents and input symbols have polylogarithmic-space access. Simulation time is unrestricted.

families.title: Subset Sum in $O(2^{0.49n})$ time
families.summary: Gives a uniform randomized classical algorithm for worst-case Subset Sum in ordinary $O(2^{0.49n})$ word-RAM time on polynomial-bit inputs, where n counts the integers. The time bound holds on every execution and success probability is at least 2/3 on every input. Inputs may repeat positive integers; words have $O(n+b)$ bits for maximum input bit length b.

families.title: Subpolynomial query complexity for log-concave sampling
families.summary: For C2 potentials with a supplied minimizer and $I\preceq\nabla^2V\preceq2I$, proves that sampling within total variation 1/10 requires only $C_\varepsilon d^\varepsilon$ exact value-and-gradient queries for every fixed ε > 0. The bound holds on every run, with unrestricted computation between queries. A logarithmic lower bound also holds, so the optimal power-law exponent in this oracle model is zero.

families.overviewTitle: Subpolynomial queries for log-concave sampling
families.overviewSummary: For $C^2$ potentials with a supplied minimizer and $I\preceq\nabla^2V\preceq2I$, proves that sampling within total variation $1/10$ requires only $C_\varepsilon d^\varepsilon$ exact value-and-gradient queries for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$. families.title: Memory–sample lower bounds for noiseless Gaussian regression
families.summary: For fixed A > 0, a one-pass learner with $Ad^2$ persistent bits needs $\Omega_A(d\log(1/\epsilon))$ noiseless Gaussian samples to recover a unit vector to angular error $0\lt \epsilon\le1/10$ with probability 2/3, uniformly in accuracy for large d. Computation and randomized updates are unrestricted, but output uses only the terminal state, stopping index and fresh randomness.

families.title: Existential–universal real sentences in the counting hierarchy
families.summary: Proves that the existential theory of the reals lies in the counting hierarchy. More generally, truth of existential–universal real sentences can be decided at one fixed level of that hierarchy, even when their integer polynomials are specified by arithmetic circuits.

families.title: Deterministic polynomial factorization over prime fields
families.summary: Gives a uniform deterministic algorithm that completely factors every nonzero dense degree-n polynomial over a prime field 𝔽p, including multiplicities, in bit complexity polynomial in $(n+1)\log p$. The prime is supplied in binary. No randomness, integer-factorization or primitive-root oracle, or GRH assumption is required.

families.title: Hilbert's sixteenth problem: uniform bounds for limit cycles
families.summary: Resolves the uniform boundedness assertion in Hilbert's sixteenth problem: the number of isolated periodic orbits of a real planar polynomial vector field is bounded by a finite constant depending only on its degree. For classical quintic Liénard systems, the exact maximum is two limit cycles.

families.title: Banach’s simple Lebesgue-spectrum problem
families.summary: Resolves the probability-preserving form of Banach's simple Lebesgue-spectrum problem within smooth dynamics. A smooth volume-preserving diffeomorphism of the standard-volume three-torus has simple Lebesgue spectrum on its entire complex mean-zero L2 space: the bilateral iterates of one real observable form an orthonormal basis of that space.

families.title: Rokhlin’s multiple-mixing problem
families.summary: Proves that every invertible mixing probability-preserving transformation is mixing of all finite orders, resolving Rokhlin's multiple-mixing problem for a single transformation. Correlations among any finite collection of measurable sets converge to the product of their measures whenever all pairwise time separations diverge.

families.title: Positive metric entropy for the standard map
families.summary: Proves that the standard sine map on the two-dimensional torus has positive metric entropy with respect to area for every sufficiently large positive parameter. This establishes Sinai's positive-parameter-measure conjecture for the original family, with the stronger conclusion of a full parameter tail.

families.title: The near-boundary Birkhoff conjecture
families.summary: Resolves the near-boundary Birkhoff conjecture for smooth strictly convex planar billiards of positive curvature. Such a billiard is an ellipse whenever a full grazing annulus is continuously foliated by individually invariant essential curves. A continuous physical collar of smooth closed convex caustics also suffices.

families.title: The entropy-rate dimension formula for self-similar measures
families.summary: For every self-similar measure on the line generated by finitely many contracting similarities, proves $\dim_{\mathrm H}\mu=\min\{1,h_{\mathrm{RW}}/\chi\}$, where $h_{\mathrm{RW}}$ is the entropy rate of random composed maps and χ the average logarithmic contraction. families.title: Classwise permanence for weakly reversible mass-action systems
families.summary: Proves the permanence conjecture for every finite weakly reversible mass-action system with fixed positive rate constants. Every positive stoichiometric compatibility class, even an unbounded one, has a common compact convex forward-invariant absorbing set. All positive trajectories in that class therefore eventually share positive lower and finite upper concentration bounds.

families.title: Weak mixing of triangular billiards with an irrational angle
families.summary: Proves that the billiard flow in every nondegenerate Euclidean triangle with at least one angle irrational relative to π is weakly mixing for normalized area times uniform direction. families.title: A C1 counterexample to the entropy conjecture
families.summary: Constructs a noninvertible C1 self-map of a compact smooth manifold with zero topological entropy but eigenvalue 2 on second homology. This disproves the homological entropy lower bound for general C1 self-maps: homological growth need not force positive orbit complexity.

families.title: Zero entropy does not guarantee a smooth positive-volume model
families.summary: Constructs a zero-entropy ergodic invertible transformation of a standard nonatomic probability space that is not measurably conjugate to any C∞ diffeomorphism preserving a strictly positive smooth probability density on a compact finite-dimensional manifold. families.summary: Proves almost-everywhere convergence of consecutive multiple ergodic averages of every finite length for invertible mixing probability-preserving transformations. The example consists of rank-one orthogonal projectors onto lines in $\mathbb R^4$, with the Frobenius metric.

families.title: Graph coloring, clique minors, and Colin de Verdière invariants
families.summary: Disproves Hadwiger's conjecture even for fractional coloring: arbitrarily large finite simple graphs with independence number at most two satisfy $\chi_f(G)\gt h(G)$, where $h(G)$ is the largest clique-minor order. Also disproves the fractional Colin de Verdière chromatic bound $\chi_f(G)\le\mu(G)+1$. In the positive direction, every finite nonempty graph satisfies $\chi_{\mathrm{list}}(G)\le C h(G)$ for a universal constant C.
families.subject: Combinatorics
families.overviewTitle: Counterexamples to the Hadwiger and Colin de Verdi\`ere conjectures
families.overviewSummary: Disproves Hadwiger's conjecture even for fractional coloring: arbitrarily large finite simple graphs with independence number at most two satisfy $\chi_f(G)>h(G)$, where $h(G)$ is the largest clique-minor order. Also disproves the fractional Colin de Verdi\`ere chromatic bound $\chi_f(G)\le\mu(G)+1$. In the positive direction, every finite nonempty graph satisfies $\chi_{\mathrm{list}}(G)\le C h(G)$ for a universal constant $C$.

families.title: The Euclidean plane cannot be colored with five colors
families.summary: Proves that every five-coloring of the Euclidean plane has a monochromatic pair at distance one, with no restriction on the color classes. This advances the Hadwiger–Nelson problem: together with the classical seven-coloring, only six and seven remain possible chromatic numbers of the plane.
families.subject: Combinatorics
families.overviewTitle: The Euclidean plane cannot be colored with five colors
families.overviewSummary: Proves that every five-coloring of the Euclidean plane has a monochromatic pair at distance one, with no restriction on the color classes. This advances the Hadwiger--Nelson problem: together with the classical seven-coloring, only six and seven remain possible chromatic numbers of the plane.

families.title: Erdős’s reciprocal-sum conjecture and quasipolynomial Szemerédi bounds
families.summary: Proves Erdős's conjecture that every set of positive integers with divergent reciprocal sum contains arithmetic progressions of every finite length. Quantitatively, for each fixed k ≥ 3, every subset of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with no nonconstant k-term progression has size at most $C_kN\exp[-c_k(\log N)^{\varepsilon_k}]$, with positive constants depending only on k.
families.subject: Combinatorics
families.overviewTitle: Erd\H{o}s's reciprocal-sum conjecture and quasipolynomial Szemer\'edi bounds
families.overviewSummary: Proves Erd\H{o}s's conjecture that every set of positive integers with divergent reciprocal sum contains arithmetic progressions of every finite length. Quantitatively, for each fixed $k\ge3$, every subset of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with no nonconstant $k$-term progression has size at most $C_kN\exp[-c_k(\log N)^{\varepsilon_k}]$, with positive constants depending only on $k$.

families.title: Superexponential van der Waerden numbers
families.summary: Resolves Erdős's superexponential-growth question for van der Waerden numbers. If $W_r(k)$ is the least interval length forcing a monochromatic k-term progression in every r-coloring, then $W_r(k)\gt k^{ck\lfloor\log_2 r\rfloor}$ for an absolute c > 0, all r ≥ 2 and sufficiently large k, uniformly in r. In particular, $W_r(k)^{1/k}\to\infty$ for each fixed r.
families.subject: Combinatorics
families.overviewTitle: Superexponential van der Waerden numbers
families.overviewSummary: Resolves Erd\H{o}s's superexponential-growth question for van der Waerden numbers. If $W_r(k)$ is the least interval length forcing a monochromatic $k$-term progression in every $r$-coloring, then $W_r(k)>k^{ck\lfloor\log_2 r\rfloor}$ for an absolute $c>0$, all $r\ge2$ and sufficiently large $k$, uniformly in $r$. In particular, $W_r(k)^{1/k}\to\infty$ for each fixed $r$.

families.title: Counterexamples to Sidorenko’s conjecture and the forcing conjecture
families.summary: Disproves Sidorenko's conjecture with a connected bipartite pattern on 35 vertices and 66 edges that occurs less frequently than in a random graph of the same edge density. The same pattern disproves the forcing conjecture of Skokan and Thoma: matching its density and the edge density of a constant graphon need not force quasirandomness.
families.subject: Combinatorics
families.overviewTitle: Counterexamples to Sidorenko's conjecture and the forcing conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Disproves Sidorenko's conjecture with a connected bipartite pattern on $35$ vertices and $66$ edges that occurs less frequently than in a random graph of the same edge density. The same pattern disproves the forcing conjecture of Skokan and Thoma: matching its density and the edge density of a constant graphon need not force quasirandomness.

families.title: Counterexamples to Ryser’s covering conjecture
families.summary: Disproves Ryser's covering conjecture by constructing intersecting $(q+1)$-partite, $(q+1)$-uniform hypergraphs with covering number $q+1$, rather than the predicted bound q, for every sufficiently large prime q. A separate construction over extension fields also disproves Gyárfás's monochromatic tree-cover conjecture.
families.subject: Combinatorics
families.overviewTitle: Counterexamples to Ryser's covering and Gy\'arf\'as's tree-cover conjectures
families.overviewSummary: Disproves Ryser's covering conjecture by constructing intersecting $(q+1)$-partite, $(q+1)$-uniform hypergraphs with covering number $q+1$, rather than the predicted bound $q$, for every sufficiently large prime $q$. A separate construction over extension fields also disproves Gy\'arf\'as's monochromatic tree-cover conjecture.

families.title: Hindman’s finite sums and products conjecture
families.summary: Proves Hindman's finite sums and products conjecture: every finite coloring of the positive integers contains sets of any prescribed finite size whose nonempty subset sums and nonempty subset products all have one common color.
families.subject: Combinatorics
families.overviewTitle: Hindman's finite sums and products conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Proves Hindman's finite sums and products conjecture: every finite coloring of the positive integers contains sets of any prescribed finite size whose nonempty subset sums and nonempty subset products all have one common color.

families.title: The Harary–Hill and Zarankiewicz crossing-number formulas
families.summary: Resolves the Harary–Hill conjecture and Turán's brickyard problem in the Zarankiewicz formulation, determining the crossing numbers of every complete and complete bipartite graph. The result proves the optimality of the classical drawings among all plane drawings with continuous edge arcs.
families.subject: Combinatorics
families.overviewTitle: Exact crossing numbers of complete and complete bipartite graphs
families.overviewSummary: Resolves the Harary--Hill conjecture and Tur\'an's brickyard problem in the Zarankiewicz formulation, determining the crossing numbers of every complete and complete bipartite graph. The result proves the optimality of the classical drawings among all plane drawings with continuous edge arcs.

families.title: The higher-dimensional Erdős distinct-distances conjecture
families.summary: For every fixed d ≥ 3, any n ≥ 2 distinct points in ℝd determine at least $c_dn^{2/d}$ distinct distances, with $c_d\gt 0$ depending only on dimension. This matches the integer-grid order and resolves the higher-dimensional Erdős distinct-distances conjecture with a constant-factor bound.
families.subject: Combinatorics
families.overviewTitle: The higher-dimensional Erd\H{o}s distinct-distances conjecture
families.overviewSummary: For every fixed $d\ge3$, any $n\ge2$ distinct points in $\mathbb R^d$ determine at least $c_dn^{2/d}$ distinct distances, with $c_d>0$ depending only on dimension. This matches the integer-grid order and resolves the higher-dimensional Erd\H{o}s distinct-distances conjecture with a constant-factor bound.

families.title: Planar distinct distances and unit-distance bounds
families.summary: Proves the weak pinned Erdős distance conjecture: for every fixed ε > 0, all but $o(n)$ points of any n-point planar set determine at least $n^{1-\varepsilon}$ distinct nonzero distances. A complementary theorem bounds the number of unit-distance pairs by $O(n^{4/3-\delta})$ for an absolute δ > 0.
families.subject: Combinatorics
families.overviewTitle: Pinned distances and a power saving for planar unit distances
families.overviewSummary: Proves the weak pinned Erd\H{o}s distance conjecture: for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$, all but $o(n)$ points of any $n$-point planar set determine at least $n^{1-\varepsilon}$ distinct nonzero distances. A complementary theorem bounds the number of unit-distance pairs by $O(n^{4/3-\delta})$ for an absolute $\delta>0$.

families.title: Combinatorial invariance of Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials
families.summary: Resolves the full combinatorial invariance conjecture: isomorphic Bruhat intervals in arbitrary Coxeter systems have identical equal-parameter Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials. Thus the abstract order of the interval determines the polynomial, even across different Coxeter systems.
families.subject: Combinatorics
families.overviewTitle: Combinatorial invariance of Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials
families.overviewSummary: Resolves the full combinatorial invariance conjecture: isomorphic Bruhat intervals in arbitrary Coxeter systems have identical equal-parameter Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials. Thus the abstract order of the interval determines the polynomial, even across different Coxeter systems.

families.title: Shareshian–Wachs elementary positivity
families.summary: Resolves the elementary-positivity part of the Shareshian–Wachs conjecture: the chromatic quasisymmetric function of every natural unit interval graph has elementary-basis coefficients in $\mathbb N[q]$. The coefficients count explicitly described permutations, giving a combinatorial explanation of positivity.
families.subject: Combinatorics
families.overviewTitle: The Shareshian--Wachs $e$-positivity conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Resolves the elementary-positivity part of the Shareshian--Wachs conjecture: the chromatic quasisymmetric function of every natural unit interval graph has elementary-basis coefficients in $\mathbb N[q]$. The coefficients count explicitly described permutations, giving a combinatorial explanation of positivity.

families.title: Sharp logarithmic exponents for off-diagonal Ramsey numbers
families.summary: For every fixed integer s ≥ 5, proves $r(s,t)=t^{s-1}/(\log t)^{s-2+o(1)}$ as $t\to\infty$, determining the logarithmic exponent and matching the classical upper bound at that scale. Here $r(s,t)$ is the least number of vertices forcing an s-clique or a t-vertex independent set.
families.subject: Combinatorics
families.overviewTitle: Sharp logarithmic exponents for off-diagonal Ramsey numbers
families.overviewSummary: For every fixed integer $s\ge5$, proves $r(s,t)=t^{s-1}/(\log t)^{s-2+o(1)}$ as $t\to\infty$, determining the logarithmic exponent and matching the classical upper bound at that scale. Here $r(s,t)$ is the least number of vertices forcing an $s$-clique or a $t$-vertex independent set.

families.title: The hypercube Ramsey conjecture
families.summary: Resolves the Burr–Erdős hypercube Ramsey conjecture: the two-color Ramsey number of the n-dimensional cube is $\Theta(2^n)$. Thus every red-blue coloring of a complete graph on a universal constant times the cube's number of vertices contains a monochromatic copy of the cube.
families.subject: Combinatorics
families.overviewTitle: The hypercube Ramsey conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Resolves the Burr--Erd\H{o}s hypercube Ramsey conjecture: the two-color Ramsey number of the $n$-dimensional cube is $\Theta(2^n)$. Thus every red-blue coloring of a complete graph on a universal constant times the cube's number of vertices contains a monochromatic copy of the cube.

families.title: Classification of finite Euclidean Ramsey configurations
families.summary: Classifies finite point configurations that occur monochromatically, at their original scale, in every finite coloring of sufficiently high-dimensional Euclidean space. The characterization is an algebraic condition over the coordinate field. It also disproves the Leader–Russell–Walters conjecture that every such configuration is a subset of a finite transitive set.
families.subject: Combinatorics
families.overviewTitle: Classification of finite Euclidean Ramsey configurations
families.overviewSummary: Classifies finite point configurations that occur monochromatically, at their original scale, in every finite coloring of sufficiently high-dimensional Euclidean space. The characterization is an algebraic condition over the coordinate field. It also disproves the Leader--Russell--Walters conjecture that every such configuration is a subset of a finite transitive set.

families.title: Seymour’s second-neighborhood conjecture
families.summary: Proves Seymour's second-neighborhood conjecture: every nonempty finite oriented graph has a vertex with at least as many vertices at directed distance exactly two as at directed distance one. Oriented graphs may be arbitrary apart from the exclusion of loops and oppositely directed edge pairs.
families.subject: Combinatorics
families.overviewTitle: Seymour's second-neighborhood conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Proves Seymour's second-neighborhood conjecture: every nonempty finite oriented graph has a vertex with at least as many vertices at directed distance exactly two as at directed distance one. Oriented graphs may be arbitrary apart from the exclusion of loops and oppositely directed edge pairs.

families.title: Deterministic construction of strong thin spanning trees
families.summary: Resolves the strong thin-tree conjecture constructively. Every finite loopless k-edge-connected multigraph on at least two vertices has a spanning tree containing at most a universal $C/k$ fraction of the edges of every cut. Such a tree can be found deterministically in polynomial time, even with binary-encoded parallel-edge multiplicities.
families.subject: Combinatorics
families.overviewTitle: Deterministic construction of strong thin spanning trees
families.overviewSummary: Resolves the strong thin-tree conjecture constructively. Every finite loopless $k$-edge-connected multigraph on at least two vertices has a spanning tree containing at most a universal $C/k$ fraction of the edges of every cut. Such a tree can be found deterministically in polynomial time, even with binary-encoded parallel-edge multiplicities.

families.title: Talagrand’s expectation thresholds, discrete convexity, and graph decompositions
families.summary: Proves that integral and fractional expectation thresholds differ by at most a universal factor, and resolves Talagrand's discrete-convexity conjecture. An application proves the Ascoli–He–Park–Talagrand graph-decomposition conjecture: every graph's edges split into a universally bounded number of fixed pieces, each with containment threshold at most a universal constant times the original graph's integral expectation threshold. The pieces' embeddings need not agree on shared vertices.
families.subject: Combinatorics
families.overviewTitle: Talagrand's conjectures and graph decompositions at expectation thresholds
families.overviewSummary: Proves that integral and fractional expectation thresholds differ by at most a universal factor, and resolves Talagrand's discrete-convexity conjecture. An application proves the Ascoli--He--Park--Talagrand graph-decomposition conjecture: every graph's edges split into a universally bounded number of fixed pieces, each with containment threshold at most a universal constant times the original graph's integral expectation threshold. The pieces' embeddings need not agree on shared vertices.

families.title: The second Kahn–Kalai conjecture with an edge-count bound
families.summary: Proves the second Kahn–Kalai conjecture: for every finite simple graph H with h ≥ 1 edges and at most n vertices, its appearance threshold in $G(n,p)$ is at most $C p_{\mathrm E}(n,H)(1+\log_2 h)$, with universal C. Here $p_{\mathrm E}$ is the least density at which every subgraph of H has expected copy count at least 1/2.
families.subject: Combinatorics
families.overviewTitle: The second Kahn--Kalai conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Proves the second Kahn--Kalai conjecture: for every finite simple graph $H$ with $h\ge1$ edges and at most $n$ vertices, its appearance threshold in $G(n,p)$ is at most $C p_{\mathrm E}(n,H)(1+\log_2 h)$, with universal $C$. Here $p_{\mathrm E}$ is the least density at which every subgraph of $H$ has expected copy count at least $1/2$.

families.title: Bounded-degree coboundary expanders
families.summary: Constructs arbitrarily large finite d-dimensional simplicial complexes, for every d ≥ 3, with uniformly bounded vertex degrees and uniform 𝔽2 coboundary expansion in every degree below d. Together with the known graph and two-dimensional cases, this establishes the existence of such expanders in every positive dimension.
families.subject: Combinatorics
families.overviewTitle: Bounded-degree coboundary expanders in every dimension
families.overviewSummary: Constructs arbitrarily large finite $d$-dimensional simplicial complexes, for every $d\ge3$, with uniformly bounded vertex degrees and uniform $\mathbb F_2$ coboundary expansion in every degree below $d$. Together with the known graph and two-dimensional cases, this establishes the existence of such expanders in every positive dimension.

families.title: Deterministic nonbipartite Ramanujan graphs in every fixed degree
families.summary: For every fixed d ≥ 3, constructs a simple d-regular nonbipartite Ramanujan graph on every sufficiently large even number n of vertices, with every nonconstant adjacency eigenvalue strictly between $-2\sqrt{d-1}$ and $2\sqrt{d-1}$. A deterministic algorithm outputs the full adjacency list in polynomial bit time, with exponent depending on d.
families.subject: Combinatorics
families.overviewTitle: Deterministic nonbipartite Ramanujan graphs in every fixed degree
families.overviewSummary: For every fixed $d\ge3$, constructs a simple $d$-regular nonbipartite Ramanujan graph on every sufficiently large even number $n$ of vertices, with every nonconstant adjacency eigenvalue strictly between $-2\sqrt{d-1}$ and $2\sqrt{d-1}$. A deterministic algorithm outputs the full adjacency list in polynomial bit time, with exponent depending on $d$.

families.title: The circulant Hadamard and Barker-sequence conjectures
families.summary: Proves that real circulant Hadamard matrices exist exactly in orders 1 and 4, resolving the circulant Hadamard conjecture. Together with classical Barker-sequence results, this shows that binary sequences whose nontrivial aperiodic autocorrelations have magnitude at most 1 exist at lengths n > 1 exactly when $n\in\{2,3,4,5,7,11,13\}$.
families.subject: Combinatorics
families.overviewTitle: The circulant Hadamard conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Proves that real circulant Hadamard matrices exist exactly in orders $1$ and $4$, resolving the circulant Hadamard conjecture. Together with classical Barker-sequence results, this shows that binary sequences whose nontrivial aperiodic autocorrelations have magnitude at most $1$ exist at lengths $n>1$ exactly when $n\in\{2,3,4,5,7,11,13\}$.

families.title: Barnette’s Hamiltonian-cycle conjecture
families.summary: Proves that every finite simple cubic bipartite planar 3-vertex-connected graph has a Hamiltonian cycle, resolving Barnette's conjecture. Equivalently, every three-edge path in a finite simple cubic 3-vertex-connected bipartite Pfaffian graph lies in a Hamiltonian cycle.
families.subject: Combinatorics
families.overviewTitle: Barnette's Hamiltonian-cycle conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Proves that every finite simple cubic bipartite planar $3$-vertex-connected graph has a Hamiltonian cycle, resolving Barnette's conjecture. Equivalently, every three-edge path in a finite simple cubic $3$-vertex-connected bipartite Pfaffian graph lies in a Hamiltonian cycle.

families.title: The Erdős–Gallai cycle-decomposition conjecture
families.summary: Proves that the edges of every finite simple undirected graph on n vertices can be partitioned into at most $Cn$ simple cycles and single edges, for an absolute constant C. This resolves the Erdős–Gallai cycle-decomposition conjecture, bounding the number of pieces linearly even for dense graphs.
families.subject: Combinatorics
families.overviewTitle: The Erd\H{o}s--Gallai cycle-decomposition conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Proves that the edges of every finite simple undirected graph on $n$ vertices can be partitioned into at most $Cn$ simple cycles and single edges, for an absolute constant $C$. This resolves the Erd\H{o}s--Gallai cycle-decomposition conjecture, bounding the number of pieces linearly even for dense graphs.

families.title: Power savings for intersective polynomial differences and prime arguments
families.summary: For every fixed intersective integer polynomial h of degree k ≥ 2 with positive leading coefficient, proves that a subset of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ avoiding nonzero values $h(1),h(2),\ldots$ as differences has size $O_h(N^{1-c_k})$, with $c_k\gt 0$ depending only on degree. Here intersective means having a root modulo every modulus. For prime arguments, a power saving also holds when h has a unit root modulo every modulus, with exponent allowed to depend on h.
families.subject: Combinatorics
families.overviewTitle: Power savings for polynomial-difference-free sets
families.overviewSummary: For every fixed intersective integer polynomial $h$ of degree $k\ge2$ with positive leading coefficient, proves that a subset of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ avoiding nonzero values $h(1),h(2),\ldots$ as differences has size $O_h(N^{1-c_k})$, with $c_k>0$ depending only on degree. Here intersective means having a root modulo every modulus. For prime arguments, a power saving also holds when $h$ has a unit root modulo every modulus, with exponent allowed to depend on $h$.

families.title: Power savings for planar halving lines and k-sets
families.summary: Improves the planar halving-line bound to $O(n^{4/3-\varepsilon})$ for sets with no three collinear and an absolute ε > 0. More generally, an n-point set with no three collinear has $O(n(k+1)^{1/3-\varepsilon_0})$ strictly separable k-subsets for $1\le k\le n/2$, with an absolute $\varepsilon_0\gt 0$. The constants and positive exponents are nonquantitative.
families.subject: Combinatorics
families.overviewTitle: Power savings for planar halving lines and $k$-sets
families.overviewSummary: Improves the planar halving-line bound to $O(n^{4/3-\varepsilon})$ for sets with no three collinear and an absolute $\varepsilon>0$. More generally, an $n$-point set with no three collinear has $O(n(k+1)^{1/3-\varepsilon_0})$ strictly separable $k$-subsets for $1\le k\le n/2$, with an absolute $\varepsilon_0>0$. The constants and positive exponents are nonquantitative.

families.title: Correspondence coloring with a fixed forbidden subgraph
families.summary: Proves the Alon–Krivelevich–Sudakov coloring conjecture in correspondence-coloring form: graphs avoiding any fixed subgraph F need $O_F(\Delta/\log\Delta)$ colors when their maximum degree Δ is sufficiently large. Also proves the Ajtai–Erdős–Komlós–Szemerédi independence conjecture: for fixed r ≥ 4, every n-vertex Kr-free graph of average degree d ≥ 2 has an independent set of size $\Omega_r(n\log d/d)$.
families.subject: Combinatorics
families.overviewTitle: Coloring and independence in graphs with forbidden subgraphs
families.overviewSummary: Proves the Alon--Krivelevich--Sudakov coloring conjecture in correspondence-coloring form: graphs avoiding any fixed subgraph $F$ need $O_F(\Delta/\log\Delta)$ colors when their maximum degree $\Delta$ is sufficiently large. Also proves the Ajtai--Erd\H{o}s--Koml\'os--Szemer\'edi independence conjecture: for fixed $r\ge4$, every $n$-vertex $K_r$-free graph of average degree $d\ge2$ has an independent set of size $\Omega_r(n\log d/d)$.

families.title: Counterexamples to infinite matroid intersection and packing/covering
families.summary: Disproves the unrestricted infinite matroid intersection and packing/covering conjectures in ZFC, using two self-dual partitional matroids on a countably infinite ground set. The same examples answer Joó’s partitional-matroid question negatively. They are neither finitary nor cofinitary, so Nash-Williams’ original finitary conjecture remains outside the result.
families.subject: Combinatorics
families.overviewTitle: Counterexamples to infinite matroid intersection and packing/covering

The same examples answer Jo\'o’s partitional-matroid question negatively. They are neither finitary nor cofinitary, so Nash-Williams’ original finitary conjecture remains outside the result.

families.title: Uniform influence and sharp thresholds for graph and hypergraph properties
families.summary: Proves the Friedgut–Kalai threshold-width conjectures for graphs and fixed-uniformity hypergraphs. For fixed $0\lt \varepsilon\lt 1/2$, every nontrivial increasing relabeling-invariant property crosses from probability ε to $1-\varepsilon$ within width $O((\log n)^{-2})$ for graphs and $O_r((\log n)^{-r/(r-1)})$ for r-uniform hypergraphs, r ≥ 3. The hypergraph influence bound also applies to nonmonotone properties.
families.subject: Combinatorics
families.overviewTitle: The Friedgut--Kalai graph and hypergraph threshold conjectures
families.overviewSummary: Proves the Friedgut--Kalai threshold-width conjectures for graphs and fixed-uniformity hypergraphs. For fixed $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, every nontrivial increasing relabeling-invariant property crosses from probability $\varepsilon$ to $1-\varepsilon$ within width $O((\log n)^{-2})$ for graphs and $O_r((\log n)^{-r/(r-1)})$ for $r$-uniform hypergraphs, $r\ge3$. The hypergraph influence bound also applies to nonmonotone properties.

families.title: Snaky in 21 Maker moves
families.summary: Settles the Snaky achievement problem: Maker can force the six-cell Snaky shape within 21 of its own moves on the initially empty infinite square board. Maker moves first, each player claims one free cell per turn, and translations, rotations and reflections count as wins.
families.subject: Combinatorics

families.title: The sharp terminal leave in random triangle removal
families.summary: Starting from the complete graph on n vertices, repeatedly delete a uniformly chosen remaining triangle. The terminal edge count is asymptotic to $n^{3/2}/(2\sqrt2)$, with mean-square convergence after normalization by n3/2. This proves the triangle case of the Joos–Kühn sharp-constant conjecture.
families.subject: Combinatorics
families.overviewTitle: The sharp constant in random triangle removal

The terminal edge count is asymptotic to $n^{3/2}/(2\sqrt2)$, with mean-square convergence after normalization by $n^{3/2}$. This proves the triangle case of the Joos--K\"uhn sharp-constant conjecture.

families.title: Cycle–clique Ramsey numbers
families.summary: Proves the Erdős–Faudree–Rousseau–Schelp conjecture: $R(C_m,K_n)=(m-1)(n-1)+1$ for every $m\ge n\ge3$, except $R(C_3,K_3)=6$. This is the exact threshold forcing a red m-cycle or a blue n-clique in every red–blue coloring of a complete graph.
families.subject: Combinatorics
families.overviewTitle: Exact cycle--clique Ramsey numbers
families.overviewSummary: Proves the Erd\H{o}s--Faudree--Rousseau--Schelp conjecture: $R(C_m,K_n)=(m-1)(n-1)+1$ for every $m\ge n\ge3$, except $R(C_3,K_3)=6$. This is the exact threshold forcing a red $m$-cycle or a blue $n$-clique in every red--blue coloring of a complete graph.

families.title: Polynomial removal fails for ordered binary matrices
families.summary: Disproves polynomial ordered binary matrix removal with one fixed $66\times66$ zero–one pattern. Matrices can require many binary-entry changes to become pattern-free while their copy density is smaller than every proposed polynomial bound in that distance. Copies preserve row and column orders and match both zeros and ones.

families.title: A power improvement in the Heilbronn triangle lower bound
families.summary: For every sufficiently large n, constructs n points in the unit square such that every triangle has area at least $n^{-2+c}$ for one absolute c > 0. This disproves the conjectured almost-n−2 upper bound in Heilbronn's triangle problem, which asks how large the smallest determined triangle can be.
families.subject: Combinatorics
families.overviewTitle: A power improvement in the Heilbronn triangle problem

families.title: Boolean functions violate the square-root degree bound by arbitrary factors
families.summary: Disproves the proposed square-root bound relating a Boolean function's linear Fourier coefficients to its polynomial degree. For every C > 0, there is a sign-valued Boolean function f with $\sum_i\widehat f(\{i\})\gt C\sqrt{\deg(f)}$. Thus its total signed correlation with individual input bits can exceed the proposed bound by an arbitrary factor.

families.title: Serre’s intersection-multiplicity conjecture
families.summary: Proves strict positivity of Serre's intersection multiplicity $\chi^R(M,N)$ for nonzero finitely generated modules over any regular local ring, provided $M\otimes_R N$ has finite length and $\dim M+\dim N=\dim R$. This resolves the positivity conjecture, including ramified mixed characteristic.

families.title: Lech’s multiplicity conjecture
families.summary: Proves $e(R)\le e(S)$ for every flat local homomorphism of nonzero Noetherian local rings, where e is Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity. This resolves Lech's conjecture in every dimension and characteristic.
