families.title: Threshold and positive-energy bound states of the BFSS matrix model
families.summary: Proves that the undeformed relative $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ BFSS model has exactly one normalizable zero-energy state for every finite N ≥ 2, resolving the threshold-bound-state conjecture. For $\mathrm{SU}(2)$, a companion proves infinitely many normalizable positive-energy eigenstates with unbounded energies, contradicting the original BFSS paper's exclusion of additional bound states at N = 2.
families.subject: Mathematical physics
families.overviewTitle: Threshold and positive-energy bound states of the BFSS model
families.overviewSummary: Proves that the undeformed relative $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ BFSS model has exactly one normalizable zero-energy state for every finite $N\ge2$, resolving the threshold-bound-state conjecture. For $\mathrm{SU}(2)$, a companion proves infinitely many normalizable positive-energy eigenstates with unbounded energies, contradicting the original BFSS paper\textquotesingle s exclusion of additional bound states at $N=2$.

families.title: Bloch's law, its lattice correction, and the spherical magnetization law
families.summary: Proves Bloch's T3/2 law with its exact coefficient for three-dimensional quantum Heisenberg ferromagnets at every positive quantum spin, allowing nonnegative symmetric finite-range couplings whose support generates ℤ3. The thermodynamic limit precedes the zero-field derivative and low-temperature limit. The family also proves spontaneous magnetization for nearest-neighbor models in every dimension d ≥ 3 and determines the first lattice correction for three-dimensional nearest-neighbor couplings.
families.subject: Mathematical physics
families.overviewTitle: Bloch's law and spontaneous ferromagnetic order
families.overviewSummary: Proves Bloch's $T^{3/2}$ law with its exact coefficient for three-dimensional quantum Heisenberg ferromagnets at every positive quantum spin, allowing nonnegative symmetric finite-range couplings whose support generates $\mathbb Z^3$. The thermodynamic limit precedes the zero-field derivative and low-temperature limit. The family also proves spontaneous magnetization for nearest-neighbor models in every dimension $d\ge3$ and determines the first lattice correction for three-dimensional nearest-neighbor couplings.

families.title: Entanglement without distillable secret key
families.summary: Constructs an entangled state on $\mathbb C^{10}\otimes\mathbb C^{10}$ with zero distillable secret key for the specified local-instrument protocols that complete almost surely. These allow joint local processing and authenticated two-way public communication, with no other shared private resource and an eavesdropper holding the input purification and public record. A trace-preserving PPT channel on $M_{21}(\mathbb C)$ whose square is not entanglement breaking disproves Christandl's PPT-square conjecture.
families.subject: Mathematical physics
families.overviewTitle: Entanglement without secret key and the PPT-square conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Constructs an entangled state on $\mathbb C^{10}\otimes\mathbb C^{10}$ with zero distillable secret key for the specified local-instrument protocols that complete almost surely. These allow joint local processing and authenticated two-way public communication, with no other shared private resource and an eavesdropper holding the input purification and public record. A trace-preserving PPT channel on $M_{21}(\mathbb C)$ whose square is not entanglement breaking disproves Christandl\textquotesingle s PPT-square conjecture.

families.title: The entropy photon-number inequality
families.summary: Proves the entropy photon-number inequality for beam-splitter mixing of two independent finite-energy bosonic inputs in any finite number of modes: the output's entropy photon number is at least the transmissivity-weighted average of the inputs'. Arbitrary entanglement within each input is allowed, and product thermal inputs attain equality even when their entropies differ.
families.subject: Mathematical physics
families.overviewTitle: The entropy photon-number inequality
families.overviewSummary: Proves the entropy photon-number inequality for beam-splitter mixing of two independent finite-energy bosonic inputs in any finite number of modes: the output\textquotesingle s entropy photon number is at least the transmissivity-weighted average of the inputs\textquotesingle. Arbitrary entanglement within each input is allowed, and product thermal inputs attain equality even when their entropies differ.

families.title: Parity is not in QAC0
families.summary: Resolves Moore's parity conjecture in the measured-output model: constant-depth quantum circuits with arbitrary one-qubit gates, unbounded-arity Toffoli gates and polynomially many total qubits cannot compute parity with any fixed positive worst-case advantage. Ancillas start in zero, one output qubit is measured, and all other registers may be discarded. Xu–Li's reductions give the same bounded-error obstruction for strict majority.
families.subject: Mathematical physics
families.overviewTitle: Moore's parity conjecture for $\mathrm{QAC}^0$
families.overviewSummary: Resolves Moore's parity conjecture in the measured-output model: constant-depth quantum circuits with arbitrary one-qubit gates, unbounded-arity Toffoli gates and polynomially many total qubits cannot compute parity with any fixed positive worst-case advantage. Ancillas start in zero, one output qubit is measured, and all other registers may be discarded. Xu--Li's reductions give the same bounded-error obstruction for strict majority.

families.title: QMA-hardness of continuum Coulomb energy
families.summary: Proves QMA-hardness of approximating the electronic Coulomb energy infimum in three dimensions, minimizing over the full spinful fermionic continuum space. Deterministic polynomial-time reductions work even with only unit-charge nuclei at distinct rational positions, polynomially many electrons and an energy-threshold separation of at least one.
families.subject: Mathematical physics
families.overviewTitle: QMA-hardness of continuum Coulomb energy
families.overviewSummary: Proves QMA-hardness of approximating the electronic Coulomb energy infimum in three dimensions, minimizing over the full spinful fermionic continuum space. Deterministic polynomial-time reductions work even with only unit-charge nuclei at distinct rational positions, polynomially many electrons and an energy-threshold separation of at least one.

families.title: Classical capacity of generalized amplitude damping
families.summary: Determines the unassisted classical capacity of every qubit generalized amplitude-damping channel, including all damping and thermal parameters. An explicit one-variable optimization gives the capacity, attained by independent two-state signal ensembles with collective decoding. Holevo capacity, minimum output entropy and regularized classical capacity are additive when tensoring with any finite-dimensional quantum channel.
families.subject: Mathematical physics
families.overviewTitle: The classical capacity of generalized amplitude damping
families.overviewSummary: Determines the unassisted classical capacity of every qubit generalized amplitude-damping channel, including all damping and thermal parameters. An explicit one-variable optimization gives the capacity, attained by independent two-state signal ensembles with collective decoding. Holevo capacity, minimum output entropy and regularized classical capacity are additive when tensoring with any finite-dimensional quantum channel.

families.title: Threshold repetition for entangled games
families.summary: Proves exponential threshold repetition for every finite two-player one-round game: if its entangled value is v < 1, the probability of winning at least a fraction $v+\delta$ of k independent repetitions decays exponentially in k, for $0\lt \delta\lt 1-v$. Arbitrary joint finite-dimensional entangled strategies and correlated question distributions are allowed.
families.subject: Mathematical physics
families.overviewTitle: Threshold repetition for entangled games
families.overviewSummary: Proves exponential threshold repetition for every finite two-player one-round game: if its entangled value is $v<1$, the probability of winning at least a fraction $v+\delta$ of $k$ independent repetitions decays exponentially in $k$, for $0<\delta<1-v$. Arbitrary joint finite-dimensional entangled strategies and correlated question distributions are allowed.

families.title: Failure of Kohn–Sham ensemble representation
families.summary: Constructs a three-electron Coulomb molecule with two equal positive-integer-charge nuclei whose absolute ground-state density has no noninteracting ground-state ensemble representation by a single real spin-independent local potential in $L^{3/2}(\mathbb R^3)+L^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$. This disproves Kohn–Sham ensemble representability for that potential class; the required nuclear charge is specified nonnumerically.
families.subject: Mathematical physics
families.overviewTitle: Failure of Kohn--Sham ensemble representation
families.overviewSummary: Constructs a three-electron Coulomb molecule with two equal positive-integer-charge nuclei whose absolute ground-state density has no noninteracting ground-state ensemble representation by a single real spin-independent local potential in $L^{3/2}(\mathbb R^3)+L^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$. This disproves Kohn--Sham ensemble representability for that potential class; the required nuclear charge is specified nonnumerically.

families.title: Exact quantum factoring over a fixed finite gate set
families.summary: Gives a polynomial-time uniform quantum circuit family that outputs the complete prime factorization of every integer with probability one. Both gate count and qubit count are polynomial in the input length, and one fixed finite gate set suffices.
families.subject: Mathematical physics
families.overviewTitle: Exact quantum factoring over a fixed finite gate set
families.overviewSummary: Gives a polynomial-time uniform quantum circuit family that outputs the complete prime factorization of every integer with probability one. Both gate count and qubit count are polynomial in the input length, and one fixed finite gate set suffices.

families.title: Unitary vertex operator algebras and conformal nets
families.summary: Proves the strongly rational case of the strong-locality conjecture: every simple unitary strongly rational complex vertex operator algebra generates a completely rational conformal net. Its simple modules are unitarizable, and its representation category agrees with the net’s finite-index sectors as a braided unitary tensor category.
families.subject: Mathematical physics
families.overviewTitle: Strong locality for strongly rational unitary vertex operator algebras
families.overviewSummary: Proves the strongly rational case of the strong-locality conjecture: every simple unitary strongly rational complex vertex operator algebra generates a completely rational conformal net. Its simple modules are unitarizable, and its representation category agrees with the net’s finite-index sectors as a braided unitary tensor category.

families.title: QAOA attains the SK optimum in the thermodynamic-first limit
families.summary: Proves that QAOA approaches the ground-state energy of the Gaussian zero-field Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model when system size tends to infinity before circuit depth. For every accuracy, finite depth and deterministic angles independent of size and disorder achieve the required limiting expected energy per spin. This also yields leading-order optimal expected MaxCut values on large-degree random regular graphs, with size tending to infinity before degree.
families.subject: Mathematical physics
families.overviewTitle: QAOA optimality for the SK model
families.overviewSummary: Proves that QAOA approaches the ground-state energy of the Gaussian zero-field Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model when system size tends to infinity before circuit depth. For every accuracy, finite depth and deterministic angles independent of size and disorder achieve the required limiting expected energy per spin. This also yields leading-order optimal expected MaxCut values on large-degree random regular graphs, with size tending to infinity before degree.

families.title: From scale symmetry to local conformal symmetry in four-dimensional QFT
families.summary: Under the stated bounded-local-net and field-reconstruction hypotheses, proves that scale symmetry implies local conformal symmetry for four-dimensional unitary positive-energy theories with a discrete bounded-below scaling spectrum of finite multiplicity, finite scaling support and a physical local scale current. The stress tensor has a traceless improvement with unchanged spacetime charges. The conclusion concerns local Ward identities, not a global conformal action on the whole net.
families.subject: Mathematical physics
families.overviewTitle: Scale-to-conformal enhancement in four-dimensional QFT
families.overviewSummary: Under the stated bounded-local-net and field-reconstruction hypotheses, proves that scale symmetry implies local conformal symmetry for four-dimensional unitary positive-energy theories with a discrete bounded-below scaling spectrum of finite multiplicity, finite scaling support and a physical local scale current. The stress tensor has a traceless improvement with unchanged spacetime charges. The conclusion concerns local Ward identities, not a global conformal action on the whole net.

families.title: Polynomial-time unitary synthesis from a Boolean oracle
families.summary: Solves the constant-error Aaronson–Kuperberg unitary synthesis problem: a uniform polynomial-size quantum oracle circuit approximates every n-qubit unitary channel within diamond-norm error 1/2, after a suitable Boolean oracle is chosen. Gates, qubits, oracle calls and query length are polynomially bounded. The target-dependent oracle may have an unrestricted truth table; its efficient classical construction is not asserted.
families.subject: Mathematical physics
families.overviewTitle: Polynomial-time, constant-error unitary synthesis from a Boolean oracle
families.overviewSummary: Solves the constant-error Aaronson--Kuperberg unitary synthesis problem: a uniform polynomial-size quantum oracle circuit approximates every $n$-qubit unitary channel within diamond-norm error $1/2$, after a suitable Boolean oracle is chosen. Gates, qubits, oracle calls and query length are polynomially bounded. The target-dependent oracle may have an unrestricted truth table; its efficient classical construction is not asserted.

families.title: The optimal quartic separation between randomized and quantum queries
families.summary: Shows that the universal bound $R(f)=O((1+Q(f))^4)$ for total Boolean functions is sharp in its exponent, ruling out every smaller power and disproving the conjectured cubic relation. Here R and Q are randomized and quantum worst-case bit-query complexities with error at most 1/3; computation between queries is unrestricted.
families.subject: Mathematical physics
families.overviewTitle: The optimal randomized--quantum query exponent
families.overviewSummary: Shows that the universal bound $R(f)=O((1+Q(f))^4)$ for total Boolean functions is sharp in its exponent, ruling out every smaller power and disproving the conjectured cubic relation. Here $R$ and $Q$ are randomized and quantum worst-case bit-query complexities with error at most $1/3$; computation between queries is unrestricted.

families.title: Counterexamples to Baum–Connes and Kadison–Kaplansky
families.summary: Disproves the coefficient-free reduced Baum–Connes conjecture through a failure of rational injectivity and a separate failure of surjectivity of assembly. A finitely generated torsion-free example witnesses the injectivity failure. Separately, a torsion-free group has a nontrivial projection in its reduced group C∗-algebra, disproving the Kadison–Kaplansky conjecture.
families.subject: Operator algebras
families.overviewTitle: Counterexamples to Baum--Connes and Kadison--Kaplansky
families.overviewSummary: Disproves the coefficient-free reduced Baum--Connes conjecture through a failure of rational injectivity and a separate failure of surjectivity of assembly. A finitely generated torsion-free example witnesses the injectivity failure. Separately, a torsion-free group has a nontrivial projection in its reduced group $C^*$-algebra, disproving the Kadison--Kaplansky conjecture.

families.title: Rigidity and arithmetic of lattice von Neumann algebras
families.summary: Classifies finite-index bimodules between scalar-twisted group factors of ICC groups commensurable with property-$(T)$ lattices over characteristic-zero local fields and arbitrary ICC group factors. Every such bimodule is a summand of finite sums of models arising from finite-index subgroup isomorphisms and finite-dimensional projective representations. The classification also recovers the group, scalar cocycle and amplification scale up to the stated stable equivalence.
families.subject: Operator algebras
families.overviewTitle: Arithmetic rigidity of lattice von Neumann algebras
families.overviewSummary: Classifies finite-index bimodules between scalar-twisted group factors of ICC groups commensurable with property-$(T)$ lattices over characteristic-zero local fields and arbitrary ICC group factors. Every such bimodule is a summand of finite sums of models arising from finite-index subgroup isomorphisms and finite-dimensional projective representations. The classification also recovers the group, scalar cocycle and amplification scale up to the stated stable equivalence.

families.title: Isomorphism of the free group factors
families.summary: Resolves the free group factor isomorphism problem: $L(\mathbb F_2)\cong L(\mathbb F_3)$, and hence all interpolated free group factors, including $L(\mathbb F_\infty)$, are isomorphic. Their common factor has fundamental group $\mathbb R_{\gt 0}$.
families.subject: Operator algebras
families.overviewTitle: All nonabelian free group factors are isomorphic
families.overviewSummary: Resolves the free group factor isomorphism problem: $L(\mathbb F_2)\cong L(\mathbb F_3)$, and hence all interpolated free group factors, including $L(\mathbb F_\infty)$, are isomorphic. Their common factor has fundamental group $\mathbb R_{>0}$.

families.title: Kadison's similarity conjecture
families.summary: Proves Kadison's similarity conjecture: every bounded complex-linear unital algebra homomorphism from a unital complex C∗-algebra to operators on a Hilbert space becomes a $*$-homomorphism after conjugation by a bounded invertible operator.
families.subject: Operator algebras
families.overviewTitle: Kadison's similarity conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Proves Kadison's similarity conjecture: every bounded complex-linear unital algebra homomorphism from a unital complex $C^*$-algebra to operators on a Hilbert space becomes a $*$-homomorphism after conjugation by a bounded invertible operator.

families.title: Strong Kadison–Kastler stability and its spatial boundaries
families.summary: Proves that sufficiently close unital von Neumann algebras on the same Hilbert space are conjugate by a unitary arbitrarily close to the identity, with a universal tolerance in the operator-norm distance between unit balls. Counterexamples show that near-identity conjugacy fails for one-sided near inclusions, and that arbitrarily close norm-separable C∗-algebras need not be ambiently unitarily conjugate.
families.subject: Operator algebras
families.overviewTitle: The strong Kadison--Kastler conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Proves that sufficiently close unital von Neumann algebras on the same Hilbert space are conjugate by a unitary arbitrarily close to the identity, with a universal tolerance in the operator-norm distance between unit balls. Counterexamples show that near-identity conjugacy fails for one-sided near inclusions, and that arbitrarily close norm-separable $C^*$-algebras need not be ambiently unitarily conjugate.

families.title: Relative bicentralizers and modular spectral recovery
families.summary: Proves Connes' bicentralizer conjecture for every type III1 factor with separable predual and every faithful normal state. More generally, for every inclusion $N\subset M$ of von Neumann algebras with separable preduals admitting a faithful normal conditional expectation, constructs an amenable expected subalgebra $P\subset N$ with $P'\cap c(M)=N'\cap c(M)$, resolving the relative bicentralizer conjecture.
families.subject: Operator algebras
families.overviewTitle: Connes' bicentralizer conjecture and relative bicentralizers
families.overviewSummary: Proves Connes' bicentralizer conjecture for every type $\mathrm{III}_1$ factor with separable predual and every faithful normal state. More generally, for every inclusion $N\subset M$ of von Neumann algebras with separable preduals admitting a faithful normal conditional expectation, constructs an amenable expected subalgebra $P\subset N$ with $P'\cap c(M)=N'\cap c(M)$, resolving the relative bicentralizer conjecture.

families.title: Cuntz comparison, nuclear dimension, and equivariant Jiang–Su stability
families.summary: Proves equivariant Jiang–Su stability for every countable discrete amenable group action on a simple separable unital infinite-dimensional nuclear stably finite Jiang–Su-stable C∗-algebra, resolving this case of Szabó's conjecture without restrictions on trace dynamics. The family also proves the unital Toms–Winter conjecture, equating strict comparison, finite nuclear dimension and Jiang–Su stability in the simple separable unital infinite-dimensional nuclear setting.
families.subject: Operator algebras
families.overviewTitle: Toms--Winter and equivariant Jiang--Su stability
families.overviewSummary: Proves equivariant Jiang--Su stability for every countable discrete amenable group action on a simple separable unital infinite-dimensional nuclear stably finite Jiang--Su-stable $C^*$-algebra, resolving this case of Szab\'o's conjecture without restrictions on trace dynamics. The family also proves the unital Toms--Winter conjecture, equating strict comparison, finite nuclear dimension and Jiang--Su stability in the simple separable unital infinite-dimensional nuclear setting.

families.title: Kirchberg's $\mathcal O_2$ norm-ultrapower embedding problem
families.summary: Constructs an explicit separable unital full group C∗-algebra that cannot embed unitally into the norm ultrapower of any fixed nonzero unital nuclear C∗-algebra, for any free ultrafilter on the natural numbers. Taking the target to be $\mathcal O_2$ answers Kirchberg's norm-ultrapower embedding problem negatively.
families.subject: Operator algebras
families.overviewTitle: A counterexample to Kirchberg's norm-ultrapower embedding problem
families.overviewSummary: Constructs an explicit separable unital full group $C^*$-algebra that cannot embed unitally into the norm ultrapower of any fixed nonzero unital nuclear $C^*$-algebra, for any free ultrafilter on the natural numbers. Taking the target to be $\mathcal O_2$ answers Kirchberg's norm-ultrapower embedding problem negatively.

families.title: Invariant projections, hyperinvariant subspaces, and transitive algebras
families.summary: Constructs a nonzero norm-quasinilpotent operator on every infinite-dimensional separable complex Hilbert space with no nonzero proper closed subspace invariant under every commuting operator. The construction also gives operators with no nontrivial invariant projection in the hyperfinite type II1 factor.
families.subject: Operator algebras
families.overviewTitle: A counterexample to the hyperinvariant-subspace problem
families.overviewSummary: Constructs a nonzero norm-quasinilpotent operator on every infinite-dimensional separable complex Hilbert space with no nonzero proper closed subspace invariant under every commuting operator. The construction also gives operators with no nontrivial invariant projection in the hyperfinite type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor.

families.title: Kaplansky's quasitrace conjecture and failure of tensor-product stable finiteness
families.summary: Disproves Kaplansky's quasitrace conjecture by constructing a separable unital complex C∗-algebra admitting normalized 2-quasitraces, all of which are nonadditive. As a consequence, two unital simple stably finite C∗-algebras can have a properly infinite minimal tensor product, with one factor $C_r^*(\mathbb F_2)$.
families.subject: Operator algebras
families.overviewTitle: A counterexample to Kaplansky's quasitrace conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Disproves Kaplansky's quasitrace conjecture by constructing a separable unital complex $C^*$-algebra admitting normalized $2$-quasitraces, all of which are nonadditive. As a consequence, two unital simple stably finite $C^*$-algebras can have a properly infinite minimal tensor product, with one factor $C_r^*(\mathbb F_2)$.

families.title: The Kadison–Ringrose cohomology conjecture
families.summary: Proves that every bounded Hochschild cocycle of degree at least two on a complex von Neumann algebra, with coefficients in the algebra itself, has a bounded primitive. Equivalently, all higher bounded Hochschild cohomology groups vanish, resolving the Kadison–Ringrose conjecture.
families.subject: Operator algebras
families.overviewTitle: The Kadison--Ringrose cohomology conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Proves that every bounded Hochschild cocycle of degree at least two on a complex von Neumann algebra, with coefficients in the algebra itself, has a bounded primitive. Equivalently, all higher bounded Hochschild cohomology groups vanish, resolving the Kadison--Ringrose conjecture.

families.title: The generator problem for finite factors
families.summary: Proves that every type II1 factor with separable predual is generated by a single operator, equivalently by two self-adjoint operators, resolving the generator problem. More strongly, for every irreducible inclusion $P\subset M$ of such factors, the unitaries u with $M=W^*(P,u)$ form a dense Gδ subset in the trace 2-norm topology.
families.subject: Operator algebras
families.overviewTitle: The generator problem for finite factors
families.overviewSummary: Proves that every type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor with separable predual is generated by a single operator, equivalently by two self-adjoint operators, resolving the generator problem. More strongly, for every irreducible inclusion $P\subset M$ of such factors, the unitaries $u$ with $M=W^*(P,u)$ form a dense $G_\delta$ subset in the trace $2$-norm topology.

families.title: A ZFC counterexample to Naimark's problem
families.summary: Gives an alternative to [Tanaka's ZFC construction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.26930v1) of a unital infinite-dimensional simple complex C∗-algebra with a faithful tracial state and exactly one nonzero irreducible representation up to unitary equivalence. Thus the unrestricted compact-operator characterization fails without additional set-theoretic assumptions; the counterexample is nonseparable.
families.subject: Operator algebras
families.overviewTitle: A ZFC counterexample to Naimark's problem
families.overviewSummary: Gives an alternative to \href{https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.26930v1}{Tanaka's ZFC construction} of a unital infinite-dimensional simple complex $C^*$-algebra with a faithful tracial state and exactly one nonzero irreducible representation up to unitary equivalence. Thus the unrestricted compact-operator characterization fails without additional set-theoretic assumptions; the counterexample is nonseparable.

families.title: Two notions of free entropy differ even when both are finite
families.summary: Constructs a bounded self-adjoint tuple in a tracial von Neumann algebra whose microstates and nonmicrostates free entropies satisfy $-\infty\lt \chi\lt \chi^*\lt \infty$. This answers Voiculescu’s finite-entropy equality question negatively: the matrix-approximation and free-Fisher-information definitions differ even when both are finite.
families.subject: Operator algebras
families.overviewTitle: A counterexample to Voiculescu’s free-entropy equality conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Constructs a bounded self-adjoint tuple in a tracial von Neumann algebra whose microstates and nonmicrostates free entropies satisfy $-\infty<\chi<\chi^*<\infty$. This answers Voiculescu’s finite-entropy equality question negatively: the matrix-approximation and free-Fisher-information definitions differ even when both are finite.

families.title: The Kirchberg–Rørdam character criterion and infinite tensor-power Jiang–Su stability
families.summary: A nonzero unital separable complex C∗-algebra is Jiang–Su stable exactly when its norm central-sequence algebra has no characters, for every free ultrafilter. This answers the Kirchberg–Rørdam character question. Also, the infinite minimal tensor power of every such algebra without characters is Jiang–Su stable, answering the Dadarlat–Toms question.
families.subject: Operator algebras
families.overviewTitle: The Kirchberg--R\o rdam character criterion
families.overviewSummary: A nonzero unital separable complex $C^*$-algebra is Jiang--Su stable exactly when its norm central-sequence algebra has no characters, for every free ultrafilter. This answers the Kirchberg--R\o rdam character question. Also, the infinite minimal tensor power of every such algebra without characters is Jiang--Su stable, answering the Dadarlat--Toms question.

families.title: Approximation and quadratic strong-operator paving
families.summary: Proves that every self-adjoint element of a complex von Neumann algebra admits strong-operator paving relative to any maximal abelian subalgebra with $O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ blocks. The norm bound holds after compression by a projection arbitrarily close to the identity in the strong topology, resolving the Popa–Vaes quadratic paving conjecture.
families.subject: Operator algebras
families.overviewTitle: The Popa--Vaes quadratic strong-operator paving conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Proves that every self-adjoint element of a complex von Neumann algebra admits strong-operator paving relative to any maximal abelian subalgebra with $O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ blocks. The norm bound holds after compression by a projection arbitrarily close to the identity in the strong topology, resolving the Popa--Vaes quadratic paving conjecture.

families.title: Trace cones and Razak–Jacelon stabilization
families.summary: Classifies separable nuclear complex C∗-algebras after tensoring with the Razak–Jacelon algebra and the compact operators, using their full topological cones of extended lower-semicontinuous tracial weights. This answers Robert’s trace-cone question, including algebras with arbitrary ideal structure and both finite and infinite subquotients.
families.subject: Operator algebras
families.overviewTitle: Classification by trace cones after Razak--Jacelon stabilization
families.overviewSummary: Classifies separable nuclear complex $C^*$-algebras after tensoring with the Razak--Jacelon algebra and the compact operators, using their full topological cones of extended lower-semicontinuous tracial weights. This answers Robert’s trace-cone question, including algebras with arbitrary ideal structure and both finite and infinite subquotients.

families.title: Radius of comparison equals half the mean dimension
families.summary: For every minimal homeomorphism h of an infinite compact metrizable space X, the radius of comparison of $C(X)\rtimes_h\mathbb Z$ equals $\tfrac12\mathrm{mdim}(X,h)$, including infinite values. Zero mean dimension is equivalent to the small boundary property, Jiang–Su stability and finite nuclear dimension; in this case nuclear dimension is at most one.
families.subject: Operator algebras
families.overviewTitle: The Phillips--Toms formula for minimal integer actions
families.overviewSummary: For every minimal homeomorphism $h$ of an infinite compact metrizable space $X$, the radius of comparison of $C(X)\rtimes_h\mathbb Z$ equals $\tfrac12\mathrm{mdim}(X,h)$, including infinite values. Zero mean dimension is equivalent to the small boundary property, Jiang--Su stability and finite nuclear dimension; in this case nuclear dimension is at most one.

families.title: Weak pure infiniteness and Cuntz-algebra absorption
families.summary: Resolves the ordinary-to-strong pure-infiniteness question of Kirchberg and Rørdam for complex C∗-algebras. For exact algebras, proper infiniteness of one fixed finite amplification of every positive element also suffices. Consequently, every separable nuclear algebra with this property absorbs $\mathcal O_\infty$, without unitality or simplicity assumptions.
families.subject: Operator algebras
families.overviewTitle: From ordinary to strong pure infiniteness
families.overviewSummary: Resolves the ordinary-to-strong pure-infiniteness question of Kirchberg and R{\o}rdam for complex $C^*$-algebras. For exact algebras, proper infiniteness of one fixed finite amplification of every positive element also suffices. Consequently, every separable nuclear algebra with this property absorbs $\mathcal O_\infty$, without unitality or simplicity assumptions.

families.title: The Hilbert–Smith conjecture in every dimension
families.summary: Every locally compact second-countable Hausdorff group acting faithfully and jointly continuously on a connected finite-dimensional topological manifold is a Lie group. This proves the Hilbert–Smith conjecture in all finite dimensions, for Hausdorff second-countable manifolds without boundary.
families.subject: Topology
families.overviewTitle: The Hilbert--Smith conjecture in every dimension
families.overviewSummary: Every locally compact second-countable Hausdorff group acting faithfully and jointly continuously on a connected finite-dimensional topological manifold is a Lie group. This proves the Hilbert--Smith conjecture in all finite dimensions, for Hausdorff second-countable manifolds without boundary.

families.title: Four-dimensional disk embedding and Wall's conjecture
families.summary: The unrestricted four-dimensional disk-embedding conjecture fails: framed algebraic dual spheres do not suffice to obtain disjoint locally flat spanning disks. In particular, the free group F2 is not good in the sense of Freedman–Quinn. Also constructs a finitely presented integral Poincaré duality group of dimension four with a finite classifying space but no realization as the fundamental group of a closed aspherical topological four-manifold, disproving Wall's conjecture.
families.subject: Topology
families.overviewTitle: Counterexamples to disk embedding and Wall's manifold conjecture
families.overviewSummary: The unrestricted four-dimensional disk-embedding conjecture fails: framed algebraic dual spheres do not suffice to obtain disjoint locally flat spanning disks. In particular, the free group $F_2$ is not good in the sense of Freedman--Quinn. Also constructs a finitely presented integral Poincaré duality group of dimension four with a finite classifying space but no realization as the fundamental group of a closed aspherical topological four-manifold, disproving Wall's conjecture.

families.title: The purely cosmetic surgery conjecture
families.summary: Distinct Dehn surgery slopes on a nontrivial smooth knot in S3 never produce orientation-preservingly homeomorphic manifolds, proving the purely cosmetic surgery conjecture. The statement includes the meridional slope.
families.subject: Topology
families.overviewTitle: The purely cosmetic surgery conjecture for knots in $S^3$
families.overviewSummary: Distinct Dehn surgery slopes on a nontrivial smooth knot in $S^3$ never produce orientation-preservingly homeomorphic manifolds, proving the purely cosmetic surgery conjecture. The statement includes the meridional slope.

families.title: Failure of rational injectivity for maximal coarse assembly
families.summary: Constructs a uniformly discrete bounded-geometry space whose maximal coarse assembly map is not rationally injective. The example is a coarse disjoint union of finite connected graphs of uniformly bounded degree, with an infinite-order kernel class. A companion gives the analogous failure for reduced coarse assembly, disproving the rational coarse Novikov conjecture.
families.subject: Topology
families.overviewTitle: Failure of rational injectivity for maximal coarse assembly
families.overviewSummary: Constructs a uniformly discrete bounded-geometry space whose maximal coarse assembly map is not rationally injective. The example is a coarse disjoint union of finite connected graphs of uniformly bounded degree, with an infinite-order kernel class. A companion gives the analogous failure for reduced coarse assembly, disproving the rational coarse Novikov conjecture.

families.title: Finite Smith–Toda complexes at every height
families.summary: For every n ≥ 0, constructs a finite Smith–Toda spectrum at a prime p depending on n, with Brown–Peterson homology $BP_*/(p,v_1,\ldots,v_n)$ and the canonical comodule structure. Thus Smith–Toda complexes exist at every height when the prime may vary; an explicit example realizes $V(4)$ at p = 1009.
families.subject: Topology
families.overviewTitle: Smith--Toda complexes at every height with varying primes
families.overviewSummary: For every $n\ge0$, constructs a finite Smith--Toda spectrum at a prime $p$ depending on $n$, with Brown--Peterson homology $BP_*/(p,v_1,\ldots,v_n)$ and the canonical comodule structure. Thus Smith--Toda complexes exist at every height when the prime may vary; an explicit example realizes $V(4)$ at $p=1009$.

families.title: The Kervaire invariant problem at the prime three
families.summary: Resolves the odd-primary Kervaire invariant problem at the prime three: exactly the standard classes with indices 0, 2, and 3 survive in the mod-three Adams spectral sequence, in stems 10, 106, and 322. Each surviving detection coset contains an element of exact additive order three.
families.subject: Topology
families.overviewTitle: The Kervaire invariant problem at the prime three
families.overviewSummary: Resolves the odd-primary Kervaire invariant problem at the prime three: exactly the standard classes with indices $0$, $2$, and $3$ survive in the mod-three Adams spectral sequence, in stems $10$, $106$, and $322$. Each surviving detection coset contains an element of exact additive order three.

families.title: Quillen's conjecture in rational homology
families.summary: Proves the rational-homology form of Quillen's conjecture for every finite group and every prime. If the largest normal p-subgroup of G is trivial, the poset of nontrivial elementary abelian p-subgroups has nonzero augmented reduced rational homology and is therefore not contractible.
families.subject: Topology
families.overviewTitle: Quillen's conjecture in rational homology
families.overviewSummary: Proves the rational-homology form of Quillen's conjecture for every finite group and every prime. If the largest normal $p$-subgroup of $G$ is trivial, the poset of nontrivial elementary abelian $p$-subgroups has nonzero augmented reduced rational homology and is therefore not contractible.

families.title: The Hovey–Strickland and Chai conjectures
families.summary: Proves Chai's invariant-ideal conjecture for Lubin–Tate deformation rings over finite residue fields, at every prime and positive height n. Through the implication of Barthel–Heard–Naumann, this proves the Hovey–Strickland conjecture: dualizable $K(n)$-local spectra have exactly $n+2$ thick tensor ideals, and their Balmer spectrum is a chain of $n+1$ points.
families.subject: Topology
families.overviewTitle: Chai's invariant-ideal conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Proves Chai's invariant-ideal conjecture for Lubin--Tate deformation rings over finite residue fields, at every prime and positive height $n$. Through the implication of Barthel--Heard--Naumann, this proves the Hovey--Strickland conjecture: dualizable $K(n)$-local spectra have exactly $n+2$ thick tensor ideals, and their Balmer spectrum is a chain of $n+1$ points.

families.title: The Grothendieck homotopy hypothesis
families.summary: Proves the Grothendieck homotopy hypothesis for ∞-groupoids associated with every Grothendieck coherator in the Ara–Henry convention: these algebraic objects recover the homotopy theory of spaces.
families.subject: Topology
families.overviewTitle: The Grothendieck homotopy hypothesis
families.overviewSummary: Proves the Grothendieck homotopy hypothesis for $\infty$-groupoids associated with every Grothendieck coherator in the Ara--Henry convention: these algebraic objects recover the homotopy theory of spaces.

families.title: Finite generation for the $K(n)$-local sphere
families.summary: Answers the degreewise finiteness question of Hovey and Hovey–Strickland: every homotopy group of the $K(n)$-local sphere is a finitely generated ℤp-module, for every prime, positive height and integer degree. The same conclusion holds after $K(n)$-localizing any finite p-local spectrum.
families.subject: Topology
families.overviewTitle: Finite generation for the $K(n)$-local sphere
families.overviewSummary: Answers the degreewise finiteness question of Hovey and Hovey--Strickland: every homotopy group of the $K(n)$-local sphere is a finitely generated $\mathbb Z_p$-module, for every prime, positive height and integer degree. The same conclusion holds after $K(n)$-localizing any finite $p$-local spectrum.

families.title: Cyclic length and chromatic fixed-point loss
families.summary: Determines the optimal chromatic loss from geometric H-fixed points to geometric G-fixed points for every subgroup H of a finite p-group G. At every nonnegative height, the loss equals the shortest subnormal-chain length from H to G with cyclic quotients. Each quotient counts once regardless of order, and finite spectra witness sharpness.
families.subject: Topology
families.overviewTitle: The chromatic Smith fixed-point problem for finite $p$-groups
families.overviewSummary: Determines the optimal chromatic loss from geometric $H$-fixed points to geometric $G$-fixed points for every subgroup $H$ of a finite $p$-group $G$. At every nonnegative height, the loss equals the shortest subnormal-chain length from $H$ to $G$ with cyclic quotients. Each quotient counts once regardless of order, and finite spectra witness sharpness.

families.title: The four-dimensional Singer conjecture
families.summary: Proves that the L2-Betti numbers of the universal cover of every closed connected aspherical topological four-manifold vanish outside degree two. More generally, the same conclusion holds for every finite connected aspherical integral Poincaré complex of formal dimension four, proving the four-dimensional Singer conjecture in this wider class.
families.subject: Topology
families.overviewTitle: The four-dimensional Singer conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Proves that the $L^2$-Betti numbers of the universal cover of every closed connected aspherical topological four-manifold vanish outside degree two. More generally, the same conclusion holds for every finite connected aspherical integral Poincar\'e complex of formal dimension four, proving the four-dimensional Singer conjecture in this wider class.

families.title: Curtis’s conjecture
families.summary: Proves Curtis’s conjecture: the positive-degree mod-two stable Hurewicz image of the sphere is spanned by the images of the Hopf-invariant-one classes η, ν, σ and the Kervaire-invariant-one classes that exist.
families.subject: Topology
families.overviewTitle: Curtis’s conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Proves Curtis’s conjecture: the positive-degree mod-two stable Hurewicz image of the sphere is spanned by the images of the Hopf-invariant-one classes $\eta,\nu,\sigma$ and the Kervaire-invariant-one classes that exist.

families.title: Thomason model structures in all strict higher dimensions
families.summary: Resolves the Ara–Maltsiniotis conjecture: for every n ≥ 1 and n = ω, small strict globular n-categories admit proper combinatorial Thomason model structures Quillen equivalent to simplicial sets. Thus strict higher categories model the homotopy theory of spaces in every stated dimension.
families.subject: Topology
families.overviewTitle: Thomason model structures in every strict higher dimension
families.overviewSummary: Resolves the Ara--Maltsiniotis conjecture: for every $n\ge1$ and $n=\omega$, small strict globular $n$-categories admit proper combinatorial Thomason model structures Quillen equivalent to simplicial sets. Thus strict higher categories model the homotopy theory of spaces in every stated dimension.

families.title: Chromatic splitting: filtrations and counterexamples
families.summary: Disproves strong chromatic splitting at height three for primes p ≥ 5, and weak splitting for the derived p-completed sphere at heights p (p ≥ 5) and $p+1$ (p ≥ 7). Nevertheless, for n ≥ 1 and $p\gt n+1$, the overlap $L_{n-1}L_{K(n)}S_p^\wedge$ admits a $2^n$-stage filtration by the predicted localized-sphere pieces. At height three and prime three, even finite assembly from such pieces fails in the category of $E(2)$-local modules over the derived completed sphere.
families.subject: Topology
families.overviewTitle: Chromatic splitting: counterexamples and filtrations
families.overviewSummary: Disproves strong chromatic splitting at height three for primes $p\ge5$, and weak splitting for the derived $p$-completed sphere at heights $p$ ($p\ge5$) and $p+1$ ($p\ge7$). Nevertheless, for $n\ge1$ and $p>n+1$, the overlap $L_{n-1}L_{K(n)}S_p^\wedge$ admits a $2^n$-stage filtration by the predicted localized-sphere pieces. At height three and prime three, even finite assembly from such pieces fails in the category of $E(2)$-local modules over the derived completed sphere.

families.title: Counterexamples to finite generation at chromatic height two
families.summary: Refutes the Hahn–Wilson conjecture at chromatic height two. For every sufficiently large prime p, constructs a connective p-complete spectrum of exact fp-type two that cannot be built from completed $\mathrm{BP}\langle2\rangle$ by finitely many sums, shifts, cones and retracts. The examples nevertheless satisfy the finite and telescopic localization comparisons.
families.subject: Topology
families.overviewTitle: Counterexamples to the Hahn--Wilson conjecture at height two
families.overviewSummary: Refutes the Hahn--Wilson conjecture at chromatic height two. For every sufficiently large prime $p$, constructs a connective $p$-complete spectrum of exact fp-type two that cannot be built from completed $\mathrm{BP}\langle2\rangle$ by finitely many sums, shifts, cones and retracts. The examples nevertheless satisfy the finite and telescopic localization comparisons.

families.title: Nonhomeomorphic closed aspherical four-manifolds
families.summary: Constructs closed connected aspherical topological four-manifolds that are homotopy equivalent but not homeomorphic, with a common word-hyperbolic fundamental group. This disproves even the homeomorphism-existence formulation of the Borel conjecture in dimension four.
families.subject: Topology
families.overviewTitle: A four-dimensional counterexample to Borel rigidity
families.overviewSummary: Constructs closed connected aspherical topological four-manifolds that are homotopy equivalent but not homeomorphic, with a common word-hyperbolic fundamental group. This disproves even the homeomorphism-existence formulation of the Borel conjecture in dimension four.

families.title: A counterexample to Wall's finite D(2) problem
families.summary: Constructs a finite connected three-dimensional CW complex whose universal cover has no integral homology above degree two and whose third cohomology vanishes for every local coefficient module, but which has no finite two-dimensional homotopy model. This disproves Wall's finite D(2) conjecture; the example has infinite fundamental group.
families.subject: Topology
families.overviewTitle: A counterexample to Wall's finite D(2) conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Constructs a finite connected three-dimensional CW complex whose universal cover has no integral homology above degree two and whose third cohomology vanishes for every local coefficient module, but which has no finite two-dimensional homotopy model. This disproves Wall's finite D(2) conjecture; the example has infinite fundamental group.

families.title: Tingley’s sphere-isometry problem
families.summary: Resolves Tingley's problem: every surjective isometry between the unit spheres of nonzero real Banach spaces extends uniquely to a surjective real-linear isometry of the whole spaces. No dimension restriction is imposed, so the metric geometry of the unit sphere determines the Banach space up to linear isometry.
families.subject: Functional analysis
families.overviewTitle: Tingley's sphere-isometry problem
families.overviewSummary: Resolves Tingley's problem: every surjective isometry between the unit spheres of nonzero real Banach spaces extends uniquely to a surjective real-linear isometry of the whole spaces. No dimension restriction is imposed, so the metric geometry of the unit sphere determines the Banach space up to linear isometry.

families.title: Independence of the separable quotient problem
families.summary: Establishes, relative to the consistency of a measurable cardinal, that the separable quotient problem is independent of ZFC. The assertion that every infinite-dimensional Banach space has a separable infinite-dimensional quotient can hold for all real and complex Banach spaces, whereas the continuum hypothesis yields counterexamples over both fields.
families.subject: Functional analysis
families.overviewTitle: Relative independence of the separable quotient problem
families.overviewSummary: Establishes, relative to the consistency of a measurable cardinal, that the separable quotient problem is independent of ZFC. The assertion that every infinite-dimensional Banach space has a separable infinite-dimensional quotient can hold for all real and complex Banach spaces, whereas the continuum hypothesis yields counterexamples over both fields.

families.title: Lipschitz equivalent Banach spaces need not be linearly isomorphic
families.summary: Constructs separable real Banach spaces that are globally bi-Lipschitz equivalent but not linearly isomorphic, resolving the separable Lipschitz-isomorphism problem negatively. Thus even the complete metric structure up to bi-Lipschitz equivalence does not determine a separable Banach space's linear isomorphism class.
families.subject: Functional analysis
families.overviewTitle: Lipschitz equivalence without linear isomorphism
families.overviewSummary: Constructs separable real Banach spaces that are globally bi-Lipschitz equivalent but not linearly isomorphic, resolving the separable Lipschitz-isomorphism problem negatively. Thus even the complete metric structure up to bi-Lipschitz equivalence does not determine a separable Banach space's linear isomorphism class.

families.title: The complete Crouzeix conjecture
families.summary: Resolves the complete Crouzeix conjecture: for every bounded operator A on a complex Hilbert space and every finite matrix-valued polynomial P, one has $\lVert P[A]\rVert\le2\sup_{z\in W(A)}\lVert P(z)\rVert$, where $W(A)$ is the numerical range. The constant 2 is sharp, independent of the matrix size, and valid in infinite dimensions.
families.subject: Functional analysis
families.overviewTitle: The complete Crouzeix conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Resolves the complete Crouzeix conjecture: for every bounded operator $A$ on a complex Hilbert space and every finite matrix-valued polynomial $P$, one has $\lVert P[A]\rVert\le2\sup_{z\in W(A)}\lVert P(z)\rVert$, where $W(A)$ is the numerical range. The constant $2$ is sharp, independent of the matrix size, and valid in infinite dimensions.

families.title: The cotype–cotype conjecture under the approximation property
families.summary: Resolves the cotype–cotype conjecture for real Banach spaces with the approximation property. Such a nonzero space is K-convex if and only if both it and its dual have finite Rademacher cotype, with possibly different exponents. Equivalently, these cotype assumptions force nontrivial Rademacher type.
families.subject: Functional analysis
families.overviewTitle: The cotype--cotype conjecture under the approximation property
families.overviewSummary: Resolves the cotype--cotype conjecture for real Banach spaces with the approximation property. Such a nonzero space is $K$-convex if and only if both it and its dual have finite Rademacher cotype, with possibly different exponents. Equivalently, these cotype assumptions force nontrivial Rademacher type.

families.title: Markov type characterizes superreflexivity
families.summary: Proves that every real Banach space with Markov type p for some p > 1 admits an equivalent uniformly convex norm, answering Naor's renorming question. Together with the known converse, this characterizes superreflexivity by nontrivial Markov type.
families.subject: Functional analysis
families.overviewTitle: Markov type characterizes superreflexivity
families.overviewSummary: Proves that every real Banach space with Markov type $p$ for some $p>1$ admits an equivalent uniformly convex norm, answering Naor's renorming question. Together with the known converse, this characterizes superreflexivity by nontrivial Markov type.

families.title: Nonexpansive fixed points in reflexive Banach spaces
families.summary: Resolves Kirk's reflexive-space fixed-point problem: every nonexpansive selfmap of a nonempty closed bounded convex subset of a real reflexive Banach space has a fixed point. The result uses the original norm, without assuming uniform convexity.
families.subject: Functional analysis
families.overviewTitle: Fixed points of nonexpansive maps in reflexive Banach spaces
families.overviewSummary: Resolves Kirk's reflexive-space fixed-point problem: every nonexpansive selfmap of a nonempty closed bounded convex subset of a real reflexive Banach space has a fixed point. The result uses the original norm, without assuming uniform convexity.

families.title: A counterexample to metric-entropy duality
families.summary: Disproves Pietsch's dimension-free duality conjecture for metric entropy. Origin-symmetric convex bodies violate every proposed choice of universal constants in the conjectured comparison between covering numbers and those of the polar bodies, even when the covering body is a cube.
families.subject: Functional analysis
families.overviewTitle: A counterexample to Pietsch's metric-entropy duality conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Disproves Pietsch's dimension-free duality conjecture for metric entropy. Origin-symmetric convex bodies violate every proposed choice of universal constants in the conjectured comparison between covering numbers and those of the polar bodies, even when the covering body is a cube.

families.title: A uniformly discrete counterexample to bounded approximation in Lipschitz-free spaces
families.summary: Constructs a countable uniformly discrete metric space whose real Lipschitz-free Banach space has the approximation property but not the bounded approximation property, answering Kalton's question negatively. Finite-rank operators approximate the identity on every compact set, but their norms cannot share a finite bound.
families.subject: Functional analysis
families.overviewTitle: A negative answer to Kalton's Lipschitz-free approximation question
families.overviewSummary: Constructs a countable uniformly discrete metric space whose real Lipschitz-free Banach space has the approximation property but not the bounded approximation property, answering Kalton's question negatively. Finite-rank operators approximate the identity on every compact set, but their norms cannot share a finite bound.

families.title: Reflexive midpoint convexity and diamond distortion
families.summary: Constructs a real reflexive Banach space with an asymptotically midpoint uniformly convex norm but no equivalent asymptotically uniformly convex norm, extending Baudier's separation to reflexive spaces. In the same space, depth-k countably branching diamonds require distortion at least $\sqrt{1+k/12}$, so midpoint uniform convexity does not force uniformly bounded diamond distortion even under reflexivity.
families.subject: Functional analysis
families.overviewTitle: Asymptotic midpoint uniform convexity without asymptotically uniformly convex renorming
families.overviewSummary: Constructs a real reflexive Banach space with an asymptotically midpoint uniformly convex norm but no equivalent asymptotically uniformly convex norm, extending Baudier's separation to reflexive spaces. In the same space, depth-$k$ countably branching diamonds require distortion at least $\sqrt{1+k/12}$, so midpoint uniform convexity does not force uniformly bounded diamond distortion even under reflexivity.

families.title: Metric Markov cotype of ℓ1 and Hilbert-space Lipschitz extension
families.summary: Proves that real ℓ1 has metric Markov cotype two, answering Mendel and Naor's question. Consequently, every Lipschitz map from an arbitrary subset of a real Hilbert space into ℓ1 extends to the whole space with a universal multiplicative loss in its Lipschitz constant, resolving Ball's extension problem for this target.
families.subject: Functional analysis
families.overviewTitle: Metric Markov cotype two for $\ell_1$
families.overviewSummary: Proves that real $\ell_1$ has metric Markov cotype two, answering Mendel and Naor's question. Consequently, every Lipschitz map from an arbitrary subset of a real Hilbert space into $\ell_1$ extends to the whole space with a universal multiplicative loss in its Lipschitz constant, resolving Ball's extension problem for this target.

families.title: Smooth isometric immersions of surfaces into ℝ4
families.summary: Every closed smooth Riemannian surface admits a smooth isometric immersion into ℝ4, resolving the closed-surface form of the four-dimensional isometric-immersion problem. This includes nonorientable surfaces and metrics of arbitrary Gaussian curvature.
families.subject: Differential geometry
families.overviewTitle: Smooth isometric immersions of surfaces into $\mathbb R^4$
families.overviewSummary: Every closed smooth Riemannian surface admits a smooth isometric immersion into $\mathbb R^4$, resolving the closed-surface form of the four-dimensional isometric-immersion problem. This includes nonorientable surfaces and metrics of arbitrary Gaussian curvature.

families.title: A smooth surface metric with no local isometric immersion in ℝ3
families.summary: Constructs a smooth positive-definite metric on $(-1,1)^2$ for which no neighborhood of the origin admits a smooth isometric immersion into ℝ3. This answers the unrestricted smooth local isometric realization problem for surfaces negatively, even after shrinking the neighborhood.
families.subject: Differential geometry
families.overviewTitle: A smooth surface metric with no local immersion in $\mathbb R^3$
families.overviewSummary: Constructs a smooth positive-definite metric on $(-1,1)^2$ for which no neighborhood of the origin admits a smooth isometric immersion into $\mathbb R^3$. This answers the unrestricted smooth local isometric realization problem for surfaces negatively, even after shrinking the neighborhood.

families.title: Gromov’s integral scalar-curvature bound for simplicial volume
families.summary: Proves $\int_M(\mathrm{Scal}_g^-)^{n/2}\,dV_g\ge a_n\lVert M\rVert$ for every closed connected oriented smooth n-manifold, n ≥ 3, and every smooth metric, with $a_n\gt 0$ depending only on dimension. Here $\mathrm{Scal}_g^-=\max\{0,-\mathrm{Scal}_g\}$ and $\lVert M\rVert$ is real simplicial volume. Also proves rational inessentiality under positive scalar curvature, resolving the Gromov–Lawson conjecture; every nonnegative-scalar-curvature metric on a closed aspherical manifold is flat.
families.subject: Differential geometry
families.overviewTitle: Gromov's integral scalar-curvature inequality
families.overviewSummary: Proves $\int_M(\mathrm{Scal}_g^-)^{n/2}\,dV_g\ge a_n\lVert M\rVert$ for every closed connected oriented smooth $n$-manifold, $n\ge3$, and every smooth metric, with $a_n>0$ depending only on dimension. Here $\mathrm{Scal}_g^-=\max\{0,-\mathrm{Scal}_g\}$ and $\lVert M\rVert$ is real simplicial volume. Also proves rational inessentiality under positive scalar curvature, resolving the Gromov--Lawson conjecture; every nonnegative-scalar-curvature metric on a closed aspherical manifold is flat.

families.title: Spectral scalar curvature, Urysohn width, and macroscopic dimension
families.summary: Every complete connected smooth boundaryless n-manifold, n ≥ 3, satisfying $-4\Delta+\mathrm{Scal}\ge1$ as a quadratic-form inequality admits a continuous map to a simplicial complex of dimension at most $n-2$ whose entire fibers have diameter bounded only by n in the original metric. This strengthens Gromov's width conclusion to spectral scalar curvature. Universal covers of closed positive-scalar-curvature manifolds also have continuous macroscopic dimension at most $n-2$ for every n ≥ 2.
families.subject: Differential geometry
families.overviewTitle: Spectral scalar curvature and codimension-two width
families.overviewSummary: Every complete connected smooth boundaryless $n$-manifold, $n\ge3$, satisfying $-4\Delta+\mathrm{Scal}\ge1$ as a quadratic-form inequality admits a continuous map to a simplicial complex of dimension at most $n-2$ whose entire fibers have diameter bounded only by $n$ in the original metric. This strengthens Gromov's width conclusion to spectral scalar curvature. Universal covers of closed positive-scalar-curvature manifolds also have continuous macroscopic dimension at most $n-2$ for every $n\ge2$.

families.title: Sharp Cartan–Hadamard isoperimetry and rigidity
families.summary: Proves generalized Cartan–Hadamard isoperimetry in every dimension: in a complete simply connected manifold with sectional curvature at most κ ≤ 0, every finite-volume finite-perimeter set satisfies the sharp comparison with the equal-volume model ball. Bounded positive-volume equality regions for κ = 0 are Euclidean balls. Also proves sharp Euclidean filling bounds for compactly supported integral n-cycles, n ≥ 2, in arbitrary proper CAT$(0)$ spaces.
families.subject: Differential geometry
families.overviewTitle: Cartan--Hadamard isoperimetry and CAT$(0)$ fillings
families.overviewSummary: Proves generalized Cartan--Hadamard isoperimetry in every dimension: in a complete simply connected manifold with sectional curvature at most $\kappa\le0$, every finite-volume finite-perimeter set satisfies the sharp comparison with the equal-volume model ball. Bounded positive-volume equality regions for $\kappa=0$ are Euclidean balls. Also proves sharp Euclidean filling bounds for compactly supported integral $n$-cycles, $n\ge2$, in arbitrary proper CAT$(0)$ spaces.

families.title: Yau's uniformization conjecture
families.summary: Proves Yau's uniformization conjecture: every complete connected noncompact Kähler manifold with strictly positive holomorphic bisectional curvature is biholomorphic to ℂn.
families.subject: Differential geometry
families.overviewTitle: Yau's uniformization conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Proves Yau's uniformization conjecture: every complete connected noncompact K\"ahler manifold with strictly positive holomorphic bisectional curvature is biholomorphic to $\mathbb C^n$.

families.title: Katok's entropy rigidity conjecture
families.summary: Proves Katok's entropy rigidity conjecture for closed connected Riemannian manifolds of dimension at least three with strictly negative sectional curvature: normalized Liouville measure maximizes entropy for the geodesic flow if and only if the metric is locally symmetric.
families.subject: Differential geometry
families.overviewTitle: Katok's entropy rigidity conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Proves Katok's entropy rigidity conjecture for closed connected Riemannian manifolds of dimension at least three with strictly negative sectional curvature: normalized Liouville measure maximizes entropy for the geodesic flow if and only if the metric is locally symmetric.

families.title: A counterexample to the nearby Lagrangian conjecture
families.summary: Disproves the unrestricted nearby Lagrangian conjecture. For some sufficiently large even N, constructs a closed exact embedded Lagrangian in $T^*(S^9\times S^{N-1})$ that is diffeomorphic to the base but not Hamiltonian isotopic to its zero section.
families.subject: Differential geometry
families.overviewTitle: A counterexample to the nearby Lagrangian conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Disproves the unrestricted nearby Lagrangian conjecture. For some sufficiently large even $N$, constructs a closed exact embedded Lagrangian in $T^*(S^9\times S^{N-1})$ that is diffeomorphic to the base but not Hamiltonian isotopic to its zero section.

families.title: Donaldson's hypersymplectic deformation conjecture
families.summary: Proves Donaldson's hypersymplectic deformation conjecture in a cohomology-preserving form. Every positive triple of smooth closed two-forms on a closed connected oriented four-manifold, normalized by $\int\omega_i\wedge\omega_j=\delta_{ij}$, deforms through positive closed triples to a hyperkähler triple while preserving all three cohomology classes. Any positive triple can first be normalized by a constant linear change.
families.subject: Differential geometry
families.overviewTitle: Donaldson's hypersymplectic deformation conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Proves Donaldson's hypersymplectic deformation conjecture in a cohomology-preserving form. Every positive triple of smooth closed two-forms on a closed connected oriented four-manifold, normalized by $\int\omega_i\wedge\omega_j=\delta_{ij}$, deforms through positive closed triples to a hyperk\"ahler triple while preserving all three cohomology classes. Any positive triple can first be normalized by a constant linear change.

families.title: Donaldson's tamed-to-compatible conjecture
families.summary: Proves Donaldson's tamed-to-compatible conjecture: every smooth almost complex structure on a closed four-manifold that is tamed by a symplectic form admits a compatible symplectic form. The almost complex structure stays fixed; the form's cohomology class may change.
families.subject: Differential geometry
families.overviewTitle: Donaldson's tamed-to-compatible conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Proves Donaldson's tamed-to-compatible conjecture: every smooth almost complex structure on a closed four-manifold that is tamed by a symplectic form admits a compatible symplectic form. The almost complex structure stays fixed; the form's cohomology class may change.

families.title: Symplectic ball packing in higher dimensions
families.summary: Resolves the Siegel–Yao conjecture for arbitrary capacities in every dimension $2n\ge6$. Finitely many closed symplectic balls of capacities $R_1,\ldots,R_k$ embed disjointly into an open ball of capacity R exactly when $\sum_iR_i^n\lt R^n$ and $R_i+R_j\lt R$ for every distinct pair i, j.
families.subject: Differential geometry
families.overviewTitle: Sharp symplectic ball-packing criteria in higher dimensions
families.overviewSummary: Resolves the Siegel--Yao conjecture for arbitrary capacities in every dimension $2n\ge6$. Finitely many closed symplectic balls of capacities $R_1,\ldots,R_k$ embed disjointly into an open ball of capacity $R$ exactly when $\sum_iR_i^n<R^n$ and $R_i+R_j<R$ for every distinct pair $i,j$.

families.title: The metric Blaschke conjecture
families.summary: Proves the metric Blaschke conjecture: every closed connected Riemannian manifold of positive dimension whose injectivity radius equals its diameter is, up to scaling, a standard compact rank-one symmetric space.
families.subject: Differential geometry
families.overviewTitle: The metric Blaschke conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Proves the metric Blaschke conjecture: every closed connected Riemannian manifold of positive dimension whose injectivity radius equals its diameter is, up to scaling, a standard compact rank-one symmetric space.

families.title: Infinitely many closed geodesics on Riemannian spheres and closed three-manifolds
families.summary: Proves that every smooth Riemannian metric on Sn, n ≥ 2, has infinitely many prime closed geodesics with pairwise distinct images. The same conclusion holds on every closed manifold admitting a finite smooth spherical cover and on every closed three-manifold, without orientability or nondegeneracy restrictions.
families.subject: Differential geometry
families.overviewTitle: Infinitely many closed geodesics on spheres and three-manifolds
families.overviewSummary: Proves that every smooth Riemannian metric on $S^n$, $n\ge2$, has infinitely many prime closed geodesics with pairwise distinct images. The same conclusion holds on every closed manifold admitting a finite smooth spherical cover and on every closed three-manifold, without orientability or nondegeneracy restrictions.

families.title: Sharp singular-set bounds for stationary integral varifolds
families.summary: Proves that every stationary integral m-varifold in a Euclidean open set has singular set of Hausdorff dimension at most $m-1$, a sharp bound in every positive dimension and codimension. On round spheres, the family also proves almost-everywhere regularity: the singular set has zero m-dimensional Hausdorff measure.
families.subject: Differential geometry
families.overviewTitle: Sharp singular-set bounds for stationary integral varifolds
families.overviewSummary: Proves that every stationary integral $m$-varifold in a Euclidean open set has singular set of Hausdorff dimension at most $m-1$, a sharp bound in every positive dimension and codimension. On round spheres, the family also proves almost-everywhere regularity: the singular set has zero $m$-dimensional Hausdorff measure.

families.title: Counterexamples to stable-Morse and strong Arnold fixed-point bounds
families.summary: Disproves stable-Morse lower bounds for nondegenerate Hamiltonian fixed points: on simply connected closed Kähler manifolds of real dimension 22, the deficit below the stable Morse number is unbounded. A separate Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of the complex quadric threefold has exactly three fixed points, fewer than the four critical points required of every smooth function.
families.subject: Differential geometry
families.overviewTitle: Counterexamples to strong forms of Arnold's fixed-point conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Disproves stable-Morse lower bounds for nondegenerate Hamiltonian fixed points: on simply connected closed K\"ahler manifolds of real dimension $22$, the deficit below the stable Morse number is unbounded. A separate Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of the complex quadric threefold has exactly three fixed points, fewer than the four critical points required of every smooth function.

families.title: Nonnegative-curvature Einstein classification and an L2 topological gap
families.summary: Classifies closed connected Einstein four-manifolds with positive Einstein constant and nonnegative sectional curvature: up to scaling, their universal Riemannian covers are the round S4, Fubini–Study $\mathbb{CP}^2$, or a product of equal round two-spheres. A closed simply connected nonnegatively curved four-manifold is diffeomorphic to one of these whenever the scale-invariant L2 norm of its trace-free Ricci curvature lies below a universal positive constant.
families.subject: Differential geometry
families.overviewTitle: Nonnegatively curved Einstein four-manifolds and a topological gap
families.overviewSummary: Classifies closed connected Einstein four-manifolds with positive Einstein constant and nonnegative sectional curvature: up to scaling, their universal Riemannian covers are the round $S^4$, Fubini--Study $\mathbb{CP}^2$, or a product of equal round two-spheres. A closed simply connected nonnegatively curved four-manifold is diffeomorphic to one of these whenever the scale-invariant $L^2$ norm of its trace-free Ricci curvature lies below a universal positive constant.

families.title: The Solomon–Yau least-volume conjecture
families.summary: Proves the Solomon–Yau least-volume conjecture for minimal hypersurfaces of round spheres. For every m ≥ 2, a closed connected minimal immersion into the unit sphere $S^{m+1}$ with non-totally-geodesic image has volume at least that of the smallest minimal Clifford product, counting covering multiplicity.
families.subject: Differential geometry
families.overviewTitle: The Solomon--Yau least-volume conjecture
families.overviewSummary: Proves the Solomon--Yau least-volume conjecture for minimal hypersurfaces of round spheres. For every $m\ge2$, a closed connected minimal immersion into the unit sphere $S^{m+1}$ with non-totally-geodesic image has volume at least that of the smallest minimal Clifford product, counting covering multiplicity.

families.title: Yau’s nodal bounds: surfaces and higher dimensions
families.summary: Proves the sharp $C\sqrt\lambda$ upper bound for nodal length on every fixed smooth closed surface, completing Yau's conjecture there. The upper bound fails for fixed smooth metrics in dimensions three and four, including metrics on S3 arbitrarily close to round. In dimension five, nodal measure can grow faster than $\lambda^{1/2+\varepsilon_0}$ for some fixed $\varepsilon_0\gt 0$, ruling out even arbitrarily small power losses.
families.subject: Differential geometry
families.overviewTitle: Yau's nodal conjecture: surfaces and counterexamples
families.overviewSummary: Proves the sharp $C\sqrt\lambda$ upper bound for nodal length on every fixed smooth closed surface, completing Yau's conjecture there. The upper bound fails for fixed smooth metrics in dimensions three and four, including metrics on $S^3$ arbitrarily close to round. In dimension five, nodal measure can grow faster than $\lambda^{1/2+\varepsilon_0}$ for some fixed $\varepsilon_0>0$, ruling out even arbitrarily small power losses.

families.title: Scalar curvature and finite-time Ricci-flow singularities
families.summary: Proves that a smooth Ricci flow on a closed four-manifold extends past any finite time at which scalar curvature remains uniformly bounded. A higher-dimensional counterexample has bounded scalar curvature but unbounded full curvature at its finite maximal time, disproving the unrestricted scalar-curvature extension conjecture.
families.subject: Differential geometry
families.overviewTitle: Scalar curvature detects four-dimensional Ricci-flow singularities
families.overviewSummary: Proves that a smooth Ricci flow on a closed four-manifold extends past any finite time at which scalar curvature remains uniformly bounded. A higher-dimensional counterexample has bounded scalar curvature but unbounded full curvature at its finite maximal time, disproving the unrestricted scalar-curvature extension conjecture.

families.title: A finite-time singularity of Calabi flow
families.summary: Disproves Chen's smooth long-time existence conjecture for Calabi flow by constructing a smooth $U(10)$-invariant Kähler metric on $\mathbb{CP}^{10}$ whose flow develops a finite-time singularity. The metric lies in the Fubini–Study class, so the failure occurs even in a class containing a constant-scalar-curvature metric.
families.subject: Differential geometry
families.overviewTitle: Finite-time singularity of Calabi flow
families.overviewSummary: Disproves Chen's smooth long-time existence conjecture for Calabi flow by constructing a smooth $U(10)$-invariant K\"ahler metric on $\mathbb{CP}^{10}$ whose flow develops a finite-time singularity. The metric lies in the Fubini--Study class, so the failure occurs even in a class containing a constant-scalar-curvature metric.

families.title: Affine Bernstein rigidity through dimension nine and a smooth dimension-ten counterexample
families.summary: Proves that every smooth locally uniformly convex affine-maximal graph of dimension three through nine, complete for its induced Euclidean metric, is an elliptic paraboloid. A smooth entire nonquadratic example in dimension ten makes this range sharp. In dimensions three through nine, the paraboloid classification also holds for connected open locally uniformly convex affine-maximal hypersurfaces complete for the affine Berwald–Blaschke metric.

families.title: The isoperimetric profile of the cubic three-torus
families.summary: Determines the isoperimetric profile of the unit cubic flat three-torus and classifies every finite-perimeter minimizer: balls, circular tubes around shortest closed geodesics, coordinate slabs, and their complements. The transition volumes are $4\pi/81$ and $1/\pi$, with exactly the adjacent two types minimizing at each transition.

families.overviewTitle: Isoperimetric regions in the cubic three-torus
