families.title: Unique tangent flows at the first surface singularity
families.summary: Proves the first-singular-time case of tangent-flow uniqueness for smooth compact connected embedded surfaces without boundary in ℝ3. At every singular point, all fixed-center backward tangent flows agree as area measures at every negative time in the original ambient coordinates, without mean-convexity or a prescribed tangent model.
families.subject: Differential geometry
families.overviewTitle: Unique tangent flows at the first surface singularity
families.overviewSummary: Proves the first-singular-time case of tangent-flow uniqueness for smooth compact connected embedded surfaces without boundary in $\mathbb R^3$. At every singular point, all fixed-center backward tangent flows agree as area measures at every negative time in the original ambient coordinates, without mean-convexity or a prescribed tangent model.

families.title: Gigli’s characterization of Alexandrov curvature
families.summary: Proves Gigli's conjecture: in every integer dimension n ≥ 2, Alexandrov curvature at least κ is characterized by the full-support $\mathop{\mathrm{RCD}}\nolimits ((n-1)\kappa,n)$ condition with reference measure $\mathcal H^n$ and distributional sectional curvature at least κ in the original global test classes. The RCD condition is unreduced.
families.subject: Differential geometry
families.overviewTitle: Gigli's characterization of Alexandrov curvature
families.overviewSummary: Proves Gigli's conjecture: in every integer dimension $n\ge2$, Alexandrov curvature at least $\kappa$ is characterized by the full-support $\operatorname{RCD}((n-1)\kappa,n)$ condition with reference measure $\mathcal H^n$ and distributional sectional curvature at least $\kappa$ in the original global test classes. The RCD condition is unreduced.

families.title: Bi-Lipschitz coordinates at every regular RCD point
families.summary: Proves that every regular point of a noncollapsed $\mathop{\mathrm{RCD}}\nolimits (K,n)$ space, for K ∈ ℝ and integer n ≥ 2, has an open neighborhood bi-Lipschitz to an open subset of ℝn. Regularity requires all pointed tangents to be Euclidean, the reference measure is exactly $\mathcal H^n$, and the chart compares ambient distances with a point-dependent finite constant.
families.subject: Differential geometry
families.overviewTitle: Bi-Lipschitz coordinates at every regular RCD point
families.overviewSummary: Proves that every regular point of a noncollapsed $\operatorname{RCD}(K,n)$ space, for $K\in\mathbb R$ and integer $n\ge2$, has an open neighborhood bi-Lipschitz to an open subset of $\mathbb R^n$. Regularity requires all pointed tangents to be Euclidean, the reference measure is exactly $\mathcal H^n$, and the chart compares ambient distances with a point-dependent finite constant.

families.title: A three-manifold without conjugate points or nonpositive curvature
families.summary: Constructs a closed connected orientable smooth three-manifold that admits a metric without conjugate points but no metric of nonpositive sectional curvature. This answers negatively, already in dimension three, whether the first metric-existence property implies the second.
families.subject: Differential geometry
families.overviewTitle: A three-manifold with no conjugate points and no nonpositively curved metric
families.overviewSummary: Constructs a closed connected orientable smooth three-manifold that admits a metric without conjugate points but no metric of nonpositive sectional curvature. This answers negatively, already in dimension three, whether the first metric-existence property implies the second.

families.title: Negative Kähler curvature without bounded holomorphic coordinates
families.summary: Constructs a contractible domain in ℂ3 with a complete negatively pinched Kähler metric but no bounded holomorphic coordinates, disproving bounded-domain uniformization in this setting. A higher-dimensional example has sectional curvature at most −1 and only constant bounded holomorphic functions; its curvature is not bounded below.
families.subject: Differential geometry
families.overviewTitle: Negative K\"ahler curvature without bounded holomorphic coordinates
families.overviewSummary: Constructs a contractible domain in $\mathbb C^3$ with a complete negatively pinched K\"ahler metric but no bounded holomorphic coordinates, disproving bounded-domain uniformization in this setting. A higher-dimensional example has sectional curvature at most $-1$ and only constant bounded holomorphic functions; its curvature is not bounded below.

families.title: Weak MTW curvature gives convexity and regular optimal transport
families.summary: On every closed connected Riemannian manifold of dimension at least two satisfying weak Ma–Trudinger–Wang curvature, all tangent injectivity domains are convex, resolving Villani’s conjecture in this setting. For squared-distance transport between measurable probability densities bounded above and away from zero, the optimal map and its inverse are Hölder continuous.
families.subject: Differential geometry
families.overviewTitle: Villani’s convexity conjecture and regular optimal transport
families.overviewSummary: On every closed connected Riemannian manifold of dimension at least two satisfying weak Ma--Trudinger--Wang curvature, all tangent injectivity domains are convex, resolving Villani’s conjecture in this setting. For squared-distance transport between measurable probability densities bounded above and away from zero, the optimal map and its inverse are H\"older continuous.

families.title: Failure of integer-degree harmonic dimension comparison
families.summary: Disproves Yau's proposed Euclidean dimension bound for harmonic functions of integer growth on manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature. For every sufficiently large integer k, a complete smooth metric on ℝ3 has at least $(k+2)^2$ independent harmonic functions of growth at most k, exceeding the Euclidean count $(k+1)^2$. The metric may depend on k.
families.subject: Differential geometry
families.overviewTitle: Counterexamples to Yau's harmonic dimension bound
families.overviewSummary: Disproves Yau's proposed Euclidean dimension bound for harmonic functions of integer growth on manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature. The metric may depend on $k$.

families.title: Global smoothness for relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell
families.summary: Proves large-data global existence and uniqueness for the three-dimensional, one-species relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell system. Smooth admissible initial data may be arbitrary provided the particle density is compactly supported and the electromagnetic fields have finite energy and bounded derivatives of every order; the solution remains smooth on every finite time interval.

families.title: Nonuniqueness with local conservation for the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation
families.summary: Constructs two distinct global entropy solutions of the three-dimensional periodic hard-sphere Boltzmann equation from the same nonnegative initial density, with bounded velocity support and finite mass, energy and absolute entropy. Both are strongly continuous in L1 and satisfy exact local conservation of mass, momentum and kinetic energy.
families.subject: Partial differential equations
families.overviewTitle: Boltzmann nonuniqueness with exact local conservation
families.overviewSummary: Constructs two distinct global entropy solutions of the three-dimensional periodic hard-sphere Boltzmann equation from the same nonnegative initial density, with bounded velocity support and finite mass, energy and absolute entropy. Both are strongly continuous in $L^1$ and satisfy exact local conservation of mass, momentum and kinetic energy.

families.title: Kinetic limits and fluctuations over the Boltzmann lifespan
families.summary: Derives the nonlinear Boltzmann equation from three-dimensional grand-canonical Newtonian gases throughout every regular kinetic interval with uniform Gaussian decay. Stable finite-range radial potentials may have attractive wells and a singular repulsive core; initial pair exclusion and spatially summable Gaussian density and gradient bounds are assumed. A companion gives finite-dimensional hard-sphere Gaussian fluctuations, centered at the exact microscopic expectation and governed by the linear fluctuating Boltzmann equation.

families.title: Joint metric and connection recovery from one boundary patch
families.summary: Zero-frequency measurements on any nonempty open boundary patch determine a smooth metric and smooth unitary connection on a trivial Hermitian rank-two bundle over a compact connected manifold of dimension at least three, up to diffeomorphism and gauge fixed on that patch. Inputs and observations use the same patch. In contrast, distinct uniformly positive bounded measurable scalar conductivities on a three-dimensional ball can have identical full-boundary data.

families.title: The planar Mumford–Shah regularity conjecture and local weak-L4 gradient bounds
families.summary: Resolves the interior regularity conjecture for reduced absolute planar Mumford–Shah minimizers with bounded fidelity data. Locally, the closed discontinuity set is a $C^{1,\alpha}$ arc, a regular crack tip, or three arcs meeting at $120^\circ$; only finitely many global connected components meet any compact interior region.

families.title: The critical dimension for the one-phase Bernoulli problem
families.summary: Establishes seven as the first dimension admitting a nonflat, one-homogeneous global minimizer of the one-phase Bernoulli energy. Consequently, minimizing free boundaries are smooth through dimension six, and their singular sets have dimension at most $n-7$ in higher dimensions.

families.title: The three-dimensional Ball–Evans approximation problem
families.summary: Resolves the three-dimensional Ball–Evans approximation problem: every $W^{1,p}$ homeomorphism between arbitrary bounded domains in ℝ3, for $1\le p\lt \infty$, is a strong $W^{1,p}$ limit of smooth diffeomorphisms onto the same target.
families.subject: Partial differential equations
families.overviewTitle: The three-dimensional Ball--Evans approximation problem
families.overviewSummary: Resolves the three-dimensional Ball--Evans approximation problem: every $W^{1,p}$ homeomorphism between arbitrary bounded domains in $\mathbb R^3$, for $1\le p<\infty$, is a strong $W^{1,p}$ limit of smooth diffeomorphisms onto the same target.

families.title: The hot spots conjecture for simply connected planar domains
families.summary: Proves a strict form of Burdzy's simply connected hot spots conjecture. On every smooth bounded simply connected planar domain, each nonzero eigenfunction for the first positive Neumann eigenvalue has no interior critical point, so all global extrema lie on the boundary. Eigenvalue multiplicity is allowed.

families.title: The Lane–Emden and Hénon–Lane–Emden conjectures
families.summary: Resolves the subcritical Lane–Emden conjecture and its weighted Hénon extension. For n ≥ 2, $p,q\gt 0$ and real A, B, the system $-\Delta u=|x|^A v^p$, $-\Delta v=|x|^B u^q$ has no positive entire solution when $(n+A)/(p+1)+(n+B)/(q+1)\gt n-2$, with solutions continuous at the origin and classical elsewhere. No symmetry or growth assumption is needed. Known radial existence gives the exact existence criterion for n ≥ 3 and $A,B\gt -2$.
families.subject: Partial differential equations
families.overviewTitle: The subcritical Lane--Emden and H\'enon--Lane--Emden conjectures
families.overviewSummary: Resolves the subcritical Lane--Emden conjecture and its weighted H\'enon extension. For $n\ge2$, $p,q>0$ and real $A,B$, the system $-\Delta u=|x|^A v^p$, $-\Delta v=|x|^B u^q$ has no positive entire solution when $(n+A)/(p+1)+(n+B)/(q+1)>n-2$, with solutions continuous at the origin and classical elsewhere. No symmetry or growth assumption is needed. Known radial existence gives the exact existence criterion for $n\ge3$ and $A,B>-2$.

families.title: Stable blowup for the defocusing Schrödinger equation
families.summary: For a sufficiently large odd nonlinearity power, constructs a nonempty open set of initial data in $H^k(\mathbb T^{12})$, with k > 8, whose solutions of the scalar defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation blow up in finite time. Thus finite-time blowup is stable under Sobolev perturbations in this supercritical regime.
families.subject: Partial differential equations
families.overviewTitle: Stable blowup for a defocusing Schr\"odinger equation
families.overviewSummary: For a sufficiently large odd nonlinearity power, constructs a nonempty open set of initial data in $H^k(\mathbb T^{12})$, with $k>8$, whose solutions of the scalar defocusing nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation blow up in finite time. Thus finite-time blowup is stable under Sobolev perturbations in this supercritical regime.

families.title: Global uniqueness in smooth isotropic elasticity
families.summary: Proves that full static boundary displacement-to-traction data determine both smooth real Lamé moduli on every bounded connected smooth domain in ℝ3, provided μ > 0 and $3\lambda+2\mu\gt 0$ on the closure. Neither analyticity, proximity to constant coefficients nor prior knowledge near the boundary is required.
families.subject: Partial differential equations
families.overviewTitle: Global uniqueness in smooth isotropic elasticity

Neither analyticity, proximity to constant coefficients nor prior knowledge near the boundary is required.

families.title: Nonattainment of the three-marginal Coulomb Monge problem
families.summary: An optimal three-particle Coulomb configuration need not be a deterministic function of the first particle, even for smooth identical spatial densities. The Monge and Kantorovich infima agree, but the Monge infimum is not attained. The same phenomenon occurs for every inverse-power Riesz exponent in each dimension at least two, with a suitable density in each case.

families.title: Sharp one-third stability of Brenier maps
families.summary: For uniform source measure ρ on a compact convex body with interior in dimension at least two, quadratic optimal transport maps satisfy $\|T_\mu-T_\nu\|_{L^2(\rho)}\le C W_2(\mu,\nu)^{1/3}$ uniformly over targets in a fixed compact set. The exponent is sharp, even for three-atom targets, disproving Letrouit's conjectured square-root bound.

families.title: De Giorgi's conjecture in dimension eight
families.summary: Proves De Giorgi's conjecture at its sharp dimension-eight endpoint: every entire C2 solution $u:\mathbb R^8\to(-1,1)$ of $\Delta u=u^3-u$ that is strictly increasing in one direction depends on only one linear coordinate. A stronger theorem classifies all stable entire solutions $v:\mathbb R^7\to[-1,1]$ as constant wells or planar transitions, without an energy-growth assumption.

families.title: Universal computation in forced Navier–Stokes flows
families.summary: Constructs viscous incompressible flows starting from rest on a fixed flat three-dimensional domain that perform universal computation under smooth external forcing. A terminating compiler turns a Turing machine and input into a finite program for the force, so a designated particle reaches a fixed region exactly when the machine halts. The viscosity is fixed, positive and computable.

families.title: Interior $C^{1,\alpha}$ regularity for infinity-harmonic functions
families.summary: Proves uniform interior $C^{1,\alpha_d}$ regularity for bounded infinity-harmonic functions in every dimension d ≥ 3, for a positive exponent depending only on dimension. The gradient's supremum norm and Hölder seminorm on the half unit ball are bounded by a dimension-dependent constant times the oscillation on the unit ball. The exponent is not explicit.

papers.title: Milne's rationality conjecture for abelian varieties
papers.abstract: We prove Milne's rationality conjecture for abelian varieties, including residue characteristic 2. After good reduction, the pairing of a rational Hodge class with any complementary product of divisor classes on the reduction is the same rational number in every prime-to-p realization and in crystalline cohomology. Using the Hodge theorem for CM abelian varieties, we also show that every such specialized Hodge class is represented by a single rational algebraic cycle in all these realizations.
papers.familySummary: Proves Milne's rationality conjecture for abelian varieties over $\overline{\mathbb Q}$ with good reduction: specialized Hodge classes pair rationally with complementary divisor products, independently of cohomology theory. Together with result 032, every specialized Hodge class is represented by a single rational algebraic cycle simultaneously in all prime-to-p and crystalline realizations, for every residue characteristic p.
papers.subject: Number theory
papers.sourceAbstract: We prove Milne's rationality conjecture for abelian varieties, including residue characteristic \(2\). After good reduction, the pairing of a rational Hodge class with any complementary product of divisor classes on the reduction is the same rational number in every prime-to-\(p\) realization and in crystalline cohomology. Using the Hodge theorem for CM abelian varieties, we also show that every such specialized Hodge class is represented by a single rational algebraic cycle in all these realizations.

sections.title: A divisor identity on a rational summand
CM classes as pullbacks of Weil classes
Specialization in a fixed good theory

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let \(A/\Qbar\) be an abelian variety of dimension \(d\) with good reduction \(A_0/\F\) at \(w\). Let \(0\leq r\leq d\), and let \[ \gamma\in H^{2r}(A(\C),\Q(r)) \] be a rational Hodge class. For every list of Cartier divisors \(D_1,\ldots,D_{d-r}\) on \(A_0\), there is a number \(q\in\Q\) such that \begin{align*} \Tr_\ell\bigl(\gamma_{0,\ell} c_{1,\ell}(D_1)\cdots c_{1,\ell}(D_{d-r})\bigr)&=q &&\text{in }\Q_\ell\quad(\ell\ne p),\\ \Tr_p\bigl(\gamma_{0,p} c_{1,\mathrm{cris}}(D_1)\cdots c_{1,\mathrm{cris}}(D_{d-r})\bigr)&=q &&\text{in }\Cw. \end{align*} Here \(\gamma_{0,\ell}\) is the smooth proper specialization of the \(\ell\)-adic realization, and \(\gamma_{0,p}\) is the de Rham--crystalline specialization in \[ H^{2r}_{\mathrm{cris}}(A_0/W(\F))[1/p](r) \otimes_{\Kzero}\Cw. \] The traces use the top Tate twist and send the class of a zero-cycle to its degree. If \(r=d\), the divisor product is \(1\).

primaryStatements.name: Transport
primaryStatements.label: prop:transport
primaryStatements.text: Let $A/\Qbar$ be an abelian variety of positive dimension with good reduction at $w$, and put $V=H_1(A(\C),\Q)$. Suppose \[ G\subset\GSp(V,\psi) \] is connected reductive, its Hodge homomorphism $h$ gives the Hodge structure of $A$, and its conjugacy class $X$ makes this inclusion a Hodge embedding. Let $\gamma$ be a rational Hodge class of codimension $r$, represented on $V$ by an alternating form satisfying \eqref{eq:transport-multiplier}. Then there exist a positive integer $n$, an auxiliary good-reduction abelian variety $B$, a quasi-isogeny $a:A_0^n\to B_0$, and a rational Hodge class $\kappa$ of codimension $r$ on $B$ such that, for the first-factor inclusion $j:A_0\to A_0^n$, \begin{equation} (aj)^*\kappa_0=\gamma_0. \end{equation} The equality holds simultaneously in every $\ell$-adic realization with $\ell\ne p$ and in the crystalline realization after extension to $\Cw$. Either of the following two further specifications can be imposed. \begin{enumerate} \item The variety $B$ is of CM type and is defined over $\Qbar$, with its indicated good reduction at $w$. \item Put $D_A=H^1_{\mathrm{cris}}(A_0/W(\F))[1/p]$. Suppose $\mathcal F_A$ is a filtration in degrees $0,1$ on $D_A$, over a finite extension of $\Kzero$, which is weakly admissible and has finite local-field descent together with the specialized tensors specifying the $G$-structure. Suppose also that, after a geometric tensor-preserving identification, it lies in the $G$-orbit of the original Hodge filtration. Then $B$ can be defined over a finite extension $K/\Kzero$ inside $\Cw$, and $a$ can be chosen so that \begin{equation} a^*\Fil^1H^1_{\mathrm{dR}}(B/K) =(\mathcal F_A^1)^{\oplus n}. \end{equation} Here the equality is made after a common finite extension and crystalline--de Rham identification. To discuss Hodge classes on this $B$, choose a complex embedding of an algebraic closure of $K$ extending the fixed embedding of $\Qbar$. \end{enumerate} In the second case the realizations of $\kappa$ are supplied by the canonical tensor sections of the Hodge-type model and the polarization. In the first case these agree with the usual realizations and specialization of its absolute Hodge class.

primaryStatements.name: CM transport of a Hodge class
primaryStatements.label: cor:cm-transport
primaryStatements.text: Let \(A/\Qbar\) be an abelian variety of positive dimension with good reduction at \(w\), and let \(\gamma\in H^{2r}(A(\C),\Q(r))\) be a rational Hodge class, where \(0\leq r\leq\dim A\). There are a positive integer \(n\), a CM abelian variety \(B/\Qbar\) with good reduction at \(w\), a rational Hodge class \(\kappa\) of codimension \(r\) on \(B\), and a quasi-isogeny \(a:A_0^n\to B_0\) such that \[ \gamma_0=(aj)^*\kappa_0, \] where \(j:A_0\to A_0^n\) is the first-factor inclusion. This is an equality of the usual absolute-Hodge specializations in every prime-to-\(p\) realization and in crystalline cohomology extended to \(\Cw\).

primaryStatements.name: The filtration construction
primaryStatements.label: thm:filtration
primaryStatements.text: Let $A_0/\overline{\F}_p$ be an abelian variety equipped with a rational action of a CM field $E$ and a polarization whose Rosati involution restricts to conjugation on $E$. Suppose that \[ D=H^1_{\mathrm{cris}}(A_0/W(\overline{\F}_p))[1/p] \] has rank $2s$ over $E\otimes_\Q\Kzero$, where $s\geq 1$. Suppose also that there is an invertible $u\in\End^0(A_0)$ such that \[ u^\dagger=u,\qquad ue=\bar e u\quad(e\in E). \] Let $\beta$ be the dual polarization pairing on $D$, with values in the isocrystal line of slope $1$. Then there are a finite extension $K/\Kzero$ and a subspace $L\subset D_K$ with the following properties: \begin{enumerate} \item The one-step filtration with $\Fil^1D_K=L$ is weakly admissible. \item $L$ is stable under the cohomological actions of $E$ and $u$, and is Lagrangian for $\beta$. \item After extending to an algebraically closed field $\Omega/K$, one has $\dim_\Omega L_\tau=s$ for every embedding $\tau:E\hookrightarrow\Omega$. \item The isocrystal, its indicated tensors, and this filtration have finite local field descent. \end{enumerate} Moreover, geometrically $L$ belongs to the balanced polarized cocharacter orbit. More explicitly, define \[ G_D=\left\{g\in\GSp(D,\beta)\cap \GL_{E\otimes_\Q\Kzero}(D): \det_{E\otimes_\Q\Kzero}(g)=c(g)^s\right\}, \] where the scalar on the right is viewed in $(E\otimes_\Q\Kzero)^\times$. The balanced $E$-stable $\beta$-Lagrangians form a single $G_D(\Omega)$-orbit. Each is the weight-$1$ space of a cocharacter of $G_{D,\Omega}$ with weights $0,1$. In particular $L$ belongs to the orbit of any original filtration of this type under a tensor-preserving comparison.

primaryStatements.label: cor:filtration-admissible
primaryStatements.text: The filtration of Theorem \ref{thm:filtration}, with its finite local field descent, is admissible: the descended filtered isocrystal is the filtered crystalline module of a crystalline representation.

primaryStatements.name: The divisor filtration condition
primaryStatements.label: cor:filtration-divisor
primaryStatements.text: Let \(D,L\) be as in Theorem \ref{thm:filtration}, and let \(\psi\) and \(U\) denote the homological polarization and the homological action of \(u\) on \(D_K^\vee\). The untwisted divisor form \(\psi(\cdot,U\cdot)\) belongs to \[ \Fil^1\bigl(\bigwedge^2D_K\bigr)=L\wedge D_K, \] and hence to filtration degree zero after its codimension-one Tate twist. If a marked power is realized by an abelian lift, the corresponding pulled-back divisor satisfies the filtration condition for its symmetric homomorphism in Lemma \ref{lem:lift-hom}.

primaryStatements.label: prop:weil
primaryStatements.text: Every $\gamma\in W_E^s(A)$ satisfies the Lefschetz pairing property at $w$. More precisely, if $\mathcal U$ in \eqref{eq:weil-U} has no invertible element, all complementary pairings are zero. If it has an invertible element, $\gamma_0$ is a simultaneous rational Lefschetz class.

primaryStatements.label: cor:cm-pairing
primaryStatements.text: The Lefschetz pairing property holds for the specialization of every rational Hodge class on a CM abelian variety over $\Qbar$ with good reduction at $w$.

definitions.text: A tuple \(\alpha=(\alpha_v)_v\), with \(\alpha_v\in H_v^{2r}(X)(r)\), has the Lefschetz pairing property if, for every \(\delta\in\Lef^{\dim X-r}(X)\), the numbers \(\Tr_v(\alpha_v\delta_v)\) are the images of one number in \(\Q\).

definitions.label: def:weil-space
definitions.text: The rational space of Weil classes associated with $E$ is the subspace \[ W_E^s(A)\subset \bigwedge\nolimits_{\Q}^{2s} V^\vee\otimes\Q(s) =H^{2s}(A(\C),\Q(s)) \] whose scalar extension to a splitting field $\Omega$ of $E$ is \begin{equation} W_E^s(A)\otimes_\Q\Omega =\bigoplus_{\tau:E\hookrightarrow\Omega} \bigwedge\nolimits_\Omega^{2s}V_\tau^\vee \otimes\Q(s)_\Omega. \end{equation} Here each summand is extended by zero on the other eigenspaces. The right side is Galois stable, so it defines the indicated rational subspace.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let $E/\Q$ be an elliptic curve and let $q$ be any prime. If $s_q(E)\in\{0,1\}$, then \[ r(E)=a(E)=s_q(E),\qquad \#\Sha(E/\Q)<\infty, \] and, with $r=r(E)$ and the preceding normalizations, \begin{equation} \frac{L^{(r)}(E,1)}{r!} =\frac{\Omega_E\Reg_E\,\#\Sha(E/\Q) \prod_{\ell\text{ finite}}c_\ell(E)} {\#E(\Q)_{\rm tors}^{2}}. \end{equation} There are no additional hypotheses on reduction, rational torsion, isogenies, complex multiplication, or residual Galois representations.

primaryStatements.name: Unrestricted low-corank converse
primaryStatements.label: classical:low-corank
primaryStatements.text: For every elliptic curve $A/\Q$, every prime $q$, and $u\in\{0,1\}$, the equality $s_q(A)=u$ implies \[ a(A)=r(A)=u,\qquad \#\Sha(A/\Q)<\infty. \]

primaryStatements.name: Two-primary leading term
primaryStatements.label: classical:two-primary
primaryStatements.text: For every elliptic curve $A/\Q$ with $s_2(A)\leq1$, the quotient $Q_A$ of \eqref{eq:normalized-quotient}, with the total real period and the full-lattice regulator of \eqref{eq:height-convention}, is a positive rational number, and \[ v_2(Q_A)=v_2(\#\Sha(A/\Q)). \]

primaryStatements.name: Analytic rank zero and one
primaryStatements.label: classical:analytic-low-rank
primaryStatements.text: If an elliptic curve $A/\Q$ has $a(A)\leq1$, then $r(A)=a(A)$ and the entire group $\Sha(A/\Q)$ is finite.

primaryStatements.name: Isogeny invariance
primaryStatements.label: classical:isogeny
primaryStatements.text: Suppose $A$ and $A'$ are isogenous elliptic curves over $\Q$ of analytic rank at most one. Then \[ \frac{Q_A}{\#\Sha(A/\Q)} =\frac{Q_{A'}}{\#\Sha(A'/\Q)}. \] In particular $X(A)=X(A')$. Over a number field, the corresponding analytic-to-arithmetic BSD ratio is likewise invariant under isogeny when the Tate--Shafarevich groups are finite. It is compatible with products and restriction of scalars.

primaryStatements.name: Analytic twist densities
primaryStatements.label: classical:twist-density
primaryStatements.text: For every elliptic curve $A/\Q$, among nonzero squarefree integers $d$ ordered by $|d|$, the twists $A^d$ of analytic rank zero and one each have density $1/2$. Consequently the set of $d$ with $a(A^d)\geq2$ has density zero.

primaryStatements.name: Split Gross--Zagier normalization
primaryStatements.label: classical:gross-zagier
primaryStatements.text: With the preceding conventions, $D$ odd fundamental, $(D,N)=1$, all level primes split, and $\mathcal O_K^\times=\{\pm1\}$, one has \begin{align} \frac{\sqrt{d_K}}{8\pi^2(f,f)_N}L'(f/K,1) &=2H_{\rm abs,f}(P_X),\\ L'(E/K,1)&=\frac{A_E}{\sqrt{d_K}\,c_E^2}\cdot 2H_{\rm abs}(P_K). \end{align} In the simple-zero case $P_K$ is nontorsion.

primaryStatements.name: Full-index discrepancy identity
primaryStatements.label: classical:discrepancy-identity
primaryStatements.text: Assume $L(E/K,s)$ has a simple zero under the hypotheses of Theorem \ref{classical:gross-zagier}. Then \begin{equation} \frac{Q_E}{\#\Sha(E/\Q)} \frac{Q_{E^D}}{\#\Sha(E^D/\Q)} =\frac{[E(K):\Z P_K]^2} {c_E^2\prod_\ell c_\ell(E)^2\,\#\Sha(E/K)}. \end{equation} The index on the right is the full group index, including torsion. Consequently, at any prime $p$, if \[ n_P=v_p\bigl([E(K)/E(K)_{\rm tors}:\Z\overline P_K]\bigr), \qquad \tau_g=v_p(\#E(K)_{\rm tors}), \] then \begin{equation} X_p(E)+X_p(E^D) =2(n_P+\tau_g)-2v_p(c_E) -2\sum_\ell v_p(c_\ell(E))-v_p(\#\Sha(E/K)). \end{equation}

papers.title: The Selmer converse for elliptic curves at every prime
papers.abstract: We prove the Selmer converse in coranks zero and one for every elliptic curve over ℚ and every prime p: if the full p-power Selmer group has ℤp-corank $r\in\{0,1\}$, then the analytic and Mordell–Weil ranks both equal r, and the entire Tate–Shafarevich group is finite. As an application at the additive prime 3, we prove that for every prime $\ell\equiv4,7,8\pmod9$, the cubic $X^3+Y^3=\ell Z^3$ has analytic and Mordell–Weil rank one and finite Tate–Shafarevich group. In particular, every such ℓ is a sum of two rational cubes.

In particular, every such $\ell$ is a sum of two rational cubes.

primaryStatements.name: The unrestricted low-corank Selmer converse
primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: For every elliptic curve $A_0/\Q$, every prime $p$, and $r\in\{0,1\}$, \[ s_p(A_0)=r \quad\Longrightarrow\quad a(A_0)=\rank_{\Z}A_0(\Q)=r, \qquad \#\Sha(A_0/\Q)<\infty. \] There is no restriction on reduction type, complex multiplication, the residual representation, rational torsion, or rational isogenies.

primaryStatements.name: Established converse at $2$
primaryStatements.label: thm:two-converse-input
primaryStatements.text: If $E/\Q$ is any elliptic curve and $\corank_{\Z_2}\Sel_{2^\infty}(E/\Q)=r\in\{0,1\}$, then \[ \ord_{s=1}L(E,s)=\rank E(\Q)=r, \qquad \Sha(E/\Q)\text{ is finite}. \]

primaryStatements.name: Established analytic twist-density theorem
primaryStatements.label: thm:twist-density-input
primaryStatements.text: For any elliptic curve $E/\Q$, among nonzero squarefree integers $d$ ordered by $|d|$, the quadratic twists $E^{(d)}$ of analytic rank zero and one each have density $1/2$. In particular the exceptional set of twists of analytic rank at least two has density zero.

primaryStatements.label: prop:arithmetic-reduction
primaryStatements.text: With these choices, \[ \dim H^1_f(K,V)=1, \qquad \dim H^1_f(K,V^{DD'})=1. \] The second line localizes nontrivially at both places of $K$ over $p$. Let $y\in A_0(K)$ be the norm of the conductor-one Heegner point under a modular parametrization taking the cusp $\infty$ to zero. If $y$ is non-torsion, Theorem \ref{thm:main} follows.

primaryStatements.label: prop:tame-primes
primaryStatements.text: There are rational primes $q_i\notin S$, split completely in $L$, distinguished places $\mathfrak q_i$ of $K$ above them, cyclic $p$-quotients $\Delta_i$ of the ring class group of conductor $q_i$, and surjections \[ \ell_i:G_K\longrightarrow\Delta_i\simeq\Z/p^{n_i}\Z, \qquad n_i\longrightarrow\infty, \] with the following properties. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item $\ell_i$ is unramified outside the pair above $q_i$, its restriction to inertia at $\mathfrak q_i$ is surjective, $\ell_i^c=-\ell_i$, and $\ell_i|_{G_{K_s}}=0$ for every $s\in S$. \item $v_p(q_i-1)-n_i$ is bounded. At either place above $p$, the full ring class field of conductor $q_i$ is unramified and its local degree has bounded $p$-part. \item Frobenius at $\mathfrak q_i$, on all fixed data unramified outside $S$, tends to an element $\gamma\in G_L$ such that \[ \eps(\gamma)=1,\qquad \det(V(\gamma)-1)\ne0,\qquad \cC(\gamma)\text{ is not a root of unity}. \] Moreover $\gamma$ fixes all $p$-power radicals of a fixed, conjugation-stable finite list in $K^\times$ spanning $\cO_{K,S}^{\times}\otimes\Q_p$ under the Kummer map. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.label: prop:green-length
primaryStatements.text: For the primes of \cref{prop:tame-primes}, chosen in the strict case as in \cref{lem:nonzero-obstruction}, every fixed $b\ge1$, and either $\eta=1$ or $\eta=-1$, one has \begin{equation} \length_{R_b}\GrH(L,V\otimes\psi^{\eta}) \begin{cases} =0,&\text{outside the strict case},\\ \le2,&\text{in the strict case}. \end{cases} \end{equation} In the strict case this module is killed by $t$ and is the image of its two-dimensional base space under multiplication by $t^{b-1}$. Put \begin{equation} b_*=1\quad\text{outside the strict case},\qquad b_*=3\quad\text{in the strict case}. \end{equation} Thus in both cases the length in \cref{eq:green-length} is strictly smaller than $b_*$.

primaryStatements.label: prop:heegner-log
primaryStatements.text: At the distinguished place over $p$, and for either sign, \begin{equation} \sum_{g\in\mathcal G_i}(1+t)^{\pm\ell_i(g)} \log_{A_0,p}(y_i^g) \longrightarrow0\pmod {t^{b_*}}. \end{equation} More precisely, every coefficient of degree less than $b_*$ has valuation tending to $+\infty$ along $\cU$. The coefficients through any other fixed degree have a common lower valuation bound. These assertions hold in a common $p$-adic algebraic closure, with its fixed extension of the valuation.

primaryStatements.label: prop:theta-family
primaryStatements.text: For the characters \eqref{eq:theta-character} and every sufficiently large positive $m$ on the prescribed branch, the theta construction gives holomorphic algebraic forms $\Theta_{i,m}$ of weight \eqref{eq:theta-weight}. In the canonical ordinary monomial-dual lattice their coefficients have a common bounded denominator, coefficientwise in the tame group algebra and in every fixed truncated substitution $R_b$. They have spherical parameters \eqref{eq:theta-eigenparameters}, and at both distinguished $p$-places they satisfy \[ p^{-2}U_2\Theta_{i,m}=\Theta_{i,m},\qquad p^{-2}U_3\Theta_{i,m}=\Theta_{i,m}. \] These assertions allow arbitrary fixed split tests of the stipulated bounded levels. They remain valid for the particular tests with all the finite local controls in Proposition \ref{prop:bounded-content}.

definitions.label: def:admissible
definitions.text: An admissible cochain with coefficients in $M_b^{\eta}$ is a function on sequences of Galois elements which is the coefficientwise ultralimit of continuous finite-stage cochains, in the fixed basis of $V\otimes R_b$, with one denominator $p^C$ independent of $i$. Finite-stage cochain identities are required modulo precisions $A_i\longrightarrow\infty$ along $\cU$, with $A_i\le n_i-c_b$. Equivalently, the limiting identity holds on every sequence of arguments. Cohomology is the cohomology of this cochain complex, so coboundaries are also required to be admissible. Local complexes are defined by the chosen embeddings of decomposition groups. The same definition applies over $L$ by restriction and inverse image of the finite-stage Galois groups.

papers.title: The two-primary Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer formula in Selmer corank at most one
papers.abstract: We prove the two-primary Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer leading-term formula for every elliptic curve over the rationals whose two-power Selmer group has corank at most one. In this range, the algebraic rank, analytic rank, and Selmer corank are equal, and the Tate–Shafarevich group is finite. Combined with the quadratic-twist Selmer distribution, this gives the exact two-primary formula for a density-one set of signed squarefree twists of each fixed curve, ordered by absolute value; the common rank is zero or one, with each value having density one half.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let \(E/\mathbb Q\) be any elliptic curve with \(s_2(E)\leq1\). Then \[ r:=\operatorname{rank}E(\mathbb Q) =\operatorname{ord}_{s=1}L(E,s)=s_2(E), \qquad \#\Sha(E/\mathbb Q)<\infty. \] Moreover, \[ Q_E=\frac{L^{(r)}(E,1)\,(\#T_E)^2} {r!\,\Omega_E\Reg_E\prod_{\ell\ \mathrm{finite}}c_\ell(E)} \in\mathbb Q_{>0}, \qquad v_2(Q_E)=v_2\bigl(\#\Sha(E/\mathbb Q)\bigr). \] There is no restriction on \(E[2]\) or on the reduction of \(E\) at two.

primaryStatements.name: An any-prime input criterion
primaryStatements.label: cor:any-prime-bsd
primaryStatements.text: Let \(E/\mathbb Q\) be an elliptic curve. Suppose that, for some prime \(p\), its full \(p\)-power Selmer group with the usual local Kummer conditions at every place satisfies \[ s_p(E):=\corank_{\mathbb Z_p}\Sel_{p^\infty}(E/\mathbb Q)\le1. \] Then all conclusions of Theorem \ref{thm:main} hold, with common rank \(r=s_p(E)\).

primaryStatements.name: Positive comparison
primaryStatements.label: prop:positive
primaryStatements.text: Let \(A/\mathbb Q\) be non-CM. If \(\an(A)\leq1\), then \(X(A)\geq0\). Suppose a positive fundamental discriminant \(a\) prime to \(2N_A\), or \(a=1\), satisfies \(\an(A^a)\leq1\) and \(X(A^a)=0\). Then \(s_2(A)\leq1\) implies \(\an(A)=s_2(A)\) and \(X(A)=0\).

primaryStatements.name: Split-pair anchor
primaryStatements.label: prop:anchor
primaryStatements.text: Let \(A/\mathbb Q\) be non-CM. There exist a fundamental discriminant \(h\) prime to \(2N_A\), allowing \(h=1\), and an imaginary quadratic field of discriminant \(k\) prime to \(2hN_A\), in which all primes dividing \(2hN_A\) split, such that \[ \an(A^h)+\an(A^{hk})=1, \qquad X(A^h)+X(A^{hk})=0. \]

primaryStatements.name: CM comparison
primaryStatements.label: prop:cm
primaryStatements.text: If \(A/\mathbb Q\) has complex multiplication and \(s_2(A)\leq1\), then \(\an(A)=s_2(A)\) and \(X(A)=0\).

primaryStatements.name: Split Gross--Zagier formula
primaryStatements.label: thm:classical-gz
primaryStatements.text: With the preceding hypotheses and units modulo signs one, \[ \frac{\sqrt D}{8\pi^2(f,f)_N}\,L'(f/K,1)=2H_{\rm abs,f}(P_X). \tag{GZ} \]

primaryStatements.name: The full-index discrepancy
primaryStatements.label: cor:classical-G
primaryStatements.text: Under these assumptions, the single Hilbert-class trace satisfies \[ X(E)+X(E^k) =v_2\!\left(\frac{[E(K):\mathbb ZP]^2} {c_E^2\,\prod_\ell c_\ell(E)^2\ \#\Sha(E/K)}\right). \tag{G} \] Here \([E(K):\mathbb ZP]\) is the full group index, including torsion.

primaryStatements.name: Integral classes and dyadic compatibility
primaryStatements.label: prop:siegel-integral
primaryStatements.text: The classes obtained from \eqref{eq:K1} are integral for support containing the primes of \(2n_2\) and infinity. They are compatible with the dyadic division traces and, after the mark and determinant projection, with corestriction as the dyadic part of \(M\) increases with \(c,d,A,\xi\) fixed. The projected smoothed classes on \(\mathbb Q\), with group or character coefficients, admit integral lifts to ordinary positive cohomology.

definitions.name: Horizontal data
definitions.label: tame:data
definitions.text: A horizontal sequence consists of primes \(r_i\), integers \(m_i\to\infty\), and even surjective residue exponents \[ \lambda_i:(\Z/r_i)^\times\longrightarrow\Z/2^{m_i}, \] with the following properties. The primes avoid the fixed data, \(r_i\equiv1\pmod{ND}\), \(r_i\to1\) dyadically, and \(r_i\) splits in the Hilbert class field of \(K\) and in any fixed twisting field in use. The characters kill every prime of \(S_f\) and of the fixed smoothing integers \(c,d\), including \(2\). We may require them also to kill any specified finite list, in particular \(3\), the primes of \(D\), the tested indices and Hecke operators, and the bad primes of the fixed models and lifts below. Chosen arithmetic Frobenius lifts converge in the Tate representation to a determinant-one element with trace \(a_*\ne\pm2\) and with two eigenvalues that are not roots of unity. As a global character, \(\lambda_i\) has value \(\lambda_i(q)\) on a uniformizer at \(q\ne r_i\), is zero at infinity, and is the negative residue character at \(r_i\), with uniformizer value zero. Characters over extensions are obtained by norm.

Prime amplitudes and refined row counts
Selected prime slots and the row counts

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Every finite-order Hecke $L$-function over $F=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$ has no zero in $\Re s>7/8$. The same holds for every Dirichlet $L$-function, including $\zeta(s)$. A pole at $s=1$ for a principal character is allowed.

primaryStatements.label: cor:nonresidues-square-roots
primaryStatements.text: There are absolute constants $A,C>0$ such that, for every odd prime $p$, the least positive quadratic nonresidue $n(p)$ satisfies \[ n(p)\le C(\log p)^A. \] In particular, $n(p)\ll_\delta p^\delta$ for every $\delta>0$, proving Vinogradov's least quadratic nonresidue conjecture \cite[Conjecture 1.1]{TaoNonresidues}. Given an odd prime $p$ and $a\in\mathbb F_p$ in binary representation, there is a deterministic algorithm, with running time polynomial in $\log p$, that returns a square root of $a$ or reports that none exists.

primaryStatements.name: Continuation from a common signal
primaryStatements.label: lem:continuation-criterion
primaryStatements.text: Fix $\sigma_0\in(1/2,1)$ and suppose $\Delta_0=\beta_*-\sigma_0>0$. Let $C(s)=s+c$, where $c\in\mathbb R$ is fixed. Suppose that numbers $\omega,\sigma$ satisfying \[ 0<\omega<\Delta_0,\qquad \sigma>0 \] can be chosen independently of the target character. For every primitive finite-order Hecke character $\eta$, suppose there exist a finite set $\mathcal S$, a holomorphic function $H_\eta$ on $\Re s>\sigma_0$, and a function $J_\eta(Z)$ defined for all sufficiently large real $Z$, such that \begin{equation} \sup_{\Re s>\sigma_0}|H_\eta(s)-1|\le\frac12. \end{equation} For $Z>0$, define \begin{equation} f_\eta(Z)=\frac1{2\pi i}\int_{\Re s=2} Z^{C(s)}e^{(s-5/6)^2} \frac{H_\eta(s)}{L_F^{\mathcal S}(s,\eta)}\,ds. \end{equation} Assume that, as $Z\to\infty$, \begin{align} |J_\eta(Z)|&\ll_\eta Z^{C(\sigma_0)+\omega}, \\ |J_\eta(Z)-f_\eta(Z)|&\ll_\eta Z^{C(\beta_*)-\sigma}. \end{align} The implied constants, lower thresholds, excluded set, and function $H_\eta$ may depend on $\eta$. Then these assumptions contradict $\beta_*>\sigma_0$.

primaryStatements.name: The $11/12$ half-plane
primaryStatements.label: thm:eleven-twelfths
primaryStatements.text: Every finite-order Hecke $L$-function over $F=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$ has no zero in $\Re s>11/12$. The same holds for every Dirichlet $L$-function, including $\zeta(s)$. A pole at $s=1$ for a principal character is allowed.

primaryStatements.name: Completed cubic reflection
primaryStatements.label: prop:completed-reflection
primaryStatements.text:
Fix a finite family $\mathcal X$ of finite-ray characters whose conductors are supported on $S$. Choose one fixed integral modulus $\mathfrak E$ with prime support exactly $S$, divisible by every conductor in this family. On primary elements extend each member of $\mathcal X$ by zero away from the $\mathfrak E$-units. primaryStatements.name: Balanced low estimate
primaryStatements.label: prop:balanced-low
primaryStatements.text: Fix the arithmetic data and smooth weights used to define $I_\eta$. For every $\epsilon>0$, as $Z\to\infty$, \[ \bigl|I_\eta(Z^{1/2},Z^{1/2},Z)\bigr| \ll_{\mathcal A,\epsilon} Z^{1/4+\epsilon}. \] The exponent is independent of the target character; the implied constant and lower threshold may depend on its fixed arithmetic data.

primaryStatements.name: Two saturated witnesses
primaryStatements.label: prop:detector-witness
primaryStatements.text: Let \(u\) have a bin \((i,a)\) with \(a>51/100\), and assume the loss and height hypotheses of Lemma \ref{lem:detector-dyads}. For every \(t\in[1,3/2]\), and every prescribed \(\epsilon>0\), after reducing its preliminary losses, there are \(\psi\in\mathcal X_u\), a zero \(\rho=\sigma+i\gamma\) as in Lemma \ref{lem:buffered-bins}, dyadic lengths \(D=U^r\), \(N=U^m\), and two polynomials \(M_r,S_m\) for the common row character \(\psi\) such that \begin{equation} r\le t+O(1/\log U),\qquad r+m\ge t-O(1/\log U),\qquad |M_rS_m|^2\gg_{\mathcal A,\epsilon} U^{\delta(r+m)-\epsilon}. \end{equation} Their lengths and individual values also satisfy \begin{equation} \begin{gathered} t-\tfrac12-O(\epsilon)\le r\le t+O(1/\log U), \qquad 0\le m\le\tfrac12+O(\epsilon),\\ |M_r|^2\gg_{\mathcal A,\epsilon}U^{\delta r-\epsilon}, \qquad |S_m|^2\gg_{\mathcal A,\epsilon}U^{\delta m-\epsilon}. \end{gathered} \end{equation} The constants in the \(O(\epsilon)\) terms are absolute on the stated parameter ranges. Both polynomials have the same twist height \(\gamma-\nu\), where \(|\nu|\le cT_1\) for a fixed \(c>0\) chosen within the cumulative frequency allowance. Their untwisted profiles form a uniformly smooth annular family. For each row, both witnesses use one presentation \(\psi_{u,\vartheta,\varsigma}\), selected by a label \((\vartheta,\varsigma)\) in the fixed finite set \(\Theta\times\{-1,1\}\). The presentation itself varies with \(u\). The dyadic pair can likewise be selected separately for each row from \(O((\log U)^2)\) possibilities.

primaryStatements.name: Sextic-sieve row envelope
primaryStatements.label: prop:sextic-row-count
primaryStatements.text: Fix the arithmetic data $\mathcal A$, the bounded physical range $d_{\min}\le d\le d_{\max}$, and the height and loss hypotheses of Lemmas \ref{lem:buffered-bins} and \ref{lem:detector-dyads}. Put $U=Z^d$ and retain the notation $T_1$ of those lemmas. Let $\mathcal B$ be any set of retained sixth-power-free element rows $u$ with $q_u\asymp U$, all in one bin $(i,a)$ with $a>51/100$. Put $\delta=2a-1$, so $1/50<\delta\le1$. For every $\epsilon>0$, after reducing the preliminary losses in Proposition \ref{prop:detector-witness}, for all sufficiently large $Z$, \begin{equation} \#\mathcal B\ll_{\mathcal A,\epsilon} U^{R(\delta)+\epsilon}(1+T_1)^{A_{\mathcal A}}, \qquad R(\delta)=\min\left\{1, \max\left(1-\frac\delta2,\frac43-\delta\right)\right\}. \end{equation} The finite order $A_{\mathcal A}$ is uniform in the physical dyad, the bin, and all moving rows. It may be fixed before the positive exponent in $T_1=Z^\tau$ is chosen. The estimate is valid for each fixed retained tuple of external parameters and for the original row restrictions. The implied constant may depend on the fixed comparison constants and finitely many of the shared profile seminorms. The rowwise profile choices are precisely those permitted by Proposition \ref{prop:detector-witness} and Lemma \ref{lem:smooth-calculus}; no arbitrary row-dependent coefficients are allowed. The floor bin $a=51/100$ is excluded from the witness assertion. For that bin the elementary bound $\#\mathcal B\ll_{\mathcal A}U$ applies; it agrees with the numerical value $R(1/50)=1$.

definitions.name: An unmarked reflected block
definitions.label: def:unmarked-reflected-block
definitions.text: Fix $Z\ge2$, $X=Z^N$, one of the fixed characters $\Psi_0$ and its common modulus $L$ from Proposition \ref{prop:completed-reflection}, and put $M_{\rm ref}=\lambda^{12}L^4$. For the current norm over $R$, freeze a finite set $\mathcal F$ of good primes with exponents $j_p\in\{0,\ldots,5\}$. Let $R$ range over squarefree primary good ideals coprime to every prime of $\mathcal F$, in one fixed class modulo $M_{\rm ref}^2$ and with any further fixed row restrictions. These restrictions are independent of the dual variables. On primary elements prime to $S$ set \[ \Psi_R(A)=\Psi_0(A)\prod_{p\in\mathcal F}\chi_p(A)^{j_p} \prod_{p\mid R}\chi_p(A). \] Every local power retains its zero. In the reflection for $\Psi_R$, fix $h_0$, the active or inactive decision at every $j_p=0$ prime of $\mathcal F$, and one of the two summands of every $j_p=4$ Ramanujan factor. All primes of $R$ are active and have exponent one. Let $F_{\rm act}$ be the product of the active primes in $\mathcal F$. For each chosen divisibility summand at $j_p=4$, use the exact partition \[ 1_{p\mid n_0b_0^3}=1_{p\mid n_0}+1_{p\nmid n_0}1_{p\mid b_0}. \] Choose one term. Let $N_F$ be the product of the primes assigned to the squarefree ideal $n_0$, and let $B_F$ be the product assigned to $b_0$ but not $n_0$. Write $n_0=N_Fn$ and $b_0=B_Fb$. In the first assignment only the occurrence in $n_0$ is extracted, even if $b_0$ contains that prime; in the second exactly one occurrence is extracted from $b_0$. All remaining source restrictions are retained on $n,b$. Let $F_{\rm sm}$ be the product of the small $j_p=4$ summands and the active $j_p=0$ primes, and put \[ A_0=\log_Zq_{F_{\rm act}},\qquad S_0=\log_Zq_{F_{\rm sm}},\qquad N_0=\log_Zq_{N_F},\qquad B_0=\log_Zq_{B_F}. \] Empty products have log-norm zero. Fix a unit $u$, an integer $k\ge-4$, and dual ranges \[ \mu=u\lambda^kN_Fn(B_Fb)^3,\qquad q_n\asymp Z^v,\quad q_b\asymp Z^{\ell_b},\quad q_{\lambda^k}=Z^{e_\lambda}, \] where $v,\ell_b\ge0$. The squarefree $n$ and the primary $b$ retain the full source support of Equation \eqref{old-eq:4.3}, including permitted primes of $S$ and shared primes. Let $H\ge0$, and choose a common smooth profile $W_1(y_R,y_n,y_b)$ on a fixed compact logarithmic box, where \[ y_R=q_R/Z^H,\qquad y_n=q_n/Z^v,\qquad y_b=q_b/Z^{\ell_b}. \] Choose fixed smooth annular cutoffs $\chi_{\rm row},\chi_n,\chi_b$ for these three ranges, and put \[ W_0(\boldsymbol y)=\chi_{\rm row}(y_R)\chi_n(y_n)\chi_b(y_b)W_1(\boldsymbol y). \] The supports and invoked seminorms are fixed uniformly over the block. Denote by $\mathcal U_{v,\ell_b,e_\lambda}(R)$ the specified term of the right side of Equation \eqref{eq:reflection}, restricted to this dual representation and multiplied by $W_0(y_R,y_n,y_b)$. The original row set $\mathcal I_H$ consists of the allowed $R$ for which $\chi_{\rm row}(q_R/Z^H)\ne0$. This definition is made separately for every fixed choice above.

definitions.name: Data for an exact high representation
definitions.label: def:stage-high-data
definitions.text: Fix real numbers $l_x,l_y>0$ and $\ell\ge0$ such that \begin{equation} X=Z^{l_x},\qquad Y=Z^{l_y},\qquad h=1-l_x+\ell>0, \qquad C(s)=s+\frac{l_x}{2}-1+\frac h6 =s-\frac56+\frac{l_x}{3}+\frac\ell6. \end{equation} These real numbers are fixed before the target character. For each primitive finite-order target $\eta$, fix the data $S,\xi,W_0,W_1$ of Section \ref{sec:probe}, independently of $Z$. Data for an exact high representation consist of the following objects and assertions. First, $\mathscr I_\eta(Z)$ is an independently specified complex-valued quantity for every sufficiently large real $Z$. In each application it is given by a finite linear combination, for that $Z$, of the completed sums in Equation \eqref{eq:general-probe}, allowing specified restrictions on the completed index $A$ and specified rescalings of its three positive scales. The number of terms and coefficients in this finite combination may depend on $Z$. Any direct estimate for $\mathscr I_\eta$ refers to this expression, not to a separately defined high integral. Second, for every nonzero sixth-power-free element $u$ with $(u,S)=1$ and every such $Z$, there is a function $\mathfrak H_{\eta,u,Z}(s,w,z)$. It is holomorphic on a neighborhood of each point of $\mathcal D_2$ and of every $\mathcal D_1(\epsilon_0)$. For every $D>0$ and every real box $\mathcal K$ contained in one of these regions, there are finite constants $B_{\eta,\mathcal K,D}$ and $J_{\eta,\mathcal K,D}$ such that, uniformly for $1\le q_u\le Z^D$, all imaginary parts, and real parts in $\mathcal K$, \begin{equation} |\mathfrak H_{\eta,u,Z}(s,w,z)| \ll_{\eta,\mathcal K,D} Z^{B_{\eta,\mathcal K,D}} (1+|\Im s|+|\Im w|+|\Im z|)^{J_{\eta,\mathcal K,D}}. \end{equation} The constants and exponents are independent of $Z,u$ and of any later order of integration by parts. No nonvanishing of $\mathfrak H$ or of any of its local factors is assumed. Finally, the following identity is asserted for the independently given $\mathscr I_\eta(Z)$, with absolute convergence of the sum and integrals on the displayed lines: \begin{equation} \begin{split} \mathscr I_\eta(Z)=\frac1{(2\pi i)^3} \int_{(3)}\int_{(3)}\int_{(2)} &\mathcal W(X,Y,Z;s,w,z) \sum_u^{(6)}q_u^{-z}\overline{\xi(u)}\\ &\cdot \frac{\zeta_F^S(6z)L^S(w,\chi_\bullet(u))} {L^S(s,\eta\overline{\chi_\bullet(u)})} \mathfrak H_{\eta,u,Z}(s,w,z)\,dz\,dw\,ds, \end{split} \end{equation} where the sum has the physical restrictions of Equation \eqref{eq:probe-poisson-identity}, and \[ \mathcal W(X,Y,Z;s,w,z) =X^{1/2-z}Z^{s+z-1}Y^{w-1} e^{(s+z-1)^2}M(z)\widehat W_1(w). \] Thus Equation \eqref{eq:stage-high-identity} is a hypothesis to be proved for the physical expression, not its definition.

lean.scopeText:
The quasi-Riemann hypothesis asks for a fixed zero-free half-plane $\Re s>\theta$ with $\theta<1$. The formalization gives $\theta=7/8$ for the Riemann zeta function and every Dirichlet $L$-function, uniformly over all positive moduli and all characters. It also establishes the same bound for finite-order Hecke $L$-functions over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$.

The principal-character poles at $s=1$ are excluded in the Dirichlet and Hecke statements. The paper's later applications are not included.

The formalized result gives a uniform logarithmic exclusion region for Landau–Siegel zeros. There is one constant $c>0$ such that every primitive nonprincipal real Dirichlet character of conductor $q\ge3$ and every real zero $0<\beta<1$ of its $L$-function satisfy $1-\beta\ge c/\log q$.

Both character parities are included. No explicit value of $c$ is given. This excludes real zeros in $1-c/\log q<\beta<1$, but does not rule out real zeros elsewhere in $(0,1)$.

papers.title: The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis (alternate 11/12 proof)
papers.abstract: We establish the quasi-Riemann hypothesis by proving that every Dirichlet L-function, including Riemann's zeta function, has no zeros in the half-plane $\mathop{\mathrm{Re}}\nolimits s\gt 11/12$. More generally, we prove the same zero-free half-plane for every finite-order Hecke L-function over $K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$. In particular, this rules out the existence of Landau–Siegel zeros.

The same half-plane is zero-free for every finite-order Hecke L-function over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$. A companion gives a different proof of the zero-free half-plane $\Re s\gt 11/12$.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Every finite-order Hecke $L$-function over $K$ has no zeros in the half-plane $\Rea s>11/12$. Thus every Dirichlet $L$-function, including $\zeta(s)$, has no zeros for $\Rea s>11/12$.

primaryStatements.label: cor:primes-ap
primaryStatements.text: Let $\pi(x;q,a)$ count the primes $p\le x$ with $p\equiv a\pmod q$. Write $\varphi$ for Euler's totient function. For $x\ge2$, \[ \sup_{\substack{1\le q\le x\\(a,q)=1}} \biggl|\pi(x;q,a)-\frac1{\varphi(q)} \int_2^x\frac{\dd t}{\log t}\biggr| \ll x^{11/12}\log x, \] where the implied constant is absolute and effective.

primaryStatements.label: thm:ms
primaryStatements.text: For every fixed $0<\vartheta\le1/10$ and $\varepsilon>0$, there exists an integer $k=k(\vartheta,\varepsilon)\ge1$ such that, for every compact interval $I\subset(0,\infty)$, all smooth $W$ supported in $I$, and $D\ge2$, \begin{equation} \sum_{0<\NK(u)\le D^{1+\vartheta}}|A_u(D)|^2 \ll_{\nu,S,I,\vartheta,\varepsilon} \Bigl(\max_{0\le j\le k}\|W^{(j)}\|_\infty\Bigr)^2 D^{2+\vartheta+\varepsilon}. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.label: prop:poisson-reduction
primaryStatements.text: Fix $0<\vartheta\le1/10$ and put $H=D^{1+\vartheta}$. For each fixed $C\ge1$ and all real $B,F\ge1$, consider the ranges \begin{equation} X=\frac D{BF},\qquad 0<\mathcal{H}\le\frac{CD^2}{HB^2},\qquad XF=\frac DB. \end{equation} Suppose that for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists an integer $J=J(\vartheta,\varepsilon)\ge1$ such that, for every compact interval $I\subset(0,\infty)$ and every smooth $W$ supported in $I$, \begin{equation} \E(\mathcal H,X,F;\xi,W) \ll_{\nu,S,I,C,\vartheta,\varepsilon}\|W\|_{C^J(I)}^2D^\varepsilon XF, \end{equation} where \[ \|W\|_{C^J(I)}=\max_{0\le j\le J}\sup_{x\in I}|W^{(j)}(x)|. \] For functions of several variables, the norm uses all partial derivatives of total order at most $J$. Then the original mean-square estimate in Proposition \ref{thm:ms} holds.

primaryStatements.label: prop:canonical
primaryStatements.text: Fix $\kappa>0$ and $C_0\ge1$. Suppose that \begin{equation} \mathcal H,X,F\ge1,\qquad \Sigma=XF\le D^{C_0},\qquad \mathcal H\le\Sigma D^{-\kappa}. \end{equation} For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is an integer $J=J(\kappa,C_0,\varepsilon)\ge1$ such that \begin{equation} \E(\mathcal H,X,F;\xi,W) \ll_{I,\nu,S,\kappa,C_0,\varepsilon} \|W\|_{C^J(I)}^2D^\varepsilon\Sigma \end{equation} for every compact interval $I\subset(0,\infty)$ and smooth $W$ supported in $I$.

primaryStatements.label: prop:R
primaryStatements.text: Fix $\varepsilon>0$, $C_0\ge1$, and a character $\xi$ of the fixed ray class group. There is $J=J(\varepsilon,C_0)\ge1$ such that \begin{equation} \sum_{0<\NK(k)\ll\mathcal H}|T(X;k,f)|^2 \ll_{I,\xi,S,\varepsilon,C_0} D^\varepsilon\|W\|_{C^J(I)}^2 \Bigl(\mathcal H+\frac{\mathcal H^2\NK(f)}{X}\Bigr) \end{equation} whenever \[ 1\le\mathcal H,X,\NK(f)\le D^{C_0}. \] Here $f$ is squarefree and primary with $(f,S)=1$, $W$ is smooth and supported in a compact interval $I\subset(0,\infty)$, and $T$ is defined by \eqref{eq:completed-twist}.

primaryStatements.label: prop:transfer
primaryStatements.text: Assume $1\le\mathcal H,L,F,\Sigma\le D^{C_0}$ and $\max\{\mathcal H,LF\}\le\Sigma$, for fixed $C_0\ge1$. For every integer $m\ge0$ and $\varepsilon>0$, \begin{equation} \mathcal A(W)\ll D^\varepsilon\Sigma\|W\|_{C^{4m+12}(I)}^2 \Bigl(1+\sup\frac{\E(\mathcal H',X',F';\xi',U)}{\Sigma'}\Bigr) \end{equation} where the supremum is over the family \eqref{eq:energy}, with $\Sigma'=X'F'$, $\mathcal H',X',F'\ge1$, and \begin{equation} \mathcal H'\le\frac{\mathcal HL}{\Sigma F},\qquad \frac{\mathcal H'}{\Sigma'}\le \frac{\mathcal H}{\Sigma},\qquad \Sigma'\le L. \end{equation} For $I=[u,v]$, the tests satisfy $U\in C_c^\infty(I')$, $I'=[u/16,4v]$, and $\|U\|_{C^m(I')}\le1$; an empty supremum is zero. The estimate holds for every compact $I\subset(0,\infty)$ and $W\in C_c^\infty(I)$, with implied constant depending on $m,C_0,\varepsilon,I,\nu,S$ and the fixed ray class group.

primaryStatements.label: lem:reflection
primaryStatements.text: The quantity $T(X;\Psi)$ defined in \eqref{eq:T} is a sum of $O_{\Psi_0,S}(2^{|\mathcal P|})$ terms of the form \begin{equation} C\sum_{0\ne\ell\in\lambda^{-4}\OO} \frac{d(\ell)\alpha(\ell)}{\sqrt{\NK(\ell)}}\, \psi(\lambda^4\ell) \prod_{p\in\mathcal A}B_{p,j_p}(\lambda^4\ell) V_*^\sharp\!\Bigl(\frac{\NK(\ell) X}{\NK(c)^2}\Bigr). \end{equation} Here $\mathcal A$ and $c$ are as above, and $|C|\ll_{\Psi_0,S}1$. The triples $(d,\psi,c_0)$ belong to a fixed finite family depending only on $\Psi_0,S$, where $d\in\{d_0,d_+,d_-\}$, $c_0\in\OO\setminus\{0\}$, and $\psi$ is a unit-modulus additive character on $\OO$.

definitions.label: eq:energy
definitions.text: The parameters $\mathcal H$, $X$, and $F$ are the norm scales of $k$, $n$, and $f$, respectively. Here $k$ ranges over elements of $\OO$, and a star restricts a sum to squarefree ideals prime to $S$, represented by their primary generators. For a smooth compactly supported weight $W$ on $(0,\infty)$, define the dual mean square by \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} &\E(\mathcal{H},X,F;\xi,W)\\ &\qquad=\frac1{XF} \sum_{\substack{F\le\NK(f)<2F\\(f,S)=1}}^*\sum_{0<\NK(k)\le \mathcal{H}} \Bigl|\sum_{(n,S)=1}^*a_\xi(n)\chi_n(k)\chi_n(f)^4 W(\NK(n)/X)\Bigr|^2. \end{aligned} \end{equation}

papers.title: Uniform exclusion of Landau–Siegel zeros
papers.abstract: We prove the uniform exclusion of Landau–Siegel zeros. There is an absolute constant c > 0 such that every real zero $\beta\in(0,1)$ of every primitive nonprincipal real Dirichlet L-function of conductor q ≥ 3 satisfies $(1-\beta)\log q\ge c$.

The same half-plane is zero-free for every finite-order Hecke L-function over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$. A companion gives a different proof of the zero-free half-plane $\Re s\gt 11/12$.

For integers $1\le H\le N$, set \[ U=N^{4/3},\qquad T_1=32H^{2/3}U, \qquad T_2=T_3=32H^{-1/3}U. \] The rows $((An)_1^{\alpha_1}(An)_2^{\alpha_2}(An)_3^{\alpha_3})_{n\in E_N}$, with $\alpha\in\N^3$ and $\alpha_j\le T_j$, span $\C^{E_N}$. lean.scopeText:
The quasi-Riemann hypothesis asks for a fixed zero-free half-plane $\Re s>\theta$ with $\theta<1$. The formalization gives $\theta=7/8$ for the Riemann zeta function and every Dirichlet $L$-function, uniformly over all positive moduli and all characters. It also establishes the same bound for finite-order Hecke $L$-functions over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$.

The principal-character poles at $s=1$ are excluded in the Dirichlet and Hecke statements. The paper's later applications are not included.

The formalized result gives a uniform logarithmic exclusion region for Landau–Siegel zeros. There is one constant $c>0$ such that every primitive nonprincipal real Dirichlet character of conductor $q\ge3$ and every real zero $0<\beta<1$ of its $L$-function satisfy $1-\beta\ge c/\log q$.

Both character parities are included. No explicit value of $c$ is given. This excludes real zeros in $1-c/\log q<\beta<1$, but does not rule out real zeros elsewhere in $(0,1)$.

primaryStatements.name: Five-point height estimate
primaryStatements.label: hei:height
primaryStatements.text: There exist five distinct points $\mathcal C\subset\mathbf P^1(\Q)$, including $\infty$, a finite set $S$ of rational primes, and constants $H,c>0$ with the following property. For each $b\in\mathcal C$, choose a primitive integral linear form $L_b(U,V)$ vanishing at $b$, with $L_\infty(U,V)=V$. For $s=(u:v)\in\mathbf P^1(\Q)\setminus\mathcal C$, let $M_S(s)$ be the product, taken without repetition, of primes $q\notin S$ for which at least one of the integers \begin{equation} v_q(L_b(u,v))-\min\{v_q(u),v_q(v)\},\qquad b\in\mathcal C, \end{equation} is odd. Here $v_q(q)=1$ and $v_q(0)=+\infty$. Then \begin{equation} \hgt(s)\le H M_S(s)^c. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.label: hei:enlarge-exceptions
primaryStatements.text: If $S'\supset S$ is any fixed finite set of primes, then \[ \hgt(s)\le H\left(\prod_{q\in S'\setminus S}q\right)^c M_{S'}(s)^c \qquad(s\in\mathbf P^1(\Q)\setminus\mathcal C). \] In particular enlarging the exceptional set changes the constant but leaves the exponent unchanged.

primaryStatements.name: Ordinary contact representations
primaryStatements.label: pri:integer-coverage
primaryStatements.text: Let \(\mathcal K\subset\Z_{>0}\) be the finite multiplier set supplied by Lemma \ref{pri:pattern} in Section \ref{pri:section}. It has the following property. For every integer \(K\ge1\), every \(A\in\Z\), and every real lower bound \(Y_0>0\), there exist integers \(u_1,u_2,v\), with \(v\ne0\), such that, on setting \(u_3=Av-u_1-u_2\), the following hold. \begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*),leftmargin=*] \item \textup{Representation and primes.} Each of the thirteen numbers \begin{equation} v,\qquad L_b(u_i,v) \quad(1\le i\le3,\ b\in\mathcal C\setminus\{\infty\}) \end{equation} equals \(\varepsilon k r\), where \(\varepsilon\in\{1,-1\}\), \(k\in\mathcal K\), and \(r>Y_0\) is a positive rational prime. Every such \(r\) splits in \(F\), is a prime of good reduction for both \(E\) and \(E^\sigma\), lies outside \(S_E\), and satisfies \(r>K+1\). \item \textup{Witnesses at each place.} For each occurrence of a prime \(r\) in this list and each of the two places \(v_r\) of \(F\) above it, there are nonzero integers \(h,j_0\), chosen independently of \(a\in\Z\), such that every \(a\in\Z\) satisfies conditions (i) and (ii) of Lemma \ref{red:local-comparison} in the ordinary setting: take \(R=\Z\), its identity embedding in the ordinary structure, \(T_a=aP\), \(q=r\), and \(v_*=v_r\), normalized by \(v_r(r)=1\). In this specialization the tildes disappear. The choices of \(h,j_0\) may differ at different occurrences and at the two places. \end{enumerate} The set \(\mathcal K\) is independent of \(K,A,Y_0\).

primaryStatements.label: par:pole-parity
primaryStatements.text: There are a positive existential formula $\Phi(b)$ in the language of rings, with fixed rational coefficients, and a finite set $S_1$ of rational primes such that: \begin{enumerate} \item $\Q\models\Phi(b)$ for every $b\in\Z$; \item if $b\in\Q^\times$ and $\Q\models\Phi(b)$, then, for every $q\notin S_1$, the inequality $v_q(b)<0$ implies $v_q(b)\in2\Z$. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.label: red:index-congruence
primaryStatements.text: Fix an ordinary \(K\ge1\) and use the exceptional set \(S_K\) above. Choose a representation supplied at precision \(K\) for an arbitrary \(A\in R\), and put \(\widetilde s_i=(\widetilde u_i:\widetilde v)\). For every prime \(q\) of \({}^*\Z\) counted by any \(M_K(\widetilde s_i)\), and every \(a\in R\), the element \(\widetilde a\) is integral at \(q\) and \begin{equation} v_q(\widetilde a-\eta(a))\ge K. \end{equation}

papers.title: A pointwise 2-converse for elliptic curves with rational two-torsion
papers.abstract: We prove a pointwise 2-converse for elliptic curves over $\mathbf Q$ with nonzero rational two-torsion: if the $2^\infty$-Selmer corank is zero or one, then the analytic rank and Mordell–Weil rank equal that corank, and the Shafarevich–Tate group is finite. primaryStatements.label: cy:central

primaryStatements.label: rd:missing-vertex

primaryStatements.label: rl:characters

primaryStatements.name: Integral evaluation through the outer limit
primaryStatements.label: rl:outer-evaluation
primaryStatements.text: Let $C_j$ be any family of the preceding limiting complexes, completed over $\mathcal O_j=\widehat{\Lambda_{(2)}}$, possibly for different quadratic fields $K_j$. Suppose their minimal ranks are bounded. Keep their actual evaluation matrices, and transport them through the integral contractions to these minimal models. For a nonprincipal ultrafilter $\mathcal U$, put \[ \mathcal O_\infty= \left(\prod_{\mathcal U}\mathcal O_j\right)/\mathfrak a, \qquad \mathfrak a=\{(x_j): \{j:v_2(x_j)\geq n\}\in\mathcal U\text{ for every }n\}. \] Then $\mathcal O_\infty$ is a DVR with uniformizer $2$ and a characteristic-zero fraction field $L_\infty$. The outer complex has an injection of its $H^1$ over $L_\infty$ into crossed classes on the product of the inner sequence groups. Its restriction to the product of their exact common kernels is injective. All arbitrary-sequence degree-two evaluation identities survive. definitions.text: A witness is a finite graph on which the symbol is $1$. A graph is partitionable for the symbol if its vertices can be partitioned into nonempty clusters, each with at most one simple vertex, with a choice of oriented contraction trees whose contracted graph is a witness. papers.title: Goldfeld's analytic density conjecture and the 2-converse for elliptic curves
papers.abstract: We prove Goldfeld's analytic density conjecture: for every elliptic curve E over ℚ, the quadratic twists of E with analytic rank zero and one each have density 1/2 among signed squarefree twist parameters ordered by absolute value. We also prove the low-corank 2-converse: if the $2^\infty$-Selmer corank of E is zero or one, then it equals the analytic and Mordell–Weil ranks, and the Tate–Shafarevich group is finite.

primaryStatements.name: The $2$-converse
primaryStatements.label: thm:main-converse
primaryStatements.text: For every elliptic curve $E/\Q$ with $c_2(E)\in\{0,1\}$, \[ a(E)=r(E)=c_2(E),\qquad \Sha(E/\Q)\text{ is finite}. \]

primaryStatements.name: Goldfeld's analytic density conjecture
primaryStatements.label: thm:main-density
primaryStatements.text: For every elliptic curve $E/\Q$ and each $j\in\{0,1\}$, \[ \lim_{X\to\infty} \frac{\#\{d\in\mathcal D(X):a(E^{(d)})=j\}}{\#\mathcal D(X)} =\frac12. \] Consequently the twists of analytic rank at least two have density zero. For a density-one set of signed squarefree parameters $d$, the analytic and Mordell--Weil ranks of $E^{(d)}$ agree and its whole Tate--Shafarevich group is finite.

primaryStatements.name: A finite Selmer criterion
primaryStatements.label: cor:finite-descent
primaryStatements.text: If $d_2(E)\in\{0,1\}$, then \[ a(E)=r(E)=c_2(E)=d_2(E),\qquad \Sha(E/\Q)\text{ is finite},\qquad \Sha(E/\Q)[2^\infty]=0. \]

primaryStatements.name: Cyclotomic missing vertex
primaryStatements.label: thm:cyclotomic-interpolation
primaryStatements.text:
There is a constant $C_E$, depending only on $E$, with the following property. Fix an odd fundamental discriminant $h_0$, prime to $2N$, with $c_2(E^{(h_0)})=0$. Suppose that for arbitrarily large $b$ there is a family  egin{equation} h_x=h_0\prod_{q\in\mathcal Q}(q^*)^{\lambda_q(x)}, \qquad x\in\F_2^b,\qquad \lambda_q\in(\F_2^b)^*, \end{equation} where $\mathcal Q$ consists of distinct primes outside $2Nh_0$, $q^*=(-1/q)q$, and every $h_x$ has the same sign and the same local squareclasses at $2N$. Assume that a constant $B$, independent of $b$, satisfies  egin{equation} L(E^{(h_x)},1)
e0,\qquad D(h_x)\le B\qquad(x
e0). \end{equation} If $E[2]$ is irreducible, assume also that some $L$, independent of $b$, satisfies  egin{equation} v_2(q^2-1)\le L\qquad(q\in\mathcal Q). \end{equation} Then $L(E^{(h_0)},1)
e0$ and  egin{equation} D(h_0)\le B+C_E. \end{equation} The necessary dimension may depend on $h_0$, its finite Selmer group, and the bound in Equation \eqref{eq:cy:prime-bound}; $C_E$ does not.

primaryStatements.name: Comparison of the two Heegner constructions
primaryStatements.label: prop:heegner-comparison
primaryStatements.text: For either set of data, \begin{equation} \widehat h(P_c(e)) =C_E\,c\sqrt{|k|}\, \left[L(E^{(e)},s)L(E^{(ek)},s)\right]'_{s=1}, \end{equation} with a fixed nonzero constant determined by the parametrization and height conventions. In particular, a simple zero of the product gives total Mordell--Weil rank one and finite Shafarevich--Tate groups. Suppose $h$ has analytic rank one, and use genus data with a fixed partner $h_*$ of analytic rank zero and ring data with a possibly varying $k$, where $L(E^{(hk)},1)\ne0$. Then \begin{equation} 2j(P_{|h|}(h))-2j(P_1(h_*)) =v(\mathcal L(hk))+O_{E,h_*}(1). \end{equation} Here the two points are formed in their respective quadratic fields. If instead $h_*$ has analytic rank one and $L(E^{(h)},1)\ne0$, genus data give \begin{equation} 2j(P_1(h_*))=v(\mathcal L(h))+O_{E,h_*}(1). \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Heegner interpolation
primaryStatements.label: thm:heegner-interpolation
primaryStatements.text: Fix $E$ and an initial discriminant $h_0$. Consider families $h_x$, $x\in\F_2^b$, obtained from $h_0$ by adjoining new prime factors with linear activation functions on $\F_2^b$. No old factor is removed; the signed factor belonging to an odd prime $q$ is $q^*=(-1/q)q$. Suppose the local twisting classes at $2N$ are constant. For each family let $k$ define an imaginary field satisfying the standing Heegner conditions, with $(k,h_x)=1$ for every $x$. Each new prime must either split in $K$ or satisfy $t_q=0$. Assume that the following bounds are fixed independently of $b$: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item a bound for $\omega(k)$; \item a bound for the length of the finite quotient of $\Sel_{2^\infty}(E^{(h_0)}/K)$ by its divisible subgroup; \item a constant $B$. \end{enumerate} Assume this base Selmer group has corank one. Suppose, for every $x\ne0$, the product $L(E^{(h_x)},s)L(E^{(h_xk)},s)$ has a simple zero and \begin{equation} 2j(P_{|h_x|}(h_x))-4w(h_x)-s(h_x)-s(h_xk)\le B. \end{equation} Then, for sufficiently large $b$, the base product has a simple zero. The dimension threshold depends only on the fixed base and the displayed bounds, not on the number or sizes of the new primes. The field $K$ may vary with the family.

primaryStatements.name: Cyclotomic lower bound
primaryStatements.label: thm:cyclotomic-bound
primaryStatements.text: Suppose that $E[2]$ is an extension of two trivial $\F_2$-modules. There is a constant $C_E$ such that every odd fundamental discriminant $h$ prime to $2N$ with $L(E^{(h)},1)\ne0$ satisfies \begin{equation} v(\mathcal L(h))\ge 2w(h)+s(h)-C_E. \end{equation} The constant is independent of the number and sizes of the primes that divide $h$.

primaryStatements.name: Genus bound
primaryStatements.label: thm:heegner-genus-bound
primaryStatements.text: In genus data, suppose the product in Equation \eqref{eq:h:height} has a simple zero and $E[2]$ is irreducible. Then, uniformly in $h$, \begin{equation} 2j(P_1(h_*))\ge 2w(h)+s(h)-O_{E,h_*}(1). \end{equation} In proving the uniform estimate, one may omit the finitely many $h$ for which $K$ meets $\Q(E[2])$ nontrivially.

definitions.name: Witnesses and permitted partitions
definitions.label: gr:partitionable
definitions.text: A witness is a finite graph with symbol $1$. A graph is partitionable if it admits a partition into nonempty clusters, each containing at most one simple vertex, and oriented contraction trees whose contracted graph is a witness. The contraction trees are part of the data; this definition makes no assertion about a Selmer group.

definitions.label: def:h:determinant-coordinate
definitions.text: Choose an integral basis of $\det^{-1}_{\Lambda}C$. In generic rank one, the element formed by $P$ in $H^1$ and the functional $\langle P,\cdot\rangle$ on $H^2$ determines a scalar $u(C,P)\in\operatorname{Frac}(\Lambda)$ in that basis. Put $u=0$ if $P=0$ or the generic rank is zero. Integral changes of determinant basis multiply $u$ by a unit.

primaryStatements.name: Independent-model estimates for the weight pieces
primaryStatements.label: model:main-model-estimates
primaryStatements.text: With the weights and sums $S_{j,Z}(x)$ defined in Section \ref{sec:weights}, there is a fixed exponent $C_5$ such that \begin{align} \|H_0(Z)S_{0,Z}(x)-A_x\|_2&\ll k^{-1}, \\ \|H_j(Z)S_{j,Z}(x)\|_2&\ll(k2^j)^{C_5}\delta_j^k \qquad(1\le j\le J). \end{align} These bounds are uniform in $x\in\mathcal X$ and over the entire range $k_0\le k\le\ell^{3/5}$, with one fixed $k_0$ and one sufficiently large $X$ threshold.

primaryStatements.label: thm:mean
primaryStatements.text: For every elliptic curve \(E/\Q\), \[ \lim_{Y\to\infty}\frac{1}{\#\mathcal D(Y)} \sum_{d\in\mathcal D(Y)}a(E^{(d)})=\frac12. \]

primaryStatements.label: thm:tail
primaryStatements.text: For every elliptic curve \(E/\Q\), there are constants \(C_E>0\) and an integer \(R_E\ge1\) such that, for every integer \(R\ge R_E\), \[ \limsup_{Y\to\infty}\frac1Y \sum_{\substack{d\in\mathcal D(Y)\\a(E^{(d)})>R}}a(E^{(d)}) \le \frac{C_E}{R}. \]

primaryStatements.name: Fixed algebraic-rank moments
primaryStatements.label: cor:algebraic-moments
primaryStatements.text: Fix an elliptic curve \(E/\Q\). For every fixed real \(t\), \[ \lim_{Y\to\infty}\frac1{\#\mathcal D(Y)} \sum_{d\in\mathcal D(Y)}\exp\!\bigl(t\,r(E^{(d)})\bigr) =\frac{1+e^t}{2}. \] For every fixed positive integer \(m\), \[ \lim_{Y\to\infty}\frac1{\#\mathcal D(Y)} \sum_{d\in\mathcal D(Y)}r(E^{(d)})^m=\frac12. \]

primaryStatements.name: Logarithmic second moments
primaryStatements.label: analytic:moment
primaryStatements.text: There are fixed positive integers $A,B$ such that, for every dyadic $M\geq1$, every $F\in\mathcal F$, every $t\in\mathbb R$, and $1/2\leq\sigma\leq2$, \begin{equation} \frac1M\sum_{\substack{d\ \mathrm{admissible}\\M\leq|d|<2M}} |L_{F^{(d)}}(\sigma+it)|^2 \ll_{\mathcal F}\log^B(3M)(1+|t|)^A. \end{equation} For arbitrary signed squarefree twisting parameters and $H\geq1$, \begin{equation} \sum_{\substack{0<|h|\leq H\\h\ \mathrm{squarefree}}} |L_{F^{(h)}}(\sigma+it)|^2 \ll_{\mathcal F}H\log^B(3H)(1+|t|)^A. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Dirichlet-polynomial second moments
primaryStatements.label: analytic:polynomial-moment
primaryStatements.text: With the same fixed integers $A,B$, every fixed smooth $G$ of compact support in $(0,\infty)$ satisfies \begin{equation} \frac1M\sum_{\substack{d\ \mathrm{admissible}\\M\leq|d|<2M}} |P_d(N,t;G)|^2 \ll_{\mathcal F,G} \log^B(3M)(1+|t|)^A(1+N/M)^A \qquad(N>0). \end{equation} The bound is uniform for fixed uniformly smooth families of weights with common compact support.

primaryStatements.name: Comparison with the independent model
primaryStatements.label: analytic:comparison
primaryStatements.text: Let $\ell=\log X$, where $X$ is sufficiently large, and let \[ c_1\ell^{-1/10}\leq\Delta\leq\frac12 \] for a fixed $c_1>0$. There are fixed constants $\eta,c_2>0$ for which the following holds. Let \[ S_V(x)=\sum_{n\geq1}\frac{\lambda_F(n)V(n)}{\sqrt n}\, w_x(\ell^{-1}\log n),\qquad H_V=\sum_{r'\leq R_0}h(r')V(r'), \] where $V=z_m$ or $Z$. Suppose that $S_V$ has length at most $X^{1-\Delta}$, that \begin{equation} 1\leq R_0\leq X^{\eta\Delta},\qquad \sum_{r'\leq R_0}|h(r')|\leq C_H R_0^2, \end{equation} and that $w_x$ and a function $A(x)$ have bounds by a fixed power of $\ell$ for all derivatives up to a sufficiently large fixed order. For $w_x$ these bounds are required after smooth dyadic localization in $n$, on the scaled variables $n/N$ and $x$ in a fixed neighborhood of $\operatorname{supp}\Psi$. They may in particular follow from bounds in $u=\ell^{-1}\log n\geq0$ and $x$, with a smooth extension at $n=1$. Then \begin{align} &\frac1X\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}\Psi(m/X) |H_{z_m}S_{z_m}(m/X)-A(m/X)|^2 \nonumber\\ &\hspace{8mm}= \int_{\mathbb R}\Psi(x)\, \mathbb E|H_ZS_Z(x)-A(x)|^2\,dx +O\big(\exp(-c_2\Delta\ell)\big). \end{align} The constants and the sufficiently large $X$ threshold are uniform when the stated support, coefficient, and derivative bounds are uniform. They do not depend on $\Delta$ or on an index parametrizing such weights. One may take \begin{equation} C'=C_{\rm ar}+1=257,\qquad \eta=\frac1{4(4+2C')},\qquad c_2=\frac12. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Comparison interface
primaryStatements.label: weights:comparison-interface
primaryStatements.text: For every fixed derivative order \(r\), the short weights satisfy the smoothness assumptions of Proposition \ref{analytic:comparison} with derivative bounds \(\ell^{C_r}\), uniformly in \(j,k,X\). They have length \(X^{1-\Delta_j}\), with \[ \Delta_j=\delta_j/4,\qquad \tfrac14\ell^{-1/10}\le\Delta_j\le\tfrac14 . \] The deterministic term \begin{equation} s=k/\ell,\qquad A_x=(C_F|x|)^s\Gamma(1+s) \end{equation} has uniformly bounded derivatives of each fixed order on \(\mathcal K\), and is bounded above and below by positive constants. The endpoint enlargement at \(n=1\) can be made inside the fixed range \(n\ge1/2\).

papers.title: Ordinary two-point correlations of multiplicative functions
papers.abstract: We prove the ordinary two-point Chowla conjecture. For every fixed pair of nonproportional affine forms, the Liouville correlation has a power-of-logarithm saving at every cutoff, with an absolute exponent. We also prove the binary corrected Elliott conjecture for ordinary averages of complex multiplicative functions of modulus at most one, under uniform nonpretentiousness of at least one original factor. This qualitative conclusion holds in fixed residue classes and for fixed nonproportional affine forms.
