primaryStatements.name: A logarithmic saving for affine Liouville correlations
primaryStatements.label: thm:q-affine
primaryStatements.text: There is an absolute constant \(c>0\) such that, for every fixed choice of integers \(a_1,a_2\ge1\) and \(b_1,b_2\ge0\) with \(a_1b_2-a_2b_1\ne0\), there is a constant \(C_{a_1,a_2,b_1,b_2}\) for which \[ \left|\sum_{1\le n\le X} \lambda(a_1n+b_1)\lambda(a_2n+b_2)\right| \le C_{a_1,a_2,b_1,b_2}\frac{X}{(\log X)^c} \qquad(X\ge3). \] The cutoff \(X\) may be any real number. No coprimality condition is imposed on the coefficients.

primaryStatements.name: Binary corrected Elliott
primaryStatements.label: thm:elliott
primaryStatements.text: Let \(f_1,f_2:\N\to\mathbb D\) be multiplicative, and suppose that at least one satisfies \eqref{eq:unp}. For every fixed pair of distinct nonnegative integers \(h_1,h_2\), \[ \frac1N\sum_{n=1}^N f_1(n+h_1)f_2(n+h_2)\longrightarrow0 \qquad(N\longrightarrow\infty,\ N\in\N). \]

primaryStatements.name: Affine correlations
primaryStatements.label: cor:affine
primaryStatements.text: Let \(f_1,f_2:\N\to\mathbb D\) be multiplicative, with at least one satisfying \eqref{eq:unp}. For all fixed integers \(a_1,a_2\ge1\) and \(b_1,b_2\ge0\) with \(a_1b_2-a_2b_1\ne0\), \[ \frac1N\sum_{n=1}^N f_1(a_1n+b_1)f_2(a_2n+b_2) \longrightarrow0. \]

primaryStatements.name: Quantitative correlations in every progression
primaryStatements.label: q:progression
primaryStatements.text: There is one absolute \(c>0\) such that, for every fixed \(h,l\ge1\) and \(b\in\Z\), \[ F(X):=\frac1X\sum_{1\le n\le X} \1_{n\equiv b\pmod l}\lambda(n)\lambda(n+h) \ll_{h,l}(\log X)^{-c}\qquad(X\ge3). \] The estimate holds for every real \(X\), with no condition on \(\gcd(b,l)\).

primaryStatements.name: Scalar expansions
primaryStatements.label: q:finite-expansion
primaryStatements.text: Under the hypotheses of \Cref{q:finite-law}, write $\E$ for expectation under $\mu$. Suppose $\Phi=\sum_\alpha c_\alpha\1_{\mathcal E_\alpha}$, where every event has the stated circuit bounds and $\sum_\alpha|c_\alpha|\le\exp(C L^5)$ for a fixed constant $C$. Then, for sufficiently large $L$, \begin{equation} |\E_I\Phi-\E\Phi|\le e^{-L^9}. \end{equation} This also applies to the sum of errors for a family of such expansions when the same bound holds for their total absolute coefficient sum.

primaryStatements.name: Truncated weight average
primaryStatements.label: q:truncated-weight
primaryStatements.text: For every offset $a$ and every interval $I$ allowed in \Cref{q:finite-law}, \begin{equation} \E_I\bigl[w(n+a)\1_{\omega_Q(n+a)\le400\log L}\bigr] \le S+e^{-L^9}\le2S \end{equation} for sufficiently large $L$. The analogous sum over $M$ fixed offsets is at most $2MS$.

primaryStatements.name: Matom\"aki--Radziwi\l\l--Tao, \cite{MRT15}, Theorem 1.3
primaryStatements.label: q:MRT-short
primaryStatements.text: For every pair of real numbers $10\le H\le Z$, \[ \sup_{\alpha\in\mathbb R} \int_0^Z \left|\sum_{x\le n\le x+H}\lambda(n)\mathrm e(\alpha n)\right|\,dx \ll HZ\left(\frac{\log\log H}{\log H} +(\log Z)^{-1/700}\right), \] with an absolute implied constant. The supremum is outside the integral.

primaryStatements.name: The nonbacktracking moment
primaryStatements.label: q:trace
primaryStatements.text: There is an absolute constant $C_2$ such that \begin{equation} \E\|H^k\|_{\mathrm{HS}}^2 \le\bigl[K(C_2\sqrt W)^J\bigr]^{2k}. \end{equation} The norm is the unnormalized Hilbert--Schmidt norm. The same estimate, after increasing $C_2$ absolutely, holds when block origins are averaged over any integer interval of length at least $\exp(\tfrac12L^A)$. The threshold for $L$ may depend on the fixed data.

definitions.label: q:prohibited
definitions.text: A numerical word is forward prohibited if it has length $3\le m\le s$ and satisfies three conditions: \begin{enumerate} \item Consecutive whole tuples $d_i,d_{i+1}$ are unequal. \item For every prime in $P$, its indices of appearance among $d_1,\ldots,d_m$ form an interval, if nonempty. \item Some prime $p\mid d_1$, absent from $d_m$, satisfies \begin{equation} p\mid\sum_{i=a}^m D_i\qquad\text{for some }1<a<m. \end{equation} \end{enumerate} A forward prohibited word is minimal if no shorter contiguous subword is forward prohibited in either orientation. A witness is a positive path realizing a minimal forward prohibited word. Let $\mathcal B_j$ be the set of sites at which a witness starts, and set $\sigma_j(n)=\1_{n\notin\mathcal B_j}$.

definitions.name: Path specifications
definitions.label: def:primitive-specification
definitions.text: A specification consists of a path with distinct integer offsets $z_0=0,z_1,\ldots,z_m$, where $1\le m\le L$ and \[ z_i-z_{i-1}=\varepsilon_i h e_i, \qquad e_i\in\mathcal D,\quad \varepsilon_i\in\{-1,1\}, \] an extra prime $p\in\mathcal S$ dividing none of the $e_i$, and an index $i_0\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$ such that $p\mid z_m-z_{i_0-1}$. It qualifies at $x$ when \[ p\mid x,\qquad e_i\mid x+z_{i-1}\quad(1\le i\le m). \] Its prime support $\Pi$ is the union of $\{p\}$ and the prime factors of all its edge labels. Its cylinder is the set of starting integers $x$ satisfying these qualification conditions. The cylinder is either empty or fixes one residue at each prime in $\Pi$; in the latter case its measure is $\prod_{q\in\Pi}q^{-1}$. When testing a contiguous subpath as a specification, translate its offsets to start at zero. If it starts at $z_a$, test qualification at $x+z_a$. For the reversed subpath, use the same convention with its new initial vertex. The extra prime may be any member of $\Pi$ absent from the subpath's edge labels. All these tests are constant as $x$ ranges over a nonempty original cylinder, since they use only its fixed prime coordinates. A specification is primitive if its cylinder is nonempty and no shorter nonempty contiguous subpath, in either orientation, can be made into a specification, with an extra prime from $\Pi$, that qualifies at its own initial vertex for $x$ in that cylinder. Set \[ Y=\{x\in\Z:\text{no primitive specification qualifies at }x\}. \]

lean.scopeText:
The formalization proves ordinary two-point cancellation for multiplicative functions. For the Liouville function on every fixed pair of nonproportional affine forms, the correlation sum up to $X$ is $O(X/(\log X)^c)$ for an absolute $c>0$, with the implied constant depending on the forms.

For two one-bounded multiplicative functions, if at least one is uniformly nonpretentious against all Dirichlet-character twists with frequency $|t|\le N$, then their shifted and nonproportional affine correlation sums divided by $N$ tend to zero. These are ordinary averages, with no logarithmic averaging.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: There are homogeneous elements \(\sigma_{2k+1}\in W_{2k+1}\), one for each \(k\ge1\), for which \[ \Lie_{\Q}\langle e_3,e_5,e_7,\ldots\rangle \longrightarrow (W,\{\, ,\,\}),\qquad e_{2k+1}\longmapsto\sigma_{2k+1}, \] is an isomorphism of graded Lie algebras. In particular, \(W\) is closed under the bracket \eqref{eq:ihara}. The induced map on completions by weight is a continuous graded isomorphism.

primaryStatements.name: Saturated reduction
primaryStatements.label: prop:saturated-reduction
primaryStatements.text: Let \[ K_n=\Lie_R\langle x,y\rangle_n, \qquad L_n=W_n\cap K_n. \] Then \(L_n\) is a saturated finite free \(R\)-submodule of \(K_n\), and its reduction embeds in \(K_n/2K_n\). Writing its image as \(\overline L_n\), one has \begin{equation} \dim_{\F}\overline L_n=\dim_{\Q}W_n. \end{equation} More generally, for any rational subspace \(V_n\subset W_n\), the lattice \(M_n=V_n\cap K_n\) has an embedded reduction \(\overline M_n\subset\overline L_n\) of dimension \(\dim_{\Q}V_n\). Every element of \(\overline L_n\) satisfies the reductions of the three defining identities. If \(n>2\), it also satisfies \eqref{eq:special} and \eqref{eq:special-linearization} after reduction, together with all formal coefficient consequences of these identities. In particular, putting \(z=x+y\), \begin{equation} [x,\overline\psi(x,y)+\overline\psi(z,y)] +[y,\overline\psi(z,y)]=0 \qquad(\overline\psi\in\overline L_n). \end{equation}

primaryStatements.label: prop:leading-pentagon
primaryStatements.text: Let $\bar\psi\in\overline L_n$, $n>2$, and suppose its expression $\Psi(A,C,B)$ lies in $F^r$. Let $\chi$ be its component of count $r$, and write $n=2m+r$, with $m>0$. In $U(\mathfrak h)$ let $\mathcal U_{\ell,<r}$ be the span of all products of exactly $\ell$ symbols from $\{a_i,v_{ij},u_{ij}\}$ that contain fewer than $r$ symbols $u$. Then \begin{equation} \begin{split} 0\equiv{}&\chi(a_1,v_{12}+v_{13},u_{12}+u_{13}) +\chi(a_2+v_{12},v_{23},u_{23})\\ &+\chi(a_1+a_2+v_{12},v_{13}+v_{23},u_{13}+u_{23})\\ &+\chi(a_1,v_{12},u_{12})\pmod{\mathcal U_{m+r,<r}}. \end{split} \end{equation} For $r=0$ the indicated lower-count subspace is zero.

primaryStatements.label: prop:deletion-representation
primaryStatements.text: The assignment $t_H\mapsto T_H$ defines a representation of $\mathfrak h_{\Z}$ on $E_N$. Equivalently, for every codimension-two flat $X$ and every hyperplane $H_0\supset X$, \begin{equation} \left[T_{H_0},\sum_{H\supset X}T_H\right]=0. \end{equation} It therefore extends to the ordinary enveloping algebra, over $\Z$ and after reduction over $\F$.

primaryStatements.label: prop:projection-injective
primaryStatements.text: For $n>2$ and every $r\geq0$, the leading projection \[ \operatorname{gr}^{r}\overline L_n\longrightarrow \Lie_{\F}\langle C,B\rangle,\qquad \chi\longmapsto\chi(0,C,B) \] is injective. Its source is zero unless $n=2m+r$ for an integer $m\geq0$; in that case its image has $C$-count $m$ and $B$-count $r$.

primaryStatements.name: The image bound
primaryStatements.label: prop:image-bound
primaryStatements.text: Set $g_k=\ad_C^kB$ for $k\geq1$. These elements freely generate an ordinary free Lie algebra inside $\Lie_{\F}\langle C,B\rangle$. For $n>2$, the image of the leading projection of $\operatorname{gr}^r_F\overline L_n$ belongs to its weight-$n$, length-$r$ component, where $\wt(g_k)=2k+1$ and each $g_k$ has length one. The associated graded piece with $r=0$ is zero.

primaryStatements.name: The all-weight upper bound
primaryStatements.label: cor:dimension-bound
primaryStatements.text: For every $n$ and $r\geq0$ there is an injection \[ \operatorname{gr}^r_F\overline L_n \lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow \mathfrak f_{\mathrm{odd},n,r}, \] obtained by the leading projection and the identification $g_k\leftrightarrow z_k$. In particular, \begin{equation} \dim_{\Q}W_n =\dim_{\F}\overline L_n \leq\sum_{r\geq0}d_{n,r}=d_n. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: The leading Ihara bracket
primaryStatements.label: prop:leading-ihara
primaryStatements.text: Let $\psi\in F^r\overline L_n$ and $\phi\in F^s\overline L_{n'}$, where $n,n'>2$ and $r,s\geq1$. Write $f,g$ for their leading projections at counts $r,s$. Their Ihara bracket, computed in the ambient Lie algebra in $x,y$, belongs to $F^{r+s}$ in the $A,C,B$ presentation, and the projection of its component of count $r+s$ is \begin{equation} [f,g]. \end{equation} This assertion does not require prior closure of the full solution space under the Ihara bracket.

lean.scopeText:
The Deligne–Drinfeld conjecture predicts that the rational Grothendieck–Teichmüller Lie algebra is freely generated by one element in each odd weight $3,5,7,\ldots$. The formalization establishes this for the rational solution space of antisymmetry, the three-term equation, and the four-strand pentagon with the Ihara bracket. It also gives the corresponding continuous isomorphism after completion by weight.

The regularized-transport proposition and graph-complex consequences are not included.

papers.title: Reconstruction of Function Fields from Mod-ℓ Milnor K-Theory
papers.abstract: We prove a mod-ℓ Bogomolov–Pop reconstruction theorem for function fields of transcendence degree at least two over arbitrary algebraically closed fields of characteristic different from ℓ. The groups $K^{\mathrm M}_1/\ell$ and $K^{\mathrm M}_2/\ell$, together with their full bilinear product, determine the perfect closure and its constant field. Every compatible isomorphism of these data is induced by a field isomorphism up to a single scalar in $\mathbb F_\ell^\times$, with only Frobenius ambiguity in the field isomorphism in positive characteristic.
papers.familySummary: Reconstructs function fields of transcendence degree at least two over algebraically closed constants from $K^{\mathrm M}_1/\ell$, $K^{\mathrm M}_2/\ell$, and their product. These data recover the perfect closure and constants when ℓ differs from the characteristic, and the original field and its named base in equal characteristic. Also proves Bogomolov–Pop reconstruction from abelian-by-central pro-ℓ Galois data away from the characteristic.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let $\ell$ be any prime. Let $K/k$ and $L/l$ be finitely generated extensions of arbitrary algebraically closed fields, with $\charac k,\charac l\ne\ell$ and $\trdeg(K/k),\trdeg(L/l)\ge2$. Then \eqref{eq:main-map} is bijective. In particular, a compatible isomorphism $V_K\to V_L$ forces equality of the characteristics and of the relative transcendence degrees.

primaryStatements.name: Alternating-pair valuation theory
primaryStatements.label: thm:local-input
primaryStatements.text: Let \(F\) be a field and set \(A_F^{\pm}=\{f\in A_F:f(-1)=0\}\). \begin{enumerate} \item Every valuative subset \(\Sigma\subset A_F\) has a unique coarsest valuation \(v_\Sigma\) with \(\Sigma\subset I_{v_\Sigma}\). In particular, \(v_\Sigma\) coarsens every valuation whose inertia contains \(\Sigma\). For such a valuation \(w\), this coarsening is obtained by quotienting \(wF\) by its largest convex subgroup contained in \(w(\bigcap_{f\in\Sigma}\ker f)\). \item If \(S\subset A_F^{\pm}\) is an alternating linear subspace, its valuative elements form a valuative subspace \(S_0\) of codimension at most one. Moreover \(S\subset D_{v_{S_0}}\). \item If \(\Sigma\subset A_F^{\pm}\) is valuative and \(g\in A_F^{\pm}\) is alternating with every element of \(\Sigma\), then \(g\in D_{v_\Sigma}\). \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.label: prop:local-dimension
primaryStatements.text: The maximum dimension of an alternating subspace of \(A_F\) is \(s\). If \(S\subset A_F\) is alternating of dimension \(s\), and \(v\) is the valuation associated to its valuative part \(S_0\), then \(S_0=I_v\) and equality holds in \eqref{eq:local-abhyankar} for \(v\).

primaryStatements.label: prop:quasi-recovery
primaryStatements.text: Assume \(s\geq2\). A line \(H\subset A_F\) is the inertia of a quasi-divisorial valuation if and only if \begin{equation} H=S_1\cap S_2 \quad\text{for alternating subspaces }S_1,S_2\subset A_F \text{ of dimension }s. \end{equation} The quasi-divisorial valuation \(v\) with \(I_v=H\) is unique. For any nonzero \(h\in H\), its decomposition space is \begin{equation} D_v=\{g\in A_F:(h,g)\text{ is alternating}\}. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.label: cor:flag-matching
primaryStatements.text: For the fields \(K/k,L/l\) of Theorem \ref{thm:main}, a compatible isomorphism \(\Theta\) forces \(\trdeg(K/k)=\trdeg(L/l)=d\), say. Its dual \(\Phi\) matches the inertia--decomposition pairs of quasi-prime divisors, and, successively, the pairs of quasi-prime \(r\)-divisors for \(1\leq r\leq d-1\). For a matched pair of valuations \(v\) on \(K\) and \(w\) on \(L\), it induces a topological linear isomorphism \[ A_{Lw}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }A_{Kv} \] preserving alternating pairs in both directions.

primaryStatements.name: Pop's residual density input
primaryStatements.label: thm:density-input
primaryStatements.text: Let \(F/\kappa\) be a function field over an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from \(\ell\). Suppose that a valuation \(v\) of \(F\), with \(Fv/\kappa v\) a function field, has the following properties: \begin{enumerate} \item \(vF\) has no nonzero \(\ell\)-divisible convex subgroup; \item there is a subfield \(\kappa\subset\kappa_1\subset F\) such that \[ \kappa_1v=\kappa v,\qquad \trdeg(F/\kappa_1)=\trdeg(Fv/\kappa_1v)=1. \] \end{enumerate} Then \(\widehat J_v\) contains the full minimized inertia group \(\widehat I_u\) of every c.r.\ quasi-prime divisor \(u\) of \(Fv/\kappa v\).

primaryStatements.label: prop:point-recognition
primaryStatements.text: For a quasi-prime \((d-1)\)-divisor \(v\) of \(F/\kappa\), the family \(\mathcal L_v\) satisfies the preceding two conditions if and only if \(\kappa v\) is algebraic over a finite field. When this holds, \(\mathcal L_v\) consists exactly of the point inertia lines of the smooth projective curve of \(Fv/\kappa v\). Consequently the matching in Corollary \ref{cor:flag-matching} recognizes these terminal valuations and matches their full point families.

primaryStatements.name: Finite curve test
primaryStatements.label: prop:finite-curve-test
primaryStatements.text: There is an integer $G_X\ge0$, depending only on the embedded model $X$, with the following property. Given $g_1,\ldots,g_m\in L^\times$ whose classes in $V_L$ are independent, there is a quasi-prime $(d-1)$-divisor $w$ of $L/l$ such that: \begin{enumerate} \item $lw$ is algebraically closed and algebraic over a finite field of characteristic different from $\ell$, and $Lw$ is the function field of a smooth projective curve $C_w/lw$ of genus at most $G_X$; \item the $g_j$ are $w$-units and their residue classes are independent in $V_{Lw}$; \item for every $j$, \[ \#\{x\in C_w(lw):\ord_x(\overline{g_j})\not\equiv0\pmod\ell\} =s_X([g_j]). \] \end{enumerate}

definitions.text: A quasi-divisorial valuation, or quasi-prime divisor, of \(F/\kappa\) is a valuation minimal under coarsening among those with \[ vF/v\kappa\cong\Z,\qquad \trdeg(Fv/\kappa v)=s-1. \] A quasi-prime divisor trivial on \(\kappa\) is called a prime divisor, or a true prime divisor. A quasi-prime \(r\)-divisor is a composition of \(r\) successive quasi-prime divisors on the resulting residue fields.

definitions.label: def:good-subfield
definitions.text: A curve subfield $E\subset F$ is good if it is rational over the constants and every point line in $A_E$ is the nonzero image of the inertia of some true divisor of $F$. A good function is an element $t\in F$ generating a good subfield $\kappa(t)$.

papers.title: Reconstruction from Milnor K-theory modulo the characteristic
papers.abstract: Let K and L be finitely generated extensions of transcendence degree at least two over algebraically closed fields of characteristic p. We prove that every isomorphism of their first Milnor K-groups modulo p preserving the degree-two Steinberg relations is a nonzero scalar multiple of the map induced by a unique field isomorphism. The proof recovers projective lines over the subfields of pth powers by an elementary calculation with derivations.

primaryStatements.text: Let $K/k$ and $L/l$ be finitely generated extensions of algebraically closed fields of characteristic $p$, with \[ \trdeg(K/k)\ge2,\qquad \trdeg(L/l)\ge2. \] The canonical map \[ \Isom(K,k;L,l)\longrightarrow \Isom_{\mathrm M}(V_K,V_L)/\Lambda^\times, \qquad \alpha\longmapsto[\alpha_*], \] is bijective.

primaryStatements.text:
Let $F$ be a field of characteristic $p$ with $[F:F^p]<\infty$, and put $C=F^p$. Let $X,Y\in F^	imes$ be $p$-independent. Suppose \[ U\in C(X)^	imes,\qquad V\in C(Y)^	imes, \qquad [U]

primaryStatements.label: prop:lines
primaryStatements.text: Let $K/k$ and $L/l$ be finitely generated extensions of algebraically closed fields of characteristic $p$, both of transcendence degree at least two. For every compatible isomorphism $\Theta:V_K\to V_L$, there is a unique $n\in\Fp^\times$ such that $\Psi=n\Theta$ sends every projective line over $K^p$ onto a projective line over $L^p$.

primaryStatements.name: Projective lifting
primaryStatements.label: prop:projective-lift
primaryStatements.text: Let $E$ and $E'$ be finite-dimensional vector spaces over fields $H$ and $C$, respectively, with dimensions at least three. Every bijection $\psi:\PP_H(E)\to\PP_C(E')$ that maps lines onto lines is induced by an additive bijection $S:E\to E'$ satisfying \[ S(av)=\sigma(a)S(v)\qquad(a\in H,\ v\in E) \] for a field isomorphism $\sigma:H\to C$. The map $\sigma$ is unique, and $S$ is unique up to multiplication by an element of $C^\times$.

primaryStatements.name: Bogomolov--Pop reconstruction
primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let $k$ and $l$ be arbitrary algebraically closed fields of characteristics different from $\ell$, and let $K/k$ and $L/l$ be function fields with $\trdeg(K/k),\trdeg(L/l)\ge2$. Then \[ \Phi_{K,L}:\Isom_F^i(K,L)\longrightarrow \Isom^c(\Pi_L^a,\Pi_K^a)/\Zell^\times, \qquad [\alpha]\longmapsto[\alpha^*], \] is a bijection.

primaryStatements.label: local:transport
primaryStatements.text: Let $K/k$ and $L/l$ be function fields over algebraically closed fields of characteristic different from $\ell$, each of transcendence degree at least two. Let $\varphi:W_L\to W_K$ be a continuous bracket-compatible $\Zell$-module isomorphism. Then their transcendence degrees agree, say they are $d$. For every $1\leq r<d$, the map $\varphi$ carries exactly the pairs $I_w\subset D_w$ of quasi-prime $r$-divisors of $L/l$ onto the corresponding pairs of $K/k$. For matched pairs it induces a continuous isomorphism \[ D_w/I_w\cong W_{Lw}\ \longrightarrow\ D_v/I_v\cong W_{Kv} \] that preserves alternating pairs.

primaryStatements.label: local:curves
primaryStatements.text: In the setting of Proposition \ref{local:transport}, let $w$ and $v$ be matched quasi-prime $(d-1)$-divisors. Then $lw$ is algebraic over a finite field if and only if $kv$ is. When this holds, the induced isomorphism $W_{Lw}\to W_{Kv}$ carries the full family of point inertia subgroups of the respective smooth projective curves onto each other. Corresponding normalized order characters differ by units of $\Zell$.

primaryStatements.name: Uniform pencil support
primaryStatements.label: pencil:uniform
primaryStatements.text: For every $t\in K\setminus k$, there is a finite constant $B_t$ such that \[ \sum_{D\in\operatorname{Supp}_X(\Theta[t-a])}\deg D\le B_t \qquad\text{for every }a\in k. \] In particular, all these supports are finite, with a bound independent of the member of the pencil.

primaryStatements.label: pencil:finite
primaryStatements.text: For every $z\in K^\times$, the class $\Theta[z]$ has finite support on $X$.

primaryStatements.label: recovery:curves
primaryStatements.text: The map $\Theta$ gives a bijection between the completed curve subfields of $K/k$ and those of $L/l$. More precisely, for every curve subfield $E\subset K$ there is a unique curve subfield $P\subset L$ such that \[ \Theta(\widehat E)=\widehat P. \]

primaryStatements.label: recovery:divisorial
primaryStatements.text: A quasi-prime divisor $v$ of $K/k$ is divisorial if and only if \begin{equation} D_v^\perp\cap\widehat E=0 \end{equation} for some curve subfield $E$ of $K/k$. Consequently $\varphi$ preserves divisorial inertia and decomposition groups in both directions.

primaryStatements.label: recovery:rational
primaryStatements.text: The point inertia lines of every curve subfield $E$ are precisely the saturations of the nonzero images $\rho_E(I_v)$ for divisorial valuations $v$ of $K/k$. The correspondence of Theorem \ref{recovery:curves} preserves these lines and the genus. In particular, it matches exactly the relatively algebraically closed rational subfields. If $\Theta(\widehat E)=\widehat P$, the induced continuous isomorphism $\varphi_E:W_P\to W_E$ makes the diagram \begin{equation} \begin{tikzcd}[column sep=large] W_L \arrow[r,"\varphi"] \arrow[d,two heads,"\rho_P"'] & W_K \arrow[d,two heads,"\rho_E"] \\ W_P \arrow[r,"\varphi_E"'] & W_E \end{tikzcd} \end{equation} commute and matches the point inertia lines on its targets. For rational $E$ and $P$, these are the geometric rational quotient diagrams, with their point decomposition data.

lean.scopeText:
The Bogomolov–Pop reconstruction conjecture concerns recovering a function field and its constants from pro-$\ell$ abelian-by-central Galois data. The linked formalization proves injectivity of the reconstruction correspondence for function fields of transcendence degree at least two over algebraically closed fields of characteristic different from the prime $\ell$.

If two isomorphisms of perfect closures preserving the constant fields induce the same Galois-data isomorphism modulo $\ell$-adic unit scaling, then they agree modulo Frobenius. The selected statement proves this uniqueness; existence of a field isomorphism for every admissible Galois-data isomorphism is outside it.

papers.title: Unrestricted pro-modularity at the prime two
papers.abstract: Every continuous, odd, absolutely irreducible two-dimensional 2-adic representation of $G_{\mathbb Q}$ that is unramified outside finitely many finite primes occurs in the full completed Hecke algebra at some odd tame level. The level may contain auxiliary tame primes, and scalar and reducible residual representations are included. This is a completed-Hecke occurrence result, with no de Rham hypothesis; it does not assert classical modularity.
papers.familySummary: Every continuous odd absolutely irreducible two-dimensional 2-adic representation of $G_{\mathbb Q}$ unramified outside finitely many primes occurs in a completed Hecke algebra at some odd tame level. Also proves classical modularity up to Tate twist for irreducible odd representations with these finiteness conditions that are de Rham at 2 with distinct Hodge–Tate weights, resolving the dyadic Fontaine–Mazur case without residual restrictions.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let $E/\Q_2$ be finite, with ring of integers $\OO_E$, and let $r:G_{\Q}\longrightarrow\GL_2(E)$ be continuous and absolutely irreducible. Suppose that $r$ is unramified outside finitely many finite primes and is odd: $\det r(c)=-1$ for complex conjugation $c$. Then there exist an odd positive integer $N$, divisible by every odd prime where $r$ ramifies, and a continuous $\Z_2$-algebra homomorphism \[ \lambda:\mathbb T_2(N)\longrightarrow\OO_E \] such that, for every prime $\ell\nmid2N$, \[ \lambda(T_\ell)=\tr r(\operatorname{Frob}_\ell),\qquad \lambda(\ell S_\ell)=\det r(\operatorname{Frob}_\ell). \]

primaryStatements.label: prop:potential-support
primaryStatements.text: Let $B$ be the family in Lemma \ref{lem:large-family}, with the normalized determinant of Lemma \ref{lem:normalization}. There is a solvable totally real Galois extension $F/\Q$, of even degree and completely split at $2$, such that the closed trace image of $B|_{G_F}$ is pro-modular at one fixed tame level and central character $\psi|_{G_F}$. This assertion includes scalar and reducible semisimple residual representations.

primaryStatements.label: prop:family
primaryStatements.text: For the normalized representation $r$, the preceding constructions give a horizontal complete local domain $D$ of dimension at least three containing its coefficient point, and continuous maps \[ \mathbb T\longrightarrow D,\qquad R\longrightarrow D \] that make $D$ finite over both source rings. There is a right $\mathcal E^{\widehat\otimes b}$-module $L_0$, finite and faithful over $\mathbb T$, whose inverse under the product block equivalence is the residual summand of compact definite forms. The module \[ L=\bigl(L_0\otimes_{\mathbb T}D\bigr) \big/\bigl(\text{$D$-torsion}\bigr) \] is nonzero, finite and torsion-free over $D$. All $b$ central $R$-actions on $L$ are the same map $R\to D$. Its inverse under the product block equivalence is finite over the completed group algebra of a sufficiently small product of determinant-one compact subgroups.

primaryStatements.name: One-factor admissibility
primaryStatements.label: prop:diagonal
primaryStatements.text: Let \(D\) be a complete noetherian local \(\OO\)-domain in which \(\varpi\ne0\), and suppose that \(R\to D\) is a finite continuous local map. Let \(L\ne0\) be a finite torsion-free \(D\)-module with a commuting continuous right \(\mathcal E^{(b)}\)-action. Suppose that every copy of \(R\) acts through the same map \(R\to D\), and that \[ M=L\widehat\otimes_{\mathcal E^{(b)}}P^{(b)} \] is admissible in the compact category. Then, using the first \(\mathcal E\)-action, \[ V=L\widehat\otimes_{\mathcal E}P \] is nonzero, \(\OO\)-torsion-free, and finite over \(\mathscr A=\OO[[K]]\), for every sufficiently small uniform open subgroup \(K\subset\SL_2(\Z_2)\). It has a continuous commuting \(D\)-action.

primaryStatements.name: Pa\v{s}k\=unas--Tung
primaryStatements.label: input:local-blocks
primaryStatements.text: The following statements hold for every such block at \(p=2\), including the block of a scalar residual Galois representation. \begin{enumerate} \item The functor \(\Hom(P,-)\) is an exact equivalence from the compact block to right pseudocompact \(\mathcal E\)-modules, with inverse \(-\widehat\otimes_{\mathcal E}P\). The algebra \(\mathcal E\) is finite over \(R\). \item Let \(\mathrm{CH}_R\) be the universal Cayley--Hamilton algebra for the local pseudorepresentation, and let \(\mathrm{CH}_R^{\mathrm{tf}}\) be its maximal \(\OO\)-torsion-free quotient. There is an \(R\)-compatible identification \[ \mathrm{CH}_R^{\mathrm{tf}}\simeq \begin{cases} (e\mathcal E e)^{\mathrm{op}},&\text{in a nonsupersingular block},\\ M_2((e\mathcal E e)^{\mathrm{op}}),&\text{in a supersingular block}. \end{cases} \] The corner equivalence is induced by the Montr\'eal functor on the quotient by the objects with trivial \(\SL_2(\Q_2)\)-action. \item An \(\mathcal E\)-module finite and torsion-free over \(\OO\) gives, after duality and inversion of \(2\), an admissible Banach representation of finite length. At an absolutely irreducible Galois coefficient parameter there is a unique absolutely irreducible Banach object. At a sum of characters \(\gamma_1+\gamma_2\), the simple objects have the following description. If the characters coincide, the unique simple is \(\Ind_B^G(1\otimes\eps^{-1})^{\cts}\otimes\gamma_1\circ\det\). If their sum is \(\gamma+\gamma\eps\), the simples are \[ \{1,\widehat{\mathrm{St}}, \Ind_B^G(\eps\otimes\eps^{-1})^{\cts}\} \otimes\gamma\circ\det, \] where \(\widehat{\mathrm{St}}\) is continuous Steinberg. If \(\gamma_1\gamma_2^{-1}\notin\{1,\eps,\eps^{-1}\}\), they are exactly \[ \Ind_B^G(\gamma_1\otimes\gamma_2\eps^{-1})^{\cts}, \qquad \Ind_B^G(\gamma_2\otimes\gamma_1\eps^{-1})^{\cts}. \] Here \(B\) is the upper Borel, induction is unnormalized, and Galois characters are viewed as characters of \(\Q_2^\times\) by reciprocity. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.label: prop:positive-rank
primaryStatements.text: The module $V$ satisfies \[ \rank_{\mathscr A}V>0. \]

primaryStatements.label: prop:regular-point
primaryStatements.text: There is a coefficient point $x:D\to\OO'$ at which the global pseudorepresentation is that of a continuous absolutely irreducible representation \[ r_x:G_{\Q}\longrightarrow\GL_2(E'), \qquad E'=\Frac(\OO'), \] after a finite coefficient extension if necessary. This representation is odd and finitely ramified. Its restriction to $G_{\Q_2}$ is absolutely irreducible and regular de Rham, and $\WD(r_x|_{G_{\Q_2}})$ is trivial on wild inertia. Consequently $r_x$ is attached to a classical cuspidal eigenform up to Tate twist.

primaryStatements.label: prop:hecke-level
primaryStatements.text: Let $N\geq5$ be odd, and let $f$ be a classical cuspidal eigenform of positive weight and level dividing $2^aN$, for some $a\geq0$. Its eigenvalues away from $2N$ define a continuous homomorphism \[ A(N)\longrightarrow\OO_{E_f} \] after choosing a finite $2$-adic coefficient field $E_f$ containing them. The associated determinant has the Frobenius polynomials of $f$ in \eqref{eq:hecke-frobenius}.

papers.title: The Dimension of the Two-Adic Hecke Algebra at Odd Level
papers.abstract: For every odd positive integer N, every irreducible component of the full two-adic Hecke algebra of level $\Gamma_1(N)$ has Krull dimension four. This proves the p = 2 case of Emerton's dimension conjecture, including all residual components.
papers.familySummary: Every continuous odd absolutely irreducible two-dimensional 2-adic representation of $G_{\mathbb Q}$ unramified outside finitely many primes occurs in a completed Hecke algebra at some odd tame level. Also proves classical modularity up to Tate twist for irreducible odd representations with these finiteness conditions that are de Rham at 2 with distinct Hodge–Tate weights, resolving the dyadic Fontaine–Mazur case without residual restrictions.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: For every odd positive integer $N$, every irreducible component of $\Spec T_2(N)$ has dimension exactly $4$.

primaryStatements.label: prop:noetherian
primaryStatements.text: The ring $A$ is a finite product of complete Noetherian local rings with finite residue fields. Its given topology on each factor is the maximal-ideal-adic topology.

primaryStatements.name: Emerton
primaryStatements.label: thm:lower
primaryStatements.text: For the algebra $A$ in \eqref{eq:algebra}, every irreducible component of $\Spec A$ has dimension at least $4$.

primaryStatements.label: prop:exceptional
primaryStatements.text: The closure of the classical points of bounded weight has dimension at most $1$. The closure of all Eisenstein points has dimension at most $2$.

primaryStatements.label: cor:classical-point
primaryStatements.text: For every minimal prime $P$ of $A$, there is a classical cuspidal map $\lambda:A\to\OO_E$ of weight at least $3$ such that $P\subseteq\frakx:=\ker\lambda$ and $\frakx$ belongs to no other irreducible component of $\Spec A$.

primaryStatements.label: prop:tangent
primaryStatements.text: Let $R$ be a compact Hausdorff Noetherian topological $\Z_p$-algebra, with continuous structure map $\Z_p\to R$. Suppose a profinite group $H$ has a continuous two-dimensional determinant over $R$, with trace $t$ and determinant $d$, and that their values topologically generate $R$ over $\Z_p$. Let $\lambda:R\to\OO_E$ be a continuous $\Z_p$-algebra map, where $E/\Q_p$ is finite, and suppose its specialized determinant is that of an absolutely irreducible continuous representation $r:H\to\GL_2(E)$. For $\frakx=\ker\lambda$, \begin{equation} \dim R_{\frakx}\leq\edim R_{\frakx} \leq\dim_E H^1(H,\ad r). \end{equation}

primaryStatements.label: prop:cohomology
primaryStatements.text: For the representation $r$ of a cuspidal newform of weight at least $3$ and odd level dividing $N$, \[ \dim_E H^1(G_{\Q,S},\ad r)\leq3. \]

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let \[ r:G_{\mathbb Q}\longrightarrow\GL_2(\overline{\mathbb Q}_2) \] be continuous and irreducible. Suppose that \(r\) is odd, is unramified outside finitely many primes, and is de Rham at \(2\) with distinct Hodge--Tate weights. Then \(r\) is isomorphic to a Tate twist of the \(2\)-adic Galois representation associated with a classical cuspidal eigenform.

primaryStatements.name: Representation spaces
primaryStatements.label: prop:rep-space
primaryStatements.text: Let $G$ satisfy $\Phi_2$, let $\overline D$ be a continuous two-dimensional determinant over the finite field $\kk$, and fix a continuous lift $\chi$ of its determinant character. The following statements hold. \begin{enumerate} \item The determinant deformation functor is represented by a complete Noetherian local $\OO$-algebra $R^{\mathrm{ps}}$. There is a finite $R^{\mathrm{ps}}$-algebra $\mathscr E$ carrying its universal Cayley--Hamilton representation. Matrix representations of $\mathscr E$ compatible with the universal determinant form an affine scheme of finite type over $R^{\mathrm{ps}}$. Its completion at a closed residual matrix representation is that representation's framed deformation space. \item Invariant lines at finitely many closed subgroups can be imposed by closed incidence conditions in products of projective lines. On the absolutely irreducible global locus, existence of such a line with a specified character is closed in the trace and character parameters. \item Suppose the subgroups' abelianizations have finitely generated maximal pro-$2$ quotients. Adjoining the characters on the specified lines gives a finite extension of the completed trace-and-determinant image. \item At an absolutely irreducible representation over a coefficient field, determinants classify unframed deformations. After a splitting extension, the framed fiber is a conjugacy orbit of dimension three. \end{enumerate} These assertions do not require the residual determinant to be multiplicity-free.

primaryStatements.name: Relative relation bounds
primaryStatements.label: prop:relative-presentation
primaryStatements.text: Let $F$ be totally real of degree $d$, let $S$ contain the real and dyadic places, and let $\rho$ be a representation over a finite residue field, a curve field as above, or a finite $2$-adic field. Use one global frame and a fixed determinant. Let $T\subset S$ consist of all real places and $m$ dyadic places, each isomorphic to $\QQ_2$. Over the completed product of the unrestricted local framed deformation rings at $T$, the global framed ring has a power-series presentation with $g$ relative variables and $r$ relations satisfying \begin{equation} g-r\ge 3-6m-h^0\bigl(D^\vee(1)\bigr). \end{equation} Local quotient conditions and local line charts may then be imposed by base change without changing this bound. This includes replacing the local base by its reduction. For the variable-determinant problem with independent frames at the places of $S$, the relative tangent dimension over the local framed base is \begin{equation} h^1_{\mathrm{Sel}}(\ad\rho) +\sum_{v\in S}h^0_v(\ad\rho)-h^0(\ad\rho), \end{equation} where the Selmer condition is zero at $S$ and any other prescribed conditions are included in the Selmer group. On the absolutely irreducible locus, forgetting these independent frames has smooth fiber dimension $4|S|-1$.

primaryStatements.name: A characteristic-zero line chart
primaryStatements.label: cor:charzero-line-dimension
primaryStatements.text: For a two-dimensional representation of $G_{\QQ_2}$ over a finite $2$-adic field with a chosen invariant line and fixed determinant, every component of its framed line-deformation chart has dimension at least five. The odd fixed-determinant real chart has dimension two. In particular, over $\QQ$, the relative bound for these two local charts is $-3$ whenever $h^0(D^\vee(1))=0$.

primaryStatements.name: Local component geometry
primaryStatements.label: prop:local-geometry
primaryStatements.text: The ring $A^{\mathrm{rd}}$ is a flat complete-intersection normal domain over $\mathcal L$, of dimension $1+8d$, and its special fiber is a normal domain of dimension $8d$. Set \[ e=1+8d+4u+g. \] Then the following statements hold for the model \eqref{eq:tame-model}. \begin{enumerate} \item $\Spec B_i$ is irreducible of dimension $e$, and its unique irreducible component is horizontal. \item The two rings have a canonical common special fiber, compatible with their universal matrices and the variables $X_1,\ldots,X_g$. Its irreducible components have dimension $e-1$ and are indexed by a choice, at each tame place, of the unramified component or the closure of the nontrivial-unipotent component. \item The irreducible components of $\Spec B_1$ are horizontal and have dimension $e$. They are indexed by the same choices. The specialization of each has precisely its corresponding special-fiber component as underlying support. In particular the generic point of a special-fiber component lies on exactly one component of $\Spec B_1$. \end{enumerate} The assertions remain valid after finite extension of the constants and curve field and the resulting enhanced completion. No condition on the dyadic curve representations is required.

primaryStatements.label: prop:completed-forms
primaryStatements.text: For the tame level \(U^2\), central character \(\psi=\chi\eps\), and full compact forms module \(M\) just defined, the following properties hold. In the second assertion weights and local parameters use the normalization of Section \ref{sec:preliminaries}. \begin{enumerate} \item For a sufficiently small product \(K\) of uniform open subgroups of \(\SL_2(F_v)\), the full compact module \(M\) is finite free over \(\OO[[K]]\). The integral and torsion function spaces are admissible and commute with reduction of coefficients. \item Locally algebraic vectors are classical definite quaternionic forms of the corresponding algebraic weight. Their regular noncharacter eigenpackets transfer to Hilbert cuspidal eigenforms. They have Galois representations of determinant \(\chi\), with the local compatibility described below. \item The regular classical vectors are dense in the Banach space. They remain dense if, at each \(v\mid2\), one fixes a smooth principal-series type with two distinct inertial characters and varies the algebraic factor with the prescribed central degree. \item Every residual local factor \(\mathbb T\) of the completed Hecke algebra away from \(S\) is a complete quotient of \(R_F^{\mathrm{ps},\chi}\). It is reduced and \(\OO\)-torsion-free, and its spectrum is the closure of its classical coefficient points. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.label: prop:block-comparison
primaryStatements.text: The residual Hecke summand belongs to the product block just specified. The exact projective-generator functor gives \[ L=\Hom_{\mathrm{cts},G_2}(P,M), \] taken in the compact dual category of the specified product block, with the right \(E_{\mathrm{loc}}\)-action by precomposition. It is faithful over \(\mathbb T\), finite over \(R_{\mathrm{loc}}^{\mathrm{ps}}\), and finite over \(\mathbb T\). The local pseudodeformation action on \(L\) is the restriction of the global Galois action, with the stated cyclotomic twist. In particular, \(\mathbb T\) is finite over \(R_{\mathrm{loc}}^{\mathrm{ps}}\). At a coefficient point \(x:\mathbb T\to E'\), after finite extension of \(E'\), its Banach Hecke eigenspace contains \[ \widehat\bigotimes_{v\mid2}\Pi_v, \] where \(\Pi_v\) is an irreducible unitary Banach representation with local parameter \((r_x|_{G_{F_v}}\otimes\eps)^{\mathrm{ss}}\), of determinant \(\chi_v\eps^2\), in the block normalization of Section \ref{sec:preliminaries}. If every local parameter is absolutely irreducible, de Rham, and regular, the eigenspace has a nonzero locally algebraic vector. If the untwisted parameter at \(v\) is \(\gamma_{1,v}\oplus\gamma_{2,v}\), with ratio outside \(\{1,\eps,\eps^{-1}\}\), the possibilities are the continuous unnormalized upper-Borel inductions \[ \Ind_B^{\GL_2(\mathbb Q_2)} (\gamma_{i,v}\eps\otimes\gamma_{j,v}), \qquad \{i,j\}=\{1,2\}. \]

primaryStatements.label: prop:hecke-dimension
primaryStatements.text: For every irreducible component \(C\) of \(\Spec\mathbb T\), \[ \dim C\ge1+2d. \]

papers.title: Weighted dilation graphs, smooth shifted primes and totient fibers
papers.abstract: We prove Erdős's conjecture on the largest fibers of Euler's totient function: for every ε > 0, infinitely many positive integers n have more than $n^{1-\varepsilon }$ preimages. We also show that, for every fixed δ > 0, there are at least $x^{1-o(1)}$ primes p in $2x\lt p\le5x$ whose predecessors have no prime factor exceeding xδ.
papers.familySummary: Proves that the normalized ordered logarithms of the prime factors of $p-1$, counted with multiplicity, converge jointly to the Poisson–Dirichlet law $\mathrm{PD}(1)$ as p ranges uniformly over primes up to x and $x\to\infty$. This resolves the Ford–Konyagin–Luca conjecture. It also proves that infinitely many integers n have more than $n^{1-\varepsilon}$ totient preimages, for every ε > 0.

primaryStatements.label: thm:totient
primaryStatements.text: For every real $\eps>0$, there are infinitely many positive integers $n$ such that \[ g(n)>n^{1-\eps}. \]

primaryStatements.label: thm:smooth
primaryStatements.text: For every fixed $0<\delta<1/4$, as $x\to\infty$, \begin{equation} \#\{p:\ p\text{ prime},\ 2x<p\le5x, \ P^+(p-1)\le x^\delta\} \ge x^{1-o(1)}. \end{equation} The quantity $o(1)$ may depend on $\delta$.

primaryStatements.name: Siegel--Walfisz
primaryStatements.label: thm:sw
primaryStatements.text: For fixed $A,C>0$, uniformly for $(a,r)=1$ and $1\le r\le(\log y)^C$, \[ \#\{p\le y:p\equiv a\pmod r\} =\frac{\Li(y)}{\varphi(r)} +O_{A,C}\!\left(\frac{y}{(\log y)^A}\right). \] The constants, which need not be effective, are independent of $y,a,r$.

primaryStatements.name: Multiplicative large sieve
primaryStatements.label: thm:large-sieve
primaryStatements.text: Let $I$ be a real interval of length $H$, let $a_n$ be complex numbers supported on $I\cap\Z$, and let $R\ge1$. Then \[ \sum_{r\le R}\frac r{\varphi(r)} \sum_{\chi\bmod r}^{*} \left|\sum_{n\in I\cap\Z}a_n\chi(n)\right|^2 \ll (H+1+R^2)\sum_n|a_n|^2, \] where the asterisk restricts the sum to primitive Dirichlet characters.

primaryStatements.name: Harmonic character estimates
primaryStatements.label: cor:harmonic-sw
primaryStatements.text: Fix $c,C,B,A>0$. If $\chi$ is nonprincipal modulo $r\le L^B$, then, uniformly for real $|t|\le L^B$ and intervals $I\subset[\exp(L^c),x^C]$, \[ \sum_{p\in I}\frac{\chi(p)p^{it}}p\ll_{c,C,B,A}L^{-A}. \] The same conclusion holds for a nonprincipal character induced from a smaller modulus.

primaryStatements.name: A polynomial for rough integers
primaryStatements.label: lem:rough-sieve-polynomial
primaryStatements.text: For the ordinary bad conditions $p\mid n$ at primes $p\le z$, let $U(n)=\sum_{d\mid n}\lambda_d$ be the upper polynomial in \Cref{eq:sieve-polynomials}, and put $D=z^{4h+2}$. Then \[ U(n)\ge\ind_{\Pminus(n)>z}\ge0,\quad |\lambda_d|\le1,\quad \lambda_d=0\quad\text{unless $d\le D$ is squarefree}, \] and \begin{equation} \sum_{n\in I\cap\N} \bigl(U(n)-\ind_{\Pminus(n)>z}\bigr) \ll |I|e^{-h}+D \end{equation} for every finite interval $I\subset[1,\infty)$ and all sufficiently large even $h$. The bound is uniform in $h,z,I$. Moreover, \begin{equation} \sum_d\frac{|\lambda_d|}{d} \le\prod_{p\le z}(1+p^{-1})\ll\log(2z). \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Local transference
primaryStatements.label: thm:transference
primaryStatements.text: For every fixed $E>0$ there is $E_{\rm id}>0$, depending only on $E$ and the fixed data in \Cref{def:prime-groups}, with the following property. Assume \begin{equation} \sup_{\Theta\in\R}\norm{\mathcal T(\Theta)}\le L^{-E_{\rm id}}. \end{equation} Then, for every sufficiently large fixed $J$, where the lower bound on $J$ may also depend on $m,C_1$, put \[ R=\lceil L^{0.52}\rceil,\qquad N=2R. \] For every fixed $\gamma>0$ and $I=[X,2X)$ with $x^\gamma\le X\le x^{1/\gamma}$, one has \begin{equation} \frac1{|I\cap\Z|}\sum_{n\in I\cap\Z} \langle u_n,(\mathcal A\mathcal A^*)^Ru_n\rangle \le L^{-EN}, \end{equation} for all sufficiently large $x$. Here $u_n$ is one on every physical state at position $n$ and zero elsewhere. The threshold for $x$ may depend on all fixed parameters, including $J,C_2, \gamma$, and the bound is uniform subject to these parameters and \Cref{eq:ideal-norm-hypothesis}. No bound on $\zeta$ is needed apart from the assumed ideal estimate.

primaryStatements.label: cor:transference-pairing
primaryStatements.text: Under the hypotheses and choices of \Cref{thm:transference}, let $f\in\mathcal H_{\rm ph}$ be supported on positions $I=[X,2X)$ and independent of the chosen marks, with value $f_n$ at position $n$. Suppose \[ \sup_{n\in I}|f_n|\le\exp(O(\sqrt L)),\qquad \norm f,\norm g\le X^{1/2}L^{C_3}. \] Then \begin{equation} |\langle f,\mathcal A g\rangle| \ll XL^{-E+2C_3}. \end{equation} Only the first endpoint must be independent of its mark list.

definitions.name: Prime groups
definitions.label: def:prime-groups
definitions.text: Fix constants \[ 0<a<b<c<d<0.47,\qquad c_0,C_0,v_-,v_+>0, \qquad 0<q<1,\qquad \ell\in\N. \] For each sufficiently large $x$, let the finite, pairwise disjoint sets of primes $\mathcal P_g$ be indexed by the disjoint sets $\mathcal S$ and $\mathcal B$, where \[ c_0T\le |\mathcal S|,|\mathcal B|\le C_0T. \] The small and big groups, respectively, satisfy \begin{align} \exp(L^a)\le p\le\exp(L^b)&\quad(p\in\mathcal P_g, \ g\in\mathcal S),\notag\\ \exp(L^c)\le p\le\exp(L^d)&\quad(p\in\mathcal P_g, \ g\in\mathcal B),\\ v_-\le V_g:=\sum_{p\in\mathcal P_g}\frac1p&\le v_+, \qquad \mu_g(p):=\frac1{V_gp}.\notag \end{align} Write $s=|\mathcal S|+|\mathcal B|$ and \[ \omega_g(n)=\sum_{p\in\mathcal P_g}\ind_{p\mid n}, \qquad \omega(n)=\sum_g\omega_g(n) \quad(n\in\Z). \] Thus divisibility at $n=0$ has its usual meaning. We call primes in $\bigcup_g\mathcal P_g$ group primes.

definitions.name: Ideal operator
definitions.label: def:ideal-operator
definitions.text:
On the space \[ \mathcal H_{m id} =L^2\left(\prod_{g\in\mathcal B}\mathcal P_g^M, \  igotimes_{g\in\mathcal B}\mu_g^{\otimes M}ight), \] repetitions of prime values are allowed. For a real $\zeta$, the unsymmetrized ideal row operation for $
u$ retains shared labels, samples all unshared target labels independently with laws $\mu_g$, and samples the auxiliary labels of $D_{\mathcal B}$ independently with the same laws. Its multiplier is \[ K_
u D_{\mathcal B}^{i\zeta}\ee{\Theta D_{\mathcal B}}. \] The sum over $
u$, composed on both sides with big-group symmetrization, is denoted $\mathcal T(\Theta)$.

definitions.name: Physical operator
definitions.label: def:physical-operator
definitions.text: A physical state $(n,\mathbf p)$ consists of $n\in\Z$ and an ordered list $\mathbf p=(p_{g,i})_{g,1\le i\le M}$ such that, within each group, the labels are distinct and divide $n$. Give every state at $n$ mass $\prod_gV_g^{-M}$ and use counting measure in $n$. This defines $\mathcal H_{\rm ph}$. Fix an integer $k$ with $0<|k|\le L^{C_2}$. For pattern $\nu$, sample the auxiliary labels forming $D$ as above and move from $n$ to $n'=n+kD$. Sum over physical target states at $n'$ with the prescribed shared labels, with coefficient $\prod_g V_g^{-t_g}$ for each target. Forbid every auxiliary free label of $D$ from both endpoint lists. Auxiliary free labels may equal one another. Multiply this row action by \begin{equation} K_\nu D^{i\zeta} q^{(\omega(n)-Ms)/2}q^{(\omega(n')-Ms)/2}. \end{equation} The sum over patterns, symmetrized in all groups on both sides, is $\mathcal A$.

papers.title: The Poisson-Dirichlet law for prime predecessors
papers.abstract: For a prime p chosen uniformly from $3\le p\le x$, list the prime factors of $p-1$ in decreasing order, with multiplicity. As $x\to\infty$, their logarithms, divided by $\log(p-1)$, converge in every finite joint distribution to the Poisson–Dirichlet distribution with parameter one. This proves the conjecture of Ford, Konyagin and Luca.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: For every fixed $k\ge1$ and every bounded continuous function $F:[0,1]^k\to\R$, \begin{equation} \lim_{x\to\infty}\frac1{\pi(x)-1} \sum_{\substack{3\le p\le x\\p\text{ prime}}} F\bigl(V_1(p),\ldots,V_k(p)\bigr) =\E F(L_1,\ldots,L_k). \end{equation} The limit holds through all real $x$ and uses ordinary equal weighting of the primes.

primaryStatements.name: One-sided marked Type II estimate
primaryStatements.label: thm:type-II
primaryStatements.text: Fix $\delta,C,D_*>0$ and $q\in(0,1)$. Suppose $H_m,H_n\geq x^\delta$ and $X=H_mH_n\asymp x$. Let $F$ satisfy $|F(h)|\leq1$ and $F(ph)=F(h)$ for every prime in the groups \eqref{det:bands}. Let $\alpha_m$ be supported on an arbitrary interval in $[H_m,2H_m]$, where it has the value \[ \alpha_m=m^{iv}\left(\1_{m\text{ prime}} -\frac{\1_{m\text{ rough}}}{V(W)\log m}\right), \qquad |v|\leq L^C. \] Let $\beta_n$ be supported on rough integers in $[H_n,2H_n]$, with $|\beta_n|\leq L^C$. If $K$ is sufficiently large in terms of $\delta,C,D_*,q$, then \begin{equation} \left|\sum_{m,n}\alpha_m\beta_n F(mn-1)\mathcal W(mn-1)\right| \ll X L^{-D_*}. \end{equation} The required lower bound on $K$ is independent of the particular $a_i$. The implicit constant and the threshold for $x$ may depend on all the fixed parameters, including the $a_i$.

primaryStatements.name: The minor-arc moment
primaryStatements.label: prop:minor-moment
primaryStatements.text: For every fixed $E_0>0$, one can choose $A_0$ sufficiently large and then $K$ sufficiently large, in terms of $E_0,q$ and the fixed parameters of Theorem \ref{thm:type-II}, so that the operator with the good-state projections satisfies \begin{equation} \frac{1}{UV}\sum_{\substack{P\in\Omega\\P\ \mathrm{primitive}}} \inner{\mathbf u_P}{(\mathcal A\mathcal A^*)^R\mathbf u_P} \le L^{-E_0N}. \end{equation} The choices of $A_0,K$ do not depend on the particular fixed band exponents $a_1<\cdots<a_K$; the threshold for $x$ may depend on them. Consequently, for any prescribed fixed $A>0$, the determinant indicator in the expanded square of the preceding section can be replaced by \eqref{eq:det-major}, with error $O_A(XY L^{-A})$. In the resulting major term the disjointness restriction on the two unshared products $a,b$ can be omitted. Equivalently, with the notation of \eqref{det:cauchy-square} and \eqref{maj:sum}, \begin{equation} \abs{\mathcal Q_Y-\mathcal Q_Y^{\mathrm{maj}}} \ll_A XY L^{-A}. \end{equation} The precision needed in the pairing estimate \eqref{eq:det-pairing} for this consequence is independent of $K$.

primaryStatements.name: The determinant major term
primaryStatements.label: prop:major-term
primaryStatements.text: For every fixed $D>0$, the unrestricted major sum \begin{equation} \begin{split} \mathcal Q_Y^{\mathrm{maj}}={}& \left(\prod_{i=1}^K V_i^{-2}\right) \sum_{a,b,m,n,r,s} \eta(a/Y)\eta(b/Y)\alpha_m\overline{\alpha_r} \beta_n\overline{\beta_s}\, \mathcal H_{\mathfrak M}(bmn-ars;a,b) \end{split} \end{equation} satisfies \begin{equation} |\mathcal Q_Y^{\mathrm{maj}}|\ll_D XYL^{-D}. \end{equation} Here $a,b$ run independently over products of one prime from each $\mathcal P_i$, with no disjointness condition, and $\mathcal H_{\mathfrak M}$ denotes the kernel in \eqref{eq:det-major}. The estimate is uniform in the coefficient intervals, in $|v|\le L^C$, and in the admissible scale $Y$.

primaryStatements.name: Two-sided correlation
primaryStatements.label: thm:two-sided
primaryStatements.text: Fix $d\geq1$, $\eps>0$, and intervals $I_1,\ldots,I_d$ whose lower endpoints are at least $x^\eps$ and whose upper endpoints have product at most $x^{1-\eps}$. Let $\mathbf l=(l_1,\ldots,l_d)$ run over ordered tuples of distinct primes with $l_i\in I_i$, and put \begin{equation} l:=l_1\cdots l_d,\qquad C_x:=\sum_{\mathbf l}\frac1l,\qquad F_x(n):=\mathcal W(n) \left(\sum_{\mathbf l}\1_{l\mid n}-C_x\right). \end{equation} Suppose $G(n)=G(n_*)$ and $|G(n)|\leq L^C\tau(n_*)^C$, for fixed $C$. For every fixed smooth compactly supported $\Psi:(0,\infty)\to\C$ and every fixed $A>0$, \begin{equation} \sum_{w\geq1}\frac{\Psi(w/x)}w F_x(w)G(w+1)W_1(w)W_1(w+1)\ll_A L^{-A}. \end{equation} The constants and sufficiently-large-$x$ threshold may depend on all the fixed data, including the fixed inert bands, but the estimate is uniform over the active groups and slot intervals satisfying the stated bounds. The slots have no joint restriction other than distinctness.

primaryStatements.name: General graph transference input
primaryStatements.label: prop:graph-transfer
primaryStatements.text: Assume $\sum_\nu\sup|K_\nu|\leq L^{C_1}$, where $m_0,C_1$ are fixed independently of $J$. For every fixed $E>0$ there is $E_{\rm id}>0$, depending only on $E$ and the fixed group data, such that \[ \sup_{\Theta\in\R} \|\mathcal T_\zeta(\Theta)\|_{2\to2}\leq L^{-E_{\rm id}} \] has the following consequence for all sufficiently large fixed $J$. Let $I=[X,2X)$, with $x^\gamma\leq X\leq x^{1/\gamma}$ for fixed $\gamma>0$. If $f$ is supported on positions in $I$, is independent of the chosen marks, and satisfies \[ \sup|f|\leq\exp(O(\sqrt L)),\qquad \|f\|,\|g\|\leq X^{1/2}L^{C_3}, \] then \begin{equation} |\langle f,\mathcal A_\zeta g\rangle| \ll XL^{-E+2C_3}. \end{equation} The lower bound on $J$ may also depend on $m_0,C_1$. The threshold for $x$ may depend on $J,C_2,\gamma$. No further restriction on $\zeta$ is imposed beyond the ideal norm hypothesis. Taking absolute values of the individual transition coefficients gives row and column sums at most $L^{C_{\rm abs}}$, where $C_{\rm abs}$ is independent of $J$.

primaryStatements.name: Interior prime statistic
primaryStatements.label: thm:interior
primaryStatements.text: For every nonnegative $\Phi\in C_c^\infty((0,\infty))$, \begin{equation} \sum_{p\text{ prime}}\Phi((p-1)/x) \bigl(f_x(p-1)-C_x\bigr)=o(x/\log x). \end{equation} The limit holds through all real $x\to\infty$ for the slot intervals just described.

papers.title: Prime Predecessors with an Even Number of Prime Factors
papers.abstract: We prove that there are infinitely many primes p for which $p-1$ is squarefree and has an even number of prime factors. Equivalently, there are infinitely many primes p with $\mu(p-1)=1$.
papers.familySummary: Proves that the normalized ordered logarithms of the prime factors of $p-1$, counted with multiplicity, converge jointly to the Poisson–Dirichlet law $\mathrm{PD}(1)$ as p ranges uniformly over primes up to x and $x\to\infty$. This resolves the Ford–Konyagin–Luca conjecture. It also proves that infinitely many integers n have more than $n^{1-\varepsilon}$ totient preimages, for every ε > 0.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: There are infinitely many primes $p$ such that $p-1$ is squarefree and $\Omega(p-1)$ is even. In particular, there are infinitely many such primes under either convention for counting prime factors.

primaryStatements.name: Prime estimates
primaryStatements.label: pre:primes
primaryStatements.text: The prime number theorem holds with an error smaller than every fixed negative logarithmic power. Mertens' estimates give \[ \sum_{p\le y}\frac1p=\log\log y+O(1),\qquad \prod_{p\le y}\left(1-\frac1p\right) \sim\frac{e^{-\gamma_E}}{\log y}, \] where $\gamma_E$ is Euler's constant. For fixed $A,C>0$, uniformly for $r\le(\log y)^C$ and $(a,r)=1$, the Siegel--Walfisz estimate is \[ \#\{p\le y:p\equiv a\pmod r\} =\frac{\Li(y)}{\varphi(r)} +O_{A,C}\left(\frac{y}{(\log y)^A}\right). \] Its constants need not be effective.

primaryStatements.name: Large sieve and moment bounds
primaryStatements.label: pre:moments
primaryStatements.text: For arbitrary coefficients supported on the integers of an interval of length $H$, \[ \sum_{r\le R}\frac r{\varphi(r)} \sum_{\chi\bmod r}^{*} \left|\sum_n a_n\chi(n)\right|^2 \ll (H+1+R^2)\sum_n|a_n|^2. \] The asterisk denotes primitive characters. For every fixed integer $k\ge0$ there is $C_k$ such that \[ \sum_{n\le Y}\tau(n)^k\ll_k Y(\log(2Y))^{C_k},\qquad \sum_{n\le Y}\frac{\tau(n)^k}{n} \ll_k(\log(2Y))^{C_k}. \] If $P(t)=\sum_{n\le Y}c_n n^{it}$, then on any real interval $I$ of length $H$, \[ \int_I|P(t)|^2\,dt \ll (H+Y\log(2Y))\sum_n|c_n|^2. \] For a set $\mathcal T\subset I$ with mutual spacing at least one, \[ \sum_{t\in\mathcal T}|P(t)|^2 \ll (H+1+Y\log(2Y))(\log(2Y))^2\sum_n|c_n|^2. \] The constants in the last two estimates are absolute, independently of how the coefficients were formed.

primaryStatements.name: Derivative tests
primaryStatements.label: pre:derivatives
primaryStatements.text: Let $f$ be real-valued on an interval containing $H$ consecutive integers. If $f'$ is monotone and remains in $[j+\lambda,j+1-\lambda]$ for an integer $j$ and $0<\lambda\le1/2$, then \[ \sum_n\e(f(n))\ll\lambda^{-1}. \] If instead $f$ is twice continuously differentiable and $\lambda\le|f”|\le C\lambda$ throughout the interval, then \[ \sum_n\e(f(n))\ll_C H\sqrt\lambda+\lambda^{-1/2}. \] Both estimates apply on every subinterval satisfying their hypotheses.

primaryStatements.name: Twisted prime-slot correlation
primaryStatements.label: sh:correlation
primaryStatements.text: Let $F,G$ have the form \eqref{sh:core}, with possibly different coefficients, characters, intervals, and frequencies, subject to fixed bounds as above. For every fixed $D_0>0$ there is a fixed $B>0$ with the following property. Suppose that the sequence $\alpha$ in $F$ satisfies \begin{equation} \left|\sum_{m\in I}\alpha_m\chi(m)m^{-1+it}\right|\leq L^{-B} \quad\left( \begin{array}{l} I\subset[1,x^2]\text{ an interval},\\ \operatorname{mod}(\chi)\leq L^B,\quad |t|\leq L^B \end{array}\right). \end{equation} There is no discrepancy requirement on $G$. Uniformly for $xL^{-C}\leq Z\leq xL^C$, integers $0<|k|\leq L^C$, $|a_1|,|a_2|\leq L^C$, and smooth functions $\psi$ supported in a fixed compact subinterval of $(0,\infty)$ with $\|\psi^{(j)}\|_\infty\ll_j L^{C(j+1)}$, one has \begin{equation} \sum_{\substack{z>0\\z+k>0}}\frac{\psi(z/Z)}z z^{ia_1}(z+k)^{ia_2}\overline{F(z)}G(z+k) W_\ell(z)W_\ell(z+k)\varepsilon(z)\varepsilon(z+k) \ll L^{-D_0}. \end{equation} The exponent $B$ depends only on $D_0$ and the displayed fixed data.

primaryStatements.name: Transference input
primaryStatements.label: sh:transference
primaryStatements.text: The following are the Local Transference Theorem, its Endpoint Pairing Corollary, and the Absolute Physical Bounds Lemma of \cite[Section 3, Theorem 3.5, Corollary 3.11, and Lemma 3.4]{SmoothShifted}. Assume $\sum_\nu\sup|K_\nu|\leq L^{C_1}$, where $m_0,C_1$ are fixed independently of $J$. For every fixed $E>0$ there is an $E_{\rm id}>0$, depending only on $E$ and the group data, such that \[ \sup_{\Theta\in\mathbb R} \|\mathcal T_\zeta(\Theta)\|_{2\to2}\leq L^{-E_{\rm id}} \] implies the following conclusion for all sufficiently large fixed $J$. Let $I=[X,2X)$ with $x^\gamma\leq X\leq x^{1/\gamma}$ for some fixed $\gamma>0$. If $f$ is supported on positions in $I$, is independent of the chosen marks, and \[ \sup|f|\leq\exp(O(\sqrt L)),\qquad \|f\|,\|g\|\leq X^{1/2}L^{C_3}, \] then \begin{equation} |\langle f,\mathcal A_\zeta g\rangle| \ll XL^{-E+2C_3}. \end{equation} The lower bound for $J$ may depend on $m_0,C_1$; the threshold for $x$ may also depend on $J$, the fixed exponent bounding $|k|$, and $\gamma$. There is no additional restriction on $\zeta$ beyond the ideal norm hypothesis. The operator obtained by taking absolute values of all transition coefficients has row and column sums at most $L^{C_{\rm abs}}$, with $C_{\rm abs}$ independent of $J$.

primaryStatements.name: Residual ideal family and comparison kernels
primaryStatements.label: sh:ideal
primaryStatements.text:
The following are the Residual Ideal Operator Theorem and Comparison Kernel Lemma of \cite[Section 4, Theorem 4.1 and Lemma 4.3]{SmoothShifted}. For every prescribed $E_{m id}>0$ and fixed $C_4\geq0$, there are fixed $m_0,J_0,C_1$ such that, for each fixed $J\geq J_0$, a family consisting of the raw pattern $C_g=\varnothing$, $K_0=1$, and signed comparison patterns satisfies  egin{equation} \sum_
u\sup|K_
u|\leq L^{C_1},\qquad \sup_{\substack{\Theta\in\mathbb R\|\zeta|\leq L^{C_4}}} \|\mathcal T_\zeta(\Theta)\|_{2	o2} \leq L^{-E_{m id}}. \end{equation} The family is independent of the individual values of $\Theta,\zeta$, and all its defining parameters are independent of $J$. Split the big groups into two blocks. Every comparison frees nonempty sets of probes $A,B$ in the respective blocks and has coefficient  egin{equation} -(-1)^{|A|+|B|}\mathcal K_A(D_A,X_A)\mathcal K_B(D_B,X_B). \end{equation} Here $D_A,D_B$ are the free products, $X_A$ is the corresponding target-mark product, and $X_B$ the corresponding source-mark product. No shared label or final $\ell$ mark enters these kernels. For a slot set $\Lambda$, their exact form is  egin{equation} \mathcal K_\Lambda(D,X) =\sum_{j:
u_{\Lambda j}\geq\xi}  rac{\1_{\log D\in I_j}\1_{\log X\in I_j}}{
u_{\Lambda j}} \sum_{\substack{\chi\ {m primitive}\ \operatorname{cond}(\chi)\leq Q}} \overline{\chi(D)}\chi(X), \quad I_j=[jh,(j+1)h), \end{equation} where $
u_{\Lambda j}$ is the probability of the indicated cell under the independent slot laws. The quantities $Q,h^{-1},\xi^{-1}$ are fixed powers of $L$, with $h\leq1$. There are at most $Q^2$ characters and $O_{m_0}(1+TL^d/h)$ nonempty cells, and \[ \sup|\mathcal K_\Lambda|\leq Q^2\xi^{-1},\qquad \sup_X\mathbb E_D|\mathcal K_\Lambda(D,X)|\leq Q^2. \] More precisely, the parameters can be chosen, independently of $J$, so that for any fixed $A_0>0$, any tuple tests $f(X_B),g(X_A)$, and every $	heta\in\mathbb R$, $|\zeta|\leq L^{C_4}$,  egin{align} \Big|\mathbb E\,\overline{f(X_B)}g(X_A)  ig[&(X_AX_B)^{i\zeta}\e(	heta X_AX_B)
otag\ &-\mathcal K_A(D_A,X_A)\mathcal K_B(D_B,X_B) (D_AD_B)^{i\zeta}\e(	heta D_AD_B) ig]\Big| \leq L^{-A_0}\|f\|_2\|g\|_2. \end{align} All four label tuples in this expectation are independent. The tests need not be functions only of their products. Expanding the two kernels in \eqref{sh:comparison-kernel-product}, including all patterns, has total coefficient mass and number of terms bounded by fixed powers of $L$.

primaryStatements.name: Type II distribution
primaryStatements.label: ti:distribution
primaryStatements.text: Fix $D_*,b_*,C>0$. Let $U,V$ be dyadic scales such that \[ UV\asymp x,\qquad x^{b_*}\le U,V\le x^{1-b_*}, \] and let $K\subset[U,2U)$ and $J\subset[V,2V)$ be intervals. Suppose $|\alpha_m|,|\beta_n|\le L^C$ and $\alpha_m=0$ unless $P^-(m)>W$. There is a fixed $B$, depending only on these fixed data and on the fixed weight and cutoff data, for which the following holds. Assume that the sequence $\alpha_m\1_{m\in K}$ satisfies \eqref{sh:discrepancy}; explicitly, assume \begin{equation} \left|\sum_{m\in I}\alpha_m\1_{m\in K} \chi(m)m^{-1+it}\right|\le L^{-B} \quad\left( \begin{array}{c} I\subset[1,x^2]\text{ an interval},\\ \operatorname{mod}(\chi)\le L^B,\quad |t|\le L^B \end{array}\right). \end{equation} Then \begin{equation} \sum_{\substack{m\in K,\ n\in J,\ u\ge1\\mn=2u+1}} \alpha_m\beta_n A(u)\Psi(u/x) \ll xL^{-D_*}. \end{equation} The estimate is uniform in the intervals and coefficient sequences satisfying these assumptions. No discrepancy or smoothness assumption is imposed on $\beta$.

papers.title: The joint Dickman law for consecutive integers
papers.abstract: Let $P^+(n)$ denote the largest prime factor of n. We prove that $\log P^+(n)/\log n$ and $\log P^+(n+1)/\log n$ are asymptotically independent in ordinary natural density, with Dickman marginals. This resolves the Erdős–Pomerance joint Dickman conjecture positively and implies that the ordering $P^+(n)\lt P^+(n+1)$ has natural density 1/2.
papers.familySummary: Resolves the Erdős–Pomerance joint Dickman conjecture: the logarithmic sizes of the largest prime factors of n and $n+1$ are asymptotically independent in ordinary natural density. In particular, the integers satisfying $P^+(n)\lt P^+(n+1)$ have density 1/2.

papers.sourceAbstract: Let $P^+(n)$ denote the largest prime factor of $n$. We prove that $\log P^+(n)/\log n$ and $\log P^+(n+1)/\log n$ are asymptotically independent in ordinary natural density, with Dickman marginals. This resolves the Erd\H{o}s--Pomerance joint Dickman conjecture positively and implies that the ordering $P^+(n)<P^+(n+1)$ has natural density $1/2$.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main

primaryStatements.name: Mixed decorrelation
primaryStatements.label: prop:mixed

primaryStatements.name: Real short-interval comparison
primaryStatements.label: thm:labels-real-MR
primaryStatements.text: There is a function $r(H)$ tending to zero as $H\to\infty$ such that, for every real multiplicative function $g:\N\to[-1,1]$ and $2\leq H\leq X$, \begin{equation} \frac1X\int_X^{2X} |\mathcal A_Hg(z)-\mathcal L_Xg|^2\,dz\leq r(H). \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Complex short averages
primaryStatements.label: thm:labels-complex-MRT
primaryStatements.text: For every multiplicative function $g:\N\to\C$ with $|g|\leq1$ and $X\geq H\geq10$, \begin{equation} \frac1X\int_X^{2X}|\mathcal A_Hg(z)|^2\,dz \ll (1+M(g;X))e^{-M(g;X)} +\left(\frac{\log\log H}{\log H}\right)^2 +(\log X)^{-1/50}, \end{equation} with an absolute implied constant.

primaryStatements.name: Local coefficient and product laws
primaryStatements.label: prop:arith-local-laws
prop:amp-energy
primaryStatements.text: There is $c_5>0$, independent of all sufficiently large fixed $C_*$, for which the nonnegative energy below satisfies the displayed lower bound: \begin{equation} \begin{gathered} I_{2,x} = \frac1x\sum_{c\ge1} \rho_0(\log c/B)A(c) \sum_{m\ge1}K(m) \left| \sum_{\substack{a\ge1\\c\mid am+1}} A(a)K(l_a)\psi(a/(Tc)) \phi(am/x)F_x(am+1) \right|^2, \\ \liminf_{B\to\infty}\ \liminf_{x\to\infty} \frac{I_{2,x}}{BT}\ge c_5 \end{gathered} \end{equation} Its diagonal contribution is negligible: \[ \lim_{B\to\infty}\ \limsup_{x\to\infty} \frac{I_{2,x}^{\mathrm{diag}}}{BT}=0. \] Here $I_{2,x}^{\mathrm{diag}}$ denotes the terms with equal coefficient indices on expanding the square, and $l_a=(am+1)/c$ as in \eqref{eq:10}.

definitions.name: Regular prime sets
definitions.label: def:arith-regularity
definitions.text: For $S\subset\mathcal P$ put \[ N_g(S)=\begin{cases} |\{p\in S:\log p\le B^g\}|,&g<1,\\ |S|,&g=1. \end{cases} \] Let $Y_i=2^i\log P_0$, $0\le i\le i_{\max}$, where $i_{\max}$ is the first index with $Y_i\ge4B$. The set $S$ is regular if both of the following conditions hold: \[ (g/2-\tau)\ell\le N_g(S)\le(g/2+\tau)\ell \quad\hbox{for every grid point }g, \] and \[ |\{p\in S:\log p>Y_i\}| \ge0.4\log(B/Y_i)-C_* \quad(0\le i\le i_{\max}). \] An integer or profinite integer is regular when its set of dividing primes from $\mathcal P$ is regular. Multiplicities are not counted in these cutoffs.

Let $P^+(n)$ be the largest prime factor of $n$. The formalization proves the joint Dickman law in ordinary natural density: for every $0<a,b<1$, the density of integers satisfying $P^+(n)\le n^a$ and $P^+(n+1)\le n^b$ tends to $\rho(1/a)\rho(1/b)$, where $\rho$ is the Dickman function.

It also proves that each of the orderings $P^+(n)<P^+(n+1)$ and $P^+(n+1)<P^+(n)$ has natural density $1/2$.

lean.scopeText: The formalization proves Ostmann's inverse Goldbach conjecture. For any two sets $A,B$ of nonnegative integers, each containing at least two elements, the symmetric difference between their sumset $A+B$ and the set of primes is infinite. Thus no set differing from the primes by only finitely many elements can be decomposed as such a sumset. The linked statements include the full result and its two-infinite-summands case.

papers.title: Global Arthur Enhancements of Cuspidal Excursion Parameters
papers.abstract: Under the finite-level Ramanujan–Arthur decomposition stated in Theorem 1.1, we construct a global Arthur enhancement for every occurring cuspidal excursion parameter at a specified full finite level for a split connected semisimple group over a global function field. A single algebraic SL2 and a commuting Weil centralizer map recover the given parameter by diagonal specialization on the entire Weil group, including inertia. The result does not assert ellipticity, Arthur-packet classification, or a multiplicity formula.

primaryStatements.name: Restricted geometric Langlands
primaryStatements.label: inp:langlands
primaryStatements.text: There is a Frobenius-invariant union $Z$ of connected components of $\LocSys^{\mathrm{restr}}_{\Ghat}(\overline X)$ and an equivalence \[ \mathbb L_G^{\mathrm{restr}}:\cC \xrightarrow{\sim}\IndCoh_{\Nhat}(Z). \] It identifies $\cC_Y$ with $\IndCoh_Y(Z)$ for every closed $\Ghat$-invariant $Y\subset\Nhat$ and intertwines Hecke functors with tensoring by the corresponding evaluation bundles. If $f:Z\to Z$ sends a local system to its pullback along geometric Frobenius of $\overline X$, the functor corresponding to $\Phi=(\operatorname{Frob}_{\Bun})_*$ is $f^!$. The embedding $\cC\hookrightarrow\Shv(\Bun_G(\overline X),\E)$ preserves compact objects.

primaryStatements.name: Trace and ordinary local terms
primaryStatements.label: inp:trace
primaryStatements.text: There is a canonical isomorphism of complexes \[ \operatorname{LT}:\Tr(\Phi,\cC)\xrightarrow{\sim}\cA_{\E}, \] with the right-hand side in degree zero. For a compact object $M$ and a morphism $b:M\to\Phi M$, it sends the categorical class $[M,b]$ to the ordinary alternating trace function of the adjoint morphism $(\operatorname{Frob}_{\Bun})^*M\to M$. The function has finite support. This comparison is compatible with Hecke operations and with the sheaf--function operations of pullback, star tensor product, and compactly supported pushforward.

primaryStatements.name: Nonstandard duality
primaryStatements.label: inp:duality
primaryStatements.text: The pairing \begin{equation} \cC\otimes\cC\longrightarrow\operatorname{Vect}_{\E},\qquad (M,N)\longmapsto R\Gamma_c\bigl(\Bun_G(\overline X),M\overset{*}{\otimes}N\bigr) \end{equation} defines a self-duality of $\cC$. It is invariant under simultaneous Frobenius. If $M,N$ are compact, its value is a perfect complex, also after any finite Hecke representation is inserted in either variable.

primaryStatements.name: Components and deformation theory
primaryStatements.label: inp:components
primaryStatements.text: Every connected component $Z_\sigma$ of the restricted local-system stack has a unique semisimple isomorphism class $\sigma$. Its automorphism group $J=\Aut(\sigma)$ is reductive, possibly disconnected. There is a formal affine coarse space $S_\sigma$ with reduced space a point, and $Z_\sigma\to S_\sigma$ is relatively algebraic. After choosing a frame at a geometric point, the component is formal affine. For an affine infinitesimal stage $S_n\to S_\sigma$, its base change is affine; almost finite type stages and bounded Postnikov truncations may be used. These affine stages have coherent cohomology in each bounded range. The tangent complex at a local system $\tau$ is \begin{equation} T_\tau\LocSys^{\mathrm{restr}}_{\Ghat}(\overline X) \simeq R\Gamma(\overline X,\ghat_\tau)[1]. \end{equation} In particular the stack is quasi-smooth.

primaryStatements.name: Pure Weil lift
primaryStatements.label: inp:pure-lift
primaryStatements.text: Fix an abstract field isomorphism $\iota:\E\xrightarrow{\sim}\C$. If $Z_\sigma$ is Frobenius invariant, its semisimple point $\sigma$ admits a Weil structure that is $\iota$-pure of weight zero. In particular, writing $\ghat_\sigma$ for its adjoint local system, every Frobenius eigenvalue on $H^i(\overline X,\ghat_\sigma)$ has $\iota$-absolute value $q^{i/2}$, for $0\leq i\leq2$.

primaryStatements.name: The framed quadratic model
primaryStatements.label: mod:model
primaryStatements.text: The retained component $Z_\sigma$, with its Frobenius action, evaluation bundles at the chosen cyclic tuple, and singular-support map, admits the model \begin{equation} Z_\sigma\simeq \bigl[(\mu^{-1}(0))^{\wedge}_{\mathrm{unst}}/J\bigr]. \end{equation} Here $\mathrm{unst}$ is the inverse image of the origin under $V\to V/\!/J$, and completion is along this invariant null fiber. In this model: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item the singularity scheme has points $(x,z)$ satisfying $\mu(x)=0$ and $zx=0$, with $z\in\mathfrak j$; \item the support condition defined by $Y$ is the condition that the image of $z$ under $\mathfrak j\hookrightarrow\ghat$ belongs to $Y$; \item every evaluation representation of $K=\Ghat^d$ is the bundle associated to its restriction along $J\hookrightarrow K$; Frobenius has constant cyclic transport on these bundles; \item after removing the scalars $q^{1/2}$ on deformation points and $q^{-1}$ on singular points, Frobenius is a linear automorphism of the moment-map data, normalizing $J$ and the framed representation labels. Its eigenvalues on these normalized linear data have modulus one. \end{enumerate} The meaning of Frobenius on Hom complexes in \textup{(iv)} is fixed explicitly in Lemma \ref{mod:hom-action} below.

primaryStatements.name: Orbit generation
primaryStatements.label: orb:generation
primaryStatements.text: The objects $M_P$, for simple $P\in\mathsf E_e$, generate the compact category supported on $J.e$ in an open where it is closed. Here “generate” allows finite cones, shifts and summands. The category $\mathsf E_e$ is semisimple.

definitions.label: intro:characteristic
definitions.text: The following four conditions hold. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item The Lie algebra $\mathfrak h$ has an $H$-invariant nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form whose restriction to the center of $\Lie(M)$ is nondegenerate for every Levi subgroup $M$ of $H$. \item For each Levi subgroup $M$ of $H$, including $H$ itself, and each maximal torus $T_M\subset M$, restriction induces an isomorphism \[ k_0[\mathfrak m]^M\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } k_0[\mathfrak t_M]^{W_M},\qquad \mathfrak m=\Lie(M),\quad \mathfrak t_M=\Lie(T_M),\quad W_M=N_M(T_M)/T_M. \] \item The scheme-theoretic centralizer in $H$ of every semisimple element of $\mathfrak h$ is a Levi subgroup. \item For every extension $K/k_0$ and every nilpotent $n\in\mathfrak h\otimes_{k_0}K$, there is a parabolic subgroup $P\subset H_K$, defined over $K$, such that $n\in\Lie(R_u(P))$. \end{enumerate} Here a Levi subgroup is a Levi factor of a parabolic subgroup. Semisimple means geometrically conjugate into the Lie algebra of a maximal torus; nilpotent means that the geometric adjoint orbit closure contains zero.

papers.title: Ramanujan-Arthur Decompositions of Cuspidal Functions at Full Finite Level
papers.abstract: We prove rational and $\overline{\mathbb Q}_\ell$ decompositions of cuspidal automorphic functions for split semisimple groups over global function fields into subspaces indexed by nilpotent orbits of the dual group. The decompositions hold at every full finite level, with arbitrary divisor multiplicities. Each summand is governed by the same orbit at every unramified place and every complex embedding. At trivial level this proves Conjectures 3.4.5 and 3.4.6 of Gaitsgory–Lafforgue–Raskin. For split connected adjoint absolutely simple groups, we also prove that a cuspidal automorphic representation with one generic unramified local component is tempered at every unramified place. Thus globally generic cuspidal representations in this scope satisfy the unramified part of the generalized Ramanujan conjecture.

primaryStatements.label: main:generic-ramanujan
primaryStatements.text: Let \(F\) be the function field of a smooth projective geometrically connected curve over a finite field, and let \(G/F\) be split connected adjoint absolutely simple. Let \(\pi=\bigotimes'_x\pi_x\) be a complex cuspidal automorphic representation of \(G(\mathbb A_F)\). If \(\pi_v\) is unramified and generic at one place \(v\), then \(\pi_x\) is tempered at every place \(x\) at which it is unramified. primaryStatements.name: Derived Satake with Frobenius
primaryStatements.label: cat:satake
primaryStatements.text: The stable idempotent-complete tensor category generated by the normalized spherical Satake complexes is monoidally equivalent to \[ \operatorname{Perf}^{\Gd}(S). \] The normalized Satake object $\operatorname{Sat}(V)$ corresponds to $S\otimes V$. With the split Weil structures, Frobenius pullback corresponds to extension of scalars by \[ S\longrightarrow S,\qquad \alpha\longmapsto q\alpha \quad(\alpha\in\gd^*[-2]), \] and acts trivially on the representation labels.
