primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: For sufficiently large positive integers $H$, there are nonnegative functions $A_H(1;\cdot):[0,1)\to\mathbb R$, given by the finite arithmetic formula \eqref{eq:AH} below, which converge uniformly as $H\to\infty$ to a function $A(1;\cdot)$ satisfying \[ 0<\inf_{0\le s<1}A(1;s) \le\sup_{0\le s<1}A(1;s)<\infty. \] With the parameters \eqref{eq:renewal}--\eqref{eq:Gj}, \[ V(x)\sim\frac{x}{\log x}\,G_m A(1;\theta). \] Moreover, for every fixed real $c>0$, \[ \frac{V(cx)}{V(x)}\longrightarrow c. \]

primaryStatements.label: thm:companion
primaryStatements.text: For each fixed positive integer $k$, the functions $A_H(f_k;s)$ converge uniformly for $0\le s<1$, and \[ N_k(x)=\frac{x}{\log x}\,G_m\bigl(A(f_k;\theta)+o(1)\bigr). \] There are two possibilities. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item If some $d\in\mathcal V$ satisfies $\ell(d)>kd$, then \[ \inf_{0\le s<1}A(f_k;s)>0,\qquad N_k(x)\sim\frac{x}{\log x}\,G_m A(f_k;\theta) \asymp_k V(x). \] \item If no such $d$ exists, then $N_k(x)=0$ for every $x>0$, and $A(f_k;s)=0$ for every $s\in[0,1)$. \end{enumerate} The first alternative holds for $k=1,2$.

primaryStatements.label: prop:basic
primaryStatements.text: There is a set \(E_x\subseteq\mathcal V\cap[1,x]\) with \[ |E_x|\le\{\varepsilon_H+o_{x;H}(1)\}V(x) \] such that every preimage of every \(v\in(\mathcal V\cap[1,x])\setminus E_x\) is \(p_0\cdots p_La\) for a basic witness. One may take \[ \varepsilon_H\ll \e^{-cP}+K_H\exp\{-\exp(cP\rho^{-P})\}. \] For every basic witness, putting \(w=p_{R+1}\cdots p_La\), we have \begin{equation} \begin{gathered} p_1\cdots p_La\le\exp((\log x)^{0.8}),\\ \log w\le H\exp(0.62b_R)+\exp(2\widetilde b_L), \qquad w<p_R. \end{gathered} \end{equation} In particular \(w\) is bounded in terms of \(H\) alone, uniformly in the phase.

primaryStatements.label: prop:discard
primaryStatements.text: For \(t=x\) and \(t=x/c\), with the same \(x\)-dependent parameters, \[ |\mathcal D(t)| \le\{\varepsilon_H+o_{x;H}(1)\}\frac{xG_m}{\log x}. \] One may take \(\varepsilon_H\ll K_HH^{-2}\). For all the witnesses in \eqref{eq:good-conditions} we also have \begin{equation} P^+(D_i)<z_i,\qquad S_i<z_i,\qquad c h_i^{-20}\le b_{i+J_i}/b_i\le C h_i^{-18}. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.label: prop:comparison
primaryStatements.text:
There are absolute constants $C$ and $y_0$ such that the following holds. Let $y\ge y_0$, put $B_y=\log_2 y$, and let $b$ be an integer with $1\le b\le B_y$. Suppose that real cutoffs satisfy \[ Y_0=y,\qquad \e^\e\le S\le Y_b, \qquad Y_{j+1}<U_j<Y_j\quad(0\le j<b). \] Put \[ 
u_j= rac{\log_2 Y_j}{B_y}\quad(0\le j\le b), \qquad \mu_j= rac{\log_2 U_j}{B_y}\quad(0\le j<b), \qquad \delta=\sqrt{ rac{\log_2 S}{B_y}}. \] Fix a positive integer $D$ with $P^+(D)\le Y_b$ and a real $r\ge1$. Let $N$ count the ordered tuples \[ (p_0,\ldots,p_{b-1},q_0,\ldots,q_{b-1},D') \] in which $D'$ is a positive integer and the following conditions hold:  egin{enumerate}[label=	extup{(oman*)}] \item The $p_j,q_j$ are $S$-normal primes, $p_j
e q_j$, and \[ U_j\le P^+(p_j-1),P^+(q_j-1)\le Y_j \qquad(0\le j<b). \] \item $P^+(D')\le Y_b$ and \[ D\prod_{j=0}^{b-1}(p_j-1) =D'\prod_{j=0}^{b-1}(q_j-1)\le rac yr. \] \item The common product in 	extup{(ii)} is squarefree on primes greater than $Y_b$. \item The part of $p_0-1$ supported above $Y_1$ exceeds $\sqrt y$. \end{enumerate} Then  egin{equation}  egin{split} N\le{}& rac{y}{rD}(CB_y^6)^b(b+1)^{\Omega(D)} (\log Y_b)^{1+3b\log(b(b+1))}\ &\quad	imes (\log y)^{-2+\sum_{j=1}^{b-1}a_j
u_j+E_b}, \end{split} \end{equation} where  egin{equation} E_b=2\sum_{j=1}^{b-1}(
u_j-\mu_j) +\delta\sum_{i=2}^b(i\log i+i). \end{equation} Here $a_j$ is as defined in \eqref{eq:aj}. Empty sums are zero; in particular, when $b=1$ the cutoff in 	extup{(iv)} is $Y_1=Y_b$.

primaryStatements.name: Prefix collisions
primaryStatements.label: prop:collisions
primaryStatements.text: Fix $c>1$, and form all parameters from $x$, with $H$ fixed before $x$ tends to infinity. For $t=x$ or $t=x/c$, let \[ K(t)=\#\{(\tau,\sigma)\in\mathcal G(t)^2: \tau\ne\sigma,\ F(\tau)=F(\sigma)\}. \] There is a quantity $\epsilon_H\to0$, independent of the phase, such that \[ K(t)\le\bigl(\epsilon_H+o_{x;H}(1)\bigr) \frac{xG_m}{\log x}. \] The pairs counted here are ordered pairs of distinct tuples.

primaryStatements.name: A common prefix for all preimages
primaryStatements.label: prop:unique-prefix
primaryStatements.text: For $t=x$ or $t=x/c$, with the same parameters formed from $x$, \begin{equation} \bigl|\,|\mathcal T(t)|-V(t)\,\bigr| \le\bigl(\epsilon_H+o_{x;H}(1)\bigr)\frac{xG_m}{\log x}, \qquad\epsilon_H\longrightarrow0. \end{equation} There is a set $E^*(t)\subset\mathcal V\cap[1,t]$ for which both $|E^*(t)|$ and the number of tuples in $\mathcal T(t)$ with values in $E^*(t)$ are at most $(\epsilon_H+o_{x;H}(1))xG_m/\log x$, after enlarging $\epsilon_H$. For every $v\in(\mathcal V\cap[1,t])\setminus E^*(t)$ there is a unique tuple $(p_0,\ldots,p_R,d)\in\mathcal T(t)$ of value $v$, and every preimage of $v$ has this prefix and a remaining factor of totient $d$. In particular, \begin{equation} \ell(v)=p_0\cdots p_R\ell(d). \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: The unweighted prime sum
primaryStatements.label: prop:mass
primaryStatements.text: For each fixed $c>1$, both $t=x$ and $t=x/c$ satisfy \begin{equation} V(t)=\frac{t}{\log x} \bigl(M_1(x;H)+E_H(t;x)G_m\bigr), \qquad \lim_{H\to\infty}\limsup_{x\to\infty} \max_{t\in\{x,x/c\}}|E_H(t;x)|=0. \end{equation} All parameters in the two formulas are formed from the same $x$.

definitions.label: def:normal
definitions.text: For \(S\ge\e^\e\), a prime \(p\) is \(S\)-normal if \[ \Omega(p-1,1,S)\le2\log_2S \] and, for every \(S\le U<T\le p-1\), \[ \left|\Omega(p-1,U,T)-(\log_2T-\log_2U)\right| <\sqrt{\log_2S\,\log_2T}. \]

definitions.label: def:basic
definitions.text: A basic witness is a choice of primes \(p_0,\ldots,p_L\) and an integer \(a\ge1\) satisfying \begin{equation} \begin{gathered} p_0\ge x^{0.9},\qquad 0.9\widetilde b_i\le\log_2p_i\le1.1\widetilde b_i \quad(1\le i\le L),\\ (u_1,\ldots,u_L)\in S_L(\boldsymbol\xi),\qquad P^+(a)\le p_L,\qquad \log a\le\exp(2\widetilde b_L). \end{gathered} \end{equation} Here \(u_0=B\), and \(u_i=\log_2p_i\) for \(i\ge1\).

lean.scopeText:
Let $V(x)$ count the distinct values of Euler's totient function up to $x$. The formalization constructs the paper's explicit positive main term from finite arithmetic approximants and proves that their ratio tends to one. In particular, $V(cx)/V(x)\to c$ for every fixed $c>0$, answering the Erdős–Hall regular-variation question.

The formalization also gives asymptotics for totients $v\le x$ whose least preimage $\ell(v)=\min\{n\ge1:\varphi(n)=v\}$ lies between $kx$ and $(k+1)x$. The associated coefficient is positive under the stated existence condition; when no totient $d$ satisfies $kd<\ell(d)$, the count and coefficient are identically zero. The cases $k=1,2$ have positive coefficients.

papers.title: Short Egyptian fractions
papers.abstract: We prove a conjecture of Erdős: for every sufficiently large integer b, every rational number $a/b$ with $1\le a\lt b$ is a sum of $O(\log\log b)$ distinct positive unit fractions, with an absolute implied constant. This order is best possible when the numerator varies. We also show that both the number of expansions of 1 with exactly k distinct terms and the least integer at least 2 that never occurs as a denominator in such an expansion grow doubly exponentially in k: their double logarithms have order k.
papers.familySummary: Every rational $a/b$ with $1\le a\lt b$ is a sum of $O(\log\log b)$ distinct positive unit fractions. The worst-case minimum number of terms has the same order, resolving Erdős’s conjecture on short Egyptian fractions.
papers.subject: Number theory
papers.sourceAbstract: We prove a conjecture of Erd\H{o}s: for every sufficiently large integer $b$, every rational number $a/b$ with $1\le a<b$ is a sum of $O(\log\log b)$ distinct positive unit fractions, with an absolute implied constant. This order is best possible when the numerator varies. We also show that both the number of expansions of $1$ with exactly $k$ distinct terms and the least integer at least $2$ that never occurs as a denominator in such an expansion grow doubly exponentially in $k$: their double logarithms have order $k$.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: There are absolute constants $c_1,c_2>0$ and $b_0$ such that, for every integer $b\ge b_0$, \[ c_1\log\log b\le N(b)\le c_2\log\log b. \] In particular, the upper bound holds for every integer numerator $1\le a<b$.

primaryStatements.label: cor:counting
primaryStatements.text: There are absolute constants $c,C>0$ and $k_0$ such that, for every integer $k\ge k_0$, \[ ck\le\log\log F(k)\le Ck. \]

primaryStatements.label: cor:prescribed
primaryStatements.text: For every sufficiently large integer $k$, \[ \exp\bigl(\exp(k/600)\bigr)\le v(k)\le1+k^{2^{k-1}}. \] More precisely, \[ \frac{\log2}{257} \le\liminf_{k\to\infty}\frac{\log\log v(k)}k \le\limsup_{k\to\infty}\frac{\log\log v(k)}k \le\log2. \] Equivalently for the lower bound, every fixed $c<\log2/257$ satisfies $v(k)\ge\exp(\exp(ck))$ for every sufficiently large integer $k$. In particular $\log\log v(k)=\Theta(k)$.

primaryStatements.name: A dense set of short expansions
primaryStatements.label: prop:density
primaryStatements.text: There are absolute constants \(D_M>1\), \(L>0\), and \(S_0>1\) with the following property. Put \(D_X=D_M+2\) and \(D_C=4D_X\). For every real \(S\ge S_0\) and every integer \(C\) satisfying \[ e^{D_CS}\le C\le e^{2D_CS}, \] there are an integer \(M\) and a set \(G\subseteq\{1,\ldots,\lfloor X\rfloor\}\), where \(X=e^{D_XS}\), such that \[ e^S<M\le e^{D_MS}, \qquad \bigl|\{1,\ldots,\lfloor X\rfloor\}\setminus G\bigr|\le \frac X8. \] For each \(u\in G\), the fraction \(u/(MC)\) is a sum of at most \(L\log S\) unit fractions with integer denominators at least \(2\). Repetitions are allowed.

primaryStatements.label: prop:marked-length
primaryStatements.text: For every $\varepsilon>0$ there is an integer $m_\varepsilon$ such that every integer $m\ge m_\varepsilon$ occurs as an exact denominator in a representation of $1$ by distinct positive unit fractions with at most \[ \left(\frac{257}{\log 2}+\varepsilon\right)\log\log m \] terms.

lean.scopeText:
An Egyptian-fraction expansion writes a rational number as a sum of distinct unit fractions. The formalization proves that every $a/b$ with $1\le a<b$ has such an expansion and that the largest minimum length at denominator $b$ is $\Theta(\log\log b)$. If $F(k)$ counts exact $k$-term expansions of $1$, it also proves $\log\log F(k)=\Theta(k)$ and bounds every denominator in such an expansion.

Every integer $m\ge2$ occurs as a denominator in an expansion of $1$, with length eventually at most $(257/\log2+\varepsilon)\log\log m$ for every $\varepsilon>0$; padding can preserve that denominator. If $v(k)$ is the least integer at least $2$ absent from all exact $k$-term expansions of $1$, then eventually $e^{e^{k/600}}\le v(k)\le1+k^{2^{k-1}}$, and $\liminf_{k\to\infty}\log\log v(k)/k\ge\log2/257$.

papers.title: Positive lower density of large prime gaps
papers.abstract: For every fixed C > 0, we prove that a positive proportion of consecutive prime gaps exceed $C\log p$, where p is the smaller prime. The proportion is bounded below for every sufficiently large initial segment of the prime sequence, with a constant depending on C. It follows that the indices at which $p_n/n$ increases have positive lower asymptotic density, answering a question of Erdős and Prachar.
papers.familySummary: For every fixed C > 0, a positive proportion of consecutive prime gaps exceed $C\log p_n$, throughout every sufficiently large initial segment of the primes. The proportion may depend on C. Consequently, the indices where $p_n/n$ increases have positive lower density, answering Erdős and Prachar.
papers.subject: Number theory
papers.sourceAbstract: For every fixed $C>0$, we prove that a positive proportion of consecutive prime gaps exceed $C\log p$, where $p$ is the smaller prime. The proportion is bounded below for every sufficiently large initial segment of the prime sequence, with a constant depending on $C$. It follows that the indices at which $p_n/n$ increases have positive lower asymptotic density, answering a question of Erd\H{o}s and Prachar.

sections.title: From two adjacent intervals to gap counts

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: For every fixed real $C>0$, there are constants $c(C)>0$ and $N_0(C)$ such that, for every integer $N\ge N_0(C)$, \[ \#\{1\le n\le N:p_{n+1}-p_n>C\log p_n\}\ge c(C)N. \]

primaryStatements.label: cor:ratios
primaryStatements.text: The set \[ \left\{n\ge1:\frac{p_n}{n}<\frac{p_{n+1}}{n+1}\right\} \] has positive lower asymptotic density.

primaryStatements.name: Weights for adjacent intervals
primaryStatements.label: prop:weights
primaryStatements.text: For each fixed $\lambda>0$ there is a finite constant $K_\lambda>0$ with the following property. For every $\varepsilon>0$, there are weights $W_X(m)\ge0$, defined for integers $X<m\le2X$, such that \begin{align} \mathbb E_X W_X&\longrightarrow1, &\mathbb E_X(W_XV_J)&\longrightarrow\lambda,\\ \limsup_{X\to\infty}\mathbb E_X(W_XV_I)&\le\varepsilon, &\limsup_{X\to\infty}\mathbb E_X(W_XV_J^2)&\le K_\lambda,\\ \mathbb E_X W_X^2&=O_{\lambda,\varepsilon}(1). \end{align} The constant $K_\lambda$ is independent of $\varepsilon$.

primaryStatements.name: Moment identities and a detector bound
primaryStatements.label: prop:weight-moments
primaryStatements.text: Hold $\lambda$, $k$, and the family $(f_j)_{0\le j\le k}$ fixed. Then, as $X\to\infty$, \begin{align} \mathbb E_XZ^2&\longrightarrow w:=\sum_{j=0}^k\alpha_j\|f_j\|_2^2, &\mathbb E_XZ^4&=O_{\lambda,k,\mathbf f}(1), \\ \mathbb E_X(Z^2V_J)&\longrightarrow\lambda w, &\mathbb E_X(Z^2V_I)&\longrightarrow v:=\lambda\sum_{j=0}^k\alpha_j \|f_j+Tf_{j+1}\|_2^2. \end{align} Choose once and for all a real $G\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)$ with $G(0)=1$ and $G(u)=0$ for $u\ge\tau$, and put \[ c_G=\int_0^\infty |G'(u)|^2\,du, \qquad C_*=\lambda+\lambda^2c_G^2. \] For every fixed family as above, \begin{equation} \limsup_{X\to\infty}\mathbb E_X(Z^2V_J^2)\le C_*w. \end{equation} In particular, $C_*$ is independent of $k$ and of the family $(f_j)$.

primaryStatements.name: Cancellation between high dimensions
primaryStatements.label: prop:dimension-cancellation
primaryStatements.text: For every fixed $\lambda>0$, there are families of the type used in Proposition \ref{prop:weight-moments}, with increasing finite maximum dimension $k$, for which $w\to1$ and $v\to0$.

primaryStatements.name: Uniform mixed moments
primaryStatements.label: prop:mixed-moments
primaryStatements.text: Put $L=\log X$, where $X$ tends to infinity through integers, and let $\mathbb E_X$ denote the average over $X<m\le2X$. Fix nonnegative integers $j_1,\ldots,j_R$. For each $r$, let $F_r$ be a real function on $[0,\infty)^{j_r}$ admitting a smooth compactly supported extension to $\mathbb R^{j_r}$, and suppose that on the orthant it vanishes outside \[ v_1+\cdots+v_{j_r}\le\rho_r. \] Here the support budgets $\rho_r\ge0$ are fixed. Dimension zero means a scalar, with support budget zero. For positive divisors define \[ D_{F_r}(m;\mathbf b^{(r)})= \sum_{d_{r,\ell}\mid m+b_{r,\ell}\ (1\le\ell\le j_r)} \prod_{\ell=1}^{j_r}\mu(d_{r,\ell}) F_r\left(\left(\frac{\log d_{r,\ell}}L\right)_{\ell=1}^{j_r}\right). \] For $j_r=0$, this means $D_{F_r}=F_r$. Let $\Gamma=\{(r,\ell):1\le r\le R,\ 1\le\ell\le j_r\}$, and fix a surjection $\kappa:\Gamma\to\{1,\ldots,t\}$. Write $\mathcal M_i=\kappa^{-1}(\{i\})$. Take distinct integer shifts $a_1,\ldots,a_t$ with $|a_i|\le DL^B$, where $D>0$ and $B\ge1$ are fixed, and set $b_{r,\ell}=a_{\kappa(r,\ell)}$. Choose $\delta\in\{0,1\}$. In the marked case take one more shift $a_0$, distinct from these and satisfying the same bound. Put \[ (\chi_\delta(m),\mathcal H)= \begin{cases} (1,\{a_1,\ldots,a_t\}),&\delta=0,\\ (\vartheta(m+a_0),\{a_0,a_1,\ldots,a_t\}),&\delta=1, \end{cases} \qquad \vartheta(n)=(\log n)1_{\{n\text{ prime}\}}. \] Assume $\sum_r\rho_r<1$ if $\delta=0$, and $\sum_r\rho_r<1/2$ if $\delta=1$. Then there is a real constant $\mathcal C$, depending only on the functions and $\kappa$, such that \begin{equation} \mathbb E_X\left[\chi_\delta(m)\prod_rD_{F_r}(m;\mathbf b^{(r)})\right] =L^{-t}\left\{\mathfrak S(\mathcal H)\mathcal C +O\!\left(L^{-1/2}(\log L)^A\right)\right\}. \end{equation} Here $A$ is a fixed finite number depending only on $\sum_rj_r$; the implied constant may depend on all the fixed data, but is uniform in the actual shifts. In particular the error is additive when $\mathfrak S(\mathcal H)=0$. If each $|\mathcal M_i|$ is at most two, the constant is \begin{equation} \mathcal C= \int\prod_r\left((-1)^{j_r}\partial_1\cdots\partial_{j_r}F_r\right) \big((y_{\kappa(r,\ell)})_{\ell=1}^{j_r}\big) \prod_{i:\,|\mathcal M_i|=2}dy_i, \end{equation} where $y_i=0$ for $|\mathcal M_i|=1$, and each integrated variable ranges over $[0,\infty)$. The zero-dimensional derivative is the original scalar. When $\Gamma$ is empty, take $t=0$ and $\mathcal C=\prod_rF_r$.

Thus the normalized prime sequence has a positive-density set of increases. This is the prime-ratio corollary associated with the paper's theorem on a positive lower density of large prime gaps.

papers.title: Integral points on character varieties of curves
papers.abstract: We prove potential Zariski density of integral points on SLr-character varieties of smooth complex curves in every rank. The result allows prescribed quasi-unipotent boundary monodromy, including exact nonsemisimple conjugacy classes, and holds on every component over the full ring of integers of one finite extension. Here integrality is measured in the ambient character variety, while the exact boundary conditions are imposed on the complex representation.
papers.familySummary: Resolves the determinant-one curve case of Litt's integral-density question. For every smooth connected complex algebraic curve and every rank, integral points become Zariski dense in every component of its SLr character variety over the full ring of integers of one number field. Prescribed quasi-unipotent boundary conjugacy classes are allowed, including nonsemisimple classes.
papers.subject: Number theory
papers.sourceAbstract: We prove potential Zariski density of integral points on $\SL_r$-character varieties of smooth complex curves in every rank. The result allows prescribed quasi-unipotent boundary monodromy, including exact nonsemisimple conjugacy classes, and holds on every component over the full ring of integers of one finite extension. Here integrality is measured in the ambient character variety, while the exact boundary conditions are imposed on the complex representation.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let $X$ be a smooth connected complex algebraic curve and let $r\geq1$. For prescribed quasi-unipotent conjugacy classes $C_1,\ldots,C_s$ as above, let $K\subset\C$ be a number field containing their eigenvalues. There is a finite extension $L/K$ such that \[ M_r(X)(\cO_L)\cap Y(\C) \] is Zariski dense in $Y$, and hence in every irreducible component of $Y$. The same conclusion holds when only the characteristic polynomial of each boundary monodromy is prescribed, with all its roots roots of unity. It also holds for the entire character variety without boundary conditions; in that case one may take $K=\Q$. For the relative statements and for projective $X$, one may take distinct primes $p,q>r$ and \begin{equation} F=K(\sqrt2,\zeta_{pq}),\qquad L=F\bigl(\zeta_r,\{u^{1/r}:u\in\cO_F^\times\}\bigr), \end{equation} where $\zeta_m$ denotes a primitive $m$th root of unity. In the projective case there are no boundary conditions and $K=\Q$.

primaryStatements.name: Diagram density
primaryStatements.label: thm:diagram-density
primaryStatements.text: For every surface diagram $D$ with ranks at most $r$ and prescribed scalar puncture monodromies in $F$, its integral solutions over $R$ are Zariski dense in $\mathcal S(D)$.

primaryStatements.label: prop:nonclosed-reduction
primaryStatements.text: Let $2\leq n\leq r$, and suppose integral solutions are dense for every surface diagram of ranks less than $n$. Then they are dense for every normalized diagram of ranks at most $n$ whose rank-$n$ facets have nonempty boundary. Closed facets of smaller rank are allowed.

primaryStatements.label: prop:surface-irreducibility
primaryStatements.text: For \(n\geq2\), \(g\geq2\), and \(c^n=1\), the variety \(\mathcal R_{n,g}(c)\) is irreducible of dimension \((2g-1)n^2+1\).

lean.scopeText:
The integral-density question asks whether integral points become Zariski dense in every component of a curve character variety after one finite extension of the number field. The linked formalization proves a supporting compatibility result for its marked-surface construction. Given a proper diagram with finitely many vertices, a chosen seam with maximal adjacent facet rank and a positive-genus parent, puncture data, an existing solution over a field, and a chosen boundary occurrence, the produced marked values satisfy every seam equation.

This is conditional compatibility of the produced solution. Potential integral density, including the prescribed-boundary and all-component conclusions, remains outside the selected statement.

papers.title: Bounded-Step Walks on Gaussian Primes
papers.abstract: We prove the Gaussian moat conjecture: no infinite walk through distinct Gaussian primes can have bounded steps. More strongly, for each fixed finite step bound, the connected components of the Gaussian-prime graph have uniformly bounded size. This bound applies to every starting prime, including primes on the coordinate axes, and is nonexplicit. The proof constructs a finite periodic sieve obstruction using geometric sampling and information-theoretic estimates.

More strongly, for every distance bound D, the graph joining Gaussian primes at distance at most D has uniformly bounded finite component sizes, depending only on D, including primes on the coordinate axes.

primaryStatements.name: Uniform component bound
primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: For every finite real $D$ there is a finite $B_D$ such that every connected component of $G_D$ has at most $B_D$ vertices. The bound is independent of the starting prime and includes primes on the coordinate axes. Consequently every sequence of distinct Gaussian primes whose successive distances are at most $D$ has at most $B_D$ terms.

primaryStatements.name: Finite sieve obstruction
primaryStatements.label: thm:sieve
primaryStatements.text: For every $D\ge1$ there is a finite set $\mathcal P_D$ of rational primes congruent to $1$ modulo $4$ such that $\mathcal A(\mathcal P_D)$ contains no infinite sequence of distinct points with successive distances at most $D$. The set $\mathcal P_D$ depends only on $D$.

primaryStatements.name: From a periodic obstruction to a uniform bound
primaryStatements.label: prop:periodic
primaryStatements.text: Fix $D\ge1$ and a finite set $\mathcal P$ of rational primes congruent to $1$ modulo $4$. Suppose that $\mathcal A(\mathcal P)$ contains no infinite self-avoiding walk with steps at most $D$. Put \[ Q=\prod_{p\in\mathcal P}p,\qquad K_D=\#\{v\in\Z[i]:|v|\le D\}, \] and let $E$ be the set of associates of the selected Gaussian factors. For every component $C$ of $G_D$, \[ \#C\le\max\{Q^2,\ |E|+(K_D-1)|E|Q^2\}. \]

primaryStatements.name: One-step coverage transfer
primaryStatements.label: thm:transfer
primaryStatements.text: Use the signed coordinates and the experiment just defined, with integers $1\le s\le k$ and $n\ge1$. Let \[ 0<\tau\le3/8,\quad 0<\delta\le1/64,\quad \tau'=\tau+4\delta,\quad 0<\beta'\le\beta<1, \quad 0<\eta\le1,\quad 0\le\eta'\le1. \] Suppose that at every $a$ in the support of $A$, all but a fraction at most $\eta'$ of the signed coordinates have $(\tau',\beta')$ coverage for $\phi_c(y(a)+h_1)$ under the law conditional on $A=a$. Assume also \begin{align} \E_S H(F_S(Y))&\ge(1-\epsilon)s\overline L, &H(\calH)&\le\kappa s\overline L,\\ \eta'&\le\eta\delta/100, &\epsilon+\kappa&\le\eta\delta\beta'/16, \end{align} where $\epsilon,\kappa\ge0$. Finally, for every coordinate size $p=p_j$, assume \begin{align} p\exp(-\delta^2np^{-\beta}/2)&\le\delta/100, &\delta^{-1}&<p^{\beta'/2},\\ \log(2e/\delta)&\le(\beta'/4)\log T. \end{align} Then all but a fraction at most $\eta$ of the coordinates have $(\tau,\beta)$ coverage for $\phi_c(Z)$.

primaryStatements.name: Terminal residue coverage
primaryStatements.label: prop:coverage
primaryStatements.text: For all sufficiently large \(M\), uniformly over the batches, \(0\le i\le J\), and all exact start times \(a\ge0\) at \(A_i\), all but a fraction at most \(\eta_i\) of the signed primes satisfy \begin{equation} \#\{u\in\Z[i]/(\pi):b_{i,a,\pi}(u)<\tau_i/p\} <p^{1-\beta_i}. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Information cost of one batch
primaryStatements.label: prop:information-rate
primaryStatements.text: There is a constant \(c_1>0\), depending only on the fixed schedule parameters, such that for all sufficiently large \(M\) and every batch in \eqref{eq:batches}, \begin{equation} \frac{1}{L_T}\, \E_{\mathcal C} I\bigl(X'_T;W_{L_T}(t_*)\mid O'_T\bigr) \ge \frac{c_1}{\log T}. \end{equation} The threshold for \(M\) is uniform over all infinite self-avoiding \(D\)-step walks in \(\mathcal A(\mathcal P_M)\).

lean.scopeText: The Gaussian moat problem asks whether an infinite walk through distinct Gaussian primes can have bounded step lengths. The formalized result gives a negative answer for every real step bound $D$. More strongly, one finite bound depending only on $D$ limits the size of every connected component of the bounded-step graph and the length of every injective bounded-step walk. Axis primes and all associates are included. No explicit function of $D$ is supplied.

papers.title: Primitive roots for every admissible integer base
papers.abstract: We prove the infinitude assertion in Artin's primitive root conjecture: for every integer a that is neither −1 nor a square, there are at least $c_a x/(\log x)^2$ primes in $(x,2x)$ with primitive root a, for some $c_a\gt 0$ and every sufficiently large x.

primaryStatements.label: thm:primitive-root
primaryStatements.text: For every admissible integer $a$, there are constants $c_a>0$ and $x_a\ge2$ such that, for every real $x\ge x_a$, \[ \#\{p\text{ prime}:x<p<2x,\ p\nmid a,\ \ord_p(a)=p-1\} \ge c_a\frac{x}{(\log x)^2}. \]

primaryStatements.label: thm:hecke-zero-free
primaryStatements.text: Let $F$ be a cyclotomic number field containing $\mu_{12}$. For every finite-order Hecke character $\eta$ of $F$, the meromorphic continuation of $L_F(s,\eta)$ has no zeros in \[ \re s>1-10^{-6}. \]

primaryStatements.name: Primes with controlled predecessors
primaryStatements.label: prop:controlled
primaryStatements.text: Let $M$ be a fixed positive multiple of $8$, let $c\in\{2,4\}$, and let $u$ be an integer satisfying \begin{equation} (u,M)=1,\qquad c\mid u-1,\qquad \left(\frac{u-1}{c},\frac Mc\right)=1. \end{equation} For every sufficiently large real $x$, there are $\gg_{M,c,u}x/L^2$ distinct primes $p\in(x,2x)$ satisfying \begin{equation} p\equiv u\pmod M,\qquad p-1=crQ, \qquad Q>x^{0.9}\ \text{prime}, \end{equation} where $r$ is a positive integer all of whose prime divisors lie in \[ \bigl(\exp(L^{0.1}),\exp(L^{0.3})\bigr). \]

primaryStatements.name: Uniform bound for complete splitting
primaryStatements.label: prop:splitting
primaryStatements.text: Fix an integer $a$ with $|a|>1$, and put $\delta_0=10^{-6}$. For all sufficiently large real $x$ and all primes $q$ sufficiently large in terms of $a$, with $q\le\exp(L^{0.3})$, one has \begin{equation} \#\{p\text{ prime}:x<p\le2x,\ p\text{ splits completely in }K_q\} \ll_a \frac{x}{q(q-1)L}+x^{1-\delta_0}. \end{equation} The implied constant and the threshold for $x$ are independent of $q$. For $a=2$, every prime $q\ge5$ is allowed, with absolute constants and an absolute threshold for $x$.

primaryStatements.name: Reflected second moment
primaryStatements.label: prop:reflection
primaryStatements.text: Let \(F\) be a fixed cyclotomic field containing \(\mu_{12}\), let \(S\) and the arithmetic data be as above, and fix a compact subset \(\mathscr K\subset F_S^\times\). For every \(\epsilon>0\), every \(Z\geq2\), and all dyadic lengths \(P,D\geq1\), \begin{equation} \sum_{\substack{m\in\mathscr B_Z(\mathscr K)\\ P\leq q_{\mathfrak h(m)}<2P\\ D\leq q_{\mathfrak d(m)}<2D}} |B_m(Z)|^2 \ll_{F,S,\eta,\mathscr K,\epsilon} Z^\epsilon P^{1/2}\left(D+\frac{D^2P}{Z}\right). \end{equation} In particular, \begin{equation} \sum_{m\in\mathscr B_Z(\mathscr K)}|B_m(Z)|^2 \ll_{F,S,\eta,\mathscr K,\epsilon} Z^{2M_0-1+\epsilon}. \end{equation} The estimate is uniform if \(\mathscr K\) is multiplied by an element of any fixed compact subset of the norm-one group of \(F_S^\times\).

primaryStatements.name: The exterior theta coefficient
primaryStatements.label: cor:theta-exterior-coefficient
primaryStatements.text: At every exterior prime use an allowed prime generator as the uniformizer in \Cref{prop:theta-input}. Let \(A\in R\setminus\{0\}\) be an allowed generator of an integral exterior ideal \(\mathfrak A\). Then \begin{equation} \prod_{\mathfrak p\notin S}W_{\mathfrak p}(a(A)) = \begin{cases} \displaystyle \frac{\gamma_2(\mathfrak c)} {q_{\mathfrak c}^{1/2}q_{\mathfrak n}}, &\mathfrak A=\mathfrak c\mathfrak n^3,\quad \mathfrak c\ \text{squarefree},\\[2mm] 0,&\text{otherwise}. \end{cases} \end{equation} In the first case \(\mathfrak c,\mathfrak n\) are uniquely determined; they need not be coprime.

primaryStatements.label: prop:probe-low

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Assume Inputs \ref{input:hecke}, \ref{input:marked}, \ref{input:block}, and \ref{input:density}. Let \(k\ge1\) and let \(q_1,\ldots,q_k\) be distinct positive primes. There are constants \(c_{\mathbf q}>0\) and \(x_{\mathbf q}>1\) such that, for every real \(x\ge x_{\mathbf q}\), at least \[ c_{\mathbf q}\frac{x}{(\log x)^2} \] primes \(p\in(x,2x)\) satisfy \[ p\nmid q_1\cdots q_k, \qquad \ord_p(q_i)=p-1\quad(1\le i\le k). \]

primaryStatements.name: A prime reservoir in a fixed progression
primaryStatements.label: prop:reservoir
primaryStatements.text: Assume Inputs \ref{input:marked}, \ref{input:block}, and \ref{input:density}. Let \(M\ge1\) be odd and squarefree, and let \(a\) be a residue class modulo \(M\) with \(\gcd(a(a-1),M)=1\). There are constants \(c_{M,a}>0\) and \(x_{M,a}>1\) such that, for every real \(x\ge x_{M,a}\), at least \(c_{M,a}x/L^2\) primes \(p\) satisfy \[ x<p<2x,\qquad p\equiv a\pmod M,\qquad p=4rQ+1, \] where \(r\) is a positive integer, \(Q>x^{0.9}\) is prime, and \[ \exp(L^{0.1})<\ell<\exp(L^{0.3}) \qquad\text{for every prime }\ell\mid r. \] The case \(M=1\) is included.

primaryStatements.name: A uniform bound for order obstructions
primaryStatements.label: prop:splitting
primaryStatements.text: Assume Input \ref{input:hecke}. For each fixed positive prime \(q\), for all sufficiently large real \(x\), and uniformly over primes \(\ell\) with \(\exp(L^{0.1})<\ell<\exp(L^{0.3})\), one has \[ \#\left\{\,p\text{ prime}: \begin{array}{l} x<p<2x,\quad p\nmid q\ell,\quad p\equiv1\pmod\ell,\\ q^{(p-1)/\ell}\equiv1\pmod p \end{array}\right\} \ll_q \frac{x}{\ell(\ell-1)L}+x^{1-\eta}. \]

definitions.name: Marked Type II estimate
definitions.label: input:marked
definitions.text: (i) Coefficient criterion. Fix \(\delta,C,D_*>0\). Suppose \(H_m,H_n\ge x^\delta\) and \(X=H_mH_n\asymp x\), with fixed comparison constants. Let \(F:\mathbb Z_{>0}\to\mathbb C\) satisfy \(|F(h)|\le1\) and \(F(ph)=F(h)\) for every group prime \(p\) and every \(h\ge1\). Let \((\alpha_m)\) and \((\beta_n)\) be scalar sequences supported on \(W\)-rough integers in \([H_m,2H_m]\) and \([H_n,2H_n]\), respectively, with \(\alpha\) supported on an arbitrary interval \(I\subseteq[H_m,2H_m]\), and with \(|\alpha_m|,|\beta_n|\le L^C\). Suppose that for every fixed \(A_0,B,A>0\), every Dirichlet character \(\chi\) modulo \(k\le L^{A_0}\), and every \(|t|\le2XL^B\), \begin{equation} \left|\frac1{H_m}\sum_m\alpha_m\chi(m)m^{it}\right|\ll_A L^{-A}, \end{equation} uniformly in the permitted interval, character, and frequency. The constant and threshold in this hypothesis may depend on \(A_0,B,A\), the fixed setup, and all further fixed parameters defining the coefficients. Then \begin{equation} \left|\sum_{m,n}\alpha_m\beta_n F(mn-1)\mathcal W(mn-1)\right| \ll XL^{-D_*} \end{equation} when \(K\) is sufficiently large in terms of the fixed data, independently of the particular \(a_i\). Its implicit constant and threshold may depend on all fixed data, including the common constants and thresholds in \eqref{eq:marked-cancellation} and the \(a_i\). With those data fixed, the bound is uniform over the permitted \(F\), dyads, intervals, and coefficients. (ii) Rough coefficient cancellation. Retain the marked data and the hypotheses on \(F,\beta,H_m,H_n\), without assuming a previously chosen \(\alpha\). Fix \(0<\gamma<w_-<w_+<1\), and assume \begin{equation} [\log H_m/L,\log(2H_m)/L]\subseteq[w_-,w_+]. \end{equation} For every interval \(I\subseteq[H_m,2H_m]\) and every \(|v|\le L^C\), the coefficient \begin{equation} \alpha_m^{(0)}=m^{iv}\left( \one_{P^-(m)>x^\gamma} -\frac{D_\gamma(\log m/L)}{LV(W)}\one_{P^-(m)>W}\right) \quad(m\in I), \end{equation} set equal to zero outside \(I\), satisfies \eqref{eq:marked-cancellation} with \(\alpha^{(0)}\) in place of \(\alpha\), for every fixed \(A_0,B,A>0\). This assertion is uniform in the permitted dyads, interval, character, frequency \(t\), and \(v\). Its constant and threshold may depend on the fixed parameters, including \(\gamma,w_-,w_+\); in particular \(\gamma\) and \(w_--\gamma\) are fixed before \(x\) grows.

definitions.name: Block sieve
definitions.label: input:block
definitions.text:
Let $z>1$, let $\mathcal A$ be a finite set with nonnegative weights $\lambda_
u$ for $
u\in\mathcal A$, and let $\mathcal D$ be a set of designated primes at most $z$. For each $p\in\mathcal D$ let $\mathcal A_p\subseteq\mathcal A$ be its bad condition. For a squarefree product $\ell$ of primes in $\mathcal D$, put $\mathcal A_\ell= igcap_{p\mid\ell}\mathcal A_p$, with $\mathcal A_1=\mathcal A$. Suppose that, including for $\ell=1$, \[ \sum_{
u\in\mathcal A_\ell}\lambda_
u=Yg(\ell)+R(\ell), \qquad Y\ge0, \] where $g$ is multiplicative on these squarefree products and $g(1)=1$. Extend $g(p)$ by zero at primes outside $\mathcal D$. Suppose that for fixed constants $\eta_0>0$ and $C_0<\infty$, \[ 0\le g(p)\le1-\eta_0, \qquad \sum_{u<p\le u^2}g(p)\le C_0\quad(u>1). \] Write \[ S=\sum_{
u\in\mathcal A\setminus igcup_{p\in\mathcal D}\mathcal A_p} \lambda_
u. \] For every sufficiently large even integer $H$, the weight avoiding all the bad conditions is  egin{equation}  egin{split} S={}&Y\prod_{p\le z}(1-g(p)) igl(1+O_{\eta_0,C_0}(e^{-H}) igr)\ &+O_{\eta_0,C_0}\left( \sum_{\substack{\ell\le z^{4H+2}\ \ell\ \mathrm{squarefree}\ p\mid\ell\Rightarrow p\in\mathcal D}} |R(\ell)|ight). \end{split} \end{equation} The threshold for $H$ and the implied constants depend only on $\eta_0,C_0$. In particular, the constants are uniform when $H$ grows, and the remainder sum has no additional coefficient or multiplicity factor. For $H=2$ there is the upper bound  egin{equation} S\ll_{\eta_0,C_0} Y\prod_{p\le z}(1-g(p))+ \sum_{\substack{\ell\le z^{10}\ \ell\ \mathrm{squarefree}\ p\mid\ell\Rightarrow p\in\mathcal D}} |R(\ell)|. \end{equation} Both remainder sums include only squarefree products of the designated primes, with $\ell=1$ included. This is the form stated in \cite[Lemma 11.1, Equations (11.2)--(11.3)]{PrimitiveRoot2}.

definitions.name: Rough-number density
definitions.label: input:density
definitions.text: For the density $D_\gamma(w)$ defined in Section \ref{sec:marked-family}, there are absolute constants $b_d,c_d,C_d>0$ such that, for every fixed $0<b<\min(b_d,1/2)$, \begin{equation} \int_b^{1/2}D_t(1-t)\frac{\dd t}{t}=D_b(1)-1, \qquad D_b(1)\le\frac{e^{-\gamma_E}}{b} \bigl(1+C_de^{-c_d/b}\bigr). \end{equation} Here $\gamma_E$ is Euler's constant, and the value of the integrand at $t=1/2$ is immaterial. These are the assertions of \cite[Lemma 11.2, Equations (11.6)--(11.7)]{PrimitiveRoot2}.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let $K$ be an imaginary quadratic number field and $E/K$ an elliptic curve. There is an isobaric automorphic representation $\pi_E$ of $\GL_2(\A_K)$ with trivial central character and weight zero such that, for every prime $l$ and every isomorphism $\iota:\overline\Q_l\xrightarrow{\sim}\C$, \[ r_\iota(\pi_E)\simeq H^1_{\et}(E_{\overline K},\overline\Q_l). \] At every finite place $v\nmid l$ one has \[ \iota\WD\bigl(H^1_{\et}(E_{\overline K},\overline\Q_l) |_{G_{K_v}}\bigr)^{\Fss} \simeq \rec_{K_v}\bigl(\pi_{E,v}\otimes|\det|_v^{-1/2}\bigr). \] The unitary parameter at the complex place is $z\mapsto\diag(z/|z|,\overline z/|z|)$. In particular every local factor agrees, and \[ L(E/K,s)=L(\pi_E,s-1/2). \] If $E$ has no complex multiplication, $\pi_E$ is cuspidal. In the CM case it is given by automorphic induction of a Hecke character, or by an isobaric sum when the CM field is already $K$.

primaryStatements.label: geo:compact-type
primaryStatements.text: Suppose that $k$ contains $\mu_m$. At $R=O$, the special fiber of the model in Lemma \ref{geo:semistable-models} is a rational curve joined at distinct points to $m$ copies of $E$, all defined over $k$. Rotations cyclically permute the elliptic components. The Jacobian family of $C_{m,R}$ therefore extends to an abelian scheme on a Zariski neighborhood of $O$ in the parameter curve, with fiber $E^m$ at $O$.

primaryStatements.label: mon:integral-module
primaryStatements.text: The cycles $a_i,b_i$ form an integral symplectic basis of $H_1(C_{m,R_s},\Z)$. Consequently, for every smooth fiber of the family, \begin{equation} H_1(C_m,\Z)\simeq\Z[\Gamma_m]^2, \qquad H^1(C_m,\Z)\simeq\Z[\Gamma_m]^2. \end{equation} In particular, after comparison, $H^1_{\mathrm{et}}(C_m,\Z_\ell)$ is free of rank two over $\Z_\ell[\Gamma_m]$ for every prime $\ell$, including $\ell\mid m$.

primaryStatements.label: mon:transvections
primaryStatements.text: In one integral basis $a_i,b_i$ as above, the geometric monodromy of the constant-$E$ family contains operators $T_a,T_b$ satisfying \begin{align} T_a(a_j)&=a_j,& T_a(b_j)&=b_j+\sigma_a(2a_j-a_{j-1}-a_{j+1}), \\ T_b(b_j)&=b_j,& T_b(a_j)&=a_j+\sigma_b(2b_j-b_{j-1}-b_{j+1}), \end{align} where $\sigma_a,\sigma_b\in\{1,-1\}$ are independent of $j$. Equivalently, their two off-diagonal entries, in the basis of the free $\Z[\Gamma_m]$-module, are $\sigma_a(2-u-u^{-1})$ and $\sigma_b(2-u-u^{-1})$. The geometric monodromy of the family over $U$ contains these actions as well, under the pullback identification.

primaryStatements.label: sys:properties
primaryStatements.text: For every $t\in U(K)$ and every rotation character $\theta$, the representations $V_{\theta,\ell}$ have the following properties. \begin{enumerate} \item They are semisimple of dimension two, with determinant $\eps_\ell^{-1}$. \item At every place of $F$ above $\ell$, they are potentially semistable with labelled Hodge--Tate weights $\{0,1\}$. \item There is a finite set of places $S$ of $F$, independent of $\ell$, such that $V_{\theta,\ell}$ is unramified at every $v\notin S$ of residue characteristic different from $\ell$. At such a place its Frobenius characteristic polynomial is the image under $j_\ell$ of a polynomial in $M[T]$ independent of $\ell$. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.label: sys:elliptic
primaryStatements.text: If $\theta$ has order $m>1$ dividing $n$, the system $V_\theta$ is realized by the corresponding character space in $H^1(C_m)$. For the trivial character, \[ V_{1,\ell}\simeq H^1_{\mathrm{\acute et}} (B_{t,\overline F},\overline\Q_\ell). \] Let $D_t=C_3(t)/\langle w\rangle$ and $A_t=\Jac(D_t)$. Then $D_t$ has genus one, $A_t$ is an elliptic curve over $F$, and for either nontrivial order-three character $\eta$ there are $G_F$-equivariant isomorphisms \[ V_{\eta,\ell}\simeq H^1_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(A_{t,\overline F},\overline\Q_\ell) \qquad\text{for every }\ell. \]

primaryStatements.label: sys:congruences
primaryStatements.text: For every $t\in U(K)$ there are isomorphisms \begin{equation} \overline V_{\eta,p}\simeq\overline V_{\chi,p}, \qquad \overline V_{\chi,3}\simeq\overline V_{\psi,3}, \qquad \overline V_{\psi,p}\simeq\overline V_{1,p}. \end{equation} These hold with the elliptic-curve realizations of Proposition \ref{sys:elliptic} at the two ends.

primaryStatements.name: Caraiani--Newton, specialized form
primaryStatements.label: aut:lift
primaryStatements.text: Let $L$ be a CM number field and $l$ an odd prime other than $5$. Let $r:G_L\to\GL_2(\overline\Q_l)$ be continuous, unramified outside finitely many places, with determinant $\eps_l^{-1}$. Suppose that $r$ is potentially semistable with labeled Hodge--Tate weights $0,1$ at every $v\mid l$, that $\overline r$ is decomposed generic, and that $\overline r|_{G_{L(\zeta_l)}}$ is absolutely irreducible. Suppose there are a cuspidal weight-zero regular algebraic representation $\pi$ of $\PGL_2(\A_L)$ and an isomorphism $\iota:\overline\Q_l\xrightarrow{\sim}\C$ for which $\overline{r_\iota(\pi)}\simeq\overline r$. At each $v\mid l$, assume one of the following: \begin{enumerate}[(i)] \item Both local Galois representations are potentially crystalline; one is potentially ordinary of weight zero if and only if the other is; and $\rec_{L_v}(\pi_v)$ has zero monodromy. \item Neither local Galois representation is potentially crystalline, and $\pi$ is $\iota$-ordinary of weight zero at $v$. \end{enumerate} Then $r\simeq r_\iota(\Pi)$ for a cuspidal weight-zero regular algebraic representation $\Pi$ of $\PGL_2(\A_L)$.

papers.abstract: We prove Uchida's conjecture on open homomorphisms of Galois groups. Every continuous open homomorphism between Galois groups of solvably closed Galois extensions of number fields is induced by a unique equivariant field embedding in the opposite direction. No restriction on the kernel or additional compatibility hypothesis is required.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let $F_1,F_2$ be number fields, and let $E_i/F_i$ be possibly infinite solvably closed Galois extensions. Every continuous open homomorphism \[ \alpha:\Gal(E_1/F_1)\longrightarrow\Gal(E_2/F_2) \] is induced by a unique field embedding $j:E_2\hookrightarrow E_1$.

primaryStatements.label: thm:uchida-isomorphism
primaryStatements.text: Let $E_i/F_i$ be solvably closed Galois extensions of number fields. Every isomorphism $\theta:\Gal(E_1/F_1)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gal(E_2/F_2)$ is induced by a unique field isomorphism $j:E_2\xrightarrow{\sim}E_1$, with $g j=j\theta(g)$ for all $g$.

primaryStatements.name: Uchida's partial local correspondence
primaryStatements.label: thm:local-correspondence
primaryStatements.text: Let $M$ be a number field, let $N\subset\Q^s$ be a number field, and let $\varphi:G_M\to P_N$ be open. Fix an odd prime $\ell$. Every prime $v\nmid\ell$ active at $\ell$ determines a unique prime $w\nmid\ell$ of $N$ for which, with suitable prolongations, \[ \varphi(D_v)\subset D_w. \] Moreover, $\varphi$ is injective on a pro-$\ell$ Sylow subgroup of $I_v$, and sends this subgroup into $I_w$. All but finitely many primes of $N$ arise from such active primes of $M$.

primaryStatements.name: Hoshi
primaryStatements.label: thm:hoshi
primaryStatements.text: Let $E_i/F_i$ be solvably closed Galois extensions of number fields, and let $\alpha:\Gal(E_1/F_1)\to\Gal(E_2/F_2)$ be open. There exists an equivariant field embedding $E_2\hookrightarrow E_1$ if and only if \[ \chi_{E_2/F_2}\circ\alpha=\chi_{E_1/F_1} \quad\text{in }\widehat{\Z}^{\times}. \]

primaryStatements.name: Frobenius detection
primaryStatements.label: prop:character-detection
primaryStatements.text:
Let $M$ be a number field, let $\ell$ be a rational prime, and let $x\in\X{\ell}{M}$.  egin{enumerate} \item[(i)] If $x(\Fr_v)=0$ at infinitely many primes $v
mid\ell$ of absolute residue degree one, then $x=0$. \item[(ii)] Suppose that $M/\Q$ is Galois, and fix $\delta\in\Gal(M/\Q)$. If $x(\Fr_v)=0$ at infinitely many primes $v
mid\ell$ lying over rational primes unramified in $M$ whose Frobenius element at $v$ in $\Gal(M/\Q)$ is $\delta$, then $E_{\langle\deltaangle}x=0$. \item[(iii)] If $\cor_{M/\Q}x
e0$, then $x(\Fr_v)=0$ at only finitely many primes $v
mid\ell$, with no restriction on their residue degrees. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.label: prop:signed-representation
primaryStatements.text: Let $M/\Q$ be a finite, totally imaginary Galois extension, put $R=\Gal(M/\Q)$, and let $c\in R$ be a complex conjugation. For every rational prime $\ell$, there are $R$-equivariant embeddings \begin{equation} W_M:=\Ind_{\langle c\rangle}^{R}(\mathrm{sign}) \lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow\X{\ell}{M} \lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow\Q_\ell[R], \end{equation} where $\mathrm{sign}(c)=-1$. In particular, the action of $R$ on $\X{\ell}{M}$ is faithful.

primaryStatements.name: Frobenius generation
primaryStatements.label: prop:frobenius-generation
primaryStatements.text: Fix an odd prime $\ell$, a finite quotient $R_0$ of $P$, and $\gamma_0\in R_0$. There are a quotient \[ P\twoheadrightarrow R=\Gal(L/\Q)\twoheadrightarrow R_0 \] and a lift $\gamma\in R$ of $\gamma_0$ with the following property. There are infinitely many $\ell$-active primes $v$ of $k$, over distinct rational primes $p\ne\ell$, for which compatible prolongations can be chosen so that: \begin{enumerate} \item the corresponding target rational prime $q\ne\ell$ is unramified in $L$, and the target prolongation restricts to a prime $w'$ of $L$ whose Frobenius in $R$ is $\gamma$; \item the image in $R$ of an arithmetic Frobenius lift at $v$ generates $\langle\gamma\rangle$. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.label: thm:normalized-map
primaryStatements.text: The extension $\beta:G_k\to P$ is surjective. Put \[ m_0=[k:\Q]!,\qquad \mathcal L=\{\ell:\ell\text{ is an odd prime and } \ell\equiv1\pmod{m_0}\}. \] The set $\mathcal L$ is infinite, and for every $\ell\in\mathcal L$, \begin{equation} \log\chi_\ell\circ\beta=\log\chi_{k,\ell} \quad\text{as additive characters on }G_k. \end{equation} Here $\chi_\ell$ is the $\ell$-adic cyclotomic character on $P$, and $\chi_{k,\ell}$ is the ordinary cyclotomic character on $G_k$.

papers.title: The rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties
papers.abstract: We prove the rational Hodge conjecture for complex abelian varieties with complex multiplication: every rational Hodge class on such a variety is a rational linear combination of algebraic cycle classes. As consequences, we obtain the generalized Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, the Tate conjecture for abelian varieties over finite fields, and the Hodge standard conjecture for abelian varieties in arbitrary characteristic.

primaryStatements.label: thm:cm
primaryStatements.text: Let \(A\) be a complex CM abelian variety. For every integer \(p\geq0\), the Betti cycle-class map \[ \operatorname{cl}_B:\CH^p(A)_{\Q} \longrightarrow H^{2p}(A,\Q)\cap H^{p,p}(A) \] is surjective, where \(\CH^p(A)_{\Q}=\CH^p(A)\otimes_{\Z}\Q\) and the intersection is taken in \(H^{2p}(A,\C)\). In particular, the rational Hodge conjecture holds in every codimension on every finite product of complex CM abelian varieties and on every power of such a product.

primaryStatements.name: Four-factor switch
primaryStatements.label: thm:switch
primaryStatements.text: Let \(E\) be a Galois CM field and let \(v_1,v_2,v_3,v_4:G_E\to\{1,-1\}\) be odd sign functions satisfying \(v_1+v_2=v_3+v_4\). Under the Künneth inclusion, the following line is algebraic: \begin{equation} U(v_1)_1\otimes U(v_2)_1\otimes U(v_3)_c\otimes U(v_4)_c \ \subset\ H^4\!\left(\prod_{i=1}^4B(v_i),\Qbar\right) \end{equation}

primaryStatements.label: prop:switch-reduction
primaryStatements.text: If Theorem \ref{thm:switch} holds for every Galois CM field and every quadruple of odd sign functions satisfying its relation, then Theorem \ref{thm:cm} holds.

primaryStatements.name: Surface criterion
primaryStatements.label: prop:surface-switch
primaryStatements.text: Let \(E\) be a Galois CM field with conjugation \(c\), and let \(v_1,v_2,v_3,v_4:G_E\to\{1,-1\}\) be odd sign functions satisfying \(v_1+v_2=v_3+v_4\). Put \(\lambda=(1,1,c,c)\). Suppose that \(S\) is a smooth connected projective complex surface and that there are rational Hodge maps \[ h_i:U(v_i)\longrightarrow H^1(S,\Q),\qquad 1\leq i\leq4, \] and nonzero vectors \(\alpha_i\in U(v_i)_{\lambda_i}\subset U(v_i)_{\Qbar}\) such that \begin{equation} \int_S h_1(\alpha_1)\smile h_2(\alpha_2) \smile h_3(\alpha_3)\smile h_4(\alpha_4)\ne0. \end{equation} Here each \(h_i\) is extended to \(\Qbar\)-coefficients. Then the line in Equation \eqref{eq:switch-line} is algebraic.

primaryStatements.name: Surface criterion for complex spans
primaryStatements.label: cor:surface-span
primaryStatements.text: Let \(E\), \(v_1,\ldots,v_4\), and \(\lambda=(1,1,c,c)\) be as in Proposition \ref{prop:surface-switch}, and let \(S\) be a smooth connected projective complex surface. Suppose that, for each \(1\leq i\leq4\), a class \(\eta_i\in H^1(S,\C)\) belongs to \[ \operatorname{span}_{\C} \{h(U(v_i)_{\lambda_i}): h\in\Hom_{\mathrm{Hdg}}(U(v_i),H^1(S,\Q))\} \] and that \[ \int_S\eta_1\smile\eta_2\smile\eta_3\smile\eta_4\ne0. \] Then the line in Equation \eqref{eq:switch-line} is algebraic.

primaryStatements.label: prop:theta-one
primaryStatements.text: For every finite input \(\phi\), the form \(\Theta_i(\phi)\) is holomorphic on \(D\) and descends to every sufficiently deep principal congruence quotient. At any fixed point of \(D\), the values \(\Theta_i(\phi)\), as \(\phi\) varies over finite Schwartz inputs, span the cotangent fiber. Finitely many actual inputs already span that fiber and descend at a common sufficiently deep principal level.

primaryStatements.label: prop:theta-top
primaryStatements.text: The rank-two construction has the following properties. \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item At period data induced by a rational orthogonal decomposition \(W=W_1\perp W_2\), the form \(\Xi_W(\phi)\) is holomorphic. On a sufficiently deep common principal quotient it is a finite sum, with constant coefficients, of forms \(\Theta_1(\phi_{1,r})\wedge\Theta_2(\phi_{2,r})\). \item There is an input which is a product in adapted rational coordinates and for which \(\Xi_W(\phi)\) is nonzero. \item Fix \(W\), the total finite input \(\phi\), and a torsion-free principal quotient \(X\) whose finite level fixes \(\phi\) under \(\omega_{W,f}\). With locally smooth constant-line trivializations, the map \[ t\longmapsto\Xi_W(\phi;t) \] is continuous in the \(C^\infty\) topology of differential forms on this fixed compact quotient. The same finite level works throughout the parameter neighborhood. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.label: cor:theta-switch-continuity
primaryStatements.text: Suppose \(d_1+d_2=d_3+d_4\), with \(d_i(\mu)=1\) for all \(i\). Start with \(W=W_1\perp W_2\) as above, let \(t_0\) be its compact-place data, and choose a total input \(\phi\) for which \(\xi=\Xi_W(\phi;t_0)\) is a nonzero holomorphic top form on a sufficiently deep compact principal quotient \(X\). There are rational orthogonal decompositions \(W=W_3\perp W_4\) with line signs \(d_3,d_4\) whose total compact-place positive Lagrangians are arbitrarily close to those at \(t_0\). The total active positive Lagrangian is exactly unchanged. For a sufficiently close rational choice \(t'\), the form \(\xi'=\Xi_W(\phi;t')\) is holomorphic on the same quotient \(X\), with the same total finite input, and \begin{equation} \int_X\xi\wedge\overline{\xi'}\ne0. \end{equation} Both endpoints admit the wedge expansions of Proposition \ref{prop:theta-top} on a further common principal cover, and their pairing remains nonzero there.

papers.title: Algebraic Kuga–Satake correspondences and Hodge conjectures on a K3 quadratic locus
papers.abstract: We prove the rational Hodge and generalized Hodge conjectures in every cohomological degree of every self-power of a projective complex K3 surface whose transcendental quadratic space, with its cup-product form, admits a rational isometric embedding in $\mathbb U_{\mathbb Q}^{\oplus2}\perp\langle-1\rangle^4$. This includes every ample P-polarized K3 surface, including all Picard jumps, for $P=\mathbb U\oplus D_8(-1)\oplus D_4(-1)$. On this locus we construct algebraic correspondences inducing every prescribed standard even-Clifford Kuga–Satake tensor. More generally, for any projective complex K3 surface, algebraicity of one exact standard even-Clifford Kuga–Satake tensor implies both conjectures for every self-power.
papers.familySummary: Proves the rational Hodge conjecture for every complex CM abelian variety, in every dimension and codimension. Through Milne's theorems, this also gives the Tate conjecture for all abelian varieties over finite fields and the Hodge standard conjecture for abelian varieties in every characteristic.

This includes every ample $P$-polarized K3 surface, including all Picard jumps, for $P=\mathbb U\oplus D_8(-1)\oplus D_4(-1)$. primaryStatements.label: main:theorem
primaryStatements.text: Let $S$ be a smooth projective complex K3 surface. Suppose that there is a rational isometric embedding \[ (T_S,q)\hookrightarrow V_P. \] For any full even-Clifford realization $H^1(A,\Q)=C^+(T_S,q)$, any rational nonisotropic $w\in T_S$, and any rational polarization $E$ of this weight-one Hodge structure, there is a cycle \[ \Gamma_S\in\CH^2(S\times A\times A)_{\Q} \] whose action on every $x\in T_S$ is exactly $\iota_{w,E}(x)$ in $H^2(A\times A,\Q)$. The same assertion holds on a transported isogenous model with its specified tensor. Moreover, the rational Hodge conjecture and the rational generalized Hodge conjecture hold in every cohomological degree of every self-power $S^m$, for every integer $m\ge1$.

primaryStatements.label: ext:criterion
primaryStatements.text: Let $S$ be a projective K3 surface. Suppose that, for one rational nonisotropic $w\in T_S$, one rational polarization, and one full even-Clifford realization, the tensor of $j_w(v)(a)=vaw$ is induced by a cycle in $\CH^2(S\times A^2)_{\Q}$. Then rational HC and rational GHC hold in every degree of every self-power of $S$.

primaryStatements.label: ext:conditional
primaryStatements.text: Let $S$ be a projective K3 surface with transcendental space $(T,q)$ of rational dimension $t$, put $V=T(1)$, and let $W=C^+(T,q)=H^1(A,\Q)$ be an even-Clifford Kuga--Satake realization. Suppose that for one rational nonisotropic $w\in T$ the tensor form of \begin{equation} j_w:V\longrightarrow\End(W),\qquad j_w(v)(a)=vaw, \end{equation} is induced by a cycle in $\CH^2(S\times A^2)_{\Q}$, using a rational polarization of $W$. Then, for every $1\leq k\leq t$, there is an injective algebraic Hodge map \[ F_k:\bigwedge^kV\longrightarrow\End(W) \] with an algebraic left inverse on cohomology. More precisely, put $Z=A^2$ and $n=\dim Z$. There are correspondences \[ \Gamma_k\in\CH^{k+1}(S^k\times Z)_\Q,\qquad R_k\in\CH^{n+k-1}(Z\times S^k)_\Q. \] Viewing $\bigwedge^kV$ in $H^{2k}(S^k,\Q)(k)$ and identifying $\End(W)\simeq(H^1(A,\Q)\otimes H^1(A,\Q))(1)\subset H^2(Z,\Q)(1)$ by a rational polarization, their weight-zero actions satisfy $(\Gamma_k)_*|_{\wedge^kV}=F_k$ and $(R_k)_*F_k=\id$. Every rational Hodge class in $\bigwedge^kV$ is the class of a rational algebraic cycle of codimension $k$ on $S^k$.

primaryStatements.name: Exterior-power coniveau
primaryStatements.label: ghc:prop:exterior-coniveau
primaryStatements.text: Let $S$ satisfy the exact even-Clifford algebraicity hypothesis of Proposition \ref{ext:conditional}, and put $t=\dim_\Q T$. For every $1\le k\le t$, \[ \bigwedge^kT\subset N^{k-1}H^{2k}(S^k,\Q). \] Moreover every rational sub-Hodge structure of this exterior power satisfies the generalized Hodge conjecture in its ambient $H^{2k}(S^k,\Q)$. In particular, the top exterior line is supported in codimension $t$.

primaryStatements.label: geom:structure
primaryStatements.text: There is a smooth double cover $Y\to K=\Km(B')$, with $K$ the resolved Kummer surface, satisfying the following assertions. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item The anti-invariant lattice \[ V=H^2(Y,\Z)^{\delta=-1} \] (with torsion removed) is even, has signature $(2,14)$, and has $2$-elementary discriminant group. For fixed $(B,M,\chi)$, monodromy acts trivially on this discriminant group. \item There are eight mutually orthogonal algebraic anti-invariant classes $a_1,\ldots,a_8$, each of square $-4$. Their perpendicular \[ U=\langle a_1,\ldots,a_8\rangle^\perp\subset V_\Q \] is a Hodge structure of signature $(2,6)$ and, with the intersection form inherited from $Y$, is rationally isometric to \[ V_P=(\mathbb U\oplus\mathbb U(2)\oplus D_4(-1))_\Q. \] \item Resolved pullback gives a flat Hodge isomorphism $\beta:U\xrightarrow{\sim}U_X$ with \[ (\beta x,\beta y)_X=2(x,y)_Y. \] The algebraic projector \begin{equation} e=\frac14(\Delta_X+\Gamma_j-\Gamma_\delta-\Gamma_{j\delta}) \in\CH^2(X\times X)_\Q \end{equation} has image $U_X$ in degree two and is zero in every other degree. \end{enumerate} The constructions are compatible with variation on the indicated smooth parameter opens.

primaryStatements.label: geom:period
primaryStatements.text: The period map of $U$, equivalently of $U_X$, has rank six on a nonempty Zariski-open subset of the six-dimensional parameter space. For a very general parameter, its rational Hodge structure is simple, has no nonzero rational $(1,1)$-class, and has Hodge group $\SO(U)$.

primaryStatements.label: geom:domination
primaryStatements.text: For every parameter in a nonempty Zariski-open subset of the parameter space, there exist smooth projective connected curves $C_1,C_2$ and a dominant generically finite morphism \[ g:C_1\times C_2\longrightarrow X. \] Whenever additionally $U_X$ has no nonzero rational $(1,1)$-class, an algebraic correspondence induces an injection \[ U_X\hookrightarrow H^1(C_1,\Q)\otimes H^1(C_2,\Q). \] In particular, this injection exists at a very general parameter.

primaryStatements.name: K3 realization of a section pencil
primaryStatements.label: pencil:realization
primaryStatements.text: Choose the abelian data and the pencil \(d_t=d_0+t d_1\) in the generic sets of Lemma \ref{geom:genericity}. There is a nonempty algebraic open \(O\subset\AA^1_t\) and a smooth projective family of K3 surfaces \(S^0\to O\) with a flat isometric embedding of rational Hodge variations \[ U\ \hookrightarrow\ R^2(S^0/O)_*\Q. \] The form on \(U\) here is its cup-product form inherited from \(Y\). For very general \(t\), this summand is the transcendental part of \(H^2(S^0_t,\Q)\). For every \(s\) in a nonempty Zariski-open subset of \(\AA^1_s\), every smooth projective model of the total family obtained by \(t=s+u^2\) is uniruled. The K3 family over \(O\) is defined over the original \(t\)-line; an additional unspecified finite base change is not part of the conclusion.

papers.title: Weil classes and Hodge classes on abelian powers
papers.abstract: We prove the rational Hodge conjecture in every codimension on every self-power of a complex abelian sixfold with an imaginary-quadratic action and a compatible polarization whose rational homological Hermitian form is hyperbolic of signature $(3,3)$. We also prove it in every codimension on every self-power of a complex abelian variety of dimension at most five admitting an imaginary-quadratic action. Both results include nonsimple varieties and special periods with additional endomorphisms. The proof uses the companion theorem on the rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties.

primaryStatements.name: Split Weil sixfolds
primaryStatements.label: p3ab:split-sixfolds
primaryStatements.text: Let \(E\) be an imaginary quadratic field and let \(A\) be a complex abelian sixfold with an \(E\)-action. Suppose a compatible polarization has hyperbolic rational Hermitian form of signature \((3,3)\). Then the rational Hodge conjecture holds in every codimension on \(A^m\), for every \(m\geq1\).

primaryStatements.name: Quadratic actions in dimension at most five
primaryStatements.label: p3ab:quadratic-five
primaryStatements.text: Let \(A\) be a complex abelian variety of dimension at most five admitting an action of an imaginary quadratic field. The rational Hodge conjecture holds in every codimension on \(A^m\), for every \(m\geq1\).

primaryStatements.name: A determinant criterion for all powers
primaryStatements.label: p3:tensor-criterion
primaryStatements.text: Let $A$ be a complex abelian variety, $H=H^1(A,\Q)$, $J=\operatorname{Hdg}(H)$, and $R=J^{\mathrm{der}}$. Suppose the following data exist. \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)] \item A rational Hodge summand $H_0\subset H$ has toric Hodge group. Choose a decomposition of $H_{0,k}$ into CM embedding lines, with repeated occurrences distinguished, and call this finite list $\mathcal E_0$. \item The complement of $H_{0,k}$ is a direct sum of blocks of nonzero admissible spaces. In a symplectic or an orthogonal block, each space is equipped with an admissible isomorphism to a representative $V_i$ chosen as an actual summand of that block, with, respectively, an alternating or a symmetric pair tensor on itself. A linear block has $\dim V_i\ge2$, with $V_i$ again an actual summand, and each space is equipped with an admissible isomorphism to either $V_i$ or $\overline V_i$, paired with each other as in Lemma \ref{p3:admissible-operations}. The pair identifies $\overline V_i$ with $V_i^*(-1)$ as a Hodge-graded space and with the dual as a group representation. \item Under these identifications the image of $R_k$ contains \[ P=\prod_{i\in I_{\mathrm{Sp}}}\operatorname{Sp}(V_i) \times\prod_{i\in I_{\mathrm{SO}}}\operatorname{SO}(V_i) \times\prod_{i\in I_{\mathrm{SL}}}\operatorname{SL}(V_i). \] Each factor acts by its standard representation on its own copies, by the dual representation on the opposite copies of a linear block, and trivially on every other block and on $H_{0,k}$. The symplectic and orthogonal forms are the inverse pairings. \item Let $W_1,\ldots,W_s$ be any list, with arbitrary repetitions, from \[ \{V_i:i\in I_{\mathrm{SO}}\} \ \cup\ \{V_i,\overline V_i:i\in I_{\mathrm{SL}}\}. \] Whenever there are $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_r\in\mathcal E_0$, again with arbitrary repetitions, such that \begin{equation} \sum_{j=1}^s\epsilon_\gamma(W_j) +\sum_{a=1}^r\epsilon_\gamma(\ell_a)=0 \quad\text{for every }\gamma\in\operatorname{Gal}(k/\Q), \end{equation} the line $\bigotimes_{j=1}^sD(W_j)$ is CM-supplied on its separate tensor slots. Empty lists are allowed. \end{enumerate} Then for every $p\ge0$ every rational balanced tensor in $H^{\otimes 2p}$ is the class of a rational algebraic cycle on its separate $A$-slots. The rational Hodge conjecture holds in every codimension of $A^m$ for every $m\ge1$. Call the data saturated if every singleton $D(V_i)$ for an orthogonal or linear block is CM-supplied, without any balance condition. For saturated data and any CM abelian variety $M$, the induced data on $A\times M$ are saturated. In particular the same tensor and Hodge-conjecture conclusions hold for every power of $A\times M$.

primaryStatements.name: Algebraicity of the hyperbolic Weil plane
primaryStatements.label: p3sw:weil-plane
primaryStatements.text: Let \(E\) be an imaginary quadratic field. Let \(A\) be a complex abelian sixfold with a unital \(E\)-action and a compatible polarization whose actual homological Hermitian form \(h_E\) is hyperbolic of signature \((3,3)\). Then \[ \mathcal W_E(A)\ \subset\ \operatorname{im}\bigl(\CH^3(A)_\Q \longrightarrow H^6(A,\Q)\bigr). \] The assertion holds at every compatible period, including nonsimple varieties and periods with additional endomorphisms.

primaryStatements.name: Simultaneous equivariant seeds
primaryStatements.label: p3sw:seed
primaryStatements.text: For every integer \(d\geq3\), put \(n=d+1\). There exist a smooth nonhyperelliptic genus-three curve \(C\), a point \(p\in C\), and cyclic subgroups \(G_1,G_2\subset X=\operatorname{Pic}^2(C)\) of order \(n\), with \(G_1\cap G_2=0\), as follows. There are cosets \(\{s_1,\ldots,s_n\}=s_0+G_2\) and \(\{t_1,\ldots,t_n\}=t_0+G_1\) such that \begin{equation} C_i=t_{s_i}C_p,\qquad \Sigma_j=t_{t_j}\Sigma_p,\qquad A=\coprod_{i=1}^n C_i,\qquad \Sigma=\coprod_{j=1}^n\Sigma_j \end{equation} are disjoint within each of the two indicated unions, and \begin{equation} H^0(X,I_A\otimes H^{\otimes2}\otimes N) = H^0(X,I_\Sigma\otimes H^{\otimes2}\otimes N)=0 \quad\text{for every }N\in\widehat X. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: The relative kernel and all its base changes
primaryStatements.label: p3sw:relative-kernel
primaryStatements.text: For the seed of Proposition \ref{p3sw:seed}, the derived tensor in \eqref{p3sw:support-kernel-sheaf} is the ordinary coherent sheaf \(\mathscr I\mathscr J\subset\mathcal O_{X\times M}\). Both this ideal and its quotient in \(\mathcal O_{X\times M}\) are flat over \(M\). Ideal multiplication and both ideal sequences commute with every base change \(T\to M\). In particular, \(\mathscr F\) is \(M\)-flat, and at \(m=(x,N)\) it has the ordinary fiber \begin{equation} \begin{split} \mathscr F_m&=I_{Z_x}\otimes\mathcal M_{x,N},\\ I_{Z_x}&=I_A I_{\Sigma_x},\qquad \Sigma_x=\coprod_jt_{-x}\Sigma_j,\qquad \mathcal M_{x,N}=H^{\otimes2}\otimes a(-x)\otimes N^{-1}. \end{split} \end{equation} Moreover \(G=R\pi_*\mathscr F\) has a local finite locally free model, and for every \(h:T\to M\), \begin{equation} Lh^*G\simeq R\pi_{T,*}(\mathscr F|_{X\times T}). \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: The actual coherent dual sheaf
primaryStatements.label: p3sw:coherent-sheaf
primaryStatements.text: Let \(D_M(-)=R\mathcal Hom_M(-,\mathcal O_M)\). Every derived fiber of \(G\) has cohomology only in degrees one and two, and its degree-two cohomology vanishes on a nonempty open set. Consequently \begin{equation} E=D_M(G)[-1] \end{equation} is an actual coherent perfect sheaf on \(M\), locally with a length-one locally free resolution, of rank \begin{equation} r=8d>0. \end{equation} No reflexivity or codimension assertion is required for this claim.

primaryStatements.name: Coherent conjugation and the graph quotient
primaryStatements.label: p3sw:coherent-action
primaryStatements.text: For \(g=(g_1,g_2)\in G_1\times G_2\), put \begin{equation} \begin{split} b_g&=(g_1-g_2,\ a(-g_1-g_2))\in M,\\ N_g&=\operatorname{pr}_X^*a(-g_1) \otimes\operatorname{pr}_{\widehat X}^*\mathcal P_{-g_2}, \qquad \mathcal P_v=\mathcal P|_{\{v\}\times\widehat X}. \end{split} \end{equation} The conjugation of the source translations by \(\widetilde\Phi\) has explicit functors \begin{equation} T_g(-)=N_g\otimes t_{b_g,*}(-). \end{equation} There are unital associative line isomorphisms \begin{equation} N_g\otimes t_{b_g,*}N_h\simeq N_{g+h} \end{equation} and compatible isomorphisms \(T_gG\simeq G\). Perfect duality gives actual sheaf isomorphisms \begin{equation} N_g^{-1}\otimes t_{b_g,*}E\simeq E \end{equation} with the corresponding unital associative line compositors. The homomorphism \(g\mapsto b_g\) is injective. Its image \(\bar G\) has order \(n^2\), acts freely by translations, and \begin{equation} q:M\longrightarrow Y_0=M/\bar G \end{equation} is a finite \'etale isogeny of abelian sixfolds.

papers.title: Abelian covers, Gale correspondences, and the Hodge conjecture for powers
papers.abstract: We prove the rational Hodge conjecture on every self-power of the Jacobian at each tensor Hodge-generic point of the full marked variation of a connected abelian cover of curves. This holds in every base genus and for every compatible branching pattern. For any CM abelian variety, the conclusion also holds for every self-power of its product with the Jacobian, on the same Hodge-generic locus. We also prove the conjecture on every self-power of a very general member of the full smooth labelled family of diagonal complete intersections cut out by at most two equations of a common degree, in every dimension and every degree at least two.

primaryStatements.text: Fix \(n\geq2\), \(d\geq0\), \(c\in\{0,1,2\}\), and put \(m=d+c+1\). Outside a countable union of proper closed algebraic subsets of \(\D_{c,m}\), the rational Hodge conjecture holds in every codimension on \(X_A^u\) for every \(u\geq1\). primaryStatements.text: For each fixed connected topological abelian cover as above, every \(s\in\mathcal T_\phi^{\mathrm{Hg}}\), every complex CM abelian variety \(M\), and every integer \(N\geq1\), the rational Hodge conjecture holds in every codimension of \[ \bigl(\Jac(C_s)\times M\bigr)^N. \] It also holds for \(C_s^a\times M^b\) for all integers \(a,b\geq0\), where a zeroth power means a point. primaryStatements.name: Determinants for abelian covers
primaryStatements.label: p4:abelian-determinants
primaryStatements.text: Let a finite abelian group $P$ act faithfully on a smooth connected projective complex curve $C$, and put $B=C/P$. For every character $\chi:P\to k^\times$, the line $D(H^1(C,k)_\chi)$ is CM-supplied. This includes the zero character spaces. For the trivial character the line is generated by a rational algebraic cycle class. For $\chi\ne1$, let $r_\chi$ be the number of branch points of $C/\ker\chi\to B$. Then \[ \dim_k H^1(C,k)_\chi=2g(B)+r_\chi-2. \] The number $r_\chi$ counts precisely the original branch points whose inertia is not killed by $\chi$. For a fixed $P$, the CM sources for all these lines can be taken to be powers of one fixed product of Fermat-curve Jacobians depending only on $P$, not on the complex structure of $C$.

primaryStatements.name: Saturated data for the marked cover family
primaryStatements.label: p4:cover-saturation
primaryStatements.text: For every connected topological abelian cover and full marked family defined above, and every \(s\in\mathcal T_\phi^{\mathrm{Hg}}\), the Jacobian \(\operatorname{Jac}(C_s)\) admits saturated data in Companion results \ref{comp:saturated}.

primaryStatements.name: Positive-genus character projections
primaryStatements.label: p4:positive-projections
primaryStatements.text: For $h\ge1$, every nonzero nontrivial character space is mixed in Hodge type at every scalar conjugate. At every $s\in\mathcal T_\phi^{\mathrm{Hg}}$ the image of the derived Hodge group on that space is the full standard special linear or full standard symplectic group. The invariant character space, when nonzero, has Hodge dimensions $(h,h)$ and full standard symplectic derived action.

primaryStatements.name: Sphere projections
primaryStatements.label: p4:sphere-projections
primaryStatements.text: At every $s\in\mathcal T_\phi^{\mathrm{Hg}}$ the following assertions hold. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item If $n\ge3$, then either $M_\chi$ is finite and the Hodge action on its rational scalar orbit is toric, or \[ M_\chi^\circ= \begin{cases} \operatorname{Sp}(W_\chi),&\chi^2=1,\\ \operatorname{SL}(W_\chi),&\chi^2\ne1. \end{cases} \] In the infinite case the derived Hodge projection is the same standard group. \item In dimensions at most two every non-toric character space has dimension two and has standard derived Hodge projection $\operatorname{SL}_2$. \end{enumerate} Here the symplectic group is for the restricted polarization on the order-two character space. Each non-toric character space is supported by a single simple ideal of $\operatorname{Lie}(J^{\mathrm{der}})_k$.

primaryStatements.name: Links within one sphere cover
primaryStatements.label: p4:sphere-links
primaryStatements.text: Suppose two non-toric character spaces $W_\chi,W_{\chi'}$ are supported by the same simple Hodge Lie ideal. They have the same dimension $n$ and standard derived representations equivalent up to duality. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item If $n\ge3$, then $\chi'=\chi$ or $\chi^{-1}$. The inverse character is identified by the polarization with the polarized dual. If the standard group is symplectic, the character has order two and the space is mixed at every scalar translate. \item If $n=2$, one can choose either $W_\chi$ or its polarized dual as model so that an equivalence of its derived representation with $W_{\chi'}$ respects the Hodge circle at every scalar translate. \end{enumerate}

definitions.label: def:root
definitions.text: Let \(m,n\geq2\) and \(0\leq d\leq m-2\). A subspace \(P\subset\C^m\) of dimension \(d+1\) is coordinate-general if every \(d+1\) coordinate functionals restrict to a basis of \(P^*\). Let \(\U_{d,m}\subset\Gr(d+1,m)\) be this open locus. For \(P\in\U_{d,m}\), define \[ X_P=\{[x_i]\in\PP^{m-1}:(x_1^n,\ldots,x_m^n)\in P\},\qquad G_{m,n}=(\mu_n)^m/\mu_n, \] where the denominator is diagonal. The phase action preserves \(X_P\), and \(q_P:X_P\to\PP(P)\), \([x_i]\mapsto[x_i^n]\), is its coordinate-power map.

papers.title: A Conditional Reduction for Algebraic Kuga–Satake Correspondences
papers.abstract: For a polarized K3 surface whose primitive cohomology has full orthogonal Hodge group, one algebraic correspondence inducing a nonzero map from that cohomology to the second cohomology of an abelian variety suffices to recover the prescribed full Kuga–Satake correspondence. We give an equivalent condition using holomorphic one-forms on a generically finite surface cover. If this input holds very generally in a polarized component, the prescribed correspondence is algebraic throughout that component, for every choice of standard data on the transcendental part. The existence of the initial correspondence remains a hypothesis.
papers.familySummary: Proves the rational Hodge conjecture for every complex CM abelian variety, in every dimension and codimension. Through Milne's theorems, this also gives the Tate conjecture for all abelian varieties over finite fields and the Hodge standard conjecture for abelian varieties in every characteristic.

primaryStatements.name: Recovery at a point with full Hodge group
primaryStatements.label: main:generic
primaryStatements.text: Suppose $\operatorname{Hg}(V)=\operatorname{SO}(V,q)$. The following conditions are equivalent. \begin{enumerate} \item There are an abelian variety $B$ and a cycle $\alpha\in\operatorname{CH}^2(S\times B)_{\mathbb Q}$ such that \[ \alpha_*:V\longrightarrow H^2(B,\mathbb Q) \] is nonzero. \item There are a smooth connected projective surface $Y$ and a dominant generically finite morphism $f:Y\to S$ such that \begin{equation} f_*\!\left(\operatorname{im}\!\left[ \bigwedge\nolimits^2 H^0(Y,\Omega_Y^1) \longrightarrow H^0(Y,\Omega_Y^2)\right]\right)\ne0. \end{equation} \item The prescribed full Kuga--Satake map is realized as in \eqref{eq:cycle-target}, for any stipulated standard data on $T$. \end{enumerate} In this situation $T=V$. The same input realizes the standard map for the full primitive Clifford construction with the cup form.

primaryStatements.name: Specialization in a polarized component
primaryStatements.label: main:specialization
primaryStatements.text: Fix a component of the moduli space of primitively amply polarized K3 surfaces of degree $2d$. Assume that condition \textup{(i)} or condition \textup{(ii)} of Theorem \ref{main:generic} holds very generally in that component. Then every $(S,h)$ in the component satisfies \eqref{eq:cycle-target}, with all the stipulated standard data on $T(S)$. Here it suffices that, about each desired point, the input holds outside a countable union of proper closed analytic subsets of a full polarized period chart. In particular an input outside countably many proper algebraic subsets of the moduli component suffices. The witness cycles, abelian varieties, or surface covers need not vary in a family.

primaryStatements.label: main:all-degrees
primaryStatements.text: If the hypothesis of Theorem \ref{main:specialization} holds in the required polarized components in every degree, then \eqref{eq:cycle-target} holds for every projective K3 surface.

primaryStatements.name: Correspondences and surface covers
primaryStatements.label: cyc:equivalence
primaryStatements.text: Conditions \textup{(i)} and \textup{(ii)} of Theorem \ref{main:generic} are equivalent. The implication from the surface condition to a nonzero correspondence on $V$ does not require the full Hodge-group hypothesis.

primaryStatements.label: cliff:construction
primaryStatements.text: The Hodge structures $P_H^\pm$ are polarizable, and \begin{equation} m^Q:H(1)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(P_H^+,P_H^-), \qquad x\longmapsto L_x \end{equation} is a rational Hodge embedding. The parity spaces are rationally Hodge-isomorphic by right multiplication by any fixed invertible odd Clifford element. On a sufficiently small period chart, their Hodge filtrations vary holomorphically and admit fixed rational polarizations.

primaryStatements.label: gen:genericity
primaryStatements.text: In any sufficiently small, full-dimensional marked polarized period chart, Equation \eqref{gen:full-group} holds outside a countable union of proper closed analytic subsets. At every point satisfying Equation \eqref{gen:full-group}, the Hodge structure $V$ is irreducible and $T(S)=V$.

primaryStatements.label: gen:generation
primaryStatements.text: Assume Equation \eqref{gen:full-group}. Suppose that $\alpha\in\operatorname{CH}^2(S\times B)_{\mathbb Q}$ induces a nonzero map $V\to H^2(B,\mathbb Q)$ for some complex abelian variety $B$. Let $\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2\in\{+,-\}$, and let $A_1,A_2$ be abelian varieties realizing $W^{\epsilon_1},W^{\epsilon_2}$ as their first rational cohomology. Every rational Hodge map \[ \beta:V\longrightarrow W^{\epsilon_1}\otimes W^{\epsilon_2} \subset H^2(A_1\times A_2,\mathbb Q) \] is the restriction of the action of a cycle $\Gamma\in\operatorname{CH}^2(S\times A_1\times A_2)_{\mathbb Q}$. In particular, this recovers the full primitive Clifford multiplication tensor and its prescribed even-Clifford realization.

primaryStatements.name: Specialization from very general algebraicity
primaryStatements.label: spec:specialization
primaryStatements.text: Let $D$ be a connected polydisc, and let $p:\mathcal X\to D$ be a smooth proper holomorphic family of $n$-dimensional varieties, $n\geq2$, with a relative embedding in $D\times\mathbb P^N$. Let \[ \theta\in H^0(D,R^4p_*\mathbb Q) \] be a flat rational class. If $\theta_t$ is the class of a rational codimension-two algebraic cycle for very general $t\in D$, then the same holds for every $t\in D$.

papers.title: Orbifold and logarithmic Iitaka subadditivity
papers.abstract: We prove Campana's orbifold Iitaka subadditivity conjecture for rational simple normal crossing boundaries on compact manifolds in Fujiki class $\mathcal C$, including coefficient one. Ordinary and logarithmic subadditivity follow.
papers.familySummary: Proves Campana's orbifold Iitaka subadditivity conjecture for smooth Fujiki-class-$\mathcal C$ manifolds with rational simple-normal-crossing boundaries. For projective fibrations $f:U\to V$ of smooth complex quasi-projective varieties with connected fibers, general fiber F, and $\bar\kappa(V)\ge0$, proves Popa's inequality $\bar\kappa(U)\ge\kappa(F)+\max\{\bar\kappa(V),\mathop{\mathrm{Var}}\nolimits (f)\}$, where variation measures the whole geometric generic fiber.
