primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: For every smooth integral complex projective surface $S$ and every ample line bundle $L$ on $S$, there is an integer $r_0=r_0(S,L)$ with the following property. For each integer $r\ge r_0$, there is a countable union $Z_r$ of proper Zariski-closed subsets of $U_r$, with nonempty complement, such that for every $\mathbf p\in U_r\setminus Z_r$ the class \[ \pi^*L-\sqrt{\frac{L^2}{r}}\sum_{i=1}^r E_i \] is nef on the blow-up at $\mathbf p$. Consequently, \[ \varepsilon(S,L;\mathbf p)=\sqrt{\frac{L^2}{r}}. \]

primaryStatements.name: Transfer from initial monomials
primaryStatements.label: prop:initial-transfer
primaryStatements.text: Let $F\subset\C\{x,z\}$ be a finite-dimensional complex vector space of convergent holomorphic germs, and let $t>0$. The set $E_t(F)$ has exactly $\dim F$ elements, and $F$ admits a basis whose initial exponents are these distinct elements. Let $r,m$ be positive integers. If the monomial space \[ \Span_{\C}\{X^\alpha Z^\beta:(\alpha,\beta)\in E_t(F)\} \] has an injective order-$m$ jet test at some distinct points $q_1,\ldots,q_r\in\T$, then representatives of $F$ on a common neighborhood of the origin have an injective order-$m$ jet test at distinct points arbitrarily close to the origin.

primaryStatements.name: The quadrilateral bound
primaryStatements.label: prop:quadrilateral
primaryStatements.text: For the surface, line bundle, nodal divisor, coordinates and frame fixed above, every integer $k\ge1$, every $t>T$, and every nonzero $s\in H^0(S,kL)$ satisfy \[ \nu_t(s)\in kQ_t. \] Moreover, $H^0(S,kL)$ has a basis with pairwise distinct initial exponents in $kQ_t$; the basis is empty if this section space is zero.

primaryStatements.name: Diagonal compression
primaryStatements.label: prop:compression
primaryStatements.text: Let $k,m,r$ be positive integers. If $\mathcal M(kP_t)$ has injective order-$m$ jets at some $r$ distinct points of $\T$, then $\mathcal M(kQ_t)$ has injective order-$m$ jets at some $r$ distinct points of $\T$.

primaryStatements.name: From the triangle to the surface
primaryStatements.label: cor:surface-transfer
primaryStatements.text: Let $k,m,r$ be positive integers. If $\mathcal M(kP_t)$ has injective order-$m$ jets at some $r$ distinct torus points, then $H^0(S,kL)$ has injective order-$m$ jets at some $r$ distinct points of $S$.

primaryStatements.label: prop:subgroup-test
primaryStatements.text: Let $H>0$, let $r$ be a positive integer, and let $P\subset\R^2$ be a triangle of area $H/2$. Suppose there is a primitive vector $u\in\Z^2$ such that \[ \max_{\xi\in P}\det(u,\xi) -\min_{\xi\in P}\det(u,\xi)=\sqrt{rH}. \] Then there is a subgroup $G\subset\T$ of exactly $r$ distinct points such that, for all positive integers $k,m$ with $m>k\sqrt{H/r}$, the order-$m$ jet test on $\mathcal M(kP)$ at $G$ is injective.

primaryStatements.label: cor:torus-test
primaryStatements.text: For the fixed parameters $d,H,T$ of Section \ref{sec:node}, there is an integer $r_0$ such that for every integer $r\geq r_0$ one can choose a single $t>T$ and a subgroup $G\subset\T$ of $r$ distinct points for which the following holds: for all positive integers $k,m$ satisfying \[ m>k\sqrt{H/r}, \] the order-$m$ jet test on $\mathcal M(kP_t)$ at $G$ is injective.

primaryStatements.name: Homogeneous tests imply nefness
primaryStatements.label: prop:homogeneous-nef
primaryStatements.text: Let $S$ be a smooth integral complex projective surface, let $L$ be ample, and let $p_1,\ldots,p_r$ be distinct points. Put $H=L^2$ and $w=\sqrt{H/r}$. Suppose that, for all positive integers $k,m$ with $m>kw$, no nonzero section of $L^{\otimes k}$ vanishes to order at least $m$ at every $p_i$. On the blow-up $\pi:Y\to S$ of these points, with exceptional curves $E_i$, the real divisor class \[ D_0=\pi^*L-w\sum_{i=1}^rE_i \] is nef.

lean.scopeText:
Nagata's conjecture asserts that a nonzero effective plane curve of degree $d$, with multiplicities at least $m_i$ at $r\ge10$ very general points, satisfies $\sum_i m_i<d\sqrt r$.

The formalization establishes this inequality simultaneously for all curves and multiplicity vectors outside one countable union of proper Zariski-closed exceptional sets with nonempty complement. Reducible curves, repeated components, and unequal multiplicities are included, in both effective-curve and homogeneous-polynomial formulations. The formalization also includes the passage from homogeneous effective cycles to equations.

The maximality question asks whether the multipoint Seshadri constant reaches the upper bound $\sqrt{L^2/r}$ at very general points once $r$ is sufficiently large. The formalized result establishes this for every smooth integral complex projective surface $S$ and ample line bundle $L$.

For every $r$ above a threshold depending on $(S,L)$, it gives a countable union of proper closed exceptional sets with nonempty complement. Outside it, the constant is $\sqrt{L^2/r}$ and the boundary class defining this Seshadri constant on the point blowup is nef. The threshold is not explicit or uniform over all surfaces.

papers.title: Maximal Multipoint Seshadri Constants in Higher Dimensions
papers.abstract: Let L be an ample line bundle on a smooth integral complex projective variety X of dimension n ≥ 3. We prove that there is a threshold $r_0=r_0(X,L)$ such that for every integer $r\ge r_0$, the ordinary multipoint Seshadri constant at r very general points equals the volume bound $(L^n/r)^{1/n}$. This establishes the qualitative Nagata–Biran–Szemberg assertion in these dimensions.
papers.familySummary: Proves Nagata's strict inequality $\sum_i m_i\lt d\sqrt r$ for every nonzero effective plane curve of degree d through r ≥ 10 very general complex points, with arbitrary multiplicities mi. It also proves maximal multipoint Seshadri constants $(L^n/r)^{1/n}$ for every smooth polarized projective variety of dimension n ≥ 2 and all sufficiently large r: at very general points over ℂ, and at the geometric generic tuple over any algebraically closed field of positive characteristic.

We prove that there is a threshold $r_0=r_0(X,L)$ such that for every integer $r\ge r_0$, the ordinary multipoint Seshadri constant at $r$ very general points equals the volume bound $(L^n/r)^{1/n}$. primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let $X$ be a smooth integral complex projective variety of dimension $n\ge3$, and let $L$ be an ample line bundle on $X$. There is an integer $r_0=r_0(X,L)\ge1$ such that for every integer $r\ge r_0$ there is a countable union $Z_r$ of proper Zariski-closed subsets of $U_r(X)$, with nonempty complement, for which \[ \eps(X,L;\mathbf p)=\left(\frac{L^n}{r}\right)^{1/n} \qquad\text{for every }\mathbf p\in U_r(X)\setminus Z_r. \]

primaryStatements.name: The initial simplex
primaryStatements.label: prop:flag-simplex
primaryStatements.text: Let $X$ be a smooth integral complex projective variety of dimension $n\geq3$, let $L$ be ample, and put $V=L^n$. Choose a positive integer $D$ such that $DL$ is very ample. There is a graded support family $S_k\subset\Z_{\geq0}^n$ such that \begin{align} S_k&\subset kP_0, &P_0&=\Delta(1/D,\ldots,1/D,D^{n-1}V), \\ \#S_k&=h^0(X,kL) =\frac{V}{n!}k^n+O(k^{n-1}), &\vol(P_0)&=\frac{V}{n!}. \end{align} For all integers $k\geq1$, $m\geq0$, and $r\geq1$, if $\M(S_k)$ separates jets through degree $m$ at some distinct $r$-tuple in $\Torus^n$, then $H^0(X,kL)$ does so at some distinct $r$-tuple in $X$.

primaryStatements.name: Two-intercept reshaping
primaryStatements.label: prop:reshape
primaryStatements.text: Let $n\ge2$, let $A,B,a_3,\ldots,a_n$ be positive real numbers, and let $(S_k)_{k\ge1}$ be finite exponent sets satisfying \[ S_k\subset k\Delta(A,B,a_3,\ldots,a_n)\cap\Z^n, \qquad S_k+S_l\subset S_{k+l}\quad(k,l\ge1). \] Set $H=AB$ and $d=\max(3/A,2/B)$. For every real number $w>0$ with $dw<1/16$, there are finite sets $(S'_k)_{k\ge1}$ such that \begin{align} S'_k&\subset k\Delta(w,H/w,a_3,\ldots,a_n)\cap\Z^n, \\ \#S'_k&=\#S_k, \qquad S'_k+S'_l\subset S'_{k+l}. \end{align} Moreover, for every $k\ge1$, $m\ge0$, and $r\ge1$, if $\M(S'_k)$ surjects onto jets through degree $m$ at some $r$ distinct points of $\Torus^n$, then $\M(S_k)$ does so at some $r$ distinct points of $\Torus^n$.

primaryStatements.name: Jets from full-volume supports
primaryStatements.label: prop:asymptotic-jets
primaryStatements.text: Let $n\ge2$ and $r\ge1$ be integers, let $w>0$, and set \[ P=\Delta(w,\ldots,w,rw). \] Suppose that finite sets $F_k\subset kP\cap\Z^n$, indexed by all integers $k\ge1$, satisfy \[ F_k+F_l\subset F_{k+l}, \qquad \#F_k=\vol(P)k^n+o(k^n). \] For every $0<\theta<w$ and every choice of distinct $c_1,\ldots,c_r\in\C^*$, the space $\M(F_k)$ surjects onto jets through degree $\lfloor k\theta\rfloor$ at $(1,\ldots,1,c_i)$ for all sufficiently large $k$.

definitions.label: def:graded-support
definitions.text: A graded support family in $\Z^n$ is a sequence of finite sets $(S_k)_{k\geq1}$ such that \begin{equation} S_k+S_l\subset S_{k+l}\qquad(k,l\geq1). \end{equation} Empty sets are allowed. Equivalently, $\M(S_k)\M(S_l)\subset\M(S_{k+l})$, where a product of spaces denotes the span of their pairwise products.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let $X/k$ be a smooth integral projective variety over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$, with $\dim X=n\ge3$, and let $L$ be ample. There is an integer $r_0=r_0(X,L)$ such that \[ \varepsilon_r(X,L)=\left(\frac{L^n}{r}\right)^{1/n} \qquad\text{for every integer }r\ge r_0. \]

primaryStatements.label: prop:initial-simplex
primaryStatements.text: Let $X$ be a smooth integral projective $n$-dimensional variety over an algebraically closed field, with $n\geq2$, and let $L$ be ample. Put $V=L^n$, and choose an integer $D\geq1$ such that $DL$ is very ample. There is a graded family of finite sets $S_N\subset\Z_{\geq0}^n$ such that \begin{align} S_N&\subset NP_0, &P_0&=\Delta(1/D,\ldots,1/D,D^{n-1}V), \\ \#S_N&=h^0(X,NL) =\frac{V}{n!}N^n+o(N^n). \end{align} For every $N,r\geq1$ and $m\geq0$, if $M(S_N)$ separates jets through order $m$ at some $r$ distinct torus points, then $H^0(X,NL)$ separates the same jets at some $r$ distinct points of $X$.

primaryStatements.name: Two-intercept reshaping
primaryStatements.label: prop:reshape
primaryStatements.text: Let $n\ge2$, let $A,B,a_3,\ldots,a_n>0$, and let $(S_N)_{N\ge1}$ be a graded family of finite subsets of $\Z^n$ satisfying \[ S_N\subset N\Delta(A,B,a_3,\ldots,a_n). \] Put $H=AB$ and $d=\max\{3/A,2/B\}$. For every $w>0$ with $dw<1/16$, there is a graded family $(S'_N)_{N\ge1}$ such that \[ S'_N\subset N\Delta(w,H/w,a_3,\ldots,a_n), \qquad \#S'_N=\#S_N \quad(N\ge1). \] The transformation from $S_N$ to $S'_N$ has backward jet transfer in every degree. For $n=2$, the lists $a_3,\ldots,a_n$ are empty.

primaryStatements.name: Jets at the geometric generic tuple
primaryStatements.label: prop:generic-jets
primaryStatements.text: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic, let $X/k$ be a smooth integral projective variety of dimension $n\ge2$, and let $L$ be ample. Put $V=L^n$. There is an integer $r_0=r_0(X,L)$ such that, for every integer $r\ge r_0$ and every real number \[ 0<\theta<\left(\frac Vr\right)^{1/n}, \] there is an integer $N_0=N_0(r,\theta)$ such that, for every $N\ge N_0$, the sections of $NL$ separate jets through order $\lfloor N\theta\rfloor$ at some ordered $r$-tuple of distinct $k$-points, which may depend on $N$. For each such $N$, the same jet separation holds after base change to $K_r$ at the geometric generic tuple $p_1,\ldots,p_r$.

definitions.label: def:graded
definitions.text: A family of finite sets $(S_N)_{N\geq1}$ in $\Z^d$ is graded if \[ S_N+S_{N'}\subset S_{N+N'}\qquad(N,N'\geq1). \] A transformation $(S_N)\mapsto(T_N)$ has backward jet transfer if, for every $N,r\geq1$ and $m\geq0$, separation of jets through order $m$ by $M(T_N)$ at some $r$ distinct torus points implies the same assertion for $M(S_N)$, possibly at a different tuple.

primaryStatements.label: thm:bloch
primaryStatements.text: Let \(S\) be a smooth connected projective surface over \(\mathbb C\) with \(p_g(S)=q(S)=0\). Then \[ \deg:\CH_0(S)\longrightarrow\mathbb Z \] is an isomorphism, where \(\CH_0(S)\) has integral coefficients.

primaryStatements.name: Bloch's conjecture for surfaces with \(p_g=0\)
primaryStatements.label: cor:bloch-pg-zero
primaryStatements.text: Let \(S\) be a smooth connected projective surface over \(\mathbb C\) with \(p_g(S)=0\). Then the Albanese homomorphism \[ \operatorname{alb}_S:\CH_0(S)^0\longrightarrow\Alb(S)(\mathbb C) \] is an isomorphism of abelian groups, where \(\CH_0(S)\) has integral coefficients.

primaryStatements.name: Motivic consequences
primaryStatements.label: cor:tate-motives
primaryStatements.text: Let \(S\) be a smooth connected projective surface over \(\mathbb C\) with \(p_g(S)=0\). Then \(h(S)_{\mathbb Q}\) is finite-dimensional in the sense of Kimura and \(t_2(S)=0\). If, in addition, \(q(S)=0\), then \[ h(S)_{\mathbb Q}\simeq \mathbf 1\oplus\mathbb L^{\oplus b_2(S)}\oplus\mathbb L^2. \] In this case, for every \(m,n\ge0\), the rational Chow motives of the power \(S^m\) and the Hilbert scheme \(S^{[n]}\) of length-\(n\) zero-dimensional subschemes are pure Tate, with \(S^0=S^{[0]}=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C\). For \(Y=S^m\) or \(Y=S^{[n]}\), the rational cycle-class maps satisfy \[ \operatorname{cl}_Y^i:\CH^i(Y)_{\mathbb Q} \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;}H^{2i}(Y,\mathbb Q), \qquad H^{2i+1}(Y,\mathbb Q)=0 \quad\text{for every }i\ge0. \]

primaryStatements.label: prop:reduction
primaryStatements.text: To prove Theorem \ref{thm:bloch} with rational coefficients, it is enough to prove it for smooth minimal surfaces \(X_0\) of general type with \(p_g=q=0\). For such a surface, putting \(k_0=K_{X_0}^2\), one has \begin{equation} 1\le k_0\le9,\qquad \chi(\mathcal O_{X_0})=1,\qquad \int_{X_0}c_2(X_0)=12-k_0,\qquad b_2(X_0)=10-k_0. \end{equation} It is also enough to prove the assertion on any chosen sequence of point blowups of each such \(X_0\).

primaryStatements.name: The determinant-fixed Quot theory
primaryStatements.label: prop:quot-pot
primaryStatements.text: In either setting \textup{(i)} or \textup{(ii)}, the enhancement $\mathfrak B$ induces a perfect obstruction theory $E_B\to L_B$, with virtual tangent \begin{equation} E_B^\vee\simeq \fib\left\{ \RHom(S',Q)\xrightarrow{d\det^o} \RGamma(\mathcal I_o)[1]\otimes\mathcal O_B \right\}. \end{equation} It is $G$-equivariant. Its virtual dimension is \begin{equation} v=2n+(A-K)D. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: The actual fixed obstruction theory
primaryStatements.label: prop:fixed-pot
primaryStatements.text: The enhancement $\mathfrak W$ induces a perfect obstruction theory $E_W\to L_W$. For $k:W\hookrightarrow B$, there is a natural isomorphism of obstruction theories \begin{equation} (Lk^*E_B)^{\mathrm{fix}}\xrightarrow{\sim}E_W, \end{equation} compatible with their maps to $L_W$. Its virtual tangent is \begin{equation} E_W^\vee\simeq \fib\left\{ \bigoplus_{i=1}^2\RHom(S'_i,Q_i) \longrightarrow\RGamma(\mathcal I_o)[1]\otimes\mathcal O_W \right\}. \end{equation} The moving virtual normal complex is \begin{equation} N_W^{\vir}=\bigoplus_{i\ne j}\RHom(S'_i,Q_j), \end{equation} where the $(i,j)$ summand has the difference between the characters on $L_j$ and $L_i$, or evaluated weight $w_j-w_i$.

primaryStatements.label: prop:fixed-pg0
primaryStatements.text: Assume \(p_g=q=0\). A nonempty fixed part with lines \(T,H\) and lengths satisfying \eqref{eq:length} is the smooth product \[ W=|T|\times|H|\times X^{[n_1]}\times X^{[n_2]}. \] Let \(x_i=c_1(\mathcal O_{|D_i|}(1))\), with \(D_1=T,D_2=H\). The fixed virtual class is \begin{equation} [W]^\vir= \prod_{i=1}^2\bigl(x_i^{h^1(D_i)}\eu(F_i)\bigr)\cap[W], \qquad F_i=\bigl((K-D_i)^{[n_i]}\bigr)^\vee\otimes\mathcal O(1_i). \end{equation} A part with either \(m_T<0\) or \(m_H<0\) contributes zero. For the other parts, after including \(\eu(F_1)\eu(F_2)\), pushforward over the linear systems is coefficient extraction at \([x_1^{m_T}x_2^{m_H}]\).

primaryStatements.label: prop:fixed-auxiliary
primaryStatements.text: Assume \(p_g=q=1\), \(K\) ample, and \(D=3K\). Every fixed contribution vanishes except those obtained from a low divisor equal to the empty divisor or to the canonical divisor. In either surviving case the contribution is computed on the actual fiber \[ |D_a|\times X^{[n_a]}\times X^{[n_b]}, \] with the factors \(\eu(F_a)\eu(F_b)\). The low hyperplane is \(x_b=0\) and \(m_{D_b}=0\); pushforward over \(|D_a|\) is extraction at \(x_a^{m_{D_a}}\). The overall multiplier is \(1\) for the empty divisor and \(-s\), with the same \(s>0\) as in \eqref{eq:canonical-cycle}, for the canonical divisor. The statement applies to operational insertions in universal perfect complexes, also after adjoining marked surface factors.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let \(n\geq1\), and let \(X\) be a compact irreducible holomorphic symplectic Kähler manifold of dimension \(2n\), with symplectic form \(\sigma\). Suppose that \[ f:X\longrightarrow B \] is a projective surjective holomorphic morphism with connected fibers, where \(B\) is a normal projective variety of dimension \(n\). Assume that every irreducible component of every fiber has dimension \(n\) and that the restriction of \(\sigma\) to its smooth locus is zero. Then \(B\) is isomorphic to \(\PP^n_{\C}\).

primaryStatements.name: Background for the given fibration
primaryStatements.label: prop:background
primaryStatements.text: In the setting of Theorem \ref{thm:main}, the following hold. \begin{enumerate} \item $X$ is projective, $e\neq0$ is nef and $q(e)=0$. The base is $\Q$-factorial and klt, has Picard number one, and $-K_B$ is ample as a $\Q$-Cartier divisor. A smooth fiber is an abelian variety after choosing an origin. \item There are reflexive identifications \[ R^j f_*\cO_X\simeq\Omega_B^{[j]}. \] For every integral Weil divisor $A$ ample as a $\Q$-divisor, \[ H^i\!\left(B, (\Omega_B^{[j]}\otimes\cO_B(A))^{**}\right)=0 \quad(i>0,\ j>0). \] The reflexivity assertion also applies locally to the projective equidimensional fibrations with connected fibers, smooth source \(Z\) satisfying \(\omega_Z\simeq\cO_Z\), and normal Cohen--Macaulay \(\Q\)-Gorenstein target that occur below. \item The rational intersection cohomology of $B$ has the Betti numbers of $\PP^n$, and the restriction of $H^2(X,\Q)$ to a smooth fiber has one-dimensional image. \item If $B$ is smooth, then $B\simeq\PP^n$. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.label: cor:tangent-rigidity
primaryStatements.text: If $n>1$, then $H^1(B,T_B)=0$.

primaryStatements.name: Strong hyperkähler SYZ, companion input
primaryStatements.label: thm:strong-syz
primaryStatements.text: Let $Y$ be a compact IHS Kähler manifold of dimension $2m$. If a holomorphic line bundle $L$ satisfies \[ c_1(L)\neq0,\qquad c_1(L)\in\overline{\mathcal K_Y},\qquad q_Y(c_1(L))=0, \] then a positive tensor power of $L$ is generated by its global sections. Its associated map with connected fibers has a normal projective base of dimension $m$. Every component of every fiber has dimension $m$ and is Lagrangian.

primaryStatements.name: Rational smoothness
primaryStatements.label: loc:rational-smoothness
primaryStatements.text: The space $B$ is an oriented rational homology manifold of real dimension $2n$. Its rational intersection complex is $\Q_B[n]$. Consequently its ordinary rational cohomology has the Betti numbers of $\PP^n$. The local rational homology-manifold assertion holds for every normal germ finitely dominated by a smooth germ, in particular for the maximal charts constructed below.

primaryStatements.name: Maximal quasi-\'etale charts and normalized source charts
primaryStatements.label: loc:maximal-charts
primaryStatements.text: Every pointed germ $(B,b)$ has a connected finite normal Galois quasi-\'etale cover $(C,c)$ which dominates every connected finite quasi-\'etale cover of that germ. The chart $(C,c)$ is klt, is finitely dominated by a smooth germ, and has no nontrivial connected finite quasi-\'etale cover. The finite diagrams can be defined over an algebraic \'etale neighborhood of $b$. More generally, let $U\to B$ be an integral separated \'etale algebraic neighborhood and let $\pi:C\to U$ be an integral finite normal quasi-\'etale cover. Put $X_U=X\times_B U$. The base change $X_U\times_U C$ has a unique irreducible component dominating $C$; let $Z$ be its normalization and $h:Z\to C$ its structure map. Then $h$ is projective and equidimensional of relative dimension $n$, has connected fibers, and satisfies $h_*\cO_Z=\cO_C$. The finite map $p:Z\to X_U$ is \'etale. Consequently $Z$ is smooth, the pullback of the symplectic form on $X$ is symplectic on $Z$, its canonical bundle is trivial, and the fibers of $h$ are Lagrangian. If $\pi$ is Galois with group $\Gamma$, then $p$ is a $\Gamma$-torsor. Ordinary \'etale base change on $C$ preserves projectivity, equidimensionality, connected fibers, the equality $h_*\cO_Z=\cO_C$, and the smooth symplectic source. The torsor in the statement belongs to the original finite chart.

primaryStatements.name: The residual tensor group
primaryStatements.label: loc:tannakian
primaryStatements.text: The residual category $\overline{\mathcal C}=\mathcal C/\mathcal R$ admits a fiber functor $\omega$ to complex vector spaces. For a choice of $\omega$, tensor reconstruction identifies it with $\operatorname{Rep}_{\C}(G)$, where $G=\Aut^\otimes(\omega)$ is a reductive algebraic subgroup of $\operatorname{GL}(V_{\mathrm{fib}})$ and $V_{\mathrm{fib}}=\omega(\overline V)$. This representation is faithful and has dimension $n$.

primaryStatements.name: Connectedness and semisimplicity
primaryStatements.label: loc:connected-semisimple
primaryStatements.text: The reductive group $G$ of Proposition \ref{loc:tannakian} is connected and semisimple.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let $X$ be a compact irreducible holomorphic symplectic K\"ahler manifold of complex dimension $2n$, where $n\ge1$. If a holomorphic line bundle $L$ satisfies \[ c_1(L)\ne0,\qquad c_1(L)\in\overline{\mathcal K_X}, \qquad q_X(c_1(L))=0, \] then $L$ is semiample. More precisely, there exist a positive integer $m$, a normal projective variety $B$, an ample line bundle $A$ on $B$, and a surjective holomorphic map with connected fibers \[ f:X\longrightarrow B,\qquad L^m\simeq f^*A, \] such that $\dim_{\C}B=n$. Every irreducible component of every fiber has complex dimension $n$, and $\sigma$ vanishes on its smooth locus.

primaryStatements.label: cor:finiteness
primaryStatements.text: For each integer $n\ge1$, there are only finitely many smooth deformation types of compact irreducible holomorphic symplectic K\"ahler manifolds of complex dimension $2n$ with $b_2\ge5$.

primaryStatements.name: Projective case
primaryStatements.label: cor:projective-base
primaryStatements.text: In Theorem \ref{thm:main}, assume additionally that $X$ is projective, and let $f:X\to B$ be the associated connected-fiber map furnished there. Then $B\simeq\mathbb P^n_{\C}$. Moreover, there do not exist a prime divisor $D\subset B$, an effective divisor $E$ on $X$, and an integer $r>1$ such that $f^*D=rE$.

primaryStatements.name: A special Lagrangian torus near a maximal crossing
primaryStatements.label: thm:torus
primaryStatements.text: Let $\pi:\mathcal Y\to\Delta$ be the restriction to a disk of a projective algebraic family over a smooth curve. Assume that $\mathcal Y$ is smooth, $\mathcal Y_0$ is a reduced simple normal crossings divisor, and the fibers $Y_t$ for $t\ne0$ are smooth connected projective manifolds of complex dimension $d\ge2$ with trivial canonical bundle. Let $a_t$ be polarizing classes given by a line bundle on $\mathcal Y$; this line bundle need not be relatively ample at $0$. Let $\eta_t$ be nowhere vanishing holomorphic $d$-forms which extend as a section of the relative logarithmic canonical line bundle. Put $s=-\log|t|$, and suppose that, for constants $c,C>0$, \begin{equation} c s^d\le I_t:=\int_{Y_t}|\eta_t|^2\le C s^d, \qquad 0<|t|\ll1. \end{equation} Suppose, moreover, that at some point $o\in\mathcal Y_0$ exactly $d+1$ components meet and that the logarithmic coefficient of $\eta$ at $o$ is nonzero. Thus in a coordinate neighborhood of $o$, \begin{equation} z_0z_1\cdots z_d=t, \qquad \eta_t=f(z)\,\frac{\dd z_1}{z_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge \frac{\dd z_d}{z_d}, \qquad f(o)\ne0. \end{equation} Equip $Y_t$ with the Ricci-flat K\"ahler metric in $a_t$. For every sufficiently small nonzero $t$, the fiber $Y_t$ contains a smooth embedded special Lagrangian real $d$-torus isotopic in $Y_t$ to an angular coordinate torus in \eqref{eq:crossing-chart}. Here special Lagrangian means that the K\"ahler form restricts to zero and that $\eta_t$ has constant phase on the oriented torus.

primaryStatements.label: cor:family-torus
primaryStatements.text: Fix an irrational $\lambda$ and choose the lifted path in Proposition \ref{prop:family} with $\tau=\lambda+iy$. For every sufficiently large $y$, the corresponding smooth fiber contains an embedded special Lagrangian real $d$-torus for its Ricci-flat metric in the polarization class. papers.title: Every complex K3 surface is Oka
papers.abstract: We prove that every complex K3 surface X is Oka, resolving the K3 Oka conjecture. Equivalently, for every m ≥ 1, every holomorphic map to X from a neighborhood of a compact convex set in ℂm can be approximated uniformly on that set by entire maps $\mathbb C^m\to X$.
papers.familySummary: Proves that every complex K3 surface is Oka, including nonprojective surfaces. More generally, every connected minimal compact complex surface of Kodaira dimension zero is Oka; a connected minimal compact complex surface of class VII is Oka exactly when it is a Hopf or Enoki surface.
papers.subject: Algebraic and complex geometry
papers.sourceAbstract: We prove that every complex K3 surface $X$ is Oka, resolving the K3 Oka conjecture. Equivalently, for every $m\geq1$, every holomorphic map to $X$ from a neighborhood of a compact convex set in $\C^m$ can be approximated uniformly on that set by entire maps $\C^m\to X$.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let $X$ be a complex K3 surface, with any smooth Hermitian distance $d_X$. For every integer $m\geq1$, every nonempty compact convex set $K\subset\C^m$, every open neighborhood $U$ of $K$, every holomorphic map $f:U\to X$, and every $\epsilon>0$, there exists a holomorphic map $F:\C^m\to X$ such that \[ \sup_{z\in K}d_X(F(z),f(z))<\epsilon. \]

primaryStatements.label: cor:dense
primaryStatements.text: Let $S$ be a complex K3 surface. For every $x\in S$ and every nonzero vector $v\in T_xS$, there is a holomorphic immersion $f:\C\to S$ such that \[ f(0)=x,\qquad f'(0)=v,\qquad \overline{f(\C)}=S, \] where closure is taken in the ordinary complex topology. If $S$ is projective, then $f(\C)$ is Zariski dense.

primaryStatements.name: Two complete directions
primaryStatements.label: loc:criterion
primaryStatements.text: Suppose there are holomorphic maps \[ \sigma_1:\C\times\Delta_b\longrightarrow X,\qquad \sigma_2:\Delta_b\times\C\longrightarrow X \] which are locally biholomorphic at $(0,0)$ and satisfy $\sigma_1(z,0)=\sigma_2(z,0)$ for small $z$. If $\sigma_2$ is locally biholomorphic at $(0,c)$, then $L$ holds at $x=\sigma_2(0,c)$. The same conclusion holds for a sequence of pairs whose long coordinate domains are discs of radii tending to infinity, whose bounded-coordinate radii are bounded below, and whose maps converge near $(0,0)$ and, for the second map, near $(0,c)$ to the above nondegenerate germs. Exact axis agreement is required for every pair. In this version $x$ is the value of the limiting second germ at $(0,c)$.

primaryStatements.label: loc:planar
primaryStatements.text: Let $K$ be a closed circular disc of radius $r$, or a closed circular annulus with outer radius $r$, and let $f$ be holomorphic near $K\times P$, where $P$ is a closed polydisc. Suppose that for every $\zeta$ on the outer circle there is a coordinate witness neighborhood $V_\zeta$ for $L$ containing $f(\{\zeta\}\times P)$. For every $R>r$ and $P_0\Subset\operatorname{int}P$, one can approximate $f$ uniformly on $K\times P_0$ by a map holomorphic near the enlarged disc, respectively annulus with the same inner radius and outer radius $R$, times $P_0$.

primaryStatements.name: Propagation across a small disc
primaryStatements.label: loc:disc
primaryStatements.text: Suppose a coordinate neighborhood contains a closed affine complex-line disc centered at $x$, with its boundary in the open locus where $L$ holds. Then $L$ holds at $x$. In particular, if the complement of that locus is contained locally in a proper analytic subset, $L$ holds everywhere.

primaryStatements.label: ana:cap
primaryStatements.text: Let \(Y\) be a complex surface with a complete compatible distance. If the local operation \(L\) holds at every point of \(Y\), then \(Y\) has the convex approximation property in every source dimension.

primaryStatements.label: ana:polydisc
primaryStatements.text: Under the hypotheses of Theorem \ref{ana:cap}, a map holomorphic near a closed polydisc in \(\C^m\) can be approximated uniformly there by entire maps \(\C^m\to Y\). More precisely, a map near \(\overline\Delta_1^{\,m}\) can be approximated there by maps holomorphic near \(\overline\Delta_R^{\,m}\), for every finite \(R>1\).

primaryStatements.label: prj:strips
primaryStatements.text: Let $S$ be a smooth projective complex K3 surface. There is a nonempty Zariski open subset $U\subset S$ such that, for every $x\in U$, there are $b>0$ and holomorphic maps \[ \sigma_1:\C\times\Delta_b\longrightarrow S,\qquad \sigma_2:\Delta_b\times\C\longrightarrow S \] which are locally biholomorphic at the origin and satisfy \[ \sigma_1(0,0)=\sigma_2(0,0)=x,\qquad \sigma_1(z,0)=\sigma_2(z,0)\quad (|z|<b). \] The complement $S\setminus U$ is algebraic of dimension at most one. Consequently $S$ has property $L$ everywhere.

definitions.label: loc:property
definitions.text: A complex surface $X$ has property $L$ at $x$ if there is an open neighborhood $V$ of $x$ with the following property. For every special pair $D\subset D'$, every pair of closed polydiscs $P_0\Subset\operatorname{int}P\subset\C^q$, and every holomorphic map $f$ from a neighborhood of $D\times P$ into $V$, the restriction $f|_{D\times P_0}$ is a uniform limit of maps holomorphic near $D'\times P_0$ with values in $X$. The case $q=0$ is included. We call $V$ a witness neighborhood.

papers.title: P=W in composite rank for fixed determinant
papers.abstract: We prove the P = W conjecture on the full rational cohomology of fixed-determinant, trace-free Higgs moduli spaces in composite rank and coprime degree, for smooth projective complex curves of genus at least two. Together with the established prime-rank cases, this gives the equality in every coprime rank.

This includes variant cohomology and, together with the known prime-rank theorems, establishes the fixed-determinant P = W conjecture in every coprime rank.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: For every smooth projective complex curve $C$ of genus $g\ge2$, every composite integer $n\ge4$, every integer $d$ with $\gcd(n,d)=1$, and every $L\in\Pic^d(C)$, one has \[ P_kH^m(X^B,\Q)=W_{2k}H^m(X^B,\Q) =W_{2k+1}H^m(X^B,\Q) \] for all $m,k\ge0$.

primaryStatements.label: norm:relative-lefschetz
primaryStatements.text: Cup product by $e$ sends $P_kH^m(X)$ into $P_{k+2}H^{m+2}(X)$. For every $i\ge0$ and every $m$, it induces an isomorphism \begin{equation} e^i:\operatorname{Gr}^P_{R-i}H^m(X) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \operatorname{Gr}^P_{R+i}H^{m+2i}(X). \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Comparison by a common lowering operator
primaryStatements.label: alg:comparison
primaryStatements.text: Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over a field of characteristic zero, with finite, exhaustive, separated increasing integer-indexed filtrations $F_\bullet$ and $G_\bullet$. Suppose that $e,f\in\operatorname{End}(H)$ satisfy, for $A_\bullet=F_\bullet$ and $A_\bullet=G_\bullet$, \[ e(A_k)\subseteq A_{k+2},\qquad f(A_k)\subseteq A_{k-2}. \] Assume that the induced raiser on each associated graded is Lefschetz with the same center $r$, and that \begin{equation} [[f,e],e]=-2e, \qquad [u,v]=uv-vu. \end{equation} Then $F_k=G_k$ for every integer $k$. If $H$ has a further grading respected by both filtrations, and $e,f$ have degrees $2,-2$ for that grading, the equality holds degree by degree.

primaryStatements.label: betti:lefschetz
primaryStatements.text: The mixed Hodge structure on $H^*(X^{\mathrm B},\mathbb Q)$ is Hodge--Tate. Under the nonabelian-Hodge identification, the class $e$ has nonzero image in $\operatorname{Gr}^W_4H^2(X^{\mathrm B},\mathbb Q)$, and \[ e^i:\operatorname{Gr}^W_{2R-2i}H^m(X^{\mathrm B},\mathbb Q) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \operatorname{Gr}^W_{2R+2i}H^{m+2i}(X^{\mathrm B},\mathbb Q) \qquad(i\geq0). \] In particular, $W_{2k}=W_{2k+1}$ on this cohomology. These assertions concern the entire cohomology, including all nontrivial $\Gamma$-character summands after complexification.

primaryStatements.name: Diagram weights
primaryStatements.label: diag:variation
primaryStatements.text: Under the preceding hypotheses, $H^j(\mathscr H_t,\mathbb Q)$ carries a graded-polarizable mixed Hodge structure, functorial for maps of flat bundles that are algebraic in flat trivializations. As $t$ varies, these structures form an admissible graded-polarizable variation of mixed Hodge structures, with an integral underlying local system up to torsion. They are computed by $H^j(i_t^*K_{\mathscr H})$. If $H^j(H_t,\mathbb Q)$ is Hodge--Tate for every $j$ and $t$, then $H^j(\mathscr H_t,\mathbb Q)$ is Hodge--Tate as well. We call its weight filtration the diagram weight filtration.

primaryStatements.name: Weight shifts
primaryStatements.label: diag:gysin
primaryStatements.text: The diagram weight filtrations have the following properties. \begin{enumerate} \item For the product $S\times M$, with $M$ a complex algebraic variety, the ordinary K\"unneth isomorphism identifies its mixed Hodge structure with that on \[ H^*(S,\mathbb Q)\otimes H^*(M,\mathbb Q), \] where every $H^a(S,\mathbb Q)$ is pure of weight zero and type $(0,0)$, and $H^*(M,\mathbb Q)$ has its Deligne mixed Hodge structure. If $S$ is oriented and closed of real dimension $d_S$, projection pullback and integration over $S$ preserve weight; the latter has cohomological degree $-d_S$. \item Pullbacks by maps of flat bundles preserve weight. \item Suppose $u:\mathscr H_t\to\mathscr H'_t$ is a proper map of flat bundles with smooth equidimensional algebraic fibers. Put $c=\dim_{\mathbb C}H'_t-\dim_{\mathbb C}H_t$. With the complex orientations on the fibers, its ordinary Gysin map satisfies \[ u_*:W_aH^j(\mathscr H_t)\longrightarrow W_{a+2c}H^{j+2c}(\mathscr H'_t). \] If $S$ is oriented, this is the Gysin map for the induced orientations on the total spaces. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.label: log:families
primaryStatements.text: The morphism $\mathcal Y\to S\times\Lambda$ is smooth of relative dimension $2R+2b$, and $\mathcal X\to\mathbb A^1$ is smooth of relative dimension $2R$. Their total spaces are semiprojective for scaling the operators, which scales $\lambda$ and every $u_i$ with weight one. The same holds for the inverse image in $\mathcal Y$ of every linear subspace of $\Lambda$ through zero. In Figure \ref{log:scalar-correspondence}, $\pi$ is a smooth proper flag projection of relative dimension $b$, and $\iota$ is a regular embedding of codimension $b$ with normal bundle $T_\pi^*$.

primaryStatements.label: log:restriction
primaryStatements.text: For every $(\lambda,u)\in\Lambda$, restriction induces an isomorphism \begin{equation} \rho_{\lambda,u}:H^*(\mathcal Y,\mathbb Q) \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^*(Y_{\lambda,u},\mathbb Q). \end{equation} Restriction to the inverse image of any line through zero in $\Lambda$ is also an isomorphism, as is restriction from that inverse image to any of its fibers. The analogous restriction isomorphisms hold for all four families in Figure \ref{log:scalar-correspondence} over the $\lambda$-line. They commute with pullbacks and with the proper Gysin maps in that correspondence, including integration in the $S$ factor.

papers.title: The equivariant cohomological Hikita conjecture for arbitrary quivers
papers.abstract: We prove the equivariant cohomological Hikita conjecture for arbitrary finite quivers, including loops and multiple arrows. For any dimension and framing vectors, any commuting flavor torus, and a stability character whose semistable locus is stable and has free gauge action, the equivariant cohomology of the Nakajima variety is canonically isomorphic to the coordinate ring of the scheme-theoretic fixed locus of the stability cocharacter on the flavor-deformed Coulomb branch. This is an isomorphism of graded algebras over the common coefficient ring, retaining nilpotents and including the empty case.

When every semistable point is stable and the gauge action is free, the equivariant cohomology of the Nakajima variety is canonically the coordinate ring of the scheme-theoretic cocharacter-fixed locus of its flavor-deformed Coulomb branch.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: For every datum \eqref{eq:gauge-data}, every commuting flavor torus $F$, and every regular stability character $\nu$, both coefficient maps are surjective and have the same kernel. They therefore induce a canonical isomorphism of graded $R$-algebras \[ H_F^*(X;\C)\ \cong\ \C[Y_{\mathfrak f}^{\nu}]. \] The gradings are ordinary cohomological degree and BFN homological degree, respectively. The assertion includes the empty case, whose ring is zero.

primaryStatements.name: Abelianization and minuscule generation
primaryStatements.label: prop:minuscule
primaryStatements.text: There is an injective coefficient-preserving algebra map from $A_F$ into \[ \bigl(\operatorname{Frac}(P_F)[X_*(T)]\bigr)^{\mathcal W},\qquad e^\lambda e^\gamma=e^{\lambda+\gamma}. \] Besides $R$, the algebra is generated by the dressed classes associated with all nonzero positive and negative minuscule coweights. For $p\in P_F^{\mathcal W_\lambda}$, the class has expression \begin{equation} \sum_{\lambda'\in\mathcal W\lambda} e^{\lambda'}p_{\lambda'} \frac{\prod_{\beta\in\wt(N)} \beta^{(-\langle\beta,\lambda'\rangle)_+}} {\eu_T(T_{t^{\lambda'}}\Gr_G^\lambda)}. \end{equation} Each distinct translate occurs once, and the dressing is translated with the coweight. Denote this class by $M_{\lambda,p}$. Weights $\beta$ include their flavor components, but pairings use only the gauge components; factors with exponent zero are omitted. The class has charge $[\lambda]$. On charge zero, the BFN grading is twice the ordinary polynomial degree of the rational coefficients in this description.

primaryStatements.label: prop:kernel-inclusion
primaryStatements.text: For every datum and regular stability in Theorem \ref{thm:main}, the coefficient map induces a graded $R$-algebra surjection \begin{equation} B_F\twoheadrightarrow H_F^*(X). \end{equation}

primaryStatements.label: prop:laurent-model
primaryStatements.text: Under the abelianization embedding of Proposition \ref{prop:minuscule}, the no-flavor Coulomb algebra is \begin{equation} A_0=\left(\bigoplus_{\lambda\in\Z^\Omega}P r_\lambda\right)^{\mathcal W}. \end{equation} The identification preserves the coefficient ring $R_0=P^{\mathcal W}$ and the topological grading.

primaryStatements.label: prop:filtration-bound
primaryStatements.text: The quotient $B_0$ for the full topological torus satisfies the coefficientwise graded bound \begin{equation} \Hilb(B_0;q)\ \leq \sum_{m\in\mathcal M(\mathbf v)} q^{C(\mathbf v)-D_m+\mathbf w\cdot(\mathbf v-\mathbf l)}h_m(q). \end{equation} Every exponent displayed in the sum is a nonnegative integer.

primaryStatements.label: prop:cut-recurrence
primaryStatements.text: For every finite array $m$, \begin{equation} \frac{1}{(q)_m} =\sum_{k+m'=m} q^{w(k)+b(k,m')}\frac{h_{m'}(q)}{(q)_k}. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.label: cor:cut-generating-ratio
primaryStatements.text: In the formal power series ring $\C(q)[[z_i:i\in Q_0]]$, \begin{equation} \sum_m z^{\|m\|}q^{-D_m-w(m)}h_m(q) = \frac{\displaystyle\sum_m z^{\|m\|}q^{-D_m-w(m)}/(q)_m} {\displaystyle\sum_m z^{\|m\|}q^{-D_m}/(q)_m}. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.label: prop:hausel-identification
primaryStatements.text: For a quiver with a loop at every vertex of positive dimension, \begin{equation} P_{X_{\det}(v,w)}(q) =\sum_{\|m\|=v} q^{C(v)-D_m+w\cdot(v-l)}h_m(q). \end{equation}

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: There exist a smooth connected projective complex fourfold $X$ and a simple abelian surface $A\subset X$ such that \begin{enumerate} \item $X$ has large fundamental group; \item $\im\bigl(\pi_1(A)\to\pi_1(X)\bigr)\simeq\Z$. \end{enumerate} The universal cover $\widetilde X$ contains no positive-dimensional compact complex analytic subvariety and is not Stein.

primaryStatements.label: prop:large-reduction
primaryStatements.text: Let $A$ be a simple abelian surface and let $A\hookrightarrow S'$ be a closed embedding in a smooth connected projective complex variety. Suppose that \[ \im\bigl(\pi_1(A)\longrightarrow\pi_1(S')\bigr)\simeq\Z. \] There exist a smooth connected projective fourfold $X$ with large fundamental group and a closed embedding $A\hookrightarrow X$ with infinite cyclic image on fundamental groups, such that the universal cover of $X$ is not Stein.

primaryStatements.name: Exact local arrangements
primaryStatements.label: prop:arrangement-local
primaryStatements.text: Given $W>0$ and $R_0>0$, there is a torsion-free principal congruence subgroup $\Gamma_0$, normalized by $\sigma$, with the following properties. Let $\mathcal A_0$ be the union of all $\Gamma_0$-translates of the labeled hyperplanes of $\cD$. \begin{enumerate} \item The arrangement $\mathcal A_0$ is locally finite. The hyperplanes meeting any ball of radius $W$ have distinct labels and are carried to the corresponding subarrangement of $\cD$ by a holomorphic isometry induced by a unitary map sending each prescribed translated normal to its prototype normal. \item The injectivity radius of $\Gamma_0\backslash\BB$ is greater than $R_0$. \item In the ball of radius $R_0$ about $o$, the arrangement is exactly $\cD$ restricted to that ball. The analogous assertion holds in every $\Gamma_0$-translate of this ball. \end{enumerate} All these conclusions concerning the lifted arrangement remain valid on any subsequent finite cover of $\Gamma_0\backslash\BB$, provided one uses the full inverse image of the arrangement.

primaryStatements.name: Virtual cyclic ramified covers
primaryStatements.label: geo:stover-toledo
primaryStatements.text: Let $M_0$ be a compact ball quotient of complex dimension at least two by a torsion-free congruence arithmetic lattice of simplest type. Let $D$ be a nonempty totally geodesic divisor whose components are smooth, embedded, and pairwise disjoint. For every integer $d\ge2$ there is a finite unramified cover $M_1\to M_0$ such that $M_1$ admits a cyclic cover of degree $d$, branched over the full inverse image of $D$.

primaryStatements.name: The geometric construction
primaryStatements.label: prop:orbifold-surface
primaryStatements.text: After any prescribed finite lower bounds on the arrangement radii and injectivity radius, the construction above gives a smooth connected proper effective orbifold $\cS$ with projective coarse space, a simple abelian surface $A=\Jac(C)$, an iterated point blowup $Y\to A$, and a morphism $f:Y\to\cS$ with image in its ordinary locus. The distinguished fiber is obtained from the product $C\times C$, its normal bundle $\operatorname{pr}_1^*L\oplus\operatorname{pr}_2^*L$, and the action \eqref{geo:line-action} by the explicit blowups and coarse quotients above. Away from that fiber the orbifold is $[V/\langle s\rangle]$, with $V$ given by the two parity covers and the filling rules of Section \ref{geo:fill}.

primaryStatements.name: Compatibility of kernels
primaryStatements.label: prop:kernel-compatibility
primaryStatements.text: For every $R>0$ there are constants $B(R)>R$ and $J_0(R)$, depending only on $\cD$, with the following properties. \begin{enumerate} \item Suppose two finite-model descriptions, with their prescribed normal matches, agree on all hyperplanes meeting $B(x,B(R))$. Identify their sign covers there by a fixed choice of sheets. On loops in this sign cover that project into $B(x,R)$, their individual $z$ kernels agree and their individual $w$ kernels agree. More precisely, for each family the corresponding integer homomorphisms agree up to sign. The descriptions may include additional hyperplanes outside the buffered ball. \item In the full model, if $\dist(x,o)>J_0(R)$, then on such loops \[ \ker(\ell_z+\ell_w)=\ker\ell_z\cap\ker\ell_w. \] \end{enumerate} Both statements remain valid after restricting the loops to avoid any further analytic subsets. The first statement is equivariant under the symmetry interchanging the families.

primaryStatements.name: Hyperbolicity of the models
primaryStatements.label: prop:model-hyperbolicity
primaryStatements.text: There are $u>0$ and $\delta\ge0$, depending only on $\cD$, such that every connected component of every $\mathcal G_T(u)$ and of $\mathcal G_{\mathrm{cen}}(u)$ is $\delta$-hyperbolic. The same $\delta$ can be used if an arbitrary locally finite union of proper complex analytic subsets of $\BB$ is additionally omitted, with invariant omissions in the central case. On the vertices retained after such an omission, graph distances are unchanged.

primaryStatements.label: thm:orbifold-cyclic
primaryStatements.text: For a sufficiently deep choice of the arithmetic level in the construction of Proposition \ref{prop:orbifold-surface}, the map $f:Y\longrightarrow\cS$ satisfies \[ \im\bigl(f_*:\pi_1(Y)\longrightarrow\pi_1(\cS)\bigr)\cong\Z. \] Here $Y$ is an iterated point blowup of the simple abelian surface $\Jac(C)$, and its image lies in the ordinary locus of $\cS$.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: There is a smooth connected projective complex surface $X$ containing a connected nodal curve $Z_0$ with smooth rational irreducible components such that \[ \im\bigl(\pi_1(Z_0)\longrightarrow\pi_1(X)\bigr) \quad\text{is infinite}. \] In the simply connected universal cover of $X$, a connected component above $Z_0$ is a closed, connected, noncompact, locally finite union of compact rational curves. The holomorphic hull of any one of its points is noncompact. In particular, this universal cover is not holomorphically convex.

primaryStatements.label: prop:based-monodromy
primaryStatements.text: The actions $\varphi_m$ form a homomorphism $\Gamma\to\Aut(F)$, are pure, and commute with $\iota_*$. They preserve $K$. If $\beta_m\in\Aut(\Pi)$ is the actual based monodromy of the punctured sphere family, then \begin{equation} p\circ\varphi_m|_K=\beta_m\circ p. \end{equation} Moreover, $p:K\to\Pi$ is surjective.

primaryStatements.label: prop:monodromy-raising
primaryStatements.text: For every $m\in\Gamma$, the induced operator $\varphi_m-\id$ on the weighted completed Magnus algebra of $\widehat F$ raises degree by at least one.

primaryStatements.label: prop:involution
primaryStatements.text:
Let \(L\) be the free pro-\(2\) group on \(a_{h,j}\), with \(h\in(\Z/4)^2\) and \(0\le j\le2\), and let \(\sigma(a_{h,j})=a_{b_j-h,j}^{-1}\), where \(b_j mod2
e0\). Equip \(L\) with the basis and weights of \Cref{lem:shift-basis}. There are 24 elements \(g\in L\), with assigned positive weights \(w_g\), such that \[ 
u_L(g)\ge w_g,\qquad 
u_L(r_g)\ge w_g+1, \qquad r_g=\sigma(g)g^{-1}, \] and the closed normal subgroup generated by the \(r_g\) imposes \(\sigma=\id\) on all of \(L\). The basis polynomial and the polynomial of the chosen weights are  egin{equation}  egin{split} P(t)&=\sum_{i,\ell,j}t^{i+\ell+1} =3t(1+t+t^2+t^3)^2,\ G(t)&=\sum_g t^{w_g} =3t(1+t)(1+t^2)^2. \end{split} \end{equation} In particular, \(P=(1+t)G\), and these involution relations have degree cost at most \(tG(t)\).

primaryStatements.label: prop:infinite-quotient
primaryStatements.text: The group $Q$ is infinite. The homomorphism \[ \rho:\pi_1(U)\longrightarrow Q \] induced by $\rho_0$ has dense image on every punctured fiber. Each component meridian of $D$ has finite image, and every component meridian of $D_*$ has trivial image.

papers.title: An explicit failure of complex affine-space cancellation
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit integral complex affine fourfold X with $X\times\mathbb A^1\cong\mathbb A^5$ but $X\not\cong\mathbb A^4$. This gives a negative answer to Zariski's affine-space cancellation problem over ℂ in dimension four. The same construction disproves the Stable Coordinate Conjecture in ambient dimension five and yields smooth 𝔸3-fibrations over 𝔸1 and 𝔸2 that are not Zariski-locally trivial. These fibrations disprove the Dolgachev–Weisfeiler affine-fibration conjecture over these bases.
papers.familySummary: Constructs an integral complex affine fourfold $X\not\cong\mathbb A^4$ with $X\times\mathbb A^1\cong\mathbb A^5$, disproving affine-space cancellation over ℂ in dimension four. It also disproves the Dolgachev–Weisfeiler affine-fibration conjecture: smooth surjections $X\to\mathbb A^1$ and $\mathbb A^5\to\mathbb A^2$ have every residue-field fiber isomorphic to affine three-space but are not Zariski-locally trivial.

papers.sourceAbstract: We construct an explicit integral complex affine fourfold $X$ with $X\times\mathbb A^1\cong\mathbb A^5$ but $X\not\cong\mathbb A^4$. This gives a negative answer to Zariski's affine-space cancellation problem over $\mathbb C$ in dimension four. The same construction disproves the Stable Coordinate Conjecture in ambient dimension five and yields smooth $\mathbb A^3$-fibrations over $\mathbb A^1$ and $\mathbb A^2$ that are not Zariski-locally trivial. These fibrations disprove the Dolgachev--Weisfeiler affine-fibration conjecture over these bases.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: The algebra $A$ in \eqref{eq:example} is an integral complex algebra of dimension four. For an independent variable $w$, \[ A[w]\simeq\kk\poly5, \qquad A\not\simeq\kk\poly4. \] Consequently the Zariski cancellation problem over the complex numbers has a negative answer in dimension four.

primaryStatements.label: prop:principalization
primaryStatements.text: The morphism $\Spec\Rt\to\Spec R$ is the complement of the zero section in a line bundle, with fiber scaling specified by the weights \[ \wt(a)=\wt(d)=1,\qquad \wt(b)=\wt(c)=-1,\qquad \wt(u)=0. \] The homomorphism $R\to\Rt$ is faithfully flat, and $I\Rt=(v)$. Moreover, base change gives a faithfully flat inclusion $G\hookrightarrow\Gt$, where \begin{equation} \Gt:=G\otimes_R\Rt =\Rt[\tau,v/\tau^2]\subset\Rt[\tau,\tau^{-1}],\qquad \Gt\cong\Rt[\tau,V]/(\tau^2V-v). \end{equation} Thus $V$ denotes the element $v/\tau^2$ in the displayed subalgebra. The ring $\Gt$ is a domain and has the following commuting gradings: \begin{center} \begin{tabular}{c@{\qquad}rrrrr} \toprule & $a,d$ & $b,c$ & $u$ & $\tau$ & $V$\\ \midrule Valuation degree & $0$ & $0$ & $0$ & $-1$ & $2$\\ Fiber weight & $1$ & $-1$ & $0$ & $0$ & $2$\\ \bottomrule \end{tabular} \end{center}

primaryStatements.name: Failure of the Stable Coordinate Conjecture
primaryStatements.label: cor:stable-coordinate
primaryStatements.text: The polynomial $H$ in \eqref{eq:example} is not a coordinate of $P=\kk[p,s,u,F,J]$, but it is a coordinate of $P[w]$ for one independent variable $w$. Thus the Stable Coordinate Conjecture over $\kk$ fails in ambient dimension five after one stabilization.

primaryStatements.label: prop:stabilization
primaryStatements.text: For the algebra \(A\) in \Cref{con:setup}, there is an algebraic \(\kk\)-isomorphism \[ A[w]\cong\kk\poly{5}. \]

primaryStatements.label: prop:graded
primaryStatements.text: Under \Cref{deg:graded-injection}, the associated graded algebra is the following specific subalgebra of $R[\tau,\tau^{-1}]$: \begin{equation} G:=\gr A =R[\tau,I/\tau^2] =R[\tau,f/\tau^2,g/\tau^2]. \end{equation} It is a smooth domain. Give $P=\kk[p,s,u,F,J]$ the presentation weights \begin{equation} (\omega(p),\omega(s),\omega(u),\omega(F),\omega(J)) =(-1,0,0,2,2). \end{equation} Then every nonzero $h\in A$ has a polynomial representative whose maximum weight is exactly $\deg h$, and there is a graded isomorphism \begin{equation} G\cong P/(H_{\mathrm{top}}),\qquad H_{\mathrm{top}}=x^2F-(1+2sx)J-p^2J^2, \quad x=s^2+u^3+p^2F. \end{equation} The images of $p,s,u,F,J$ in this isomorphism are respectively $\tau,s_R,u,f/\tau^2,g/\tau^2$.

primaryStatements.label: prop:positive-invariant
primaryStatements.text: If $A\cong\kk\poly{4}$, then $G$ admits a nonzero homogeneous LND with a nonzero homogeneous invariant of strictly positive valuation degree.

primaryStatements.label: prop:linearization
primaryStatements.text: Let $X$ be a smooth integral affine variety over $\kk$, and let $\pi\colon\Aff^1\times X\to X$ be the projection. Then \[ \pi^*\colon\Pic(X)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } \Pic(\Aff^1\times X). \] For every algebraic additive action $\alpha\colon\Ga\times X\to X$ and every line bundle $L$ on $X$, there is a unique isomorphism of line bundles \begin{equation} \phi\colon\pi^*L\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\alpha^*L \end{equation} whose restriction to $\{0\}\times X$ is $\mathrm{id}_L$. This isomorphism obeys the action cocycle. It therefore defines a unique action on $L$ that lifts $\alpha$, is linear on its fibers, and acts as the identity at the group identity. The action preserves $L^\times$ and commutes with fiber scaling. If $L^\times$ is affine, the induced derivation of its coordinate ring is locally nilpotent and preserves the fiber weights.

primaryStatements.label: prop:homogeneous-lift
primaryStatements.text: Let $D_0$ be a homogeneous locally nilpotent derivation of $G$ of valuation degree shift $j$. There is a locally nilpotent derivation $\Dt$ of $\Gt$ restricting to $D_0$ on $G$, with fiber weight zero and valuation degree shift $j$. If $D_0\ne0$, then $\Dt\ne0$.

lean.scopeText:
Affine-space cancellation asks whether $X\times\mathbb A^1\cong\mathbb A^{n+1}$ forces $X\cong\mathbb A^n$. The formalized result gives an explicit finite-type complex domain $A$ of Krull dimension four with $A[w]\cong\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_5]$ but $A\not\cong\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_4]$. Thus adjoining one variable erases a genuine algebraic distinction.

The separate stable-coordinate and general line-bundle lifting consequences are not included.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: There exist a finitely generated normal integral $\CC$-algebra $A$ of Krull dimension two and a maximal ideal $\m\subset A$ such that \[ \Der_{\CC}(A)\simeq A^{\oplus2}, \qquad A_{\m}\text{ is not regular}. \]

primaryStatements.label: prop:curve-data
primaryStatements.text: The construction above produces a smooth connected projective curve $C$, a reduced divisor $Z=q_1+\cdots+q_6$, line bundles $H,L,\theta$, and a basis $u=(u_1,u_2)$ of $H^0(C,H)$ with the following properties. \begin{enumerate} \item The numerical and canonical data are \[ \begin{gathered} g(C)=21,\qquad \deg H=4,\qquad\deg L=10,\\ L=H+Z,\qquad\theta=2L,\qquad K_C=4L, \end{gathered} \] where the last isomorphism is normalized by \eqref{curve:adjunction-normalization} and $\xi^4\mapsto\gamma|_C$. The curve $C$ has exactly fourth-order contact with the auxiliary elliptic curve $\Gamma$ at every $q_j$. \item The pencil $u$ defines a finite degree-four morphism $f:C\to\PP^1$ unramified at every $q_j$, and the values $f(q_j)$ are not all equal. The zero divisor of $u_1$ can be chosen to be a reduced fiber disjoint from $Z$. \item The section dimensions are \begin{equation} \begin{gathered} h^0(C,jH)=j+1\quad(0\le j\le3),\\ h^0(C,L)=h^0(C,H+2Z)=2,\qquad h^0(C,\theta)=3,\qquad h^0(C,\OO_C(Z))=1,\\ h^0(C,\theta+H)=6. \end{gathered} \end{equation} More precisely, \begin{equation} \begin{split} H^0(C,L)&=\xi H^0(C,H),\\ H^0(C,H+2Z)&=\xi^2H^0(C,H),\\ H^0(C,\theta)&=\xi^2H^0(C,2H). \end{split} \end{equation} In particular $r=\xi u$ is a basis of $H^0(C,L)$ with simple common zero divisor exactly $Z$, and every section of $\theta$ vanishes twice along $Z$. \item For every $k\ge2$, the evaluation map \begin{equation} H^0(C,(k+1)L)\longrightarrow H^0(Z,((k+1)L)|_Z) \end{equation} is surjective. \item The auxiliary data on $\Gamma\subset\Sigma$, including the compatible bundle identities, the logarithmic volume $\Omega$, and the quadratic form $Q$, are as in \eqref{curve:bundle-identities} and \eqref{curve:quadratic}; the divisor $Z$ belongs to $|M|$. The six nonzero vectors $w_j\in H^0(\Gamma,\Phi)^*$ have the projective evaluation directions at $q_j$, use three distinct directions, and satisfy \eqref{curve:vector-conditions}, with $w^2=90=9\deg L$. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.name: Residue data
primaryStatements.label: prop:residue-data
primaryStatements.text: For the curve, line bundles, fixed fourth-root isomorphism, and six vectors $w_j\in H^0(\Gamma,\Phi)^*$ of Proposition \ref{prop:curve-data}, one can choose the basis $u$ with unchanged determinant so that $(u_1)_0$ is an unramified fiber of $f$ disjoint from $Z$. Set $r=\xi u$ and define \[ v_j^*=\iota^*w_j\in W^*,\qquad V=\sum_{j=1}^6v_j^*. \] For any mutually disjoint compatible coordinate disks as above there are nonzero constants $c_j$ and a global pair \[ P=(P_1,P_2)\in H^0(C,\theta+Z)^{\oplus2} \] with the following properties. First, \begin{equation} c_jl_j=v_j^*,\qquad V^2=90=9\deg L,\qquad (v_j^*)^2+v_j^*\cdot V=1. \end{equation} On disk $j$, using coefficient rows in the indicated frames, put \begin{equation} m_j=\frac{c_j}{z_j},\qquad R_j=m_jr,\qquad W_j=R_j(0)\wedge R_j'(0),\qquad p_j=P-m_jr'. \end{equation} The pair $P$ has principal part $R_j(0)/z_j$ in the frame $(\ell_j^{\mathrm{fr}})^2$ of $\theta$; the rows $R_j,p_j$ are holomorphic on the disk, and $R_j(0)\ne0$. Moreover, \begin{equation} W_j=(v_j^*)^2,\qquad p_j(0)\wedge R_j(0)=1,\qquad \sum_{j=1}^6(W_j-1)=-9\deg L. \end{equation} Globally, \begin{equation} J=u\wedge P\in H^0(C,\Lambda),\qquad \langle[J],[T]\rangle=-V([T]) \quad\text{for every }T\in H^0(C,\Lambda). \end{equation} Changing $P$ by a holomorphic pair of sections of $\theta$ does not change $[J]$. The pole prescription is consistent under changes of compatible coordinates.

primaryStatements.name: Finite compatible jets
primaryStatements.label: prop:jets
primaryStatements.text: For the data of Propositions \ref{prop:curve-data} and \ref{prop:residue-data}, there are finitely many holomorphic disk-to-outside transition germs, each a composition of flows \eqref{jets:generator} of orders $1,\ldots,7$, together with holomorphic local rows $A_k,B_k$ for $0\leq k\leq7$, such that: the transitions fix $C$ and preserve its conormal bundle $L$; the vector fields \eqref{jets:fields} match through row index seven; and $A\wedge B=t^2(1+O(t))$ on every chart. On any surface neighborhood $Y$ realizing these transition germs, write $\cI=\OO_Y(-C)$ and $\cF=\cT_Y(-\log C)$. The rows give two sections of $\cF/\cI^9\cF$, lying in $\cI\cF/\cI^9\cF$. Their determinant has leading term $t^4E_t\wedge\partial_z$, equivalently $t^5\partial_t\wedge\partial_z$, with coefficient one.

primaryStatements.label: prop:analytic-counterexample
primaryStatements.text: There is a normal complex surface germ $(X,x)$ with an isolated singular point and free analytic derivation sheaf of rank two: \[ \cT_X=\mathcal{H}om_{\OO_X}(\Omega_X^1,\OO_X) \simeq\OO_X^{\oplus2}. \] It has a resolution $\pi:Y\to X$ whose exceptional set is the smooth curve $C$ of genus $21$ and self-intersection $-10$.

primaryStatements.name: Algebraization of an isolated analytic germ
primaryStatements.label: prop:algebraization
primaryStatements.text: Let $(X,x)$ be a normal complex analytic germ of dimension $d\ge1$, smooth away from $x$, and suppose that its holomorphic tangent module is free of rank $d$. There exist a finitely generated normal integral $\CC$-algebra $A$ and a maximal ideal $\mathfrak p\subset A$ such that \[ \dim A=d,\qquad A/\mathfrak p=\CC,\qquad \widehat{A_{\mathfrak p}}\simeq\widehat{\OO_{X,x}},\qquad \Der_{\CC}(A)\simeq A^d. \] The affine variety $\Spec A$ can be chosen smooth away from $\mathfrak p$. If $x$ is singular, $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is nonregular.

primaryStatements.label: algebra:log-kodaira
primaryStatements.text: The smooth locus $U$ of the affine surface $X=\Spec A$ constructed in Theorem \ref{thm:main} has $\overline\kappa(U)=2$.

primaryStatements.label: algebra:derivation-blowups
primaryStatements.text: Starting with the singular surface $X=\Spec A$ of Theorem \ref{thm:main}, every iteration of blowing up at the derivation module is isomorphic to $X$. The same holds if each blowup is followed by normalization. Neither procedure resolves its singular point.

papers.title: A stable coordinate that is not a coordinate in four variables
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit degree-five polynomial over $\mathbf C$ that is not a coordinate in four variables but becomes one after adjoining a single variable. This gives a counterexample to the stable coordinate conjecture in four variables. Every fiber is isomorphic to affine three-space, yet its embedding in affine four-space is not rectifiable. Thus the example also disproves the Abhyankar–Sathaye embedding conjecture in ambient dimension four.

primaryStatements.label: cor:fibers

primaryStatements.label: prop:polynomial
primaryStatements.text: There are polynomial coordinates $p',s',F',J$ on $A$ such that \begin{equation} x=(s')^2-J^2+p'F',\qquad p=p'-2x\bigl(x(s'+J)+p'J\bigr). \end{equation} Thus, under the identification $(p',s',F',J)=(x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4)$, the element $p$ is the polynomial $f$ in Theorem \ref{thm:main}.

primaryStatements.label: prop:stable
primaryStatements.text: For an independent variable $w$, the ring $A[w]$ is a polynomial ring in five variables with $p$ as one of its coordinates.

primaryStatements.label: prop:fibers
primaryStatements.text: For every $\lambda\in k$, the quotient $A/(p-\lambda)$ is a polynomial ring in three variables over $k$.

primaryStatements.label: prop:graded
primaryStatements.text: The filtration on $A$ is exhaustive and separated. Its associated graded ring is the domain \begin{equation} G:=\gr A \simeq k[p,s,u,F,J]/(H_*), \qquad H_*=x^2F-(1+2sx)J-pJ^2, \quad x=s^2-u^2+pF, \end{equation} with the grading induced by \eqref{gr:weights}. primaryStatements.label: prop:coordinate-obstruction

primaryStatements.label: prop:lift

The formalization gives an explicit degree-five polynomial in four complex variables that becomes a coordinate after adjoining one variable but is not a coordinate in four variables. Every fiber is isomorphic to affine three-space, yet no fiber can be carried to a coordinate hyperplane by an ambient polynomial automorphism.

The Abhyankar–Sathaye conjecture predicts that a polynomial defining an affine-space quotient must be an ambient coordinate. For every $n\ge4$, the formalized counterexample gives $F\in\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ with quotient $\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(F)\cong\mathbb C[y_1,\ldots,y_{n-1}]$, although $F$ is not a coordinate.

A companion gives $n-1$ commuting, locally nilpotent derivations, linearly independent over the polynomial ring, whose common kernel is generated by the construction's explicit polynomial and contains no ambient coordinate. The extra $n-4$ derivations are ordinary partial derivatives in the added variables. The three-variable case is not covered.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: There is an algebraic vector bundle $G$ of rank two on $S$ such that, for every positive integer $m$, the bundle \[ E_m=f_m^*G\otimes P \] is ample. There is an integer $m_0$ such that $E_m$ admits no smooth Hermitian metric with strictly Griffiths-positive Chern curvature for every $m\ge m_0$.

primaryStatements.label: prop:construction
primaryStatements.text: These three isomorphisms glue to an algebraic isomorphism \begin{equation} \alpha:L_1^{-1}|_D\xrightarrow{\sim}L_2^{-1}|_D, \qquad \alpha|_{\Gamma_M}=M^{\otimes b}. \end{equation} Let $\beta=(\alpha^\vee)^{-1}:L_1|_D\to L_2|_D$ and define \begin{equation} G=\bigl\{(u_1,u_2)\in L_1\oplus L_2: u_2|_D=\beta(u_1|_D)\bigr\}. \end{equation} Then $G$ is an algebraic vector bundle of rank two. Both projections $\rho_i:G\to L_i$ are surjective, with exact sequences \begin{equation} 0\longrightarrow L_i(-D)\longrightarrow G \xrightarrow{\rho_j}L_j\longrightarrow0, \qquad \{i,j\}=\{1,2\}. \end{equation} For $F=G^\vee$, the dual inclusions $\iota_i=\rho_i^\vee:L_i^{-1}\hookrightarrow F$ span each fiber over $S\setminus D$ and satisfy \begin{equation} \iota_2\circ\alpha=\iota_1\qquad\text{on }D. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.label: prop:ampleness
primaryStatements.text: For every positive integer $m$, the bundle $E_m=f_m^*G\otimes P$ is ample. More precisely, $\OO_{\PP(E_m)}(n)$ is very ample for every even integer $n$ with $n-1\geq3m$.

primaryStatements.label: prop:limit
primaryStatements.text: Let $G$ be a holomorphic vector bundle of positive rank on $S=\PP^1\times\PP^1$, and put $F=G^\vee$. Suppose that $f_m^*G\otimes P$ admits a smooth strictly Griffiths-positive Hermitian metric for infinitely many positive integers $m$. Then there is a function \[ q:F\longrightarrow [0,\infty) \] which is plurisubharmonic on the total space, is not identically zero, and has the following property: for every $x\in S$ there is a finite positive semidefinite Hermitian form $H_x$ on $F_x$ such that \[ q(x,v)=H_x(v,v)\qquad(v\in F_x). \] In particular, this fiberwise assertion holds at every base point.

primaryStatements.label: prop:obstruction
primaryStatements.text: For the bundle $G$ of Proposition \ref{prop:construction}, every finite nonnegative plurisubharmonic function on the total space of $F=G^\vee$ whose restriction to each fiber is a Hermitian quadratic form is identically zero.

Griffiths' positivity conjecture predicts that every ample holomorphic vector bundle on a smooth complex projective variety admits a smooth Hermitian metric with strictly Griffiths-positive curvature. The formalized counterexample starts with a rank-two algebraic bundle $G$ on $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$. Its coordinatewise power pullbacks, tensored with $\mathcal O(1,1)$, are ample for every positive power but admit no such metric for all sufficiently large powers.

The separate very-ampleness result for all admissible even exponents is not included.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let $X$ be a compact connected K\"ahler manifold of positive complex dimension. If every holomorphic map $\C\to X$ is constant, then $K_X$ is ample. In particular, a positive tensor power of $K_X$ defines a holomorphic embedding of $X$ into a complex projective space.

primaryStatements.name: Existence of a maximizing disc
primaryStatements.label: ex:maximizer
primaryStatements.text: The functional in Equation \eqref{eq:disc-functional} has finite supremum, attained by a finite-area holomorphic disc centered at $x$.

primaryStatements.name: Boundary regularity of maximizing discs
primaryStatements.label: ex:regularity
primaryStatements.text: Every disc maximizing the functional in Equation \eqref{eq:disc-functional} extends continuously to $\overline\D$ and belongs to $W^{1,p}(\D,X)$ for every $2<p<4$. In particular, it has continuous $W^{1,3}$ regularity up to the boundary. More precisely, there is a constant $C_f$ such that \begin{equation} |f'(z)|_k\leq C_f(1-|z|)^{-1/2} \end{equation} for $z$ sufficiently close to $\partial\D$.

primaryStatements.name: Boundary-unitary frame
primaryStatements.label: var:frame
primaryStatements.text: Let $h$ be a smooth Hermitian metric on $X$. There exist a number $p_0$ with $2<p_0\le p$ and a holomorphic frame $B=(b_1,\ldots,b_n)$ of $f^*T^{1,0}X$ which is continuous, nonsingular, and $W^{1,p_0}$ on $\overline\D$, such that \begin{equation} B(z)^*h(f(z))B(z)=I, \qquad z\in\partial\D. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Centered holomorphic variations
primaryStatements.label: var:spray
primaryStatements.text: Let $B$ and $p_0>2$ be as in Proposition \ref{var:frame}, and set $x=f(0)$. For some $\eta>0$, there is a map \[ F\colon\{t\in\C^n:|t|<\eta\}\times\overline\D\longrightarrow X \] which is continuous on its domain and jointly holomorphic on $\{|t|<\eta\}\times\D$, and satisfies \begin{equation} F(0,z)=f(z),\qquad F(t,0)=x,\qquad \frac{\partial F}{\partial t_j}(0,z)=z b_j(z). \end{equation} In fixed local target coordinates covering the graph of $f$, the maps $t\mapsto F(t,\cdot)$ are holomorphic with values in $W^{1,p_0}$ on the corresponding source patches. In particular every $F(t,\cdot)$ is a finite-area holomorphic disc centered at $x$.

primaryStatements.name: Trace identities
primaryStatements.label: hes:trace
primaryStatements.text: For every smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form $q$, \begin{align} \cL d(F_t)&=\tr(B(0)^*k(x)B(0)),\\ \cL P_q(F_t)&=\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi} (\tr_h q)(f(e^{i\theta}))\,\dd\theta,\\ \cL A_h(F_t)&=n-A_{R_h}(f). \end{align} Here $F_t$ means the disc $z\mapsto F(t,z)$, not a parameter derivative.

primaryStatements.name: Maximizing inequality
primaryStatements.label: hes:maximum
primaryStatements.text: For a maximizer of $d+P_q-\delta A_h$ centered at $x$, the boundary-unitary frame satisfies \begin{equation} \tr(B(0)^*k(x)B(0)) +\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}(\tr_hq)(f(e^{i\theta}))\,\dd\theta \le\delta\bigl(n-A_{R_h}(f)\bigr). \end{equation} It also satisfies Equation \eqref{eq:determinant-identity}, and $A_q(f)\ge-d(f)$.

primaryStatements.name: Uniform Ricci-disc bound
primaryStatements.label: nef:disc-bound
primaryStatements.text: There is a constant $C\geq 0$, depending only on the fixed metric $k$, such that \begin{equation} P_{R_k}(f)\leq C \end{equation} for every finite-area holomorphic disc $f:\D\to X$.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let $X$ be a compact connected K\"ahler manifold of complex dimension $n\geq2$, and let \[ T_X=E_1\oplus E_2 \] be a specified decomposition into integrable holomorphic subbundles of positive ranks $r_1,r_2$. If $\pi:\widetilde X\to X$ is the ordinary universal covering map, there are connected simply connected complex manifolds $Y_1,Y_2$ and a biholomorphism $\Phi:\widetilde X\to Y_1\times Y_2$ such that \[ \dd\Phi(\pi^*E_i)=\pr_i^*T_{Y_i}\qquad(i=1,2), \] where $\dd\pi$ identifies $T_{\widetilde X}$ with $\pi^*T_X$. In particular, $\dim_\C Y_i=r_i$.

primaryStatements.name: Non-uniruled projective manifolds
primaryStatements.label: cor:non-uniruled
primaryStatements.text: Let $X$ be a smooth connected non-uniruled projective complex manifold, and let $T_X=E_1\oplus E_2$ be a specified holomorphic splitting into subbundles of positive ranks. Then both summands are integrable and the ordinary universal cover has a compatible product decomposition as in Theorem \ref{thm:main}.

primaryStatements.label: thm:nef-big
primaryStatements.text: Let $X$ be a smooth connected projective complex manifold of dimension $n\geq2$ with nef and big canonical bundle $K_X$. Every specified holomorphic splitting $T_X=E_1\oplus E_2$ into positive-rank subbundles is integrable and induces a compatible product decomposition of the ordinary universal cover as in Theorem \ref{thm:main}.

primaryStatements.name: Hartogs extension
primaryStatements.label: prop:hartogs
primaryStatements.text: Let $(s,t)$ be the standard coordinates of $\C^2$, and let $(w,v)$ be any invertible complex-affine coordinate system. For real numbers $0<e<a$ and $0<c<b$, put \[ H=\bigl\{|w|<e,\ |v|<b\bigr\} \ \cup\ \bigl\{|w|<a,\ c<|v|<b\bigr\}, \qquad Q=\bigl\{|w|<a,\ |v|<b\bigr\}. \] Every holomorphic map $f:H\to X$ satisfying \[ \dd f(\partial_s)\in E_1, \qquad \dd f(\partial_t)\in E_2 \] extends uniquely to a holomorphic map $Q\to X$ with the same tangencies. Thus the affine coordinates defining the Hartogs figure need not be the coordinates defining the box.

primaryStatements.name: Mixed-boundary extension
primaryStatements.label: prop:mixed
primaryStatements.text: Let $B\subset\C^2_{s,t}$ be a convex open set, and let $f:B\to X$ be a holomorphic box. Suppose that $p\in\partial B$ has a $C^2$ defining function with nonzero differential. If the complex tangent line to $\partial B$ at $p$ is generated by a vector with both components nonzero, then $f$ extends as a holomorphic box to a neighborhood of $p$, agreeing with $f$ on its intersection with $B$.

primaryStatements.name: Disk axes
primaryStatements.label: prop:disk-axes
primaryStatements.text: Let \(\alpha,\beta:\D\to X\) be holomorphic maps with \(\dd\alpha(T_\D)\subset E_1\), \(\dd\beta(T_\D)\subset E_2\), and \(\alpha(0)=\beta(0)\). There is a unique holomorphic box \(F:\D^2\to X\) such that \[ F(s,0)=\alpha(s),\qquad F(0,t)=\beta(t). \]

primaryStatements.name: Polydisk axes
primaryStatements.label: prop:polydisk-axes
primaryStatements.text: Let \(S\) and \(T\) be unit polydisks of positive dimensions. Suppose \(\alpha:S\to X\) and \(\beta:T\to X\) are holomorphic maps tangent to \(E_1\) and \(E_2\), respectively, and \(\alpha(p_0)=\beta(q_0)\) for some \((p_0,q_0)\in S\times T\). There is a unique holomorphic box \(F:S\times T\to X\) with \[ F(p,q_0)=\alpha(p),\qquad F(p_0,q)=\beta(q). \]

primaryStatements.name: Path rectangles
primaryStatements.label: prop:rectangles
primaryStatements.text: The following assertions hold. \begin{enumerate} \item If \(\alpha,\beta:[0,1]\to X\) locally follow \(E_1\)- and \(E_2\)-plaques, respectively, and \(\alpha(0)=\beta(0)\), there is a continuous box \(R:[0,1]^2\to X\) with \(R(s,0)=\alpha(s)\) and \(R(0,t)=\beta(t)\). \item Every continuous path \(\gamma:[0,1]\to X\) is the diagonal of a continuous box: \(R(s,s)=\gamma(s)\). \end{enumerate}

definitions.label: def:box
definitions.text: Let $U\subset\C^a\times\C^b$ be open, with parameter blocks $(s,t)$. A holomorphic map $f:U\to X$ is a holomorphic box if \[ \dd f(T\C^a\oplus0)\subset E_1,\qquad \dd f(0\oplus T\C^b)\subset E_2. \] The conditions are imposed at every point of $U$. They do not require $f$ to be an immersion.

definitions.label: rat:definition
definitions.text: Let $A,B$ be locally path connected spaces. A continuous map $R:A\times B\to M$ is a box if, near every parameter pair, there are a product neighborhood $A'\times B'$ and a product chart on its image in which \[ z\bigl(R(a,b)\bigr)=\bigl(r_1(a),r_2(b)\bigr). \] Thus first-parameter slices locally follow $\mathcal F_1$ plaques and second-parameter slices locally follow $\mathcal F_2$ plaques. In particular these slices are continuous into their leaves with the leaf topology. A rational tree is a connected nodal curve whose irreducible components are copies of $\Pp^1$ and whose dual graph is a finite tree.

definitions.label: cross:attained
definitions.text: A germ over \((a,b)\in Q\) is attained if it is the crossing germ of Lemma \ref{rat:germs} associated to a rational-tree box \(R_u\) of Proposition \ref{rat:boxes}, at two distinct smooth marked points \(s,t\) of its parameter tree, with \(u(s)=a\) and \(u(t)=b\).

lean.scopeText:
The splitting question asks whether a holomorphic decomposition of the tangent bundle comes from a product decomposition of the universal cover. The formalized result gives an affirmative answer for a compact connected Kähler manifold whose tangent bundle splits into two positive-rank, integrable holomorphic subbundles. The universal cover is a product of connected simply connected complex manifolds of the prescribed dimensions, and the differential identifies the two tangent factors with the original summands.

Both integrability assumptions are required. Automatic integrability and the paper's additional corollaries are not included.

The formalization proves integrability of both summands in a holomorphic splitting of the tangent bundle of a rationally connected projective manifold. More precisely, for a compact connected complex manifold of dimension at least two with a projective embedding witnessing rational connectedness, each positive-rank summand of a holomorphic tangent-bundle splitting is integrable. The paper's compatible product decomposition is a separate consequence, outside this selected statement.

primaryStatements.name: Automatic integrability
primaryStatements.text: \label[theorem]{thm:main} Let \(X\) be a smooth connected projective complex manifold of dimension at least two. Suppose that two general points of \(X\) lie on the image of a morphism \(\PP^1\to X\). For every specified holomorphic decomposition \[ T_X=E_1\oplus E_2 \] into subbundles of positive rank, both \(E_1\) and \(E_2\) are integrable.

primaryStatements.name: Compatible product
primaryStatements.text: \label[corollary]{cor:product} Under the hypotheses of \cref{thm:main}, there are smooth projective manifolds \(X_1,X_2\) and an isomorphism \(X\simeq X_1\times X_2\) under which \[ E_i=\pr_i^*T_{X_i}\qquad (i=1,2). \]

primaryStatements.name: Tangent box
primaryStatements.label: eq:box
primaryStatements.text: \label[proposition]{prop:box} Every holomorphic map \(g:C\to X\) admits a holomorphic map \(F:S\to X\) such that \begin{equation} F|_\Delta=g,\qquad dF(T^{(1)})\subset F^*E_1,\qquad dF(T^{(2)})\subset F^*E_2. \end{equation} Neither summand is assumed integrable.

primaryStatements.label: eq:transport
primaryStatements.text: \label[proposition]{prop:transport} Let \(F:S\to X\) be a tangent box of \(g:C\to X\). Transport along the fibers of \(\pr_i\) gives holomorphic bundle isomorphisms \begin{equation} \Theta_i:\pr_i^*(g^*E_i)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }F^*E_i, \qquad i=1,2, \end{equation} whose restrictions to the diagonal are the identity.

\label[corollary]{cor:rational-quotient} Let \(X\) be a connected uniruled compact K\"ahler manifold with a holomorphic splitting \(T_X=V_1\oplus V_2\). Let \(Z\) be a general fiber of its rationally connected quotient and set \(W_i=T_Z\cap V_i|_Z\). For each \(i=1,2\), there is an almost-holomorphic fibration \(\phi_i:X\dashrightarrow Y_i\) whose general fiber \(F_i\) is rationally connected and, for compatible choices \(F_i\subset Z\), satisfies \[ T_{F_i}=W_i|_{F_i}\subset V_i|_{F_i}. \] If \(W_i=0\), one may take \(\phi_i=\id_X\), with point fibers. If \(\rk V_1=2\), exactly one of the following holds: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item \(W_1=V_1|_Z\), and \(X\) admits an analytic fiber bundle \(X\to Y\) with rationally connected general fiber and \(T_{X/Y}=V_1\). \item \(W_1\) is a line bundle, and there is an equidimensional holomorphic map \(X\to Y\) whose general fiber \(F\) is a rational curve with \(T_F\subset V_1|_F\). \item \(W_1=0\), equivalently \(T_Z\subset V_2|_Z\). \end{enumerate}
