primaryStatements.name: Feasible-simplex identity
primaryStatements.label: prop:simplex-integral
primaryStatements.text: Let $b_1,\ldots,b_m$ be nonzero, pairwise nonproportional real rows spanning $(\R^d)^*$, and let $F,D,\lambda$ be as in Lemma \ref{lem:planar-lens}. With $A$, $S$, and $\Sigma_X$ defined in \eqref{eq:strip-body}, \eqref{eq:feasible-probabilities}, and \eqref{eq:feasible-simplex-union}, respectively, \begin{equation} 1\leq S =\frac{d!}{4^d}\int_A|\Sigma_X|\,dX \leq\frac{d!}{4^d}|A|\,|A^\circ|. \end{equation} In particular, $|A|\,|A^\circ|\geq4^d/d!$, and \begin{equation} 0\leq\int_A\bigl(|A^\circ|-|\Sigma_X|\bigr)\,dX \leq |A|\,|A^\circ|-\frac{4^d}{d!}. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: The symmetric volume-product inequality
primaryStatements.label: cor:symmetric-inequality
primaryStatements.text: For every origin-symmetric convex body $K\subset\R^d$, $d\geq1$, \[ |K|\,|K^\circ|\geq\frac{4^d}{d!}. \]

primaryStatements.name: A representation minimizing the lens cost
primaryStatements.label: prop:optimal-representation
primaryStatements.text: Let $K\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge1$, be an origin-symmetric convex body with $P(K)=4^n/n!$. Put $Q=K^\circ$, $d=n+1$, and define the lifted bodies $B,C$ by \eqref{eq:segment-lift}. For every $X\in\operatorname{int}B$ and every nonzero $\xi=(q,a)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R$, put \[ T=p_C(\xi)=\max\{p_Q(q),|a|\}. \] There are $1\le r\le d$ vectors $c_i=(b_i,\sigma_i)$ with $b_i\in Q$ and $\sigma_i\in\{-1,1\}$, nonnegative numbers $\alpha_i$, and a vector $Y\in\mathbb R^d$, such that \begin{equation} \xi=\sum_{i=1}^r\alpha_i c_i, \qquad \sum_{i=1}^r\alpha_i=T, \end{equation} and \begin{equation} |h\cdot Y|\le\lambda(h\cdot X)\quad(h\in C), \qquad c_i\cdot Y=\lambda(c_i\cdot X)\quad(1\le i\le r). \end{equation} In particular, for every finite representation $\xi=\sum_{j=1}^s\beta_jh_j$ with $\beta_j\ge0$ and $h_j\in C$, \begin{equation} \sum_{i=1}^r\alpha_i\lambda(c_i\cdot X) \le \sum_{j=1}^s\beta_j\lambda(h_j\cdot X). \end{equation} The choices may depend on $X$ and $\xi$; the same choice satisfies \eqref{eq:optimal-cost} for all the competing representations.

primaryStatements.name: Medians of an equality body
primaryStatements.label: prop:metric-median
primaryStatements.text: Let $K\subset\R^n$, $n\ge1$, be an origin-symmetric convex body with $P(K)=4^n/n!$, and put $Q=K^\circ$. Every triple of points in $(\R^n,p_Q)$ has a metric median.

primaryStatements.name: Hansen--Lima
primaryStatements.label: thm:hansen-lima
primaryStatements.text: A nonzero finite-dimensional real Banach space with the 3.2 intersection property is linearly isometric to a space obtained from the real line by finitely many $\ell_1$ and $\ell_\infty$ direct sums.

lean.scopeText:
The symmetric Mahler conjecture predicts $|K||K^\circ|\ge4^n/n!$ for every origin-symmetric convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$. The formalization establishes this for every $n\ge1$ and characterizes equality exactly by invertible linear images of Hanner bodies, built from intervals using Cartesian products and convex-hull joins.

The nonsymmetric Mahler conjecture and the functional inequalities are not included.

The general Mahler conjecture gives a sharp lower bound for the volume product of a convex body and its polar. For every $n\ge1$ and compact convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$ with nonempty interior, the formalization proves
$\inf_{z\in\mathrm{int}\,K}|K|\,|(K-z)^\circ|\ge (n+1)^{n+1}/(n!)^2$.
Equality holds exactly when $K$ is a simplex. The paper's functional inequality is outside this selected statement.

For an origin-symmetric convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, the formalized result determines the symplectic ball capacity of $\mathrm{int}\,K\times\mathrm{int}\,K^\circ$: its Gromov width is $4$, and every ball of capacity $0<c<4$ embeds symplectically into it. The normalization assigns capacity $\pi r^2$ to a ball of radius $r$.

No boundary smoothness or strict convexity is assumed. An embedding at capacity exactly $4$ is not asserted.

primaryStatements.name: A ball from a holomorphic zero
primaryStatements.label: thm:holomorphic-ball
primaryStatements.text: Let $n,m\ge1$, let $\Omega\subset\C^n$ be an open set containing $0$, and let $f=(f_1,\ldots,f_m):\Omega\to\C^m$ be holomorphic. Suppose that, for some integer $k\ge1$, \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item $f^{-1}(0)=\{0\}$ and $|f(z)|=O(|z|^k)$ as $z\to0$; \item for every $0<s<1$, the set $\{z\in\Omega:|f(z)|^2\le s\}$ is a compact subset of $\Omega$. \end{enumerate} Set \[ \tau=|f|^2,\qquad V=\{z\in\Omega:\tau(z)<1\}, \qquad \omega=\ddc(|z|^2+\tau). \] For every $0<c<\pi k$, there is a smooth symplectic embedding \[ \bigl(B^{2n}(c),\omega_0\bigr)\longrightarrow(V,\omega). \]

papers.title: Petty’s projection-volume conjecture in dimensions at least four
papers.abstract: We prove that ellipsoids uniquely minimize the volume of the projection body among convex bodies of fixed volume in every dimension at least four. This proves Petty's projection-volume conjecture in these dimensions.
papers.familySummary: Proves Petty's projection-volume conjecture in the remaining dimensions n ≥ 4: ellipsoids uniquely minimize projection-body volume at fixed body volume. Also establishes the full Lutwak–Petty projection inequalities. In contrast, products of simplices exceed Brannen's proposed simplex maximum for normalized projection-body volume by an exponential factor in every sufficiently large dimension.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: For every integer $n\ge4$ and every convex body $K\subset\R^n$, \begin{equation} \frac{|\Pi K|}{|K|^{n-1}} \ge \kappa_{n-1}^{\,n}\kappa_n^{\,2-n}. \end{equation} Equality holds if and only if $K=a+TB_2^n$ for some $a\in\R^n$ and some invertible linear map $T$.

primaryStatements.name: Brunn--Minkowski inequality
primaryStatements.label: thm:brunn-minkowski
primaryStatements.text: For every integer $d\ge1$ and convex bodies $A,B\subset\R^d$, write $|\cdot|$ for $d$-dimensional volume. For $0\le t\le1$, \begin{equation} |(1-t)A+tB|^{1/d} \ge (1-t)|A|^{1/d}+t|B|^{1/d}. \end{equation} If $0<t<1$, equality holds if and only if $B=a+cA$ for some $a\in\R^d$ and $c>0$.

primaryStatements.name: First variation of volume
primaryStatements.label: cor:volume-first-variation
primaryStatements.text: Let $K,M\subset\R^n$ be convex bodies, with the origin interior to $K$. Then \begin{align} \left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{0+}|K+tM| &=n\kappa_n\E\!\left[g_K(u)^{-n} h_M\bigl(\nabla g_K(u)\bigr)\right] \\ &\ge n|K|^{(n-1)/n}|M|^{1/n}.\nonumber \end{align} Equality in the inequality holds if and only if $K$ and $M$ are homothetic up to translation. The derivative identity remains valid when $M$ is an arbitrary nonempty compact convex set.

primaryStatements.name: Projection measure
primaryStatements.label: prop:projection-measure
primaryStatements.text: Translate and dilate a convex body $K$ so that $0\in\operatorname{int}K$ and $|K|=\kappa_n$. Define $\eta_K$ by \begin{equation} \int \psi(x)\,d\eta_K(x) =\E\!\left[g_K(u)^{-n}\psi\bigl(\nabla g_K(u)\bigr)\right] \end{equation} for nonnegative Borel functions $\psi$; the choice of the gradient on its null exceptional set is immaterial. Then $\eta_K$ is an admissible probability measure of bounded support. Equality in \eqref{eq:functional-condition} for $\eta_K$ and a symmetric body $M$ holds if and only if $K$ is a translate of a positive dilate of $M$. Moreover, \begin{equation} h_{\Pi K}(y)=\frac{n\kappa_n}{2} \int |x\cdot y|\,d\eta_K(x) \qquad(y\in\R^n), \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \int h_K(x)\,d\eta_K(x)=1. \end{equation} For the unit ball, $\eta_{B_2^n}=\sigma$, and consequently \begin{equation} \frac{n\kappa_n b_n}{2}=\kappa_{n-1}. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.label: prop:sign-estimate
thm:norm-estimate
primaryStatements.text: Let $g$ be a norm on $\R^n$, where $n\ge4$, normalized by $\E g^{-n}=1$ on $\Sph$. Then \begin{equation} c_{n,k}\|Q(g^k)\|_2^2 \le (\E g^k)^2-(\E g^{k-1})^2. \end{equation} The inequality is strict unless $g=1$ on $\Sph$.

primaryStatements.name: Variational representation
primaryStatements.label: prop:representation
primaryStatements.text: Suppose $A$ is positive definite, and let $L$ be any positive dilate of $L_A$, with gauge $g=g_L$. For every continuous even function $\phi:\R^n\to\R$ that is positively homogeneous of degree one, \begin{equation} \int\phi(Ax)\,d\eta(x) =s\,\E\phi\bigl(X_{g^k}(u)\bigr), \qquad s=\frac{\tau_A(L)}{\E g^{k-1}}. \end{equation} Here, almost everywhere on the sphere, \begin{equation} X_{g^k}=g^ku+g^{k-1}\gradS g=g^{k-1}\nabla g. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Affine position
primaryStatements.label: prop:position
primaryStatements.text: There is a symmetric positive definite matrix $A$ with $\det A=1$ such that $g_A^k$ has zero component in $\mathcal H_2$.

definitions.label: def:admissible-measure
definitions.text: We call $\eta$ admissible if its support spans $\R^n$ and \begin{equation} \tau_\eta(M)\ge\left(\frac{|M|}{\kappa_n}\right)^{1/n} \quad\text{for every origin-symmetric convex body }M\subset\R^n. \end{equation} The measure itself is not required to be symmetric.

lean.scopeText:
Petty's projection-volume conjecture predicts

$\displaystyle \frac{|\Pi K|}{|K|^{n-1}}\ge \kappa_{n-1}^{n}\kappa_n^{2-n},$

with equality exactly for ellipsoids; here $\kappa_j$ is the volume of the Euclidean unit ball in dimension $j$. The formalization establishes this for every convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$ and every $n\ge4$.

Other inequalities in the projection-body family are not included.

Brannen's simplex-maximization conjecture predicts that a simplex maximizes normalized projection-body volume $|\Pi K|/|K|^{n-1}$ in dimension $n$. The formalized counterexample is the product of two ten-dimensional simplices. Its normalized projection volume, divided by that of a twenty-dimensional simplex, is

$\displaystyle \frac{22{,}355{,}476}{22{,}020{,}096}>1.$

Thus the proposed maximum fails in dimension $20$. The paper's exponential-factor result for every sufficiently large dimension is not included.

primaryStatements.label: thm:counterexample
primaryStatements.text: Let \(T_{10}=\conv(0,e_1,\ldots,e_{10})\subset\R^{10}\), where the \(e_i\) are the coordinate unit vectors, and let \(K=T_{10}\times T_{10}\subset\R^{20}\). Then \[ \frac{R_{20}(K)}{c_{20}} =\frac{121\binom{20}{10}}{21\cdot2^{20}} =\frac{22\,355\,476}{22\,020\,096}>1. \] Thus \(K\) violates \eqref{eq:proposed-bound} in dimension twenty.

primaryStatements.label: prop:product
primaryStatements.text: Let \(A\subset\R^r\) and \(B\subset\R^s\) be full-dimensional convex polytopes, where \(r,s\ge2\). In the orthogonal product space \(\R^{r+s}=\R^r\times\R^s\), \begin{equation} \Pi(A\times B)=(|B|\Pi A)\times(|A|\Pi B). \end{equation} In particular, \begin{equation} R_{r+s}(A\times B)=R_r(A)R_s(B). \end{equation}

primaryStatements.label: prop:simplex
primaryStatements.text: For \(d\ge2\), the standard simplex \(T_d=\conv(0,e_1,\ldots,e_d)\subset\R^d\) satisfies \[ |T_d|=\frac1{d!},\qquad |\Pi T_d|=\frac{d+1}{((d-1)!)^d},\qquad R_d(T_d)=c_d. \] Every full-dimensional \(d\)-simplex has the same value \(c_d\).

primaryStatements.label: cor:exponential-excess
primaryStatements.text: There exist a constant \(\lambda>1\) and an integer \(N\ge20\) such that, for every integer \(n\ge N\), some full-dimensional convex polytope \(K_n\subset\R^n\) satisfies \[ \frac{R_n(K_n)}{R_n(T_n)}\ge\lambda^n. \] The polytopes \(K_n\) may be chosen as Cartesian products of simplices.

papers.title: Planar Graph Metrics Embed into L1 with Constant Distortion
papers.abstract: We prove that every finite connected planar graph with arbitrary positive real edge lengths embeds into real L1 with a universal distortion bound. This resolves the planar embedding conjecture positively.
papers.familySummary: Resolves the planar and bounded-treewidth cases of the Gupta–Newman–Rabinovich–Sinclair conjecture. Shortest-path metrics of finite connected graphs with arbitrary positive edge lengths embed into real L1 with universal distortion for planar graphs, and distortion depending only on treewidth for bounded-treewidth graphs. The corresponding multicommodity flow–cut gaps are uniformly bounded.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: There is a finite universal constant $C\ge1$ with the following property. For every finite connected planar graph $G=(V,E)$ with strictly positive real edge lengths, there exist a measure space $(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mu)$ and a map $f:V\to L_1(\Omega,\mathcal F,\mu;\R)$ such that \[ d_G(x,y)\le\|f(x)-f(y)\|_1\le C d_G(x,y) \qquad(x,y\in V). \]

primaryStatements.name: Separation supplied by the main test
primaryStatements.label: main:pair-separation
primaryStatements.text: Let $(x,y)$ be an eligible pair satisfying the interior requirements, $1\le d(x,y)\le2$, and $|s(x)-s(y)|\le E_A$. If either endpoint has no descending path, then, conditional on main-update mode, the independent cell coins give probability at least $1/4$ of system-A symmetric-difference separation at least $\kappa_A E_A$ at this step.

primaryStatements.name: Planar graphs admit column models
primaryStatements.label: geo:realization
primaryStatements.text: Every finite connected planar graph with positive edge lengths has an isometric realization of its geometric edge metric in a noncrossing column model satisfying the terminal-switch condition. The added parts of the model consist of separate infinite tails and do not shorten distances in the original graph.

primaryStatements.name: Thin-band interpolation
primaryStatements.label: int:interpolation
primaryStatements.text: Let $0<\zeta<1$, let $E>0$, and set \begin{equation} \begin{gathered} \delta=E/8,\qquad a_0=10^{-6}\zeta\delta,\qquad q=\zeta\delta/20,\\ \rho_0=\zeta\delta/1000,\qquad M=\lceil15/\zeta\rceil+3,\qquad N=6(M+1). \end{gathered} \end{equation} Suppose $0<a\le a_0$, and let $p:Y\to\R$ be $(1-\zeta)$-Lipschitz for $d_J$. There is a random function $Q:Y\to\R$, obtained using finitely many independent scalar noises uniform on $[q,2q]$, with the following properties. \begin{enumerate} \item For every realization, $Q$ respects all switches, is $1$-Lipschitz for $d_J$, and satisfies $|Q(v)-p(v)|\le6\delta<E$. \item Its pieces use finitely many named atoms of the form \begin{equation} A(v)=C+\varepsilon d_J(k,v),\qquad \varepsilon\in\{-1,1\},\quad k\in Y. \end{equation} Each name specifies a source $k$ and sign $\varepsilon$ fixed before the noises are sampled; the intercept $C$ is random. Whenever the construction reuses an atom, it retains its name. \item For a fixed $x\in Y$ and $0<\rho\le\rho_0$, there is a list $\mathcal A(x,\rho)$ of at most $N$ atom names and sources, determined without the noises, that contains the name of every atom selected by $Q$ on $B_{d_J}(x,\rho)$. Except on an event of probability at most \begin{equation} \frac{N^2}{q}(8\rho+\eta), \end{equation} one named atom is selected throughout this ball. \end{enumerate} Here $\eta=0$ for continuous uniform noises. Alternatively, each noise may be uniform on an equally spaced grid including both endpoints of $[q,2q]$, and $\eta$ in \eqref{int:probability} may be the largest grid spacing. The same conclusions hold for any set of points reached from $x$ by band paths of length at most $\rho$, including the points and representatives encountered on those paths.

primaryStatements.name: Comparison with other branches
primaryStatements.label: int:comparisons
primaryStatements.text: Condition on arbitrary prior data. Let $W$ be the union of a nonempty family of band paths issuing from a fixed point $x$, each of length at most $\rho$. The set $W$ and these paths are fixed by the prior data. Suppose that $Q_1,\ldots,Q_s$ are interpolation constructions, each on a band component containing all these paths. Their geometries, inputs, and portals are fixed by the prior data, and their fresh noise families are mutually independent. The bands and their intrinsic metrics may differ; each of the specified paths must be permitted in every band. Denote the constants of $Q_i$ in \eqref{int:constants} by $q_i,N_i,\rho_{0,i}$. Allow inputs $c_i+\varepsilon_iQ_i$, with $\varepsilon_i\in\{-1,1\}$ and $c_i$ fixed by the prior data. Also allow one fixed branch $f$ and $t$ branches $g_j+\beta_j$, where $f$ and the $g_j$ are fixed functions whose restrictions to each specified path, parametrized by arclength, are $L$-Lipschitz. The $\beta_j$ are fresh independent uniform noises on intervals of length $w_j>0$, independent also of the interpolation noises. All functions respect the switches used by the paths. Set \[ L_* =\max(1,L),\qquad S=1+t+\sum_{i=1}^sN_i,\qquad q_* =\min\bigl(\{q_i:1\le i\le s\}\cup \{w_j:1\le j\le t\}\bigr). \] Assume that there is at least one randomized input and that $\rho\le\min_i\rho_{0,i}$ when $s>0$. Any fixed expression formed from these inputs by finitely many minima and maxima selects one branch and, for a selected interpolation, one atom throughout $W$, except with conditional probability at most \begin{equation} \frac{S^2}{q_*}(8L_*\rho+\eta). \end{equation} Continuous noises have $\eta=0$; for equally spaced endpoint grids $\eta$ can be the largest spacing of any noise used here. The expression uses each interpolation with a single chosen sign and shift; repeated appearances of that same input are given the same name.

primaryStatements.name: Restricted packing bound
primaryStatements.label: pack:bound
primaryStatements.text: Fix a narrow band $J_2$. In any component of $X_{J_2}$, every closed $d_{J_2}$-ball of radius $4R$ meets seeds from at most \begin{equation} M_{\mathrm{pack}}=2+\left\lceil1600R/g\right\rceil \end{equation} groups. This bound is independent of the graph, the number of columns, and the history of the construction.

primaryStatements.name: Movement and success
primaryStatements.label: pad:success
primaryStatements.text: There are constants $M<\infty$ and $b,p>0$ such that the following hold at every step of scale $r$. \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item At every point of $X$, in either system, the symmetric-difference movement of the unrefined set is at most $Mr$. \item Given any past for which a vertex pair at distance in $[r,2r)$ is eligible, the step has probability at least $p$ of producing one of these certificates: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)] \item unrefined symmetric-difference separation at least $br$ in one system; \item a non-neighbor tip $e$ and a set of labels of measure at least $br$ in system $A$ on which both pair vertices are active and $e$ is inactive, with the vertices strictly on opposite sides of that link. \end{enumerate} \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.name: Chart persistence
primaryStatements.label: pad:persistence
primaryStatements.text: There exist constants $C_0<\infty$ and $\rho_0>0$ such that the following holds. Condition on the past at a step of scale $r$. Suppose a fixed closed ball $B_d(v,\rho r)$ lies in a single old region in each system. For $0<\rho\le\rho_0$, the probability that this ball is split between different new regions in either system is at most \begin{equation} C_0(\rho+\eta_0). \end{equation} Here $\eta_0$ is the relative mesh allowance from Section \ref{sets:setup}.

definitions.label: geo:column-model
definitions.text: A column model consists of a finite cyclically ordered set $V_0$ of indices, a copy $\{i\}\times\R$ of the height line for each $i\in V_0$, and a finite collection of links. A link $ij$ has a prescribed closed bounded set $S_{ij}\subset\R$ of switch heights. At $H\in S_{ij}$ we identify $(i,H)$ with $(j,H)$. The resulting quotient is denoted by $X$, and its height function by $h$. Paths consist of finitely many vertical segments and permitted switches; their length is the sum of the lengths of the vertical segments. The distance $d$ is the infimum of these lengths. The links are noncrossing if no two have four distinct endpoints alternating in the cyclic order. We require all column models below to have noncrossing links. We additionally require that every link between nonconsecutive indices is a switch at a single height $H_e$, and that neither endpoint column has any switch above $H_e$. Such a switch will be called a terminal switch. Its quotient point is called the tip of the link. For a closed interval $I\subset\R$, possibly unbounded, write $X_I=h^{-1}(I)$. The intrinsic distance $d_I$ only permits paths with heights in $I$; different components have distance $+\infty$. The active column graph $G_I$ has vertex set $V_0$ and the links whose switch sets meet $I$ as edges.

definitions.name: Radial cells
definitions.label: geo:cell-definition
definitions.text: Fix $D>0$ and an offset $\theta\in[0,D)$. Partition the indices into layers by assigning $i$ to the unique half-open interval \[ [\theta+nD,\theta+(n+1)D),\qquad n\in\mathbb Z, \] containing $b_i$. Split each layer into the connected components of its induced subgraph of $G_J$. A cell is the image in $X_J$ of all intervals $\{i\}\times J$ belonging to one such component. Its frontier $\partial C$ is the union of their images for indices adjacent in $G_J$ to an index outside the cell.

definitions.name: Descending path
definitions.label: main:ray-definition
definitions.text: A descending path at a point $w$ is a shortest path in $J_1$, of length $d_0\in[10^{-5},0.02]$, whose terminal point $z$ satisfies \begin{equation} s(z)\le s(w)-d_0+\epsilon. \end{equation} It is parametrized by arclength $t\in[0,d_0]$. All descending paths used below lie in the old ordinary chart band, so $s$ can be evaluated at every point of the path.

definitions.label: ord:definition
definitions.text: Let $a,b$ be two distinct column indices. A real field $s$ on $X_I$ is ordered from $a$ to $b$, with slope bound $M$, if it respects every switch, is $M$-Lipschitz on every vertical column, and, at each height $H\in I$, is nondecreasing on each of the two circular arcs oriented from $a$ to $b$. In particular, the value on column $a$ is a global minimum at that height, and the value on column $b$ is a global maximum. We call the two open arcs the positive and negative arcs, with either assignment of these names.

definitions.label: ord:transverse-definition
definitions.text: Let $s$ be ordered from $a$ to $b$ with slope bound $4$. In $\R^2$ define the set \[ \begin{split} Z_s={}&\{(s(a,H),H),(s(b,H),H):H\in I\}\\ &{}\cup\{(s(p,H),H): H\in I\cap S_{pq},\ p\text{ and }q\text{ lie on opposite open arcs}\}. \end{split} \] For a representative $(i,H)$ define \[ t_s(i,H)= \begin{cases} \dist_\infty((s(i,H),H),Z_s),&i\text{ on the positive arc},\\ -\dist_\infty((s(i,H),H),Z_s),&i\text{ on the negative arc},\\ 0,&i\in\{a,b\}. \end{cases} \] Here $\dist_\infty$ is distance for the maximum norm on $\R^2$.

lean.scopeText:
The planar case of the Gupta–Newman–Rabinovich–Sinclair embedding problem asks for a universal distortion bound in $L_1$. The formalized result gives one constant $C$ for every finite connected planar graph with arbitrary positive real edge lengths: its weighted shortest-path metric embeds into real $L_1$ with distortion at most $C$. The constant is independent of the number of vertices and the ratios between edge lengths; singleton graphs are included.

The formalized result gives a uniform $L_1$ embedding bound for each bounded-treewidth class. For every bag-size bound $k\ge2$, there is a constant $C(k)$ such that the weighted shortest-path metric of every nonempty finite connected graph with a tree decomposition of bag size at most $k$ embeds into finite-dimensional real $L_1$ with distortion at most $C(k)$. Edge lengths may be arbitrary positive real numbers, and the constant is independent of the graph and decomposition size.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: For every integer $k\ge2$ there is a finite constant $C_k\ge1$ with the following property. If a finite connected graph $G=(V,E)$ admits a tree decomposition with bags of size at most $k$, then, for every edge-length function $\ell:E\to(0,\infty)$, there is a map $F$ from $V$ into a real $L_1$ space such that \begin{equation} d_{G,\ell}(u,v) \le \|F(u)-F(v)\|_1 \le C_k\,d_{G,\ell}(u,v) \qquad(u,v\in V). \end{equation} The constant is independent of the number of vertices, the depth of the decomposition, and all ratios of edge lengths.

primaryStatements.name: Symmetric Markov flow bound { \cite[Theorem 4.4
primaryStatements.label: thm:markov-flow
primaryStatements.text: {CKR}}] For every integer $w\geq2$ there is a finite constant $C(w)\geq1$ with the following property. Suppose a symmetric Markov flow graph has at most $w$ states per layer, first layer $\{s_0,s_1\}$, and last layer $\{t_0,t_1\}$, and its involutions interchange the two states in each endpoint layer. Every capacity-respecting flow from $s_0$ to $t_1$ has value at most \[ C(w)\Pr[X_0=s_0,\ X_r=t_1]. \] The constant is independent of the number of layers and of all transition probabilities.

primaryStatements.name: Transport of uncertainty
primaryStatements.label: prop:uncertainty
primaryStatements.text:
Let $\mu$ be a consistent family of symmetric bag measures, with bags of size at most $k$. Consider the path $B_0,\ldots,B_r$ from a bag containing $y$ to a bag containing $z$, and let $P=B_j$ lie on this path. Suppose a labeled cut measure $
u$ on $V$ satisfies \[ 
u|_{B_i}\leq\mu_{B_i}\qquad(j\leq i\leq r). \] Then the Markov-glued pseudometric satisfies  egin{equation} D_\mu(y,z)\geq b_k E_
u(z\mid P). \end{equation} The measure $
u$ need not be symmetric.

primaryStatements.name: Realization by particles
primaryStatements.label: prop:particle-realization
primaryStatements.text: Suppose a finite schedule requires at most $q$ simultaneous reserved pairs in each memory copy, including any temporary reservation made before another is released. Updates may be made at the current bag, or on a child-specific copy at its parent bag before moving to the child. Before processing the root, updates at the empty interface are also allowed. Every update uses a perturbation satisfying the bounds above and vanishing on its interface. Choose \[ N=2q+k!+2, \qquad M=\bigl(B(N-1)+2\bigr)\Delta. \] Then all requested updates and reservations can be carried out. They produce symmetric bag measures $\mu_t$ with the following properties. \begin{enumerate} \item Each $\mu_t$ has the same total mass $m=2NM$, and neighboring bag measures have equal traces on their intersection. \item Every particle height is at distance at least $2\Delta$ from each endpoint of the sweep interval $[-M,M]$. \item The pseudometric $D_\mu$ obtained by Markov gluing satisfies \[ D_\mu(u,v)\le U\,d(u,v) \quad\text{for all }u,v\in V, \qquad U=NL(N-1). \] \item If a pair is reserved from a launch bag through a later bag on a descending path, its fixed symmetric two-particle cut measure has trace dominated by $\mu_t$ at every bag on that segment. The segment includes the launch and release bags, even when the particles are reused at the release bag. A reservation launched at the empty interface has the same property from the root onward. \end{enumerate} The statements hold for each realization of any auxiliary randomness. For measurable randomized choices, taking expectations also gives an $L_1$ pseudometric with the same upper bound.

primaryStatements.name: Padded partitions
primaryStatements.label: thm:padded
primaryStatements.text: There are constants $\alpha\in(0,1/8]$ and $\pi\in(0,1]$ such that, for every metric as above and every $r>0$, there is a random partition $\mathcal P$ of $V$ satisfying \[ \operatorname{diam}(C)\leq r\quad(C\in\mathcal P), \qquad \mathbb P\bigl[B_d(x,\alpha r)\subseteq\mathcal P(x)\bigr]\geq\pi \quad(x\in V). \] Here $\mathcal P(x)$ denotes the part containing $x$.

primaryStatements.name: The co-bag embedding
primaryStatements.label: prop:cobag
primaryStatements.text: For every rooted tree decomposition with nonempty bags of size at most $k$, there is an $L_1$ pseudometric $D_{\mathrm{bag}}$ on $V$ and constants $U_{\mathrm{bag}}<\infty$ and $a_{\mathrm{bag}}>0$, depending only on $k$, such that \[ D_{\mathrm{bag}}(u,v)\leq U_{\mathrm{bag}}d(u,v) \quad(u,v\in V), \] and \[ D_{\mathrm{bag}}(u,v)\geq a_{\mathrm{bag}}d(u,v) \quad\text{whenever $u,v$ belong to a common bag}. \] One may take \[ R=4\binom{k}{2},\qquad N=2R+k!+2,\qquad U_{\mathrm{bag}}=3N(N-1),\qquad a_{\mathrm{bag}}=\frac{\pi\alpha}{64}. \]

primaryStatements.name: Uniform lower comparison
primaryStatements.label: prop:combined-lower
primaryStatements.text: For each fixed $k\geq2$ there is a constant $\lambda_k>0$ such that, for every admissible weighted graph with a tree decomposition of bag size at most $k$ and every pair of vertices $u,v$, \begin{equation} D_{\mathrm{bag}}(u,v)+D_{\mathrm{anc}}(u,v) \geq\lambda_k d(u,v). \end{equation}

lean.scopeText:
The planar case of the Gupta–Newman–Rabinovich–Sinclair embedding problem asks for a universal distortion bound in $L_1$. The formalized result gives one constant $C$ for every finite connected planar graph with arbitrary positive real edge lengths: its weighted shortest-path metric embeds into real $L_1$ with distortion at most $C$. The constant is independent of the number of vertices and the ratios between edge lengths; singleton graphs are included.

The formalized result gives a uniform $L_1$ embedding bound for each bounded-treewidth class. For every bag-size bound $k\ge2$, there is a constant $C(k)$ such that the weighted shortest-path metric of every nonempty finite connected graph with a tree decomposition of bag size at most $k$ embeds into finite-dimensional real $L_1$ with distortion at most $C(k)$. Edge lengths may be arbitrary positive real numbers, and the constant is independent of the graph and decomposition size.

primaryStatements.label: thm:universal
primaryStatements.text: For every smooth nonnegative completely monotone function $g$ on $(0,\infty)$ and every locally finite planar set $\mathcal C$ of centered disk density one, \[ E_g(\mathcal C)\ge \sum_{a\in A\setminus\{0\}}g(|a|^2)=E_g(A). \] The comparison and the equality are in the extended nonnegative reals.

primaryStatements.name: Sharp Gaussian minorants
primaryStatements.label: thm:gaussian
primaryStatements.text: For every $\alpha>0$ there is a real radial Schwartz function $f_\alpha:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R$ such that \[ f_\alpha(x)\le k_\alpha(x),\qquad \widehat f_\alpha(\xi)\ge0 \quad(x,\xi\in\mathbb R^2), \] and \[ f_\alpha(a)=k_\alpha(a)\quad(a\in A\setminus\{0\}),\qquad \widehat f_\alpha(w)=0\quad(w\in A^*\setminus\{0\}). \] For $\alpha\ge1$, the construction uses two finite $20$-by-$20$ interpolation blocks and an absolutely summable infinite correction.

primaryStatements.name: Density-only linear programming
primaryStatements.label: energy:lp
primaryStatements.text: Let $f$ be a real even Schwartz function on $\mathbb R^2$ with $\widehat f\ge0$, and let $\mathcal C$ be locally finite with $N_R/(\pi R^2)\to1$. Then \begin{equation} \liminf_{R\to\infty}\frac1{N_R} \sum_{\substack{x,y\in\mathcal C_R\\x\ne y}}f(x-y) \ge\widehat f(0)-f(0). \end{equation} The same lower bound holds if the summands are replaced by $\Phi(x-y)$, where $\Phi(z)\ge f(z)$ for every $z\ne0$.

primaryStatements.name: Exact interpolation and approximation
primaryStatements.label: prop:exact-interpolation
primaryStatements.text: For every $\alpha\ge1$, let $z$ and $e$ be its Gaussian parameter and data vector defined in Sections \ref{sec:construction} and \ref{sec:finite-certificate}. Retain the fixed coefficients $c_{i,0},d_{i,0},C_i$ in \eqref{analytic:input-functions}. There are unique real coefficient lists \[ u_i\in\mathbb R^{20},\qquad w_i\in\ell^1(T;\mathbb R^2)\qquad(i=1,2), \] indexed respectively by the pairs $(c_{i,n},d_{i,n})$ on $f$ and $T$, for which the functions $J_i=e^{\pi hs}F_i$ from that construction satisfy \[ J_1(n)=G_z(n),\quad J_1'(n)=G_z'(n),\qquad J_2(n)=J_2'(n)=0\qquad(n\in\mathcal N). \] Relative to the finite coefficient lists $A_i e$, they obey \begin{equation} \|w_i\|_1<3\cdot10^{-9},\qquad \|u_i-(A_i e)_f\|_1<10^{-5}\qquad(i=1,2). \end{equation} The resulting $F_i$ are real radial Schwartz functions with $\widehat F_1=F_2$. Uniqueness concerns these coefficient lists with the prescribed fixed columns, not all radial Schwartz functions with the same interpolation data.

primaryStatements.name: Global signs
primaryStatements.label: prop:global-signs

lean.scopeText:
The formalization proves that the density-one triangular lattice minimizes lower energy per particle among all locally finite planar configurations of centered-disk density one, for every nonnegative completely monotone function of squared distance. Infinite energies are allowed in the comparison.

It also constructs sharp radial Schwartz minorants for every Gaussian potential: each minorant lies below the Gaussian, has nonnegative real Fourier transform, agrees with the Gaussian at nonzero triangular-lattice points, and vanishes on nonzero dual-lattice points after Fourier transformation. For the stated parameter range, the formalization includes the explicit atomic interpolation construction.

The planar Cohn–Elkies sharpness conjecture asks whether the two-point Fourier method attains the optimal circle-packing density. The formalization constructs a radial Schwartz function $f$ on $\mathbb R^2$ with $\widehat f(0)=1$, $f(0)=2/\sqrt3$, $\widehat f$ real and nonnegative everywhere, and $f(x)\le0$ whenever $\|x\|\ge1$. These are the sharp Fourier certificate conditions yielding density $\pi/(2\sqrt3)$. The separate uniqueness statement for periodic equality cases is outside this selected theorem.

papers.title: Universal optimality of the triangular lattice
papers.abstract: We prove universal energy minimality for the triangular lattice in the plane. Among locally finite configurations of centered density one, it minimizes the lower limit of centered-ball energy averages for every nonnegative completely monotone function of squared distance, including when the energy is infinite. We also prove triangular minimality for planar logarithmic and Riesz renormalized energies, with $0\lt s\lt 2$ in the Riesz case, and the corresponding jellium minima. The proof uses sharp Gaussian Fourier bounds, positive mixtures, and heat-kernel comparison.

primaryStatements.name: Linear programming with centered disk density
primaryStatements.label: prop:density-lp
primaryStatements.text: Let $f$ be a real even Schwartz function on $\R^2$ whose Fourier transform is nonnegative. Every locally finite configuration $\mathcal C\subset\R^2$ with centered disk density one satisfies \begin{equation} \liminf_{R\to\infty}\frac1{N_R} \sum_{\substack{x,y\in\mathcal C_R\\x\ne y}}f(x-y) \ge \widehat f(0)-f(0). \end{equation} The same lower bound holds if $f(x-y)$ is replaced by $\Phi(x-y)$, where $\Phi:\R^2\setminus\{0\}\to[0,\infty)$ satisfies $\Phi(z)\ge f(z)$.

primaryStatements.name: Positive-mixture transfer
primaryStatements.label: prop:energy-reduction
primaryStatements.text: Let $\mathcal C\subset\R^2$ be locally finite with centered disk density one. Suppose that, for every $\alpha>0$, \[ \liminf_{R\to\infty}\frac1{N_R} \sum_{\substack{x,y\in\mathcal C_R\\x\ne y}}e^{-\pi\alpha|x-y|^2} \ge\sum_{a\in A\setminus\{0\}}e^{-\pi\alpha|a|^2}. \] Then every smooth completely monotone $g:(0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ satisfies \begin{equation} E_g(\mathcal C)\ge\sum_{a\in A\setminus\{0\}}g(|a|^2) \end{equation} in the extended nonnegative reals, with the ordered-pair energy defined in \eqref{eq:energy-definition}.

primaryStatements.name: Planar renormalized and jellium energies
primaryStatements.label: cor:riesz-jellium
primaryStatements.text: Let $0\le s<2$. For every positive integer $n$, put $N=n^2$ and enumerate $A/(nA)$ by $a_1^\triangle,\ldots,a_N^\triangle$. Every configuration of $N$ distinct points in $\R^2/(nA)$ satisfies \[ W_{s,nA}(a_1,\ldots,a_N) \ge W_{s,nA}(a_1^\triangle,\ldots,a_N^\triangle). \] Moreover, $A$ minimizes $W_s$ among density-one planar configurations, and $e_{\mathrm{Jel}}^{(s)}=\kappa_s^{-1}W_s(A)$.

primaryStatements.name: Normalized cubic approximation
primaryStatements.label: prop:normalized-cubic-approximation
primaryStatements.text: Let $0\le s<2$, and fix $1<p<2$ for $s=0$, or $1<p<\min(2,2/s,3/(s+1))$ for $s>0$. Let $\mathcal A_1$ be the compatible gradient fields in this fixed $L^p_{\rm loc}$ class, with simple locally finite configurations and unit background. Then the limit \[ \mathcal W(E)=\lim_{\eta\downarrow0} \left[\limsup_{R\to\infty}R^{-2}Q_\eta(E,R) -\kappa g(\eta)\right] \] exists in $\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ and is bounded below uniformly over $\mathcal A_1$. Its infimum $m$ is finite. There are integers $R_j\to\infty$ and simple configurations $\mathcal C_j$, periodic under $2R_j\mathbb Z^2$, with $4R_j^2$ points per period cell, whose canonical periodic values satisfy \[ V(\mathcal C_j)\longrightarrow m. \] The approximating fields may therefore be chosen to be canonical periodic gradients in the same fixed-$p$ class.

primaryStatements.label: interpolation:solution
primaryStatements.text: There are unique real lists $x_1,x_2\in X$ satisfying \eqref{fourier:coefficient-equations} with the fixed data \eqref{fourier:fixed}. For each $i=1,2$, \begin{equation} \sum_{n\in\mathcal N} \bigl(\abs{c_{i,n}-\widetilde c_{i,n}} +\abs{d_{i,n}-\widetilde d_{i,n}}\bigr)<.00003. \end{equation} The norm of each exact list, including its node-zero coefficients, is less than $2.3$. Consequently $F(x)\le0$ when $b\abs{x}^2\ge1$, and $\widehat F(\xi)\ge0$ for every $\xi\in\RR^2$.

primaryStatements.label: ind:taylor-budgets
primaryStatements.text: The following choices give sufficient rational error enclosures for the same finite quantities used in Appendix \ref{sec:certificates}. For a basis input at $n\in J=\{1,3,4\}$, a row $m\in J$, $y=1$, and $\ell=0,1$, take $D=63$, $h_D=32$, $M=10^6$, and $\delta=10^{-14}$ in \eqref{ind:coefficient-budget}. There are no atoms. If $Q_m,D_m$ have rational errors at most $10^{-25}$, either entry of \eqref{cert:pair} has error less than $2.13\cdot10^{-13}<10^{-12}$. For the full rational finite-input domain at the start of this subsection, take $D=255$, $h_D=128$, $M=10^{53}$, and $\delta=4\cdot10^{-15}$ in \eqref{ind:coefficient-budget}, and require each of the seven atom-product radii in \eqref{ind:atom-radii} to be at most $4\cdot10^{-15}/7$. Each $U$ and $X$ moment then has error less than $10^{-14}$. For node rows $m\in I_f$, with rational $Q_m,D_m$ errors at most $10^{-25}$, either entry of \eqref{cert:pair} has error less than $1.8\cdot10^{-14}$.

primaryStatements.label: ind:node-taylor-proposition
primaryStatements.text: Let $p=PR$ have a real $\ell^1$ coefficient list as in \eqref{fourier:list-norm}. Define \begin{equation} A_k(m)=\frac{P^{(k)}(m)}{k!} =\frac1{k!}\sum_{v=-6}^6P_v(i\pi t_v)^k e^{i\pi t_vm}. \end{equation} Then $A_0(m)=A_1(m)=0$. The regular series has coefficients \begin{equation} r_j(m)=C\mathbf1_{\{j=0\}}+ (-1)^j\sum_{\substack{n\in\mathcal N_0\\n\ne m}} \left(\frac{(j+1)c_n}{(m-n)^{j+2}} +\frac{d_n}{(m-n)^{j+1}}\right), \end{equation} and converges for $|u|<\rho_m$. For $0<|u|<\rho_m$, the Laurent expansion is \[ R(m+u)=\frac{c_m}{u^2}+\frac{d_m}{u} +\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}r_j(m)u^j. \] For every integer $\ell\ge0$ the direct derivative is therefore \begin{equation} \frac{p^{(\ell)}(m)}{\ell!} =c_mA_{\ell+2}(m)+d_mA_{\ell+1}(m) +\sum_{k=2}^{\ell}A_k(m)r_{\ell-k}(m), \end{equation} where the last sum is empty for $\ell=0,1$.

papers.title: Triangular minimality for planar Coulomb renormalized energy
papers.abstract: We prove the Sandier–Serfaty conjecture: the triangular lattice of covolume one minimizes planar Coulomb renormalized energy over all admissible curl-free fields with a unit uniform background. The proof uses a direct Voronoi-cell comparison with rigorous interval arithmetic.

primaryStatements.name: Spherical logarithmic energy
primaryStatements.label: cor:bhs
primaryStatements.text: Let $S^2=\{y\in\R^3:\|y\|=1\}$ be the unit sphere. For each integer $n\ge2$, define \[ E_{\log}(n)=\min_{(y_1,\ldots,y_n)\in(S^2)^n} \left(-\sum_{\substack{1\le i,j\le n\\i\ne j}} \log\|y_i-y_j\|\right), \] where the sum is over ordered pairs, $\|\cdot\|$ is the Euclidean norm in $\R^3$, $\log$ is the natural logarithm, and a collision has energy $+\infty$. Then, as $n\to\infty$ through the integers, \begin{equation} E_{\log}(n)=\left(\frac12-\log2\right)n^2 -\frac n2\log n+C_{\mathrm{BHS}}n+o(n), \end{equation} where \begin{equation} C_{\mathrm{BHS}} =2\log2+\frac12\log\!\left(\frac23\right) +3\log\!\left(\frac{\sqrt\pi}{\Gamma(1/3)}\right), \end{equation} and $\Gamma$ is Euler's gamma function.

primaryStatements.name: Reduction to square tori
primaryStatements.label: red:reduction
primaryStatements.text: Let $C\in\R$. Suppose that for every integer $n\ge2$ and every configuration of $n$ distinct points of $T_n$, the mean-zero potential in \eqref{eq:torus-energy} satisfies $\mathcal W_n(h)\ge nC$. Then $W(E)\ge C$ for every $E\in\mathcal A_1$. In particular, if these finite-torus bounds hold with $C=W(E_\triangle)$, then \[ \inf_{E\in\mathcal A_1}W(E)=W(E_\triangle). \]

primaryStatements.name: Dual identity
primaryStatements.label: dual:identity
primaryStatements.text: For compatible periodic Voronoi data on \(\mathbb T=\R^2/\Gamma\) with \(N\geq1\) distinct sites, lower edge distance \(d_0>0\), and \(|\mathbb T|=N\), let \(h\) be the mean-zero potential \eqref{dual:torus-potential}. Let \(I\) be finite or countable, let \(k_i\geq6\) be integers with repetitions permitted, and let \(B,D_i\in C^1((0,\infty))\) satisfy \eqref{dual:radial-origin}--\eqref{dual:radial-sum}. Let \(H\) be the function supplied by Lemma \ref{dual:gluing}. Then \begin{equation} \mathcal W_{\mathbb T}(h) =\sum_S J(S)+ \frac12\int_{\mathbb T}|\nabla(h-H)|^2\,\dd x \geq\sum_S J(S). \end{equation} The sum runs over all face--edge incidences in one torus. No incidence bound or square-torus separation hypothesis is imposed.

primaryStatements.name: From sector bounds to energy bounds
primaryStatements.label: dual:assembly
primaryStatements.text: Let \(d_0>0\), let \(I\) be finite or countable, let \(k_i\geq6\) be integers with repetitions permitted, and let \(B,D_i\in C^1((0,\infty))\) satisfy \eqref{dual:radial-origin} and \eqref{dual:radial-sum} with this lower distance \(d_0\). For every sector \eqref{geo:sector} with \(d\geq d_0\), use these same radial data in \eqref{dual:trial} and let \(J(S)\) be the functional \eqref{dual:sector-functional}. Suppose that \(K\leq0\) and \(\lambda,\mu\in\R\) satisfy \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} J(S(d,\alpha,\beta)) &\geq K+\lambda A(S(d,\alpha,\beta))\\ &\qquad+\mu\theta(S(d,\alpha,\beta)), \end{aligned} \end{equation} for every \(d\geq d_0\), \(|\alpha|,|\beta|<\pi/2\), and \(\alpha+\beta>0\). Compatible tori. Let \(\mathbb T=\R^2/\Gamma\) have area \(N\), where \(N\geq1\) is an integer. Suppose \(N\) distinct sites supply compatible periodic Voronoi data with lower edge distance \(d_0\) and at most \(6N\) face--edge sectors. Their mean-zero potential \eqref{dual:torus-potential} satisfies \begin{equation} \mathcal W_{\mathbb T}(h)\geq N(6K+\lambda+2\pi\mu). \end{equation} All square-torus configurations. Assume in addition \(d_0\leq d_*=1/(2\sqrt\pi)\). For every integer \(n\geq2\) and every configuration of \(n\) distinct points \(v_1,\ldots,v_n\) on \(T_n=\R^2/(\sqrt n\,\Z^2)\), let \(h\) be the mean-zero solution of \[ -\Delta h=2\pi\left(\sum_{i=1}^n\delta_{v_i}-1\right). \] Then its puncture-first energy \eqref{eq:torus-energy}, with embedded and pairwise disjoint punctures, satisfies \begin{equation} \mathcal W_n(h)\geq n(6K+\lambda+2\pi\mu). \end{equation} More generally, if a periodic locally integrable field \(E\) on \(T_n\) satisfies, distributionally, \[ \operatorname{div}E=2\pi\left(\sum_{i=1}^n\delta_{v_i}-1\right), \qquad \operatorname{curl}E=0, \] then \(E=-\nabla h+c\) for a constant \(c\in\R^2\), and its energy with the same punctures and counterterm obeys \[ \mathcal E_{T_n}(E)=\mathcal W_n(h)+\frac n2|c|^2 \geq n(6K+\lambda+2\pi\mu). \] The energy identity remains valid after applying the same fixed orthogonal rotation to both fields.

primaryStatements.label: cal:scalar-to-torus
primaryStatements.text: Assume \eqref{cal:scalar-bounds} for the functions and constants just constructed. Let $\mathbb T=\R^2/\Gamma$ be a flat torus of area $N$, where $N\ge1$ is an integer, and let $v_1,\ldots,v_N$ be distinct sites. Suppose their full periodic lift gives compatible periodic Voronoi data with lower edge distance $d_0=b$ and at most $6N$ face-edge sectors. Let $h$ be the mean-zero potential \eqref{dual:torus-potential}, with energy $\mathcal W_{\mathbb T}(h)$ defined by \eqref{dual:torus-energy}. Then \[ \mathcal W_{\mathbb T}(h)\ge NW(E_\triangle). \]

papers.title: The logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski conjecture for arbitrary origin-symmetric convex bodies in every dimension. The theorem also gives the symmetric Lp Brunn–Minkowski inequality for every $0\lt p\lt 1$. Combined with Saroglou's transfer theorem and a support-subspace reduction, it yields the logarithmic inequality for every even log-concave Radon measure and the scalar-dilation $(B)$-conjecture.

primaryStatements.name: Even logarithmic Brunn--Minkowski inequality
primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let $n\ge1$ and let $K,L\subset\R^n$ be convex bodies satisfying $K=-K$ and $L=-L$. For every $0\le\lambda\le1$, \begin{equation} \left|\mathcal W[h_K^{1-\lambda}h_L^\lambda]\right| \ge |K|^{1-\lambda}|L|^\lambda. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Symmetric $L_p$ Brunn--Minkowski inequality
primaryStatements.label: cor:lp
primaryStatements.text: Let $n\ge1$, let $K,L\subset\R^n$ be full-dimensional origin-symmetric convex bodies, and let $0<p<1$. For every $0\le\lambda\le1$, \begin{equation} \left|\mathcal W\!\left[ \bigl((1-\lambda)h_K^p+\lambda h_L^p\bigr)^{1/p} \right]\right|^{p/n} \ge (1-\lambda)|K|^{p/n}+\lambda|L|^{p/n}. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Variance bound
primaryStatements.label: prop:variance
primaryStatements.text: Let $n\ge2$, $N\ge1$, $q\ge2$ be an even integer, and $\eps>0$. Let $p_1,\ldots,p_N\in\R^n\setminus\{0\}$ and $h_1,\ldots,h_N>0$. Set \begin{equation} \psi_i(x)=\left(\frac{\langle p_i,x\rangle}{h_i}\right)^q, \qquad V(x)=\frac{\eps}{2}|x|^2+\sum_{i=1}^N\psi_i(x), \qquad d\mu=Z^{-1}e^{-V(x)}\,dx, \end{equation} where $Z=\int_{\R^n}e^{-V(x)}\,dx$. For all real $b_1,\ldots,b_N$, \begin{equation} \Var_\mu\left(\sum_{i=1}^N b_i\psi_i\right) \le\sum_{i=1}^N b_i^2\E_\mu\psi_i. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Measure inequality and scalar $(B)$-conjecture
primaryStatements.label: cor:measure
primaryStatements.text: Let $n\ge1$, let $\mu$ be an even log-concave Radon measure on $\R^n$, and let $K,L\subset\R^n$ be origin-symmetric convex bodies. Then, for every $0\le\lambda\le1$, \begin{equation} \mu\bigl(\mathcal W[h_K^{1-\lambda}h_L^\lambda]\bigr) \ge \mu(K)^{1-\lambda}\mu(L)^\lambda. \end{equation} Consequently, for every origin-symmetric convex body $K\subset\R^n$, the function \begin{equation} \R\ni t\longmapsto \mu(e^tK) \end{equation} is log-concave.

lean.scopeText: The logarithmic Brunn–Minkowski conjecture asserts that logarithmic interpolation of origin-symmetric convex bodies preserves the geometric-mean lower bound for volume. The formalized result proves, for every dimension $n\ge1$, such bodies $K,L\subset\mathbb R^n$, and $0\le t\le1$, that their logarithmic Wulff combination has volume at least $|K|^{1-t}|L|^t$. It assumes neither boundary smoothness nor coordinatewise unconditionality.

primaryStatements.name: Weighted vertical patterns
primaryStatements.label: prop:vertical
primaryStatements.text: There are absolute constants $B,C,c,\kappa>0$ such that, for every integer $b_1\ge B$, the construction above has \begin{equation} D\le C(b_1+1),\qquad R^2:=\sum_{i=1}^{r+1}b_i h_i^2 \le C\bigl(b_1\log(b_1+1)+1\bigr). \end{equation} For every $y\in\R^D$ there is a finite nonempty pattern $\mathcal P_y\subset L$ such that \begin{align} \|(y-M\ell)_i\|_\infty&\le h_i \qquad(\ell\in\mathcal P_y,\ 1\le i\le r+1), \\ \sum_{\ell\in\mathcal P_y}D_v\gamma_D(y-M\ell)&\ge\kappa, \\ \max_{\ell\in\mathcal P_y}D_v\gamma_D(y-M\ell) &\le \exp(-c b_1^{0.70}). \end{align} The terminal block is constant on the pattern. For each ordinary block $i$ and each fixed suffix $(\ell_{i+1},\ldots,\ell_{r+1})$, its retained values belong to $\lambda_i+\{0,1\}^{b_i}$ for one $\lambda_i\in L_i$ depending on that suffix. In particular $|\mathcal P_y|\le 2^D$. Order the scalar coordinates by increasing block index and denote them by $\ell[1],\ldots,\ell[D]$. Conditional on any fixed scalar suffix $\ell[j+1],\ldots,\ell[D]$, the possible next values $\ell[j]$ are at most two; if there are two, they differ by $1$. This property is preserved upon deleting any subset of the pattern. If $y\in M[0,1)^D$, all raw coordinates can in addition be restricted to the fixed finite alphabets \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \ell_i&\in\bigl(p_i^{-1}\Z\cap[-Q_{\rm raw},Q_{\rm raw}]\bigr)^{b_i} &&(i\le r),\\ \ell_{r+1}&\in\bigl(\Z\cap[-Q_{\rm raw},Q_{\rm raw}]\bigr)^T, &&Q_{\rm raw}=1+(D+2)^D. \end{aligned} \end{equation} For an ordinary block the logarithm of each scalar alphabet size is $O(D\log(D+2)+b_i\log b_i)$; the terminal version omits the second term. All implicit constants are absolute.

The formalized result gives an absolute constant $C>0$ such that every convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, admits a covering by translates along one full-rank lattice $L$ with density $|K|/\mathrm{covol}(L)\le Cn\log n$. The covering is exact, and no symmetry, boundary regularity, or volume normalization is assumed.

The formalization determines the order of the largest covering density in dimension $n$. For all sufficiently large $n$, the suprema of translative covering density and lattice covering density are each bounded above and below by absolute positive multiples of $n\log n$, both over all convex bodies and over centrally symmetric convex bodies.

primaryStatements.name: Deterministic localization
primaryStatements.label: prop:localization
primaryStatements.text: For all sufficiently large $n$, uniformly for $1\le R\le n^2$, the family $\mathcal F_n$ has the following properties. With $\lambda_0=\log(1+D/a)$, \begin{equation} N_n\le n^{C_1}\exp(\lambda_0n),\qquad \log|\mathcal F_n| \le\exp\bigl(\lambda_0n+O(\log n)\bigr), \end{equation} where $C_1$ and the implicit constant depend only on the fixed parameters. Let $\mathcal U\subset S^{n-1}$ be any finite set, and put \[ K=bB\cap\bigcap_{u\in\mathcal U}\{x:|u\cdot x|\le1\},\qquad K^+=(b+3\eta)B\cap \bigcap_{u\in\mathcal U}\{x:|u\cdot x|\le1+3\eta\}. \] Suppose that $\Lambda$ is any full-rank lattice, $T\subset\mathbb R^n$ is finite, and \[ \frac{|T|}{\det\Lambda}\le \rho_0:=\frac{R}{2v\omega_na^n}. \] If $K+\Lambda+T$ covers $\mathbb R^n$, there is a list $P=(p_1,\ldots,p_m)\in\mathcal F_n$ such that \begin{equation} B_D\subseteq\bigcup_{j=1}^{m}(p_j+K^+). \end{equation} The constructed list in fact satisfies $|G_P|\ge|B_D|/2$. For every $P\in\mathcal F_n$ and $y\in G_P$, list all residual vectors $x_i=y-p_j$ with $|y-p_j|\le b+3\eta$, retaining their indices, and denote their number by $m_y$. Then \begin{equation} \begin{gathered} r_--2\eta\le |x_i|\le b+3\eta,\qquad m_y\le2C_{\mathrm{loc}}R,\qquad \sum_{i=1}^{m_y}w_a(|x_i|)\le2C_{\mathrm{loc}}R,\\ m_y+\sum_{i=1}^{m_y}w_a(|x_i|)\le4C_{\mathrm{loc}}R. \end{gathered} \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Block estimates
primaryStatements.label: prop:blocks
primaryStatements.text: Fix constants $C_0\ge1$, $c_0>0$, and $L\ge1$. There are constants $B_0,K,C\ge1$ and $n_1$, depending only on these three constants, with the following property. Let $n\ge n_1$, let $(X,\mu)$ be an atomless finite measure space, and let $(C_i)_{i\in I}$ be an indexed list of measurable sets with $0<c_i:=\mu(C_i)<\infty$ and $1\le m:=|I|\le n^2$. Set \[ \bar c_i=\min(c_i,1/2),\qquad s_i=-\log\bar c_i, \] and let $d$ be a pseudometric on $I$. For nonempty $S\subseteq I$, write \[ r(S)=\min_{j\in S}\max_{i\in S}d(i,j)^2, \] and choose an index $i(S)\in S$ minimizing the uncapped measure $c_i$. Assume that \begin{equation} \frac{\mu(C_i\cap C_j)}{\sqrt{\bar c_i\bar c_j}} \le C_0e^{-c_0d(i,j)^2}\qquad(i,j\in I), \end{equation} and that, whenever $r(S)\le B_0\log n$, \begin{equation} \mu\left(\bigcap_{i\in S}C_i\right) \ge e^{-L(1+r(S)+\log|S|)}\bar c_{i(S)}. \end{equation} Then there is a partition $\mathcal P$ of $I$ and measurable sets $E_S\subseteq\bigcap_{i\in S}C_i$, $S\in\mathcal P$, of measures $\lambda_S=\mu(E_S)$ such that \begin{equation} n^{-K}\bar c_{i(S)}\le\lambda_S\le\frac12. \end{equation} Writing $q_S=-\log\lambda_S$ and \[ w_{ST}= \frac{\mu(E_S\cap E_T)} {\sqrt{\lambda_S(1+\lambda_S)\lambda_T(1+\lambda_T)}}, \] we have \begin{align} \sum_{S\in\mathcal P}q_S &\le\sum_{i\in I}s_i+\frac{m}{10}, \\ \sum_{S\in\mathcal P}\log(1+\lambda_S^{-1}) &\le C\left(m+\sum_{i\in I}s_i\right), \\ \sum_{S\in\mathcal P} \log\left(1+\sum_{T\in\mathcal P\setminus\{S\}}w_{ST}\right) &\le C\left(m+\sum_{i\in I}s_i\right). \end{align}

primaryStatements.text: If Theorem \ref{thm:main} fails, there is a sequence of dimensions and centered compactly supported log-concave laws $\mu$ satisfying Equation \eqref{eq:critical-normalization}. Fix $s=1/8$, form $\mu_s,b_s,M_s,K_s$ as in Equation \eqref{eq:critical-posterior}, and put $\lambda=R_s^{-1}$. After passage to a subsequence there are smooth positive probabilities $\eta$ and smooth vector fields $w$ such that, with $A=A_\eta$ and $I=\E_\eta|w|^2$, \begin{gather} \lambda\longrightarrow1,\qquad R(\eta)\le\lambda^{-1}, \qquad 0<I<\infty,\qquad w\in\Dom(A)^n, \\ A w=(\lambda\Id-K_s)w,\qquad \|(A-1)w\|_{L^2(\eta)}+|\E_\eta w|=o(\sqrt I), \\ \E_\eta|K_sw|^2=o(I),\qquad \E_\eta|Dw|^2=(1+o(1))I. \end{gather} The spectral gap of $A$ is at least $\lambda$. Each coordinate function belongs to $\Dom(A)$. Exactly one of the following constructions can be used throughout the subsequence: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item $R_s>R_s^P$, $\eta=f^2\mu_s$ for the positive unit-norm optimizer, $w=D\log f^2$, and $I=2\lambda H(\eta\mid\mu_s)$. The exact deficit identity in Equation \eqref{eq:critical-exact-deficit} holds for compact square-root tests relative to $\eta$, and $A Y=(Y-b_s)/s-w$. \item $R_s=R_s^P$, $\eta=\mu_s$, $A\varphi=\lambda\varphi$, $\E_\eta\varphi=0$, $w=D\varphi$, and $I=\lambda\E_\eta\varphi^2$. One may rescale $\varphi$ so that $I\to0$. \end{enumerate} All $o$-terms refer to the counterexample sequence with fixed finite parameters. In particular no relation between dimension, $I$, and the rate of convergence is asserted or needed here.

primaryStatements.name: The prediction curve
primaryStatements.label: prop:prediction
primaryStatements.text: For the strict and gap critical sequences, for every fixed $0<r<1/4$, \begin{equation} m(r)\longrightarrow e^{-r}. \end{equation} In the strict case, for every fixed finite $T\ge0$ one also has $p_T(r)\to e^{-r}$. In the gap case the eigenfunction may be rescaled so that $I\to0$, without changing Equation \eqref{eq:prediction-curve} or Equation \eqref{eq:prediction-input}.

primaryStatements.name: Symmetric tensor hierarchy
primaryStatements.label: prop:hierarchy
primaryStatements.text: Consider a sequence of smooth positive probability densities $\eta$ on finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces, with finite second moments. Let $A=-\Delta-D\log\eta\cdot D$, and suppose that $\eta$ satisfies Poincar\'e with constant at most $\lambda^{-1}$, where $\lambda\to1$. Fix $s=1/8$. Suppose smooth vector fields $b,w$ and a symmetric matrix field $K$ satisfy \[ D\log\eta=-\frac{y-b(y)}s+\omega(y),\qquad Db=\Id-sK,\qquad 0\le K\le s^{-1}\Id, \] where either $\omega=w$ throughout the sequence or $\omega=0$ throughout the sequence. Assume $b,w\in L^2(\eta)$, $w$ is a gradient, and, with $I=\|w\|_2^2>0$, \begin{equation} w\in\Dom A,\qquad \|(A-1)w\|_2=o(\sqrt I),\qquad |\E_\eta w|=o(\sqrt I),\qquad \langle w,Kw\rangle_2=o(I). \end{equation} Assume also the following prediction and projection properties. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item For $Y\sim\eta$ and an independent standard Gaussian $G$, set \[ U_r=Y+\sqrt r\,G,\quad h_r(u)=\E[w(Y)\mid U_r=u],\quad m(r)=I^{-1}\E|h_r(U_r)|^2. \] For every fixed $0<r<1/4$, one has $m(r)\to e^{-r}$. \item For every fixed $c<\infty$, \begin{equation} \sup_{\substack{\Pi^2=\Pi=\Pi^*\ \mathrm{deterministic}\\ \rank\Pi\le cI}} \|\Pi w\|_2^2=o(I). \end{equation} For every $\epsilon>0$ there is a deterministic projection $\Pi_\epsilon$ of rank at most $C_\epsilon I$ such that \begin{equation} \left\|\E[(1-\Pi_\epsilon)bb^*(1-\Pi_\epsilon)]\right\|_{\op} +\left\|\E[(1-\Pi_\epsilon)\omega\omega^* (1-\Pi_\epsilon)]\right\|_{\op}\le\epsilon \end{equation} eventually along the sequence. \item If $\omega=w$, the conditional covariance $C_r=\Cov(w(Y)\mid U_r)$ satisfies, for every fixed $r\in(0,1/4)$ and $a>0$, \begin{equation} \E\tr\bigl(C_r\1_{\{C_r>a\}}\bigr)=o(I). \end{equation} No conditional covariance-tail assumption is made when $\omega=0$. \end{enumerate} Then there are totally symmetric tensor fields $T_l$ of order $l+1$, for every fixed integer $l\ge0$, with $T_0=w$, such that \begin{equation} \begin{gathered} \|T_l\|_2^2=(1+o(1))I,\qquad \|(A-1)T_l\|_2=o(\sqrt I),\\ \|DT_l-T_{l+1}\|_2=o(\sqrt I). \end{gathered} \end{equation} \begin{equation} \langle T_l,K_1T_l\rangle_2=o(I). \end{equation} \begin{equation} \sup_{\substack{\Pi^2=\Pi=\Pi^*\ \mathrm{deterministic}\\ \rank\Pi\le cI}} \|\Pi_1T_l\|_2^2=o(I) \qquad\text{for every fixed }c<\infty. \end{equation} Every $T_l$ belongs componentwise to $\Dom A$. For $l\ge1$ it can be chosen in $\bigcap_{p\ge1}\Dom A^p$. By symmetry, the specified slot in Equations \eqref{eq:hierarchy-curvature} and \eqref{eq:hierarchy-projection} may be any slot. All assertions can be made simultaneous for any fixed finite collection of levels and parameters.

primaryStatements.name: Frozen diffusion law
primaryStatements.label: prop:frozen-law
primaryStatements.text: Let $Y_u$ be the stationary diffusion with invariant law $\eta$ and driving Brownian motion $B_u$, and fix $t>0$. Make the matrix construction of Lemma \ref{lem:matrix-blocks} at $Y_0$, using an independent random block offset. In its orthonormal frame put $N=B_t/\sqrt t$; conditionally on the initial data and block offset, $N$ is a standard Gaussian vector. Define, in the initial spatial coordinates, \begin{equation} \sigma=\bigoplus_\beta\beta^2 \exp\bigl(\sqrt{8t}\,H[N]-4t\Id_\beta\bigr), \end{equation} and set $\sigma=0$ on the omitted kernel. Then \begin{equation} \E\|R(Y_t)-\sigma^{1/2}\|_{\HS}^2\longrightarrow0. \end{equation} The matrices defining $\sigma$ obey the bounded-column and input-map bounds \eqref{eq:matrix-column-bound} and \eqref{eq:flattening-bound}, the weighted defects \eqref{eq:matrix-tracial-defects}, and the mixed moment law of Lemma \ref{lem:matrix-gaussian-moments}.

primaryStatements.name: Universal integrated upper bound
primaryStatements.label: prop:information-upper
primaryStatements.text: There is an absolute constant $C_0$ such that, for every fixed $t>0$ and $L\ge1$, the observations in Equation \eqref{eq:obs-covariance-definition} satisfy \begin{equation} \limsup\int_0^\infty\MI(Y_t;Z_T)\,\frac{dT}{T^2}\le C_0. \end{equation} In particular, one may take $C_0=9/4$.

papers.title: Subpolynomial dimension reduction in Lp
papers.abstract: For every fixed $1\lt p\lt \infty$ and D > 1, every n-point subset of a real Lp space embeds into $\ell_p^d$ with distortion at most D and subpolynomial dimension $d=n^{o(1)}$. The target has the same exponent p, and the embedding need not be linear.

In contrast, exact embeddings require worst-case dimension $\Theta(n^2)$ when p ≠ 2.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Fix $1<p<\infty$, $p\ne2$, and put \[ \gamma(p)= \begin{cases} 2-p,&1<p<2,\\ 1-2/p,&2<p<\infty. \end{cases} \] For every $D>1$ there is a constant $C_{p,D}<\infty$ such that, for every integer $n\ge2$, \begin{equation} \frac{\log n}{\log(1+2D)} \le d_p(n,D) \le \exp\!\bigl(C_{p,D}(\log n)^{\gamma(p)}\bigr). \end{equation} For exact embeddings, \begin{equation} \left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{4}\right\rfloor^2 \le d_p(n,1)\le\binom n2\qquad(n\ge9). \end{equation} Consequently, \[ \lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log d_p(n,D)}{\log n} =\begin{cases}0,&D>1,\\2,&D=1.\end{cases} \]

lean.scopeText: For $p>1$, $p\ne2$, the formalization bounds the least dimension needed to embed every $n$-point subset of real $L_p$ with distortion $D$. For each fixed $D>1$, there is a constant $C=C(p,D)$ such that this dimension lies between $\log n/\log(1+2D)$ and $\exp(C(\log n)^{\gamma(p)})$ for every $n\ge2$, where $\gamma(p)=2-p$ for $p<2$ and $1-2/p$ for $p>2$. At distortion $1$ and $n\ge9$, it lies between $\lfloor(n-1)/4\rfloor^2$ and $\binom n2$. The least dimension is attained, and its logarithm divided by $\log n$ tends to $0$ for $D>1$ and to $2$ for $D=1$.

papers.title: Hyperbolicity Cones Without Semidefinite Lifts
papers.abstract: We prove that not every hyperbolicity cone is a spectrahedral shadow: some closed hyperbolicity cones admit no finite affine semidefinite lift, even with arbitrary real coefficients and any finite number of auxiliary variables. This disproves the Projected Lax Conjecture and hence the generalized Lax conjecture.

This also disproves the generalized Lax conjecture that every hyperbolicity cone is spectrahedral.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: There exists a real homogeneous hyperbolic polynomial whose closed hyperbolicity cone has no finite semidefinite lift.

primaryStatements.label: prop:hyperbolic
primaryStatements.text: The polynomial $p_Q$ is homogeneous of degree $n(n+1)$ and hyperbolic with respect to $e=(I_n,I_n,0)$, with $p_Q(e)=1$. Fix $y$ and choose vectors $b_1,\ldots,b_n\in\R^r$ with $Q(y)=\sum_{j=1}^n b_jb_j^\top$. Define \[ B_j=\begin{pmatrix}0&b_j^\top\\-b_j&0\end{pmatrix}, \qquad \mathcal B=\begin{pmatrix}B_1\\\vdots\\B_n\end{pmatrix}. \] Then the closed hyperbolicity cone $K_Q$ of $p_Q$ is characterized, at this value of $y$, by \begin{equation} (X,Z,y)\in K_Q \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \begin{pmatrix}I_n\otimes X&\mathcal B\\ \mathcal B^\top&Z\end{pmatrix}\succeq0. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.label: prop:epigraph
primaryStatements.text: The set $E_Q$ is the image of the affine section $K_Q\cap\{X=\diag(1,A):A\in\Sym_r\}$ under the projection $(X,Z,y)\mapsto(A,Z_{00},y)$. Consequently, if $K_Q$ is a spectrahedral shadow, then so is $E_Q$.

primaryStatements.label: prop:finite-normalized-fiber
primaryStatements.text: The matrix $T$ in Lemma \ref{lem:seed} may be chosen so that, for $K=\operatorname{proj}_P\ker T$, \begin{enumerate} \item the fiber $\mathcal M_K$ of $\mathcal M\to\Gr(k,P)$ is finite; \item no point of $\overline{\mathcal M}\setminus\mathcal M$ projects to $K$. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.label: prop:no-lift
primaryStatements.text: For the admissible quadratic matrix map $Q$ of \eqref{eq:constructed-Q}, the set $E_Q$ is not a spectrahedral shadow. Consequently its associated entire closed hyperbolicity cone $K_Q$ is not a spectrahedral shadow.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: The polynomial \eqref{eq:polynomial} is homogeneous of degree $20$ and hyperbolic with respect to $e=(I_4,I_4,0)$, with $p(e)=1$. Its closed hyperbolicity cone $K=\Lambda_+(p,e)$ is not spectrahedral: for every finite $N\geq1$ and every real linear map $L:\Sym^4\times\Sym^4\times\R^3\to\Sym^N$, \[ K\ne\{(X,Z,y):L(X,Z,y)\succeq0\}. \]

primaryStatements.label: cor:reduced
primaryStatements.text: The quotient $q=p/\det X$ extends to a homogeneous polynomial of degree $16$ in the same $23$ variables. It is hyperbolic with respect to $e$, with $q(e)=1$, and $\Lambda_+(q,e)=K$. In particular, its closed hyperbolicity cone is not spectrahedral.

primaryStatements.label: prop:hyperbolic
primaryStatements.text: The polynomial $p$ in \eqref{eq:polynomial} is homogeneous of degree $20$ on $\Sym^4\times\Sym^4\times\R^3$, a real vector space of dimension $23$. It satisfies $p(e)=1$ and is hyperbolic with respect to $e=(I_4,I_4,0)$.

primaryStatements.label: prop:slices
primaryStatements.text: Let $K=\Lambda_+(p,e)$. For real symmetric $X,Z$ and $y\in\R^3$, \begin{align} X\succ0:\qquad (X,Z,y)\in K &\ \Longleftrightarrow\ Z\succeq\Phi_y(X^{-1}), \\ (X,Z,0)\in K &\ \Longleftrightarrow\ X\succeq0\ \text{and}\ Z\succeq0. \end{align} Moreover, $e$ lies in the interior of $K$ in the full ambient space.

primaryStatements.label: prop:pencil
primaryStatements.text: Let $K=\Lambda_+(p,(I_4,I_4,0))$ for the polynomial in \eqref{eq:polynomial}. Suppose that $K$ admits a representation by a finite homogeneous real symmetric linear pencil. Then there are integers $a,c\geq1$, positive linear maps \[ D:\Sym^4\longrightarrow\Sym^a, \qquad E:\Sym^4\longrightarrow\Sym^c, \qquad D(I_4)=I_a,\quad E(I_4)=I_c, \] and a linear map $B:\R^3\longrightarrow\R^{a\times c}$ such that, for every $X\succ0$, $Z\in\Sym^4$ and $y\in\R^3$, \begin{equation} Z\succeq\Phi_y(X^{-1}) \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad E(Z)\succeq B(y)^\top D(X)^{-1}B(y). \end{equation}

primaryStatements.label: prop:norm
primaryStatements.text: Let $a,c\geq1$, let $D:\Sym^4\to\Sym^a$ and $E:\Sym^4\to\Sym^c$ be positive unital linear maps, and let $B:\R^3\to\R^{a\times c}$ be linear. Assume that \eqref{eq:schur-equivalence} holds for every $X\succ0$, $Z\in\Sym^4$ and $y\in\R^3$, with $\Phi_y$ defined by \eqref{eq:phi}. Define $P(v)$ and $R(u)$ by \eqref{eq:projections}. For every pair of unit vectors $u=(u_0,u'),v=(v_0,v')\in\R^4$ and every $y\in\R^3$, \begin{equation} b(v_0u'-u_0v',y) =\norm{P(v)B(y)R(u)}_{\op}^{2}. \end{equation} Here the operator norm uses the Euclidean structures on the two block spaces.

lean.scopeText: The generalized Lax conjecture predicts that every hyperbolicity cone is spectrahedral. The formalized counterexample is an explicit homogeneous polynomial of degree $20$ in $23$ real variables. It is hyperbolic, but its closed hyperbolicity cone cannot be represented as the positive-semidefinite region of any finite real symmetric linear matrix pencil, in any positive matrix size.

papers.title: The Gaussian propeller bound in every dimension
papers.abstract: We prove the Gaussian propeller conjecture: for every finite measurable partition of a Euclidean space, the sum of the squared lengths of its Gaussian first moments is at most $9/(8\pi)$. For dimension at least two and at least three cells, three planar sectors of angle $2\pi/3$, extended by an orthogonal Euclidean factor, attain the bound.

Combined with the separate Unique Games theorem, this proves NP-hardness of improving the loss factor $(8\pi/9)(1-1/k)$ for identity-target kernel clustering with fixed k ≥ 3 on rational centered positive semidefinite inputs.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: For all positive integers $d$ and $k$, every measurable partition $(A_1,\ldots,A_k)$ of $\mathbb R^d$ satisfies \[ \sum_{i=1}^k\left\|\int_{A_i}x\,d\gamma_d(x)\right\|^2 \le\frac9{8\pi}. \] Empty cells are allowed. The constant is sharp whenever $d\ge2$ and $k\ge3$: three planar sectors of angle $2\pi/3$, multiplied by the orthogonal complement of their plane, attain equality, with any further cells empty.

primaryStatements.name: Kernel-clustering hardness
primaryStatements.label: kc:main
primaryStatements.text: For each fixed \(k\ge3\) and every fixed \(1\le\alpha<\alpha_k\), it is NP-hard, given a rational symmetric matrix \(A\succeq0\) with \(A\one=0\) and the identity-target objective \eqref{kc:value}, to find \(\sigma:[N]\to[k]\) such that \[ \val_A(\sigma)\ge\Clust(A\mid I_k)/\alpha. \] In particular, such a deterministic polynomial-time approximation would imply \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\).

primaryStatements.name: Constraints on the three largest radii
primaryStatements.label: geo:constraints
primaryStatements.text: The quantities $L,c,t$ satisfy \begin{align} (c-t^2)(L-c-2t^2) &\le8\left(\frac3\pi\right)^2t^2, \\ \frac32(c-t^2)^2 &\le10\left(\frac3\pi\right)^2t^2. \end{align}

primaryStatements.name: Gaussian maxima
primaryStatements.label: cor:gaussian-maxima
primaryStatements.text: Let $d,k$ be positive integers, let $g$ be standard Gaussian in $\mathbb R^d$, and let $v_1,\ldots,v_k\in\mathbb R^d$, with $\bar v=k^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^k v_i$. Then \[ \mathbb E\max_{1\le i\le k}\langle v_i,g\rangle \le\frac{3}{2\sqrt{2\pi}} \left(\sum_{i=1}^k\|v_i-\bar v\|^2\right)^{1/2}. \] The constant is sharp already for three vectors in the plane.

primaryStatements.name: Khot--Naor low-influence bound
primaryStatements.label: kc:kn-input
primaryStatements.text: For fixed \(k\) and every \(\eta>0\), there exists \(0<\tau_0<1/2\), independent of \(r\), such that every \(r\in\N\) and every \(f:\Omega^r\to\Delta_k\) satisfying \[ \Inf_j^{\le\log(1/\tau_0)}(f_i)\le\tau_0 \quad(i\in[k],\ j\in[r]) \] obey \(\OBJ(f)\le C_k+\eta\).

primaryStatements.name: Unique Games input
primaryStatements.label: kc:ug-input
primaryStatements.text: For every fixed \(\varepsilon,\delta\in(0,1/2)\), there are an integer \(s\ge1\) and a deterministic polynomial-time reduction from \(\mathrm{3SAT}\) to explicit unweighted simple bipartite Unique Games instances over \(\mathbb F_2^s\). If the formula is satisfiable the game has a labeling satisfying at least \(1-\varepsilon\) of its edges; if it is unsatisfiable every labeling satisfies at most \(\delta\) of its edges. The edge set is nonempty and each constraint is a translation of the alphabet. The alphabet size and the polynomial's degree and constants depend only on \(\varepsilon,\delta\).

lean.scopeText: The Gaussian propeller problem asks how large the sum of squared Gaussian first moments can be over a partition. The formalized result proves the sharp bound $9/(8\pi)$ for every positive dimension and every positive number of labelled cells, allowing empty cells and arbitrary masses. In dimension at least two with at least three cells, three planar sectors of angle $120^\circ$, extended in orthogonal directions, attain equality. The separate Gaussian-maxima and kernel-clustering consequences are not included.

papers.title: The Euclidean Steinitz–Bergström theorem
papers.abstract: Every prescribed-order finite sequence of vectors in the Euclidean unit ball of ℝd has one signing for which every signed prefix has norm at most $C\sqrt d$, with C absolute and independent of the sequence length. Consequently, every indexed zero-sum family of unit-ball vectors admits an ordering with the same bound for its unsigned partial sums. This determines the Euclidean Steinitz constant up to absolute factors, $S_2(d)=\Theta(\sqrt d)$, and resolves the Euclidean Steinitz–Bergström conjecture.
papers.familySummary: Proves that any finite sequence in the Euclidean unit ball of ℝd admits signs keeping every partial sum within $C\sqrt d$, independently of length. Consequently every zero-sum family can be reordered with the same bound on unsigned partial sums. A matching lower bound gives the optimal order $S_2(d)=\Theta(\sqrt d)$.

primaryStatements.label: thm:signing
primaryStatements.text: There is an absolute constant $C$ such that, for all integers $d,N\ge1$ and every sequence $v_1,\ldots,v_N\in\R^d$ with $\lVert v_i\rVert_2\le1$, there are signs $\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_N\in\{-1,1\}$ for which \[ \max_{0\le k\le N} \left\lVert\sum_{i=1}^k\varepsilon_i v_i\right\rVert_2\le C\sqrt d. \] The same signs control all prefixes, and $C$ is independent of $d$, $N$ and the sequence.

primaryStatements.name: Euclidean Steinitz--Bergstr\"om bound
primaryStatements.label: thm:steinitz
primaryStatements.text: There is an absolute constant $C$ such that, for all integers $d,N\ge1$ and every indexed family $v_1,\ldots,v_N\in\R^d$ satisfying $\lVert v_i\rVert_2\le1$ and $\sum_{i=1}^N v_i=0$, some permutation $\pi\in\mathfrak S_N$ satisfies \[ \max_{0\le k\le N}\left\lVert\sum_{i=1}^k v_{\pi(i)}\right\rVert_2 \le C\sqrt d. \] The constant in Theorem \ref{thm:signing} also suffices here.

primaryStatements.name: Signs with adaptive shifts
primaryStatements.label: prop:adaptive
primaryStatements.text: Let $K\subset\R^m$ be nonempty, bounded, open, convex and centrally symmetric. Suppose that \begin{equation} \lambda_Q(K)\le\kappa^2\tr Q \quad\text{for every positive definite diagonal }Q. \end{equation} Let $j_1,\ldots,j_s$ be distinct elements of $\{1,\ldots,m\}$, and let $q_i:\R^{i-1}\to[-\delta,\delta]$ be arbitrary functions, for $1\le i\le s$. There exist signs $\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_s$ such that the recursion \[ x^{(0)}=0,\qquad x^{(i)}=x^{(i-1)}+ \bigl(q_i(x^{(i-1)}_{j_1},\ldots,x^{(i-1)}_{j_{i-1}}) +\varepsilon_i\bigr)e_{j_i} \] has $x^{(s)}\in K$. For $i=1$, the function $q_1$ has a one-point domain.

primaryStatements.name: Energy of a filtered path body
primaryStatements.label: prop:filtered
primaryStatements.text: There are positive absolute constants $A_0,B_0,H_0$ with the following property. Let $d\ge1$ and $n\ge0$ be integers and put $m=d+n$. For $1\le t\le n$, let $C_t$ be an invertible real $d\times d$ matrix and let $b_t\in\R^d$ satisfy \[ C_tC_t^T+b_tb_t^T=I_d. \] Define linear maps $R_t:\R^m\to\R^d$ by \begin{equation} R_0x=(x_1,\ldots,x_d),\qquad R_tx=C_tR_{t-1}x+b_tx_{d+t}\quad(1\le t\le n). \end{equation} Then the bounded open convex centrally symmetric set \begin{equation} \mathcal D= \left\{x\in\R^m: \begin{array}{ll} |x_j|<B_0 & (1\le j\le m),\\ \lVert R_tx\rVert_2<A_0\sqrt d & (0\le t\le n) \end{array}\right\} \end{equation} satisfies \[ \lambda_Q(\mathcal D)\le H_0\tr Q \quad\text{for every positive definite diagonal }Q. \]

primaryStatements.name: Finite-dimensional $\ell_p$ bounds
primaryStatements.label: cor:lp-steinitz
primaryStatements.text: Let $1\le p\le\infty$, with $1/\infty=0$, and let $d,N\ge1$ be integers. Every sequence $v_1,\ldots,v_N\in\R^d$ with $\lVert v_i\rVert_p\le1$ admits signs $\varepsilon_i\in\{-1,1\}$ such that \[ \max_{0\le k\le N} \left\lVert\sum_{i=1}^k\varepsilon_i v_i\right\rVert_p \le C d^{\max\{1/p,\,1-1/p\}}. \] If additionally $\sum_{i=1}^N v_i=0$, there is a permutation $\pi\in\mathfrak S_N$ such that \[ \max_{0\le k\le N} \left\lVert\sum_{i=1}^k v_{\pi(i)}\right\rVert_p \le C d^{\max\{1/p,\,1-1/p\}}. \] Here $C$ is the same absolute constant as in Theorems \ref{thm:signing} and \ref{thm:steinitz}, independent of $p,d,N$. For $1\le p\le2$, both bounds have sharp dimension order $d^{1/p}$: for every $d$ there is a unit-ball sequence for which every signing has a prefix of norm at least $d^{1/p}$, and a finite indexed zero-sum unit-ball family for which every permutation has a prefix of norm at least $\tfrac13d^{1/p}$.

primaryStatements.name: Euclidean colorful Steinitz bound
primaryStatements.label: cor:colorful-steinitz
primaryStatements.text: Let $d,k,n\ge1$ be integers and let $a_i^j\in\R^d$, for $1\le j\le k$ and $1\le i\le n$, satisfy \[ \lVert a_i^j\rVert_2\le1, \qquad \sum_{j=1}^k\sum_{i=1}^n a_i^j=0. \] There is one tuple of permutations $(\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_k)\in\mathfrak S_n^k$ such that \[ \max_{0\le m\le n} \left\lVert\sum_{j=1}^k\sum_{i=1}^m a_{\pi_j(i)}^j\right\rVert_2 \le 2C\sqrt d, \] where $C$ is the absolute constant in Theorem \ref{thm:signing}. The same tuple works for every $m$ and may be chosen jointly from the whole array. Only the global total sum is assumed to vanish; the bound controls the displayed aggregate synchronous prefixes, not each row separately.

lean.scopeText: The formalized result gives the Euclidean Steinitz–Bergström bound with one absolute constant $C$. For every finite family of vectors in the unit ball of $\mathbb R^d$, signs can be chosen so that every prefix in the prescribed order has norm at most $C\sqrt d$. When the vector sum is zero, a permutation makes every unsigned prefix satisfy the same bound. Repeated and zero vectors are included. The result is existential and does not supply an online algorithm.

papers.title: A doubling Hilbert subset with no finite-dimensional bi-Lipschitz embedding
papers.abstract: Every infinite-dimensional real Banach space contains a compact doubling subset that admits no bi-Lipschitz embedding into any finite-dimensional real normed space. The doubling constant has a universal bound, independent of the ambient Banach space. This answers the Lang–Plaut problem negatively, even for compact subsets of Hilbert space.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: There is a fixed subset $S$ of real $\ell_2$, equipped with its induced Hilbert distance, whose doubling constant is at most $76800$ and which admits no bi-Lipschitz embedding into $\R^k$ for any positive integer $k$, at any finite distortion.

primaryStatements.label: prop:doubling
primaryStatements.text: The doubling constant of $S$ is at most $300\cdot16^2=76800$.

primaryStatements.label: prop:energy

primaryStatements.name: Finite-$p$ function-space obstruction
primaryStatements.label: cor:lp
primaryStatements.text: For every real $1\le p<\infty$, the fixed metric space $S$ of Theorem \ref{thm:main} is isometric to a subset $S_p$ of $L_p([0,1];\R)$, where $[0,1]$ carries Lebesgue measure. With its induced $L_p$ metric, $S_p$ has doubling constant at most $76800$ and admits no bi-Lipschitz embedding into any finite-dimensional real normed space at any finite distortion.

primaryStatements.name: Compact Banach-space obstruction
primaryStatements.label: cor:banach
primaryStatements.text: There is a universal constant $\Lambda$ such that every infinite-dimensional real Banach space $B$ contains a compact subset $K_B$ whose doubling constant is at most $\Lambda$ and which admits no bi-Lipschitz embedding into any finite-dimensional real normed space at any finite distortion. The subset $K_B$ may depend on $B$, but is chosen independently of the target dimension and distortion.

lean.scopeText: The formalized result gives a doubling subset of real $\ell_2$, with doubling constant at most $76800$, that admits no bi-Lipschitz embedding into any finite-dimensional Euclidean space at any finite distortion. A companion gives one universal doubling constant such that every infinite-dimensional real Banach space contains a compact doubling subset with no bi-Lipschitz embedding into any finite-dimensional normed space.

papers.title: Edit Distance in l1: Matching Bounds up to Constants in the Exponent
papers.abstract: We determine the exponential scale of the least ℓ1 distortion of unit-cost edit distance on all strings of length at most d. For every sufficiently large d, uniformly over finite alphabets of size at least two, the distortion lies between $\exp(c\sqrt{\log d\,\log\log d})$ and $\exp(C\sqrt{\log d\,\log\log d})$ for absolute constants $c,C\gt 0$. The lower bound already holds on binary strings of one common length. Thus the order of logarithmic distortion is sharp up to absolute constants.

Insertions, deletions and substitutions have unit cost. The constants are uniform over all finite alphabets with at least two symbols, even when the alphabet grows with d; binary words already force the lower bound.
