primaryStatements.label: can:theorem
primaryStatements.text:
There are constants $\delta>0$, $C<\infty$, $\gamma>0$, and $M_0<\infty$ such that, for every $M\ge M_0$, every $i\in\Z$, and every $n\in\N$,  egin{equation} \PP\left\{  egin{array}{l} \min igl(\log_M
orm{T_{i,i-n}}, \log_M
orm{T_{i,i+n}} igr)\ge(1-\delta)n,\[2pt] \log_M
orm{T_{i-n,i+n}}\le\delta n \end{array} ight\} \le C\exp(-\gamma n). \end{equation} All four constants are independent of the center, the length, and the parameter $M$ in the indicated range.

primaryStatements.name: Product estimate across a fast bridge
primaryStatements.label: bridge:theorem
primaryStatements.text: There are absolute constants $c_b\in(0,1)$, $\kappa>0$, and $\sigma>0$ with the following property. Fix observation bounds $(R,L,B)$ and a threshold $h>0$. For sufficiently large $M$ and sufficiently large $n=b-a$, let $W,H$ be observations with these bounds, with $W\geq0$. All indices occurring in one observation are within $\kappa n$ of $a$, and all indices occurring in the other are within $\kappa n$ of $b$. Either assignment of $W,H$ to the two ends is allowed. Then \begin{equation} \E\!\left[ \one_{\{\log_M\norm{T_{a,b}}\geq c_b n\}} W\one_{\{H>h\}} \right] \leq C\bigl(\E W+M^{-\sigma n}\bigr)\PP(H>h/2). \end{equation} The constants $c_b,\kappa,\sigma$ are independent of the observation bounds and threshold. The constant $C$ and the lower size requirements for $M,n$ may depend on $(R,L,B)$ and $h$, but not on the indices, the defining functions, or the bridge location.

primaryStatements.name: Limits away from affinity
primaryStatements.label: scale:limits
primaryStatements.text:
After passing to a subsequence, the restrictions of $\mu_K$ and $
u_K$ to $\mathcal U$ converge vaguely to locally finite nonnegative Borel measures $\mu$ and $
u$, respectively. Moreover,  egin{equation} \xi_K\longrightarrow0\quad\hbox{vaguely on }\mathcal U. \end{equation} The measures $\mu$ and $
u$ are supported on the closed class $X_0\subset X$ consisting of arrays satisfying $d(s,t)\le|s-t|$ and the inequalities  egin{equation} B_v(s,t)\ge\min\{B_v(s,p),B_v(p,t)\},\qquad B_v(s,t)=d(v,s)+d(v,t)-d(s,t) \end{equation} for every $v,s,t,p\in\mathcal D$. Every member of $X_0$ extends uniquely to a continuous semimetric on $\R$, obeying the same inequalities at all real arguments. Both limiting measures are invariant under \[ (	au_r d)(s,t)=d(s+r,t+r)\qquad(r\in\mathcal D). \] For every interval $I$ as in \cref{scale:local-mass},  egin{equation} \int(J(I)+V(I))\,\dd\mu<\infty, \qquad \int(h(I)+J(I)+V(I))\,\dd
u<\infty. \end{equation} In particular,  egin{equation} \int h([0,1])\,\dd
u\le1. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Positive dilation decomposition
primaryStatements.label: scale:decomposition
primaryStatements.text: On $\mathcal U$, with the measures supported on $X_0$ as above, \begin{equation} S_*\mu=\mu+\nu. \end{equation} There is a locally finite nonnegative measure $\mu_\infty$, invariant under $S$ and every dyadic translation, such that \begin{equation} \mu=\mu_\infty+\sum_{j=1}^{\infty}(S^{-j})_*\nu, \qquad S_*\mu_\infty=\mu_\infty. \end{equation} The series is a series of positive measures dominated by $\mu$.

primaryStatements.name: Support exclusions
primaryStatements.label: shape:exclusions
primaryStatements.text: There is a measurable set of full measure for $\mu$, $\nu$, and $\mu_\infty$ on which the following statements hold for every real choice of their arguments. \begin{enumerate} \item There do not exist $r\in\R$ and $t>0$ such that \begin{equation} d(r-t,r)>(1-\delta)t,\qquad d(r,r+t)>(1-\delta)t,\qquad d(r-t,r+t)<\delta t. \end{equation} \item If $s\in P_d$ and $t\in Q_d$, then \begin{equation} d(s,t)\le c_b|t-s|. \end{equation} \end{enumerate} The same statements hold almost everywhere for every positive measure appearing in the decomposition of \cref{scale:decomposition}.

primaryStatements.name: Shape classification
primaryStatements.label: shape:classification
primaryStatements.text: Every nonaffine array in $X_0$ satisfying \cref{shape:exclusions} has one of the following forms: \begin{enumerate} \item every secant has speed at most $c_b$; \item there is one exterior ray of exact unit speed, and the complementary closed half-line has all secant speeds at most $c_b$; \item there are two exterior rays of exact unit speed, separated by a closed interval $[a,b]$ of positive length, and every secant contained in $[a,b]$ has speed at most $c_b$. \end{enumerate} The second possibility includes either orientation. These descriptions do not assert additivity of distances across the slow part. The three temporal configurations are illustrated in \cref{shape:figure}.

definitions.label: can:good-definition
definitions.text: An index $2\le j\le N-2$ is good for the selected normalized solution if \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \tau_j-\tau_l&\ge c(j-l)&& (1\le l<j),\\ \tau_{j+1}-\tau_j&\ge c,\\ \upsilon_j-\upsilon_{j+1}&\ge c, &\upsilon_{j+1}-\upsilon_{j+2}&\ge c. \end{aligned} \end{equation} For a path extending beyond a selected index, the same inequalities define goodness without reference to a particular terminal length $N$.

lean.scopeText:
The formalization proves Sinai's positive-entropy conjecture for the standard sine map on the two-dimensional torus in the stronger form of a full positive parameter tail. For every sufficiently large parameter, normalized area has positive metric entropy, and a positive-area set has positive largest Lyapunov exponent with the stated derivative-growth limit.

It also constructs a positive-area invariant ergodic hyperbolic component. That component splits into finitely many cyclic pieces on each of which the corresponding iterate is Bernoulli. No genericity assumption on the parameter is used.

primaryStatements.name: Phase-foliation rigidity
primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Suppose a \(T\)-invariant open annulus \(U\subset M\) contains \((\R/L\mathbb Z)\times(0,\eta)\) for some \(\eta>0\). Suppose there is a homeomorphism \[ H:\mathbb S^1\times(0,1)\longrightarrow U \] whose leaves are essential simple closed curves, each individually invariant under \(T\). Then \(\Omega\) is an ellipse: there are \(c\in\R^2\) and a real symmetric positive-definite matrix \(Q\) such that \[ \Omega=\{x\in\R^2:(x-c)^TQ(x-c)<1\}. \] Circles are included.

primaryStatements.name: Physical-collar rigidity, {\citep[Definition 1.1 and Theorem 1.2
primaryStatements.label: thm:nb-rigidity
primaryStatements.text: {NB}}] A bounded strictly convex planar domain with \(C^\infty\) regular boundary of positive curvature and a continuous physical caustic collar is an ellipse.

primaryStatements.name: Regularity of a phase-foliated collar
primaryStatements.label: thm:collar-regularity
primaryStatements.text: Under the hypotheses of Theorem \ref{thm:main}, the boundary is real analytic. There are \(\lambda_0>0\) and a jointly real-analytic map \[ \Gamma:\mathbb T\times[0,\lambda_0]\longrightarrow\R^2 \] such that \(\Gamma(\cdot,0)\) parametrizes \(\partial\Omega\), every curve \(\Gamma(\cdot,\lambda)\) for \(0<\lambda\le\lambda_0\) is a regular strictly convex caustic, and the restriction to \(\mathbb T\times[0,\lambda_0)\) is a homeomorphism onto a relatively open collar of \(\partial\Omega\) in \(\overline\Omega\). Here real analyticity at the parameter endpoints means extension to a neighborhood.

primaryStatements.label: prop:graph-collar
primaryStatements.text: Every leaf in $U$ is a graph $p=g_b(\theta)$. After reversing $b$ if necessary, $g_b$ is strictly decreasing in $b$, jointly continuous in $(\theta,b)$, and converges uniformly to $h$ as $b\downarrow0$. The induced angular lifts \[ F_b=\theta_b\circ G_b\circ\theta_b^{-1} \] are strictly ordered with $b$ and have positive translation numbers tending to zero at that end. Every sufficiently small positive rational $l/q$ occurs on exactly one leaf, and on that entire leaf \begin{equation} F_b^q(\theta)=\theta+2\pi l. \end{equation} Here rotation number means translation number divided by $2\pi$.

primaryStatements.label: thm:analytic-boundary
primaryStatements.text: Under the hypotheses of Theorem \ref{thm:main}, the support function \(h\) and the boundary of the table are real analytic.

primaryStatements.name: Stationary meshes, {\cite[Lemma 2.3
primaryStatements.label: prop:mesh-input
primaryStatements.text: {NB}}] Fix an integer \(m\ge2\) and a finite bound \(M\), and put \(p=m+2\), \(r_0=m+15\). There are \(R,K,N\), depending only on \(m,M\), with the following properties. For \(0\le\sigma\le1\), \(\|f\|_{r_0,\sigma}\le M\), and \(q\ge N\), the action \(D_f\) has an interior-stationary mesh with endpoints \(X_0=x\), \(X_q=x+2\pi\), of the form \[ X_j(x)=x+2\pi j/q+w_j(x),\qquad w_0=w_q=0. \] On the strip of width \(\sigma'=(1-K/q^2)\sigma\), \begin{equation} q^2\max_j\|w_j\|_{p,\sigma'}+ q^3\max_j\|w_{j+1}-w_j\|_{p,\sigma'}\le R. \end{equation} The mesh is real symmetric and differentiable in smooth real input variations; its derivative in the norm on the left of \eqref{ana:mesh-bounds} is bounded by \(C\|\dot f\|_{r_0,\sigma}\). The corresponding difference bound holds for two inputs. On the real axis the mesh is pointwise unique in the ball with these scaled position and step bounds. Any fixed enlargement of that real uniqueness ball is allowed after increasing \(N\).

primaryStatements.name: Fourier rows, {\cite[Proposition 2.4
primaryStatements.label: prop:row-input
primaryStatements.text: {NB}}] For fixed \(m\ge2\), \(M<\infty\), and \(r_0=m+15\), there are \(K,N\), independent of \(0\le\sigma\le1\), such that for \(\|f\|_{r_0,\sigma}\le M\) and \(|n|\ge N\), \begin{equation} (\dd C_n)_f(v)=[b_n(f)v]_n, \end{equation} where \begin{align} \|b_n(f)-1\|_{m,(1-K/n^2)\sigma}&\le K/|n|, \\ \|b_n(f)-b_n(\widehat f)\|_{m,(1-K/n^2)\sigma} &\le (K/|n|)\|f-\widehat f\|_{r_0,\sigma}. \end{align} The second estimate holds for two inputs with the same bound. The derivative identity holds for smooth real variations and for real-symmetric holomorphic variations with the indicated finite norms.

primaryStatements.label: ana:glancing-interface
primaryStatements.text: For the actual table, \(D=D_u\) is real symmetric and holomorphic in a uniform neighborhood of the real diagonal. It is diagonally \(2\pi\)-periodic and antisymmetric, and satisfies \begin{equation} D(x,x+b)=-\frac{b^3}{24}+O(b^5),\qquad D_1(x,x+b)=\frac{b^2}{8}+O(b^4), \end{equation} locally uniformly with each fixed number of derivatives.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: If \(\Omega\) has a continuous caustic collar, then \(\Omega\) is an ellipse. Equivalently, there are \(c\in\R^2\) and a real symmetric positive-definite matrix \(Q\) such that \[ \Omega=\{x\in\R^2:(x-c)^TQ(x-c)<1\}. \] Circles are included.

primaryStatements.name: Analytic regularity
primaryStatements.label: thm:analytic
primaryStatements.text: Under the hypotheses of \Cref{thm:main}, the support function of the table and its boundary are real analytic.

primaryStatements.label: prop:high-frequency-estimate
primaryStatements.text: For each integer \(m\ge2\) and \(M<\infty\), take \(r_0=m+15\). There are constants \(K,N\), independent of \(0\le\sigma\le1\), such that, whenever \(\|u\|_{r_0,\sigma}\le M\) and \(|n|\ge N\), the derivative of \Cref{ana:constraint-definition} has the form \begin{equation} (\dd C_n)_u(v)=[b_n(u)v]_n. \end{equation} Here \begin{equation} \|b_n(u)-1\|_{m,(1-K/n^2)\sigma}\le\frac{K}{|n|}, \end{equation} and, for two such inputs on the same strip, \begin{equation} \|b_n(u)-b_n(\widetilde u)\|_{m,(1-K/n^2)\sigma} \le\frac{K}{|n|}\|u-\widetilde u\|_{r_0,\sigma}. \end{equation} The derivative identity holds for smooth real variations, and for real-symmetric holomorphic variations with the indicated finite norms.

primaryStatements.label: ana:analytic-action-interface
primaryStatements.text: For the actual table, the normalized action in \Cref{ana:normalized-action} is holomorphic in a neighborhood of the real diagonal, diagonally \(2\pi\)-periodic, and antisymmetric. It satisfies \[ D(X,X+T)=-T^3/24+O(T^5),\qquad D_1(X,X+T)=T^2/8+O(T^4), \] locally uniformly with all fixed derivatives. The unique rational graphs and their identities in \Cref{lem:rational-periodicity} are available for every sufficiently small positive reduced \(l/q\).

primaryStatements.name: Joint glancing parametrization
primaryStatements.label: thm:joint-parametrization
primaryStatements.text: There are \(s,r_1>0\), with \(r_1<s\), and a real-symmetric holomorphic function \(U(y,t)\) on \[ \{(y,t):|\Im y|<2s,\ |t|<r_1\} \] such that \(U-y\) is \(2\pi\)-periodic in \(y\), \(U\) is even in \(t\), \(U(y,0)=y\), and \begin{equation} D_1\bigl(U(y,t),U(y+t,t)\bigr) +D_2\bigl(U(y-t,t),U(y,t)\bigr)=0 \end{equation} for \(|\Im y|<s\), \(|t|<r_1\). Here real symmetry means \(U(\bar y,\bar t)=\overline{U(y,t)}\). Set \begin{equation} \Theta(y,t)=\phi(U(y,t)),\qquad p(y,t)=-\mathcal S_1\bigl(\Theta(y,t),\Theta(y+t,t)\bigr). \end{equation} On a possibly smaller product neighborhood, both functions are holomorphic, real-symmetric, and even in \(t\). For positive small real \(t\), the billiard map sends the line \((\Theta(y,t),p(y,t))\) to the line \((\Theta(y+t,t),p(y+t,t))\). The variables \((y,t^2)\) give analytic coordinates on a full one-sided phase collar. Moreover, \begin{equation} dp\wedge d\Theta=A(t)\,dy\wedge dt, \qquad A(t)=\frac{c}{4}t+O(t^3), \end{equation} where \(A\) is holomorphic and real on the real axis. In particular \(t^2\) is a nondegenerate analytic first integral on that collar.

primaryStatements.name: A Newton step across all retained resonances
primaryStatements.label: prop:joint-newton
primaryStatements.text: There are constants \(C,B_0\), depending only on the fixed action domain and the fixed smallness bounds above, with the following property. Suppose \(U\) is real-symmetric, even in \(t\), and \(U-y\) is periodic, and \[ \|E(U)\|_{\mathcal D^1_0}\le\eps<1. \] Let \(N\ge1\) satisfy \(e^{-N\delta}\le\eps\), and put \(Q=1+N+\delta^{-1}\). If \(CQ^{B_0}\eps\) is sufficiently small, there is a real-symmetric, even correction \(\Delta U\), periodic in \(y\), such that \begin{align} \max_{0\le j\le3}\|\partial_y^j\Delta U\|_{\mathcal D^0_{20}} &\le CQ^{B_0}\eps,\\ \|E(U+\Delta U)\|_{\mathcal D^1_{20}} &\le CQ^{B_0}\eps^2. \end{align} The exponent \(B_0\) is fixed; it is independent of \(N\), the retained rationals, and the order of any formal approximation used to initialize the iteration.

primaryStatements.name: Line-endpoint determination
primaryStatements.label: thm:lens-lines
primaryStatements.text: Fix an integer \(k\ge2\), and put \(L_i=L(y+it,t)\). Every intermediate line \(L_i\), \(0<i<k\), is algebraic over the differential field generated by \(L_0,L_k\). For each fixed \(k\), finitely many endpoint derivatives suffice. The same assertion holds for translated index intervals. All derivatives of the intermediate fields are algebraic over the corresponding endpoint differential field.

primaryStatements.name: Point-endpoint determination
primaryStatements.label: thm:lens-points
primaryStatements.text: Let \(k\ge2\), and put \(P_i=X(y+it,t)\), \(0\le i\le k\). Every intermediate point and every edge of this chain is algebraic over the differential field generated by \(P_0,P_k\) and the analytic coefficient \(A(t)\) in \[ \dd p\wedge\dd\Theta=A(t)\,\dd y\wedge\dd t. \] For each fixed \(k\), finitely many jets suffice. The assertion persists under translation and analytic continuation.

definitions.name: A continuous caustic collar
definitions.label: def:caustic-collar
definitions.text: Let \(\Omega\subset\R^2\) be a bounded strictly convex domain whose boundary is a \(C^\infty\) simple closed regular curve with positive curvature. A smooth closed convex caustic is a \(C^\infty\) simple closed regular curve in \(\Omega\), bounding a strictly convex set, such that a billiard segment tangent to the curve remains tangent after reflection at either endpoint. Here reflection of an incoming unit velocity \(v\) at a boundary point with outward unit normal \(n\) is \[ v\longmapsto v-2(v\cdot n)n. \] A continuous caustic collar consists of a relatively open set \(A\subset\overline\Omega\) containing \(\partial\Omega\) and a homeomorphism \[ H_0:\mathbb S^1\times[0,1)\longrightarrow A \] such that \(H_0(\mathbb S^1\times\{0\})=\partial\Omega\), and \(H_0(\mathbb S^1\times\{b\})\) is a smooth closed convex caustic for every \(0<b<1\).

definitions.label: cont:width-definition
definitions.text: For \(F=L\) or \(F=X\), let \(h_F(t)\) be the supremum of the heights \(b>s_*\) for which the primary branch of \(F\) has a single-valued meromorphic extension to \[ \{-s_*<\Im y<b\}\times V \] for some open neighborhood \(V\subset B\) of \(t\), agreeing with the initial branch on the basic strip. The neighborhood \(V\) may depend on \(b\). The value \(+\infty\) is allowed.

definitions.label: critical:def:envelope
definitions.text: An envelope is a function \(N:[k_0,\infty)\to[1,\infty)\) for which there are fixed constants \(C_N\ge1\), \(0\le\beta<1/2\), and \(a>0\) such that \begin{equation} \frac{N(j)}{N(k)}\le C_N \begin{cases} e^{\beta(k-j)},& k_0\le j\le k,\\ e^{a(j-k)},& j\ge k. \end{cases} \end{equation}

lean.scopeText:
The formalization proves $\dim_H\mu=\min\{1,h_{\mathrm{RW}}/\chi\}$ for the lower Hausdorff dimension of every finite real self-similar probability measure with positive weights and nonzero contraction ratios of absolute value below one. Here $h_{\mathrm{RW}}$ is the entropy rate of random affine compositions and $\chi$ is the corresponding Lyapunov exponent in the same logarithmic base. Ratios may be signed and unequal, and exact overlaps are allowed.

It also gives two consequences without exact overlaps: the usual entropy-over-Lyapunov formula for a common positive contraction ratio, and the attractor formula $\dim_H K=\min\{1,s\}$, where $s\ge0$ is the unique solution of $\sum_i|r_i|^s=1$. Absolute continuity is outside these statements.

papers.title: Uniform Permanence in Weakly Reversible Mass-Action Systems
papers.abstract: We prove the permanence conjecture for finite weakly reversible mass-action systems with fixed positive reaction rates. Every positive stoichiometric compatibility class admits one compact convex forward-invariant set that every positive trajectory in that class enters in finite time, even when the class is unbounded. The set depends only on the network, the rates, and the class; the entry time may depend on the initial state. Thus, after its entry time, every concentration satisfies the same positive lower and finite upper bounds throughout that class.

sections.title: A common absorbing set for each class

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let $C\subset\Z_{\geq0}^d$ be finite, let $R\subset C\times C$ be weakly reversible, and fix positive rate constants in \eqref{eq:mass-action}. For every positive stoichiometric class $P$ there is a nonempty compact convex set $K_P\subset P$ with the following properties. Every initial point $x^0\in P$ gives a unique global positive solution, and there is a finite $T(x^0)\geq0$ such that \[ x(t)\in K_P\qquad(t\geq T(x^0)). \] Moreover, $K_P$ is forward invariant. In particular, there is $\eps_P\in(0,1)$, depending only on the network, the fixed rates, and $P$, such that every such solution satisfies \begin{equation} \eps_P\leq x_i(t)\leq\eps_P^{-1} \qquad(1\leq i\leq d,\ t\geq T(x^0)). \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Uniform activity bound
primaryStatements.label: cor:activity
primaryStatements.text: Let $m\geq1$, $a<b$, and $E:[a,b]^m\to(0,\infty)$ be as in Lemma \ref{lem:affine}. Fix a family $\Lambda$ supplied by that lemma. There is $h_0\in(0,1)$ such that, for every $0<h<h_0$ and every $p\in[a,b]^m$, each label $\lambda\in\Lambda$ active at $X_h(p)$ satisfies \[ \norm{p-r_\lambda}_\infty<E(r_\lambda). \]

primaryStatements.name: The compact plateau
primaryStatements.label: prop:plateau
primaryStatements.text: For $0<h\leq h_P$, let \[ M_h=F_h(c), \qquad K_h=\{x\in\R^d:F_h(x)=M_h\}. \] There is a constant label with value $M_h$, and $F_h\leq M_h$ on $\R^d$. The set $K_h$ is nonempty, compact, and convex, and \begin{equation} K_h\subset\operatorname{int}B_{\sqrt h}. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Increase of active affine functions
primaryStatements.label: prop:increase
primaryStatements.text: Fix $0<h\leq h_P$. For every $x\in B_h$ and every $\lambda\in A_h(x)$, \begin{equation} r_\lambda\cdot f(x)\geq0, \qquad r_\lambda\cdot f(x)>0\quad\text{if }r_\lambda\notin S^\perp. \end{equation} Moreover, there is a number $\delta_h>0$ such that \begin{equation} r_\lambda\cdot f(x)\geq\delta_h \quad\text{whenever }x\in B_h,\ \lambda\in A_h(x), \ r_\lambda\notin S^\perp. \end{equation} At every point of $P\setminus K_h$, all active slopes lie outside $S^\perp$. In particular, \eqref{eq:uniform-active-increase} applies to every active label at each $x\in B_h\cap(P\setminus K_h)$.

papers.title: Boundedness and persistence of weakly reversible mass-action systems
papers.abstract: We prove the boundedness and persistence conjectures for finite weakly reversible mass-action systems with positive constant reaction rates. For every positive initial condition, the solution exists for all forward time, and every concentration remains bounded above and bounded away from zero. The bounds may depend on the initial condition, and no boundedness assumption is imposed on its stoichiometric compatibility class.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let $d\ge1$, let $\mathcal C\subset\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^d$ be finite, let $\mathcal R$ be weakly reversible, and let all reaction rates be positive constants. For every $x^0\in\R_{>0}^d$, the solution of \eqref{eq:mass-action} with $x(0)=x^0$ exists for every $t\ge0$. There is a number $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, depending on the network, the rates, and $x^0$, such that \begin{equation} \varepsilon\le x_i(t)\le\varepsilon^{-1} \qquad(t\ge0,\ 1\le i\le d). \end{equation}

primaryStatements.label: cor:uniform-affine
primaryStatements.text: Let $m\ge1$, $a<b$, and $E:[a,b]^m\to(0,\infty)$ be as in Lemma \ref{lem:affine}. Fix a finite nonempty family $\{(r_\lambda,c_\lambda):\lambda\in\Lambda\}$ supplied by that Lemma. Here forward invariance means that every solution starting in $K$ exists for all forward time and stays in $K$.

primaryStatements.label: cor:positive-equilibrium
primaryStatements.text: For every finite weakly reversible mass-action network with positive constant rates and every $x^0\in\R_{>0}^d$, there is an equilibrium $x^*\in(x^0+S)\cap\R_{>0}^d$.

lean.scopeText: The boundedness and persistence conjectures for mass-action systems ask whether positive concentrations remain finite and separated from zero. The formalization proves this for every finite weakly reversible reaction network with positive constant reaction rates and every strictly positive initial state. A global forward solution exists, and one $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ bounds every concentration of every global forward solution between $\varepsilon$ and $\varepsilon^{-1}$ for all nonnegative times. The bound may depend on the network, rates, and initial state.

primaryStatements.text: Let \(Q\) be the interior of a nondegenerate Euclidean triangle with angles \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma\). Suppose that at least one of \[ \alpha/\pi,\qquad \beta/\pi,\qquad \gamma/\pi \] is irrational. The unit-speed billiard flow \(\Phi_t\), with specular reflection at the open sides, is ergodic on \(Q\times S^1\) for the probability measure \[ d\mu=\frac{dA\,d\theta}{2\pi\operatorname{Area}(Q)}. \] Here trajectories hitting a vertex in either time direction are discarded. primaryStatements.label: cor:quantum
primaryStatements.text: Let \(Q\) satisfy the hypotheses of Theorem \ref{thm:main}, and fix either Dirichlet (\(B=D\)) or Neumann (\(B=N\)) boundary conditions. Let \((u_j)_{j\ge1}\) be any complete orthonormal eigenbasis of \(L^2(Q)\) for the corresponding Laplacian, with \[ -\Delta_B u_j=\lambda_j^2u_j,\qquad 0\le\lambda_1\le\lambda_2\le\cdots, \] where frequencies are listed with multiplicity. A set \(S\subset\mathbb N\) has density one if \(\#(S\cap\{1,\ldots,N\})/N\to1\). Then the following conclusions hold. \begin{enumerate} \item There is a density-one set \(S_{\mathrm{int}}\) such that, for every classical order-zero pseudodifferential operator \(A\) whose Schwartz kernel is compactly supported in \(Q\times Q\), \[ \lim_{\substack{j\to\infty\\j\in S_{\mathrm{int}}}} \langle Au_j,u_j\rangle_{L^2(Q)} =\int_{Q\times S^1}\sigma_0(A)\dd\mu. \] Here the Euclidean metric identifies unit covectors with \(Q\times S^1\), and \(\sigma_0(A)\) is restricted to them. \item Let \(\Gamma\) be the regular boundary, the union of the three open sides. For \(\lambda_j>0\), let \(h_j=\lambda_j^{-1}\) and define the Cauchy data on the open sides by \[ u_j^b=\begin{cases} h_j\,\partial_\nu u_j|_\Gamma,&B=D,\\ u_j|_\Gamma,&B=N, \end{cases} \] where \(\nu\) is the outward unit normal. Write \(B^*\Gamma=\{(s,\eta)\in T^*\Gamma:|\eta|<1\}\), using arc length \(s\) and signed tangential covector \(\eta\) on each side. There is a density-one set \(S_\partial\subset\{j:\lambda_j>0\}\) such that, for every \(a\in C_c^\infty(T^*\Gamma)\) and a properly supported order-zero semiclassical quantization \(A_h=\operatorname{Op}_h(a)\), \[ \lim_{\substack{j\to\infty\\j\in S_\partial}} \langle A_{h_j}u_j^b,u_j^b\rangle_{L^2(\Gamma)} =\frac{2}{\pi\operatorname{Area}(Q)} \int_{B^*\Gamma}a(s,\eta)w_B(\eta)\dd s\,d\eta, \] where \[ w_D(\eta)=\sqrt{1-\eta^2},\qquad w_N(\eta)=(1-\eta^2)^{-1/2}. \] The Cauchy data are not further normalized to have unit boundary norm. \item If the eigenbasis is real-valued, there is a density-one set \(S_{\mathrm{nod}}\) such that the number of nodal domains of \(u_j\), the connected components of \(Q\setminus\{u_j=0\}\), tends to infinity as \(\lambda_j\to\infty\) with \(j\in S_{\mathrm{nod}}\). \end{enumerate}

papers.title: A C^1 Counterexample to the Entropy Conjecture
papers.abstract: We disprove the general C1 self-map formulation of Shub's entropy conjecture. lean.scopeText: Shub's entropy conjecture predicts that a smooth self-map's topological entropy is at least the logarithm of the spectral radius of its action on real homology. The formalization gives a counterexample to the general $C^1$ self-map version: a noninvertible $C^1$ map on a compact smooth manifold without boundary has topological entropy zero, while its action on second real homology has a nonzero eigenvector with eigenvalue $2$. Thus the homological lower bound is strictly positive and fails for this map.

primaryStatements.name: Good finite orbit segments
primaryStatements.label: prop:good-frames
primaryStatements.text: For each $\eta>0$ there is a positive sequence $(b_k)_{k\geq1}$ with \begin{equation} b_k\geq 2^{-k/10}, \qquad \sum_{k\geq1}b_k^2<\infty, \end{equation} and compact sets $\widetilde{\mathcal G}_k\subset\mathcal F M$ and $\mathcal G_k=\pi(\widetilde{\mathcal G}_k)\subset M$ such that \[ \widetilde\nu(\widetilde{\mathcal G}_k)\geq1-\eta/100, \qquad \nu(\mathcal G_k)\geq1-\eta/100. \] For $n=2^k$, $b=b_k$, and $e\in\widetilde{\mathcal G}_k$, define \[ A_t=R(\widetilde S^t e)\quad(-n\leq t<n), \qquad \lambda_j=\frac1{2n}\sum_{t=-n}^{n-1}\ln(A_t)_{jj}. \] Then for every $j$ and every integer $-n\leq u\leq n$, \begin{equation} \left|\sum_{t=-n}^{u-1}\ln(A_t)_{jj} -(u+n)\lambda_j\right|\leq bn. \end{equation} Consequently, on every subinterval $-n\leq u\leq v\leq n$, \begin{equation} \left|\sum_{t=u}^{v-1}\ln(A_t)_{jj} -(v-u)\lambda_j\right|\leq2bn. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Finite-interval splitting
primaryStatements.label: prop:finite-splitting
primaryStatements.text: Fix $d\geq1$ and $A_*>1$. There is a constant $C$, depending only on these two quantities, with the following properties. Let $n\geq2$, $b>0$, and $\ln(2n+1)\leq bn$. Suppose that $A_t$, $-n\leq t<n$, are upper triangular with positive diagonal and \[ \|A_t\|,\ \|A_t^{-1}\|\leq A_*, \qquad \left|\sum_{t=-n}^{u-1}\ln(A_t)_{jj} -(u+n)\lambda_j\right|\leq bn \] for $-n\leq u\leq n$ and $1\leq j\leq d$, where $\lambda_j=(2n)^{-1}\sum_{t=-n}^{n-1}\ln(A_t)_{jj}$. First, order the rates as $\lambda_{(1)}\geq\cdots\geq\lambda_{(d)}$. For every $0\leq q\leq d$ and every $-n\leq s\leq t\leq n$, \begin{equation} \left|\ln\|\mathord{\bigwedge}^q A(t,s)\| -(t-s)\sum_{j=1}^q\lambda_{(j)}\right|\leq Cbn. \end{equation} The analogous estimate for $A(s,t)$ uses the $q$ largest members of $\{-\lambda_1,\ldots,-\lambda_d\}$. Next, suppose that real $\gamma$ and $g>0$ separate all the rates: each $\lambda_j$ is at most $\gamma-g$ or at least $\gamma+g$. Let $F$ be the set of indices in the second group, let $p=|F|$, and put \[ \Lambda=\sum_{j\in F}\lambda_j,\qquad \Omega=-\sum_{j\notin F}\lambda_j. \] There are decompositions $\R^d=E_t^s\oplus E_t^f$, $-n\leq t\leq n$, invariant under each $A_t$, with $\dim E_t^f=p$, whose two projections have norm at most $e^{Cbn}$. For $s\leq t$ and $l=t-s$ they satisfy \begin{align} \|A(t,s)|E_s^s\|&\leq e^{(\gamma-g)l+Cbn}, & \|A(s,t)|E_t^f\|&\leq e^{-(\gamma+g)l+Cbn}, \\ \|\mathord{\bigwedge}^p A(t,s)\|&\leq e^{\Lambda l+Cbn}, & e^{\Lambda l-Cbn}\leq J_p(A(t,s)|E_s^f)&\leq e^{\Lambda l+Cbn}, \\ \|\mathord{\bigwedge}^{d-p} A(s,t)\|&\leq e^{\Omega l+Cbn}, & e^{\Omega l-Cbn}\leq J_{d-p}(A(s,t)|E_t^s)&\leq e^{\Omega l+Cbn}. \end{align} If $0<p<d$ and at least one of $v_1,\ldots,v_p$ belongs to $E_s^s$, then \begin{equation} \|A(t,s)v_1\wedge\cdots\wedge A(t,s)v_p\| \leq e^{(\Lambda-2g)l+Cbn}\prod_{j=1}^p\|v_j\|. \end{equation} The backward analogue has exterior degree $d-p$, exponent $(\Omega-2g)l+Cbn$, and at least one factor in $E_t^f$. When a group is empty its space is $\{0\}$, all statements on that space are vacuous, and the exterior-degree-zero conventions apply.

primaryStatements.label: prop:words
primaryStatements.text: Choose $s_1$ so that $K_1\ge256$, and define the parameters by \eqref{eq:word-parameters}--\eqref{eq:word-recursion}. There are families $\mathcal W_i\subset\mathcal A^{m_i}$ of cardinality $L_i$, with $\mathcal W_1=\mathcal A$, such that every $w\in\mathcal W_{i+1}$ is a concatenation of $N_i$ members of $\mathcal W_i$ and the following properties hold. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(W\arabic*)},ref=W\arabic*,leftmargin=*] \itemRelations within groups. The paper asks whether a measure-preserving system can be represented by a smooth diffeomorphism preserving positive smooth volume. The formalized supporting result constructs an ergodic invertible transformation of a standard nonatomic probability space with finite Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy that has no such model on any compact finite-dimensional manifold, including manifolds with smooth boundary. The comparison is measurable conjugacy after discarding null sets.

The linked statement gives finite entropy; the paper's stronger zero-entropy conclusion is outside this statement.

papers.title: Arithmetic classification and non-Pisot singularity for Bernoulli convolutions
papers.abstract: We give an arithmetic classification of singular and absolutely continuous unbiased Bernoulli convolutions for every parameter $\lambda\in(0,1)$. The criterion is expressed through one-sided approximation by explicitly defined finite sets of algebraic units; it is an infinite approximation condition, not a finite membership algorithm. primaryStatements.name: Arithmetic criterion
primaryStatements.label: cls:classification
primaryStatements.text: Define the parameter set \begin{equation} \mathcal C=(0,1/2)\ \cup\ \left[(1/2,1)\cap \bigcup_{d\geq2}\ \bigcap_{j\geq1}\ \limsup_{n\to\infty} \bigcup_{r\in R_*(n,d,j)}[r-4^{-n},r)\right]. \end{equation} For every $\lambda\in(0,1)$, the measure $\nu_\lambda$ is singular if and only if $\lambda\in\mathcal C$, and is absolutely continuous if and only if $\lambda\notin\mathcal C$. Replacing $\limsup$ by $\liminf$ in \eqref{cls:criterion} gives the same set.

primaryStatements.name: Many close prefixes with opposite first bits
primaryStatements.label: cls:cross-pairs
primaryStatements.text: If $\mu_\lambda$ is singular, there are constants $a\in(0,L/2)$ and $c>0$, depending only on $\lambda$, with the following property. For every $Q>1$ and all sufficiently large $n$, at least $c2^n$ words $u\in\{0,1\}^n$ with $u_0=0$ each have at least $Q(2\lambda)^n$ distinct neighbors $v\in\{0,1\}^n$ such that \begin{equation} v_0=1, \qquad |s_u-s_v|\leq(L-a)\lambda^n. \end{equation} The constants $a,c$ are independent of $Q$ and $n$.

primaryStatements.name: Realization of a polynomial prefix
primaryStatements.label: cls:realization
primaryStatements.text: Fix $\lambda\in(1/2,1)$ and $a\in(0,L)$, where $L=(1-\lambda)^{-1}$. There is an integer $d_0$ such that, for each integer $d\geq d_0$ and all sufficiently large $n$, the following assertion holds uniformly over $w\in\{-1,0,1\}^n$. If \begin{equation} w_0=-1, \qquad \left|\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}w_i\lambda^i\right| \leq(L-a)\lambda^n, \end{equation} then some $r\in R(n,d)$ satisfies \[ \lambda<r\leq\lambda+\tfrac12 4^{-n}, \qquad \pi_n(p_r)=w. \]

primaryStatements.name: Garsia parameters, \cite{Garsia1962}
primaryStatements.label: cls:garsia
primaryStatements.text: Let $\beta\in(1,2)$ be an algebraic integer of absolute norm $2$ whose conjugates all have modulus greater than $1$. Then $1/\beta\notin \mathcal C$, and $\nu_{1/\beta}$ is absolutely continuous.

primaryStatements.name: Reciprocal Pisot parameters, \cite{Erdos1939}
primaryStatements.label: cls:pisot
primaryStatements.text: If $\beta\in(1,2)$ is a Pisot number, then $1/\beta\in\mathcal C$, and $\nu_{1/\beta}$ is singular.

primaryStatements.label: sal:examples
primaryStatements.text: Let $\beta_1$ and $\beta_2$ be the respective real roots greater than one of \[ P_1(x)=x^4-x^3-x^2-x+1, \qquad P_2(x)=x^4-2x^3+x^2-2x+1. \] Then $\beta_1,\beta_2\in(1,2)$ and both $\nu_{1/\beta_1}$ and $\nu_{1/\beta_2}$ are singular.

papers.title: Pointwise Multiple Ergodic Averages for Mixing Transformations
papers.abstract: Let T be an invertible mixing probability-preserving transformation. For every integer n ≥ 2 and every fixed tuple of bounded measurable functions, we prove that the consecutive multiple ergodic averages of length n converge almost everywhere to the product of the integrals, as the averaging length tends to infinity through all positive integers. The probability space need not be standard, and no rate of mixing is required.
papers.familySummary: Proves almost-everywhere convergence of consecutive multiple ergodic averages of every finite length for invertible mixing probability-preserving transformations. For each fixed tuple of bounded functions, the limit is the product of their integrals, along all positive averaging lengths. No mixing rate or standardness assumption on the probability space is required.

For every integer $n\ge2$ and every fixed tuple of bounded measurable functions, we prove that the consecutive multiple ergodic averages of length $n$ converge almost everywhere to the product of the integrals, as the averaging length tends to infinity through all positive integers. The probability space need not be standard, and no rate of mixing is required.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Suppose that $T$ satisfies \eqref{eq:mixing}. For every integer $n\ge2$ and every fixed $f_1,\ldots,f_n\in L^\infty(\mu)$, \[ A_N(f_1,\ldots,f_n)(x) \longrightarrow\prod_{j=1}^n\int_X f_j\dd\mu \qquad\text{for $\mu$-almost every }x, \] as $N$ tends to infinity through all positive integers. The probability space need not be standard, and no rate of mixing is required.

primaryStatements.name: Higher-order mixing, companion input
primaryStatements.label: thm:multiple-mixing
primaryStatements.text: Let $T$ be an invertible mixing probability-preserving transformation. For any fixed $s\ge2$, $g_1,\ldots,g_s\in L^\infty(\mu)$, and integer times $t_1,\ldots,t_s$, \[ \int_X\prod_{j=1}^s g_j(T^{t_j}x)\dd\mu(x) \longrightarrow\prod_{j=1}^s\int_Xg_j\dd\mu \quad\text{as}\quad \min_{i\ne j}|t_i-t_j|\longrightarrow\infty. \] For $s=1$ the equality holds for every time.

primaryStatements.name: Smooth triple averages, companion input
primaryStatements.label: prop:smooth-input
primaryStatements.text: Let $R$ be any invertible probability-preserving transformation, and let $b_1,b_2,b_3$ be distinct nonzero integers with greatest common divisor one. For bounded $g_1,g_2,g_3$ and every averaging profile, \[ V_k^\varphi(y)=\sum_{l\in\Z}2^{-k}\varphi(l/2^k) \prod_{j=1}^3g_j(R^{b_jl}y) \] converges almost everywhere as $k\to\infty$. Moreover, for each $c\in[1,2]$ and $\epsilon>0$ there is such a profile with \[ \norm{\varphi-c^{-1}\mathbf1_{(0,c]}}_{L^1(\R)}<\epsilon. \]

primaryStatements.name: Relative structure
primaryStatements.label: prop:structure
primaryStatements.text: The following statements hold for standard probability-preserving systems, without an ergodicity assumption. \begin{enumerate} \item Every system $Y$ has a maximal measure-distal factor $W_Y$, and $Y\to W_Y$ is relatively weakly mixing. Every distal factor pulls into the maximal distal factor of an extension. Automorphisms commuting with the transformation preserve $W_Y$. \item Factors and joinings of distal systems are distal. A distal system is relatively distal over each of its factors. Distality is equivalent for a transformation and any of its nonzero integer powers. \item Relative weak mixing passes to nonzero integer powers. The conditional product of relatively weakly mixing fibre laws over an invariant joining of their base laws is relatively weakly mixing over that joining. \item A relatively weakly mixing extension and a relatively distal extension of the same base are relatively disjoint: every invariant joining identifying their bases is the conditional product over that base. \item For a distal transformation $R$, every $d\ge1$, and bounded $g_1,\ldots,g_d$, the averages \[ \frac1N\sum_{l=1}^N\prod_{i=1}^d g_i\circ R^{il} \] converge almost everywhere. \end{enumerate} For a flow, the maximal distal factor of time one is preserved by the flow, and its action at every nonzero rational time is distal.

primaryStatements.name: Selected joining laws
primaryStatements.label: prop:selected-law
primaryStatements.text: Every flow $Y$ over $C$ has a unique probability law $\lambda_Y$ on $Y^I$ satisfying, for all bounded measurable functions $G_i$ on $Y$, \begin{equation} \int_{Y^I}\prod_{i\in I}G_i(y_i)\,\dd\lambda_Y =\lim_{a\to\mathcal U}\int_Y\frac1{N_a(\pi_Yy)} \int_0^{N_a(\pi_Yy)}\prod_{i\in I}G_i(S_Y^{it}y) \,\dd t\,\dd m_Y(y). \end{equation} Its marginals are $m_Y$, and it is invariant under $(y_i)_i\mapsto(S_Y^{it}y_i)_i$, $t\in\R$. If $\rho:Y'\to Y$ is an extension over $C$, then $(\rho^I)_*\lambda_{Y'}=\lambda_Y$. Countable inverse limits of extensions over $C$ exist in this category. The selected law at such a limit projects to the selected law at every stage. Pullbacks of the stage selected-law spaces have dense union in $L^2$ of the limit selected law.

primaryStatements.name: Parameter and small-marginal laws
primaryStatements.label: prop:selected-parameters
primaryStatements.text: For every flow $Y$ over $C$ and bounded measurable $H_i$ on $W_Y$, \begin{equation} \E_{\lambda_Y}\prod_{i\in I}H_i(P_i) =\lim_{L\to\infty}\int_Y\frac1L\int_0^L \prod_{i\in I}H_i\bigl(\omega_Y(S_Y^{it}y)\bigr) \,\dd t\,\dd m_Y(y). \end{equation} For every nonempty $J\subseteq I$ with $\abs{J}\le3$, \begin{equation} \law_{\lambda_Y}\bigl((y_i)_{i\in J}\mid P\bigr) =\bigotimes_{i\in J}m_{Y,P_i}. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Channel closure
primaryStatements.label: prop:channel-closure
primaryStatements.text: Let $Y$ be a channel and $b\in I$. On $\mathsf M_b(Y)$ take $\pi_Y(y_b)$ as original factor and take every $D_\gamma(y_i)$, $i\in I$, as an output, in the old group of $\gamma$. These data make $\mathsf M_b(Y)$ a channel.

primaryStatements.label: cor:channel-copied-law
primaryStatements.text: For every channel $Y$, the copied spatial list $(d_Y(y_i))_{i\in I}$ under $\lambda_Y$ has its full product law conditional on $P=(\omega_Y(y_i))_{i\in I}$.

definitions.name: Channel
definitions.label: def:channel
definitions.text: A channel is a flow $Y$ over the suspension $C$, with factor map $\pi_Y:Y\to C$, together with a finite list of probability-preserving maps $D_\gamma:Y\to C$, called outputs, and positive rational numbers $q_\gamma$, such that \[ D_\gamma(S_Y^t y)=S_C^{q_\gamma t}D_\gamma(y) \] for each fixed $t$, modulo null sets. Partition the output indices into three groups, numbered $1,2,3$; empty groups are allowed. Set \[ x_0=\xi\circ\pi_Y,\qquad x_\gamma=\xi\circ D_\gamma, \qquad d_Y=(x_\gamma)_\gamma, \] and let $d_{Y,H}$ be the sublist from groups in $H\subseteq\{1,2,3\}$. Let $V$ collect the phase coordinates of $\pi_Y$ and all the $D_\gamma$. Under the measure $m_Y$ require \begin{equation} \begin{split} \law(d_Y\mid V)&=\bigotimes_\gamma\mu,\\ \law(x_0,d_{Y,H}\mid V)&= \mu\otimes\bigotimes_{\gamma\text{ in groups }H}\mu, \qquad H\subsetneq\{1,2,3\}. \end{split} \end{equation} An empty spatial list has the one-point law.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let $(X,\mathcal F,\mu)$ be a probability space and let $T:X\to X$ be invertible, bimeasurable, measure preserving, and mixing in the sense of \eqref{eq:mixing}. For every $f_1,f_2,f_3,f_4\in L^\infty(\mu)$, \[ \frac1N\sum_{n=1}^N f_1(T^nx)f_2(T^{2n}x)f_3(T^{3n}x)f_4(T^{4n}x) \longrightarrow \prod_{j=1}^4\int_X f_j\dd\mu \] for $\mu$-almost every $x$, along all positive integers $N$. The original probability space need not be standard.

primaryStatements.name: Relative structure
primaryStatements.label: prop:structure
primaryStatements.text: The following statements hold for standard probability-preserving systems. \begin{enumerate} \item There is a maximal measure-distal factor $W_Y$. It contains the invariant factor, and $Y\to W_Y$ is relatively weakly mixing. A distal factor pulls back into the maximal distal factor of any extension. Every measure-preserving automorphism commuting with $R$ preserves $W_Y$. \item Factors and joinings of distal systems are distal. A distal system is relatively distal over each of its factors. For every nonzero integer $q$, $R$ is distal if and only if $R^q$ is distal. \item Relative weak mixing passes to nonzero integer powers and to conditionally independent base change. More generally, the product of relatively weakly mixing fibre laws over any invariant joining of their base laws is relatively weakly mixing over that joining. \item A relatively weakly mixing extension and a relatively distal extension of the same base are relatively disjoint: the only invariant joining which identifies their base coordinates is the relatively independent joining. \item If $R$ is distal, then, for every $d\ge1$ and bounded $g_1,\ldots,g_d$, the averages \[ \frac1N\sum_{n=1}^N\prod_{i=1}^d g_i(R^{in}y) \] converge almost surely. \end{enumerate} If $(S_Y^t)_{t\in\R}$ is a probability-preserving flow, the maximal distal factor $W_Y$ of $S_Y^1$ is a flow factor. Its action at every nonzero rational time is distal.

primaryStatements.name: Selectors witnessing failure
primaryStatements.label: prop:selectors
primaryStatements.text: If Theorem \ref{thm:main} fails, there are real functions $f_i\in L^\infty(\mu)$ with $\|f_i\|_\infty\le1$ and $\int f_i\,\dd\mu=0$, a finite set $F\subset[1,2]$, measurable functions \[ N_a:C\longrightarrow\{c2^k:c\in F,\ k\ge a\},\qquad a\ge1, \] a continuous real function $\Psi$ on $(\R/\Z)^I$, and $\epsilon_0>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $a$, \begin{equation} \int_C\frac1{N_a(z)}\int_0^{N_a(z)} \Psi\bigl((\upsilon(S_C^{it}z))_{i\in I}\bigr) \prod_{i\in I}f_i\bigl(\xi(S_C^{it}z)\bigr) \,\dd t\,\dd m_C(z)\ge\epsilon_0. \end{equation} The selectors may be chosen independent of the initial phase.

primaryStatements.name: Selected laws
primaryStatements.label: prop:selected
primaryStatements.text: Formula \eqref{eq:selected-law} defines a probability measure $\lambda_Y$ on $Y^I$ with the following properties. \begin{enumerate} \item Every marginal is $m_Y$, and $\lambda_Y$ is invariant under $(y_i)_i\mapsto(S_Y^{it}y_i)_i$ for every $t\in\R$. If $\theta:Y'\to Y$ is an extension over $C$, then $(\theta^I)_*\lambda_{Y'}=\lambda_Y$. These projections also hold for countable inverse limits of extensions. \item The law $\Lambda_Y$ of $P$ is its deterministic-length law: for bounded $H_i$ on $W_Y$, \begin{equation} \int\prod_iH_i(w_i)\,\dd\Lambda_Y =\lim_{L\to\infty}\int_Y\frac1L\int_0^L \prod_i H_i(\omega_Y(S_Y^{it}y))\,\dd t\,\dd m_Y(y). \end{equation} \item For every proper subset $J\subsetneq I$, the conditional law of $(y_i)_{i\in J}$ given the entire parameter array $P$ is \begin{equation} \operatorname{Law}_{\lambda_Y}\bigl((y_i)_{i\in J}\mid P\bigr) =\bigotimes_{i\in J}m_{Y,P_i}. \end{equation} \end{enumerate} In a countable inverse limit, functions pulled back from the selected laws at finite stages are dense in the $L^2$ space of the limiting selected law.

primaryStatements.name: Tensor packing
primaryStatements.label: thm:packing
primaryStatements.text: There is a universal constant $C$ with the following property. Let $0<\varepsilon\le1$, $d\ge1$, and $L\ge0$ be given, with $d,L$ integers. Let $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ and $y_1,\ldots,y_m$ lie in the unit balls of real Hilbert spaces $H_1,H_2$. For each family suppose that a graph on $\{1,\ldots,m\}$ of maximum degree at most $L$ contains every off-diagonal pair whose absolute inner product exceeds $\eta$, where \[ 0\le\eta\le\varepsilon^2/10^4. \] The two exceptional graphs may differ. For every orthogonal projection $P$ on $H_1\otimes H_2$ of rank at most $d$, \begin{equation} \#\{n:\norm{P(x_n\otimes y_n)}\ge\varepsilon\} \le \frac{C(1+L)}{\varepsilon^2} \exp\!\left(C\varepsilon^{-2}\sqrt d\log(2+d)\right). \end{equation} In particular, for \begin{equation} d_m=\left\lceil(1+\log m)^{3/2}\right\rceil, \end{equation} the left side is $o_{\varepsilon,L}(m)$, uniformly over the Hilbert spaces, the vectors, the projections, and the allowed values of $\eta$.

primaryStatements.name: Closure under selected laws
primaryStatements.label: prop:channel-closure
primaryStatements.text: Let $Y$ be a channel and $b\in I$. On $\mathsf M_b(Y)$ use $\pi_Y(y_b)$ as original factor. For each $j\in\{1,2,3\}$, let the new group $j$ contain the outputs $D_\alpha(y_i)$ with $\alpha\in\mathcal D_j$ and $i\in I$. With these factors, $\mathsf M_b(Y)$ is a channel.

primaryStatements.label: cor:channel-array-distal
primaryStatements.text: In Proposition \ref{prop:channel-closure}, let $P=(\omega_Y(y_i))_{i\in I}$ be the array of old distal parameters. The spatial coordinates of all copied outputs are independent with their product law conditionally on $P$. The corresponding assertion holds after any finite iteration of that proposition, conditionally on the complete array of old $W_Y$-parameters.

primaryStatements.label: prop:role-bound
primaryStatements.text: Every nonzero correlation \eqref{eq:role-correlation} has at most two output roles. In particular, the maximal number $r$ just defined satisfies $r\le2$.

definitions.label: def:channel
definitions.text: A channel is a flow extension $\pi_Y:(Y,m_Y,S_Y^t)\to C$ together with a finite list of output factors $D_\alpha:Y\to C$, of positive rational speeds $q_\alpha$, partitioned into three groups $\mathcal D_1,\mathcal D_2,\mathcal D_3$. Empty groups are allowed. Let $x_0$ be the spatial coordinate of $\pi_Y$, let $x_\alpha$ be that of $D_\alpha$, and let $V$ collect the phases of $\pi_Y$ and of all the $D_\alpha$. The following conditional laws are required: \begin{align} \mathcal L((x_\alpha)_\alpha\mid V) &=\bigotimes_\alpha\mu, \\ \mathcal L\bigl(x_0,(x_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\cup_{j\in J}\mathcal D_j} \mid V\bigr) &=\mu\otimes \bigotimes_{\alpha\in\cup_{j\in J}\mathcal D_j}\mu \qquad(J\subsetneq\{1,2,3\}). \end{align} The product laws on the right do not depend on $V$.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: For every system satisfying \eqref{eq:mixing}, every triple of pairwise distinct nonzero integers $\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3$, and every bounded measurable $f_1,f_2,f_3:X\to\C$, the averages in \eqref{eq:averages} satisfy \[ A_N(x)\longrightarrow\prod_{j=1}^3\int_X f_j\,d\mu \quad\text{for almost every }x, \] as $N$ tends to infinity through all positive integers. The exceptional null set may depend on the slopes and the functions.

primaryStatements.name: Local estimate with variation in depth
primaryStatements.label: thm:local
primaryStatements.text: Fix the primitive distinct integers $b_0=0,b_1,b_2,b_3$ and the parameters $\delta_0,C_0$. Let $\mathcal T$ be a finite dyadic tree with root $J$ and largest depth $d$, and let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal T$. Assign an admissible kernel to every $I\in\mathcal I$. For each $0\le j\le3$, let $z_{j,s}:J\to\C$, $0\le s\le d$, be measurable, and partition $\{0,\ldots,d\}$ into $W_j\ge1$ deterministic nonempty consecutive blocks. Suppose that \[ \mathcal V_B(z_j)\le W_j^{-1/2}\quad\text{almost everywhere on }J \] for each block in the $j$th partition. Extend every input by zero outside $J$. Then \begin{equation} \sum_{I\in\mathcal I}\abs{I}\, \abs{H_I(z_{0,s(I)},z_{1,s(I)},z_{2,s(I)},z_{3,s(I)})} \le C_{b,\delta_0,C_0}\abs{J}. \end{equation} The constant is independent of the lattice, tree, depth range, subcollection, kernels, and the four partitions and their sizes.

primaryStatements.name: Finite orbit oscillation
primaryStatements.label: prop:tr-oscillation
primaryStatements.text: For every deterministic list \(0\leq k_1<\cdots<k_{w+1}\), \begin{equation} \sum_{i=1}^w\int_X \max_{k_i\leq\ell\leq k_{i+1}} |V_\ell^\varphi-V_{k_i}^\varphi|\,d\mu \leq C”_{\varphi,b}\sqrt w. \end{equation} This holds on every invertible probability preserving system, with a constant independent of that system, the functions, and the endpoints.

primaryStatements.name: Short-block comparison
primaryStatements.label: prop:short-block-b
primaryStatements.text: Let \(2<q<3\). Let a finite dyadic tree piece have root \(R\), with internal summation intervals in at most \(K\) consecutive depths and within the original range of at most \(N\) depths. Its terminal intervals, called leaves, partition \(R\) and occur in this depth block or one depth below it. In role \(j\), let \(\mathbf z_j\) be a deterministic Hilbert-space-valued function supported on \(R\), with \(\|\mathbf z_j\|_{2,L}\le s_j\) on every leaf \(L\). Suppose scalar randomizations \(z_j^\sigma\) satisfy \[ \bigl(\mathbb E_\sigma|z_j^\sigma(y)|^a\bigr)^{1/a} \le C_a\|\mathbf z_j(y)\| \] for \(a=2,4,8\), with constants independent of the tree and \(K\). For measurable signs \(|\epsilon_I(\sigma)|\le1\) and any subcollection of internal intervals, \[ \mathbb E_\sigma\left| \sum_I |I|\epsilon_I(\sigma)H_I(z_0^\sigma,z_1^\sigma, z_2^\sigma,z_3^\sigma)\right| \le (1+C_N(q))C_{q,b}(1+\log(K+2))^C (K+2)^{11(q-2)/(q-1)}|R|\prod_j s_j . \] The constant \(C_{q,b}\) may also depend on the fixed moment bounds \(C_a\) and the kernel bounds.

primaryStatements.name: Normalized absorption
primaryStatements.label: prop:absorption
primaryStatements.text: For the fixed $q$ chosen above and every sufficiently small $\tau>0$, there is $A_\tau<\infty$, independent of $N$, such that the following holds. Suppose a finite rooted dyadic subtree has root $I_*$, its summation cells lie in at most $N$ consecutive depths, and its fixed scalar inputs satisfy \[ \left(\abs I^{-1}\int_I\abs{f_j}^q\right)^{1/q}\le1 \quad(0\le j\le3, I\text{ in the subtree}). \] Then, for any subset of summation cells and admissible kernels, \[ \sum_{I\text{ a summation cell}}\abs I\,\abs{H_I(f_0,f_1,f_2,f_3)} \le (A_\tau+\tau C_N(q))\abs{I_*}. \]

definitions.name: Local kernels
definitions.label: def:kernels
definitions.text: Fix $\delta_0>0$ and $C_0\ge1$. For an interval $I$ of length $r$, a kernel $w_I\in C_c^\infty(\R^2;\C)$ is admissible if \begin{enumerate} \item $\dist(x+b_jt,\partial I)\ge\delta_0r$ and $x+b_jt\in I$ for every $(x,t)\in\supp w_I$ and $0\le j\le3$; \item for every $v\in\R$ and $0\le j\le3$, \begin{equation} \int_\R w_I(v-b_jt,t)\,dt=0; \end{equation} \item for nonnegative integers $a,d$ and $n=a+d$, \begin{equation} \norm{\partial_x^a\partial_t^d w_I}_\infty \le r^{-n}\bigl(C_0(n+2)\bigr)^{C_0(n+2)}. \end{equation} \end{enumerate} For scalar measurable inputs define \begin{equation} H_I(z_0,z_1,z_2,z_3) =r^{-2}\int_{\R^2} w_I(x,t)\prod_{j=0}^3z_j(x+b_jt)\,dx\,dt, \end{equation} whenever the integral is absolutely convergent.

definitions.name: Averaging profile
definitions.label: def:tr-profile
definitions.text: An averaging profile is a real \(\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\R)\) with \begin{equation} \int_\R\varphi=1, \qquad \int_\R t^j\varphi(t)\,dt=0\quad(1\leq j\leq3), \end{equation} and, for some \(G\geq1\), \begin{equation} \|\varphi^{(n)}\|_\infty \leq \bigl(G(n+2)\bigr)^{G(n+2)}\qquad(n\geq0). \end{equation} Write \(\varphi_a(t)=a^{-1}\varphi(t/a)\) for \(a>0\). Profiles are necessarily signed: a nonnegative smooth function of mass one cannot have zero second moment.

papers.title: Pointwise convergence of triple ergodic averages for mixing transformations
papers.abstract: We prove pointwise convergence of triple ergodic averages for every invertible mixing probability preserving transformation T of an arbitrary probability space $(X,\mathcal F,\mu)$, with measurable inverse. For every triple of bounded measurable functions $f_1,f_2,f_3:X\to\mathbb C$, $\displaystyle \frac1N\sum_{n=1}^N f_1(T^nx)f_2(T^{2n}x)f_3(T^{3n}x) \longrightarrow \prod_{j=1}^3\int_X f_j\,d\mu$ for μ-almost every x as $N\to\infty$ through all positive integers.
papers.familySummary: Proves almost-everywhere convergence of consecutive multiple ergodic averages of every finite length for invertible mixing probability-preserving transformations. For each fixed tuple of bounded functions, the limit is the product of their integrals, along all positive averaging lengths. No mixing rate or standardness assumption on the probability space is required.
papers.subject: Dynamical systems and ergodic theory
papers.sourceAbstract: We prove pointwise convergence of triple ergodic averages for every invertible mixing probability preserving transformation \(T\) of an arbitrary probability space \((X,\mathcal F,\mu)\), with measurable inverse. For every triple of bounded measurable functions \(f_1,f_2,f_3:X\to\mathbb C\), \[ \frac1N\sum_{n=1}^N f_1(T^nx)f_2(T^{2n}x)f_3(T^{3n}x) \longrightarrow \prod_{j=1}^3\int_X f_j\,d\mu \] for \(\mu\)-almost every \(x\) as \(N\to\infty\) through all positive integers.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let $(X,\mathcal F,\mu)$ be an arbitrary probability space and let $T:X\to X$ be an invertible mixing probability preserving transformation with measurable inverse. For every triple of bounded measurable functions $f_1,f_2,f_3:X\to\C$, \[ A_N(f_1,f_2,f_3)(x) \longrightarrow \prod_{j=1}^3\int_X f_j\,d\mu \quad\text{for $\mu$-almost every }x \] as $N\to\infty$ through all positive integers. The exceptional null set may depend on the triple of functions.

primaryStatements.name: Finite oscillation of smooth orbit averages
primaryStatements.label: prop:orbit-oscillation
primaryStatements.text: For every averaging profile \(\varphi\), there is a constant \(C_\varphi<\infty\) with the following property. On every invertible probability preserving system, let \(f_1,f_2,f_3:X\to\mathbb C\) be measurable with \(|f_j(x)|\leq1\) for all \(x\), and define \[ V_k^\varphi(x)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}\varphi_{2^k}(n) \prod_{j=1}^3f_j(T^{jn}x), \qquad k=0,1,2,\ldots . \] For every integer \(w\geq1\) and every deterministic list of integers \(0\leq k_1<\cdots<k_{w+1}\), \begin{equation} \sum_{i=1}^w\int_X \max_{k_i\leq\ell\leq k_{i+1}} |V_\ell^\varphi-V_{k_i}^\varphi|\,d\mu \leq C_\varphi\sqrt w. \end{equation} The constant is independent of the system, the inputs, \(w\), and the endpoints.

primaryStatements.name: Local estimate with variation in depth
primaryStatements.label: thm:depth-local
primaryStatements.text: Fix the admissibility parameters \(c_0,C_0\). Let \(J\) be an interval in any dyadic lattice, let \(\mathcal T\) be a finite rooted tree below \(J\), and let \(d\) be its largest depth in \(J\). Let \(\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal T\), with an admissible kernel on each of its intervals. For each \(j\in\{0,1,2,3\}\), let \(f_{j,s}:J\to\C\), \(0\le s\le d\), be measurable, and write \(f_j=(f_{j,s})_{s=0}^d\). Suppose that \(\{0,\ldots,d\}\) is partitioned into \(W_j\ge1\) deterministic nonempty consecutive blocks and that, on every block \(B\), \[ \mathcal V_B(f_j)(y)\le W_j^{-1/2} \quad\text{for almost every }y\in J. \] The four partitions may differ. Extend the inputs by zero outside \(J\). Then \begin{equation} \sum_{I\in\mathcal I}|I| \bigl|H_I(f_{0,s(I)},f_{1,s(I)},f_{2,s(I)},f_{3,s(I)})\bigr| \le C_{\mathrm{loc}}(c_0,C_0)|J|. \end{equation} The constant is independent of the lattice, root, tree, kernels, depth range, blocks, and their numbers.

primaryStatements.name: Increments of inherited projections
primaryStatements.label: cor:row-projections
primaryStatements.text: Use the catalog of Lemma \ref{lem:row-catalog}. On a finite interval of integers $h\ge s_R$, let $\mathcal P_h$ be the full partition of $R$ into cells of depth $h$. On each $Q\in\mathcal P_h$, let $P_{h,Q}$ be the orthogonal projection in $L^2(Q;\mathcal H)$ onto constant-coefficient combinations of a subset $\mathcal M_h(Q)\subset\mathcal V(Q)$. Assume inheritance: if $Q'\in\mathcal P_{h+1}$ is contained in $Q$, then $\mathcal M_h(Q)\subset\mathcal M_{h+1}(Q')$. Let $P_h$ be the direct sum of the $P_{h,Q}$ on $L^2(R;\mathcal H)$. Suppose $(F_s)_{s\in\mathsf S}$ satisfies Equation \eqref{eq:row-input-normalization}. For any integer $J\ge1$ and \[ r_1\le t_1\le r_2\le t_2\le\cdots\le r_J\le t_J \] in the projection depth range and nondecreasing $s_1,\ldots,s_J\in\mathsf S$, one has \begin{equation} \sum_{j=1}^J\|(P_{t_j}-P_{r_j})F_{s_j}\|_2^2 \le \mathfrak C_D^2|R|. \end{equation} If the intervals can be divided into $\mathfrak m$ such ordered families whose reads are nondecreasing, the right side is multiplied by $\mathfrak m$. For each $s\in\mathsf S$ with $s\ge s_R$, let $\mathcal U_s$ be any subcollection of the depth-$s$ cells of $R$. In particular fix an integer $\ell$ and retain only those $s$ for which $s+\ell$ and $s+\ell+1$ are in the projection range. Then \begin{equation} \sum_s\sum_{I\in\mathcal U_s}|I|\, \|(P_{s+\ell+1}-P_{s+\ell})F_s\|_{2,I}^2 \le \mathfrak C_D^2|R|. \end{equation} For every integer $L\ge0$, retaining only $s\in\mathsf S$ with $s\ge s_R$ for which $s$ and $s+L$ are in the projection range, \begin{equation} \left(\sum_s\sum_{I\in\mathcal U_s}|I|\, \|(P_{s+L}-P_s)F_s\|_{2,I}^2\right)^{1/2} \le L\mathfrak C_D|R|^{1/2} \le (1+L)\mathfrak C_D|R|^{1/2}. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: A finite predictor list for scheduled opponents
primaryStatements.label: cor:hbase-predictor-list
primaryStatements.text: Fix the two bounded scalar atoms \(\varphi_i,\varphi_j\) on \(J'\), of complexity at most \(H_{\rm low}\), and let \(B\ge1\). There is a finite index set \(\mathfrak A\), a bound \(D_{\rm pred}\), scalar coefficients \(c_{r,\alpha}\), and fixed triples \((\psi_{a,\alpha},\psi_{b,\alpha},\lambda_\alpha)\) on \(J'\) with \(\|\psi_{e,\alpha}\|_\infty\le1\), such that \[ \#\mathfrak A,\quad \operatorname{complexity}(\psi_{e,\alpha}),\quad |c_{r,\alpha}|\le D_{\rm pred},\qquad \log D_{\rm pred}\le \operatorname{poly}\bigl(1+B+\log(2H_{\rm low})\bigr). \] Here \(c_{r,\alpha}\) is a scalar depending only on the fixed pair, its scalar construction, \(B\), and the dyadic scale \(r\); it is zero unless \(|\lambda_\alpha|r^2\le D_{\rm pred}\). The list and these coefficients are chosen before any opposing sequences or completed high catalogs. Define its forms explicitly by \begin{equation} \begin{split} T_I^\alpha(z_a,z_b) :=|I|^{-2}\int_{\mathbb R^2}&w_I(x,t)e(\lambda_\alpha t^2) \psi_{a,\alpha}(y_a)z_a(y_a)\\ &\qquad\cdot\psi_{b,\alpha}(y_b)z_b(y_b)\,dx\,dt . \end{split} \end{equation} For every dyadic \(K\subseteq J'\), selected finite use collection \(\mathcal U\) below \(K\), and pair of admissible opposing sequences on \(K\), define the actual error \(e_I\) by the per-cell identity \begin{equation} \mathcal L_I^{\varphi_i,\varphi_j}(z_{a,I},z_{b,I}) =\sum_{\alpha\in\mathfrak A}c_{|I|,\alpha} T_I^\alpha(z_{a,I},z_{b,I})+e_I. \end{equation} Then, uniformly over those opposing sequences and their completed catalogs, \begin{equation} \sum_{I\in\mathcal U}|I||e_I| \le e^{-B}\operatorname{poly} \bigl(\log(2D_{\rm h}),1+L\bigr)|K|. \end{equation} The error \(e_I\) may depend on the opposing sequence; the assertion is its aggregate bound.

primaryStatements.name: Base data and active reduction
primaryStatements.label: prop:hbase-data
primaryStatements.text: Fix the constructed tuple with later accuracy \(t\), put \(k=k_t\), and use its final segments \(R\in\mathcal R_{\rm base}\) and original owner sets \(\mathcal I_R\) from Equation \eqref{eq:hbase-high-replacement}. On an owned cell of depth \(s\), define \begin{equation} \begin{gathered} Y_l=B_l+U_l,\qquad B_i=X_i,\quad B_j=X_j,\quad U_i=U_j=0,\\ B_e=P^{\rm new}_{e,s}F_{e,s}-g_{e,\mathrm{prev},I},\qquad U_e=(P^{\rm new}_{e,s+K_0}-P^{\rm new}_{e,s})F_{e,s} \quad(e=a,b),\\ \|B_{l,I}\|_{2,I},\ \|U_{l,I}\|_{2,I},\ \|Y_{l,I}\|_{2,I}\le C,\\ \Lambda_k=C(1+K_0)\log(2D_{\rm base})\le k^C,\qquad \sum_{I\in\mathcal I_R}|I|\|U_{e,I}\|_{2,I}^2 \le\Lambda_k^2|R|\quad(e=a,b). \end{gathered} \end{equation} Each \(B_l\) is a signed sum of at most two current nested-catalog projections applied to \(F_{l,s}\). Their basic catalogs have distinct private directions and inherited masks. Their path counts, column sizes, inverse private weights, bounded scalar atom complexities, and current coefficient sums are bounded by \(D_{\rm base}\), with \[ e^k\le D_{\rm base}\le\exp(k^C). \] For \(t\ge12\), the associated full \(Y\) tuple has the pair bound and pointwise form bound \(\eta\) of Equation \eqref{eq:hbase-quality}. For three available basic scalar columns \(\boldsymbol\varphi\) in distinct slots, let \(\operatorname{act}_I(\boldsymbol\varphi)\) be their form norm against a normalized \(L^2(I)\) input in the fourth slot. For a sufficiently large fixed \(C_{\rm act}\), put \[ \mathcal A_R= \left\{I\in\mathcal I_R: \operatorname{act}_I(\boldsymbol\varphi)>D_{\rm base}^{-C_{\rm act}} \text{ for some available triple }\boldsymbol\varphi\right\}. \] This common active set has path multiplicity \[ \sum_{I\in\mathcal A_R}\mathbf1_I(y)\le M\le D_{\rm base}^C. \] Define three patterns in their original slots by \[ \begin{array}{lll} z^\varnothing_l=B_l&\text{for every }l,\\ z^a_a=U_a,&z^a_l=B_l& (l\ne a),\\ z^b_b=U_b,&z^b_l=B_l& (l\ne b), \end{array} \qquad \mathcal P=\{z^\varnothing,z^a,z^b\}. \] For \(z\in\mathcal P\), let \begin{equation} \mathfrak M_R(z) :=\sum_{I\in\mathcal A_R}|I| \min\{\eta,|H_I(z_I)|\}. \end{equation} Then for \(t\ge12\), \begin{equation} \sum_{I\in\mathcal I_R}|I|\,|H_I(Y_I)| \le C\eta\Lambda_k^2|R|+e^{-k}|R| +\sum_{z\in\mathcal P}\mathfrak M_R(z). \end{equation} The \(e^{-k}|R|\) term is the total inactive error for the three patterns. The finitely many leading accuracy levels have a bound independent of the number of spatial depths. These base data and their estimates hold anew on normalized subroots with the inherited basic lists and their local continuations.

primaryStatements.name: The endpoint histories used by filter transfer
primaryStatements.label: cor:h-transfer-endpoint-variation
primaryStatements.text: Fix one source search leaf, one step in the Outgoing filters and near-band defects Lemma of \cite[Section 6]{H}, and one choice in that step's expansion of the complementary factors. In its outgoing complementary slot write \(x_{c,s}=\mathcal C_{c,s}B_{c,s}\) for exactly the input-side source history left after deleting the outgoing positive filter. This inner history is shared across groups. It retains the source order, its normalized averages or identities, its \(O(\log\mathcal L)\) length, and the specified input-side basic \(Q_s^\tau\) in each nonzero constituent. Write \(x_{d,s}\) for the whole remaining source history in the other complementary slot. All endpoint evaluations use the complete inherited families, with coupled pads at compared depths, and may occur when the group is not current. Let \(Q_{c,p,s}\), \(1\le p\le P\), be exactly that step's individual outgoing projections, and put \(Q_{c,0,s}=0\), \(Q_{c,P+1,s}=1\). For a ball transfer, each \(Q_{c,p,s}x_{c,s}\) with \(1\le p\le P\) is an eligible group-indexed ball endpoint, while \(x_{c,s}\) is shared. For a cumulative transfer the outer ball has already been removed and all these endpoints are shared. The other endpoint \(x_{d,s}\) either has its one source positive ball average outermost, with shared inner history, or is shared after that ball has been removed. Each specified eligible ball output, using its source positive average or one individual allowed pad as a singleton average, satisfies \eqref{eq:h-certified-variation}. Each specified shared output satisfies the shared conclusion of Lemma \ref{lem:h-certified-variation}, with one union of required right-endpoint cells across its uses.

definitions.name: Averaging profiles
definitions.label: def:averaging-profile
definitions.text: An averaging profile is a real function \(\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R;\mathbb R)\) such that, for some \(G\geq1\), \begin{equation} \|\varphi^{(n)}\|_\infty \leq\bigl(G(n+2)\bigr)^{G(n+2)} \qquad(n=0,1,2,\ldots), \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \int_{\mathbb R}\varphi(t)\,dt=1,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}t^j\varphi(t)\,dt=0\quad(1\leq j\leq3). \end{equation} The function may have either sign. For \(a>0\), write \(\varphi_a(t)=a^{-1}\varphi(t/a)\).

definitions.name: Admissible local kernels
definitions.label: def:transfer-local-kernels
definitions.text: Fix \(c_0>0\) and \(C_0\geq1\). For an interval \(I\) of length \(r=|I|\), a kernel \(w_I\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2;\mathbb C)\) is admissible if the following hold. \begin{enumerate} \item For every \((x,t)\in\operatorname{supp}w_I\) and \(j\in\{0,1,2,3\}\), \(x+jt\in I\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(x+jt,\partial I)\geq c_0r\). \item For every \(v\in\mathbb R\) and \(j=0,1,2,3\), \[ \int_{\mathbb R}w_I(v-jt,t)\,dt=0. \] \item For all nonnegative integers \(p,q\), with \(n=p+q\), \[ \|\partial_x^p\partial_t^q w_I\|_\infty \leq r^{-n}\bigl(C_0(n+2)\bigr)^{C_0(n+2)}. \] \end{enumerate} For measurable scalar functions \(z_j:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C\), define the associated local form, whenever its integral is finite, by \[ H_I(z_0,z_1,z_2,z_3) =r^{-2}\int_{\mathbb R^2}w_I(x,t) \prod_{j=0}^3z_j(x+jt)\,dx\,dt. \] For a Hilbert-valued argument with a distinguished physical scalar coordinate, the form uses that coordinate. We write \(\|z\|_{p,I}=(|I|^{-1}\int_I\|z\|^p)^{1/p}\) for the normalized interval norm, with the usual essential supremum when \(p=\infty\). Norms without an interval subscript use ordinary Lebesgue measure.

papers.title: A translational tile with no fully periodic tiling in dimension three
papers.abstract: We construct a finite translational tile in ℤ3 that admits tilings but no fully periodic tiling. Its unit-cube thickening has the same property in ℝ3, even when arbitrary real translations are allowed. This gives a negative resolution of the periodic tiling conjecture in dimension three.
papers.familySummary: Constructs a finite translational tile in ℤ3 that tiles space but admits no fully periodic tiling, disproving the periodic tiling conjecture in the smallest possible lattice dimension. Its unit-cube thickening gives the same counterexample in ℝ3, even with arbitrary real translation vectors.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: There is a finite nonempty set $T\subset\Z^3$ such that: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item $T$ tiles $\Z^3$ by translations, but no translation set $A$ with $A\oplus T=\Z^3$ is invariant under a subgroup of finite index in $\Z^3$; \item the set $\Omega=T+[0,1]^3$ tiles $\R^3$ by translations up to null sets, but no such tiling has a translation set invariant under a lattice of full rank in $\R^3$. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.name: The vertical-period obstruction
primaryStatements.label: word:obstruction
primaryStatements.text: There is no array $W\colon I\times\Z\to\Sigma$ satisfying the line rule, having every column nonconstant, and having a positive vertical period.

primaryStatements.label: act:nonperiodic
primaryStatements.text: No common solution of this finite system is invariant under a finite-index subgroup of $G$.

primaryStatements.label: model:system
primaryStatements.text: There are a finite cyclic group $V$ and finitely many nonempty finite sets $F_1,\ldots,F_s\subset G=\Z^2\times V$ for which the simultaneous tiling equations \[ A\oplus F_\nu=G\qquad(1\leq\nu\leq s) \] have a common solution, but no common solution is invariant under a finite-index subgroup of $G$.

primaryStatements.name: One tile with a cyclic finite coordinate
primaryStatements.label: stack:cyclic
primaryStatements.text: For some positive integer $Q$, there is a finite nonempty set $F\subset\Gamma=\Z^2\times\Zmod{Q}$ which tiles $\Gamma$ but admits no fully periodic tiling.

primaryStatements.label: geom:existence
primaryStatements.text: The tile $T$ tiles $\Z^3$, and $\Omega$ tiles $\R^3$ up to null sets.

primaryStatements.label: geom:no-periodic

definitions.name: Allowed words and the line rule
definitions.label: word:definition
definitions.text: A word $w\colon I\to\Sigma$ is allowed if there are integers $a,b$, not both divisible by $p$, such that, for every $n\in I$, \[ w(n)= \begin{cases} an+b\pmod p, & p\nmid an+b,\\[2pt] (an+b)/p\pmod p, & p\mid an+b\text{ and }p^2\nmid an+b. \end{cases} \] At indices with $p^2\mid an+b$, the value may be any member of $\Sigma$. An array $W\colon I\times\Z\to\Sigma$ satisfies the line rule if \[ n\longmapsto W(n,dn+e) \] is an allowed word for every $d,e\in\Z$. A positive vertical period of $W$ is an integer $M>0$ such that $W(n,m+M)=W(n,m)$ for all $(n,m)\in I\times\Z$.

lean.scopeText: The periodic-tiling question asks whether a finite tile that tiles a lattice must admit a periodic tiling. The formalized counterexample is a finite tile in $\mathbb Z^3$ that tiles but has no complement invariant under a finite-index subgroup. Its unit-cube thickening also tiles $\mathbb R^3$ almost everywhere but admits no fully periodic tiling, even with arbitrary real translation vectors. The result also establishes that dimension three is the least lattice dimension where this failure occurs.

papers.title: A nine-dimensional counterexample to Borsuk's covering assertion
papers.abstract: The compact set of rank-one orthogonal projectors on ℝ4, with the Frobenius metric, cannot be covered by ten sets of strictly smaller diameter. It therefore gives a counterexample to Borsuk's conjecture in dimension nine.

sections.title: From diameter covers to projective maps
The equality case gives a simplicial cycle

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: The compact set \[ X=\{uu^{\mathsf T}:u\in\mathbb R^4,\ \|u\|=1\} \subset\{A\in\operatorname{Sym}_4(\mathbb R):\operatorname{tr}A=1\}, \] with the Frobenius metric, has diameter $\sqrt2$ and cannot be covered by ten subsets of diameter strictly less than $\sqrt2$.

primaryStatements.name: The number of labels
primaryStatements.label: thm:label-bound
primaryStatements.text: If $k\ge2$, every smooth admissible map $f:\mathbb P(\mathbb R^k)\to\Delta^{m-1}$ satisfies $m\ge N_k$. If $m=N_k$, its extension $F$ has mod-two degree one and is surjective. In this equality case, every pair of labels is an edge of the support complex of $f$.

primaryStatements.name: Supports at equality
primaryStatements.label: thm:equality-complex
primaryStatements.text: Let $k\ge3$ and $m=N_k$. Suppose $f:\mathbb P(\mathbb R^k)\to\Delta^{m-1}$ is a smooth admissible map. Its support complex $K$ has every pair of labels as an edge, every facet has $k$ vertices, and \[ \sum_{I\text{ a facet of }K} I \] is a simplicial cycle over $\mathbb F_2$. Consequently every $(k-2)$-dimensional face lies in a positive even number of facets.

primaryStatements.label: thm:no-ten-labels
primaryStatements.text: There is no admissible map $\mathbb{RP}^3\to\Delta^9$.

primaryStatements.label: cor:higher-dimensions
primaryStatements.text: For every integer $d\geq9$, there is a compact subset of $\mathbb R^d$ of diameter $\sqrt2$ that cannot be covered by $d+1$ subsets of strictly smaller diameter.

definitions.label: def:admissible
definitions.text: A smooth map $f=(f_1,\ldots,f_m):\mathbb P(V)\to\mathbb R^m$ is admissible if each $f_i$ is nonnegative, $\sum_i f_i=1$, and, writing $S(x)=\{i:f_i(x)>0\}$, \begin{equation} x\perp y\quad\Longrightarrow\quad S(x)\cap S(y)=\varnothing. \end{equation} Here smoothness means smoothness of the real coordinate functions on the usual smooth manifold $\mathbb P(V)$.

definitions.label: def:six-system
definitions.text: A six-label triangle system on a set $C$ of cardinality six is a collection $\mathcal T\subseteq\binom{C}{3}$ such that \begin{enumerate} \item exactly one of $T$ and $C\setminus T$ belongs to $\mathcal T$ for each $T\in\binom{C}{3}$; \item every pair of elements of $C$ belongs to exactly two members of $\mathcal T$. \end{enumerate}

lean.scopeText: Borsuk's conjecture predicts that every bounded subset of $\mathbb R^d$ can be covered by $d+1$ sets of strictly smaller diameter. The formalized counterexample is the compact set of rank-one orthogonal projectors onto lines in $\mathbb R^4$, with the Frobenius metric. It lies in the nine-dimensional affine space of trace-one symmetric matrices, has diameter $\sqrt2$, and cannot be covered by ten arbitrary sets of smaller diameter.

papers.title: A counterexample to Hadwiger's conjecture
papers.abstract: We disprove Hadwiger's conjecture by constructing arbitrarily large graphs whose chromatic number exceeds their Hadwiger number. The examples have independence number at most two, and even their ordinary fractional chromatic number exceeds their Hadwiger number. Thus they also disprove the fractional-coloring weakening discussed by Reed and Seymour.
papers.familySummary: Disproves Hadwiger's conjecture even for fractional coloring: arbitrarily large finite simple graphs with independence number at most two satisfy $\chi_f(G)\gt h(G)$, where $h(G)$ is the largest clique-minor order. Also disproves the fractional Colin de Verdière chromatic bound $\chi_f(G)\le\mu(G)+1$. In the positive direction, every finite nonempty graph satisfies $\chi_{\mathrm{list}}(G)\le C h(G)$ for a universal constant C.
