primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: There are arbitrarily large integers \(m\) for which an \(m\)-vertex finite simple graph \(G\) satisfies \[ \alpha(G)\le2 \qquad\text{and}\qquad \cm(G)<\frac{m}{100}. \]

primaryStatements.label: cor:hadwiger
primaryStatements.text: There are finite nonempty simple graphs \(G\) of arbitrarily large order \(m\) for which \[ h(G)<\frac{26m}{75}+\frac23 <\frac m2\le\chi_f(G)\le\chi(G). \] Thus Hadwiger's conjecture and its fractional-coloring weakening \(\chi_f(G)\le h(G)\) are false.

primaryStatements.name: Raw supersaturation
primaryStatements.label: thm:raw-supersaturation
primaryStatements.text: For the construction parameters specified in \Cref{sec:geometry,sec:parameters}, for all sufficiently large \(n\), every probability law \(\sigma\) on units satisfying \begin{equation} \sigma_1\le M\mu,\qquad \sigma_2\le M\mu,\qquad \sigma\le 2^{DN}\mu^2 \end{equation} has the following property: two independent units drawn from \(\sigma\) have all four cross holes with probability at least \(2^{-100gN}\). The inequalities in \Cref{eq:raw-law-caps} are pointwise inequalities of measures on the finite raw spaces.

primaryStatements.label: prop:raw-to-graph
primaryStatements.text: Assume the conclusion of \Cref{thm:raw-supersaturation} at a given sufficiently large \(n\). For \(m=2^{C_0gN}\), the sampled graph defined in \Cref{sec:geometry} satisfies \[ \alpha(G)\le2,\qquad \cm(G)<m/100 \] with probability \(1-\exp(-\Omega(m))\). The implied positive constant is independent of \(n\).

primaryStatements.label: prop:matching-minor
primaryStatements.text: For every finite nonempty graph \(G\) of order \(m\), \[ \had(G)\le\frac{m+4\cm(G)+2}{3}. \] In particular, if \(\alpha(G)\le2\) and \(\cm(G)<m/100\), then \[ \had(G)<\frac{26m}{75}+\frac23<\frac m2\le\chi(G) \qquad(m\ge5). \]

primaryStatements.name: Gradient realization
primaryStatements.label: thm:gradient-realization
primaryStatements.text: Suppose two units in fixed leaves have lists satisfying \eqref{eq:recipe-scalars}, the binary prescriptions yielding \eqref{eq:recipe-gradients}, equal matched keys, and an admissible injecting small table. Freeze their actual cross Gram entries whenever either argument is a pin or a key direction. Then there are abstract cross bilinear forms on the full nominal spaces, extending all these frozen entries, whose primal-versus-channel entries satisfy \begin{equation} u_zU_i=r(v_{iz})\quad\text{on }\cX \qquad(i\text{ and }z\text{ in opposite units}). \end{equation} Only the primal-versus-channel entries need be prescribed in the final test. Their number is at most $16|\cE|h\dim\cB=O(n)$, with its coefficient fixed before $M_0$. Agreement of the actual cross Grams with these entries produces all four cross holes, with witnesses $(v_{iz},v_{zi})$.

primaryStatements.name: Collision criterion
primaryStatements.label: prop:collision
primaryStatements.text: Let $\sigma$ be a unit law in \Cref{thm:raw-supersaturation}, and let $\widetilde\sigma$ be a restriction of it of relative mass at least $2^{-o(N)}$, decomposed into leaves satisfying \eqref{eq:final-leaf-minentropy}. Mix the leaves with their actual masses in $\widetilde\sigma$. Suppose accepted numerical queries as above, with their leaf-pair choices of table and separate filters, satisfy \begin{equation} \E_{\text{independent leaf pair}} \int d_A d_B\,d\nu_n\ge 2^{-o(N)}. \end{equation} Then two independent units from the original $\sigma$ have all four cross holes with probability at least \begin{equation} 2^{-(k_{\max}+.03)N-o(N)}. \end{equation} It suffices to obtain \eqref{eq:overlap-criterion} after skipping some leaf pairs, or after summing over a bounded number of numerical options. Positive subsequential constants and inverse-polynomial overlap bounds both suffice. In particular, this conclusion contradicts a sequence violating \Cref{thm:raw-supersaturation}.

primaryStatements.name: Phase alternative
primaryStatements.label: thm:phase-alternative
primaryStatements.text: Suppose a marked-unit law is obtained by restricting an admissible law in \Cref{thm:raw-supersaturation} to mass at least \(10^{-12}\), and \(\Delta_O\ne0\) throughout. For all sufficiently large \(n\), one can retain a sublaw of fixed positive relative mass, bounded below using only the early parameters, such that one of the following holds for independent draws \(A,B\): \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item every nontrivial phase mean \[ \E(-1)^{u_{B,S}(\Delta_A)+u_{A,R}(\Delta_B)}, \qquad(S,R)\ne(\varnothing,\varnothing), \] has absolute value less than \(.005\); \item a componentwise cover of total dimension at most \(d_0\) covers every \(\Delta_O\), and every displayed mean for which \(|S|=1\) or \(|R|=1\) is \(2^{-\Omega(N)}\). \end{enumerate} The cover may depend on the law and on \(n\). The constants in its dimension bound and in the relative mass bound do not depend on the later selector or channel sizes.

definitions.label: def:hole
definitions.text: Two elements \(i,j\in\Omega\) have a hole between them if there exist \(\lambda_i,\lambda_j\in\cX\) such that \begin{equation} \begin{gathered} U_i\lambda_i=U_j\lambda_j,\qquad u_jU_i=r(\lambda_i),\qquad u_iU_j=r(\lambda_j),\\ a(\lambda_i)+a(\lambda_j)=1. \end{gathered} \end{equation} The middle two identities are identities of linear functionals on the whole space \(\cX\).

definitions.name: Atoms and flavors
definitions.label: def:atom
definitions.text: For a tag $l$, selector $s$, and base point $z$ allowed at $l$, let $\mathfrak a_l(s,z)\in\cX$ be the cut profile represented by $w_l=v(s,z)v(s,z)\trans$ and $w_t=0$ for $t\ne l$. Thus its component is $v(s,z)v(s,z)\trans$ at every component incident with $l$, and zero elsewhere. Its diagonal bit is $q=\eta(w_l)$ and its role bit is $a(\mathfrak a_l(s,z))$. A generic flavor retains all base coordinates allowed at $l$. A shared-only flavor sets all $O$ blocks to zero. A pure flavor sets $S$ to zero and retains a specified subset of the allowed $O$ blocks, setting the others to zero. Every flavor retains both $\#$ and $Z$ in their entirety. At a fixed label, a parameter test samples all retained bits independently and uniformly. Its tester summary is the list of all individual quadratic tester values. In addition to this summary we may record the basis values of $T(\mathfrak a_l(s,z),\cdot)|_{C_i}$.

definitions.label: def:small-table
definitions.text: For a leaf and component, put \[ \mathcal J_{O,e}^{\pm} =\bigoplus_{i\in O}(S_{i,e}^{\pm}\oplus H_i^{\pm}). \] For two leaves belonging to units $A,B$, a small table specifies the two cross bilinear forms on $\mathcal J_{A,e}^+\times\mathcal J_{B,e}^-$ and $\mathcal J_{B,e}^+\times\mathcal J_{A,e}^-$, for every $e$. It is admissible for two orientations if it agrees with their actual cross Grams whenever at least one of the two table arguments is a stored pin direction. Let $H_{i,0}^{\pm}$ be the projection of the appropriate pin space onto $H_i^{\pm}$, and fix a complement $H_i^{\pm}=H_{i,0}^{\pm}\oplus H_{i,1}^{\pm}$. The complement is called private. We identify the two channel coordinate copies with $\F^h$ in their common column order. The table is injecting if, for each component, each orientation of the roles $O,O'$, and $i\in O,z\in O'$, the following maps are injective: \begin{align} D_{O,e}^+\cap\cB_i&\longrightarrow\F^h/H_{z,0}^+, &d&\longmapsto\text{table evaluation of $d$ against $Y_z$},\\ D_{O,e}^-\cap\cB_i&\longrightarrow\F^h/H_{z,0}^-, &d&\longmapsto\text{table evaluation of $d$ against $X_z$}. \notag \end{align} These quotient conditions use the standard coordinate dot pairing on the channels. For instance, the first image is zero in the quotient precisely when it pairs to zero with all vectors annihilating $H_{z,0}^+$.

A componentwise cover is a collection of subspaces \(T_e^\pm\subseteq V_e^\pm\). It covers a tensor \(\xi=(\xi_e)_e\) if \[ \xi_e\in T_e^+\otimes V_e^-+V_e^+\otimes T_e^- \quad\text{for every }e. \] Its two mode dimensions are \(\sum_e\dim T_e^+\) and \(\sum_e\dim T_e^-\); its total dimension is their sum.

definitions.name: Common prediction
definitions.label: def:prediction
definitions.text: A prediction along a subsequence consists of common binary functions \[ f_{i,n}(l,q,\cdot):\Omega_{l,q,n}\longrightarrow\F, \qquad i=1,2, \] a set of units of mass at least \(10^{-6}\), and, on every unit in this set, choices \[ \lambda_i\in C_i^{\mathrm{old}},\qquad \alpha_i\in\F,\qquad {\cal E}_i\subseteq\F^b,\quad |{\cal E}_i|\le B_*, \] such that the following uniform statement holds. There is \(\varepsilon_n\to0\) for which, at both endpoints, at every label outside \({\cal E}_i\), at every tag, and in every permitted flavor, a uniform parameter atom \(x\) satisfies \begin{equation} p_i(x)=T(\lambda_i,x)+\alpha_i a(x) +f_{i,n}(l,q,\operatorname{key}(x)) \end{equation} except with probability at most \(\varepsilon_n\). The functions \(f_{i,n}\) are the same for all retained units. The marks \(\lambda_i,\alpha_i,{\cal E}_i\) may depend on the whole unit.

definitions.name: Numerical option
definitions.label: def:limit-option
definitions.text: A numerical option specifies a recipe shape with between one and seven positions on each cross edge, together with the following data: \begin{enumerate} \item the endpoint, tag, label, flavor, and diagonal bit at every position; \item the full numerical unary statuses required at those positions, including the tester summary, the role $a(\mathrm{atom})$, the basis coordinates of $T(\mathrm{atom},\cdot)|_{C_i}$, and the $p_i$ bit; \item the required within-endpoint binary evaluations, and the off-position Gram conditions defining the reference key space; \item the small tables and the finite coordinate formats in which they are written. \end{enumerate} The two sides have matching tags and diagonal bits position by position. All labels used at one endpoint are distinct. Coordinate formats of smaller dimension are padded by zeros.

definitions.name: Available generator
definitions.label: def:status-generator
definitions.text: On the cross edge $(i,j)$, an available generator consists of a vector \begin{equation} g=(q,h_{A,i},h_{B,j},\mathbf x_{A,i},\mathbf x_{B,j},p_{A,i},p_{B,j}) \end{equation} and a certificate: a common tag, a surviving label at each end, and allowed flavors giving positive overlap as in \eqref{eq:limit-positive-generator} for these entries. Entries of the tester summary not displayed in \eqref{eq:status-generator-vector} are summed over. All witnessing certificates remain available. Generators with the same numerical vector and different certificates may therefore be used as different occurrences. Sums and spans of generators refer to their numerical vectors. Let $V_{ij}$ be the binary span of these generators. Its base projection forgets the final two $p$ entries and has target \[ B_{ij}=\F\oplus\F\oplus\F\oplus \F^{\dim C_{A,i}}\oplus\F^{\dim C_{B,j}}. \]

lean.scopeText:
Hadwiger's conjecture predicts $\chi(G)\le h(G)$ for every finite graph, where $h(G)$ is the largest clique-minor order. The formalization constructs arbitrarily large finite simple counterexamples with independence number at most two. For a graph on $m$ vertices it proves
$h(G)<26m/75+2/3<m/2\le\chi(G)$.
This disproves the ordinary chromatic form. The paper's fractional-chromatic strengthening and the Colin de Verdière consequence are outside this selected statement.

The Linear List Hadwiger conjecture asks for a universal linear bound on list chromatic number in terms of clique-minor size. The formalization proves that there is one integer $C\ge1$ such that every finite nonempty simple graph $G$ satisfies $\chi_{\mathrm{list}}(G)\le C h(G)$, where $h(G)$ is the largest order of a clique minor. The constant is independent of the graph.

primaryStatements.name: Base graphs
primaryStatements.label: thm:base-graphs
primaryStatements.text: There is a constant \(a>0\) such that, for every \(\beta>0\), there are arbitrarily large integers \(m\) and graphs \(H\) on \(m\) vertices with \(\alpha(H)\le2\) and the following properties. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(G\arabic*)},ref=G\arabic*] \item Every matching of size at least \(m/20\), partitioned into classes of size at most \(am\), contains two conflicting edges in different classes. \item Every matching of size at least \(\beta m\) and every vertex set of size at least \(\beta m\) contain an edge and a vertex in conflict. \item Every two vertex sets of size at least \(\beta m\) contain a cross hole. \end{enumerate} The two vertex sets in \ref{item:base-holes} may overlap.

primaryStatements.name: Fractional-colouring obstruction
primaryStatements.label: cor:fractional-spectral
primaryStatements.text: There are finite nonempty simple graphs \(G\) of arbitrarily large order for which \[ \chi_f(G)\ge \frac{|V(G)|}{\alpha(G)} \ge \frac{|V(G)|}{2} >\kappa(G)+1\ge\mu(G)+1\ge h(G). \]

primaryStatements.name: A linear list-colouring bound
primaryStatements.label: cor:list-spectral
primaryStatements.text: Let \(C\) be the absolute integer in \citet[Theorem 1.1]{OpenAILinearListHadwiger2026}. Every finite nonempty simple graph \(G\) satisfies \[ \chi_{\mathrm{list}}(G)\le C\bigl(\mu(G)+1\bigr). \]

primaryStatements.name: Finite tree principle
primaryStatements.label: mt:finite-tree
primaryStatements.text: For each index \(s\), let \(P_{1,s},\ldots,P_{k,s}\) be positive subspaces in a Lorentz space, whose dimension may depend on \(s\). Fix a set \(\mathcal D\) of pairs of distinct labels, and assume \[ \sup_s d_{\mathbb H}(F_{P_{i,s}},F_{P_{j,s}})\le D<\infty \qquad (\{i,j\}\in\mathcal D). \] After passing to a subsequence, there are a finite combinatorial tree \(T\) and a nonempty connected vertex set \(S_i\subseteq V(T)\) for every label, with the following properties. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item \(S_i\cap S_j\ne\varnothing\) for every \(\{i,j\}\in\mathcal D\). \item For every vertex \(x\), called a bag, choose any Lorentz-orthonormal basis in every \(P_{i,s}\) with \(x\in S_i\). The Gram matrix of the concatenated list has operator norm bounded uniformly in \(s\). The bound depends only on \(k,D\), and not on the dimensions or on the bases. \end{enumerate} In particular, mutually orthogonal blocks can always be required to have intersecting subtrees.

primaryStatements.name: A common bag
primaryStatements.label: mt:common-bag
primaryStatements.text: Suppose the hypotheses of \Cref{mt:single-bag,mt:weighted-bag} hold in the same tree. Suppose additionally that \(S_e\cap S_v\ne\varnothing\) whenever the edge \(e\) and the vertex \(v\in V_0\) conflict. If \(q\le cm/4\), there is a vertex \(x\) such that \begin{equation} |\{v\in V_0:x\notin S_v\}|<5q, \qquad \sum_{e:\,x\in S_e}w_e\ge\frac{cm}{2}. \end{equation} If all edges of \(\mathcal E\) have both endpoints in \(V_0\) and \(q\le cm/30\), deleting every edge incident with a missing vertex leaves bag weight at least \(cm/3\).

primaryStatements.name: Matrix obstruction
primaryStatements.label: thm:matrix-obstruction
primaryStatements.text: For every $a\in(0,1]$ there are constants $\beta_0(a)>0$ and $m_0(a)\in\mathbb N$ with the following property. Let $0<\beta\le\beta_0(a)$, let $m\ge m_0(a)$, and let $G$ be an $m$-vertex graph satisfying the following conditions: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item Every matching of size at least $m/20$, partitioned into classes of size at most $am$, contains two conflicting edges in different classes. \item Every matching of size at least $\beta m$ and every vertex set of size at least $\beta m$ contain a conflicting edge--point pair. \item Every two vertex sets of size at least $\beta m$ have a cross hole. \end{enumerate} Then there is $s_0=s_0(G,a,\beta)$ such that, for every integer $s\ge s_0$, every real symmetric well-signed matrix $M$ for the clique blow-up $G[K_s]$ with exactly one negative eigenvalue satisfies \[ \rank M>\frac{ms}{2}+1. \] Consequently $\mu(G[K_s])+1<ms/2$ for all these $s$.

primaryStatements.name: Distribution tests
primaryStatements.label: thm:distribution-tests
primaryStatements.text: There is a constant \(\eta_{\rm col}>0\), depending only on the early parameters and \(M\), with the following property. For every sufficiently large \(n\), the law \(\pi\) constructed above satisfies both conclusions. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item Let \((A,c)\) have a probability law on units marked by a colour in any fixed finite palette. The colour may be randomized conditional on \(A\). papers.title: A linear list-coloring bound in terms of the Hadwiger number
papers.abstract: We prove that every finite nonempty graph G satisfies $\chi_{\mathrm{list}}(G)\le C h(G)$ for an absolute integer C, where $h(G)$ is the largest order of a clique minor. This resolves the Linear List Hadwiger conjecture affirmatively.
papers.familySummary: Disproves Hadwiger's conjecture even for fractional coloring: arbitrarily large finite simple graphs with independence number at most two satisfy $\chi_f(G)\gt h(G)$, where $h(G)$ is the largest clique-minor order. Also disproves the fractional Colin de Verdière chromatic bound $\chi_f(G)\le\mu(G)+1$. In the positive direction, every finite nonempty graph satisfies $\chi_{\mathrm{list}}(G)\le C h(G)$ for a universal constant C.

primaryStatements.text: There is an absolute integer $C\ge1$ such that every finite nonempty simple graph $G$ satisfies \[ \ell(G)\le C h(G). \]

primaryStatements.name: Fractional minor bound
primaryStatements.label: thm:fractional
primaryStatements.text: Every graph $P$ satisfies $f(P)\le4h(P)$.

primaryStatements.name: Ordinary-chromatic connectivity extraction
primaryStatements.label: thm:ordinary-extraction
primaryStatements.text: If $k\ge1$ is an integer and $\chi(P)\ge7k$, then $P$ has a $k$-connected subgraph $J$ with $\chi(J)\ge\chi(P)-6k$.

primaryStatements.name: Grouping terminals
primaryStatements.label: thm:grouping
primaryStatements.text: There is an absolute integer $\gamma\ge1$ such that the following holds. In a $\gamma m$-connected graph, every partition of $m\ge1$ distinct terminals into nonempty groups can be realized by pairwise disjoint connected vertex sets, one containing each group.

primaryStatements.label: prop:small-list
primaryStatements.text: There are an absolute positive integer $L$ and an absolute integer $t_0$ such that, for every integer $t\ge t_0$ and every graph $G$, \[ h(G)<t,\qquad |V(G)|\le t^{11/10} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \ell(G)\le Lt. \]

primaryStatements.label: density:list-district
primaryStatements.text: Fix \(K\) and \(D_K\) as in Lemma \ref{lem:district}. For all sufficiently large integers \(t\), if \[ h(P)<t,\qquad \ell(P)>2D_Kt+2, \] then \(P\) contains an induced \((Kt)\)-connected subgraph of order at most \(t^{1.06}\).

primaryStatements.label: thm:recursive-woven
primaryStatements.text: There are absolute positive integers $K,Q$ such that, for every integer $a\ge1$, every $Ka$-connected graph $P$ with $\ell(P)\ge Qa$ is $(a,3a)$-woven.

definitions.label: def:woven
definitions.text: For integers $a\ge1$ and $b\ge0$, a graph $J$ is $(a,b)$-woven if the following holds. Prescribe $a$ distinct roots $R=\{r_1,\ldots,r_a\}$ and at most $b$ pairs $(x_1,y_1),\ldots,(x_p,y_p)$ of vertices of $J$. The endpoint sets $\{x_i,y_i\}$ must be disjoint for different $i$, but $x_i=y_i$ is allowed, and endpoints may belong to $R$. Then there are a $K_a$ model with bags $M_1,\ldots,M_a$ satisfying $r_j\in M_j$, and pairwise vertex-disjoint $x_i$--$y_i$ paths $Q_i$, such that \[ V(Q_i)\cap\bigcup_{j=1}^a M_j \ \subseteq\ R\cap\{x_i,y_i\}\qquad(1\le i\le p). \] For a coincident pair the path is the single prescribed vertex. Because the model bags are disjoint and contain all the roots, any allowed intersection at $r_j$ belongs to the designated bag $M_j$.

lean.scopeText:
Hadwiger's conjecture predicts $\chi(G)\le h(G)$ for every finite graph, where $h(G)$ is the largest clique-minor order. The formalization constructs arbitrarily large finite simple counterexamples with independence number at most two. For a graph on $m$ vertices it proves
$h(G)<26m/75+2/3<m/2\le\chi(G)$.
This disproves the ordinary chromatic form. The paper's fractional-chromatic strengthening and the Colin de Verdière consequence are outside this selected statement.

The Linear List Hadwiger conjecture asks for a universal linear bound on list chromatic number in terms of clique-minor size. The formalization proves that there is one integer $C\ge1$ such that every finite nonempty simple graph $G$ satisfies $\chi_{\mathrm{list}}(G)\le C h(G)$, where $h(G)$ is the largest order of a clique minor. The constant is independent of the graph.

papers.title: The Euclidean plane is not five-colorable
papers.abstract: We prove that every coloring of the Euclidean plane with five colors has a monochromatic unit-distance pair, with no regularity assumption on the color classes. Consequently, the chromatic number of the plane is either six or seven.
papers.familySummary: Proves that every five-coloring of the Euclidean plane has a monochromatic pair at distance one, with no restriction on the color classes. This advances the Hadwiger–Nelson problem: together with the classical seven-coloring, only six and seven remain possible chromatic numbers of the plane.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: The Euclidean plane has no proper five-coloring, even when arbitrary color classes are allowed. Consequently, \[ 6\le \chi(\R^2)\le 7. \]

primaryStatements.label: thm:transfer

primaryStatements.label: thm:weak-five
primaryStatements.text: There is no weak measurable five-coloring of the Euclidean plane.

primaryStatements.name: Positive five-color badness
primaryStatements.label: cor:positive-badness
primaryStatements.text: There is a constant $\delta>0$ with the following properties. \begin{enumerate} \item[(i)] For every coloring $c:\R^2\to\{1,\ldots,5\}$ and every normalized finitely additive left-invariant measure $\mu$ on all subsets of the plane-isometry group $E(2)$, the invariant-mean badness satisfies \[ p_5^\mu(c):=\mu\bigl(\{T\in E(2):c(T^{-1}0)=c(T^{-1}1)\}\bigr) \ge\delta, \] where $\R^2$ is identified with $\C$. \item[(ii)] If $c$ is a Lebesgue-measurable five-coloring with two linearly independent periods, then $\mathbb P(c(A)=c(A+U))\ge\delta$, where $A$ is uniform in a fundamental parallelogram and $U$ is an independent uniform unit direction. For any Lebesgue-measurable five-coloring, if the conditional square-table frequencies \[ \mathbb P\bigl(c(A_R)=c(A_R+U)\mid A_R+U\in[-R,R]^2\bigr) \qquad(R>1) \] converge as $R\to\infty$, their limit is at least $\delta$; here $A_R$ is uniform in $[-R,R]^2$ and independent of $U$. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.name: From proper to weak measurable colorings
primaryStatements.label: prop:palettes-forward
primaryStatements.text: Let \(k\) be a positive integer. If the plane admits an unrestricted proper \(k\)-coloring, then it admits a weak measurable \(k\)-coloring.

primaryStatements.name: Sixty-degree exclusion
primaryStatements.label: cor:palettes-sixty-degree
primaryStatements.text: At every fixed center \(x\), \begin{equation} P_x(f)\cap P_x(Rf)=\varnothing \qquad\text{for almost every }f\in S. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Palette cardinality
primaryStatements.label: prop:palette-size
primaryStatements.text: For every center \(x\in\R^2\), \begin{equation} 1\le\abs{P_x(e)}\le2 \qquad\text{for almost every }e\in S. \end{equation} The angular exceptional set may depend on \(x\).

definitions.name: Weak measurable coloring
definitions.label: def:weak-coloring
definitions.text: Let $k$ be a positive integer, let $S^1\subset\R^2$ be the unit circle, and let $\sigma$ be its normalized arc-length measure. A weak measurable $k$-coloring is a Lebesgue measurable function $c:\R^2\to\{1,\ldots,k\}$, with color classes $A_i=c^{-1}(\{i\})$, such that, for every $R>0$, \[ \sum_{i=1}^k\int_{B(0,R)}\int_{S^1} \ind_{A_i}(x)\ind_{A_i}(x+u)\,d\sigma(u)\,dx=0. \] The integrals use the completed product measure; equivalently, one may first choose Borel representatives of the color classes forming a partition of the plane.

definitions.label: def:spectral-groups
definitions.text: Identify the plane with $\C$, and set \[ F=\overline{\Q}\cap\R,\qquad E=F(i),\qquad K=\{u\in E:u\bar u=1\}. \] We regard $E$ as an additive discrete group and $K$ as a multiplicative discrete group. Let \[ D=\widehat{E_{\mathrm{disc}}} \] be the compact character group of $E$. A point $d\in D$ is a homomorphism from the additive group $E$ to the unit complex group $\T$. We use additive notation on $D$, so $(d+d')(z)=d(z)d'(z)$. For $a,z\in E$, put \[ (ad)(z)=d(az),\qquad \psi_z(d)=d(z). \] The subgroup of ordinary continuous characters is \begin{equation} C=j(\R^2),\qquad j(\xi)(z)=\exp(i\xi\cdot z), \end{equation} where the dot product uses the real coordinates of $z$.

definitions.label: def:spectral-wild
definitions.text:
A $K$-invariant Borel probability measure $
u$ on $D$ is called wild if $
u(C)=0$. Its Fourier coefficients are denoted by \[ f_
u(z)=\int_D\psi_z(d)\,d
u(d),\qquad z\in E. \]

definitions.name: Circle traces and maximal palettes
definitions.label: def:palettes-traces
definitions.text: For each fixed center \(x\), let \(\mathcal W_x\) be the family of vector functions in \(L^\infty(S;\R^5)\) that can be obtained as \[ b=\operatorname{w}^*\!-\!\lim_{n\to\infty} (a_i(y_n+r_ne))_{i=1}^5,\qquad y_n\to x,\quad r_n\to1, \] where every \((y_n,r_n)\) is a typical circle sampling. Constant sequences are permitted. For a label \(i\), form the essential measurable union \[ D_{x,i}=\mathop{\operatorname{ess\,union}}_{b\in\mathcal W_x} \{e:b_i(e)>0\}. \] The maximal palette is the measurable set-valued function \[ P_x(e)=\{i:e\in D_{x,i}\}, \] defined up to angular null sets.

definitions.name: Transition graph
definitions.label: def:transitions-graph
definitions.text: For $x\in\R^2$, let $\Gamma_x$ be the simple graph on $\mathcal I$ in which $ij$ is an edge precisely when, for every ball $B$ centered at $x$ with positive finite radius, \begin{equation} \limsup_{\substack{h\to0\\h\ne0}} \frac{D_{ij}(B,h)}{|h|}>0. \end{equation}

lean.scopeText: The Hadwiger–Nelson problem asks for the fewest colors needed to color the plane so that points at distance one have different colors. The formalized results prove that five colors do not suffice and that seven colors do suffice. The lower bound applies to arbitrary colorings, with no measurability or continuity assumption; the upper bound includes every boundary point of the coloring regions.

papers.title: Quasipolynomial Bounds for Arithmetic Progressions
papers.abstract: We prove Erdős's conjecture that every set of positive integers with divergent reciprocal sum contains arithmetic progressions of every finite length. More quantitatively, for every fixed k ≥ 3, we show $\displaystyle r_k(N)\le C_kN\exp\bigl(-c_k(\log N)^{\varepsilon_k}\bigr)$ with $C_k,c_k,\varepsilon_k\gt 0$, where $r_k(N)$ is the largest size of a subset of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with no nonconstant k-term arithmetic progression.
papers.familySummary: Proves Erdős's conjecture that every set of positive integers with divergent reciprocal sum contains arithmetic progressions of every finite length. Quantitatively, for each fixed k ≥ 3, every subset of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with no nonconstant k-term progression has size at most $C_kN\exp[-c_k(\log N)^{\varepsilon_k}]$, with positive constants depending only on k.
papers.subject: Combinatorics
papers.sourceAbstract: We prove Erd\H{o}s's conjecture that every set of positive integers with divergent reciprocal sum contains arithmetic progressions of every finite length. More quantitatively, for every fixed $k\ge3$, we show \[ r_k(N)\le C_kN\exp\bigl(-c_k(\log N)^{\varepsilon_k}\bigr) \] with $C_k,c_k,\varepsilon_k>0$, where $r_k(N)$ is the largest size of a subset of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with no nonconstant $k$-term arithmetic progression.

primaryStatements.label: ap:main
primaryStatements.text: For each fixed integer $k\ge3$ there are constants $C_k,c_k,\varepsilon_k>0$ such that, for every $N\ge2$, \begin{equation} r_k(N)\le C_kN\exp\bigl(-c_k(\log N)^{\varepsilon_k}\bigr). \end{equation} Equivalently, there is $A_k\ge1$ such that an $\alpha$-dense subset of $[N]$ contains a nonconstant $k$-term progression whenever \begin{equation} \log N\ge A_k\bigl(2+\log(1/\alpha)\bigr)^{A_k}, \qquad 0<\alpha\le1. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Divergent reciprocal sums
primaryStatements.label: ap:reciprocal
primaryStatements.text: Every set $A\subseteq\mathbb N$ with $\sum_{a\in A}a^{-1}=\infty$ contains nonconstant arithmetic progressions of every finite length.

primaryStatements.name: Triangular increment
primaryStatements.label: ap:increment
primaryStatements.text: There are fixed $D=D_k$, $\eta=\eta_k>0$, and polynomials with degrees depending only on $k$ having the following property. Suppose $p\ge2$, $a\ge e^{-p}$, and a progression-free input on a positive-dimensional integer box has a certificate \eqref{ap:certificate}, with width logs $Q_h=\log(2/w_h)$. If every root side is sufficiently large with logarithmic cutoff polynomial in $p$, the dimension data, and all $Q_h$, then either the hypotheses are impossible or a root slice carries a new certificate at threshold $(1+\eta)a$. The new cell retains the determining data through exact integer reparametrizations and adds at most $d_0=(2+p)^{C_k}$ fresh absolute slots together with downward preparation copies. Its dimensions $d'_i$ and width logs $Q'_i$ satisfy \begin{align} d'_i-d_i &\le d_0+P_i(p,d_{i+1},\ldots,d_D),\\ Q'_i-Q_i &\le P'_i(p,\text{all dimension forecasts},Q_{i+1},\ldots,Q_D). \end{align} The root slice cost has polynomial logarithmic bound in all the same data, now including every $Q_i$. Polynomial exponents and the fixed gain are independent of the number of increments. Gap and discount choices can be made in advance from the dimension and cut-count forecasts.

primaryStatements.name: Pathwise detection and approximation
primaryStatements.label: ap:path:detection
primaryStatements.text: Prescribe finitely many testing degrees in the fixed allowed range, local test complexities, slice costs, input caps, and accuracies. The later parameters of the one-layer construction can be chosen once so that the following assertions hold for this same ensemble, uniformly in the center and the site input. For cold-pre requests, if a cold-pre-bounded input satisfies $X_r(g)\ge a>0$, with $\log(1/a)$ bounded by cold-pre data, then $g$ correlates in uniform parent measure with an ambient atom of cold-pre complexity, and the logarithm of the reciprocal correlation has a cold-pre bound. Every $|g|\le1$ can also be approximated in $X_r$, to the prescribed cold-pre accuracy, by a linear combination of such atoms with cold-pre coefficient mass and number of terms. If $r<j$ and the requests are warm, every warm-bounded input with $X_r(g)\ge a>0$ and a warm bound for $\log(1/a)$ correlates in $\mu_c$ with an ambient atom of warm complexity, with a warm bound for the logarithm of the reciprocal correlation. The atoms, coefficient mass, and number of terms in the $X_r$ approximation also have warm bounds. These bounds may use the omission threshold but do not use $Q_j$ or the height of $W$. For a specified larger input cap, include its logarithm in the request budget and rescale. Increasing the requested accuracy, test, or path budgets changes the corresponding warm or cold-pre output logarithms polynomially. All path probabilities and testing suprema refer to the law before productive paths are selected.

primaryStatements.name: Prepared system with triangular costs
primaryStatements.label: ap:major:preparation
primaryStatements.text: Given a triangular two-box certificate, forecast dimension bounds and descending numerical budgets in the sense of Definition \ref{ap:budgets}. After polynomially many rank-cut transactions, there is a certificate with an arbitrarily small prescribed total proportional target discount such that every rank-stop probability in the actual current sampling procedure is at most its prescribed bound. The procedure may restart its tests after every transaction. The dimensions added at block $i$ are polynomial in the dimensions strictly above $i$. The increase in its width logarithm is polynomial in dimension data, $p$, and higher-level numerical budgets, and is independent of its own initial width logarithm except for carrying that logarithm additively. Root slice costs and sufficient root-side cutoffs have polynomial logarithms in the full eventual budgets.

primaryStatements.name: Forward mass
primaryStatements.label: ap:scalar:forward
primaryStatements.text: For any sufficiently small fixed $\eta>0$, a prepared certificate at threshold $a$ gives a surviving set of terminal injective paths whose expected terminal input mean, with stopped paths counted as zero, is at least $(1-\eta)a$. The input is pulled back successively and masked by no bad flag at every active layer. Its support is progression-free. At least a fraction $\eta a$ of terminal paths have mean at least $(1-2\eta)a$, after harmless adjustment of the loss constants. The rank-stop probability at layer $h$ need only have inverse logarithmic cost polynomial in the data at layers $\ge h$. Discards immediately after that layer can be requested warm-small after charging the feasible-center proportions of layers $>h$. Thus this proposition does not require a lower-layer width in a higher-layer rank budget.

primaryStatements.name: Scalar comparison
primaryStatements.label: ap:scalar:comparison
primaryStatements.text: Suppose a set of productive modular-good paths has probability at least $\tau$, with $\log(1/\tau)$ pre bounded, and each has a specified pre-cost slice. Consider bounded scores depending on site and auxiliary labels. Assume that, after partitioning into pre-count many pre-cost slices, each score is uniformly approximable at the required pre accuracy, both on actual path arguments and on the joint support of $\mathcal K$, by the same menu of bounded site functions. A bounded number of successive increases of these pre bounds is allowed. Then, outside a set of paths smaller than the productive probability, the actual scalar averages and their $\mathcal K$ integrals differ by an arbitrarily prescribed pre-small error. This holds simultaneously for a pre-count menu of scores and for path-dependent slice choices. At active layers it also holds after multiplying a score by the no-bad-flag indicator. It is valid either for normalized slice averages or with full-box mass retained, paying the explicit slice fractions. The budget is warm for passive uses and cold pre otherwise.

primaryStatements.name: Passive micro replacement
primaryStatements.label: ap:passive:replacement
primaryStatements.text: Suppose $j>s$ and the ascent format holds on a warm-inverse fraction of paths at a fixed parent and feasible center. Use the group and the two fields of Lemma \ref{ap:ascent:representation}. There is a single ambient ordinary filtered polynomial \[ g^U(u)\in G^0 \] of degree at most $s$, with no $\beta$ argument, for which a warm-inverse fraction of the productive paths have warm-cost subslices on which replacing $g_\psi$ by $g^U\circ\psi$ preserves a positive signed full-mass score of warm size, after the allowed small target discounts. Both inherited cutoff functions and all their exact determining conditions are retained.

definitions.name: Descending budgets
definitions.label: ap:budgets
definitions.text: At layer $j$, the warm data consist of $p$, forecasts for all dimensions and structural variable counts, gap parameters depending only on these data, and the widths and numerical budgets already chosen at layers strictly above $j$. A warm logarithmic bound is polynomial in these data and does not use any $Q_i$ with $i\le j$. The cold preliminary data may additionally use the current width log $Q_j$, including its forecast preparation losses, but not the eventual rank threshold, long path scale, height of the prepared value space, or parent-side cutoff at layer $j$. The late data are the perturbation, range, rank, and side choices made after all preliminary modeling and algebraic requirements at that layer. Their logarithms are polynomial in the cold preliminary budget.

definitions.name: Ascent format
definitions.label: ap:ascent:format
definitions.text: At entry to layer $j$, the following data and properties constitute the ascent format. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item A warm-cost slice of the parameter box carries a full-mass score at least $\delta$, with $\log(1/\delta)$ warm. Its positive payoff contains the fixed pulled-back input $f_0(\psi(t))$, where $0\leq f_0\leq1$. When $j\leq s$, it also contains the current factor $1_{\mathrm{no\ bad}}(t)$. Its negative payoff has multiplier $-\lambda$. \item Both payoffs use, respectively, the small and large cutoffs of the absolute slots and of all determining slots $b_i$ with $i>j$. For a determining block these are cutoffs of the actual residual \[ b_i-C_i(u,b_{\leq i-1}) \] at a bounded constant center $l_i'$ and a radius whose logarithmic loss relative to $w_i$ is warm at layer $i$. Their enlarged supports lie inside fixed padded versions of the old boxes. The block may also be restricted to a residue class of warm cost at layer $i$. Payoffs are summed over their allowed integral tuples. Each unsigned sum, with or without $f_0$, is bounded by one. \item Determining polynomials never use absolute slots. Absolute polynomials may use determining slots $b_i$ with $j<i\leq s$, but not passive slots $i>s$. The combined system has a fixed joint weighted-degree bound, with determining weights exactly $i$. Absolute weights are unchanged at passive steps and may be inflated at active steps. Once active determining slots are present, absolute weights exceed their weights. \item Polynomial extensions and determining identities are formal identities. Equality of integer slot arguments is never inferred merely from closeness of the corresponding real polynomials. \end{enumerate}

definitions.name: Controlled external fields
definitions.label: ap:active:fields
definitions.text: Let $G^0/\Gamma^0$ have controlled rational filtered data. A pair of fields \[ F^{\pm}_{\psi,u}(\theta,\widetilde t) :G^0/\Gamma^0\longrightarrow[0,1] \] is controlled if it has the following properties at every requested pre-accuracy. \begin{enumerate} \item Its Lipschitz constants on the quotient, and in the normalized real labels with all other arguments fixed, have pre-cost. In the long integer labels it is periodic with a common pre-bounded modulus for each path. The moduli belong to a pre-bounded list and divide the eventual modulus $\mathfrak M$. \item The point-value family over sites, paths, and admissible labels has a supremum-norm mesh of pre-logarithmic size. \item For fixed short labels and fixed mesh and residue arguments in the remaining labels, the family indexed by $\psi$ has a mesh in supremum norm over the sites, again of pre-logarithmic size. \end{enumerate} The bounds may charge the accuracy, the auxiliary dimensions, and the short lengths. The assertion concerns only the chart and label ranges in use. Integer labels can be represented by arbitrary integers. No mesh of polynomial orbit coefficients is required.

definitions.name: Niltests
definitions.label: prelim:niltest
definitions.text: A rational filtered nilmanifold consists of a connected, simply connected nilpotent Lie group $G$, a cocompact lattice $\Gamma$, and connected rational subgroups \[ G=G_1\supseteq G_2\supseteq\cdots\supseteq G_{s+1}=\{1\}, \qquad [G_i,G_j]\subseteq G_{i+j}. \] Put $d=\dim G$. We fix rational exponential coordinates on its Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, with rational bases of the filtered subspaces $\mathfrak g_i=\log G_i$. A polynomial map $g:\Z^n\to G$ is adapted to this filtration when $\log g$ modulo $\mathfrak g_{i+1}$ has ordinary degree at most $i$. With explicitly assigned variable weights, ordinary degree is replaced by weighted degree. A degree-$s$ niltest is $t\mapsto F(g(t)\Gamma)$, where $F$ is bounded and Lipschitz for the quotient of the right-invariant Riemannian metric that makes the declared coordinate basis orthonormal at the identity. A different metric is permitted only with a comparison constant whose logarithm is included in the complexity budget. Its complexity is at most $p$ if the dimension, logarithmic heights of the structural constants and filtered bases, and $\log(2+\|F\|_\infty+\Lip F)$ are at most $p$, and if \begin{equation} l\Z^d\subseteq\log\Gamma\subseteq l^{-1}\Z^d \quad\text{for some integer }1\leq l\leq e^p. \end{equation} There is no coefficient bound on $g$. On $\Z/N\Z$ the evaluation uses representatives $0,\ldots,N-1$. Degree-zero tests are constants. The group of dimension zero is allowed.

definitions.name: Patch
definitions.label: counting:patch
definitions.text: A degree-$s$ patch on integer parameters $u$ is a function \begin{equation} B(u)=\sum_{b\in\Z^d}\Phi(S_u(b)), \qquad S_u(b)_i=b_i-A_i(u,b_1,\ldots,b_{i-1}). \end{equation} The slots $b_i$ have nondecreasing integer weights $1\leq w_i\leq s$; parameters have weight $1$; and $A_i$ has weighted degree at most $w_i$. The function $\Phi:\R^d\to[0,1]$ is Lipschitz and supported in $[-1/4,1/4]^d$. The rank is $d$. A logarithmic complexity bound bounds the number of parameters, the rank, and $\log(2+\Lip(\Phi))$, but does not bound the coefficients of the $A_i$. Rank zero includes $B=1$.

definitions.name: Parameter slice
definitions.label: counting:slice
definitions.text: A parameter slice of an integer box is a subbox intersected with one coordinatewise residue class modulo a common positive integer, followed by affine reindexing as a box. Logarithmic cost $P$ means that each new side contains at least an $e^{-P}$ proportion of the corresponding old side, counting the modulus. Successive slice costs add. The affine map is injective and sends a nonconstant integer progression to a nonconstant integer progression.

definitions.name: Rank at scale $H$
definitions.label: sampling:rank
definitions.text: The system has rank at least $R$ if, for every $h$ and every integer row $a\in\Z^{d_h}$ with $\|a\|\le R$ and $a|_{W_h}\ne0$, the homogeneous degree-$h$ part of $aC_h$ cannot be written as a polynomial with coefficient bounds $R/H^\nu$ plus a rational polynomial whose coefficients have a common denominator at most $R$.

lean.scopeText:
Erdős's reciprocal-sum conjecture asks whether every set of positive integers with divergent reciprocal sum contains arithmetic progressions of every finite length. The formalization proves this statement: for every requested length, such a set contains a progression with positive common difference.

The selected theorem is the reciprocal-sum consequence. The paper's quantitative upper bound for the largest progression-free subset of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ is outside this statement.

papers.title: Quantitative Superexponential Bounds for van der Waerden Numbers
papers.abstract: We prove that there are absolute constants c > 0 and K0 such that $W_r(k)\gt k^{ck\lfloor\log_2 r\rfloor}$ for every $k\ge K_0$ and r ≥ 2. Consequently $W_r(k)^{1/k}\to\infty$ for each fixed r ≥ 2, giving a quantitative positive resolution of Erdős's superexponential-growth question, including the two-color case.
papers.familySummary: Resolves Erdős's superexponential-growth question for van der Waerden numbers. If $W_r(k)$ is the least interval length forcing a monochromatic k-term progression in every r-coloring, then $W_r(k)\gt k^{ck\lfloor\log_2 r\rfloor}$ for an absolute c > 0, all r ≥ 2 and sufficiently large k, uniformly in r. In particular, $W_r(k)^{1/k}\to\infty$ for each fixed r.
papers.subject: Combinatorics
papers.sourceAbstract: We prove that there are absolute constants $c>0$ and $K_0$ such that $W_r(k)>k^{ck\lfloor\log_2 r\rfloor}$ for every $k\ge K_0$ and $r\ge2$. Consequently $W_r(k)^{1/k}\to\infty$ for each fixed $r\ge2$, giving a quantitative positive resolution of Erd\H{o}s's superexponential-growth question, including the two-color case.

primaryStatements.label: main:intro
primaryStatements.text: There is an absolute integer $K_0$ such that, for every integer $k\ge K_0$ and every integer $r\ge2$, \[ W_r(k)>k^{c k\lfloor\log_2r\rfloor}, \qquad c=10^{-5}. \]

primaryStatements.name: Outer-color dichotomy
primaryStatements.label: dichotomy:main
primaryStatements.text: For every sufficiently large $k$, the coloring $c_0$ from \Cref{outer:pullback} has the following property. Every cyclic progression $n_j=n_0+jd$, $0\le j<k$, with $d\ne0$ in $G$, satisfies at least one of these alternatives: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item each bit occurs among $c_0(n_0),\ldots,c_0(n_{k-1})$ at least $\gamma k$ times; \item there are $A,B\in\R^D$ such that $\tilde y(n_j)=A+jB$ for all $0\le j<k$. \end{enumerate} The threshold on $k$ is absolute.

primaryStatements.name: Balanced outer coloring
primaryStatements.label: outer:coloring
primaryStatements.text: For all sufficiently large $k$, there is a map $c_*:\cL\to\{0,1\}$ with the following properties. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item In every cyclic progression having at least $\delta k$ light positions, each bit occurs on at least one quarter of its light positions when labels are colored by $c_*$. \item In every eligible recorded pattern of \Cref{count:eligible}, each bit occurs on at least one quarter of its regular positions. \end{enumerate} The threshold on $k$ is absolute.

primaryStatements.name: A cyclic two-coloring
primaryStatements.label: perturb:cyclic
primaryStatements.text: There is an absolute integer $K_0$ such that, for every integer $k\ge K_0$, the construction in \Cref{sec:setup} gives an integer \[ N=q^D\ge k^{ck},\qquad c=10^{-5}, \] and a coloring $C:\Z/N\Z\to\{0,1\}$ for which no progression $n_0,n_0+d,\ldots,n_0+(k-1)d$ with $d\ne0$ in $\Z/N\Z$ is monochromatic.

primaryStatements.name: Digit product
primaryStatements.label: transfer:product
primaryStatements.text: Let $N,k\ge2$ be integers. Suppose that a coloring $C:\Z/N\Z\to\{0,1\}$ has no monochromatic progression $a,a+d,\ldots,a+(k-1)d$ with $d\ne0$ in $\Z/N\Z$. Then, for every positive integer $m$, \[ W_{2^m}(k)>N^m. \] Consequently $W_r(k)>N^{\lfloor\log_2r\rfloor}$ for every integer $r\ge2$.

primaryStatements.label: transfer:large-r
primaryStatements.text: For every pair of integers $r\ge256$ and $k\ge3$, \[ W_r(k)>\exp\!\left(\frac{(\log r)^2}{64\log2}\right). \]

primaryStatements.label: transfer:limits
primaryStatements.text: With integer parameters in both infima, \[ \lim_{k\to\infty} \inf_{\substack{r\in\Z\\r\ge2}} \frac{\log W_r(k)}{k\log r}=\infty, \qquad \lim_{r\to\infty} \inf_{\substack{k\in\Z\\k\ge3}} \frac{\log W_r(k)}{\log r}=\infty. \] In particular, $W_r(k)^{1/k}\to\infty$ for every fixed integer $r\ge2$, and $W_r(k)/r^A\to\infty$ as $r\to\infty$ for every fixed integer $k\ge3$ and every fixed real $A>0$.

primaryStatements.label: upper:finite
primaryStatements.text: Define $F(r,1)=1$ and $F(r,2)=r+1$ for every integer $r\ge1$. For $k\ge3$, with $r$ and $k$ fixed, define \begin{equation} m_0=1,\qquad m_{t+1}=2m_tF(r^{m_t},k-1)\quad(0\le t<r),\qquad F(r,k)=m_r. \end{equation} Then, for all positive integers $r,k$, \[ W_r(k)\le F(r,k)<\infty. \] The boundary parameter values are exactly \[ W_r(1)=1,\qquad W_r(2)=r+1,\qquad W_1(k)=k. \]

definitions.name: Eligible local patterns
definitions.label: count:eligible
definitions.text: Choose $x,y\in\T^D$ and $u,v\in\R^D$, and form \begin{equation} X_z=x+\frac z h(t+u),\qquad Y_z=y+\frac z h(\lambda t+v)\qquad(0\le z<h) \quad\text{in }\T^D. \end{equation} A position $z$ is regular if $\rho(Y_{z,i})\ge\eta$ in every rotating coordinate; if there are no rotating coordinates, every position is regular. Record $L(X_z,Y_z)$ at a regular position and a dummy symbol $*$ otherwise. The resulting word in $(\cL\cup\{*\})^h$ is eligible for $h,t$ if it admits a realization satisfying all of the following: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item At least $h/2$ positions are regular, and the full labels at those positions are pairwise distinct. \item $|u_i|\le H_x$ for every $i$, and $|v_i|\le H$ in every rotating coordinate. \item In every stationary coordinate $i$, one has $|v_i|\le |V(Y_{z,i})|$ at every regular position $z$. \end{enumerate} The recorded word is the pattern; different realizations of one word do not define additional patterns.

lean.scopeText: Let $W(r,k)$ be the least interval length forcing a monochromatic $k$-term arithmetic progression in every coloring with at most $r$ colors. The formalized result gives an absolute threshold $K$ such that $W(r,k)>k^{k\lfloor\log_2 r\rfloor/100000}$ for all $k\ge K$ and $r\ge2$. It also establishes the associated growth limits, finiteness, and boundary values. The sharper intermediate estimates used in the paper are not part of the described formalization.

papers.title: A counterexample to Sidorenko's conjecture
papers.abstract: We disprove Sidorenko's conjecture with a bipartite graph on 35 vertices and 66 edges: its homomorphism density in some finite simple graph is smaller than the conjectured lower bound. The same connected graph also disproves the forcing conjecture: at one fixed density, asymptotically matching the edge and pattern densities does not imply quasirandomness.
papers.familySummary: Disproves Sidorenko's conjecture with a connected bipartite pattern on 35 vertices and 66 edges that occurs less frequently than in a random graph of the same edge density. The same pattern disproves the forcing conjecture of Skokan and Thoma: matching its density and the edge density of a constant graphon need not force quasirandomness.
papers.subject: Combinatorics
papers.sourceAbstract: We disprove Sidorenko's conjecture with a bipartite graph on \(35\) vertices and \(66\) edges: its homomorphism density in some finite simple graph is smaller than the conjectured lower bound. The same connected graph also disproves the forcing conjecture: at one fixed density, asymptotically matching the edge and pattern densities does not imply quasirandomness.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let \(H\) be the incidence graph of the \(22\) triples on \(13\) points in Table \ref{tab:complex}. This bipartite graph has \(35\) vertices and \(66\) edges. There is a finite simple undirected graph \(G\) with at least one edge such that \[ t(H,G)<p(G)^{66}. \]

primaryStatements.name: Amplification and injective supersaturation
primaryStatements.label: cor:amplification
primaryStatements.text: For the same graph \(H\) as in Theorem \ref{thm:main}, the following hold. \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item For every \(c>0\), there is a finite simple undirected graph \(F\) with \(p(F)>0\) such that \[ t(H,F)<c\,p(F)^{66}. \] \item There are \(p_*\in(0,1)\), \(\delta_*>0\), and finite simple undirected graphs \(F_s\) of orders \(n_s\to\infty\) for which \(d_s=|E(F_s)|/\binom{n_s}{2}\to p_*\) and, for all sufficiently large \(s\), \[ \operatorname{Inj}(H,F_s) \le(1-\delta_*)(n_s)_{35}d_s^{66}. \] \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.name: Failure of the forcing conjecture
primaryStatements.label: cor:forcing
primaryStatements.text: For the same connected bipartite graph \(H\) of Theorem \ref{thm:main}, there are \(p\in(0,1)\) and a nonconstant graphon \(W\) such that \[ t(K_2,W)=p,\qquad t(H,W)=p^{66}. \] Consequently, \(H\) is not \(p\)-forcing at this density and hence is not forcing, despite being bipartite and containing a cycle.

primaryStatements.label: prop:complex
primaryStatements.text: The complex has the following properties. \begin{enumerate} \item Every pair in $E$ lies in exactly two faces, $|E|=33$, and the face-neighbor graph is connected. \item For each bit position, each of its two classes consists of $11$ faces covering all $13$ points. Each class has an ordering in which every face after the first shares a pair with an earlier face and introduces exactly one new point. \item Every $a_e$ is at least $1/3$, and some $a_e$ is greater than $1/3$. \item Color refinement of $H$, starting with a separate color for each part, eventually gives distinct colors to all vertices within either part. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.label: prop:negative-kernel
primaryStatements.text: Assuming Lemma \ref{lem:rank-layer}, there is a symmetric kernel $U:\Omega\times\Omega\to[0,1]$ on a finite probability space with mean $\mu>0$ such that \begin{equation} t(H,U)<\mu^{66}. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.label: prop:transverse-limit
primaryStatements.text: For every fixed even $D\geq12$, every activity pattern $B\subseteq\mathscr C$, and every prescribed set of incidence signs, \begin{equation} \E\left[\1_{\mathcal T} \prod_{(i,j)\in B}K_{\xi_{ij}}(X_i-Y_j)\right] =\E_\eta\prod_{j\in J}\prod_{\{i,k\}\subseteq A_j} (1+c_0\eta_{\{i,k\}}\xi_{ij}\xi_{kj})+o(1), \end{equation} where the $\eta_e$ are independent uniform signs. At each fixed $D$, the error is uniform over all activity patterns and incidence signs.

primaryStatements.name: Mass of ordered triple orbits
primaryStatements.label: prop:triple-orbits
primaryStatements.text: For three independent uniform Lagrangians, every feasible dimensional profile has probability $O_D(q^{-C})$. More strongly, there is a constant $\kappa_D>0$, independent of $q$ and of the particular orbit, such that for every occurring ordered symplectic orbit $\mathcal O$ of that profile, \begin{equation} \kappa_D q^{-C}\le \P\{(L_1,L_2,L_3)\in\mathcal O\} \le \kappa_D^{-1}q^{-C}. \end{equation} The constant can be chosen for all odd primes. Moreover, conditional on any fixed ordered pair having intersection dimension $h$, the probability that an independent third Lagrangian completes a specified dimensional profile is \begin{equation} O_D(q^{-C+b(h)}). \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Three active incidences
primaryStatements.label: prop:planted-gain
primaryStatements.text: For a local profile $(h_1,h_2,h_3,c)$, we choose one pointwise gain exponent independent of \(q\) as follows. Let \(\mathcal U\) be the union, over all odd prime fields and all ordered orbits of this profile, of the parameter tuples arising from actual quadruples $(L_1,L_2,L_3,Y)$ with the stated point profile and $\dim(L_i\cap Y)=r$, using Equations \eqref{eq:planted-reduced-parameters} and \eqref{eq:planted-subspace-parameters}. Their integer entries are bounded at fixed \(D\), so \(\mathcal U\) is finite. If \(\mathcal U\) is empty, the face factor is zero over every odd prime field. Otherwise the face factor with three active incidences is $O(q^g)$ uniformly over all triples in the profile, where \begin{equation} g=\max_{\text{tuple}\in\mathcal U}\left\{ g_C+\sum_i b(s_i)-\delta P-\sum_i p_i^2-vw -\sum_i b(t_i)+b(v)\right\}, \end{equation} so the selected exponent is independent of \(q\). Every tuple in \(\mathcal U\) satisfies the following necessary constraints: \begin{equation} \begin{gathered} 0\le u\le\min(c,r),\quad 0\le r'=r-u\le d, \quad |\delta|\le c,\quad d-\delta=2r',\\ P+T=\sum_i s_i\le d,\qquad 0\le t_i\le p_i+\delta,\qquad 0\le v\le p_i+\delta\quad(1\le i\le3),\qquad w\ge0. \end{gathered} \end{equation} In particular $T\le P+3\delta$ and $d+3\delta\ge0$. These conditions are not claimed sufficient for realizability.

lean.scopeText: Sidorenko's conjecture predicts that every bipartite graph $H$ has homomorphism density at least the host graph's edge density raised to $|E(H)|$. The formalization disproves this for the paper's fixed bipartite graph with $35$ vertices and $66$ edges: it constructs a nonempty finite simple host graph with $t(H,G)<t(K_2,G)^{66}$. The separate forcing-conjecture consequence in the paper is outside this statement.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: There exists $q_0$ such that, for every prime $q\ge q_0$, there is a finite intersecting $(q+1)$-partite $(q+1)$-uniform hypergraph $H$ with \[ |V_1|=\cdots=|V_{q+1}|=q+1, \qquad \tau(H)=q+1. \] Every vertex belongs to an edge.

primaryStatements.label: cor:tree-cover
primaryStatements.text: For every sufficiently large prime $q$, there is a finite complete graph with a $(q+1)$-edge-coloring whose vertices require exactly $q+1$ monochromatic trees to cover. The same minimum holds for connected monochromatic subgraphs.

primaryStatements.name: Deterministic reduction
primaryStatements.label: prop:deterministic-reduction
primaryStatements.text: Let $q\geq4$ be a prime power. Suppose a compatible collection of valid tuples in $\mathbb F_q^2$ satisfies occupancy, concentration of core covers, and the local condition with parameters $0<\rho<1$ and $B\geq0$. If \begin{equation} \rho q>2(1+B), \end{equation} then there is an intersecting $(q+1)$-partite $(q+1)$-uniform hypergraph with exactly $q+1$ nonisolated vertices in each part and cover number $q+1$. Its edges are in bijection with the set $X$ in \eqref{eq:det-core}.

primaryStatements.name: Robust deletion estimates
primaryStatements.label: thm:deletion
primaryStatements.text: Fix $k\ge1$ and $K\ge0$. For each $q$, let $\mathsf Q_q$ be a probability law on the same sets as $\mathsf U_{q,k}$ such that \[ \mathsf Q_q(D)\le e^{Kq}\mathsf U_{q,k}(D) \quad\text{for every }D. \] Then the following assertions hold as $q\to\infty$. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item The empirical probability measure $q^{-2}\sum_{x\in A}\delta_{i_D(x)}$ converges in probability, in total variation, to the Poisson distribution with mean $k$. \item Write $\mu=e^{-k}$. For every fixed $\lambda,\eta>0$, the probability that at least $\eta q$ lines $\ell\in\mathcal L\setminus D$ satisfy \[ \left|\frac{|\ell\cap R_D|}{q}-\mu\right|\ge\lambda \] tends to zero. \item For every fixed $\delta>0$, the probability that there is a set $C\subseteq\mathcal L\setminus D$ with $|C|\le q$ which covers $R_D$ and leaves at least $\delta q^2$ points of $A$ uncovered tends to zero. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.name: Concentration of core covers
primaryStatements.label: cor:core-pencil
primaryStatements.text: Assume the laws of Theorem \ref{thm:deletion}, and let $q$ tend to infinity through primes. For each fixed $\zeta>0$, with probability tending to one, every set $C\subseteq\mathcal L\setminus D$ of at most $q$ lines covering $R_D$ has at least $(1-\zeta)q$ members through a common projective point.

primaryStatements.label: prop:candidate-graph
primaryStatements.text: There are constants $c_*>0$ and $C_*<\infty$ such that, with probability $1-o(1)$, the following assertions hold simultaneously, with $\beta=1/8$ and $c_0=1/5$: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item $c_*q\le |Q_g|\le q$ for every direction $g$. \item Every vertex has degree at most $C_*q$, and has at most $q^\beta$ neighbors in each slot. \item For every $v$ there is a set $J(v)$ of at most $q^\beta$ vertices such that $|N(v)\cap N(w)|\le q^\beta$ for $w\notin J(v)$. Every member of $J(v)$ is adjacent to $v$ or is in its slot. \item At most $\lceil\log q\rceil$ constituents pass through any affine point, counting multiplicity. Every line other than one of the $M_g^1$ has at least $c_0q$ points outside $\bigcup_gM_g^1$. \end{enumerate} Consequently the event that these assertions hold and that $M_g^0\ne M_g^1$ for every $g$ has probability $e^{-1}+o(1)$.

primaryStatements.name: Selection with bounded cylinder probabilities
primaryStatements.label: sel:selection
primaryStatements.text: Fix constants $c_*,C_*>0$ and $0<c_0\le1$, and put $\beta=1/8$. For each sufficiently large integer $q$, let a finite graph have its vertex set partitioned into $n=2(q+1)$ slots $Q_i$, with no edge within a slot. Write $N(v)$ for the neighborhood of a vertex. Suppose that \begin{align} c_*q\le |Q_i|\le q,&\qquad |N(v)|\le C_*q, \qquad |N(v)\cap Q_i|\le q^\beta,\\ |J(v)|\le q^\beta,&\qquad |N(v)\cap N(w)|\le q^\beta\quad(w\notin J(v)), \end{align} where every $w\in J(v)$ is either adjacent to $v$ or in its slot. There are constants $K_*,\rho>0$, depending only on $c_*,C_*,c_0$, and a random procedure which either fails or returns an independent transversal $(V_i)_{i\in I_0}$, where $I_0$ is the set of slots and $V_i\in Q_i$. If $\mathcal A$ denotes its event of returning a transversal, then \begin{equation} \Prb(\mathcal A)=1-o(1). \end{equation} For any $s$ distinct slots $i_1,\ldots,i_s$ and any prescribed vertices $v_j\in Q_{i_j}$, \begin{equation} \Prb\bigl(\mathcal A, V_{i_j}=v_j\ (1\le j\le s)\bigr) \le (K_*/q)^s. \end{equation} Suppose also that the slots are indexed by $(g,k)$, with two slots for each direction $g$ of an affine plane of order $q$. Associate to each vertex in slot $(g,k)$ a line of direction $g$, injectively within that slot. For every affine line $\ell$, let $T_\ell\subseteq\ell$ be a fixed set of at least $c_0q$ points. From $T_\ell$ remove every point on a selected line different from $\ell$, and call the remaining set $T_\ell^{\rm fin}$. Then the same procedure satisfies \begin{equation} \Prb\bigl(\mathcal A, \min_\ell |T_\ell^{\rm fin}|<\rho q\bigr) =o(1). \end{equation} The errors in \eqref{sel:success} and \eqref{sel:occupancy-conclusion} are uniform in all the stated input data. By the injectivity within a slot, \eqref{sel:cylinder} also holds for prescribed candidate lines.

primaryStatements.name: Domination of the deletion-line law
primaryStatements.label: sel:deletion-domination
primaryStatements.text: Let $D$ consist of the selected split lines and the lines $M_g^1$ in the preceding experiment. Conditional on $\mathcal A$, the law of $D$ is dominated pointwise by $\exp(O(q))$ times the uniform law on sets containing three distinct lines in each direction.

lean.scopeText:
Ryser's covering conjecture predicts that an intersecting $r$-partite hypergraph has a vertex cover of size at most $r-1$. The formalization proves that every sufficiently large prime $q$ has a finite intersecting $(q+1)$-partite, $(q+1)$-uniform hypergraph with covering number $q+1$ and exactly $q+1$ nonisolated vertices in each part. Thus the conjecture fails even with equal part sizes. The prime threshold is existential.

Ryser's covering conjecture predicts $	au\le(r-1)
u$ for an $r$-partite hypergraph, where $	au$ and $
u$ are its covering and matching numbers. The formalized constructions give finite intersecting $r$-partite $r$-uniform hypergraphs with $
u=1$ and $	au=r$, contradicting the bound. The ranks have the form $r=p^n+1$: one fixed prime $p\equiv2\pmod3$ works for all sufficiently large prime degrees $n$, and a second result covers every sufficiently large such prime $p$ and every sufficiently large odd $n$, with the degree threshold allowed to depend on $p$. Infinitely many ranks occur. Equal part sizes and numerical thresholds are not asserted.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: There exists $s_0$ such that, for every prime $s\ge s_0$ with $s\equiv2\pmod3$, there is an integer $n_0(s)\ge3$ with the following property. primaryStatements.label: cor:tree-cover
primaryStatements.text: Let $s_0$ and $n_0(s)$ be as in Theorem \ref{thm:main}. For every prime $s\ge s_0$ with $s\equiv2\pmod3$ and every odd integer $n\ge n_0(s)$, put $r=s^n+1$. There is a finite simple complete graph with an $r$-edge-coloring for which the minimum number of monochromatic trees needed to cover its vertices is exactly $r$. The same minimum holds with connected monochromatic subgraphs or maximal monochromatic components in place of trees.

primaryStatements.name: Uniform incidence saving
primaryStatements.label: thm:incidence
primaryStatements.text: There exist absolute constants $\kappa\in(0,1/10)$ and $Q$ with the following property. Suppose that $q\ge Q$ is a prime power and every proper subfield of $\F_q$ has order at most $q^{1/3}$. If $P$ and $\mathcal L$ are sets of projective points and projective lines over $\F_q$ satisfying \begin{equation} |P|,|\mathcal L|\le q^{1+\kappa}, \end{equation} then \begin{equation} I(P,\mathcal L)\le q^{3/2-\kappa}. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Compatible translates from independent pools
primaryStatements.label: thm:selection
primaryStatements.text: For every positive integer $D$ there is a positive integer $K=K(D)$ with the following property. Let $q$ tend to infinity through prime powers. For each $q$, let $n\le Dq$, and for $1\le i\le n$ let $W_i\subseteq\F_q^2$ and let $D_i$ be a set of directions, with \[ |W_i|\le D,\qquad |D_i|\le D. \] Assume that each direction belongs to $D_i$ for at most $D$ indices $i$. For distinct indices $i,j$, declare the translates $b+W_i$ and $b'+W_j$ to conflict if there are $u\in W_i$, $v\in W_j$, and $d\in D_i\cup D_j$ such that \[ (b+u)-(b'+v)\in d. \] For each $i$, draw $K$ independent uniform shifts $b_{i,1},\ldots,b_{i,K}\in\F_q^2$, independently for all indices. With probability tending to one, one can choose $k_i\in\{1,\ldots,K\}$ for every $i$ so that the translates $b_{i,k_i}+W_i$ have no conflicts. The convergence is uniform over all data satisfying the stated bounds.

primaryStatements.label: con-intersection
primaryStatements.text: The hypergraph \(H\) is intersecting. Furthermore, all the edges in its displayed parametrization are distinct.

lean.scopeText:
Ryser's covering conjecture predicts that an intersecting $r$-partite hypergraph has a vertex cover of size at most $r-1$. The formalization proves that every sufficiently large prime $q$ has a finite intersecting $(q+1)$-partite, $(q+1)$-uniform hypergraph with covering number $q+1$ and exactly $q+1$ nonisolated vertices in each part. Thus the conjecture fails even with equal part sizes. The prime threshold is existential.

Ryser's covering conjecture predicts $	au\le(r-1)
u$ for an $r$-partite hypergraph, where $	au$ and $
u$ are its covering and matching numbers. The formalized constructions give finite intersecting $r$-partite $r$-uniform hypergraphs with $
u=1$ and $	au=r$, contradicting the bound. The ranks have the form $r=p^n+1$: one fixed prime $p\equiv2\pmod3$ works for all sufficiently large prime degrees $n$, and a second result covers every sufficiently large such prime $p$ and every sufficiently large odd $n$, with the degree threshold allowed to depend on $p$. Infinitely many ranks occur. Equal part sizes and numerical thresholds are not asserted.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let $r,m\ge1$ be integers, and fix real numbers $R\ge2$ and $D\ge1$. For every coloring $\chi:\N\to[r]$, there are distinct positive integers $a_1<\cdots<a_m$ and a color $c\in[r]$ such that \[ \chi\left(\sum_{j\in J}a_j\right) =\chi\left(\prod_{j\in J}a_j\right)=c \quad\text{for every }\varnothing\ne J\subseteq[m]. \] Equivalently, $\FS(A)\cup\FP(A)$ is monochromatic for a set $A\subset\N$ of cardinality $m$. The elements can additionally be chosen to satisfy \begin{equation} a_1>R,\qquad a_d>R\left(\sum_{k<d}a_k+\prod_{k<d}a_k\right)^D \quad(2\le d\le m). \end{equation}

primaryStatements.label: cor:distinct-expressions
primaryStatements.text: For every finite coloring of $\N$ and every $m\ge1$, there is an $m$-element set $A\subset\N$ for which $\FS(A)\cup\FP(A)$ is monochromatic and \[ |\FS(A)|=|\FP(A)|=2^m-1,\qquad \FS(A)\cap\FP(A)=A. \] In particular, the union has $2(2^m-1)-m$ distinct elements.

primaryStatements.name: Finite interval form with prescribed divisibility
primaryStatements.label: cor:finite-interval
primaryStatements.text: Fix integers $r,m,q\ge1$ and real numbers $R\ge2$, $D\ge1$. There exists $N$ such that every $r$-coloring of $[N]$ admits $A=\{a_1<\cdots<a_m\}\subset q\N$ with $\FS(A)\cup\FP(A)\subseteq[N]$ monochromatic and \[ a_1>R,\qquad a_d>R\left(\sum_{k<d}a_k+\prod_{k<d}a_k\right)^D \quad(2\le d\le m). \] The subset sums and products have the distinctness properties of Corollary \ref{cor:distinct-expressions}.

primaryStatements.name: Product law
primaryStatements.label: cor:product-law
primaryStatements.text: Let \(B=T\cup\{i\}\) be a block, and let \(t_j\) be the independent harmonic samples at its raw cutoffs. Let \(V=V(w)\ge1\) be an auxiliary scale, and put \(K_T=\prod_{j\in T}X_j^2\). If \(\log X_i\) dominates every fixed power of \(2+W+K_T+V\), then \begin{equation} \left\|\operatorname{Law}(t_B)- \nu_B\mu_i\right\|_1=o(V^{-C}) \qquad\text{for every fixed }C>0. \end{equation} For any fixed family of disjoint blocks the corresponding joint law differs in the same sense from the product of their weighted pivot measures, when these hypotheses hold at each pivot.

primaryStatements.name: Weighted linear forms
primaryStatements.label: prop:linear-forms
primaryStatements.text: Fix the number \(q\) of rows, the number \(d\) of base variables, and a bound \(b\) on the number of raw factors in each divisor. For each \(u\in[q]\), let \(\sigma_u\) be a product of at most \(b\) independent harmonic \(W\)-unit variables at the master cutoffs of Lemma \ref{lem:master-scales}, and write \(\nu_u(y)=\E\sigma_u\1_{\sigma_u\mid y}\). All these raw draws are independent across occurrences. Suppose \(\sigma_u\le V\) surely, where \(V\ge M\to\infty\). Let \(\boldsymbol p\) consist of independent prime slots from finitely many gaps, each having \(V_l\ge V\). These slots are independent of all divisor draws. Let \(\mathcal G\) be a domain depending only on \(\boldsymbol p\), and let \(\ell_u(\boldsymbol x;\boldsymbol p)\) be homogeneous linear rows. On \(\mathcal G\) their arguments are integers on the base sampling support. Assume the following conditions. \begin{enumerate} \item Given \(\boldsymbol p\) and any possible divisor draws, the joint residue law of \(\boldsymbol x\) modulo \(K=\prod_{u=1}^q\sigma_u\) differs in total variation by at most \(\epsilon_{\rm base}\) from the uniform law on \((\Z/K\Z)^d\). The bound is uniform on \(\mathcal G\). \item For every \(w<p\le V\), each row is nonzero modulo \(p\) on \(\mathcal G\). There is a fixed finite list of nonzero integer polynomials in the prime slots such that, if all their values are nonzero modulo \(p\), every pair of rows is linearly independent over \(\mathbb F_p\). \end{enumerate} The CRT law of all prime slots at the primes \(w<p\le V\) is within total variation \(\epsilon_{\rm CRT}\) of independent uniform units, with independence also across these primes. Then, uniformly in every further prime-only event \(\mathcal E\subseteq\mathcal G\), \begin{equation} \E_{\boldsymbol p,\boldsymbol x} \1_{\mathcal E}(\boldsymbol p) \prod_{u=1}^q\nu_u(\ell_u(\boldsymbol x;\boldsymbol p)) =\PP(\mathcal E)+ O\left(\frac1w+V^q(\epsilon_{\rm base}+ \epsilon_{\rm CRT})\right). \end{equation} The error is absolute, so the statement also applies when \(\PP(\mathcal E)\) tends to zero. The implied constant depends only on the fixed row and divisor templates and polynomial tests. In particular the error is \(o(1)\) with the scales of Lemma \ref{lem:master-scales} and base residue errors smaller than every fixed inverse power of \(V\). Rows may have rational coefficients if their denominators are units modulo every possible divisor: interpret their residues by inverting those denominators. The integer-value and row hypotheses must still hold. Clearing such denominators leaves the congruence calculation unchanged. In particular this permits smooth denominators and prime pool denominators larger than \(V\).

primaryStatements.name: Uniform correlation test
primaryStatements.label: prop:correlation-test
primaryStatements.text: For every $m\ge2$ and every nonsingleton target support $J_*$, the construction above determines a finite family of integer polynomial templates $D$, with good prime-tuple laws, such that the following holds for every fixed master chain and valid gap $l$. There are an integer $1\le d\le K_m-1$, a constant $C_m$, and $\theta>0$, all bounded in terms of $m$ alone, for which \begin{equation} \boxed{\quad |\mathcal C| \le o(1)+C_m\left| \E_{\boldsymbol p,y,u} \prod_{\omega\subseteq[d]} g_*\left(y+M(\boldsymbol p) \sum_{R\in\omega}(u_R^1-u_R^0)\right) \right|^{\theta}. \quad} \end{equation} Here $y$ has law $\mu_{i_{a_*}}$, independently of the primes and shifts; the primes have the normalized good-tuple law of Lemma \ref{lem:row-directions}; $M(\boldsymbol p)$ is given by \eqref{eq:correlation-modulus}; and the shifts have the conditional laws in \eqref{eq:correlation-shift-length}. One may take $\theta=2^{-(q_{\mathrm{mask}}+d)}$. The gap length $R_l$ is divisible by every $M(\boldsymbol p)$ that occurs. The estimate is uniform over all the masks and functions in \eqref{eq:correlation-initial}, including $g_*$, and over each fixed finite set of positive integers $J_0$. Neither $d$, $C_m$, nor $\theta^{-1}$ depends on $N$, on the scales, or on the functions. The polynomial templates and direction choices are fixed before $M$ and the prime pools are chosen. In particular, the same tests can be used both for a bounded error and for an error bounded by $1+\nu_{a_*}$.

primaryStatements.name: Bounded dense models
primaryStatements.label: prop:dense-model
primaryStatements.text: There are functions $F_{B,a,c}:\Z\to[0,1]$ such that, for every fixed $J_0$ and every dual test at $B$, \begin{equation} \E_{\mu_i}(\rho-F_{B,a,c})\mathcal D=o(1) \end{equation} uniformly over its inputs and over the finitely many master blocks, scale labels, and colors.

definitions.name: Admissible parameters
definitions.label: def:admissible
definitions.text: For a fixed $n$, an admissible family consists of positive integers $M,h_1,\ldots,h_n,H_1,\ldots,H_n$, positive powers of two $X_1,\ldots,X_n$, and independent random variables $t_1,\ldots,t_n$, all depending on $w$, with the following properties. \begin{enumerate} \item $M$ and each $h_i$ are $w$-smooth multiples of $W^w$. For every block $B$, and also for every singleton $\{i\}$, $h_B\le M$. For every $A\in\mathcal E_B$, the ratio $h_A/h_B$ is an integer multiple of $W^w$. \item Each $H_i$ is a multiple of $M$ and dominates powers of $2+M+\prod_{\ell<i}X_\ell$. The quantity $\log X_i$ dominates powers of $H_i$. \item The law of $t_i$ is the harmonic $W$-unit probability measure \begin{equation} \mu_i(y)=\frac{\1_{X_i\le y<X_i^2}\1_{(y,W)=1}}{Z_i y}, \qquad Z_i=\sum_{\substack{X_i\le y<X_i^2\\(y,W)=1}}\frac1y. \end{equation} \end{enumerate}

definitions.name: Piecewise models
definitions.label: def:piecewise-model
definitions.text: Fix finite sets $\mathcal A\subset\Q_{>0}$ and $[r]$, and an admissible family. A system of step-at-most-$s$ models consists of functions $S_{B,a,c}:\Z\to[0,1]$, one for each block $B$, $a\in\mathcal A$, and $c\in[r]$. If $i=\max B$, then on each interval $[kH_i,(k+1)H_i)$ and each residue class modulo $M$, the function is a nilsequence in the progression index. The complexity is bounded uniformly over $w$, all pieces, and all model indices. The representing observables may be, and are, chosen $[0,1]$-valued on their entire nilmanifolds.

papers.title: The crossing number of complete graphs
papers.abstract: We prove the Harary–Hill conjecture: for every positive integer n, the ordinary crossing number of the complete graph Kn is $\displaystyle \frac14\left\lfloor\frac n2\right\rfloor \left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\right\rfloor \left\lfloor\frac{n-2}{2}\right\rfloor \left\lfloor\frac{n-3}{2}\right\rfloor.$

The result proves the optimality of the classical drawings among all plane drawings with continuous edge arcs.

primaryStatements.label: prop:odd
primaryStatements.text: Every normalized minimum drawing of \(K_{2s+1}\), \(s\ge2\), has at least \(\binom{s}{2}^{2}\) crossings.

primaryStatements.label: cor:lower
primaryStatements.text: For every \(n\ge3\), \(\crn(K_n)\ge Z(n)\).

primaryStatements.label: prop:upper
primaryStatements.text: This drawing has exactly \(Z(n)\) crossings for every \(n\ge3\).

lean.scopeText:
The formalized result proves Hill's proposed formula for the crossing number of the complete graph: for every $n\ge3$, $\mathrm{cr}(K_n)=\frac14\lfloor n/2\rfloor\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\lfloor(n-3)/2\rfloor$. It proves the lower bound and constructs a matching two-page drawing. Crossings are spatial points, so repeated crossings of one edge pair count separately.

Zarankiewicz's crossing-number conjecture predicts $\mathrm{cr}(K_{m,n})=\lfloor m/2\rfloor\lfloor(m-1)/2\rfloor\lfloor n/2\rfloor\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor$. The formalized result proves this equality for every positive $m,n$ and constructs a drawing attaining it. Crossings are counted as spatial points for continuous simple edge paths, including repeated crossings between the same pair of edges.
