primaryStatements.label: red:main-contradiction
primaryStatements.text: The graph \(\mathcal H\) cannot satisfy both bounds in Lemmas \ref{red:global-concentration} and \ref{red:local-concentration}.

primaryStatements.label: red:directions
primaryStatements.text: After passing to a subsequence, there is an undirected graph \(\mathcal G\) on \(P\) with at least \(cN^2\) edges such that, for every vertex \(p\) and every irreducible projective variety \(Y\subset\mathbb P^{d-1}\) of dimension \(a\), \begin{equation} \#\{q:\{p,q\}\in\mathcal G,\ \pi_p(q)\in Y\} \le C\,\deg(Y)A^a. \end{equation} The positive constants \(c,C\) are fixed along the subsequence.

primaryStatements.name: Independent evaluations in every star
primaryStatements.label: red:independent-stars
primaryStatements.text: A further symmetric selection retains at least \(c'N^2\) pairs and has the following property: the direction-evaluation vectors of the partners in each star are linearly independent for homogeneous polynomials of degree \(D=\lfloor A\rfloor\). In particular each selected star admits homogeneous separators of degree \(D\).

primaryStatements.name: Mixed-dimensional envelopes
primaryStatements.label: poly:envelope
primaryStatements.text: Let $Z$ be a locus of equations of degree at most $L\ge1$, and let $a_k$ be the total degree of any chosen subfamily of its $k$-dimensional irreducible components. For their union $V$, \[ H_V(L)\ge c_n\sum_{k=0}^n a_kL^k. \] For an arbitrary reduced union with dimension-by-dimension degrees $a_k$, without a hypothesis on its equations, \[ H_V(D)\le\sum_{k=0}^n a_k\binom{D+k}{k}. \] In particular these statements apply to the components of $\Env_L(T)$.

primaryStatements.name: A bounded-degree test for high multiplicity
primaryStatements.label: poly:high-multiplicity
primaryStatements.text: Let $X\subsetneq\C^n$ be irreducible of degree $a$, and let $S\subset X$ be finite with $\mult_pX>a/2$ for every $p\in S$. For any specified $x_*\notin X$, there is a polynomial of degree at most $2(n+1)$ which vanishes on $S$ and is nonzero at $x_*$. In particular the specified high-multiplicity centers lie in a proper hypersurface of degree bounded in terms of the ambient dimension alone.

primaryStatements.name: A tangent hyperplane controls the projection loss
primaryStatements.label: poly:tangent-projection
primaryStatements.text: Let an irreducible affine curve $C$ lie in a variety $X$ smooth at $p\in C$. Suppose $C$ has a point $z$ for which the direction $z-p$ is not in $T_pX$. Then \[ \mult_pC\le\tfrac12\deg C. \] Consequently, if projection of $C$ from $p$ is nonconstant, its image degree times its generic map degree is at least $\tfrac12\deg C$.

primaryStatements.name: Terminal-curve deletion
primaryStatements.label: geo:terminal
primaryStatements.text: Assign sample points to finitely many irreducible physical curves $Y_i$, each containing its assigned points. Pool repetitions of a curve, and require every line member to be real. Then the number of ordered pairs $(p,q)$, $p\ne q$, for which $q$ is assigned to $Y_i$ and \[ \overline{\pi_pY_i}\subseteq C_p \] is $o(N^2)$. The estimate is uniform in the assignment and the curves.

primaryStatements.label: prop:graph
primaryStatements.text: Under the supposition above, there is a sequence of finite sets $P\subset\R^2$ of real algebraic points, with $n=|P|\to\infty$, and nonempty directed graphs $E$ on $P$, with the following properties. Their densities $d_n=|E|/[n(n-1)]$ tend to $\theta$, and every fiber has $k_e\ge n^{s-o(1)}$, uniformly in $e$. For a fixed constant $B_0$, \begin{equation} q\le B_0\pi,\qquad q_X,q_Y\le B_0\alpha,\qquad \frac{q_X+q_Y}{2}\ge(1-o(1))\alpha \end{equation} pointwise, and \begin{equation} q_Y\{y:d^-(y)<n^\gamma\}=O(n^{\gamma-1})=o(1). \end{equation} Finally, put $\lambda_n=1/\log n$. For every subset $C\subset P$, with $m=|C|$ and $p_e=\mu_e(C)$, \begin{equation} \E_e\,\1_C(x_e)p_e\1_{\{p_e\ge\lambda_n\}} \le \begin{cases} (1+o(1))\pi(C^2),&m>n^{1-c},\\ o(1)\pi(C^2),&m\le n^{1-c}. \end{cases} \end{equation} All the errors are uniform in vertices, fibers, and subsets wherever these occur.

The formalized result shows that large repeated distance fibers are rare in arbitrary finite planar point sets. For each fixed $s>0$, the largest possible fraction of ordered distinct pairs $(x,y)$ whose distance from the pin $x$ occurs at least $n^s$ times tends to zero as the set size $n$ grows. Consequently, for every $\varepsilon>0$, the fraction of pins determining fewer than $n^{1-\varepsilon}$ distances tends uniformly to zero. The separate unit-distance power-saving theorem is not included.

The planar unit-distance problem asks how many pairs at distance one can occur among $n$ points. The formalization proves that there are absolute constants $C>0$ and $1\le\beta<4/3$ such that every finite planar point set of size $n$ determines at most $Cn^\beta$ unordered unit-distance pairs. The same constants work for every $n$, giving a fixed power improvement over the classical exponent $4/3$.

primaryStatements.label: inc:piece
primaryStatements.text: From a sequence of \(n=t^3\) real planar points with at least \(t^{4-o(1)}\) ordered unit pairs, one can obtain real algebraic point and center sets \(P,Q\), and a nonempty graph \(E\subseteq P\times Q\) consisting of unit incidences, with the following properties. There is a parameter \(a=a(t)>0\) such that \(a\to0\), \(a\log t\to\infty\), and \begin{equation} |P|=t^{1+2a+o(a)},\qquad |Q|=t^{2+a+o(a)},\qquad |E|=t^{2+2a+o(a)}. \end{equation} Writing \(d(p),d(q)\) for graph degrees, uniformly over all vertices, \begin{equation} d(p)=t^{1+o(a)},\qquad d(q)=t^{a+o(a)}. \end{equation} The uniform law on \(E\) has marginals \(\mu(p)=d(p)/|E|\) and \(\kappa(q)=d(q)/|E|\) satisfying \begin{equation} \mu(p)\ge\frac{\gamma}{|P|},\qquad \kappa(q)\ge\frac{\gamma}{|Q|},\qquad \gamma=\frac{27}{50}=0.54. \end{equation} Set \(\eta=\gamma-\tfrac12=1/25\). There is a single sequence \(\xi_t\to0\) such that, for every \(F\subseteq P\) and \(G\subseteq Q\), with counting fractions \(u=|F|/|P|\) and \(v=|G|/|Q|\), \begin{equation} \Prob_E(p\in F,q\in G) \le \sqrt{uv}\bigl((uv)^\eta+\xi_t\bigr). \end{equation} The sequence \(\xi_t\) is independent of the chosen subsets.

primaryStatements.name: Combinatorial invariance
primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let $(W,S)$ and $(W',S')$ be arbitrary Coxeter systems, and let $u\le b$ in $W$ and $u'\le b'$ in $W'$. If \[ \iota:[u,b]\longrightarrow[u',b'] \] is an isomorphism of abstract Bruhat interval posets, then their equal-parameter Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials satisfy \[ P^W_{u,b}(q)=P^{W'}_{u',b'}(q). \]

primaryStatements.name: Dyer's reflection-order path formula
primaryStatements.label: bg:paths
primaryStatements.text: Fix a reflection order and use left reflection labels on Bruhat edges. Let $\widetilde R_{x,y}(T)$ be the sum of $T^r$ over directed paths of $r$ edges from $x$ to $y$ having strictly increasing labels. The empty path contributes $1$ when $x=y$. Then \begin{equation} q^{-d(x,y)/2}R_{x,y}(q) =\widetilde R_{x,y}\bigl(q^{1/2}-q^{-1/2}\bigr). \end{equation} The same polynomial counts paths with strictly decreasing labels.

primaryStatements.name: Moment-graph sheaf
primaryStatements.label: bg:bmp
primaryStatements.text: There is an indecomposable graded sheaf $B=B(b)$ on $[1,b]$, normalized by $B^b=A$, with the following properties. \begin{enumerate} \item Every vertex module $B^x$ is finitely generated and graded free. For $E:x\longrightarrow y$, \[ B^E=B^y/\alpha_E B^y, \] and restriction from $y$ is the quotient map. \item If $\Omega\subseteq[1,b]$ is upward closed, every section over $\Omega$ extends to a global section. Moreover the projection from global sections onto each $B^x$ is surjective. \item Let $U_x$ be the set of edges out of $x$. For $F\subseteq U_x$ put \[ L_x(F)=\ker\left(B^x\longrightarrow \bigoplus_{E\in F}B^E\right). \] Then $L_x(U_x)$ is graded free. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.name: Grading normalization
primaryStatements.label: bg:normalization
primaryStatements.text: For $x\le b$, write $d=d(x,b)=\ell(b)-\ell(x)$. In the degree-one convention above, \begin{equation} \operatorname{grk}_A(B^x;q)=P_{x,b}(q), \qquad \operatorname{grk}_A(L_x(U_x);q)=q^dP_{x,b}(q^{-1}). \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Graph reconstruction
primaryStatements.label: bg:graph
primaryStatements.text: An isomorphism of Bruhat intervals in arbitrary Coxeter systems preserves their directed Bruhat graphs. More explicitly, if $\iota:[u,b]\longrightarrow[u',b']$ is a poset isomorphism, then \[ y=tx>x\text{ for a reflection }t \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \iota(y)=t'\iota(x)>\iota(x)\text{ for a reflection }t'. \]

primaryStatements.name: Transport of dihedral intervals
primaryStatements.label: dih:transport
primaryStatements.text: Let $D=D_\Pi$ be a maximal root-plane subgroup of $W$. Suppose $x,c$ belong to a common coset of $D$ and to $[u,b]$, with $x\le_D c$ and $\ell_D(c)-\ell_D(x)\ge2$. Then there is a maximal dihedral plane subgroup $D'$ of $W'$ such that \[ \iota\bigl([x,c]_D\bigr) =[\iota(x),\iota(c)]_{D'}. \] The restricted map preserves and reflects relative order, relative rank differences, and all directed relative reflection edges.

primaryStatements.name: Plane localization
primaryStatements.label: loc:decomposition
primaryStatements.text: For each coset $C$ with $K=C\cap[1,b]\ne\varnothing$, there are nonnegative integers $m_c$, indexed by $c\in K$, such that \[ B_R|_K\cong \bigoplus_{c\in K}\mathcal O_{c,R}^{\oplus m_c} \] as ungraded sheaves over $R$.

primaryStatements.name: Edge-image bound
primaryStatements.label: edge:bound
primaryStatements.text: Let \(e:x\to y\) be an edge. Let \(F\subset U_x\) and \(G\subset U_y\) consist of the upward edges strictly later than \(e\) in the transported schedule. Put \[ C=A/(\alpha_e),\qquad I=\res_{x,e}L_x(F),\qquad J=\res_{y,e}L_y(G) \quad\text{inside }B^e . \] If \(L_y(G)\) is graded free over \(A\), there is a nonzero homogeneous \(f_e\in C\) such that \begin{equation} I\subseteq f_eJ,\qquad \deg f_e=\frac{d(x,y)-1}{2}. \end{equation} Moreover \(J\), and hence \(f_eJ\), is graded free over \(C\).

lean.scopeText: The combinatorial invariance conjecture asks whether a Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial depends only on its Bruhat interval as an ordered set. The formalization proves that every order isomorphism between Bruhat intervals in arbitrary Coxeter systems preserves the corresponding equal-parameter Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial. The two intervals may come from different Coxeter systems.

primaryStatements.name: Elementary positivity and a permutation witness
primaryStatements.label: main:theorem
primaryStatements.text: There is a deterministic terminating procedure which, given a natural unit interval graph $G$ on $[n]$ and $\sigma\in D_G^0$, returns a partition $\theta_G(\sigma)\vdash n$ such that \begin{equation} \chi_G(X;q)=\sum_{\sigma\in D_G^0} q^{\ginv_G(\sigma)}e_{\theta_G(\sigma)}(X). \end{equation} In particular every elementary coefficient of $\chi_G(X;q)$ belongs to $\N[q]$. The assertion holds as a formal symmetric-function identity, uniformly in $n$ and $G$.

primaryStatements.name: Young permutation modules in Hessenberg cohomology
primaryStatements.label: main:hessenberg
primaryStatements.text: Let $n\ge1$, let $h$ be as above with graph $G=G(h)$, and let $S\in M_n(\C)$ be regular semisimple. Write \[ \operatorname{Hess}(S,h)= \{F_\bullet\in\operatorname{Flag}(\C^n): SF_i\subseteq F_{h(i)}\text{ for all }i\}. \] For $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_\ell)\vdash n$, let $M^\lambda=\operatorname{Ind}_{S_\lambda}^{S_n}\mathbf{1}_{\C}$ be the Young permutation module, where $S_\lambda=S_{\lambda_1}\times\cdots\times S_{\lambda_\ell}$ is the standard Young subgroup, and put \[ m_{\lambda,d}(h)= \#\{\sigma\in D_G^0:\theta_G(\sigma)=\lambda,\ \ginv_G(\sigma)=d\}. \] Then for every integer $d\ge0$, under Tymoczko's dot action on ordinary cohomology there is an abstract $\C[S_n]$-module isomorphism \[ H^{2d}(\operatorname{Hess}(S,h);\C) \cong\bigoplus_{\lambda\vdash n}(M^\lambda)^{\oplus m_{\lambda,d}(h)}. \]

primaryStatements.name: Commuting independent-set sums
primaryStatements.label: graph:commutation
primaryStatements.text: For every natural unit interval graph $\Gamma$ and all $j,k\ge0$, $E_j(\Gamma)E_k(\Gamma)=E_k(\Gamma)E_j(\Gamma)$.

primaryStatements.name: Coloring kernel
primaryStatements.label: graph:kernel
primaryStatements.text: If $\alpha(\Gamma)\le D$, then $X_G(X;q)$ is symmetric and \begin{equation} X_G(X;v^2)=\sum_{\substack{\lambda\vdash n\\\ell(\lambda)\le D}} v^M[X_u]m_\lambda(Y)\,e_\lambda(X). \end{equation} The equality is independent of the extra vertices of $\Gamma$.

primaryStatements.name: Positive reordering
primaryStatements.label: alg:reordering
primaryStatements.text: Suppose an admissible product of elementary units is written in ray order, with $\Omega(p_i,p_j)>0$ whenever the ray of $p_i$ precedes the distinct ray of $p_j$. Its factorization in the opposite ray order is again a product of elementary units, with nonnegative integral multiplicities. The output list is admissible. Every coefficient at fixed exponent and fixed $v$-degree is a finite sum of nonnegative integers, and each exponent has bounded upper $v$-degree. The assertion also holds modulo any fixed charge cutoff. For the algorithmic assertion, assume that lattice operations, the form $\Omega$ and the charge are effectively computable, that input occurrences at bounded charge and above a given parameter threshold can be listed effectively, and that for every $B$ one can compute an integer $A_B\ge1$ such that \[ |\Omega(p,q)|\le A_B \qquad\text{whenever }p,q\in C,\quad c(p),c(q)\le B. \] Then every prescribed coefficient and every bounded part of the output unit list can be calculated by finite rational linear algebra.

primaryStatements.label: alg:bialgebra
primaryStatements.text: With $\Delta=\sum_{a+b=d}\Delta_{a,b}$, $\mathcal H$ is a connected dimension-graded bialgebra, and its coproduct is cocommutative with the interchange sign $\varepsilon(a,b)$.

primaryStatements.name: Positive factors on every wall
primaryStatements.label: wall:factors
primaryStatements.text: At every generic point of a wall, and to every specified root order, its element is a product of elementary units on its ray with the finiteness conditions above. The same conclusion holds if the simple incoming data are replaced by allowed products of elementary units. If a crossing has the sign of $-V(m)$ on its wall normal, the resulting monomial jump from $X_m$ has coefficients in $\N((v^{-1}))$.

primaryStatements.name: Positive sections
primaryStatements.label: wall:positivity
primaryStatements.text: Every $\Theta_m$ has coefficients in $\N((v^{-1}))$ in every chamber. More generally, the same is true of a section $F$ all of whose incoming coefficients belong to $\N((v^{-1}))$.

lean.scopeText: The elementary-positivity part of the Shareshian–Wachs conjecture asks whether the chromatic quasisymmetric function of every natural unit interval graph has nonnegative coefficients in the elementary basis. The formalization proves this over $\mathbb N[q]$. It constructs an explicit elementary-basis expansion indexed by the graph's permitted nondescent permutations, with each term weighted by a nonnegative power of $q$ determined by its graph inversions. The expansion holds for every finite number of color variables.

primaryStatements.text: There is an absolute constant \(C>0\) such that, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), all sufficiently large integers \(t\) satisfy \[ \frac{t^4}{(\log t)^{3+\varepsilon}} \ \le\ r(5,t)\ \le\ C\frac{t^4}{(\log t)^3}. \] The threshold for \(t\) may depend on \(\varepsilon\). primaryStatements.name: Sparse-pair description
primaryStatements.label: thm:predictor
primaryStatements.text: Fix \(0<\eta<1/10\), set \(\beta=\eta/10^7\), and let \(q\) be a sufficiently large prime. Write \(\sigma=\log q\), and suppose \[ \sigma^\beta\le D\le\sigma^{1-\eta/2},\qquad L=D\sigma^{8\beta},\qquad R\in[\sigma^\beta,2\sigma^\beta+2]\cap2\mathbb N,\qquad P=LR. \] Let \(2\le d\le4\), and let \(S\subseteq U_S\subseteq\mathcal P_d\) and \(T\subseteq U_T\subseteq\mathcal P_d^*\) be nonempty. Assume \[ |S||T|\ge q^{d+1}e^{-b},\qquad 0\le b\le C_bD\sigma^{6\beta},\qquad \frac{e(S,T)}{|S||T|}\le\frac{\tau}{q},\qquad 0<\tau\le\sigma^{-200\cdot2^{d-2}\beta}, \] where \(C_b\) is a fixed constant. Put \(d_S=\log(|U_S|/|S|)\) and \(d_T=\log(|U_T|/|T|)\). Orient the pair so that \(|S|\le|T|\). There is a public-table scheme for which, except with probability \(O(e^{-cq})\), the encoder can send a message of length at most \[ CqP(d_S+d_T+P) \] bits describing a set \(W\subseteq U_S\) such that \[ |W|\le |S|e^{CP},\qquad |W\cap S|\ge c|S|. \] The constants may depend on \(\eta,C_b\), but not on the hidden sets, \(D\), or \(q\). The decoder uses only \(U_S,U_T\), the public parameters and tables, and the message. There is no uniformity assertion for the captured subset \(W\cap S\).

primaryStatements.name: One compression stage
primaryStatements.label: prop:compression-stage
primaryStatements.text: Suppose a selected consistent tuple and context satisfy \eqref{eq:stage-input}--\eqref{eq:stage-range}, with deterministic $\ell=\Theta(k)$ and bounded stream-marginal density, and suppose the rectangle-occupancy event of Lemma \ref{lem:rectangles} holds almost surely. Then either the high-rank argument contradicts Lemma \ref{lem:stream-entropy}, or a constant-probability extraction produces another such tuple, of deterministic length $\Theta(k)$, and a new context satisfying \eqref{eq:stage-output}, where \begin{equation} w\le C\sigma^{1+\eta/2}/D. \end{equation} Its decoder is independent of the old context.

primaryStatements.name: A stream with no long consistent subsequence
primaryStatements.label: thm:stream
primaryStatements.text: For every fixed $0<\eta<1/10$ and every sufficiently large prime $q$, there is a stream of $N=\lfloor q^4\log q\rfloor$ flags whose ordered flag graph is $K_5$-free and has independence number less than $k=\lfloor q(\log q)^{1+\eta}\rfloor$.

The formalization determines the sharp logarithmic exponent of the off-diagonal Ramsey number $r(5,t)$. It proves
$r(5,t)=t^4/(\log t)^{3+o(1)}$ as $t\to\infty$.
For every $\varepsilon>0$, the lower bound $t^4/(\log t)^{3+\varepsilon}$ holds eventually, while the upper bound is $Ct^4/(\log t)^3$ for an absolute $C>0$. The corresponding logarithmic exponent converges to three along all natural values of $t$.

The formalization determines the sharp logarithmic exponent of the off-diagonal Ramsey number for every fixed integer $s\ge6$. It proves
$r(s,t)=t^{s-1}/(\log t)^{s-2+o(1)}$ as $t\to\infty$.
More explicitly, for each $\varepsilon>0$ the lower bound $t^{s-1}/(\log t)^{s-2+\varepsilon}$ holds eventually, while the upper bound is $C_s t^{s-1}/(\log t)^{s-2}$. The logarithmic exponent limit is taken along all natural values of $t$.

primaryStatements.label: intro:main
primaryStatements.text: For every fixed integer $s\ge6$ there is a constant $C_s>0$ such that, for every $\varepsilon>0$ and every sufficiently large integer $t$, \[ \frac{t^{s-1}}{(\log t)^{s-2+\varepsilon}} \le r(s,t) \le C_s\frac{t^{s-1}}{(\log t)^{s-2}}. \] In particular, \[ \lim_{t\to\infty} \frac{(s-1)\log t-\log r(s,t)}{\log\log t}=s-2. \]

primaryStatements.label: intro:prime-construction
primaryStatements.text: Fix an integer $d\ge5$ and a real number $0<\eta<1/10$. For every sufficiently large prime $q$, with $\sigma=\log q$, there is a graph $G$ such that \[ |V(G)|=\lfloor q^d\sigma\rfloor,\qquad K_{d+1}\not\subseteq G,\qquad \alpha(G)<\lfloor q\sigma^{1+\eta}\rfloor. \]

primaryStatements.name: Repeated projection
primaryStatements.label: geom:projection
primaryStatements.text: For $j\geq4$, assume Lemma \ref{geom:description} in projective dimension $j-1$, for every fixed value of its hypothesis constant. Then the lemma holds in dimension $j$.

primaryStatements.name: Low-dimensional preparation
primaryStatements.label: geom:preparation
primaryStatements.text: Suppose \eqref{geom:sparse-hypotheses} holds with $j\in\{2,3\}$ and $n=|S|\leq|T|$. Either enumeration already proves Lemma \ref{geom:description}, or the following preparation costs $O(q+\sigma)$ bits. In dimension three there is also a possible reduction to the dimension-two description lemma, with the same final cost, size, capture, and failure bounds as Lemma \ref{geom:description}. In the case not resolved by enumeration or that reduction, we have $n>100qP$, a retained set $S'\subseteq S$ of size $n'\in[n/2,n]$, and either an empty list or an ordered plane list $\Pi_1,\ldots,\Pi_J$ in $\PG(3,q)$. In the latter case the sets \begin{equation} C_i=(S\cap\Pi_i)\setminus\bigcup_{h<i}\Pi_h \quad(1\leq i\leq J) \end{equation} partition $S'$, have nonincreasing sizes, and satisfy $|C_i|<.04n'$. The decoder knows the list and all cell sizes, but need not know $S'$ or the cells themselves. Write \begin{equation} n=q^{1+v},\quad g=(v-1/2)\sigma,\quad \chi=P/100,\quad\chi_0=P/10000,\quad B=q^j/n'. \end{equation} For every ambient query point $x$, define $O_x$ to be the cell $C_i$ of its earliest containing listed plane, and $O_x=\varnothing$ if there is none. Define \begin{equation} f_x=|O_x|/n'\leq .04,\qquad X_x=S'\setminus(O_x\cup\{x\}). \end{equation} If no list is present, $O_x=\varnothing$ for all $x$. When $j=3$ and $g>\chi_0$, the preparation additionally ensures either \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item every plane meets $S'$ in fewer than $K_p=n^{4/3}q^{-1}e^{-g/5}$ points and the list is empty; or \item the list is present and $J\leq n/K_p=q^{1/2}e^{-2g/15}$. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.name: Short-row description
primaryStatements.label: learn:short-row
primaryStatements.text: Fix the constants in \eqref{learn:support-hypotheses}, the bound on $b/K_*$, the bound on $\tau\sigma^{100\beta}$, and $C_0$. For every sufficiently large prime $q$, the prepared input just specified has the following description scheme. Using a fresh public table, it either declares failure or describes a set $W\subseteq U_S$ satisfying \[ |W|\le n e^{CP},\qquad |W\cap S|\ge c n. \] Failure has probability at most $C e^{-cq}$, and the message has at most $CqP(d_S+1)+Cq+C\sigma$ bits. In particular this is within $CqP(d_S+d_T+P)$ for any $d_T\ge0$. The bounds are uniform in all supports and prepared inputs satisfying the hypotheses, including inputs fixed by earlier random history before the fresh table is sampled. The decoder uses only $U_S$, public parameters, and the new message; it need not know $S$, $T$, or $S'$.

primaryStatements.name: Good-index fractions
primaryStatements.label: mark:good-indices
primaryStatements.text: In every selected class, the expected proportion of bad unexposed indices is $o(1)$, and so is the expected proportion of bad fresh representatives. At every good index each endpoint is good with probability $1-o(1)$, uniformly over the history and fresh indices. All limits hold for fixed $d,\eta$ and the stage constants.

primaryStatements.name: Upper Ramsey estimate
primaryStatements.label: end:upper-bound
primaryStatements.text: For every fixed integer $s\ge2$ there is a constant $C_s$ such that for all sufficiently large integers $t$, \[ r(s,t)\le C_s\frac{t^{s-1}}{(\log t)^{s-2}}. \]

lean.scopeText:
The formalization determines the sharp logarithmic exponent of the off-diagonal Ramsey number $r(5,t)$. It proves
$r(5,t)=t^4/(\log t)^{3+o(1)}$ as $t\to\infty$.
For every $\varepsilon>0$, the lower bound $t^4/(\log t)^{3+\varepsilon}$ holds eventually, while the upper bound is $Ct^4/(\log t)^3$ for an absolute $C>0$. The corresponding logarithmic exponent converges to three along all natural values of $t$.

The formalization determines the sharp logarithmic exponent of the off-diagonal Ramsey number for every fixed integer $s\ge6$. It proves
$r(s,t)=t^{s-1}/(\log t)^{s-2+o(1)}$ as $t\to\infty$.
More explicitly, for each $\varepsilon>0$ the lower bound $t^{s-1}/(\log t)^{s-2+\varepsilon}$ holds eventually, while the upper bound is $C_s t^{s-1}/(\log t)^{s-2}$. The logarithmic exponent limit is taken along all natural values of $t$.

primaryStatements.text: There is an absolute constant $C>0$ such that \[ R(Q_n)\le C2^n \qquad\text{for every integer }n\ge0. \]

primaryStatements.name: The remaining deep regime
primaryStatements.label: cor:remaining-deep-regime
primaryStatements.text: The possibility remaining in this analysis has both \(H_L^\dagger\ge1\), i.e., for each fixed error exponent slack \(\epsilon>0\) one has deep discrepancy \(\le n^{-1+\epsilon}\) on retained labels at some budgets \(n^x,\alpha n\) with constants \(x,\alpha>0\), in both orientations.

primaryStatements.name: Initial discrepancy
primaryStatements.label: cor:initial-discrepancy
primaryStatements.text:
After passing to a subsequence of a bad sequence and discarding a total of \(o(N)\) labels, there is a fixed \(\eta_0>0\) such that for every pair of probability laws \(\mu,
u\) on the retained sides and either color \(G\),  egin{equation} \operatorname{width}(\mu),\operatorname{width}(
u)\le n^{\eta_0} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad |d_G(\mu,
u)-1/2|\le n^{-\eta_0} \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Asymmetric power discrepancy
primaryStatements.label: cor:asymmetric-discrepancy
primaryStatements.text: Consequently in a bad sequence with \eqref{eq:source-2}, after further stabilization for countably many budgets, we can assume: for every rational \(0<\beta<\tau/4,\ 0<\gamma<1\) there is a constant \(h_{\beta,\gamma}>0\) such that on retained sets all pairs at widths \(\le n^\beta,n^\gamma\) respectively have both-color densities \(1/2\pm n^{-h_{\beta,\gamma}}\) eventually, and similarly in reversed orientation. The exponent may depend on the budget pair; no uniform exponent over all rational pairs is asserted.

primaryStatements.name: Exclusion of intermediate bias
primaryStatements.label: prop:intermediate-bias-exclusion
primaryStatements.text: In the stabilized contradiction sequence, neither of the following situations can occur: \begin{itemize} \item some \(H^\dagger<1\); \item both \(H^\dagger\ge1\), and some \(0<H_L^\dagger<1\). \end{itemize}

primaryStatements.name: Full-dimensional cluster exclusion
primaryStatements.label: prop:full-dimensional-cluster-exclusion
primaryStatements.text: Assume \eqref{eq:source-2} on the retained sets in both orientations. Fix constants \(\zeta>0\) and \(0<\delta<\min(\eta_0,\zeta,1)/2000\). Suppose there are available patches of one color \(G\) as follows: \begin{itemize} \item a law \(\mu_i\) on the first side and a finite probability mixture \(\lambda_i\) of cluster laws \(D\) on the second side, with \(\nu_i=\mathbb E_{\lambda_i}D\); both \(\mu_i,\nu_i\) have width \(\le n^\delta\), and each \(D\) has maximum atom \(\le \exp(-n^\zeta)\); \item within the support of each \(D\) all pairs \(y,y'\) (repetitions allowed) have \(G\)-codegree (common-neighbor mass) under \(\mu_i\) at least \(1/4+a\), \(a=n^{-\delta}\). \end{itemize} Then there is a cube.

primaryStatements.name: Eventual absence of cluster witnesses
primaryStatements.label: cor:eventual-cluster-absence
primaryStatements.text: After stabilization, cluster witnesses from Proposition \ref{prop:full-dimensional-cluster-exclusion} are eventually absent for every fixed rational admissible parameter choice, in both orientations and both colors.

primaryStatements.name: Exclusion of the linear-budget jump
primaryStatements.label: prop:linear-budget-jump-exclusion
primaryStatements.text: In the stabilized contradiction sequence, it is impossible that both orientations have \(H^\dagger\ge1\) while one has \(H_L^\dagger=0\).

definitions.name: Availability
definitions.text: A witness has specified supports on the current host sides. After a pair of label removals, it remains a witness if both supports are wholly retained. A family is available along a sequence if some constant \(\kappa>0\) has the following property: eventually, after every removal of at most \(\kappa N\) labels from each side, at least one witness remains. The witness may be chosen anew for each pair of removals.

definitions.name: Raw experiments, gates, and stage histories
definitions.text: A raw experiment is the specified sampling law before the avoidance constraints currently under discussion are imposed. A local gate is an event determined by the declared local inputs; retaining the gate means multiplying by its indicator, rather than conditioning the reference law on it. A successful prehistory is an entering stage history on which that stage's stated hypotheses hold. Comparisons are made separately at each such history.

definitions.name: Limiting bias exponents
definitions.label: def:limiting-bias-exponents
definitions.text: Stabilize the absolute-bias properties at all rational budgets and exponents used below. In a specified orientation \(X,Y\), let \(H(x,y)\) be the infimum of rational \(h>0\) for which bias of magnitude at least \(n^{-h}\) is available at widths \(n^x,n^y\), where \(0<x,y<1\). Set the infimum to \(+\infty\) if there is no such exponent. If \(h<H(x,y)\), stabilization makes this witness property eventually absent: every pair of laws within these budgets then has bias less than \(n^{-h}\). Let \(H_L(x,\alpha)\) denote the corresponding infimum with second budget \(\alpha n\), for \(\alpha>0\). Both functions are nonincreasing in their width parameters, since enlarging a budget preserves availability. Taking limits through rational arguments, put \[ H^\dagger=\lim_{x\downarrow0}\lim_{y\uparrow1}H(x,y),\qquad H_L^\dagger=\lim_{x,\alpha\downarrow0}H_L(x,\alpha). \]

definitions.name: Residual scales
definitions.label: def:residual-scales
definitions.text: On the labels left after this reserve and any earlier patch removals, measure two dyadic scales (values that are powers of two with integer exponent). Both maxima are recalculated on each current residual pair: \begin{itemize} \item \(g\) is the largest dyadic value \(b\ge2\) for which two uniform sets each of size \(\ge N e^{-b^{a_B}}\) have absolute bias at least \(b/n\). \item \(q\) is the largest dyadic \(b\ge2\) for which, in some orientation, there is a uniform first set of size \(\ge N e^{-b^{a_C}}\) and a family of disjoint bins on the second side, each of size at least \(e^b\), with union of size \(\ge N e^{-b^{a_C}}\), such that all distinct pairs in each bin have inner product of their \(f\)-vectors \(>\theta\) under that first law. This inner product does not depend on color choice. \end{itemize} Use 1 for an empty maximum.

papers.title: A classification of finite Euclidean Ramsey configurations
papers.abstract: We classify finite Euclidean Ramsey configurations by a necessary and sufficient tensor condition over their coordinate fields. The Ramsey property here concerns monochromatic congruent copies at the original scale under arbitrary finite colorings. The criterion shows that every nonempty subtransitive set and every nonempty set of at most five points on a circle is Ramsey. In particular, some Ramsey cyclic quadrilaterals are not subtransitive, disproving the necessity direction of the Leader–Russell–Walters conjectured characterization.
papers.familySummary: Classifies finite point configurations that occur monochromatically, at their original scale, in every finite coloring of sufficiently high-dimensional Euclidean space. The characterization is an algebraic condition over the coordinate field. It also disproves the Leader–Russell–Walters conjecture that every such configuration is a subset of a finite transitive set.

primaryStatements.name: Classification
primaryStatements.label: thm:classification
primaryStatements.text: Let $A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_s\}\subset\R^d$ be a finite set of at least two points with affine span $\R^d$, and define $p_i,F,B,m_F$ as above. Then $A$ is Ramsey if and only if there is a matrix $P\in\operatorname{Mat}_{d+1}(B)$ such that \begin{align} (p_i\otimes1)^T P(1\otimes p_i)&=0 &&(1\le i\le s),\\ m_F(P_{\alpha\beta})&=\delta_{\alpha\beta} &&(1\le\alpha,\beta\le d). \end{align} Here the entries of $p_i\otimes1$ and $1\otimes p_i$ are formed componentwise. There are no separate conditions on the multiplied constant row or constant column of $P$.

primaryStatements.label: alg:equivalence
primaryStatements.text: The matrix condition in Theorem \ref{thm:classification} is equivalent to \eqref{alg:tensor}.

primaryStatements.label: alg:necessity
primaryStatements.text: If \eqref{alg:tensor} has no solution, then there is an integer $r_0\geq2$ such that every $\R^D$ admits an $r_0$-coloring with no monochromatic congruent copy of $A$. In particular, every Euclidean Ramsey set satisfies the matrix condition of Theorem \ref{thm:classification}.

primaryStatements.name: A path criterion
primaryStatements.label: paths:criterion
primaryStatements.text: Suppose that for every integer $n\ge1$ there are two paths with the same endpoint and weights $\lambda>0$ and $\mu\ge0$ satisfying $\mu/\lambda<1/n$. Then $A$ is Euclidean Ramsey.

primaryStatements.label: groups:endpoints
primaryStatements.text: Suppose $q>0$ and $f_i,g_i\in\R^\ell$ satisfy \[ \|f_i-f_j\|^2=\|a_i-a_j\|^2,\qquad \|g_i-g_j\|^2=q\|a_i-a_j\|^2 \quad(1\le i,j\le s), \] and each $g_i$ is a coordinate permutation of $f_i$. For every $\delta>0$ there exist two paths with the same endpoint and weights $\lambda>0$ and $\mu\ge0$ such that \[ \frac{\mu}{\lambda}\le q+s\delta. \]

primaryStatements.label: cons:spherical
primaryStatements.text: Every finite Euclidean Ramsey set is spherical.

primaryStatements.label: cons:transitive
primaryStatements.text: Every nonempty subset of a finite transitive Euclidean set is Ramsey.

primaryStatements.label: cons:quadratic
primaryStatements.text: Let $A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_s\}\subset\R^d$ be spherical and affinely span $\R^d$. Put $p_i=(1,a_i)^{\mathsf T}$ and let $F$ be its coordinate field. If the $s$ row vectors \[ (p_{i\alpha}p_{i\beta})_{0\le\alpha,\beta\le d} \quad(1\le i\le s) \] are linearly independent over $F$, then $A$ is Ramsey.

lean.scopeText:
A finite configuration is Euclidean Ramsey if every finite coloring of some sufficiently high-dimensional Euclidean space contains a monochromatic congruent copy at the original scale. The formalization gives the tensor-field classification for full-affine-span configurations, covers singleton and affine-span reductions, and proves that every Ramsey configuration is cospherical. It also proves that every nonempty subset of a finite transitive configuration and every nonempty set of at most five points on a circle is Ramsey. A further sufficient condition uses linear independence of the quadratic evaluation rows of a spherical configuration.

The formalization also gives spherical non-Ramsey examples: the specified twelve-point set on the unit circle has a fifty-color obstruction in every positive dimension, and a nine-point circle configuration built from algebraically independent parameters is non-Ramsey.

sections.title: From a counterexample to a strict subset inequality

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Every nonempty finite oriented graph has a vertex \(v\) such that \[ \abs{N_1^+(v)}\leq \abs{N_2^+(v)}. \]

primaryStatements.name: Counterexample reduction
primaryStatements.label: prop:counterexample-reduction
primaryStatements.text: If Theorem \ref{thm:main} has a counterexample, then there is a finite nonempty oriented graph $G$ in which every vertex has positive indegree and \begin{equation} \abs{U}+\abs{F_G^2(U)}<2\abs{F_G(U)} \qquad\text{for every }\varnothing\ne U\subsetneq V(G). \end{equation}

primaryStatements.label: prop:no-concavity
primaryStatements.text: There is no nonempty finite oriented graph $G$ in which every vertex has an in-neighbor and whose one-step image operator \[ F(U)=\{y\in V(G):x\to y\text{ for some }x\in U\} \] satisfies \begin{equation} \abs{U}+\abs{F^2(U)}<2\abs{F(U)} \qquad(\varnothing\ne U\subsetneq V(G)), \end{equation} where $F^2=F\circ F$.

primaryStatements.name: Weighted second-neighborhood forms
primaryStatements.label: cor:weighted-forms
primaryStatements.text: Let \(D\) be a nonempty finite oriented graph, and write \(A(D)\) for its arc set. For a vertex weighting \(\eta:V(D)\to[0,\infty)\), write \(\eta(S)=\sum_{x\in S}\eta(x)\). Then the following hold. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item For every vertex weighting \(\eta:V(D)\to[0,\infty)\), there is a vertex \(v\in V(D)\) such that \[ \eta(N_1^+(v))\leq\eta(N_2^+(v)). \] \item There is a vertex weighting \(\eta:V(D)\to[0,\infty)\) with \(\sum_{x\in V(D)}\eta(x)=1\) such that \[ \eta(N_1^+(v))\leq\eta(N_2^+(v))\qquad\text{for every }v\in V(D). \] The entries of this weighting need not all be positive. \item For every arc weighting \(w:A(D)\to[0,\infty)\), extend the notation by setting \(w(vs)=0\) when \(vs\notin A(D)\). For \(v,s\in V(D)\), put \[ \beta_v^w(s)=\max\Bigl(\{0\}\cup \{w(us)-w(vs):u\in V(D),\ v\to u\to s\}\Bigr). \] Then there is a vertex \(v\in V(D)\) such that \[ \sum_{s\in V(D)}\beta_v^w(s) \geq \sum_{u\in N_1^+(v)}w(vu). \] The maximum is zero if there is no indicated two-step path. Such paths are determined by the arcs of \(D\), so an arc of weight zero is still present and is not treated as a missing arc. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.name: Non-neighbors and directed cycles
primaryStatements.label: cor:directed-cycle-consequences
primaryStatements.text: Let \(D\) be a nonempty finite oriented graph of order \(n\). For \(v\in V(D)\), write \[ N_1^-(v)=\{u:u\to v\},\qquad d^\pm(v)=\abs{N_1^\pm(v)},\qquad \delta^\pm(D)=\min_{x\in V(D)}d^\pm(x). \] Define the non-neighbors of \(v\), excluding \(v\) itself, by \[ Z(v)=V(D)\setminus \bigl(\{v\}\cup N_1^+(v)\cup N_1^-(v)\bigr). \] Then the following hold. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item If \(D\) has no directed \(3\)-cycle, then some vertex \(v\) satisfies \[ d^+(v)\leq\abs{Z(v)},\qquad n-1\geq 2d^+(v)+d^-(v). \] \item If \(\delta^+(D)\geq n/3\) and \(\delta^-(D)\geq n/3\), then \(D\) contains a directed \(3\)-cycle. \item If \(r\geq1\) is an integer, \(d^+(v)=d^-(v)=r\) for every vertex, and \(D\) has directed girth exactly four, then \(n\geq3r+1\). \end{enumerate} Here directed girth is the length of a shortest directed cycle.

lean.scopeText: Seymour's second-neighborhood conjecture asserts that every nonempty finite oriented graph has a vertex with at least as many second out-neighbors as first out-neighbors. The formalized result proves this assertion, where the second neighborhood consists of vertices at directed distance exactly two. The initial vertex and first neighbors are excluded from that count, and sinks are included.

primaryStatements.text: There is a universal constant \(C>0\) such that, for every integer \(k\ge1\), every finite \(k\)-edge-connected undirected multigraph without loops and with at least two vertices has a spanning tree \(T\) satisfying \[ |\delta_T(S)|\le\frac Ck\,|\delta_G(S)| \qquad\text{for every }\varnothing\ne S\subsetneq V. \]

primaryStatements.name: Nash--Williams--Tutte
primaryStatements.label: thm:packing
primaryStatements.text: For a positive integer \(r\), a graph \(H\) contains \(r\) edge-disjoint spanning trees if and only if \[ |E_H(\mathcal P)|\ge r(|\mathcal P|-1) \qquad\text{for every partition }\mathcal P\text{ of }V(H). \]

primaryStatements.name: Polynomial shortcut bound
primaryStatements.label: thm:hierarchy-power
primaryStatements.text: There is an absolute integer $q_H\ge2$ such that the following holds for each integer $q\ge q_H$. Let $H$ have a locally $q$-connected hierarchy, and let $\mathcal M$ be any collection of its nonroot nodes satisfying $|O(A)|\ge |P(A)|/q$. Then $H$ has a shortcut matrix $D$ such that \begin{equation} \frac{1}{|O(A)|}\sum_{e\in O(A)}R_D(e)\le q^{-31/40} \qquad(A\in\mathcal M). \end{equation} The cutoff is independent of the graph, the hierarchy depth and the marked collection $\mathcal M$.

primaryStatements.name: Shortcut extraction
primaryStatements.label: thm:extraction
primaryStatements.text: For all sufficiently large integers \(r\), every \(r\)-tree-packable graph \(H\) admits \(X\succ0\) such that \begin{equation} L_H\preceq X,\qquad \mathbf1_S^{\mathsf T}X\mathbf1_S\le3|\delta_H(S)| \quad(\varnothing\ne S\subsetneq V), \end{equation} and the edges with \(R_X(e)\le4r^{-1/2}\) contain \(q\) edge-disjoint spanning trees. The lower threshold on \(r\) is independent of \(H\) and \(n\).

primaryStatements.name: Packing-preserving sparsification
primaryStatements.label: prop:step
primaryStatements.text: There is an absolute integer $r_{\mathrm{step}}$ such that the following holds for every integer $r\geq r_{\mathrm{step}}$. If $H$ has at least two vertices and contains $r$ edge-disjoint spanning trees, set \[ u=r^{-1/16},\qquad q=\lfloor(1-u)r\rfloor, \qquad \epsilon=6r^{-1/2},\qquad \tau=2\sqrt\epsilon+\epsilon. \] Then $H$ has a spanning subgraph $H'$ containing at least \begin{equation} r'=\left\lfloor\frac{(1-4u)r}{2}\right\rfloor \end{equation} edge-disjoint spanning trees, such that every nonempty proper $S\subset V(H)$ satisfies \begin{equation} |\delta_{H'}(S)|\leq \left(\frac12+3\tau\right)|\delta_H(S)|. \end{equation} The cutoff may be chosen so that, in addition, \begin{equation} \frac5{16}\leq\frac{r'}r\leq\frac12, \qquad \frac{\frac12+3\tau}{r'/r}\leq1+15u. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Marcus--Spielman--Srivastava, {\cite[Theorem 1.4
primaryStatements.label: thm:mss
primaryStatements.text: {MSS}}] Let $\epsilon>0$, and let $v_1,\ldots,v_m$ be independent random vectors with finite support in $\mathbb C^d$. If \begin{equation} \sum_{i=1}^m\mathbb E[v_iv_i^*]=I_d, \qquad \mathbb E\|v_i\|^2\leq\epsilon\quad(1\leq i\leq m), \end{equation} then \begin{equation} \mathbb P\left\{ \left\|\sum_{i=1}^m v_iv_i^*\right\| \leq(1+\sqrt\epsilon)^2\right\}>0. \end{equation} Here $*$ denotes conjugate transpose and the norm is the operator norm. In particular, some outcome satisfies the corresponding positive-semidefinite upper bound. Real vectors are a special case.

primaryStatements.name: Geometric bag extraction
primaryStatements.label: prop:hierarchy-bags
primaryStatements.text: Let $T$ be a nonempty finite set of $\alpha$-bad nodes with positive boundary sums, where $0<\alpha\le1$. Define \[ \begin{aligned} J&=1+\lceil\log_2(256/\alpha^2)\rceil, &C_2(\alpha)&=128J^4, &s&=\alpha/C_2(\alpha),\\ L&=2+\lceil\log_2(1/s)\rceil, &H&=1+\lceil\log_2(24/(\lambda s^2))\rceil, &C_1(\epsilon)&=1024\epsilon^{-2}. \end{aligned} \] Suppose $\beta>1$, $0<\epsilon<1/3$, $0<\lambda<1$, and $s^\epsilon\le(48\beta C_1(\epsilon))^{-1}$. There is a $\lambda$-geometric sequence of families, consisting either entirely of $\beta$-compact bags or entirely of $s^{1+2\epsilon}$-assigned bags assigned to distinct nodes of $T$, whose mass satisfies \begin{equation} \mathsf M\ge \frac{s^\epsilon}{384\beta C_1(\epsilon)C_2(\alpha)LH} \sum_{t\in T}\frac1{|O(t)|} \left(\sum_{e\in O(t)}a_e\right)^2. \end{equation} In particular, all losses are functions of $\alpha,\epsilon,\beta$ and $\lambda$, independent of the number of vertices and hierarchy depth.

primaryStatements.name: Compact-bag charging
primaryStatements.label: prop:hierarchy-compact
primaryStatements.text: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite \(k\)-edge-connected multigraph, and let \(X_v\in Q=[0,1]^h\) for \(v\in V\). Suppose \((\mathcal F_i)\) is a finite or countable \(\lambda\)-geometric sequence of nonempty families of \(\beta\)-compact bags, of respective types \((\delta_i,\Delta_i)\), where \(0<\lambda\le 1/12\) and \(\beta\ge36\). Thus all balls in \(\mathcal F_i\) are mutually disjoint ordinary balls \(B_Q(X_v,\delta_i)\), every bag \(D\in\mathcal F_i\) has at least two balls and center diameter at most \(\Delta_i\), and \[ \beta\Delta_i\le |D|\delta_i, \qquad \Delta_{i+1}\le\lambda\delta_i. \] Then \begin{equation} \frac{k}{4}\sum_i\delta_i\sum_{D\in\mathcal F_i}|D| \le \sum_{e\in E}\|X_e\|_1, \qquad X_{\{u,v\}}=X_u-X_v. \end{equation}

definitions.name: Hierarchy and its boundaries
definitions.label: def:hierarchy
definitions.text: Let $H=(V,E)$ be a finite loopless multigraph. A hierarchy on $V$ is a finite rooted tree of distinct nonempty vertex sets. Its root is $V$, its leaves are the singleton sets, and the children of every nonleaf form a partition of that node into at least two sets. For a nonroot node $A$, write $A^*$ for its parent and define \[ P(A)=\delta_H(A),\qquad O(A)=E_H(A,A^*\setminus A). \] All edge sets here retain multiplicities. Given an integer $h\ge2$, the hierarchy is locally $h$-connected if $H[A]$ is $h$-edge-connected for every node $A$. For singleton nodes this condition is vacuous.

definitions.name: Balls, bags, and geometric sequences
definitions.label: hb:definitions
definitions.text: Set $Q=[0,1]^d$ and \[ B_Q(x,r)=\{y\in Q:\|y-x\|_1<r\}\qquad(r>0). \] A bag is a nonempty collection of pairwise disjoint such balls, all of the same radius and with centers among the $X_v$. Its type is $(\delta)$ when that radius is $\delta$, and its type is $(\delta,\Delta)$ when, in addition, all distances between its centers are at most $\Delta$. Its size $|\mathrm{Bag}|$ is its number of balls. For $\beta>1$, a bag of type $(\delta,\Delta)$ is $\beta$-compact if \[ |\mathrm{Bag}|\ge2,\qquad \beta\Delta\le\delta|\mathrm{Bag}|. \] The midpoint of two centers belongs to $Q$, so disjoint radius-$\delta$ balls have centers at distance at least $2\delta$. Hence a compact bag has $\Delta\ge2\delta$. A bag of radius $\delta$ is $\eta$-assigned to $t$ if \[ |\mathrm{Bag}_t|\ge\eta|O(t)|, \] and every ball has a center $X_u$ with $u\in V(t)$ and an edge $uv\in O(t)$ such that $d_{uv}<\delta$. A family of bags is nonempty, and all balls in all its bags are mutually disjoint. A compact family has type $(\delta,\Delta)$ when its bags have that common type. An assigned family has type $(\delta,T)$ when its bags are assigned to distinct nodes in $T$ and have radius $\delta$. For $0<\lambda<1$, a sequence of compact families of types $(\delta_i,\Delta_i)$ is $\lambda$-geometric if $\Delta_{i+1}<\lambda\delta_i$ for all successive families. A sequence of assigned families of types $(\delta_i,T_i)$ is $\lambda$-geometric if $\delta_{i+1}<\lambda\delta_i$ and the sets $T_i$ are pairwise disjoint. Its mass is \[ \mathsf M=\sum_i\delta_i \sum_{\mathrm{Bag}\in\mathcal F_i}|\mathrm{Bag}|. \]

definitions.name: Bad nodes and homogeneous subsets
definitions.label: hb:bad
definitions.text: For $0<\alpha\le1$, a nonroot node $t$ with $O(t)\ne\varnothing$ is $\alpha$-bad if \[ \left(\frac{\sum_{e\in O(t)}a_e}{|O(t)|}\right)^2 \ge\frac{\alpha}{|O(t)|}\sum_{e\in O(t)}d_e. \] Only nodes with a positive boundary sum need be retained. A set of edges is $c$-homogeneous if its $a_e^2$ are positive and any two of them have ratio less than $c$, and the same holds for its $d_e$. A subset $O'(t)\subseteq O(t)$ is $\gamma$-dominating if \[ \left(\sum_{e\in O'(t)}a_e\right)^2 \ge\gamma\left(\sum_{e\in O(t)}a_e\right)^2. \]

definitions.name: Valid labeling
definitions.label: ha:valid-labeling
definitions.text: A collection $Z$ of labeled ordinary and hollow balls is valid if the following four conditions hold for every record $B$ with center $x$ and radii $a<b$. \begin{enumerate} \renewcommand{\theenumi}{L\arabic{enumi}} \renewcommand{\labelenumi}{(\theenumi)} \item The labels and conflict domain have the form just described; in particular $t(B)\in C(B)$. \item For $s\in t_P(B)$ and $\{v,w\}\in P(s)$, \[ \|x-X_v\|_1\ge b,\qquad \|x-X_w\|_1\ge b. \] \item There is $u\in L(B)$ with $\|x-X_u\|_1\le a$ and at least $k/4$ pairwise edge-disjoint paths starting at $u$ and ending at vertices of distance at least $b$ from $x$. The paths lie in $G[V(t(B))]$ if $B$ is nonavoiding, and in $G[V(t(B))\setminus V(t_d(B))]$ if it is avoiding. \item Distinct records whose geometric balls intersect have disjoint conflict domains. \end{enumerate}

The strong thin-tree conjecture asks for spanning trees that cross every cut sparsely relative to the original graph. The formalized result gives one absolute constant $C>0$ such that every finite loopless $k$-edge-connected multigraph with at least two vertices has a spanning tree crossing each nontrivial cut at most $(C/k)$ times the original cut size. Parallel edges remain distinct. No numerical value of $C$ or construction algorithm is asserted.

The strong thin-tree problem asks for a spanning tree that crosses every cut sparsely relative to the original graph. The formalization gives one deterministic polynomial-time algorithm and an absolute constant $C>0$ such that a finite $k$-edge-connected loopless multigraph yields a spanning tree using at most a $C/k$ fraction of the edges of every cut. The input may encode parallel-edge multiplicities in binary, and the running time is polynomial in that binary input length.

papers.title: A polynomial-time construction of strong thin trees
papers.abstract: We give a deterministic polynomial-time construction of strong thin trees. Given a finite k-edge-connected loopless multigraph on at least one vertex, the algorithm constructs a spanning tree meeting every cut in at most a $C/k$ fraction of its edges, for a universal constant C. The running time is polynomial in the binary input length, including when parallel-edge multiplicities are encoded in binary.

primaryStatements.name: Algorithmic strong thin trees
primaryStatements.label: thm:tt-algorithm
primaryStatements.text: There is an absolute constant $C$ with the following property. Given a finite $k$-edge-connected multigraph $G$ on at least one vertex and an integer $k\ge1$, a deterministic algorithm returns a spanning tree $T$ satisfying \begin{equation} |\delta_T(S)|\le \frac Ck\,|\delta_G(S)| \qquad(\varnothing\ne S\subsetneq V(G)) \end{equation} in time polynomial in the total binary input length, whether edges are listed explicitly or multiplicities are encoded in binary. For a one-vertex graph the answer is the empty tree.

primaryStatements.name: Hierarchy bound for the metric test cone
primaryStatements.label: thm:tg-hierarchy
primaryStatements.text: There is an absolute integer $h_0$ such that, for every integer $h\ge h_0$, every locally $h$-connected hierarchy of $G$, and every collection $\mathcal M$ of nonroot nodes satisfying $|O(A)|\ge |P(A)|/h$, there is a matrix $D\succ0$ on $\mathsf E$ with \begin{align} \ip{D}{Z}&\le\ip{L_G}{Z} &&(Z\in\mathcal N),\\ \frac1{|O(A)|}\sum_{e\in O(A)}b_e^TD^{-1}b_e &\le h^{-31/40} &&(A\in\mathcal M). \end{align} The cutoff is independent of the graph and the hierarchy depth.

primaryStatements.name: Simultaneous response
primaryStatements.label: prop:tg-response
primaryStatements.text: Let $H$ be connected and let $G\subseteq H$ be a spanning subgraph. Let $r$ be a sufficiently large integer, put $h=\lfloor r/2\rfloor$, and suppose $G$ and the subgraphs induced by all parts of a nested sequence of partitions are $h$-edge-connected, with the singleton condition vacuous. If $0<s\le r^{1/4}$, there is $Y\in\mathcal K_H$ such that, at every partition $\mathcal P$ in the sequence, all but at most $r^{-1/3}|E_G(\mathcal P)|$ crossing edges satisfy \begin{equation} Y\succeq6s\,b_eb_e^T. \end{equation} Here $E_G(\mathcal P)$ denotes the edges whose endpoints lie in different parts of $\mathcal P$.

primaryStatements.name: Constructive shortcut extraction
primaryStatements.label: prop:ta-extraction
primaryStatements.text: There are absolute constants $A$ and $r_0$ such that the following holds. If an explicit multigraph $H$ on at least two vertices contains $r\ge r_0$ edge-disjoint spanning trees, one can deterministically compute a rational $X\in\mathcal K_H$ and at least \[ (1-Ar^{-1/16})r \] edge-disjoint spanning trees, every edge $e$ of which satisfies $b_e^TX^{-1}b_e\le r^{-1/4}$. The running time and output encoding length are polynomial in $|V(H)|+|E(H)|$.

primaryStatements.name: Thin and cheap rounding of fractional cuts
primaryStatements.label: cor:ta-fractional-rounding
primaryStatements.text: Fix once and for all an integer $B\ge\max\{1,C\}$, where $C$ is the constant in Theorem \ref{thm:tt-algorithm}. Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite undirected graph on $n\ge2$ vertices, given by an explicit list of edge records; in this corollary, loops and parallel records are allowed. Given nonnegative rational numbers $x_e,c_e$ in binary, suppose that \[ x(\delta_G(S)):=\sum_{e\in\delta_G(S)}x_e\ge1 \qquad(\varnothing\ne S\subsetneq V). \] There is a deterministic algorithm, polynomial in the total binary input length, that returns a spanning tree $T\subseteq\{e\in E:x_e>0\}$ satisfying simultaneously \begin{align} |\delta_T(S)|&\le24B\,x(\delta_G(S)) &&(\varnothing\ne S\subsetneq V), \\ c(T):=\sum_{e\in T}c_e&\le24B\sum_{e\in E}c_ex_e. \end{align} The cut inequalities are a promise on the input; no metric assumption on the costs is required.

primaryStatements.name: Rational rank-one signing
primaryStatements.label: thm:rational-signing
primaryStatements.text: Given rational Hermitian matrices $H_1,\ldots,H_N$ of rank at most one, a deterministic algorithm returns signs $\sigma_i\in\{-1,1\}$ such that \[ \left\|\sum_i\sigma_iH_i\right\| \le40\left\|\sum_iH_i^2\right\|^{1/2}. \] Its running time is polynomial in the total binary encoding length. Consequently, for rational columns $v_i$ with $\sum_i v_iv_i^*=I$, the same algorithm gives discrepancy at most $40\sqrt{\max_i\|v_i\|^2}$.

papers.title: Graph Decompositions at the Integral Expectation Threshold
papers.abstract: We prove the graph-decomposition conjecture of Ascoli, He, Park, and Talagrand. Every graph admits a partition into a universally bounded number of fixed edge pieces, each having ordinary containment threshold at most a universal constant times the original graph's integral expectation threshold. The partition is chosen before sampling the random host, and the separate embeddings of the pieces need not agree on shared vertices.
papers.familySummary: Proves that integral and fractional expectation thresholds differ by at most a universal factor, and resolves Talagrand's discrete-convexity conjecture. The pieces' embeddings need not agree on shared vertices.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: There exist an absolute integer $k\geq2$ and an absolute constant $L\geq1$ such that, for every $n\geq2$ and every graph $H$ on at most $n$ vertices, the edges of $H$ admit a partition \[ E(H)=E(H_1)\,\dot\cup\,\cdots\,\dot\cup\,E(H_k) \quad\text{with}\quad p_c(H_i;n)\leq Lq(H;n)\qquad(1\leq i\leq k). \] The pieces may be empty and may share vertices. The partition depends only on $H,n$ and is fixed before the random host is sampled.

primaryStatements.name: Discrete convexity, {\cite[Theorem 1.1
primaryStatements.label: thm:discrete
primaryStatements.text: {OpenAI26DC}}] Set $K_0=2^{75}$. For every nonempty finite set $X$, every $r\in(0,1)$, and every family $\calD\subseteq2^X$ with $\mu_r(\calD)\geq1-1/K_0$, the family \[ \mathcal E_{K_0}(\calD)= \{S\subseteq X:S\not\subseteq D_1\cup\cdots\cup D_{K_0} \text{ for every }D_1,\ldots,D_{K_0}\in\calD\} \] has a cover of cost at most $1/2$ at the same parameter $r$. The family $\calD$ need not be monotone, and members of a tuple may repeat.

primaryStatements.label: cor:typical-cover
primaryStatements.text: Let $n\geq2$, let $H$ have an edge and at most $n$ vertices, and suppose $q(H;n)<r<1$. If a family of graphs on $[n]$ satisfies $\mu_r(\calD)\geq1-1/K_0$, then some copy of $H$ has its edges contained in the union of $K_0$ members of $\calD$.

primaryStatements.name: Neighborhood transfer
primaryStatements.label: prop:transfer
primaryStatements.text: There is an absolute integer $N_1$ such that the following holds for every $n\geq N_1$ and every $r,s$ satisfying \eqref{eq:parameters}. There exists $\calD=\calD(n,r,s)\subseteq2^{E(K_n)}$ with $\mu_r(\calD)\geq1-1/K_0$ such that, whenever \begin{itemize} \item $Y\subseteq[n]$ has $|Y|\leq n^{2/3}$; \item $J$ is a labelled bipartite graph with all edges between $Y$ and $[n]\setminus Y$, and $E(J)\subseteq E(G)$ for some $G\in\calD$; \item at most $n/8$ vertices outside $Y$ have positive degree in $J$, and all of those degrees are at most $s$; \end{itemize} one has \begin{equation} p_c(J;n)\leq r_*:=1-(1-r)^{32}\leq32r. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.label: prop:degree-embedding
primaryStatements.text: There is an absolute integer $N_2$ such that, for $n\geq N_2$ and $r,s$ satisfying \eqref{eq:parameters}, every graph $J$ with \[ |V_+(J)|\leq n/4,\qquad \degen(J)\leq s, \qquad\Delta(J)\leq n^{2/3} \] and at most $n$ vertices satisfies $p_c(J;n)\leq r$.

primaryStatements.label: prop:stars
primaryStatements.text: Put $A=400e^4$. There is an absolute integer $N_3$ such that, for every $n\geq N_3$ and every star forest $J$ on at most $n$ vertices with $|V_+(J)|\leq n/100$, \begin{equation} p_c(J;n)\leq2Aq(J;n). \end{equation} If $q(J;n)<1/(2A)$, the stronger bound $p_c(J;n)\leq Aq(J;n)$ holds.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: For every finite nonempty $X$ and every nonempty proper increasing family $\F\subseteq2^X$, \[ q_f(\F)\le25\cdot512^4\,q(\F). \] Both thresholds use the budget $1/2$. The constant is independent of $|X|$, the sizes of the minimal members of $\F$, and the support of the fractional cover.

primaryStatements.name: Multiscale selector estimate
primaryStatements.label: thm:multiscale-selector
primaryStatements.text: Let $X$ be a finite set, let $\F$ be a nonempty family of nonempty subsets of $X$, and suppose that $\F$ is not $p$-small, where $0<p\le 1$. For each $H\in\F$, let $\lambda_H$ be a probability mass function on $X$ supported on $H$. Set $D=256$, and let $s\ge 0$ be an integer such that \[ p\sum_{i=1}^s D^i\le \frac12. \] Independently color the elements of $X$ by a map $a:X\to\{1,\ldots,s+1\}$, with color probabilities \begin{equation} \pi_i=D^ip\quad(1\le i\le s), \qquad \pi_{s+1}=1-p\sum_{i=1}^sD^i. \end{equation} For a coloring $v$, write $A_i(v)=\{x\in X:v(x)\le i\}$. With probability at least $9/10$, there is an $H\in\F$ such that \begin{equation} \lambda_H(A_i(a))\ge 1-2^{-i} \qquad(1\le i\le s). \end{equation} In particular, with probability at least $9/10$, there is an $H\in\F$ for which \begin{equation} \sum_{x\in X}a(x)\lambda_H(x)\le 2. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.label: cor:two-unions
primaryStatements.text: Let $X$ be a finite nonempty set, let $0<p<1$, and let $\mathcal A\subseteq2^X$ satisfy $\mu_p(\mathcal A)>1/2$. Set $C=25\cdot512^4$. There is a family $\mathcal G\subseteq2^X$ such that \[ \operatorname{Bad}_2(\mathcal A)\subseteq\langle\mathcal G\rangle, \qquad \sum_{S\in\mathcal G}\left(\frac{p}{2C}\right)^{|S|}\le\frac12. \] In particular, $\operatorname{Bad}_2(\mathcal A)$ is $(p/(2C))$-small. No monotonicity assumption on $\mathcal A$ is needed.

lean.scopeText:
Talagrand's expectation-threshold conjecture asks whether the fractional and integral expectation thresholds are comparable by an absolute constant. The formalized result proves $q_f(\mathcal F)\le25\cdot512^4 q(\mathcal F)$ for every nonempty proper increasing family on a finite nonempty ground set. Both thresholds use cover budget $1/2$, and fractional covers may assign weights to every subset, including the empty set.

The formalized result proves Talagrand's discrete-convexity assertion with $k=2^{75}$. If a family of subsets of a finite nonempty ground set has Bernoulli-$p$ measure at least $1-1/k$, then the sets not contained in a union of $k$ members form a $p$-small family: they have a containment cover of total $p$-cost at most $1/2$. This holds for every $0<p<1$, with repeated members allowed in the union and no monotonicity assumption.

papers.title: The second Kahn–Kalai conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the second Kahn–Kalai conjecture. For every finite simple graph H with h ≥ 1 edges and at most n vertices, the threshold for $G(n,p)$ to contain an ordinary copy of H is at most $C p_{\mathrm E}(n,H)(1+\log_2 h)$, where C is universal. Here $p_{\mathrm E}(n,H)$ is the least density at which every subgraph of H has expected copy count at least one half.

sections.title: Graph thresholds and the main result

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: For every $n\ge2$ and every finite simple graph $H$ with $h=e(H)\ge1$ edges and at most $n$ vertices, \begin{equation} \pc(n,H)\le \min\{1,\;2048\ee^{50}\pE(n,H)(1+\log_2 h)\}. \end{equation} In particular, \[ \pc(n,H)\le6144\ee^{50}\pE(n,H)\log_2 n. \]

primaryStatements.name: Tree covering
primaryStatements.label: thm:tree
primaryStatements.text: Let $\TT$ be a disjoint probability tree on a finite set $X$, with $k\ge1$ levels. Suppose that every level is $\sigma$-spread, where $\sigma>0$, and that its positive integer capacities satisfy \[ \ell_{i+1}\ge16\ell_i\qquad(1\le i<k). \] Set \[ r=\min\{1,\;16\ee^{50}\sigma(1+\log_2\ell_k)\}. \] Then \[ \PP_{W\sim\mu_r} \bigl(\UU(P)\subseteq W\text{ for some path }P\text{ of }\TT\bigr) \ge\tfrac23. \]

lean.scopeText: The second Kahn–Kalai conjecture compares the threshold for a random graph to contain a fixed graph with its expectation threshold. The formalized result proves the comparison up to a universal factor times $1+\log_2|E(H)|$, and hence up to a universal factor times $\log_2 n$, for every graph $H$ with at least one edge and at most $n$ vertices, $n\ge2$. The bounds use the actual containment and expectation thresholds.

papers.title: Bounded-degree coboundary expanders in every dimension
papers.abstract: For every integer d ≥ 3, we construct arbitrarily large finite d-dimensional simplicial complexes with uniformly bounded vertex degrees and uniform 𝔽2 coboundary expansion in every degree below d. Together with the known graph and two-dimensional cases, this establishes the existence of bounded-degree 𝔽2 coboundary expanders in every positive dimension.
papers.familySummary: Constructs arbitrarily large finite d-dimensional simplicial complexes, for every d ≥ 3, with uniformly bounded vertex degrees and uniform 𝔽2 coboundary expansion in every degree below d. Together with the known graph and two-dimensional cases, this establishes the existence of such expanders in every positive dimension.
papers.subject: Combinatorics
papers.sourceAbstract: For every integer $d\ge3$, we construct arbitrarily large finite $d$-dimensional simplicial complexes with uniformly bounded vertex degrees and uniform $\mathbb F_2$ coboundary expansion in every degree below $d$. Together with the known graph and two-dimensional cases, this establishes the existence of bounded-degree $\mathbb F_2$ coboundary expanders in every positive dimension.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: For every integer $d\ge3$, there exist constants $D<\infty$, $\eps>0$, and finite connected pure $d$-dimensional simplicial complexes $X_m$, with $|X_m(0)|\longrightarrow\infty$, such that every vertex belongs to at most $D$ faces of dimension $d$ and, for every $f\in C^i(X_m;\F)$, \begin{equation} \norm{\delta_i f}_{X_m,i+1} \ge \eps\,\dist_{X_m,i}(f,B^i(X_m)) \qquad(0\le i<d). \end{equation} The constants are independent of $m$, $i$, and $f$.

primaryStatements.label: prop:L-acyclic
primaryStatements.text: The complex $L$ satisfies \eqref{eq:L-acyclic}.

primaryStatements.label: cor:generation
primaryStatements.text: The simple generators $x_i$, $i\in S$, generate $U$.

primaryStatements.label: prop:homology-comparisons
primaryStatements.text: For $0<j<n-1$ and $m\ge2$, \begin{equation} H_j(U;\F)=0,\qquad H_j(T_m;\F)\cong H_j(\Gamma_N(m);\F). \end{equation} Moreover, $T_m$ is connected.

primaryStatements.label: prop:quotient-homology
primaryStatements.text: For every $m\ge2$, \[ H_j(\Gamma_N(m);\F)=H_j(T_m;\F)=H^j(T_m;\F)=0 \qquad(1\le j\le d-1). \]

lean.scopeText: The formalization constructs bounded-degree $\mathbb F_2$ coboundary expanders in every dimension $d\ge3$. For each such $d$, it gives finite pure connected $d$-dimensional simplicial complexes with vertex counts tending to infinity, one uniform bound on top-dimensional degree at each vertex, and one positive coboundary-expansion constant in every degree below $d$. The constants may depend on $d$. The graph and two-dimensional cases used for the paper's all-positive-dimensions conclusion are separate.

papers.title: Deterministic nonbipartite Ramanujan graphs in every fixed degree
papers.abstract: For every fixed integer d ≥ 3, we give a deterministic algorithm that constructs a simple nonbipartite d-regular Ramanujan graph on every sufficiently large even number n of vertices. It outputs the full adjacency list in polynomially many bit operations, with an exponent that may depend on d. Every nonconstant adjacency eigenvalue lies strictly between $-2\sqrt{d-1}$ and $2\sqrt{d-1}$.

A deterministic algorithm outputs the full adjacency list in polynomial bit time, with exponent depending on d.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: For every integer $d\ge3$ there are constants $n_0(d)$ and $k_d$ and a deterministic algorithm with the following property. On input an even integer $n\ge n_0(d)$, the algorithm outputs the adjacency list of a simple $d$-regular graph $G$ on $n$ vertices in $O_d(n^{k_d})$ bit operations, and \[ -2\sqrt{d-1}<\lambda<2\sqrt{d-1} \quad\text{for every eigenvalue $\lambda$ of }A_G|_{\mathbf1^\perp}. \] In particular, $G$ is connected and nonbipartite.

primaryStatements.label: cor:target-size
primaryStatements.text: For every fixed $d\ge3$, a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm, on every sufficiently large integer input $N$, produces a simple connected nonbipartite $d$-regular Ramanujan graph $G$ with $N\le |V(G)|\le N+1\le2N$.

primaryStatements.name: Positive-excess account at a prescribed scale
primaryStatements.label: lem:positive-excess-account
primaryStatements.text: Let $B_s>0$ and $\lambda>0$. Suppose an alive scalar quantity has an ordinary increment $\Delta$ with $|\mathbb E\Delta|\le\mu$, $\mathbb E\Delta^2\le\nu$, and $|\Delta|\le\lambda B_s$. For each fixed even $p\ge2$, the upper-excess account for either sign, measured in units $\lambda B_s$, has expectation factor at most \begin{equation} 1+C_p\left(\frac{\mu}{\lambda B_s} +\frac{\nu}{\lambda^2B_s^2}\right). \end{equation} The threshold, exceptional-transition, and death conventions are those of Lemma \ref{lem:scalar-excess}.

primaryStatements.name: Early pairing
primaryStatements.label: prop:early-phase
primaryStatements.text: For the fixed parameters of the construction and all sufficiently large \(n\), the simultaneous discounted-account rule can be run from the empty pairing down to \(l_1\) unresolved stubs. It retains the structural estimates \eqref{eq:original-3}--\eqref{eq:original-7}, positivity of every tracked precision, and, at every tracked point, \[ |L_1|\le n^{.075a}/\alpha_*,\qquad |L_0|\le n^{.105a}/\alpha_*^2,\qquad \max_{i,j}|E_{ij}|\le n^{.33a}/\sqrt{l_0}. \] The low-square estimates \eqref{eq:original-23} hold with any prescribed sufficiently small fixed loss exponent, for any fixed near radius needed in the proof. At every primary point, \begin{equation} \mathcal T \ \ge\ n^{-\theta/2}(n^{-1}+\alpha/l)^{-1} \end{equation} after a fixed constant is allowed in the right-hand side.

primaryStatements.name: Cleanup estimates
primaryStatements.label: prop:cleanup
primaryStatements.text: Assume the early-phase estimates at $l_1$, and maintain the structural estimators during cleanup. With the simultaneous discounted-account choice rule, the cleanup interval can be completed so that, at every chosen state, the precision matrices remain positive definite, \eqref{eq:original-8} holds, and \[ T_S=\sum_{x\in S}e_x(x)^2\leq n^\eta,\qquad |E_{ij}|\leq2B_k. \] The second inequality holds for every surviving pair $(i,j)$ of total level $k=\nu(i)+\nu(j)$. At primary points the lower estimate for $\mathcal T$ persists in the form \[ \mathcal T\geq n^{-\theta}(n^{-1}+\alpha/l)^{-1}. \] In particular the consequences \eqref{eq:original-10} and \eqref{eq:original-11}, and a polynomial-loss form of \eqref{eq:original-13}, hold at $l_0$.

primaryStatements.name: Completion of the separated boundary
primaryStatements.label: prop:boundary-completion
primaryStatements.text: Under these inputs, the account rule can deterministically complete the pairing. Every added edge is simple and preserves the girth exclusion. At the end the precision is positive at every primary point for both signs. There is a reference matrix $\widehat P_{\rm fin}$, defined below by exact numerical updates from a smooth coefficient truncation at the stop, such that at every retained primary parameter and both signs, \[ \max_{i,j}|(W_{\rm fin}-\widehat P_{\rm fin})_{ij}| \le C B_B, \qquad B_B=\frac{n^{.40a}}{\sqrt{l_2}}. \] The construction retains the stop configuration and the matching added after it. These define the same family $\widehat P_{\rm fin}(h)$ throughout the primary interval. All the accounts, candidate values and transitions in this section can be evaluated in a number of bit operations polynomial in $n$, with an exponent depending only on the fixed parameters.

primaryStatements.name: Exact repair by simultaneous switches
primaryStatements.label: thm:exact-repair
primaryStatements.text: Fix an integer $d\ge3$ and a constant $C_0\ge1$. Put \[ \begin{gathered} q=d-1,\qquad s=2\sqrt q,\qquad a=10^{-4},\\ e=n^{-2/3+a},\qquad W_b=n^{-2/3+100a},\qquad M=\lceil n^{1/3+10a}\rceil. \end{gathered} \] There are constants $n_0,k$, depending only on $d,C_0$, and a deterministic algorithm with the following property for $n\ge n_0$. Let $G$ be a simple $d$-regular graph on $n$ vertices. Let $v_2,\ldots,v_n$ be an orthonormal eigenbasis of $A_G$ on $\mathbf1^\perp$, with eigenvalues $\lambda_i$, and put $x_i^\sigma=s-\sigma\lambda_i$ for $\sigma\in\{+1,-1\}$. Assume the following three properties. \begin{enumerate} \item Spectral confinement. For every $i=2,\ldots,n$ and both signs, $x_i^\sigma>-e/20$. \item Local spectral mass. For every vertex $p$, both signs, and every $w\in[2e,2d]$, \[ \sum_{\substack{2\le i\le n\\x_i^\sigma\le w}}|v_i(p)|^2 \le C_0w^{3/2}. \] \item Typical edge blocks. For every pair $w_B^\sigma\in[W_b,2W_b]\setminus\{x_i^\sigma:2\le i\le n\}$, define \[ R_B^\sigma=\sum_{\substack{2\le i\le n\\x_i^\sigma\ge w_B^\sigma}} \frac{v_iv_i^T}{x_i^\sigma}. \] All but a fraction $C_0n^{-.1}$ of the $dn$ oriented edges $(p,p')$ satisfy the following bound for both signs: \[ \left\| \begin{pmatrix}(R_B^\sigma)_{pp}&(R_B^\sigma)_{pp'}\\ (R_B^\sigma)_{p'p}&(R_B^\sigma)_{p'p'}\end{pmatrix} -\frac1{d-2}\begin{pmatrix}\sqrt q&\sigma\\\sigma&\sqrt q\end{pmatrix} \right\|_{\max}\le n^{-.024}. \] Here $\|\cdot\|_{\max}$ is the largest absolute entry. The exceptional edge set may depend on the chosen pair of cutoffs. \end{enumerate} Given the adjacency list of $G$, the algorithm finds $M$ vertex-disjoint switches, each deleting two edges and inserting two edges. In $O_{d,C_0}(n^k)$ bit operations it outputs the adjacency list of a simple $d$-regular graph $G'$ on the same vertices such that \[ -2\sqrt{d-1}<\lambda_i(G')<2\sqrt{d-1} \qquad (2\le i\le n). \] In particular, $G'$ is connected and nonbipartite.

primaryStatements.label: prop:bit-complexity
primaryStatements.text: For each fixed $d$ and the fixed choices in Section \ref{subsec:hierarchy}, every stage of the preceding construction is implementable with polynomially many bit operations in $n$.

papers.title: The circulant Hadamard conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the circulant Hadamard conjecture: a real circulant Hadamard matrix has order 1 or 4. As a consequence, Barker sequences of length greater than one exist exactly at lengths 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 11, 13, proving the Barker-sequence conjecture.
papers.familySummary: Proves that real circulant Hadamard matrices exist exactly in orders 1 and 4, resolving the circulant Hadamard conjecture. Together with classical Barker-sequence results, this shows that binary sequences whose nontrivial aperiodic autocorrelations have magnitude at most 1 exist at lengths n > 1 exactly when $n\in\{2,3,4,5,7,11,13\}$.
papers.subject: Combinatorics
papers.sourceAbstract: We prove the circulant Hadamard conjecture: a real circulant Hadamard matrix has order $1$ or $4$. As a consequence, Barker sequences of length greater than one exist exactly at lengths $2,3,4,5,7,11,13$, proving the Barker-sequence conjecture.

sections.title: From local units to roots of unity

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: For a positive integer \(n\), a real circulant Hadamard matrix of order \(n\) exists if and only if \(n\in\{1,4\}\).

primaryStatements.name: Barker-sequence lengths
primaryStatements.label: cor:barker
primaryStatements.text: For an integer \(n>1\), a Barker sequence of length \(n\) exists if and only if \[ n\in\{2,3,4,5,7,11,13\}. \]

primaryStatements.label: prop:order
primaryStatements.text: If a real circulant Hadamard matrix has order \(n>1\), then \(n=4u^2\) for an odd positive integer \(u\).

primaryStatements.label: prop:alternating
primaryStatements.text: Suppose \(x\in\Z[i][P]\) satisfies \(xx^*=u^2\). Then the alternating product \(\Delta(x)\) defined in \eqref{eq:delta} belongs to \(B\) and is a root of unity. For each \(p\in I\), its order is a power of \(p\). In particular, its order is odd; if \(u\) has at least two distinct prime divisors, then \(\Delta(x)=1\).

lean.scopeText:
The formalization proves the circulant Hadamard conjecture in exact form: a real circulant Hadamard matrix of positive order $n$ exists exactly when $n=1$ or $n=4$. Explicit witnesses are supplied for both orders, with no restriction on prime factors.

It also proves the even-length part of the Barker-sequence consequence. A positive even-length sign sequence whose nonzero aperiodic autocorrelations have absolute value at most one must have length $2$ or $4$. The paper's classification of odd Barker lengths is outside this selected additional statement.

papers.title: Paired states and Hamiltonian cycles in cubic bipartite planar graphs
papers.abstract: We prove Barnette's conjecture: every finite simple cubic bipartite planar 3-vertex-connected graph has a Hamiltonian cycle.
papers.familySummary: Proves that every finite simple cubic bipartite planar 3-vertex-connected graph has a Hamiltonian cycle, resolving Barnette's conjecture. Equivalently, every three-edge path in a finite simple cubic 3-vertex-connected bipartite Pfaffian graph lies in a Hamiltonian cycle.
papers.subject: Combinatorics
papers.sourceAbstract: We prove Barnette's conjecture: every finite simple cubic bipartite planar \(3\)-vertex-connected graph has a Hamiltonian cycle.

sections.title: The dual problem and the proof strategy
Plane trees and the triangulation statement
A tree on the white faces

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Every finite simple undirected graph that is cubic, bipartite, planar, and \(3\)-vertex-connected has a Hamiltonian cycle.

primaryStatements.label: thm:partition
primaryStatements.text: Let \(T\) be a sphere triangulation whose faces are colored black and white so that each edge has one incident face of each color. For any facial triangle \(t_0\) and any edge \(e_0\) of \(t_0\), the vertex set admits a partition into two sets, each inducing a tree, such that the endpoints of \(e_0\) are in one set and the third vertex of \(t_0\) is in the other.

primaryStatements.label: prop:pairs
primaryStatements.text: If \(T\) has no separating triangle, then a pair of states exists.

primaryStatements.label: prop:forest-state
primaryStatements.text: Whenever at least one pair exists, some pair \((r,s)\) has \(Q_s\) a forest.

primaryStatements.label: cor:edge-avoidance
primaryStatements.text: For every graph \(G\) satisfying Theorem \ref{thm:main} and every edge \(e\in E(G)\), there is a Hamiltonian cycle of \(G\) avoiding \(e\).

primaryStatements.name: Prescribed paths in Pfaffian graphs
primaryStatements.label: cor:pfaffian-paths
primaryStatements.text: Let \(G\) be a finite simple undirected graph that is cubic, \(3\)-vertex-connected, Pfaffian, and bipartite. Every path on four vertices (three edges) in \(G\) is contained in a Hamiltonian cycle. In other words, \(G\) is \(P_4\)-Hamiltonian; in particular, it is Hamiltonian.

lean.scopeText: Barnette's conjecture states that every finite simple cubic bipartite planar graph that is 3-vertex-connected has a Hamiltonian cycle. The formalization proves this statement for every such graph. The selected result is the existence of a cycle visiting every vertex exactly once.
