primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: There exists $\eps_0>0$ such that for every fixed $0<\eps<\eps_0$, every bounded marked Jordan domain $(D;a,b)$, and every deterministic filled square-lattice approximation satisfying \eqref{eq:jordan-approximation}, \[ d_{\mathrm{BL}}\bigl(\mu_{n,\xi}, \operatorname{Law}(\SLE_{16/3}(D;a,b))\bigr) \xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{\P_{\mathrm{env}}}0. \] The constant $\eps_0$ is independent of the domain and its approximation.

primaryStatements.name: Four-mark test in a remaining domain
primaryStatements.label: prop:moving-test
primaryStatements.text: Consider the four-change open-cap law and any sequence of switch-revealing stopping rules before completion of its strand. Let $A_n$ be events determined by the stopped history. Suppose that, on $A_n$, there are basepoints $z_n$ and constants $r_0,\alpha_0>0$, independent of $n$ and of the history, such that \begin{enumerate} \item $B(z_n,r_0)\subset U_n$; \item in the conformal disk chart normalized at $z_n$, the four current prime-end marks, including the tip, have pairwise distance at least $\alpha_0$ on the unit circle. \end{enumerate} Assume also that the stopped prefixes form a tight family in the oriented-curve topology, as in Proposition \ref{prop:curve-tightness}. Write $\mathcal F_n$ for the stopped information, $E_{\mathrm P}$ for the primal pairing, and $\chi_{U_n}$ for the ordered cross-ratio of the four current marks. Then, for every $t>0$, \begin{equation} \P_{\mathrm{open}}\left( A_n\cap\left\{ \left|\P_{\mathrm{open}}(E_{\mathrm P}\mid\mathcal F_n) -f(\chi_{U_n})\right|>t\right\}\right)\longrightarrow0. \end{equation} The basepoints may be selected from the history. The original domains lie in a fixed bounded set, so every deterministic sequence of these basepoints has a convergent subsequence.

primaryStatements.name: Critical-temperature input
primaryStatements.label: prop:critical-input
primaryStatements.text: For sufficiently small $\eps>0$, the plus-magnetization threshold for $J_e=1+\eps\xi_e$ is the unique positive solution of \begin{equation} \bigl(e^{2\beta_c(\eps)(1+\eps)}-1\bigr) \bigl(e^{2\beta_c(\eps)(1-\eps)}-1\bigr)=2. \end{equation} The plus magnetization vanishes at this temperature. If $v_\pm=e^{2\beta_c(\eps)(1\pm\eps)}-1$ and $\theta=\frac12\log(v_+/v_-)$, then \[ v_e=\sqrt2\,e^{\theta\xi_e},\qquad \theta\longrightarrow0 \quad\text{as }\eps\downarrow0. \] The scale trajectory with vanishing perturbations constructed in \cite{Q} occurs at $h=0$ in \eqref{eq:critical-coordinate}.

primaryStatements.name: Bulk scale-transformation input
primaryStatements.label: prop:bulk-input
cor:boundary-observables
primaryStatements.text: Let a spin patch of diameter at most $r$ be separated from prescribed remote spins $\zeta$ by pure shells of one of the types in Lemma \ref{lem:boundary-transfer}, out to distance $R=dr$. Allow fixed proportional buffers around the patch and the outer cut. Let $H$ be a bounded real function of the patch spins and of any independent auxiliary variables in the patch. In the free/free case assume that the region inside the shell has no pinned spins and that $H$ is invariant under reversal of all its spin arguments. There are constants $C<\infty$ and $\eta>0$ such that \begin{align} \mathop{\mathrm{osc}}_\zeta\mathbb E_{\mathrm{pure}}[H\mid\zeta] &\le C a(d)\|H\|_\infty, \\ \mathop{\mathrm{osc}}_\zeta \log\mathbb E_{\mathrm{pure}}[e^H\mid\zeta] &\le C a(d)\|H\|_\infty, \end{align} where $a(d)=d^{-2}$ at a straight homogeneous side and $a(d)=d^{-\eta}$ at a corner or boundary-condition change. Here $\mathop{\mathrm{osc}} f=\sup f-\inf f$. The bounds hold for each fixed sufficiently large $d$ and sufficiently fine mesh, with thresholds chosen simultaneously for any finite collection of ratios.

primaryStatements.name: Fixed polygon comparison
primaryStatements.label: prop:polygon-comparison
primaryStatements.text: There exists $\theta_0>0$ with the following property. Fix $0<\theta<\theta_0$, a collared orthogonal polygon $\mathcal P$, and four distinct boundary marks in straight side interiors. Wire each of two opposite marked boundary arcs separately and leave the intervening arcs free. On the rounded lifted grid assign odds \[ v_e=\sqrt2\exp(\theta\xi_e), \] where the physical-edge signs are independent and symmetric, and repeated lifted edges have the same sign. Let $\phi_{\delta,J}^{\rm sep}$ and $\phi_{\delta,0}^{\rm sep}$ denote respectively this random-cluster law and the pure law on the same graph and with the same boundary partition. If $\mathcal A_\delta$ is the event of an actual open path between the two wired arcs, then \begin{equation} \phi_{\delta,J}^{\rm sep}(\mathcal A_\delta) -\phi_{\delta,0}^{\rm sep}(\mathcal A_\delta) \longrightarrow0 \qquad\text{in environmental probability as }\delta\downarrow0. \end{equation} The disorder threshold is independent of the fixed polygon and marks. The conclusion also holds on the dual square grid.

primaryStatements.name: Pure four-point limit
primaryStatements.label: prop:pure-four-mark
primaryStatements.text: Let $P$ be a fixed collared orthogonal polygon that is a topological disk in an oriented flat surface with a locally injective translation projection to the plane. Put four distinct marks in straight boundary portions. Approximate $P$ by its lifted square grid at mesh $\delta\downarrow0$, with critical odds $\sqrt2$ on every edge. Then the open-cap probability of $E_{\mathrm P}$ tends to $f(\chi_P)$, and the probability of an actual crossing between separately wired arcs $ab$ and $cd$ tends to $g(\chi_P)$. The conclusion also holds for compatible medial approximations differing by an incident boundary layer.

primaryStatements.name: Fixed quenched tests
primaryStatements.label: cor:fixed-tests
primaryStatements.text: For each fixed polygon $P$ in Proposition \ref{prop:pure-four-mark}, assign to every lifted edge the random odds of its projected edge. At the critical inverse temperature of Theorem \ref{thm:main}, the separately wired actual crossing probability tends in environmental probability to $g(\chi_P)$. The open-cap probability tends to $f(\chi_P)$.

definitions.label: eq:projective-diameter
definitions.text: For a strictly positive kernel $T$ on two finite state spaces, its projective diameter is \begin{equation} \Delta(T)=\sup_{u,u',v,v'} \left|\log\frac{T(u,v)T(u',v')}{T(u,v')T(u',v)}\right|. \end{equation} If both boundary rays are free, write $[u]=\{u,-u\}$ and define the kernel on cap states modulo sign by \begin{equation} \overline T([u],[v]) =\sum_{\varepsilon,\varepsilon'\in\{-1,1\}} T(\varepsilon u,\varepsilon'v). \end{equation} Thus the two absolute cap signs are summed independently.

definitions.name: Polygons on sheets
definitions.label: def:sheet-polygon
definitions.text: Let $\mathcal S$ be an oriented flat surface with a map $\pi:\mathcal S\to\R^2$ whose restriction to each sufficiently small neighborhood is an orientation-preserving isometry. A collared orthogonal polygon is a compact polygonal disk $\mathcal P\subset \mathcal S$ such that $\pi$ is defined on a neighborhood of $\mathcal P$, and each side of $\mathcal P$ is horizontal or vertical in these local coordinates. The polygon has finitely many sides; the map $\pi$ need not be injective on $\mathcal P$. Its lattice approximation is obtained by rounding its sides to the lifted square grid of mesh $\delta$ and filling the resulting polygon. Boundary-condition changes are placed in straight side interiors and rounded with the sides. Distinct lifted copies of a physical lattice edge are distinct random-cluster edges with the same environmental sign. Thus the coupling of a lifted edge $\widetilde e$ is the coupling of $\pi(\widetilde e)$.

papers.title: Thermal FK–Ising interfaces and massive SLE
papers.abstract: We prove convergence of thermal FK–Ising interfaces, for every fixed nonzero mass of either sign, on uniformly angle-bounded isoradial lattices in bounded simply connected domains. The limit is independent of the lattice and the admissible domain approximation. For positive mass it is the unique massive SLE$_{16/3}$ law with locally finite-energy drift prescribed by a massive boundary value problem; negative mass follows by duality and reversal. The theorem also allows Carathéodory approximations whose diameters diverge.

For $1\le q\le4$, complete nested plane loops converge to CLEκ.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: For every $(\Omega,a,b,m)$ as above, there is a curve law $\mu_{\Omega,a,b,m}$ such that, for every sequence with mesh tending to zero and satisfying all the preceding domain, marked Carath\'eodory, angle and nome assumptions, \[ \mathcal L(\chi_\delta\circ\gamma_\delta) \ \Longrightarrow\ \chi_*\mu_{\Omega,a,b,m} \] in the metric \eqref{mod:curve-metric}, along the full sequence. The physical prime-end curve law $\mu_{\Omega,a,b,m}$ is independent of the lattices, admissible domain approximations and nome sequence. For $m>0$, $\mu_{\Omega,a,b,m}$ is the unique law in Definition \ref{def:law}. For $m<0$, it is the reversal of the positive-mass law in $(\Omega,b,a)$ with mass $|m|$, with primal and dual boundary labels interchanged. In either case we call it thermal massive $\mathrm{SLE}_{16/3}$.

primaryStatements.label: mod:bvp-unique
primaryStatements.text: Equation \eqref{mod:bvp} has exactly one solution in this class. It satisfies $0\le h\le1$. On interior compact sets, $h$ and its first derivatives depend continuously on the marked domain in the Carath\'eodory topology, when the domains lie in a fixed bounded physical region.

primaryStatements.name: Observable convergence and rectangle crossings
primaryStatements.label: prop:inputs
primaryStatements.text: Consider the weights of Section \ref{mod:section}, with \(r_\delta/\delta\to m/2\), on isoradial meshes whose rhombus half-angles belong to \([\eta,\pi/2-\eta]\). \begin{enumerate} \item For marked Carath\'eodory convergence to a bounded simply connected two-point domain, the reconstructed two-point FK fermion converges locally uniformly, up to its common sign, to a smooth massive-holomorphic function \(f\): \[ \bar\partial f+\ii m\overline f=0. \] Its square integral \(h\), normalized by its two boundary values, is the unique bounded solution \[ \lap h=-4m|\grad h|,\qquad h=1\ \hbox{on the wired bank},\qquad h=0\ \hbox{on the dual-wired bank}. \] The boundary values are prime-end limits away from the two marked ends, and \(0\le h\le1\). The convergence includes uniform interior bounds on protected compact subsets. \item For every fixed rectangle aspect ratio and every finite physical scale bound, the crossing probabilities of both colors are bounded away from zero, uniformly over all boundary conditions and all nondegenerate lattice rectangles below that scale whose side lengths exceed a fixed multiple of the mesh. The scale constants are independent of the mesh. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.name: Conditional unforced crossings
primaryStatements.label: geo:g2
primaryStatements.text: The regularly drawn medial interfaces in domains of diameter at most \(L\) satisfy condition G2 of \cite{KS}, uniformly over the allowed meshes, domains, and thermal parameters.

primaryStatements.name: Joint compactness
primaryStatements.label: geo:compactness
primaryStatements.text: Under the common diameter bound, the laws of the interfaces transferred by their normalized maps to the closed disc are tight in the oriented curve metric. Every subsequential limit is a chordal Loewner trace with a continuous driving function and strict capacity growth. It reaches the target only at the end and is continuously completed in disc coordinates. Along a further coupling, the curves and their half-plane drivers converge jointly, with uniform convergence of the drivers and capacity-parametrized curves on every finite capacity interval.

primaryStatements.name: Conditional geometric estimates in the limit
primaryStatements.label: geo:restart
primaryStatements.text: Every limit of Proposition \ref{geo:compactness} inherits the conditional crossing estimates needed below in its natural driving filtration. They hold after a live stopping time and after localization on a finite interval on which the relevant Loewner coordinates remain nondegenerate. In the following two estimates, reset capacity time to zero at the chosen live stopping time. \begin{enumerate} \item In the current half-plane chart, put the tip at \(0\), rescale a given live point to modulus \(1\), and write \(x\) for its real part. If its imaginary part is small, so \(x\) is near \(1\) or \(-1\), then \[ \Prob\{\text{the future trace visits }B(x,d)\mid\text{past}\} \le Kd^\alpha \] for all sufficiently small \(d\). \item For a live physical point \(w\), \[ \Prob\left\{ \inf_{s\text{ before swallowing}} \crad_{O_s}(w) <\varepsilon\,\crad_{O_0}(w) \,\middle|\,\text{past at the restart}\right\} \le K\varepsilon^\alpha . \] \end{enumerate} The assertions apply in particular at inverse elapsed-clock times and at first angular-level crossings used in Section \ref{eng:section}. No semimartingale property of the driver is assumed here.

primaryStatements.name: Continuum fermion martingales
primaryStatements.label: geo:martingale
primaryStatements.text: Every subsequential curve law of Proposition \ref{geo:compactness} has a joint realization with a complex field \(M_t(w)\), \(w\in O_t\), such that \[ M_t(w)^2=D h_t(w),\qquad \bar\partial M_t+\ii m\overline{M_t}=0. \] The field is continuous locally in space and time before swallowing, and is smooth in its spatial variable. On every protected compact subset of the live domain, after localization, \(M_t(w)\) is a continuous martingale in the joint natural filtration of the curve and field. In particular it is a continuous local martingale at each fixed point before its swallowing time.

primaryStatements.name: Moving-mark energy
primaryStatements.label: eng:energy
primaryStatements.text: For \begin{equation} J_t=\int_{\Hh}\frac{\mu_t(v)}{|v|^2}\,\dd A(v), \end{equation} there is a constant $K<\infty$ such that \begin{equation} \E\int_0^\infty J_t^2\,\dd t \le K m^2\area(\Omega)<\infty. \end{equation} Consequently $J_t$ is finite for almost every capacity time, almost surely.

definitions.label: def:law
definitions.text: A positive-mass interface law in $(\Omega,a,b)$ is a law of an oriented continuous curve in the prime-end compactification, from $a$ to $b$, with the following properties. In the chart $\phi$ it is the Loewner trace for the entire evolution \eqref{mod:loewner}, parametrized by half-plane capacity $2t$, $0\le t<\infty$, and completed continuously at $b$ in disc coordinates. Its driving function is a weak solution of \begin{equation} \dd W_t=\sqrt{\frac{16}{3}}\,\dd B_t +\frac{2\pi}{3}C_t\,\dd t, \qquad W_0=0, \end{equation} where $B$ is Brownian motion in a filtration to which the driver is adapted. The actual integral in Equation \eqref{mod:C} is finite almost everywhere and, for every finite $T$, \begin{equation} \int_0^T C_t^2\,\dd t<\infty\qquad\hbox{almost surely}. \end{equation} The trace requirement includes the full parametrized evolution; one cannot append curve pieces inside already swallowed hulls.

papers.title: Natural Occupation Measures for Critical Square-Lattice FK Interfaces
papers.abstract: We prove that the rescaled counting measure of a critical square-lattice Fortuin–Kasteleyn Dobrushin interface in the unit square converges to the Minkowski-content measure of its Schramm–Loewner limit, for every fixed cluster weight $1\le q\lt 4$. A single deterministic constant times the predicted power of the mesh gives the normalization. Convergence is joint with the ordered curve and includes the total mass, giving the scaling limit of the interface's total number of steps.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: For each fixed $q\in[1,4)$ there is a deterministic constant $c(q)\in(0,\infty)$ such that, along all positive integers $n$, \[ \bigl([\eta_n],\nu_{n,c(q)}\bigr) \ \Longrightarrow\ \bigl([\eta],\mu_\eta\bigr). \] The first coordinate has the ordered curve topology \eqref{eq:curve-metric}, and the second has the weak topology of finite measures on $\overline D$. The two limiting coordinates belong to the same SLE sample. In particular, \[ c(q)n^{-d}N_n\ \Longrightarrow\ \mu_\eta(\overline D) \] jointly with the curve and all continuous spatial tests of its measure.

primaryStatements.name: Radial estimates
primaryStatements.label: prop:radial
primaryStatements.text: Fix $1\le q<4$, fixed radius-comparison constants, and a compact interval $V\subset(0,\infty)$. The following bounds are uniform over the above circuit and plane states and over $v\in V$. For states $\gamma,\gamma'$ of sizes $R,R'\ge r_0$, \begin{equation} \left|\log\frac{F(\gamma;v)}{F(\gamma';v)}\right| \le C\bigl(1+|\log(R/R')|\bigr). \end{equation} There is $\delta>0$ such that every $F(\gamma;ve^w)$ is nonzero for $|w|<\delta$. Its logarithm, continued from its real value at $w=0$, has absolute value at most $C\log(2+R)$. Moreover \begin{equation} \left|\log\frac{F(\gamma;ve^w)}{F(\gamma;v)} -\log\frac{F(\gamma';ve^w)}{F(\gamma';v)}\right| \le C|w|\bigl(1+|\log(R/R')|\bigr). \end{equation} For two states of comparable size $R$, their positively tilted laws can be coupled so that their configurations agree inside a common surrounding primal-open circuit containing $B(u,s)$, except with probability $C(s/R)^c$, for $r_0\le s\le R/C$. Conditional on the common circuit, the common continuation has its circuit law tilted by $v$. Finally, let $F_{\ge h}(\gamma;v)$ count only the eligible loops with $R_u(\ell)\ge h$. For comparable starts of size $R$, \begin{equation} \frac{F_{\ge\epsilon R}(\gamma;v)/ F_{\ge\epsilon R}(\gamma';v)} {F(\gamma;v)/F(\gamma';v)}=1+o(1) \end{equation} uniformly as $\epsilon\downarrow0$ and $\epsilon R\to\infty$. The same real comparison and regeneration bounds hold with any such lower cutoff on the counted radii.

primaryStatements.name: Normalized multipoint correlations
primaryStatements.label: prop:normalization
primaryStatements.text: Suppose $p$ is fixed, $\max_j|u_j|\le Cn$, and $a=\min_{i\ne j}|u_i-u_j|\ge r_0$. Around every parameter whose singleton weights $v_{\{j\}}$ are strictly positive real numbers, the normalized correlation \begin{equation} \mathcal C_n(\mathbf v;\mathbf u) =\frac{C(\mathbf v;\mathbf u)} {\prod_{j=1}^p F_n(v_{\{j\}})} \end{equation} is holomorphic and bounded in a fixed complex neighborhood of the singleton weights, uniformly when the other weights range over a bounded set, with bound $C(n/a)^C$. For $a\ge cn$, if $u_j/n$ converge to distinct points and the point parities are fixed, \eqref{eq:normalized-correlations} has a limit locally uniformly in these complex parameter neighborhoods. When all nontrivial weights lie in a fixed compact subset of $(0,\infty)$ and $a\ge cn$, the normalized correlations are bounded above and below by positive constants. Their tilted laws are local at each point in the following quantitative sense. Consider two possibly different collections with bounded point counts, all weights in the stated positive compact set, and sizes comparable to the same $n$, satisfying the same fixed geometric bounds. Align one chosen point in each by a lattice symmetry, transporting its color, and suppose its singleton weight is the same in both. The two laws admit a coupling with identical configuration inside a common surrounding circuit containing $B(u,s)$, with error $C(s/n)^c$. For minimum separation $a$ the analogous error is at most $C(n/a)^C(s/a)^c$, whenever $r_0\le s\le a/C$.

primaryStatements.name: Macroscopic tests with local insertions
primaryStatements.label: cor:macroscopic-test
primaryStatements.text: Let $u_j/n$ converge to distinct points, with their point parities fixed, and let $P_j$ be disjoint round patches centered at $u_j$, of radii fixed positive multiples of $n$, with disjoint larger collars. Fix $v_j>0$ and define \[ U_n=\prod_jv_j^{\#\{\ell:u_j\text{ inside }\ell,\ \ell\subset P_j\}}. \] Suppose $T_n$ is a uniformly bounded discretization, $\sup_n\|T_n\|_\infty<\infty$, of a fixed bounded functional $T$ of the rescaled plane loop collection, determined in a fixed bounded region by loops of diameter at least a fixed $\delta>0$. Suppose that this functional is almost surely continuous for the plane loop limit, with its marked-point, patch-boundary and contact tests taken at continuity radii. Here discretization means that $T_n(\omega_n)\to T(\omega)$ whenever the relevant rescaled loop collections $\omega_n$ converge to a continuity configuration $\omega$. Then the following sequence converges as $n\to\infty$: \begin{equation} \frac{\E[U_nT_n]}{\prod_jF_n(v_j)}. \end{equation} The conclusion also applies to tests obtained by first excluding arbitrarily large excursions, provided the discarded part tends to zero in probability under the normalized $U_n$ law uniformly in $n$. Boundedness of $T_n$ may be replaced by $|T_n|\le K^{X_n}$, where $X_n$ is the sum of a fixed finite family of macroscopic passage counts satisfying \begin{equation} \sup_n\frac{\E[U_ne^{tX_n}]}{\E U_n}<\infty \qquad\text{for every fixed }t<\infty, \end{equation} also after the inner-radius truncations of the local weights. The bounded truncations of the test must satisfy the preceding continuity requirement.

primaryStatements.name: The current spectrum
primaryStatements.label: prop:spectral
primaryStatements.text:
Almost every spectral function on $\mathcal D$ is either $1$ or a finite Blaschke product with  egin{equation} f(0)=f(\infty)=1, \qquad f(\overline w)=\overline{f(w)}. \end{equation} There is a spectral vector $\mathsf h$, not necessarily of finite norm, such that  egin{equation} J(w)\Omega=(1-f(w))\mathsf h. \end{equation} The measure $\mu$ given by the squared fiber norm of $\mathsf h$ is invariant under dilation. On the cross-section of products whose smallest zero has modulus one, it decomposes as  egin{equation} \mu=\dd s\,
u(\dd F),\qquad f(w)=F(e^s w), \qquad 
u(1)<\infty. \end{equation} If $\mathcal W(F)$ is the difference between the largest and smallest logarithmic zero moduli, and $2n_F$ is the degree, then, for some $\eta_0>0$,  egin{equation} 
u\{\mathcal W>t\}\le C e^{-2\eta_0t},\qquad \int n_F\,
u(\dd F)<\infty. \end{equation} The physical plane height has logarithmic variance. More precisely, after an axial symmetry, write a nonzero displacement as $(k,j)$ with $k\ge1$ and $|j|\le k$. Then  egin{equation}  egin{split} \E igl(h(k,j)-h(0,0) igr)^2 &=2\Re\int igl(1-f(1)^k f(\pm i)^{|j|} igr)\,\mu(\dd f)\ &=4
u(1)\log k+O(1), \end{split} \end{equation} where the sign agrees with the direction of the second coordinate. The error is uniform over these displacements.

primaryStatements.name: A summable Laplacian error
primaryStatements.label: prop:laplacian
primaryStatements.text: For the neutral small-charge experiments of Equation \eqref{eq:electric-characteristic}, there are $c_1>0$ and $C<\infty$ such that \begin{equation} |\Delta_2H(z)|\le C n^{Cb} \left(1+\min_j|z-u_j|\right)^{-2-c_1} \qquad(z\in\Z^2). \end{equation} The constants are uniform over the stated geometry and charges.

primaryStatements.name: Coulomb formula
primaryStatements.label: prop:coulomb
primaryStatements.text: Fix a number $p$ of marked points. There are $b,c,\xi>0$ and a real-analytic function $f$ on a neighborhood of $[-b,b]$, with $f(0)=0$, such that, for neutral real charges $\max_j|t_j|\le b$ and distinct points on a tile axis satisfying \[ \max_j|u_j|\le Mn,\qquad \min_{i\ne j}|u_i-u_j|\ge n^{1-\xi}, \] one has \begin{equation} \log C(\mathbf t;\mathbf u) =\sum_{j=1}^p f(t_j) +2A\sum_{i<j}t_it_j\log|u_i-u_j|+O(n^{-c}), \qquad f(0)=0. \end{equation} Here the same local function $f$ is used for every number of points, on their common small-charge neighborhood; it is independent of the geometry and of the point parities. The constants can depend on $p,M$ and $q$. For either choice of sign, the corresponding multiplicative statement has analytic continuation along compact paths from zero in \[ \mathcal D_p^\pm =\{\mathbf t\in\R^p:\ \sum_jt_j=0, \ \pm t_j\in I_\lambda\text{ for every }j\}. \] More precisely, on a sufficiently thin complex neighborhood of each such compact path within the neutral hyperplane $\sum_jt_j=0$, there is a holomorphic function $M_p$ such that \begin{equation} \frac{C(\mathbf t;\mathbf u)} {\displaystyle\prod_{i<j}|u_i-u_j|^{2At_it_j}} =M_p(\mathbf t)+O(n^{-c}). \end{equation} The positive constants $c$ and $\xi$ may decrease with the path. Near zero, $M_p(\mathbf t)=\exp(\sum_jf(t_j))$. The error in \eqref{eq:coulomb-continued} is additive; a relative error is asserted only where $M_p$ is nonzero.

primaryStatements.name: Individual nesting amplitudes
primaryStatements.label: prop:pure-nest
primaryStatements.text: There is $\varepsilon_0>0$ and a nonvanishing holomorphic function $a(t)$ near $[-\varepsilon_0,\varepsilon_0]$, positive for real $t$, such that \[ F_n(v(t))=a(t)n^{\beta(t)}(1+o(1)) \] locally uniformly on a complex neighborhood of that interval. The limit uses the fixed cutoff and rounding in the definition of $F_n$. No rate is asserted for this individual amplitude.

The results hold under uniform marked Jordan boundary approximation and retain loop multiplicities and traversals. At q = 1 we obtain Cardy's formula for square-lattice bond percolation with free boundary edges.

primaryStatements.name: Interfaces and all nested loops
primaryStatements.label: intro:main
primaryStatements.text: For every fixed real $1\le q\le4$, the following assertions hold. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item For every bounded Jordan domain $D$ with distinct boundary marks $a,b$, and every approximation satisfying \eqref{intro:marked-jordan}, the Dobrushin strand $\eta_n$ converges in law, in \eqref{intro:curve-metric}, to chordal $\SLE_{\kappa(q)}$ from $a$ to $b$ in $D$. \item Under the specified free infinite-volume law, $\Gamma_\delta$ converges in law as $\delta\downarrow0$ to the nested whole-plane $\CLE_{\kappa(q)}$, in the spherical collection topology just defined. The limit is M\"obius invariant. \end{enumerate} Both conclusions hold along every mesh sequence. No uniformity in $q$ is asserted.

primaryStatements.name: The regular-domain field
primaryStatements.label: q4field:regular-domain
primaryStatements.text: Let $V$ be a fixed polygon and let its actual wall approximations be as above. Then \begin{equation} h_\delta\ \Longrightarrow\ u+\sigma\Phi_V \qquad\text{as distributions in }V, \end{equation} where $u=0$ for a homogeneous wall and $u$ is the harmonic extension of the boundary values $0,1$ for a mixed wall. All joint integrated moments converge. At every tuple of distinct fixed interior positions, the moment kernels converge to those of the same field.

primaryStatements.name: Cardy's formula for square-lattice bond percolation
primaryStatements.label: intro:cardy
primaryStatements.text: Let $\psi:D\to\H$ send $a,c,d$ to $0,1,\infty$, and put $x=\psi(b)\in(0,1)$. Under the boundary and approximation conventions above, \begin{equation} \lim_{n\to\infty}\mathbb P(C_n) =\frac{\displaystyle\int_0^x[t(1-t)]^{-2/3}\,\dd t} {\displaystyle\int_0^1[t(1-t)]^{-2/3}\,\dd t}. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Three logarithmic comparisons
primaryStatements.label: exp:comparisons
primaryStatements.text: With the definitions above, \begin{align} 2P+2D_*+4(C_0+C_1)&\le o(\log n),\\ C_0+C_1+L_0+L_1&\le o(\log n),\\ P+\sum_j\log\frac{F_-(a_j)}{F_+(a_j)} &\le o(\log n), \end{align} where the finite list of fixed charges in the last inequality satisfies \eqref{exp:charge-range} and $\sum_j a_j=1$.

primaryStatements.name: Balanced corner parities
primaryStatements.label: exp:polygon-budget
primaryStatements.text: Let a fixed simple rectilinear polygon have $m$ concave and $m+4$ convex true corners, with wire changes in side interiors. It has tile approximants differing by $O(1)$ mesh units such that at least $\lfloor m/2\rfloor$ corners of each relative wire type occur in each of the convex and concave sets, also after global wire reversal. For these approximants, \begin{equation} 3P+D_*+\sum_{v\,\mathrm{convex}}C_{i(v)} +\sum_{v\,\mathrm{concave}}L_{i(v)} \le\frac12P-\frac32D_*+o(\log n). \end{equation} Each fixed family of negative endpoint charges with magnitudes summing to one has total wrong-to-correct local logarithmic cost at most $-P+o(\log n)$.

primaryStatements.name: Angular transfer estimate
primaryStatements.label: bulk:angular-estimate
primaryStatements.text: Fix a compact interval $I\subset(-v,v)$. Let $B_{\rm in}$ be a product of $P_\zeta$ rows and $B_{\rm out}$ a product of $P_\xi$ rows, at real angles in $[-v,v]$. Suppose each product contains at least $n\ge1$ angles in $I$. Uniformly for $x,y\in[-v,v]$, \begin{align} \|B_{\rm out}N(x)B_{\rm in}\|&\le Cn^{-1+\rho}, \\ \|B_{\rm out}\{N(x)-e^{i\tau(x-y)}N(y)\}B_{\rm in}\| &\le Cn^{-1-\rho}. \end{align} The constant depends on $q$ and $I$. Boundedly many additional pairs of before-twist rows may be inserted immediately to the right of $N$, and additional pairs of after-twist rows immediately to its left. The two terms in \eqref{bulk:high-estimate} may use different such insertions; on each side their counts must be even. The constant may depend on a bound for these counts. Multiplication of $D$ by a common scalar multiplies the bounds by its absolute value. The same estimates hold in the physical square array sliced in a diagonal time direction: its time angles are $\pm\gamma_0$, where $\gamma_0=\pi/4$, and its space angles alternate between $\pi-\gamma_0$ and $\gamma_0$. The exterior states may contain any finite number of physical row and spin insertions outside the sandwich. A scalar contraction is bounded by the displayed rate times the two reflection norms, with the squares centered on a cut included in its reflection kernel.

primaryStatements.name: Extraction in a clear slab
primaryStatements.label: cur:slab-estimate
primaryStatements.text: Suppose a diagonal-time slab of macroscopic thickness about a low or high stencil contains no other non-diagonal tensors or endpoints. Diagonal chains may cross the slab. The stencil has an intact neighborhood disjoint from all other chains except its own prefix, and the slab has spare margins for routing and cuts. Bounded lattice errors are permitted inside these margins. Then the stencil contraction can be written as the corresponding low or high expression in Theorem \ref{bulk:angular-estimate}, between exterior states independent of the choice of stencil term. Only boundedly many compensating pairs of rows and a common bounded scalar are introduced. In particular, if the two clear parts of the slab contain at least $n$ physical steps, its scalar contraction is bounded by $Cn^{-1+\rho}$ for a low stencil, and by $Cn^{-1-\rho}$ for a high stencil, times the two exterior reflection norms. Reflected stencils satisfy the same statement.

primaryStatements.name: Identification of a holomorphic subsequential limit
primaryStatements.label: four:conditional-map
primaryStatements.text: Suppose an interior subsequential limit $h$ of $h_n$ is holomorphic in the ordinary complex coordinate, and pass simultaneously to a limit $r$ of $P_{\mathfrak A}$. Then $0<r<1$. Put \begin{equation} U_0=r+d(1-r),\qquad V_0=dr+1-r,\qquad T_0=r+y(1-r). \end{equation} The function $h$ maps $\Omega$ conformally onto the interior of the simple polygon with successive vertices $0,U_0,T_0,yV_0$, taking $p,b,c,d_0$ to those vertices. If a conformal half-plane coordinate takes the marks to $0,\chi,1,\infty$, respectively, then \begin{equation} r=\frac{\displaystyle\int_1^\infty u^{\rho-1}|u-\chi|^{\rho-1}|u-1|^{1-3\rho}\,du} {\displaystyle\int_\chi^\infty u^{\rho-1}|u-\chi|^{\rho-1}|u-1|^{1-3\rho}\,du}. \end{equation} Under deterministic separate $\mathfrak A$ caps the corresponding crossing probability is $r/(r+d(1-r))$.

papers.title: From critical crossings to quenched near-critical universality in Voronoi percolation
papers.abstract: Taking Cardy's crossing formula for critical Poisson–Voronoi percolation as an input, we prove a universal joint limit for the near-critical crossing thresholds of rational polygonal quadrilaterals under the monotone coupling. Conditional on the Poisson tessellation, the threshold law converges in probability over tessellations to the same law as on the triangular lattice. Each model is normalized by its own expected number of color-pivotal sites for a unit-square crossing.
papers.familySummary: Proves Cardy's formula for annealed critical Poisson–Voronoi crossing probabilities in every bounded Jordan quadrilateral. With each model normalized by its own expected unit-square pivotal count, the conditional joint near-critical crossing-threshold laws for rational polygonal quads converge in environment probability to the triangular-lattice reference law. This establishes quenched near-critical universality for crossing thresholds.

primaryStatements.name: Quenched scalar Cardy convergence
primaryStatements.label: prop:quenched-cardy
primaryStatements.text: For every fixed polygon quad $Q$, \[ \PP^{\eta_e}(C_Q)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Cardy}(Q) \quad\text{in probability over the Poisson geometry}. \] The assertion holds simultaneously for every member of any fixed finite collection of polygon quads.

primaryStatements.name: Chordal exploration convergence
primaryStatements.label: prop:chordal
primaryStatements.text: Let graph disks on a deterministic sequence as above approximate a bounded Jordan domain $D$, with switches converging to distinct boundary points $a,b$. Give their interiors independent fair colors and their two boundary arcs the prescribed opposite colors. The exploration from $a$ to $b$ converges in law, in the curve metric, to chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_6$ in $D$ from $a$ to $b$. This conclusion holds for every such converging sequence of disks and marks.

primaryStatements.name: Oriented loop convergence
primaryStatements.label: prop:loops
primaryStatements.text: In a Jordan disk with monochromatic boundary, along every deterministic sequence of tilings under consideration, the critical interface loops converge to the Camia--Newman $\mathrm{SLE}_6$ loop construction. For each positive cutoff chosen outside the atoms of limiting loop diameters, the loops above that cutoff can be matched in the curve metric, including their orientation, multiplicity, and order of excursions. There are no surplus macroscopic loops. The convergence holds jointly for any finite number of independent color replicas on the same fixed geometry.

primaryStatements.name: Joint critical tests with prescribed squares
primaryStatements.label: prop:critical-tests
primaryStatements.text: Fix finitely many polygon quads and finitely many closed squares of positive side length, with the squares mutually separated and separated from every quad boundary. For any finite collection of test specifications, the joint law of their exact closed-cell crossing indicators has a common limit along every deterministic good sequence of either model. The limit is continuous in the centers and positive side lengths of the squares throughout the open range where the stated separations hold, and under sufficiently small marked polygonal deformations of the quads. The conclusion remains valid when the centers and side lengths converge to such an admissible fixed configuration as the mesh tends to zero. For Poisson--Voronoi percolation the conditional law given $\eta_e$ converges in probability, in total variation on this finite Boolean space, to the same deterministic limiting law. With any fixed number of conditionally independent fair-color replicas on one Poisson geometry, the limiting law is that of independent copies of the same critical configuration, with all the prescribed tests performed in their specified replicas. In particular, two replicas sharing their geometry have the same joint critical limit as two independent triangular replicas.

primaryStatements.name: Uniform bound for the site expansion
primaryStatements.label: prop:expansion-bound
primaryStatements.text: Fix a box $B$, finitely many polygonal crossing tests, and $R\leq2$ replica labels. Let $g\in(1,2)$ be an exponent in the lower four-arm bound of Lemma \ref{lem:arm-inputs}. There is a constant $C$, depending only on this data, such that, for every $k\geq1$, every choice of nonempty $I_i$, and centered weights $w_{i,r}$, \begin{equation} \frac{(m_eq_e)^k}{k!} \int_{B^k_{\ne}} |K_e(F;\mathbf x,\mathbf I,\mathbf w)| \,d\sigma_e^{\otimes k}(\mathbf x) \leq C^k k^{-(1-g/2)k} \prod_{i,r\in I_i}\|w_{i,r}\|_{\TV}, \end{equation} uniformly for all sufficiently small meshes and all $|F|\leq1$ of the specified crossing indicators. Consequently the absolute sum in \eqref{eq:site-expansion} is bounded by $\sum_{k\geq1}C_T^k k^{-(1-g/2)k}<\infty$ when all times have absolute value at most $T$. For two replicas, the total absolute contribution of terms with $|I_i|=2$ for at least one $i$ is $O_T(q_e)$.

primaryStatements.name: Signed relative replacement
primaryStatements.label: prop:replacement
primaryStatements.text: Under the preceding assumptions, fix the types $t_2,\ldots,t_k$ and put \[ K_s=K_e^{(s,t_2,\ldots,t_k)}(F;\boldsymbol x,\boldsymbol w),\qquad K_d=K_e^{(d,t_2,\ldots,t_k)}(F;\boldsymbol x,\boldsymbol w),\qquad P_e=\prod_{i=2}^k \gamma_e(t_i). \] The empty product is $1$. In either model, \begin{equation} \lim_{h\downarrow0}\limsup_{e\downarrow0} \sup_{\boldsymbol x} \frac{|K_sD_e(h)-K_dS_e|}{P_e a_e a_{e,h}}=0. \end{equation} The supremum is over the fixed compact separated range, restricted to lattice sites in the triangular model; in Poisson insertion integrals, null general-position exceptions are omitted. The assertion is uniform for bounded total variations of the centered weights.

primaryStatements.name: Common finite-time crossing limits
primaryStatements.label: prop:nearcritical-tests
primaryStatements.text: Choose finitely many quads in $\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{rat}}$ and finitely many real parameters. Their jointly coupled crossing indicators, with the prescribed scales $r_e$, have a limiting law common to the two models. The assertion holds for one color replica and for two independent color replicas conditional on the same geometry. Every such limiting probability is continuous in the real parameter vector, and the convergence remains valid for convergent parameter vectors.

definitions.name: Scalar critical Cardy formula
definitions.label: hyp:cardy
definitions.text: For every fixed bounded Jordan quad $Q=(D;a,b,c,d)$, the annealed probability of $C_Q$ in fair-colored full-plane Poisson--Voronoi percolation converges, as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, to \begin{equation} F(x)=\frac{\displaystyle\int_0^x [u(1-u)]^{-2/3}\,du} {\displaystyle\int_0^1 [u(1-u)]^{-2/3}\,du}, \end{equation} where a conformal map from $D$ to the upper half-plane sends $(a,b,c,d)$ to $(0,x,1,\infty)$.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Under Assumption \ref{ass:cardy}, there exists a constant $c_V\in(0,\infty)$ such that \[ \lim_{\eps\downarrow0}\eps^{3/4}\E N_\eps=c_V. \] Consequently, the inverse expected pivotal count is asymptotic to $c_V^{-1}\eps^{3/4}$.

primaryStatements.name: Critical arm and localization inputs
primaryStatements.label: in:arms
primaryStatements.text: There are $g\in(1,2)$, $\alpha,\beta>0$, and constants $C,c>0$ such that, for $b_*\le r<s<t$, \begin{align} c(r/s)^g&\le A(r,s)\le C(r/s)^{1+\alpha},\\ C^{-1}A(r,s)A(s,t)&\le A(r,t)\le C A(r,s)A(s,t). \end{align} The one-arm probability is at most $C(r/s)^\beta$. The probability of three alternating arms in a straight half-plane is at most $C(r/s)^2$. For a collar of diameter comparable to $s$, an event determined by the Poisson points in a slightly enlarged collar makes the graph and all vertex stars in the smaller collar local to those points, with mesh smaller than any prescribed fixed fraction of $s$. Its failure probability is at most $C\exp(-cs^2)$. The widths and constants can depend on that fraction. Such events may be chosen rotation equivariant about the center. Events with disjoint enlarged supports use independent Poisson variables.

primaryStatements.name: Scaling-limit inputs
primaryStatements.label: in:limits
primaryStatements.text: Under Assumption \ref{ass:cardy}, the following consequences hold. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item From every sequence of Poisson meshes tending to zero one can extract, after coupling, a further subsequence along which the graphs almost surely form a deterministic good sequence in the sense of \cite[Lemma 2.5]{V}. Along such a sequence, critical crossings of Jordan quadrilaterals converge, also for graph domains whose boundaries and marked points converge in curve order. Finite joint crossing tests and tests with finitely many separated prescribed squares have the common triangular-percolation limit. \item Chordal color explorations in converging Jordan graph domains converge to chordal $\mathrm{SLE}_6$. At a pre-query stop on a crosscut, the remaining target face, its boundary banks, and its conformal maps converge in the sense of the stopped-domain results of \cite{V}. A bank is an individual boundary arc in prime-end order; distinct banks may have touching physical images. Each relevant bank is individually simple. \item For some $c_0>0$, in the mesh-first limit the probability of four bulk arms with any specified color order is at most $C(r/s)^{1+c_0}$, and that of six bulk arms with any specified color order is at most $C(r/s)^{2+c_0}$. Three free arms at a regular boundary, measured in a conformal chart, have an upper bound with exponent strictly larger than one. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.name: Calibration
primaryStatements.label: in:calibration
primaryStatements.text: There are constants $c,B\in(0,\infty)$ such that \begin{equation} m_\eps q_\eps S_\eps\longrightarrow c, \qquad q_\eps\E N_\eps\longrightarrow B. \end{equation} Moreover, \begin{equation} f(R)\asymp A(b_*,R). \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: The annular transmission limit
primaryStatements.label: an:limit
primaryStatements.text: For every sequence with admissible boundary convergence, the probability of $\mathcal T$ has a limit depending only on the round data $(p,x,y)$ and the choice of inner colors. Denote these limits by \[ T^+(p,x,y),\qquad T^-(p,x,y). \] They are continuous for $p>0$ and distinct switches. The same convergence holds for each capped connection probability. In particular, it applies to random remaining domains whenever, conditional on their geometry and explored boundary, their interior colors are fresh and their marked domains have admissible convergence almost surely in a subsequential coupling. In that case the difference between the conditional transmission probability and $T^\pm$ evaluated at the actual annular conformal data tends to zero in mean absolute value.

primaryStatements.name: Modulus equation
primaryStatements.label: sp:annular-pde
primaryStatements.text: The functions $T^\pm$ are smooth on $(0,\infty)\times\mathcal X$ and satisfy \begin{equation} \partial_pT=(L+B_p\cdot\nabla)T, \qquad L=\frac18\sum_{w=x,y} \left(3\sum_{i=1}^4\partial_{w_iw_i} +\sum_{i=1}^4\sum_{j\ne i} \cot\frac{w_i-w_j}{2}\,\partial_{w_i}\right). \end{equation} For every $p_0>0$ and every fixed finite derivative order $k$, the vector field $B_p$ extends smoothly across angle collisions and \[ \|B_p\|_{C^k}\le C_{k,p_0}e^{-p}\qquad(p\ge p_0). \] It is equivariant under permutations within either tuple, common rotations, and cyclic relabelings. In particular, its normal component at every collision face is zero.

primaryStatements.name: Uniform transmission asymptotics
primaryStatements.label: sp:transmission-asymptotics
primaryStatements.text: There are constants $K\ge0$, $\sigma>0$, and $C<\infty$ such that, uniformly over the open angle chamber and all sufficiently large $p$, \begin{align} \|W_-(p)\|_\infty&\le Ce^{-3p/4}, &\|\Pi W_-(p)\|_\infty&\le C(1+p)e^{-p}, \\ T^\pm(p,x,y)&=e^{-\lambda p} \bigl(Kh(x,y)+O(e^{-\sigma p})\bigr). \end{align} Moreover, \begin{equation} \operatorname{Lip}(W_-(p))\le Ce^{-3p/4},\qquad \|W_-(p+\ell)-W_-(p)\|_\infty \le Ce^{-3p/4}\sqrt\ell\quad(0\le\ell\le1). \end{equation} The function $h$ is uniformly $1/3$-H\"older on the closed chamber.

primaryStatements.name: Separated-end transmission
primaryStatements.label: sh:separated-ends
primaryStatements.text: There are constants $\sigma_1,\sigma_2>0$ and $C<\infty$, depending only on the fixed constants in \eqref{sh:shape-hypotheses}, such that the transmission probabilities of every such marked annulus satisfy \begin{equation} \left|T^\pm- K\,l_i^\lambda J(y^0)^{1/3}\, l_o^{-\lambda}J(x^0)^{1/3}\right| \le C(a/b)^{\lambda+\sigma_1}. \end{equation} Here $K$ is the common constant in Proposition \ref{sp:transmission-asymptotics}. If one rotates the inner end, with its marks and prescribed colors, through angle $\phi$ about $0$ while keeping the outer end fixed, then \begin{equation} \left|\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi} \bigl(T^+_\phi-T^-_\phi\bigr)\,d\phi\right| \le C(a/b)^{2+\sigma_2}. \end{equation} The same conclusion holds if the outer end is rotated instead. Both estimates remain uniform for Jordan approximants to the prime-end boundaries of Section \ref{sec:annuli}, provided they satisfy \eqref{sh:shape-hypotheses} with the same fixed constants.

definitions.name: Scalar Cardy limit
definitions.label: ass:cardy
definitions.text: For every bounded Jordan quadrilateral $Q$ with four distinct marked boundary points, the critical crossing probability converges, as $\eps\downarrow0$, to Cardy's conformally invariant value.

definitions.label: an:admissible
definitions.text: A sequence of marked graph annuli $D_n$ has admissible boundary convergence if it lies in a fixed bounded set and satisfies the following conditions. \begin{enumerate} \item Each boundary is a simple site cycle. With rotations normalized, its uniformization $\phi_n:\mathbb A_{p_n}\longrightarrow D_n$ extends continuously to the closed annulus, where $p_n\to p\in(0,\infty)$. After linear identification in logarithmic radial coordinates, these maps converge uniformly on the closed annulus to $\phi$. The map $\phi$ is conformal and one-to-one in $\mathbb A_p$, and its boundary traversal specifies the prime-end accesses of $D=\phi(\mathbb A_p)$. \item Each limiting boundary traversal is a concatenation of finitely many simple arcs, each understood with its own access. Different arcs may meet in physical projection. The two boundary components remain distinct as prime-end boundary components. \item The four switches on each component converge in these coordinates to distinct switches. Between them the prescribed run colors alternate. The sites strictly between the two cycles have fresh independent fair colors. \end{enumerate} In graph constructions a boundary is taken without chords facing the domain when that is required for a local boundary chart. Such cuts are obtained by the graph approximation and shortcut construction of \cite[Section 2]{V}; at an exploration frontier, edges between already revealed vertices are included before the frontier is taken.

primaryStatements.name: Annealed Voronoi crossing law
primaryStatements.label: thm:cardy
primaryStatements.text: For every bounded Jordan domain $D$ and every four distinct counterclockwise boundary marks $a,b,c,d$, one has \begin{equation} \lim_{\eps\downarrow0}\PP\bigl(\mathcal C_\eps(D;a,b,c,d)\bigr) =F(x) :=\frac{\displaystyle\int_0^x[u(1-u)]^{-2/3}\,\dd u} {\displaystyle\int_0^1[u(1-u)]^{-2/3}\,\dd u} =\frac{\Gamma(2/3)x^{1/3}} {\Gamma(1/3)\Gamma(4/3)} {}_2F_1\!\left(\frac13,\frac23;\frac43;x\right). \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Quenched Cardy limit for fixed rectangles
primaryStatements.label: cor:quenched-rectangles
primaryStatements.text: Let $D$ be a fixed bounded nondegenerate open rectangle and let $a,b,c,d$ be its corners in counterclockwise order, with $ab$ and $cd$ the chosen opposite sides. Write $x_D$ for its conformal parameter above and set \[ Q_\eps(\eta)=\Peta\bigl(\mathcal C_\eps(D;a,b,c,d)\bigr), \qquad \eta=X_\eps. \] If $\PP_{\mathrm{geom},\eps}$ and $\EE_{\mathrm{geom},\eps}$ denote probability and expectation for the Poisson geometry at mesh $\eps$, then \[ \lim_{\eps\downarrow0} \EE_{\mathrm{geom},\eps}\bigl[|Q_\eps-F(x_D)|^2\bigr]=0. \] In particular, for every $t>0$, $\PP_{\mathrm{geom},\eps}(|Q_\eps-F(x_D)|>t)\to0$. These limits use the geometry law at each mesh, without a coupling across meshes.

primaryStatements.name: Finite orthogonality
primaryStatements.label: fields:orthogonality-prop
primaryStatements.text: For distinct triangles $t,u$, \begin{equation} \langle Z_t,Z_u\rangle=0, \qquad \|Z_t\|^2=\frac34. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Closed-sum tail
primaryStatements.label: fields:closed-prop
primaryStatements.text: For every fixed bounded box $B\subset\C$ and every $a>0$, the full-plane model of spacing $\eps$ satisfies \begin{equation} \lim_{\eps\downarrow0} \EE\!\sum_{\substack{P\text{ a rim},\ P\subset B\\\diam(P)\ge a}} |Q_P(1)|^2=0. \end{equation} The corresponding full sums for $V_P$ vanish identically.

primaryStatements.name: Established input
primaryStatements.label: prop:probability-input
primaryStatements.text: The following estimates hold at criticality. \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item For each fixed rectangle aspect ratio, both colors have crossing probabilities bounded below by a positive constant, uniformly in its size. At sizes tending to infinity, the corresponding quenched crossing probabilities are bounded below with probability tending to one. More precisely, for each fixed finite family of buffered rectangle chains on fixed square grids, and each $\gamma>0$, the required quenched crossing lower bounds hold outside a geometry event of probability $O_\gamma(R^{-\gamma})$ when the family is dilated by $R$. The positive lower bound may depend on the family and on $\gamma$. \item For every fixed $j\ge1$, there is $C_j<\infty$ such that, for all $1\le r\le R$, \begin{equation} \EE\bigl[p_j^\eta(r,R)^2\bigr] \le C_j\alpha_j(r,R)^2. \end{equation} \item There are constants $c_1,c_4>0$ and $C<\infty$ such that, for all $1\le r\le R$, \begin{equation} \alpha_1(r,R)\le C(r/R)^{c_1},\qquad \alpha_5(r,R)\le C(r/R)^2,\qquad \alpha_4(r,R)\le C(r/R)^{1+c_4}. \end{equation} \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.name: Bulk transport
primaryStatements.label: thm:bulk-transport
primaryStatements.text: From every sequence $\eps\downarrow0$ one can extract a subsequence and a complex number $a$, depending only on that subsequence, such that $\Rea a<1/2$ and the following holds in every bulk patch. If $f\in C_c^\infty(B(x,R))$ and $\overline B(x,6R)$ lies in the patch, then \begin{equation} \max_{P:\,P\not\subset B(x,4R)} |Q_P(f)-aV_P(f)|\xrightarrow[\eps\to0]{\PP}0. \end{equation} As in the definition of a bulk patch, local tests may be set to zero on a geometry event whose probability tends to zero. The subsequence and scalar are common to all patches and tests.

primaryStatements.name: The state cochain
primaryStatements.label: prop:state-cochain
primaryStatements.text: For every fixed connector, including its actual end charts, there are functions $i_e^\eps(\sigma_s,\sigma_t)$ such that \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \widehat m_s+\widehat j_e-i_e^\eps&=o_{L^1}(1) &&\text{in every cycle experiment containing }e,\\ \sum_e i_e^\eps&=o_{L^1}(1) &&\text{on the independent state product of every simple system}. \end{aligned} \end{equation} The same functions work in all completions. For a fixed collection of normalized short templates admitting uniform short completions, \[ \|i_e^\eps\|_{L^2(\mu_s\otimes\mu_t)}\le C h \] for all sufficiently small $\eps$, after increasing a common constant.

primaryStatements.name: Affine straight means
primaryStatements.label: prop:affine
primaryStatements.text: For $X=Q,V$ there is a scalar $a_h^X$, uniformly bounded in $h$, such that every fixed straight transport in the countable family used below has mean \begin{equation} \EE_\mu i_e^\eps=a_h^X(z_t-z_s)+o(1). \end{equation} The same scalar applies to translations, common rotations and color flips of the reference type. All choices can be made simultaneously for the two fields and countably many $h$.

definitions.name: Bulk setting
definitions.label: def:bulk-setting
definitions.text: A bulk setting is either the full-plane sample or a finite simple triangulation of the sphere carrying independent fair site colors conditional on its graph and geometry. In the latter case an oriented open planar patch is coupled to a full-plane sample so that, on every fixed compact subset of the patch, the graphs and their colors agree with probability tending to one as $\eps\downarrow0$. The graph and chart agreement event is independent of color sampling conditional on the geometry. Spatial weights are used only on triangles in the agreement patch. Compactly supported tests may be set to zero on the exceptional geometry event.

definitions.name: A plug type
definitions.label: def:plug-type
definitions.text: A type consists of the following deterministic data: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item two concentric gate annuli $[a_1,b_1]$, $[a_2,b_2]$ and a cutoff radius $m$, with \[ 10<a_1<b_1<m/10,\qquad 10m<a_2<b_2; \] \item closed Jordan disks $O\subset\operatorname{int}H$, with $\overline B(0,b_2)\subset\operatorname{int}O$, and an orientation-preserving band chart \[ \Phi:[-12,12]\times[-3,3]\longrightarrow\R^2. \] Writing its coordinates as $(u,v)$, membership in $O$ and $H$ within the chart is exactly $|u|\le3$ and $|u|\le8$, respectively; membership in the interiors is given by the strict inequalities. The full section $\Phi(\{0\}\times[-3,3])$ is strictly inside $B(0,a_1)$; \item one positive integer rank for each of the two windows \[ I_B=[-.3,.3],\qquad I_W=[-1.8,-1.4]. \] \end{enumerate} No metric regularity of the Jordan disks or chart is imposed.

definitions.name: Usable states and admission
definitions.label: def:usable-state
definitions.text:
Fix positive thresholds $ eta, eta'$. The state event $G$ requires:  egin{enumerate}[label=	extup{(oman*)}] \item simple surrounding retained site circuits $S_1,S_2$ in the two gate annuli, with their edge segments in those annuli, enclosing the corresponding inner balls and containing at most two black sites each; \item both roots and the inequalities $
u(L^+\mid\sigma)\ge eta$ and $
u(L^-\mid\sigma)\ge eta$. \end{enumerate} The conditional probabilities use independent ordinary data on $O^c$; in particular they average over the exterior point geometry as well as its colors. A type is admitted when $
u(G)\ge eta'$, and its state law is \[ \mu=
u(\sigma\in\cdot\mid G). \] The finite normalized menu and thresholds will be fixed in Section ef{sec:pins}. Admission and $\mu$ may depend on $h,\eps$.

definitions.name: Connectors and simple systems
definitions.label: def:simple-system
definitions.text: A directed connector $e:s\to t$ between same-color plugs with disjoint obstacles is an oriented rectangular band, with transverse parameter $v\in[-3,3]$, attached by its full parameterized ends to the positive port $u_s=8$ of $H_s$ and the negative port $u_t=-8$ of $H_t$. Apart from these attachments it avoids both disks. Only the charts with $|u|\le8$ are prescribed at its ends. A simple system is a cyclic list of at least two distinct plugs and connectors. Its closed obstacles are pairwise disjoint, its exterior bands are pairwise disjoint and avoid all other obstacles, and the sectors from section $0$ of one plug to section $0$ of the next form an embedded annular band with the prescribed directed longitude and transverse parameter. Denote the whole closed sector of $e$ by $\mathcal B_e$.

definitions.name: Cycle experiment
definitions.label: def:cycle-experiment
definitions.text: For a simple system, sample the states independently with their laws $\mu_s$. Given the states, sample the exterior regions of the connectors independently, each conditioned on its success $S_e$, and sample the remaining plane data ordinarily. The exterior region of $e$ may be the whole sector $\mathcal B_e$ with the closed endpoint state disks removed.

definitions.name: Qualified pin
definitions.label: pin:qualification
definitions.text: Let $P$ be an oriented rim in a bulk patch. A qualified pin consists of a vertex $p\in P$, a grid center $z$ with $|p-z|\le h$, a placed menu type, its root ranks, and the following data. We describe the black case; interchanging colors gives the white case. \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item In the original configuration there are three surrounding gate circuits, in prescribed annuli $[a_kh,b_kh]$, $k=1,2,3$. The first two are the annuli of the plug. The third has $a_3>100b_2$ and isolates an ordered central subarc $\Delta$ through $p$: all visits of $P$ to $B(z,a_3h)$ belong to $\Delta$, and $\diam\Delta\le2b_3h$. \item In the nominal chart the local ordered traversal of $P$ follows the horizontal midline from before $u=-8$ to after $u=8$, with transverse error and longitudinal backtracking less than $0.1$. The arc $\Delta$ lies in $|u|<1$, and its marked point is near $u=0$. There are no other visits to $H$. The fit test has the closed-limit property of Lemma \ref{lemma:exact-fit} below. \item A prescribed local preparation, applied to the original sample using an auxiliary seed attached to this chart, placement, and color, only recolors existing sites in the opposing strip from black to white, keeping the point configuration fixed. It leaves the fitted black traversal unchanged. Its inner state $\sigma'$ belongs to $G$, and the chosen type is admitted. The black root contains vertices of the actual traversal near $u=-1.7$ and $u=1.7$, with error less than $0.05$, joined along that traversal in the root window. The two black side passages are also supplied by that traversal. All these paths are retained paths. \item For the white color separately, each of the two ordinary side-test probabilities, conditional on $\sigma'$ and the actual point geometry, is at least $\beta$. \end{enumerate} The prepared state is shared whenever the same candidate choice is used; preparations for other choices start again from the original sample.

papers.title: The Gaussian free field limit of the balanced six-vertex model with variance multiplier 1/arcsin(c/2)
papers.abstract: We prove that the height function of the square-lattice six-vertex model with weights $a=b=1$ and $0\lt c\le2$, in the plane state obtained from balanced tori, converges to a multiple of the Gaussian free field. For unit height jumps and Green kernel $-(2\pi)^{-1}\log|x-y|$, the squared multiplier is $1/\arcsin(c/2)$.
papers.familySummary: The balanced square-lattice six-vertex height field with $a=b=1$ and $0\lt c\le2$ converges to a Gaussian free field, including at the endpoint c = 2. The plane state is defined by balanced-torus limits. For unit height increments and Green kernel $-(2\pi)^{-1}\log|x-y|$, the exact variance multiplier is $1/\arcsin(c/2)$.
papers.subject: Probability and statistical mechanics

For unit height jumps and Green kernel \(-(2\pi)^{-1}\log|x-y|\), the squared multiplier is \(1/\arcsin(c/2)\).

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: For every fixed \(c\in(0,2]\), the prescribed iterated balanced-torus limit \(\P_c\) exists. Define \begin{equation} \Delta=1-\frac{c^2}{2},\qquad \sigma(c)^2=\frac2{\arccos\Delta}=\frac1{\arcsin(c/2)}. \end{equation} As \(\delta\downarrow0\) through arbitrary positive real values, the fields \(h_\delta\) converge to \(\sigma(c)\Gamma\) in each of the following senses. \begin{enumerate} \item For every finite family \(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_m\) of compactly supported finite signed measures of total mass zero and finite energy, \[ \bigl(\langle h_\delta,\mu_j\rangle\bigr)_{j=1}^m \ \Longrightarrow\ \mathcal N\!\left(0, \bigl(\sigma(c)^2\mathcal E(\mu_i,\mu_j)\bigr)_{i,j=1}^m\right). \] \item For every bounded open \(U\subset\R^2\) and \(-1<\alpha<0\), there is convergence in law, with tightness, in the ordinary restriction spaces \[ \mathcal C^\alpha_{\mathrm{res}}(U):=B^\alpha_{\infty,\infty}(U), \qquad B^\alpha_{p,q}(U),\qquad W^{\alpha,p}(U), \quad 1\le p<\infty,\quad 1\le q\le\infty, \] modulo constants. Convergence also holds in the outward completion \eqref{eq:source-holder} defined below. No regularity of \(\partial U\) is required. One may fix a smooth compactly supported \(\rho\) of integral one and replace each field \(X\) by \(X-\langle X,\rho\rangle\), using the same pinning for the limit. \item For every \(k\ge1\) and every tuple \((u_i,u_i')_{i=1}^k\) with \(\{u_i,u_i'\}\cap\{u_j,u_j'\}=\varnothing\) for \(i\ne j\), \begin{equation} \E_c\prod_{i=1}^k \bigl(h_\delta(u_i')-h_\delta(u_i)\bigr) \longrightarrow \sigma(c)^k\sum_{\pi}\prod_{\{i,j\}\in\pi}C_{ij}, \end{equation} where the sum is over pairings of \(\{1,\ldots,k\}\), is zero for odd \(k\), and \[ C_{ij}=G(u_i',u_j')-G(u_i',u_j)-G(u_i,u_j')+G(u_i,u_j). \] The convergence is uniform on compact sets of such tuples. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.name: Exact finite-word expansion
primaryStatements.label: cor:finite-word-expansion
primaryStatements.text: Expand each auxiliary mark as \[ T^{D_j}=\sum_{\alpha,\beta}(D_j)_{\beta\alpha} M_{{\rm ph},\alpha\beta}. \] For each resulting entry word, let $n_j$ be the number of minus spins after its $j$th action, with $n_0=n$. Entry words with $n_m\ne n$ have zero expectation in $\Omega_Y$. For a path of a word with $n_m=n$, let $H\subset Y$ be the roots absent at the end and let $V$ be its surviving added arguments, ordered in the same replacement slots. Then $|H|=|V|=:k\le m$, and its contribution to the normalized physical expectation is \begin{equation} \left(\prod_{j=1}^m(D_j)_{\beta_j\alpha_j}\right) (-1)^{\sum_{j=1}^m(n_{j-1}-n)} (-s_\lambda)^{-k} \frac{\prod_{j=1}^m\gamma_j} {\prod_{j=1}^m(1+q_Y(v'_j))} \frac{\det(W_{v'}(p))_{H,V}} {\det(1/[v'-p])_{H,V}} \prod_{p\in H}\ell_p. \end{equation} The expectation is the sum of these contributions. In particular, the determinant size is bounded by the word length. For diagonal entry words the parity sign in \eqref{eq:exact-path-determinant} is one. Among distinct removed original roots the correction product contains only reciprocal $f$ factors, with one for each pair. Each removed original root also contributes one factor $\beta$ joining it to the row argument at the step that removes it.

primaryStatements.name: Limits of fixed row words
primaryStatements.label: prop:word-kernel
primaryStatements.text: For each fixed integer $m\ge0$ and fixed $2\times2$ matrices $D_1,\ldots,D_m$, the homogeneous plane coefficients \begin{equation} \left\langle\Omega_L, A_L^{D_m}(x_m)\cdots A_L^{D_1}(x_1)\Omega_L\right\rangle \end{equation} converge locally uniformly on $\mathcal S_\lambda^m$ to a holomorphic function $\mathcal K_{D_m,\ldots,D_1}(x_m,\ldots,x_1)$. It is invariant under every common complex translation for which the translated arguments remain in the strip. For $\lambda>2\pi/3$, the same functions are the array limits in \eqref{eq:array-limit-convention}. If $v_L$ is any fixed finite linear combination of row words applied to $\Omega_L$, then \[ \lim\|A_L^D(x)v_L\|^2 \le4\|D\|^2\lim\|v_L\|^2. \] The two limits are determined by the word coefficients and the adjoint rule. This is the bound used to construct bounded row actions in Section \ref{sec:angular}. For $\lambda>2\pi/3$, in the regular-filling procedure the expectations of every fixed equal-time local matrix product converge to those of the homogeneous plane construction.

primaryStatements.name: Separated diagonal words
primaryStatements.label: prop:word-clustering
primaryStatements.text: Partition a fixed finite list of diagonal marked rows into groups. Within each group fix its internal arguments in the strict angle strip. Translate the arguments of group $g$ by a common imaginary amount $it_g$, and let every $|t_g-t_{g'}|$ tend to infinity. Then the plane word kernel factors into the product of the individual group kernels. Convergence is locally uniform in the internal strict arguments. The order within each group is retained.

primaryStatements.name: The angular representation
primaryStatements.label: prop:angular-space
primaryStatements.text: On $\mathcal H$ the rows act as bounded holomorphic operator families, with \[ \|A^D(z)\|\le 2\|D\|,\qquad A^D(z)^*=A^{X\overline D X}(-\overline z). \] They satisfy the finite RTT exchange identities wherever their auxiliary intertwiner is invertible. There is a strongly continuous unitary group $U_b$, $b\in\R$, fixing $\Omega$, such that \begin{equation} U_bA^D(z)U_b^*=A^D(z+ib). \end{equation} Words with real arguments in any nonempty open subinterval of $(-v,v)$ span a dense subspace. The family $P=A^I$ consists of commuting normal operators and has a simultaneous representation by almost surely holomorphic scalar functions $f$ on the strip, with \begin{equation} f(-\overline z)=\overline{f(z)},\qquad |f(z)|\le2. \end{equation} In the half-plane coordinate this reality condition reads $f(\overline w)=\overline{f(w)}$.

primaryStatements.name: Physical law, both axes, and reflection
primaryStatements.label: prop:physical-plane
primaryStatements.text: The row representation gives the local probabilities of the plane law $\P_c$ in Theorem \ref{thm:main}. In particular its prescribed iterated balanced-torus limit exists when $c<1$. Quantization with time pointing east and quantization with time pointing north describe this same law. For an ordinary observable supported on one side of either coordinate cut, the squared norm of its prepared state is its expectation paired with its complex-conjugate reflected observable, with the corresponding spin reflection. Products of neutral height observables may be prepared using paths confined to that side.

primaryStatements.name: Exact variogram and logarithmic growth
primaryStatements.label: prop:variogram
primaryStatements.text: After an axial symmetry, any nonzero lattice displacement may be written $(k,j)$ with $k\ge1$ and $|j|\le k$. Its height variance is \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \E_c\bigl(h(k,j)-h(0,0)\bigr)^2 &=2\Re\int\bigl(1-f(1)^k f(\pm i)^{|j|}\bigr)\dd\mu(f)\\ &=4\kappa\log k+O(1), \end{aligned} \end{equation} where the sign of $i$ is chosen according to the vertical direction. The error is uniform over these displacements. In particular the variance is bounded by $C(1+\log(1+|k|+|j|))$.

primaryStatements.name: The covariance constant below one
primaryStatements.label: prop:normalization
primaryStatements.text: With the row and height conventions of Sections \ref{sec:finite} and \ref{sec:angular}, \begin{equation} \kappa=\frac1{2\pi(\pi-\lambda)}. \end{equation} Consequently a limiting covariance \(-2\kappa\log|x-y|\) has squared multiplier \(4\pi\kappa=2/(\pi-\lambda)=\sigma(c)^2\) relative to \eqref{eq:green}.

papers.title: The curve scaling limit of half-plane double dimers
papers.abstract: We prove that the complete double-dimer loop ensemble for the Temperleyan square lattice in the upper half-plane converges to nested CLE4. The convergence holds along the full mesh limit and matches every macroscopic loop as an unparametrized curve. This resolves the half-plane Temperleyan form of the double-dimer CLE4 scaling-limit conjecture.
papers.familySummary: Resolves the half-plane Temperleyan form of the double-dimer scaling-limit conjecture: the complete loop ensemble formed by two independent dimer coverings of the Temperleyan square lattice converges to nested CLE4. Convergence matches every macroscopic loop as an unparametrized curve, upgrading convergence of loop observables to convergence of the loops themselves.
papers.subject: Probability and statistical mechanics
papers.sourceAbstract: We prove that the complete double-dimer loop ensemble for the Temperleyan square lattice in the upper half-plane converges to nested \(\CLE_4\). The convergence holds along the full mesh limit and matches every macroscopic loop as an unparametrized curve. This resolves the half-plane Temperleyan form of the double-dimer \(\CLE_4\) scaling-limit conjecture.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: For the half-plane Temperleyan law specified above, the family \(F(\mathcal L_\delta)\) is tight as \(\delta\downarrow0\) in the loop-collection topology just defined, and \[ F(\mathcal L_\delta)\ \Longrightarrow\ F(\mathcal L), \qquad \delta\downarrow0, \] where \(\mathcal L\) is standard nested \(\CLE_4\) in \(\HH\). The convergence holds along the full mesh limit and matches all macroscopic loops as curves.

primaryStatements.name: Cylindrical convergence {\cite[Theorem 4.2(2)
primaryStatements.label: thm:cylindrical
primaryStatements.text: {BI}}] Let \(z_1,\ldots,z_r\) be distinct interior points of \(\HH\), and choose face punctures \(z_j^\delta\to z_j\). For the two independent matchings used in Theorem \ref{thm:main}, the reduced lamination relative to \((z_j^\delta)_{j=1}^r\) converges in law to the corresponding reduced lamination of nested \(\CLE_4\). In particular the multisets of enclosed puncture subsets, with multiplicities and with subsets of size at most one deleted, converge in law.

primaryStatements.name: Standard properties of nested \(\CLE_4\)
primaryStatements.label: prop:cle-facts
primaryStatements.text: After conformal transport to the disk, nested \(\CLE_4\) consists almost surely of pairwise disjoint simple loops contained in the open disk. There are finitely many loops of diameter greater than any positive number. Every fixed interior point is almost surely off all loop traces and is surrounded by infinitely many successive nested loops.

primaryStatements.name: Crossings in a finite rectangle
primaryStatements.label: prop:rectangle-crossings
primaryStatements.text: Let the odd corner-rooted rectangles $R_\delta$ converge to a fixed nondegenerate rectangle. Let $u_\delta<v_\delta$ be parallel cuts in either lattice direction, whose limiting coordinates are strictly inside the longitudinal sides and whose limiting separation is positive. Under two independent uniform matchings of $R_\delta$, \[ \lim_{K\to\infty}\limsup_{\delta\downarrow0} \PP\{N(u_\delta,v_\delta)>K\}=0. \] The traversals are counted over all loops, with no restriction on their portions outside the slab.

primaryStatements.name: Short intervals in a rectangle
primaryStatements.label: prop:rectangle-short
primaryStatements.text: Let $R_\delta$ be corner-rooted odd lattice rectangles converging to a fixed nondegenerate rectangle, with two independent uniform dimer covers. Fix an interior longitudinal coordinate $c$, two positive numbers $\rho_-,\rho_+$, and a bounded segment $J$ of the transverse line $x=c$. The two regions $x\le c-\rho_-$ and $x\ge c+\rho_+$ are called the deep regions; if either is disjoint from the rectangle, the events below are empty. The segment $J$ may extend beyond the transverse sides of the rectangle. For each sufficiently small $h>0$, partition $J$ into at most $C_J/h$ intervals of length at most $h$, with endpoints off the graph. Use a seam converging to $x=c$ and the corresponding intervals when necessary. A tested arc is a cycle subarc, in its cycle direction, with one endpoint in each deep region. Let $B_{\delta,h}$ be the event that some partition interval $I$ satisfies at least one of the following conditions: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item a tested arc $\alpha$ on a cycle $g$ has $\iota_I(\alpha)\ne0$ and $\iota_I(\alpha)\ne\iota_I(g)$; \item tested arcs on two distinct cycles both have nonzero intersection number with $I$. \end{enumerate} The arcs may otherwise travel anywhere in the rectangle. Then \begin{equation} \lim_{h\downarrow0}\limsup_{\delta\downarrow0} \PP(B_{\delta,h})=0. \end{equation} The conclusion is unchanged by truncating intervals at a transverse side, or by placing their endpoints outside the rectangle.

primaryStatements.name: Uniform localization
primaryStatements.label: prop:localization
primaryStatements.text: Let $K$ be a bounded closed subset of $\overline{\HH}$ and let $\eps>0$. There is an $R<\infty$ such that, for every sufficiently small $\delta$, the two independent half-plane matchings can be coupled with two independent uniform matchings of $\mathcal R_{\delta,R}$ so that both matching states agree on $K$ with probability at least $1-\eps$.

primaryStatements.name: Local traversal counts
primaryStatements.label: cor:local-crossings
primaryStatements.text: Fix a bounded window $K\subset\overline{\HH}$ and two distinct parallel coordinate lines. For horizontal lines assume both have positive height. The maximum total number of parameter-disjoint portions of half-plane double-dimer cycles that lie in $K$ and traverse from one line to the other, in either direction, is tight as $\delta\downarrow0$.

primaryStatements.name: Local exclusion of opposite intersection signs
primaryStatements.label: prop:local-opposite
primaryStatements.text: Let $u$ be either the horizontal or vertical coordinate, let $L=\{u=c\}$ be a test line, and let $J\subset L$ be a bounded segment. If $u$ is the vertical coordinate, assume $c>0$. Fix a bounded window $K\subset\overline{\HH}$ and buffers $\rho_-,\rho_+>0$. Deterministically partition $J$ into $O(h^{-1})$ intervals of length at most $h$, with endpoints off the graph. Let $E_{\delta,h}$ be the event that, for one of these intervals $I$, one directed half-plane cycle has two portions $\alpha,\beta$ contained in $K$ such that each portion has one endpoint in $\{u\le c-\rho_-\}$ and the other in $\{u\ge c+\rho_+\}$, and \[ \iota_I(\alpha)\iota_I(\beta)<0. \] Then \begin{equation} \lim_{h\downarrow0}\limsup_{\delta\downarrow0} \PP(E_{\delta,h})=0. \end{equation} For a vertical line $L$, the segment may reach or extend below the bottom boundary. Test lines are chosen off lattice vertices; the same estimate holds for seam perturbations of order $\delta$.

papers.title: Universality of critical quench autocorrelations in the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model
papers.abstract: We prove joint functional convergence of the stationary and quench autocorrelations of zero-field Sherrington–Kirkpatrick heat-bath dynamics at inverse temperature β = 1, with the same random limit for Gaussian and Rademacher couplings. Each site has a rate-one clock, mean spin autocorrelations are multiplied by n1/3, and waiting times and lags are measured in units n2/3. The quench starts from independent fair spins, and convergence is uniform on compact sets of positive waiting times and lags. The quench limit is selected by these initial states and relaxes to the stationary limiting autocorrelation as the waiting time tends to infinity.
papers.familySummary: For zero-field Gaussian SK heat-bath dynamics with rate-one updates per spin, proves worst-start cutoff on the $\log n$ scale for fixed $0\le\beta\lt 1$, mixing time $n^{2/3+o(1)}$ at β = 1, and stretched-exponential mixing from a Gibbs-sampled fixed starting configuration for β > 1, in probability over disorder. At criticality, rescaled stationary and quench autocorrelation processes have universal random limits for Gaussian and Rademacher disorder; the quench limit relaxes to the stationary limit.

papers.sourceAbstract: We prove joint functional convergence of the stationary and quench autocorrelations of zero-field Sherrington--Kirkpatrick heat-bath dynamics at inverse temperature $\beta=1$, with the same random limit for Gaussian and Rademacher couplings. Each site has a rate-one clock, mean spin autocorrelations are multiplied by $n^{1/3}$, and waiting times and lags are measured in units $n^{2/3}$. The quench starts from independent fair spins, and convergence is uniform on compact sets of positive waiting times and lags. The quench limit is selected by these initial states and relaxes to the stationary limiting autocorrelation as the waiting time tends to infinity.
