primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: For every fixed $M>0$ and $0<|\mathfrak a|<M$, there is $\eps=\eps(M,\mathfrak a)>0$ such that the set of $d\in\Ueps$ for which the full development $(M_d,g_d)$ admits a future extension in the sense of Definition \ref{intro:extension} is meagre in $\Ueps$. Consequently, future $C^0\cap W^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}$-inextendible data contain a residual subset of $\Ueps$ in the weighted smooth topology \eqref{intro:seminorms}.

primaryStatements.name: Background estimates
primaryStatements.label: prop:bg-package

primaryStatements.name: First runout and corner removal
primaryStatements.label: prop:bg-runout
primaryStatements.text: Every seed whose future geodesic has finite maximal proper lifetime in $M_d$ crosses $\mathcal S$. Its first runout from $\mathcal P_d$ is either a branch, where one optical coordinate has a finite limit and the other tends to $+\infty$, or a corner, where both tend to $+\infty$. For each fixed datum, seeds whose first runout is a corner form a $\mu_d$-null set.

primaryStatements.name: A positive family supplied by every weak exit
primaryStatements.label: prop:exit-family
primaryStatements.text: Under the hypotheses of \Cref{ex:graph}, there is a measurable set $S\subset T\Sigma$ of positive smooth section measure such that every future unit geodesic with seed in $S$ has finite maximal future proper lifetime in the full $M$ and an ambient endpoint on $\partial M$. The endpoints lie in one compact subset of an ambient chart. Moreover, there are finitely many precompact ambient charts $\psi_j:U_j\to V_j\subset\R^4$ and constants $C<\infty$, $m>0$ with the following properties: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item on each entire $V_j$, the metric and inverse metric have component norms at most $C$, and $\|\widetilde\Gamma_j\|_{L^2(V_j)}\le C$; \item for every seed in $S$ and every proper time from its intersection with $\Sigma$ to its full future endpoint, excluding only the endpoint itself, at least one $j$ satisfies \begin{equation} \operatorname{dist}\bigl(\psi_j(\gamma(\tau)), \R^4\setminus V_j\bigr)\ge m, \qquad |(\psi_j)_*\dot\gamma(\tau)|\le C. \end{equation} \end{enumerate} Here the section measure is the pullback of canonical volume on $T^*\Sigma$ under $w\mapsto h(w,\cdot)$, where $h$ is the induced metric. In particular it has the same null sets as every smooth positive measure on $T\Sigma$.

primaryStatements.name: Countable cover of all future extensions
primaryStatements.label: prop:exit-cover
primaryStatements.text: Every datum in $\Ueps$ admitting a future $C^0\cap W^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ extension belongs to some $E(O,B)$. Consequently the extendible set is precisely \[ \bigcup_{O\in\mathcal B}\ \bigcup_{B=1}^{\infty}E(O,B). \] This cover includes extensions whose actual exit occurs after first runout from the comparison development.

primaryStatements.name: Packet preparation
primaryStatements.label: prop:packet-preparation
primaryStatements.text: For every finite $m\ge10$, finite jet budget $N$, positive loss tolerance $\eta_{\rm out}$, and $0<\nu<1$, one can choose $\zeta>0$ and finite construction orders so that the following objects exist for arbitrarily large $T$ along the indicated sequence. \begin{enumerate} \item There are exact smooth complete vacuum data $d_T\in\Ddata$ on the whole bridge with $p_m(d_T-d)\to0$. They agree with $d$ on the other end, the connecting region, and an expanding protected ball on the selected end. The permitted exterior correction tail is retained. \item An exact exterior evolution of $d_T$ reaches the required part of $\mathcal S$, with overlapping collars and strict outflow margins. In the fixed background wave-map description its entry spacetime jets differ from $g+h^p$ by $O(\amp^2e^{\eta_{\rm out} T})$. Here \begin{equation} h^p=\amp\,\operatorname{tr.rev.}_g\operatorname{Re} \left(e^{i\lambda v}\sum_{j=0}^{J_*}\lambda^{-j}p_j\right). \end{equation} The leading coefficient is real, trace-free, and annihilates $L_0$. On the entire observation box $\mathcal Q_T$, \begin{equation} |(p_0)_{AB}|_\gamma\ge e^{-o(T)}. \end{equation} At every fixed required base order the ordinary mixed coordinate jets of the normalized amplitude components are $e^{o(T)}$, and the linearized Ricci and gauge errors have arbitrarily high inverse-frequency accuracy. \item There is a metric $\bar g$ exactly of double-null form, with fields $\bar\gamma,\log\bar{\mathcal A},\bar b$ and their exact geometric derived fields. Through order $N$, its differences from the background fields, including $q^{-1}\partial_vb$, are $O(\amp e^{\eta_{\rm out} T})$. Its defects in the null structure and angular equations \eqref{dn:D2}--\eqref{dn:D3} are $O(\amp^2e^{\eta_{\rm out} T})$. If the actual exterior induced data are written in double-null coordinates initialized by the background values on $\mathcal S$, their full entry jets differ from this template by the same quadratic bound. \end{enumerate} All entry discrepancies and all template changes and defects vanish for $v<(1-\nu)T$. Any additional finite initial or residual jet buffers may be included in $N$. Positive frequency powers at these base orders are independent of the later orders used to improve linear accuracy. At the finitely many high entry orders ultimately requested by \Cref{thm:dn-comparison}, the actual fields have $e^{o(T)}$ bounds.

primaryStatements.name: Finite double-null experiment
primaryStatements.label: thm:dn-comparison
primaryStatements.text: For every fixed background and branch tube in \Cref{lem:bg-branch-tube}, every finite $m,s$, and every sufficiently small fixed $c>0$, the parameters in \Cref{prop:packet-preparation} can be chosen so that its exact entry data have a smooth vacuum development on \Cref{dn:domain} in the double-null gauge initialized there. The relative lapse and the sphere metric remain positive and uniformly nondegenerate. For \[ \mathcal U=(\gamma,\log\mathcal A,b,\chi_0,\chi_1, \ell_0,\ell_1,\xi_0,\xi_1) \] one has, in a fixed sphere atlas and ordinary coordinate derivatives, \begin{equation} \max_{|I|\le s}\|\partial^I(\mathcal U'-\bar{\mathcal U}) \|_{L^\infty(\Omega_T)} \le e^{-(1+c)\alpha T} \end{equation} for all sufficiently large $T$ in the selected experiment sequence. The same conclusion holds for $q^{-1}\partial_vb'-q^{-1}\partial_v\bar b$ at any preassigned finite order, after increasing the finite order budget. The individual ordinary jets of the primed relative fields through every order used in the experiment are $e^{o(T)}$, uniformly for this moving family. The exact solution and the template equal the background where $v<(1-\nu)T$. The exact solution agrees on an entry collar, by local geometric uniqueness, with the actual exterior solution of \Cref{prop:packet-preparation}.

u$ may be chosen sufficiently small, with the finite base orders fixed, so that on every existing bootstrap subslab  egin{equation} \sup_{0\le t\le L_T} \| (\Delta\gamma,\Delta\log\mathcal A,\Delta b, \Delta\chi_i,\Delta\ell_i,\Delta\xi_i) \|_{L^2(I_T(t)	imes\Sph)} \le \amp^2e^{\eta_2T}. \end{equation} The supremum is restricted to available slices. definitions.name: Future extension
definitions.label: intro:extension
definitions.text: A future $C^0\cap W^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ extension of $(M_d,g_d)$ consists of a connected time-oriented smooth four-manifold $\widetilde M$, a continuous nondegenerate Lorentzian metric $\widetilde g$ of signature $(-,+,+,+)$ whose components belong to $W^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ in smooth charts, and a smooth time-orientation-preserving isometric embedding $\iota:M_d\hookrightarrow\widetilde M$ with proper open image. There must also be a future-directed timelike $C^1$ curve $c:[0,1]\to\widetilde M$ such that \[ c([0,1))\subset\iota(M_d), \qquad c(1)\in\partial\iota(M_d). \] No field equation or global-hyperbolicity condition is imposed outside the image.

definitions.name: Necessary existential extension tests
definitions.label: def:exit-test
definitions.text: For $O\in\mathcal B$ and $B\in\N$, $B\ge1$, let $E(O,B)\subset\Ueps$ consist of the data satisfying both of the following requirements. \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item There is an extension of $M_d$ of the regularity and type specified in Definition \ref{intro:extension}, and a measurable $S\subset O$ with \begin{equation} \mu_d(S)>.99\,\mu_d(O), \end{equation} such that every seed in $S$ has finite full future lifetime. There are at most $B$ precompact ambient charts $\psi_j:U_j\to V_j$ witnessing \Cref{ex:chart-witness} along each entire such geodesic, from $\Sigma$ to its full endpoint. On the whole of every $V_j$, each of the metric norm, inverse metric norm, and Christoffel $L^2$ norm is at most $B$. At each point a selected chart has velocity norm at most $B$ and Euclidean distance to $\R^4\setminus V_j$ at least $1/B$. \item There is an observation neighborhood $\mathcal N$ satisfying all three parts of \Cref{lem:bg-branch-tube} for this datum, with $\overline O\subset\mathcal N$ and the optical ordering chosen so that $v\to\infty$. One choice of its central branch track, compact state ranges, positive $p$ bounds, transverse earlier flow tube, interval $J$, observation boxes, admissible launch patch, unbounded sequence of $T$, and constants $u_2,c_2,c_0$ serves every seed in $\overline{\mathcal N}$. In particular, the entry-to-observation portions fit \eqref{bg:experiment-domain} with its outer margins and positive slice-length bound. The admissible patch has the low-order ray and collar properties specified before \Cref{lem:bg-branch-tube}. \end{enumerate} All tube constants, charts, patches, and subsequences in this definition are existential witnesses for the given datum. They are not additional countable indices and are not required to work in a neighborhood of that datum.

primaryStatements.label: phase:main
primaryStatements.text: For each fixed \(M>0\) and \(0<\mathfrak a<M\), there is \(\eps_0=\eps_0(M,\mathfrak a)>0\) such that \(\mathcal U_{\eps_0}\) contains a dense \(G_\delta\) subset \(\mathcal G\) for which every \(\mathcal M_d\), \(d\in\mathcal G\), has no future \(C^1\) extension in the sense of Definition \ref{phase:extension}.

primaryStatements.name: Coverage of future $C^1$ exits
primaryStatements.label: test:exit-cover
primaryStatements.text: If $\mathcal M_d$, $d\in\mathcal U$, admits a future $C^1$ extension in the stated sense, then $d\in\mathcal A(O,B)$ for some $O\in\mathcal O$ and some integer $B\ge1$.

primaryStatements.name: Comparison development and first runout
primaryStatements.label: test:comparison
primaryStatements.text: After decreasing the defining $p_{10}$ radius of $\mathcal U$, each $d\in\mathcal U$ has a smooth globally hyperbolic vacuum comparison development $\mathcal P_d$ containing the whole bridge $\Sigma$ as a Cauchy hypersurface and embedded openly and isometrically in $\mathcal M_d$. It contains a spacelike cylinder $\mathcal S$ and its full future product wedge, with coordinates $t=(u+v)/2\ge0$, $x=(v-u)/2\in\mathbb R$, $\theta\in\mathbb S^2$, in which \begin{equation} \begin{split} g&=-2a\,du\,dv+ \gamma_{AB}(d\theta^A-b^Adu)(d\theta^B-b^Bdu),\\ a&=q\mathcal A,\qquad q=q_0e^{-\kappa(u+v)},\qquad q_0,\kappa>0. \end{split} \end{equation} The coefficients $\mathcal A^{\pm1}$ and $\gamma^{\pm1}$ are uniformly bounded, with $\gamma$ uniformly comparable to a fixed round sphere metric. Every seed with $T_d(w)<\infty$ crosses $\mathcal S$ before its first runout from $\mathcal P_d$, and that first runout has exactly one of the following coordinate limits: \begin{equation} \begin{array}{lll} \text{first branch:}&u\to u_*<\infty,&v\to+\infty,\\ \text{second branch:}&v\to v_*<\infty,&u\to+\infty,\\ \text{corner:}&u\to+\infty,&v\to+\infty. \end{array} \end{equation} These alternatives describe limiting coordinate regimes; they do not adjoin boundary points or identify $\mathcal P_d$ with $\mathcal M_d$.

primaryStatements.name: Corner seeds have measure zero
primaryStatements.label: test:corner-null
primaryStatements.text: For a fixed $d\in\mathcal U$, the seeds whose first runout from $\mathcal P_d$ is a corner are contained in a set of measure zero for every smooth positive measure on $T\Sigma$.

primaryStatements.name: A branch seed for every passing test
primaryStatements.label: test:branch-seed
primaryStatements.text: If $d\in\mathcal A(O,B)$, then there is $w\in O$ whose first runout from $\mathcal P_d$ is one of the two branches in Equation \eqref{test:runout}. After exchanging the optical labels and preparing the angular coordinates as in \cite[\CompanionRef{foundation}{in:label-swap}]{Foundation}, the branch can be written $u\to u_*<\infty$, $v\to\infty$. The seed is still the same initial seed in $O$.

primaryStatements.name: All-spin geometric interface
primaryStatements.label: bg:geometry
primaryStatements.text: There is a choice of $\epsilon>0$, depending only on the fixed Kerr center and the fixed preparation, such that every $p_{10}(d-d_*)<\epsilon$ in the stated smooth symbol class has the following properties. \begin{enumerate} \item The cylinder $\mathcal S$ in Proposition \ref{test:comparison} has a smooth vacuum development on the full product wedge $[0,\infty)_t\times\mathbb R_x\times\mathbb S^2$ in Equation \eqref{bg:wedge}. The quantities $\mathcal A^{\pm1},\gamma^{\pm1}$ are uniformly bounded in angular $H^6$, and $\xi_i,a^{-1}\partial_vb$ in angular $H^5$. There are nonnegative functions $g_i(y_i)$ with summable unit-cell suprema such that, in the indicated low angular norms, \begin{equation} \|\chi_i,\ell_i+\kappa\|_{H^4}\le C(q+g_i(y_i)), \qquad \|b\|_{H^5}\le C(q+g_0(u)). \end{equation} \item The following quantities are uniformly bounded, and tend to zero when $t,|u|,|v|\to\infty$: \begin{equation} \begin{gathered} \|b\|_{H^5}+\sum_i\|\chi_i,\ell_i+\kappa\|_{H^4},\\ \sum_{k=0}^1\left(\|\partial_{y_k}b\|_{H^2} +\sum_i\|\partial_{y_k}\chi_i, \partial_{y_k}\ell_i\|_{H^2}\right),\\ \sum_{k=0}^1\left(\|\partial_{y_k}\gamma\|_{H^4} +\|\partial_{y_k}\log a+\kappa\|_{H^4}\right). \end{gathered} \end{equation} In particular $D\log a,D\gamma,b,Db$ are uniformly bounded. \item For each fixed $U\in\mathbb R$, $C>0$, and finite order, all ordinary derivatives of \begin{equation} \gamma^{\pm1},\quad\log\mathcal A,\quad b, \quad a^{-1}\partial_vb \end{equation} are bounded by $e^{o(T)}$ on \begin{equation} t\ge0,\qquad y_d\le U,\qquad y_l\le CT, \qquad \{d,l\}=\{0,1\}. \end{equation} This includes every restriction and coordinate-path subsegment. Every fixed derivative of $a$, $\sqrt a$, or $\partial_vb$ retains, respectively, the factor $a$, $\sqrt a$, or $a$. \item Either branch can be put in the convention $v\to\infty$, $u\to u_*<\infty$. Exchanging the optical labels and preparing the angular coordinates anew preserves all these conclusions on the same product spacetime and initial cylinder. \end{enumerate} Only $p_{10}$ is required small; no higher seminorm, radiation coefficient, or curvature measured by a timelike observer is required small or bounded.

primaryStatements.name: Entry timing, escape, and flow estimates
primaryStatements.label: bg:exterior
primaryStatements.text:
On either prepared end use regular exterior time $t_e$, co-moving coordinates $y$, and lab coordinates $z=y+C_e(t_e)$, with fixed $\sup|C_e'|\le s_*<1/10$, after decreasing $\epsilon$ if needed. The relevant slice $t_e=0$ agrees with the original bridge sufficiently far out. There is a preparation parameter $I$ with $0<c_I\le I'\le C_I$ and $I(t_T)=T$. The launch patch near $v=x=T$ on $\mathcal S$ occurs at $t_e=t_T+O(1)$, and $t_T\asymp T$. A fixed enlargement is contained in $t_e\le t_T+C_2$. Its selected-end portion $v<(1-
u_0)T$ is earlier by at least $c
u_0T-O(1)$ for each fixed $
u_0>0$. The exterior metric has uniformly regular spacelike temporal levels. Its first and second ordinary lab derivatives are bounded on the computing region and become arbitrarily small at sufficiently large co-radius, uniformly in time. Every fixed mixed jet on the used time and radius ranges $O(1+T)$ is $e^{o(T)}$. Entry charts have a noncharacteristic collar with controlled low jets and subexponential fixed higher jets; the inner exit has a strict margin deeper than the entry cylinder. The null covectors $dv$ launched on a sufficiently small fixed patch at this entry escape towards the past to the same original end. For each fixed $ eta>0$, after fixing a sufficiently large radius and taking $T$ large, their bridge arrival points satisfy  egin{equation} (1- eta)t_T<|z-z_*|<(1+ eta)t_T, \qquad z_*=C_e(t_T). \end{equation} The entry crossing is unique and transverse, and separated from other used ray portions outside a uniform collar. Every fixed Hamiltonian flow jet, including launch-center derivatives and the propagators on all subsegments, is $e^{o(T)}$. Tensor parallel transport and its inverse are bounded. These assertions hold on short past and future launch enlargements through the deeper exit.

primaryStatements.name: Linear packet and exterior beam
primaryStatements.label: bg:packet
primaryStatements.text: Fix any finite list of output derivative orders, including an exterior base buffer $N_b$. For every fixed $\zeta>0$ and every subsequently prescribed inverse accuracy $M_1$, sufficiently high finite transport and Taylor orders yield a real interior tensor $h_T^p$ and a real exterior tensor $h_T^B$ with the following properties. Put \begin{equation} A_T=e^{-\alpha T},\qquad \alpha=7\kappa/8, \qquad\lambda_T=e^{\zeta T}. \end{equation} The interior field has the form \begin{equation} h_T^p=A_T\operatorname{tr.rev.}_g\operatorname{Re} \left(e^{i\lambda_Tv}\sum_{j=0}^{J}\lambda_T^{-j}p_j\right). \end{equation} Every fixed normalized coefficient jet of $p_j$ is $e^{o(T)}$. The field is supported in a fixed-width neighborhood of $v=T$, with angular support in the transported launch patch. Its relative array $q_T=(h_T^p(\hat e_\alpha,\hat e_\beta))$ satisfies \begin{equation} \|q_T\|_{C^N(\mathcal D_T)} \le A_T\lambda_T^N e^{o(T)} \end{equation} at each specified order. The tensor $p_0$ is trace-free and $p_0(L_0,\cdot)=0$. There is a purely angular $\gamma$-unit vector $X$ at $p_T$ for which \begin{equation} \sigma_T:=\left|\operatorname{Re} \bigl(e^{i\lambda_TT}p_0(X,X)\bigr)\right| \end{equation} has two-sided subexponential size. The $a$-scaled linear wave residual and $\sqrt a$-scaled linear gauge residual, in normalized slots and with all prescribed ordinary derivatives, are bounded by $A_T\lambda_T^{-M_1}e^{o(T)}$. In regular exterior lab components, \begin{equation} \|h_T^B\|_{C^{N_b}}\le A_T\lambda_T^{N_b+3/2}e^{o(T)}. \end{equation} Its linear wave and gauge residuals, and its difference from $h_T^p$ on the entry collar, have size $A_T\lambda_T^{-M_1}e^{o(T)}$ at all the prescribed finite orders. The latter assertion includes normal spacetime jets. On the original bridge its support lies in Equation \eqref{bg:arrival-shell} with arbitrarily thin tube margins. Increasing $M_1$ and the finite formal degrees does not increase the positive frequency powers in Equations \eqref{bg:packet-size} and \eqref{bg:beam-estimates}. Thresholds and subexponential constants may depend on those degrees.

definitions.name: Weighted constraint space
definitions.label: phase:space
definitions.text: For smooth symmetric two-tensors \(f,j\) set \begin{equation} p_m(f,j)=\sum_{i=0}^m \left\{\sup_\Sigma \rho^{1+i}|\nabla_*^if|_* +\sup_\Sigma \rho^{2+i}|\nabla_*^ij|_*\right\}, \qquad m=0,1,\ldots. \end{equation} Let \(\mathcal D\) consist of smooth pairs \(d=(h,K)\) such that \(h\) is positive definite and complete, every \(p_m(h-h_*,K-K_*)\) is finite, and \begin{equation} R(h)+(\tr_hK)^2-|K|_h^2=0,\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK-\dd(\tr_hK)=0. \end{equation} The topology on \(\mathcal D\) is the relative topology of the seminorms \eqref{phase:seminorms}. For \(\eps>0\) let \[ \mathcal U_\eps=\{d\in\mathcal D:p_{10}(d-d_*)<\eps\}, \qquad d_*=(h_*,K_*). \]

definitions.name: Future \(C^1\) extension
definitions.label: phase:extension
definitions.text: A future \(C^1\) extension of \(\mathcal M_d\) is a smooth, time-orientation-preserving isometric embedding \(\iota:\mathcal M_d\longrightarrow\widetilde{\mathcal M}\) onto a proper open subset of a connected, time-oriented smooth four-manifold with nondegenerate \(C^1\) Lorentzian metric \(\widetilde g\), together with a future-directed timelike \(C^1\) curve \(c:[0,1]\to\widetilde{\mathcal M}\) such that \[ c([0,1))\subset\iota(\mathcal M_d),\qquad c(1)\in\partial\iota(\mathcal M_d). \] Neither the vacuum equations nor global hyperbolicity are imposed on the ambient spacetime.

definitions.name: Passing test
definitions.label: test:definition
definitions.text: For $O\in\mathcal O$ and $B\in\mathbb N$, $B\ge1$, the set $\mathcal A(O,B)\subset\mathcal U$ consists of the data such that, for every $w\in O$, one has $T_d(w)\le B$ and, for every $0<\tau<T_d(w)$ and every piecewise smooth loop $\ell$ based at $\gamma_{d,w}(\tau)$ whose entire image is contained in $I^+_{\mathcal M_d}(\Sigma)$, \begin{equation} L(\ell)<B^{-1} \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \lVert P_\ell-\operatorname{Id}\rVert_{k_{d,w}(\tau)} \le B L(\ell). \end{equation}

definitions.name: Fixed-order subexponential bounds
definitions.label: bg:subexponential
definitions.text: The notation $Q_T\le e^{o(T)}$ means that, for every $\sigma>0$, $Q_T\le C_\sigma e^{\sigma T}$ for all sufficiently large $T$. The constants may depend on $d$, the fixed coordinate domains, and every fixed derivative and formal expansion order. A positive quantity has two-sided subexponential size if this holds for the quantity and its reciprocal. A finite product or sum of such bounds, including a factor polynomial in $T$, is again subexponential. No uniformity over unbounded derivative orders is intended.

primaryStatements.name: Local \(C^2\) strong cosmic censorship
primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: For every fixed \(M>0\) and \(0<\mathfrak a<M\), there exists \(\epsilon>0\) such that the data in \[ \mathcal U_\epsilon =\{d\in\mathcal D:p_{10}(d-(h_*,K_*))<\epsilon\} \] whose full maximal globally hyperbolic vacuum developments admit a \(C^2\) future extension form a meagre subset of \(\mathcal U_\epsilon\). Equivalently, the future-inextendible data contain a countable intersection of relatively open dense subsets of \(\mathcal U_\epsilon\).

primaryStatements.name: Actual-principal comparison
primaryStatements.label: co2:actual-comparison
primaryStatements.text: For each level $(U,s,A_i)$ in \eqref{co2:levels}, let $d_M^{\alpha\beta}$ be the change from $\bar g$ to $g$ of the differential order-two wave coefficient in stationary normalization. On fixed compact reaches the reduced equation has the form \begin{equation} \mathbf L_{p(t),c(t)}U+d_M^{\alpha\beta}\partial_{\alpha\beta}U =S_i^{\rm lin}+S_i^{\rm err},\qquad S_i^{\rm lin}=\pm Q(\partial_t)b_i,\qquad b_i=a,a,a', \end{equation} up to common normalizations, where \begin{equation} S_i^{\rm err}\in L^1_{A_i}H^{s-1}+L^2_{A_i}H^{s-1/2}, \qquad \|S_i^{\rm err}\|\le C_{\rm fix}\mathsf N^2 +C_{\rm fix}e_{\rm in}. \end{equation} On larger bounded differential annuli only $L^2_{A_i}H^{s-1}$ is required. There is an actual-principal correction of the frozen energy whose additional integrated derivative errors are bounded in squared estimates by $C_{\rm fix}\mathsf N^3$, up to input terms. The frozen half-loss bulk and directional improvement remain on the left side of that estimate.

primaryStatements.name: Regular-exit covering
primaryStatements.label: cat:regular-exit
primaryStatements.text: If \(d\in\mathcal U_\epsilon\) admits a \(C^2\) future extension, there exist \(O\in\mathscr O\) and \(N\geq1\) such that \(d\in A(O,N)\) and every seed in \(O\) reaches its finite MGHD endpoint on a regular ambient geodesic arc. Here regular means that position and unit tangent continue to and through the endpoint.

primaryStatements.name: Finite-observation criterion
primaryStatements.label: cat:destruction
primaryStatements.text: Suppose a single \(\epsilon>0\) has the following property. For every \(O\in\mathscr O\), \(N\geq1\), \(d\in\mathcal B(O,N)\), integer \(m\geq10\) and \(\eta>0\), there exist \(d'\in\mathcal U_\epsilon\), \(w'\in O\), and \(0\leq\tau<T_{d'}(w')\) such that \[ p_m(d'-d)<\eta,\qquad Q_{d'}(w',\tau)>N. \] Then \Cref{thm:main} holds for this \(\epsilon\).

primaryStatements.name: Normally hyperbolic trapping with escape
primaryStatements.label: geo:normal-hyperbolicity
primaryStatements.text: For each fixed subextremal Kerr metric, the energy-normalized photon trap is symplectically transverse of codimension two and has smooth local stable and unstable surfaces. Their normal expansion and contraction rates are bounded away from zero. All fixed-order tangent derivatives grow subexponentially, so the normal rates dominate the tangent dynamics at every fixed order. These properties hold on a sufficiently small interval of nearby levels of the separated fixed-frequency symbol. A departing radial tail escapes the radial trapping neighborhood and cannot return along a homoclinic orbit.

primaryStatements.name: An elliptic cone containing the projected trap
primaryStatements.label: geo:projected-ellipticity
primaryStatements.text: Choose $G'=1$ throughout the photon region. The union of the spatial projections of both trapped null sheets is contained, with a positive margin, in a spatial conic neighborhood $\mathcal T$ with compact base support separated from the horizon and from both spatial ends of the estimates. On this neighborhood, \begin{equation} b^{ij}(y)\eta_i\eta_j\geq c|\eta|^2 \end{equation} for some $c>0$ and any fixed auxiliary cotangent norm on the compact base support. Both temporal roots there are nonzero and have absolute values comparable to $|\eta|$. One can choose nested smaller and larger conic neighborhoods with these properties, and the same choices work after sufficiently small changes of exact Kerr parameters and stationary charts.

primaryStatements.name: Local spectral input
primaryStatements.label: st:hhv
primaryStatements.text: On the fixed subextremal Kerr cylinder there are arbitrarily small, stationary, smooth, compactly based bundle-map modifications of harmonic gauge and of its symmetric-gradient partner with these properties. \begin{enumerate} \item The stationary gauge-potential operator, obtained by applying the modified gauge to a pure Lie derivative, is invertible at decay strictly between the powers $1$ and $r^{-1}$. \item The modified linearized reduced vacuum operator has outgoing inversion at nonzero frequency in the closed physical half-plane. Its bounded-frequency estimates, with a weaker compact error, are uniform down to zero in the weight interval $-3/2<\ell<-1/2$. Its zero-frequency realization has index zero and a seven-dimensional kernel: four gauge-corrected Kerr variations and three translations. \item In outgoing time, a polynomial mode with coefficients of order $O(r^{-1+})$ has translation leading coefficient if its degree is one. There are no such modes of degree at least two. \end{enumerate} For tensors one may take $s>5/2$, with strict margin, also sufficient for gauge potentials. The uniform near-zero equation norm is $H_{\mathrm b}^{s-1,\ell+2}$. At nonzero frequency the outgoing conditions are $\ell<-1/2$ and $s+\ell>-1/2$.

primaryStatements.name: Stationary estimates
primaryStatements.label: st:stationary-estimates
primaryStatements.text: For sufficiently large $\Lambda$, the conically modified base operator has the following estimates. \begin{enumerate} \item Bounded-frequency estimates with weaker compact errors persist uniformly as $\Lambda\to\infty$, at the orders and zero-frequency weights of Proposition \ref{st:hhv}. The stationary index is zero, and kernel and cokernel are upper semicontinuous. On closed bounded bands excluding zero, the physical estimates persist without compact error, up to $\operatorname{Re}\zeta\downarrow0$. \item For every fixed strip $0\leq\operatorname{Re}\zeta\leq D_*$ and fixed admissible order, there are polynomial high-frequency bounds without kernel, with threshold independent of sufficiently large $\Lambda$. These include the compact $H^s$ estimate from $H^{s-1}$, for $s=5$ or a fixed higher admissible order, the supported dual solution estimate of order $1-s$, and \[ \langle r\rangle^{-1/2-\iota}(v,\partial_yv)\in L^2 \] for the physical transpose with a compact smooth source, with polynomial frequency cost. \item Zero-frequency estimates, including those for gauge potentials, persist uniformly for nearby exact Kerr principal metrics in smooth stationary, asymptotically affine charts of the prescribed type. Fixed smooth finite-dimensional supplements remove their kernel and cokernel locally in parameters. \end{enumerate} The same-sign outgoing transpose has the a priori estimate and index stated in Lemma \ref{st:transpose}.

definitions.name: Future extension
definitions.label: intro:extension
definitions.text: A \(C^2\) future extension of \((M_d,g_d)\) is a connected time-oriented smooth four-manifold \(\widetilde M\) with a nondegenerate \(C^2\) Lorentzian metric \(\widetilde g\), and a smooth time-orientation-preserving isometric embedding \(\iota:M_d\longrightarrow\widetilde M\) onto a proper open subset, such that a future-directed timelike \(C^1\) curve \(c:[0,1]\longrightarrow\widetilde M\) satisfies \[ c([0,1))\subset\iota(M_d),\qquad c(1)\in\partial\iota(M_d). \]

papers.title: A two-dimensional area law from a global spectral gap
papers.abstract: We prove an entropy area law for the unique ground state of a finite-range Hamiltonian on any finite induced subgraph of the square lattice. A lower bound on the spectral gap of the full Hamiltonian and fixed bounds on the local dimension, interaction range, and interaction strength suffice. For every set of sites, its entanglement entropy is bounded by a constant times the number of edges crossing its boundary, independently of the size and shape of the domain.
papers.familySummary: Proves an entropy area law for unique ground states of finite-range Hamiltonians on arbitrary finite induced square-lattice domains, using only a uniform full-system spectral gap and bounds on the local interactions. On open $L\times L$ squares, uniformly gapped nearest-neighbor ground states also admit projected entangled-pair state approximations with polynomial bond dimension and global vector error at most L−1.

primaryStatements.name: Area law
primaryStatements.label: thm:area
primaryStatements.text: For every $q,R,J$ as above and every $\Delta>0$, there is a finite constant $C=C(q,R,J,\Delta)$ with the following property. Suppose that $\Lambda$ is a finite induced square-lattice domain and that the Hamiltonian \eqref{eq:hamiltonian} has a unique normalized ground vector $\Omega$, up to phase, with ground energy $E_0$, and satisfies \[ H-E_0\id\ \ge\ \Delta\bigl(\id-\ket{\Omega}\bra{\Omega}\bigr). \] Then for every $A\subseteq\Lambda$, \begin{equation} S_\Omega(A)\le C\,|\partial_\Lambda A|. \end{equation} The same constant applies to all such domains, sets, and Hamiltonians.

primaryStatements.label: cor:rectangles
primaryStatements.text: The conclusion of Theorem \ref{thm:area} holds for every subset of a finite rectangular square lattice with bounded on-site and nearest-neighbor interactions and a unique ground state separated by a fixed global gap. For every domain covered by that theorem it also implies \[ S_\Omega(A)\le4C|\partial_{\rm in}A|, \qquad S_\Omega(A)\le2C|Z_A|. \]

primaryStatements.name: Initial safe-box estimate
primaryStatements.label: prop:initial-box
primaryStatements.text: There are constants $C<\infty$ and $e_0\in(0,1)$, depending only on $q,R,J,\Delta$, such that \begin{equation} F_{\mathrm{box}}(r)\le Cr^{1+e_0}\qquad(r\ge1). \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Positive replacement of the Hamiltonian
primaryStatements.label: prop:positive
primaryStatements.text: Suppose $H\Omega=E_0\Omega$, $\|\Omega\|=1$, and \[ H-E_0I\ge\Delta(I-P_\Omega),\qquad P_\Omega=|\Omega\rangle\langle\Omega|. \] For each integer $p\ge1$ and $\alpha=p/(p+1)$, there are operators $k_i$, indexed by the original supports and retaining their anchors, and a constant $c_*>0$ such that \begin{equation} 0\le k_i\le I,\qquad k_i\Omega=0,\qquad H_F:=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}k_i \ge c_*^{-1}(H-E_0I)\ge g(I-P_\Omega), \qquad g:=\Delta/c_*. \end{equation} Thus $H_F$ has the unique ground vector $\Omega$, ground energy zero, and gap at least $g$. Furthermore, \begin{equation} k_{i,l}:=E_{i,l}(k_i)\in[0,I],\qquad \|k_i-k_{i,l}\|\le Ce^{-cl^\alpha} \quad(l\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}). \end{equation} Each $k_i$ is supported in the connected component containing $a_i$.

primaryStatements.name: Truncation near a finite set
primaryStatements.label: prop:truncation
primaryStatements.text: Use Proposition \ref{prop:positive} with $p=1$, so $\alpha=1/2$. Fix $C_0>0$. There is a constant $C_1$, depending only on $q,R,J,\Delta,C_0$, with the following property for every real $n\ge2$ and every nonempty $S_0\subseteq\Lambda$ with $|S_0|\le C_0n^2$. Put $r_0=\lceil C_1(\log n)^2\rceil$. If $d_i^0:=d_\Lambda(a_i,S_0)<\infty$, define \begin{equation} r_i=\max\{r_0,\lfloor d_i^0/2\rfloor\},\qquad \widetilde h_i=k_{i,r_i},\qquad \widetilde X_i=N_{r_i}(a_i). \end{equation} If $d_i^0=\infty$, set $\widetilde h_i=k_i$ and designate its anchor's entire component as $\widetilde X_i$. Then $\widetilde H=\sum_i\widetilde h_i$ is a sum of positive contractions and \begin{equation} \|\widetilde H-H_F\|\le\epsilon_n, \qquad \epsilon_n:=\min\{n^{-1000},g/4\}. \end{equation} Its ground energy $\widetilde E_0$ lies in $[0,\epsilon_n]$, its ground vector $\widetilde\Omega$ is unique, and its gap is at least $g/2$. After a choice of phase, \begin{equation} \|\widetilde\Omega-\Omega\|\le2\sqrt{\epsilon_n/g},\qquad \frac12\big\||\widetilde\Omega\rangle\langle\widetilde\Omega| -P_\Omega\big\|_1\le\sqrt{2\epsilon_n/g}. \end{equation} For a set $X\subseteq S_0$, let $b_X=|\partial_\Lambda X|$ and let $\mathcal C_X$ be the labels whose designated supports $\widetilde X_i$ meet both $X$ and $\Lambda\setminus X$. Every such support has radius exactly $r_0$, and \begin{equation} |\mathcal C_X|\le Cb_X(r_0+1)^2,\qquad \log d_i\le C(r_0+1)^2\quad(i\in\mathcal C_X),\qquad d_i:=q^{|\widetilde X_i|}. \end{equation} Consequently the cut parameter \begin{equation} \mathcal B_X:=1+\sum_{i\in\mathcal C_X}\log^2(e d_i) \le C(1+b_X)(r_0+1)^6. \end{equation} In particular, $b_X\le C_2nD$ and $D\ge1$ imply $\mathcal B_X\le CnD(\log n)^{12}$, with the constant also depending on $C_2$.

primaryStatements.label: prop:transport
primaryStatements.text:
Fix a finite one-copy space, history and conditional choice trees, partitions, cross-band commutation, positive parameter $a$, and positive contractions with designated supports as specified above. Let $\ell$ bound the logarithmic dimensions of every transferred subsystem and every designated support $D_i$ for which $\mathcal J_i

Write $\sigma_{h,u}$ for the state at $j=(h,\mathrm{old})$, and put $C_h=A_h^{-1/2}B_hA_h^{-1/2}$. Then  egin{equation} -\partial_p\log N(p)^2 =\sum_h w_h\int_{\R}m_s(u)\Tr(\sigma_{h,u}\log C_h)\,du. \end{equation} There is $ eta_k=O_{\mathrm{fixed}}(\log(k+1))$, independent of $p$ and $\mathrm{pre}$, such that  egin{align} -\partial_p\log N(p)^2 \geq{}&ka\sum_{h,g}w_h\int_{\R}m_s(u) \int\sum_{c\in\mathcal C_h}q_{c\mid h} \eta_{h,c,g}(	heta)\,d\mu_{\sigma_{h,u}}(	heta)\,du

The constants $C$ and the exponents denoted by $C$ in \eqref{transport:entropy-gain} and \eqref{transport:energy} are universal; support dimensions enter those coefficients only through $\ell$. primaryStatements.name: Upper and lower norm comparisons
primaryStatements.label: prop:comparators
primaryStatements.text: Fix the positive gapped Hamiltonian and physical target $X$ above, a finite collection of status partitions satisfying \eqref{comparator:nesting}, a typical Schmidt set satisfying \eqref{comparator:typical-set}, and a mean tree with metrics \eqref{comparator:metrics}. There is a sequence of common auxiliary labels $\lambda_k$ and nonzero vectors \begin{equation} \mathrm{pre}_k=\pi_R^{\lambda_k} (\widetilde\Omega\otimes\mathrm{Bell}_{CR})^{\otimes k} \in\mathcal S_k, \qquad \|\mathrm{pre}_k\|\le1, \end{equation} Here $\pi_R^{\lambda_k}$ is the Schur-label projection on the $R$ copies. These vectors are physical mean-energy eigenvectors of eigenvalue $\widetilde E_0$ and have label $\lambda_k$ on both $C$ and $R$. For every tree above, set \[ N=\|\mathcal M^{-s}\mathrm{pre}_k\|, \qquad v=\mathcal M^{-s}\mathrm{pre}_k/N, \qquad E_{\mathrm{def}}= \frac{\langle v,\overline{\widetilde H}v\rangle-\widetilde E_0} {\widetilde g}, \qquad \overline{\widetilde H}=\frac1k\sum_{i=1}^k\widetilde H^{(i)}. \] Rough comparisons. For $0<\tau<1/2$, the upper bound below uses the prefix data \eqref{comparator:prefix-data}: \begin{align} -\frac{\log N^2}{k} &\le 2\log d_*-\log z+ 2sW\left(\frac{2B_{\mathrm{sh}}}{z}+2B_{\mathrm{exc}}\right) +o_k(1), \\ -\frac{\log N^2}{k} &\ge 2sW\left[ 2S'-C\left(\tau\log d_*+\frac{h(\tau)}a\right) -C\frac{E_{\mathrm{def}}}{\tau}S'\right]-o_k(1). \end{align} Here $h$ is binary entropy. The lower bound does not require \eqref{comparator:prefix-data} or \eqref{comparator:mgf-data}. Sharp comparisons. If \eqref{comparator:mgf-data} holds and $a\le c/\sqrt{\mathcal B}$, with $c$ sufficiently small in terms of $c_0$, define \begin{align*} g_{j,g}^{\mathrm{pre}} &=S(XU_{j,g})+S(V_{j,g})-S(Y_{j,g}),\\ g_{j,g}^{\mathrm{post}} &=S(U_{j,g})+S(U_{j,g}Y_{j,g})-S(Y_{j,g}), \qquad g_{\max}=\max_{j,g}g_{j,g}^{\mathrm{pre}}. \end{align*} Then $g_{j,g}^{\mathrm{pre}}\ge0$, and the sharp comparisons are \begin{align} -\frac{\log N^2}{k} &\le 2\log d_*-\log z+ 2sW\left[\langle g^{\mathrm{post}}\rangle_{\mathrm{av}} +C\left(a\mathcal B+\frac{|\log z|}{a}\right)\right] +o_k(1), \\ -\frac{\log N^2}{k} &\ge 2sW\left[2S'+(1-\tau) \langle g^{\mathrm{pre}}\rangle_{\mathrm{av}} -C\left(\tau\log d_*+\frac{h(\tau)}a+a\mathcal B\right) -C\frac{E_{\mathrm{def}}}{\tau}(S'+g_{\max})\right] -o_k(1). \end{align} The upper sharp bound does not require \eqref{comparator:prefix-data}. For every physical partition there is the exact identity \begin{equation} 2S_X+g_{j,g}^{\mathrm{pre}}-g_{j,g}^{\mathrm{post}} =I(X:V_{j,g})+I(X:Y_{j,g}V_{j,g}). \end{equation} All replica limits are taken with the physical system, auxiliary dimensions, finite status collection and tree, $a$, and $\tau$ fixed. The errors are uniform over terminal probabilities, including their dependence on $k$, and over the symmetric vectors to which the lower comparison is applied. Constants or degrees in intermediate polynomial factors in $k$ may depend on the fixed entire system. They disappear in $o_k(1)$. The displayed constants in the rough bounds are universal; those in the sharp bounds may also depend on $C_0,c_0$. None has additional dependence on the system dimensions.

primaryStatements.name: The scanner estimate
primaryStatements.label: prop:scanner
primaryStatements.text: Assume \eqref{scanner:scales} and \eqref{scanner:test-geometry}, and let \(0<e<1\) satisfy \(\kappa\le e\). Suppose \begin{equation} S_\Omega(X)\le C_e n^{1+e},\qquad S_\Omega(Q_j)\le C_e(nL^e+n)\quad(0\le j\le L). \end{equation} Let \(\epsilon=n^{-\nu}\), where \(\nu>0\) is fixed, and suppose \(a r_0^2\) is sufficiently small. Construct the auxiliary systems, the fixed label sector, and the unnormalized vector \(\mathrm{pre}\) as in Proposition \ref{prop:comparators}, using typical width \(w=n^{3/5}\). For each sufficiently large replica count \(k\), there are a charge round and a common parameter \(p_k\in[\epsilon/2,\epsilon]\) at which the normalized vector \(v_k=\mathcal M^{-s}\mathrm{pre}/N\), \(s=1/4\), has defect energy \[ E_{{\rm def},k} =\frac{\langle v_k,\overline{\widetilde H}v_k\rangle -\widetilde E_0}{\widetilde g} \] bounded by \begin{equation} E_{{\rm def},k} \le Cn^\ell D^2W^2(\log n)^C \bigl(\delta_n^{1/8}+\epsilon+n^{-100}\bigr) +Cn^{-1000}+o_k(1), \end{equation} where \begin{equation} \delta_n=C_e\epsilon^{-1} \bigl(n^{e-\mu}+a^{1/4}(\log n)^C\bigr). \end{equation} Here \(\overline{\widetilde H}\) is the mean of the physical Hamiltonian over the copies. All norm comparisons of Proposition \ref{prop:comparators} apply at the selected points, with shell entropy bound \(B_{\rm sh}\le C_e(nL^e+n)\), mismatch \(B_{\rm exc}\le CnD\), and marginal parameter \(\mathcal B\le CnD(\log n)^C\). The sharp comparisons additionally require their stated condition on \(a\sqrt{\mathcal B}\). The entire finite physical system, \(n\), the scan, and all auxiliary dimensions are fixed before \(k\to\infty\). The remainder is uniform over the selected round and parameter, although these may depend on \(k\). Constants may depend on the fixed exponents and the input constant \(C_e\).

definitions.name: A template
definitions.label: scanner:template
definitions.text: Let \(s_0\ge1\) and \(n\) be positive integers. A template with parameters \((n,s_0)\) is a nonempty finite set \(T\subset\Z^2\) of the form \[ T=\bigcup_{a=1}^{N_0}(P_a\cap\Z^2), \qquad n\ge C_{\rm tpl}N_0(s_0+1), \qquad \diam_\infty T\le n, \] where \(N_0\ge1\) is an integer and each \(P_a\) is a closed convex rectangle or triangle of sup-norm diameter at most \(s_0\), all of whose sides have slope \(0,\infty,1\), or \(-1\). Empty sampled pieces can be omitted. For the fixed cut \(A\), the template is separated from the cut if \[ \dist_\infty(T,Z)>4D_0s_0. \] As above, \(T_j\) is the ambient integer dilation, \(X=A\cap T\), and \(Q_j=A\cap(T_j\setminus T)\), for \(j\ge0\).

papers.title: Polynomial PEPS approximation of gapped square-grid ground states
papers.abstract: We prove that the unique ground state of a uniformly gapped nearest-neighbor Hamiltonian on an $L\times L$ square lattice admits a projected entangled-pair state approximation with bond dimension polynomial in L and global vector error at most L−1 after normalization. Only the gap of the full Hamiltonian is assumed. The result is an existence theorem, with constants uniform over Hamiltonians of fixed local dimension, interaction strength, and gap.
papers.familySummary: Proves an entropy area law for unique ground states of finite-range Hamiltonians on arbitrary finite induced square-lattice domains, using only a uniform full-system spectral gap and bounds on the local interactions. On open $L\times L$ squares, uniformly gapped nearest-neighbor ground states also admit projected entangled-pair state approximations with polynomial bond dimension and global vector error at most L−1.

primaryStatements.name: Entropy area law, {\cite[Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2
primaryStatements.label: prop:area-law
primaryStatements.text: {RepoAreaLaw}}] Under \eqref{eq:model}--\eqref{eq:global-gap}, there is $C_A=C_A(q,J,\Delta)$ such that every $A\subseteq\Lambda$ satisfies \[ S_\Omega(A)\le C_A|\partial_\Lambda A|, \qquad \partial_\Lambda A=\{\{x,y\}\in E(\Lambda):x\in A, \ y\notin A\}. \] The same constant works for every $L$ and every Hamiltonian in the class.

primaryStatements.name: Coarse information outside a sublinear collar
primaryStatements.label: prop:coarse
primaryStatements.text: Fix an integer $N_0\ge1$ and a constant $A_0\ge1$. There are $\beta<1$, $C<\infty$, and $u_0<\infty$ such that the following holds. Let $u\ge u_0$ and let $T$ be the full ambient lattice sample of a union of at most $N_0$ axis-parallel rectangles, with $\diam_\infty T\le A_0u$. For every physical set $E\subseteq\Lambda$ satisfying \[ \dist_\infty(E,T)>u^\beta, \] one has \[ I_\Omega(\Lambda\cap T:E)\le C. \] The same statement holds for any subset of $\Lambda\cap T$ in its first argument, for rectangles with consistently assigned open or closed sides, and after a common translation of the lattice coordinates.

primaryStatements.name: Information under angular separation
primaryStatements.label: prop:angular
primaryStatements.text: Fix $a>0$, $A_0\ge1$, an integer $m_0\ge0$, and $p>0$. There is $D<\infty$ such that the following holds for all sufficiently large $L$. Let $\mathcal V$ be a set of at most $m_0$ marked points in the plane, let $X,E\subseteq\Lambda$ be disjoint, and let \[ D\log L\le n\le A_0L, \qquad \diam_\infty X\le A_0n. \] Put $s_{\min}=D\log L$ and $d_{\mathcal V}(x)=\min_{v\in\mathcal V}|x-v|_\infty$, with $d_{\varnothing}=+\infty$. Suppose that for every $x\in X$, \begin{equation} \dist_\infty(x,E) \ge a\max\{s_{\min},\min(n,d_{\mathcal V}(x))\}. \end{equation} Then \[ I_\Omega(X:E)\le L^{-p}. \] The constant $D$ and the scale threshold are uniform in the marked points, physical sets, and Hamiltonian.

primaryStatements.name: Adaptive patch constraint
primaryStatements.label: prop:patch
primaryStatements.text: Fix \(B_0>0\) and \(p>0\). There are constants \(C,c>0\), depending only on \(q,J,\Delta,B_0,p\), with the following property. For every \(L\geq2\), center \(z\in\mathbb R^2\), and \(0<u\leq B_0\log L\), there is an orthogonal projection \(P\), supported on \(X(2u)\), such that \[ \norm{(\id-P)\Omega}\leq L^{-p}. \] There are radii \(u\leq r_1\leq\cdots\leq r_m\leq2u\), sets \(X_j=X(r_j)\), and unit vectors \(v_{j\ell}\in\mathcal H_{X_j}\), \(1\leq\ell\leq d_j\), for which \begin{equation} P=\sum_{j=1}^m\sum_{\ell=1}^{d_j} \lvert v_{j\ell}\rangle\langle v_{j\ell}\rvert_{X_j} \otimes\id_{\Lambda\setminus X_j}, \qquad \sum_{j=1}^m d_j\leq C L^c. \end{equation} All the summands in \eqref{eq:patch-cylinder-projection} have pairwise orthogonal ranges as operators on \(\mathcal H_\Lambda\). No bound on the internal tensor complexity of the individual \(v_{j\ell}\) is asserted.

primaryStatements.name: Distributed density compression
primaryStatements.label: thm:compression
primaryStatements.text: Consider a family of distributed constructions indexed by $L\ge2$ with the following uniform properties. \begin{enumerate} \item The number of parties and gates is uniformly polynomial. The initial vector is a tensor product of normalized private vectors, one at each party, and every gate is a contraction. \item There is a constant $b$ such that each nonprivate gate involves at most $b$ parties, and each party participates in at most $b$ nonprivate gates over the entire construction. \item Each nonprivate gate is a sum of uniformly polynomially many allowed monomials with uniformly polynomially bounded scalar coefficients. There is a constant $r$ bounding the number of pair sources, pair effects, and polynomial-dimensional messages in each monomial. All constituent local maps are contractions. \item At the end, the intended physical output space of each party has uniformly polynomial dimension. All other registers are traced out party by party. \end{enumerate} Write $\rho$ for the resulting physical output density operator; it is positive and may have trace less than one. For every fixed $p>0$, there is an operator tensor network $\sigma$ satisfying \[ \norm{\sigma-\rho}_1\le L^{-p}. \] It has one node per party, a bounded number of incident virtual links at each node, and uniformly polynomial link dimensions. Every link joins two parties which participate in a common nonprivate gate of the original construction. The physical legs at a node are the ket and bra legs of that party's intended output. The constants in these bounds depend only on $p$ and the fixed uniform data in the assumptions, including $b,r$ and the polynomial bounds, and not on private dimensions or source Schmidt ranks. The same conclusion holds if the gate expansions in the third assumption are available to every fixed inverse-polynomial operator-norm accuracy, with uniform polynomial bounds at each fixed accuracy.

primaryStatements.name: Distribution through a dyadic hierarchy
primaryStatements.label: prop:protocol
primaryStatements.text: For all sufficiently large $L$, there is a protocol with the following properties. All constants in this statement are uniform in the Hamiltonian and $L$. \begin{enumerate} \item There are $O(L^2)$ parties, one for each square in a padded dyadic hierarchy and at most a fixed number of additional parties for each repainting of a square. Initialization is a pure product across parties. One party initially holds the main copy of $\Omega$; all auxiliary copies are initialized privately at their designated parties. \item The schedule has at most $C L^3$ changes. Each change is implemented by a fixed number of contraction gates involving at most a fixed number of parties and having the bipartite-resource expansions established in Lemmas \ref{lem:small-rewrite}, \ref{lem:birth}, and \ref{lem:exchange}. The expansions can be made accurate to any fixed inverse power of $L$ in operator norm where an approximation is needed. Each party participates in at most a fixed number of gates involving other parties over its entire lifetime. \item Every linked gate involves parties at the same or adjacent dyadic scales. Parties at a gate have addresses at distance $O(n)$ from one another, where $n$ is either endpoint scale; additional parties have the scale and address of the square to whose repainting they belong. \item There is a designated reference vector at every stage, formed from the main encoded frame and the auxiliary encoded frames. All its factors have norm at most one. Each change takes its preceding reference vector within $C L^{-20}$ in vector norm of its following reference vector. At the end, the reference is \[ \Omega\otimes\Xi, \qquad 1-C L^{3-60}\le \norm{\Xi}\le1, \] where $\Xi$ contains only registers to be discarded. Every original physical site is a raw register at its own unit-square party. No other party has a physical output, so every party's physical output dimension is at most $q$. \end{enumerate}

definitions.name: Encoded frame
definitions.label: def:frame
definitions.text: An encoded frame $\mathcal F$ consists of a raw ownership assignment on one sheet, a collection of holes $(c,h)$ with pairwise disjoint outer squares, and a specified party holding each hole's tag. Its encoding $K_{\mathcal F}$ is the product of the maps \eqref{eq:hole-encoder}, with a fixed ordering of the newly appended tags, and its reference vector is \begin{equation} \Omega_{\mathcal F}=K_{\mathcal F}\Omega. \end{equation} A frame without holes is a raw sheet. An ownership guide in the plane specifies such an assignment by sampling its labels at the physical sites.

papers.title: The maximum number of mutually unbiased bases in dimension six
papers.abstract: We prove that the maximum number of mutually unbiased orthonormal bases in ℂ6 is three, resolving Zauner's dimension-six MUB conjecture. The upper bound is computer-assisted: under the stated binary64 arithmetic and compiler conditions, a complete execution of the documented verification pipeline excludes four arbitrary complex bases.

The exclusion is a complete certified computation under the stated binary64 arithmetic and compiler conditions. An independent companion proves the Matolcsi–Ruzsa–Weiner Fourier-vanishing conjecture for order-six complex Hadamard matrices outside Tao's cubic equivalence class.

primaryStatements.text: Under the arithmetic and compiler conditions in Appendix \ref{sec:rounding}, the fresh complete execution documented in Section \ref{execute:observed} certifies that there are no four pairwise mutually unbiased orthonormal bases in $\C^6$. Consequently, $N(6)=3$.

primaryStatements.name: Exhaustive seed cover
primaryStatements.label: seed:cover
primaryStatements.text: For a completed execution of the specified \texttt{covout} traversal under the arithmetic conditions of Section \ref{sec:rounding}, the written rational midpoint centers, each with its recorded selected position, cover the seed coordinates of every exact complex Hadamard matrix up to the equivalences of Lemma \ref{seed:equivalences}, by closed Euclidean balls of radius $0.032$. After the indicated column ordering and conversion of the centers to binary phase values, radius $0.0320001$ is sufficient.

primaryStatements.name: Dual certificates
primaryStatements.label: completion:dual-certificates
primaryStatements.text: A cell contains no feasible completion if \eqref{completion:norm-test} fails, or if some real direction $y$ violates \eqref{completion:directional-test}. The choice of $y$ may be heuristic; only its final inequality must be certified. Positive normalization of $y$ preserves the certificate.

primaryStatements.name: Completion coverage conditional on successful termination
primaryStatements.label: completion:recursion
primaryStatements.text: Fix a seed ball for which the frame and bound constructions are certified. Suppose that every final unitary cell is either excluded by a certified necessary-condition test or covered by a certified phase ball as in Section \ref{sec:phase-cover}. Then those phase balls cover all feasible Hadamard completions of the seed ball, with the equivalences specified by the phase-ball certificates. The Stage A recursion establishes precisely this conclusion if it terminates with zero unresolved cells.

primaryStatements.name: Sufficient conditions for a Root certificate
primaryStatements.label: phase:root-bounds
primaryStatements.text: Let \(P,T\) and the nonnegative constants be as in Definition \ref{phase:root-data}. Suppose the basic bounds \eqref{phase:root-basic} hold and an auxiliary stored real \(36\)-by-\(30\) matrix \(M\) satisfies \begin{equation} \|M\|\leq\mathtt{mnorm},\qquad \mathtt{mnorm}\,\mathtt{froot}\leq\mathtt{n0},\qquad \|\Pi-TT^*-ML_P\Pi\|\leq\mathtt{id}, \end{equation} and \(\mathtt C\) is an upper bound for a remainder constant \(\pi b\) in Lemma \ref{phase:remainder}. Then these data form a certified Root.

primaryStatements.name: Certificates produced by the source
primaryStatements.label: phase:stored-root-certificate
primaryStatements.text: A successful call to \texttt{buildH::patch}, under the arithmetic conditions of Section \ref{sec:rounding}, certifies \eqref{phase:root-basic}, \eqref{phase:projector-certificate}, and a valid remainder constant \(\mathtt C\). Therefore it produces certified Root data in the sense of Definition \ref{phase:root-data}.

primaryStatements.name: Finite improvement of a certified radius
primaryStatements.label: phase:bootstrap
primaryStatements.text: Suppose \(s_0\geq\|\delta\|\) and \(t_0\geq\|T^*\delta\|\) for every feasible solution in a completion cell, using the particular alignment \eqref{phase:delta}. Starting with any such upper \(s\), a further upper is \begin{equation} \left(n_P(s)^2+(1+\mathtt{ort})t_0^2\right)^{1/2}. \end{equation} Replacing \(s\) by this number only when it decreases \(s\), and stopping after any finite number of steps, preserves coverage of every feasible solution in the cell.

definitions.label: seed:extendibility
definitions.text: A matrix $H\in\mathbb C^{6\times6}$ is a complex Hadamard matrix here if every entry has modulus one and $HH^*=6I$. It is extendible if the standard basis and the columns of $H/\sqrt6$ belong to a family of four mutually unbiased orthonormal bases.

definitions.name: Root certificate
definitions.label: phase:root-data
definitions.text: A \texttt{Root} consists of a stored real center \(P\), a stored real \(36\)-by-\(k\) matrix \(T\), and nonnegative constants \[ \mathtt{C},\quad \mathtt{n0},\quad \mathtt{id},\quad \mathtt{ort},\quad \mathtt{hor},\quad \mathtt{mnorm},\quad \mathtt{froot}. \] The source stores column \(a\) of \(T\) as \texttt{T[a]} and uses \(0\leq k\leq10\). Write \begin{equation} n_P(s)=\mathtt{n0}+\mathtt{id}\,s+\mathtt{C}\,s^2, \qquad s\geq0. \end{equation} It is certified if the basic bounds \begin{equation} \|T^*T-I\|\leq\mathtt{ort},\qquad \|(I-\Pi)T\|\leq\mathtt{hor},\qquad \|F(P)\|\leq\mathtt{froot} \end{equation} hold, together with the following displacement assertions. For every horizontal \(\delta\) satisfying \(F(P+\delta)=0\), put \(\eta=T^*\delta\) and \(s=\|\delta\|\). Then \begin{align} \|(I-TT^*)\delta\|&\leq n_P(s), \\ s^2&\leq(1+\mathtt{ort})\|\eta\|^2+ \|(I-TT^*)\delta\|^2. \end{align} For every such \(\delta\) and every horizontal \(v\), with \(h'=\delta-v\), one also has \begin{equation} \|(I-TT^*)h'\| \leq\bigl[\mathtt{id}+\mathtt C(\|\delta\|+\|v\|)\bigr]\|h'\| +\mathtt{mnorm}\,\|F(P+v)\|. \end{equation} These assertions have no radius restriction. A Root certificate neither requires \(F(P)=0\) nor asserts the existence of an exact solution. A radius will be attached when a phase ball is recorded.

definitions.name: Record and its covered solution set
definitions.label: phase:record
definitions.text: A \texttt{Record} is a certified Root with a nonnegative radius \(r\). Its solution set consists of matrices \(e(P+\delta)\) with \(\delta\) horizontal, \(\|\delta\|\leq r\), and \(F(P+\delta)=0\). Coverage by Records may be up to the extendibility-preserving equivalences of Lemma \ref{phase:transport}; the chosen equivalence may differ for different assignments. The term sphere in the source includes the interior and boundary of this closed ball.

lean.scopeText:
The paper claims that at most three mutually unbiased orthonormal bases exist in $\mathbb C^6$. The linked formalization proves a weaker family bound: every family in its mutually unbiased bases model has at most five members. It also proves a Fourier character-sum vanishing statement for order-six complex Hadamard matrices not equivalent to the Tao matrix, uniformly over coordinate permutations.

The selected statement does not establish the paper's upper bound of three or its computer-assisted exclusion of four arbitrary bases.

The linked formalization proves a cancellation lemma used in the order-six complex Hadamard analysis. Let $H$ and its entrywise square both be complex Hadamard matrices, and fix two distinct rows. If the cubes of their six entrywise ratios take only two distinct values, then the sum of the row-ratio terms over either specified cube fiber is zero.

This is a supporting Fourier cancellation statement. The paper's full character-sum vanishing theorem and its mutually unbiased bases bound are outside this selected statement.

papers.title: Exact Fourier certificates for complex Hadamard matrices of order six
papers.abstract: We prove the Fourier-vanishing conjecture of Matolcsi, Ruzsa, and Weiner: every complex Hadamard matrix of order six outside Tao's cubic equivalence class has a vanishing character sum at every permutation of $(1,1,1,-1,-1,-1)$. We also give an exact certificate excluding seven mutually unbiased bases in ℂ6; by Weiner's completion theorem, this yields an upper bound of five. Both certificates use only integer and rational arithmetic, and the complete verifier is included.

An independent companion proves the Matolcsi–Ruzsa–Weiner Fourier-vanishing conjecture for order-six complex Hadamard matrices outside Tao's cubic equivalence class.

primaryStatements.name: Fourier vanishing
primaryStatements.label: thm:fourier
primaryStatements.text: Let $H$ be a complex Hadamard matrix of order six. If $H$ is not equivalent to the cubic matrix $T$ in \eqref{eq:cubic-matrix}, then \[ g_H(\pi\alpha)=0\qquad\text{for every coordinate permutation }\pi. \]

primaryStatements.name: Dichotomy
primaryStatements.label: cor:dichotomy
primaryStatements.text: For every $6\times6$ Hadamard matrix $H$, at least one of the following conditions holds: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\Alph*)},ref=\Alph*] \item[(M)] $g_{H^\pi}(\alpha)=0$ for every row permutation $\pi$; \item[(C)] the entrywise square $H^{\circ2}$ is a Hadamard matrix. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.name: Single-matrix certificate
primaryStatements.label: prop:pair-certificate
primaryStatements.text: For every $6\times6$ Hadamard matrix $H$ and for each $q\in\{q_{\mathrm{cross}},q_{\mathrm{same}}\}$, \begin{equation} 3\bigl\langle |L_{\widetilde H}|^2\bigr\rangle_H +\left\langle |g_{\widetilde H}(\alpha)g_{\widetilde H}(q)|^2 \right\rangle_H=0. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Classification of the cubic alternative
primaryStatements.label: prop:cubic-classification
primaryStatements.text: Suppose that $H$ and its entrywise square $H^{\circ2}$ are Hadamard matrices of order six. By multiplying rows and columns by unit complex numbers and permuting rows and columns, one can transform $H$ into the matrix $T$ in \eqref{eq:cubic-matrix}. In particular, every entry of the transformed matrix is a cube root of unity.

primaryStatements.label: prop:cubic-exclusion
primaryStatements.text: In a set of seven mutually unbiased bases in $\C^6$, no transition Hadamard matrix $H$ can have $H^{\circ2}$ Hadamard.

primaryStatements.name: Mixed-moment certificate
primaryStatements.label: prop:mixed-certificate
primaryStatements.text: Each matrix $Z_\lambda$ specified above is positive definite. papers.title: Bose–Einstein condensation at positive temperature in the dilute hard-sphere gas
papers.abstract: We prove Bose–Einstein condensation at positive temperature in the three-dimensional dilute hard-sphere gas. For each fixed exclusion distance and every sufficiently small fixed density, there is a strictly positive temperature, independent of the volume, at which the exact canonical Gibbs state has a positive condensate fraction in the thermodynamic limit. The condensate occupies the constant orbital.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: For every $a>0$, there is $\rho_*(a)>0$ such that for each fixed $0<\rho<\rho_*(a)$ there is a fixed temperature $T=T(a,\rho)>0$ for which \[ \liminf_{\substack{L\to\infty\\N/L^3\to\rho}} \frac{\langle u_{0,L},\gamma^{(1)}_{N,L,T}u_{0,L}\rangle}{N}>0. \] The exclusion distance, density, and temperature are held fixed in this limit.

primaryStatements.name: Scaled occupation bound
primaryStatements.label: thm:scaled
primaryStatements.text: There are constants $\alpha_0\ge2$, $D_*<\infty$, and $c_*>0$ such that $B_{\rm occ}\ge c_*$ whenever the parameters satisfy \eqref{eq:scaled-parameters}, $D\ge D_*$, and $K$ is sufficiently large. The lower threshold for $K$ can be chosen locally uniformly for $D$ in $[D_*,\infty)$, uniformly in $\alpha\in[\alpha_0/2,2\alpha_0]$ and $0<T\le D^{-1}$.

primaryStatements.name: Particle-number free-energy bounds
primaryStatements.label: prop:increments
primaryStatements.text: For sufficiently large $D$, uniformly in $K\ge100$, $0<T\le D^{-1}$, and the fixed $\alpha$ window, \begin{align} F_N&\ge c\alpha N,\\ F_{N+k}&\ge F_N+c\alpha k \qquad(0\le k\le N), \\ F_j^{(-W)}-F_{j-1}^{(-W)}&\le C\alpha \qquad(1\le j\le2N). \end{align} The last estimate holds for every bounded measurable $W\ge0$, with a constant independent of $W$. All form domains through particle number $2N$ are nonempty. The constants $c,C$ can be numerical; only the large-$D$ threshold depends on the fixed window for $\alpha$.

primaryStatements.name: Weighted local free-energy penalty
primaryStatements.label: prop:local-penalty
primaryStatements.text: There are $c,C>0$, independent of $b$, such that for every $0\le J\le N$, every bounded measurable $0\le W\le1$, and every finite-energy symmetric trace-one state $\sigma$, \begin{equation} \mathcal F_J^{(-W)}(\sigma)-F_J^{(-W)} \ge\alpha\left[\E_\sigma(f_A+cb^{-3}k_A)-CD|A|\right]. \end{equation} The threshold on $D$ may depend on $b$, but the displayed constants do not.

primaryStatements.name: Density bound in a small field
primaryStatements.label: cor:field-density
primaryStatements.text: In the $J$-particle equilibrium state with $0\le J\le N$ and $0\le W\le1$, every set $A$ of sites satisfies \begin{equation} \E n_{\ind_{\bigcup_{v\in A}B_v}}\le CD|A|. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Joint low-count bound
primaryStatements.label: prop:low-count
primaryStatements.text: One can choose $\alpha_0$ sufficiently large and then $\ell>0$ sufficiently small so that, for every set of sites $A$ and all sufficiently large $D$, \begin{equation} \mu\{n_v<\ell D\text{ for every }v\in A\} \le e^{-cD|A|}. \end{equation} The constants and thresholds are uniform in $K\ge100$ and $0<T\le D^{-1}$.

primaryStatements.name: Joint close-count bound
primaryStatements.label: prop:close-count
primaryStatements.text: For every fixed $\theta>0$, one can choose $b>0$ sufficiently small and then $D$ sufficiently large so that, for every set of sites $A$, \begin{equation} \mu\{C_v\ge\theta D\text{ for every }v\in A\} \le p_D^{|A|},\qquad p_D=\exp(-c\theta bD^{2/3})\longrightarrow0. \end{equation} Here $c>0$ can be numerical, and the bounds remain uniform in the temperature and volume ranges above.

primaryStatements.name: Thermal purification
primaryStatements.label: prop:purification
primaryStatements.text: Equation \eqref{eq:thermal-slab-law} defines a probability measure. At every fixed time $s\in[0,\delta]$, its position marginal is \[ \mu(\dd X)=Z_N^{-1}B_\beta^{\rm sym}(X,X)\,\dd X. \] The joint law of $X(t)$ and $W'$ has density $\Phi(X,W')^2$, where \begin{equation} \Phi(X,W')=Z_N^{-1/2}B_{\beta/2}^{\rm sym}(X,W'). \end{equation} This function is nonnegative, has squared integral one, and is symmetric separately in $X$ and $W'$. The constant-orbital occupation fraction of the scaled Gibbs state is \begin{equation} B_{\rm occ} =\frac1V\int\left|\int_{\Lambda_K} \Phi(x,X',W')\,\dd x\right|^2\dd X'\,\dd W', \end{equation} where $X'\in\Lambda_K^{N-1}$ is an ordered configuration.

definitions.name: Regular path
definitions.label: def:regular
definitions.text: Fix a sufficiently large numerical constant $C_{\rm reg}$. A path on $[0,2t]$ is regular if \begin{equation} \max_j A_j\le D^\gamma, \qquad \frac1{2m_t}\sum_{j=1}^{2m_t}(1+A_j)^3\le C_{\rm reg}, \end{equation} and its lifted diameter in each endpoint window $[0,h_0]$ and $[2t-h_0,2t]$ is at most $s_0/8$.

papers.title: Quantum Depletion and Momentum Distribution in the Dilute Hard-Sphere Bose Gas
papers.abstract: We prove the full scaled Bogoliubov momentum distribution for the depleted particles in the three-dimensional hard-sphere Bose gas at zero temperature. The thermodynamic limit is taken at each fixed density before the dilute limit, uniformly over all pure and mixed ground states. All thermodynamic accumulation values have the same dilute asymptotic: the limiting nonzero-momentum occupation measure has total mass $8/(3\sqrt\pi)$, giving the depletion fraction $\frac{8}{3\sqrt\pi}\sqrt{\rho a^3}+o(\sqrt{\rho a^3})$ for density ρ and hard-sphere exclusion distance a.
papers.familySummary: Proves Bose–Einstein condensation for the exact canonical Gibbs state of the three-dimensional hard-sphere gas: each fixed exclusion distance and sufficiently small fixed density admit a strictly positive temperature, independent of volume, with positive condensate fraction in the thermodynamic limit. At zero temperature, proves the Bogoliubov leading quantum-depletion law for hard spheres and fixed bounded nonnegative radial finite-range potentials of positive scattering length, taking the thermodynamic limit before the dilute limit.

primaryStatements.text: For every $a>0$, every bounded continuous real function $f$ on $\R^3$, and every $\eps>0$, there is $\rho_0(a,f,\eps)>0$ with the following property. Fix $0<\rho<\rho_0$ and put $\eta=\rho a^3$. For every sequence $N_j,L_j\longrightarrow\infty$ with $N_j/L_j^3\longrightarrow\rho$, \begin{equation} \limsup_{j\to\infty}\ \sup_{\Gamma\in\mathcal G_{N_j,L_j,a}} \left| \frac{1}{N_j\sqrt\eta} \sum_{\substack{k\in(2\pi/L_j)\Z^3\\k\ne0}} f\!\left(\frac{k}{\sqrt{8\pi\rho a}}\right)n_{\Gamma,L_j}(k) -\int_{\R^3}f\,\dd\nu_{\mathrm{Bog}} \right|\le\eps. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Remaining excitations
primaryStatements.label: asm:infrared
primaryStatements.text: Put $Q_R=P_R-P_0$. Uniformly over normalized, possibly complex, bosonic ground vectors, \begin{equation} D\|(Q_R)_1\Phi\|_2^2\le16\epsilon_j+o(1)+o_K(1), \end{equation} where $\epsilon_j\to0$. The coefficient $16$ is independent of $j$; the dilute remainder may depend on $j$. The exponents $u,w$ and the scale $R$ may be kept fixed when $j$ is increased; all dilute and volume thresholds may depend on $j$.

primaryStatements.label: cor:depletion
primaryStatements.text: In the same iterated limit, uniformly over all ground states, \[ 1-B_{N,L,a}(\Gamma) =\frac8{3\sqrt\pi}\sqrt{\rho a^3}+o(\sqrt{\rho a^3}). \]

primaryStatements.name: Removal energies
primaryStatements.label: set:removal
primaryStatements.text: For all sufficiently large $D$, uniformly in \eqref{set:scales}, \begin{equation} E_N-E_{N-m}\le C\alpha m\qquad(0\le m\le N). \end{equation} At fixed $K,r$, the ratio $E_n/n$ is nondecreasing among positive particle numbers having nonempty form domain.

primaryStatements.name: Joint low-count bound
primaryStatements.label: set:low-counts
primaryStatements.text: One can fix $\alpha_0$ sufficiently large and then $\ell_*>0$ sufficiently small so that every normalized nonnegative bosonic ground function satisfies, for every $A\subset\mathcal L$, \begin{equation} \mu\{n_{B_v}<\ell_*D\text{ for every }v\in A\} \le (C/D^2)^{|A|}. \end{equation} The estimate holds for all sufficiently large $D$, uniformly in $K$ and the ground function.

primaryStatements.name: Count exponential moments
primaryStatements.label: set:count-mgf
primaryStatements.text: For $A\subset\mathcal L$ set \[ f_A(X)=\sum_{i=1}^N e^{-d_K(x_i,A)}, \qquad f_{\varnothing}=0, \] where the distance is to the set of site centers. Every normalized nonnegative bosonic ground function obeys \begin{equation} \log\int e^{z f_A}\,\dd\mu\le CzD|A| \qquad(0\le z\le1). \end{equation} The constants are uniform for $K\ge100$, $D$ sufficiently large, and $\alpha\in I_\alpha$.

primaryStatements.name: Joint close-neighbor tail
primaryStatements.label: set:close-tail
primaryStatements.text: For each particle label $i$ let $d_i(X)=\min_{k\ne i}d_K(x_i,x_k)$, with the value $+\infty$ if $N=1$. Given $\theta>0$, one can choose $b_*>0$ sufficiently small, and then $D$ sufficiently large, so that the set \[ \mathcal Q(X)=\left\{v\in\mathcal L: \#\{i:d_K(x_i,v)\le5,\ d_i(X)\le b_*D^{-1/3}\} \ge\theta D\right\} \] satisfies, for every $A\subset\mathcal L$, \begin{equation} \mu\{A\subset\mathcal Q\}\le p_D^{|A|}, \qquad p_D=\bigl(C_\theta b_*^{-2}D^{-4/3}\bigr)^{1/q_*}\longrightarrow0, \end{equation} where $q_*$ is an absolute positive integer. The uniformity is the same as in Proposition \ref{set:count-mgf}.

primaryStatements.name: The four energy outputs
primaryStatements.label: en:energy-outputs
primaryStatements.text: There are arbitrarily small fixed $u>0$ and then $0<w<u/10000$ for which the following statements hold. Use the nested partitions fixed in \eqref{set:nested-lengths}, with $B\asymp D^u$, $R\asymp D^w$, and $d=1/j$. For every normalized nonnegative bosonic ground vector, \begin{align} \frac1{|\mathcal C_R|}\sum_{A\in\mathcal C_R} \E(q_A-1)^2&\le C D^{-1-w/6},\\ \frac1{|\mathcal C_d|}\sum_{A\in\mathcal C_d} \E(q_A-1)^4&\le C_jD^{-1-u/6}. \end{align} For every normalized, possibly complex, bosonic ground vector, \begin{align} \frac1V\left\langle\sum_{i=1}^N W_{R,i}\right\rangle &=\cD\alpha^{3/2}+o(1),\\ \frac1V\left\langle\sum_{i=1}^N W_{d,i}\right\rangle &\le \epsilon_j+o_j(1),\qquad \epsilon_j\longrightarrow0 \quad(j\longrightarrow\infty). \end{align} Here the thermodynamic limit is taken first, at fixed dilution; the remainders then tend to zero as $D\to\infty$, and $o_j(1)$ has this meaning with $j$ fixed. The bounds are uniform over the indicated ground vectors and along every density-convergent thermodynamic sequence. A sufficiently large volume threshold may depend on the dilution and on $j$.

definitions.name: Good site
definitions.label: lp:certificate
definitions.text: A unit-cell site is good if all of the following conditions hold. \begin{enumerate} \item It has at least $c f_0D$ interior labels. In its $R_*$ neighborhood, each unit cell has at most $CD$ endpoints at either time and at most $Cf_0D$ flagged endpoints at either time. \item At either endpoint time, every ball $B(z,h)$ in the neighborhood, with $r\leq h\leq1$, satisfies \begin{equation} \#\{i:\ i\text{ flagged},\ Y_i\in B(z,h)\} \leq C(f_0Dh^3+D^{1/100}), \end{equation} and the same assertion holds for $Z_i$. \item Every frozen path visiting the relevant neighborhood satisfies \eqref{lp:cutoffs} and has lifted diameter at most $Cb$. At each mesh time $q$, and for either adjacent mesh interval $J$, the frozen paths satisfy \begin{equation} \sum_{k\notin\mathcal I:\ \omega_k(q)\in B(z,h)} (1+A_J(\omega_k))^3 \leq C(Dh^3+D^{1/100})\qquad(r\leq h\leq1). \end{equation} The unweighted version is also required at endpoints and at time zero. \end{enumerate} All ball tests may be made on finite spatial nets with dyadic radii, using enlarged balls and fixed margins. The stated inequalities for arbitrary balls then follow by covering. The constants $c,C$ are fixed before taking $D$ large. Write $\mathcal B$ for the set of bad sites.

Every thermodynamic accumulation value of the fraction outside the constant mode is $\frac{8}{3\sqrt\pi}\sqrt{\rho a^3}+o(\sqrt{\rho a^3})$ as $\rho\downarrow0$. The assertion is uniform over ground-state density matrices and does not require the occupation to have a unique thermodynamic limit.
