papers.title: Scale and conformal symmetry in four-dimensional operational quantum field theory
papers.abstract: We prove that scale symmetry implies local conformal symmetry for a class of four-dimensional unitary, positive-energy quantum field theories with a Poincaré- and scale-invariant vacuum. The class has a discrete, bounded-below spectrum of scaling dimensions with finite multiplicities, and each original field has finite scaling support. The original fields and their adjoints have compatible affiliated realizations in a causally commuting bounded local net, and a physical local dilatation current generates scale transformations through its local Ward identities. The operational framework admits sharply localized reconstructed fields after their joint products and compatible affiliated realizations in the same net have been established. Under these hypotheses, the stress tensor admits a symmetric, conserved, traceless improvement with unchanged translation and Lorentz charges. The corresponding conformal currents satisfy unbroken local Ward identities on the physical field algebra. The conclusion is local; integration to a global conformal action on the whole bounded net remains a separate question.
papers.familySummary: Under the stated bounded-local-net and field-reconstruction hypotheses, proves that scale symmetry implies local conformal symmetry for four-dimensional unitary positive-energy theories with a discrete bounded-below scaling spectrum of finite multiplicity, finite scaling support and a physical local scale current. The stress tensor has a traceless improvement with unchanged spacetime charges. The conclusion concerns local Ward identities, not a global conformal action on the whole net.

primaryStatements.name: Original joint-test domain
primaryStatements.label: F:old-domain
primaryStatements.text: For every fixed finite ordered list of original fields and adjoints, the vacuum distribution has a unique tempered extension and its vacuum map has a continuous Hilbert-valued extension to all joint Schwartz kernels. The space $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{old}}$ is Hilbert-dense and invariant under old field insertions and continuous joint polynomial insertions, with their prescribed adjoints. Finite field-label identities, covariance, locality, and the compact-slab Ward identities pass to this domain with their stated support conditions. For a compactly smeared original field $B(f)$, each retained closed affiliated realization and its Hilbert adjoint agree on $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{old}}$ with these insertion actions. This assertion also holds for an originally supplied Schwartz realization. It does not require $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{old}}$ to be a graph core for that realization.

primaryStatements.name: Parabolic generators
primaryStatements.label: F:parabolic-generator
primaryStatements.text: On $\{b>0\}$ there is a boost-independent internal Hilbert space $\mathcal K$ and a nonnegative self-adjoint operator $h$ on it such that \begin{equation} \cH_{b>0}\simeq L^2(\R_+,\dd b/b)\otimes L^2(\R^2,\dd^2k)\otimes\mathcal K, \qquad H_{p_d}=b\bigl(|Y-d|^2+h\bigr),\quad Y=i\partial_k. \end{equation} Here $G=bY$, $P_i=-k_i$, and $(e^{isB}\psi)(b,k)=\psi(e^sb,k)$. The operators $H_{p_d}$ vanish on $\ker b$. Moreover $J_WbJ_W=b$, $J_WYJ_W=Y$, and $J_WhJ_W=h$.

primaryStatements.name: Bounded-profile Ward formula
primaryStatements.label: N:Ward-proposition
primaryStatements.text: The map $g\mapsto H_g=bh_g$ is real linear on $C_b^\infty(\R^2)$. For $g$ compactly supported or Schwartz, and the bounded smooth opposite tests above, \begin{equation} \ip{C\Omega}{H_gA\Omega} =\int_{\R^2}\int_\R g(y)\rho(v) \mathcal C_\epsilon(T_{vv}(0,y,v)\Omega,CA\Omega) \,\dd v\,\dd^2y. \end{equation} Here $\rho$ is any smooth step whose derivative lies in the $v$ gap between the two causal intersections with the plane. The expression is a vacuum-vector distribution paired with the indicated smooth vector, not an unsmeared operator integral.

primaryStatements.name: Polynomial extension
primaryStatements.label: N:polynomial-extension
primaryStatements.text: Equation \eqref{N:bounded-Ward} holds for compactly smeared physical polynomial tests, including their adjoints, on the common field domain $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{old}}$. The convergence to it is uniform when the smearing tests vary over a compact smooth parameter family.

primaryStatements.name: Internal measure and quadratic moment
primaryStatements.label: N:measure-proposition
primaryStatements.text: On the $b>0$ representation there is a normalized positive operator-valued Borel measure $\mu$ on $\R^2$, with mutually commuting values on the internal multiplicity space, such that \begin{equation} H_g=b\int_{\R^2}g(Y+z)\,\mu(\dd z), \qquad \mu(\R^2)=\id. \end{equation} Its values commute with $h$ and with the external variables $b,Y$. Its first moment is zero as a polarized integral on $\Dom h^{1/2}$. Its trace second moment is the increasing closed-form limit of compactly truncated moments and defines a positive self-adjoint operator $\kappa$ satisfying \begin{equation} \int z\,\mu(\dd z)=0,\qquad \kappa=\int |z|^2\,\mu(\dd z)\leq h, \qquad K_n=b(|Y|^2+\kappa). \end{equation} The second-moment inequality is a quadratic-form inequality and, since the operators strongly commute, has its usual joint spectral meaning. No assertion that $\mu$ is projection-valued, or that $\kappa=h$, is made.

definitions.name: Operational physical theory
definitions.label: ass:framework
definitions.text:
The physical Hilbert space $\cH$ is generated from a vacuum $\Omega$ by the original physical fields and their adjoints. The fields, in finite-component Lorentz multiplets, and their ordered products are operator-valued Wightman distributions on a common invariant polynomial domain, which we call the initial realization domain $\mathcal E$. They have positive translation spectrum, Poincar'e covariance, and locality, with the usual grading when fermions occur. The vacuum is invariant under Poincar'e transformations and continuous dilations; uniqueness of the invariant vector is not assumed. Let $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{fact}}\subset\mathcal E$ be the algebraic span of $\Omega$ and all finite original vacuum words with compactly supported factor tests. To specify the vacuum-generated domain, for every finite ordered list $\mathbf A=(A_1,\ldots,A_n)$ of original fields and adjoints, write $\Psi^{\mathrm{old}}_{\mathbf A}(h)$ for the continuous extension of its original factor-test vacuum map to joint kernels $h\in\mathcal S((\R^4)^n)$. These kernels include $C_c^\infty((\R^4)^n)$ and finite sums of factorized tests. Set \[ \mathcal D_{\mathrm{old}} =\Span\{\Omega,\Psi^{\mathrm{old}}_{\mathbf A}(h): n=1,2,\ldots,\ h\in\mathcal S((\R^4)^n)\}. \] The existence of these extensions and their insertion actions is proved in Proposition ef{F:old-domain}; it is not an additional assumption. This is an algebraic span: it has no Hilbert or graph completion and no bound on word length or tensor rank. The domain whose containment is required below is precisely $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{old}}$, not an independently larger choice of $\mathcal E$. Let $\mathcal F$ be the complex vector space of original point-field labels, modulo equality of their operator-valued distributions on $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{fact}}$; Proposition ef{F:old-domain} makes this equivalently equality on $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{old}}$. It is the algebraic direct sum \[ \mathcal F= igoplus_{\Delta\in\Sigma}\mathcal F_\Delta, \qquad A=\sum_{\Delta\in S_A}A_\Delta, \quad S_A\subset\Sigma\ 	ext{finite}, \] where $\Sigma\subset\R$ is a discrete set of real dimensions, bounded below and locally finite: $\Sigma\cap[a,b]$ is finite for every finite interval $[a,b]$. Each $\mathcal F_\Delta$ is a finite-dimensional Lorentz-stable space of finite-component fields satisfying \[ U_D(s)A_\Delta(x)U_D(-s) =e^{s\Delta}A_\Delta(e^s x) \] as operator-valued distributions on $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{fact}}$, and hence on $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{old}}$ by that proposition. Multiplicity counts independent component fields after including all Lorentz component indices and imposing linear field identities; equivalently, each grade contains finitely many finite-component Lorentz multiplets. Homogeneous components are themselves original physical fields. Adjunction preserves each real grade, with conjugate Lorentz components, and covariant distributional differentiation sends $\mathcal F_\Delta$ into $\mathcal F_{\Delta+1}$, with a missing grade interpreted as zero. Lorentz transformations preserve the grades and statistics; translations act on spacetime arguments. No completion by infinitely many scaling components is taken. There is a fixed isotone net $O\mapsto\cM(O)$ of weakly closed algebras of physical bounded operations, covariant under the same physical Poincar'e and dilation representations. Algebras at spacelike separation commute, with the fixed statistics twist in the graded case. Each smeared original physical field has a closed affiliated realization in its localization algebra, extending its realization on $\mathcal E$, whose adjoint also extends the field adjoint there. The corresponding extensions on $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{old}}$ are derived in Proposition ef{F:old-domain}. For any other open region $R$, \[ \cM(R)= igvee_{\overline O\subset R}\cM(O), \] where $O$ ranges over double cones. Physical point-field membership in $\Aphys$ is intrinsic to this fixed net, not to an enumeration of symbols. An operationally reconstructed finite family of homogeneous finite-component point fields of real scaling dimensions is admitted, together with its finite linear span, once its localization supports can shrink inside arbitrarily small double cones; all joint field distributions of the family with itself and with every fixed finite list of original fields and adjoints have been established at every finite length on a compatible common invariant domain containing $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{old}}$, with the required adjoints and the preceding covariance, spectrum, and locality/statistics properties; and compatible smeared realizations affiliated with the original localization algebras have been established, with their adjoints extending the field adjoints on that domain. Separately constructed fields are not combined into a common polynomial field algebra without their mutual joint distributions, common invariant domain with the required adjoints, and original-net affiliations having been established. The criterion asserts no candidate's existence or analytic properties and admits no point field merely by convergence of an infinite nonhomogeneous scaling sum. The original physical fields include a symmetric conserved stress tensor $T_{\mu
u}$ with the translation and orbital Lorentz Ward identities, and a local virial field $V_\mu$ such that \[ D_\mu=x^
u T_{\mu
u}-V_\mu,\qquad \partial^\mu D_\mu=0,\qquad T^\mu{}_{\mu}=\partial^\mu V_\mu. \] The Ward identities of $D$ generate the stated dilations. Charge Ward identities are understood through compact Cauchy slabs surrounding an insertion and extend to polynomial products by the derivation rule. The identities displayed above are flat-space field identities; the usual contact terms in time-ordered distributions are allowed.

papers.title: Polynomial-Time Unitary Synthesis from a Boolean Oracle
papers.abstract: We give a positive answer to the constant-error formulation of the Aaronson–Kuperberg unitary synthesis problem. For every n, a quantum oracle circuit generated in polynomial time from n alone can approximate the channel of every n-qubit unitary to full diamond-norm error at most 1/2, after a suitable Boolean oracle is chosen. Using the fixed gates $H,T,T^\dagger,\mathrm{CNOT}$, the circuit has polynomially many qubits, elementary gates, and oracle calls, and its oracle queries have polynomial length. The oracle may depend on the target unitary; the theorem does not give an efficient classical procedure for constructing it.

Gates, qubits, oracle calls and query length are polynomially bounded. The target-dependent oracle may have an unrestricted truth table; its efficient classical construction is not asserted.

primaryStatements.name: Polynomial-time unitary synthesis
primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: There are a polynomial $p$ and a deterministic classical algorithm which, on input $1^n$ for any integer $n\ge1$, outputs in time at most $p(n)$ a quantum oracle circuit $A_n$ with the following properties. The circuit uses the gates $H,T,T^\dagger,\mathrm{CNOT}$ and a single Boolean oracle of input length $m(n)\le p(n)$. Its total number of qubits, elementary gates, and oracle calls are each at most $p(n)$. For every unitary $U\in U(2^n)$ there is a function $f:\{0,1\}^{m(n)}\to\{0,1\}$ for which the output channel $\Phi_{n,f}$ of $A_n^{O_f}$ satisfies \[ \norm{\Phi_{n,f}-\mathcal U}_\diamond\le\frac12. \]

primaryStatements.name: A block of uniformly small norm
primaryStatements.label: contract:block
primaryStatements.text: For every unitary $U$ on $\C^d$, there are unitaries $P_{\mathrm L}$ and $P_{\mathrm R}$ on $\C^d$ such that \begin{equation} V=P_{\mathrm L}UP_{\mathrm R} =\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\C&D\end{pmatrix}, \qquad \norm D\leq r, \end{equation} where the block sizes are $k,s$ from \eqref{contract:orders}. The transformations $P_{\mathrm L},P_{\mathrm R}$ and their inverses have implementations using $O(n)$ programmable slots and $O(n)$ clean working qubits, with a structure determined by $n,d$. The same structure works simultaneously for any family $U_\lambda$, using the label $\lambda$ as an additional control.

primaryStatements.label: fields:gram
primaryStatements.text: For either $\mathcal T=\mathcal E_L$ or $\mathcal T=\mathcal R_L$, \begin{equation} (1-r^{2L})I_d\ \le\ \mathcal T^*\mathcal T\ \le\ I_d. \end{equation} In addition, let $\widetilde F$ apply $F(z)$ to the port register, controlled on $z$. Then \begin{equation} \norm{\widetilde F\mathcal E_L-\mathcal R_L V}\le2\tau. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.label: fields:sparsity
primaryStatements.text: In these Fourier coordinates, every row of $\mathcal E_L$ and of $\mathcal R_L$ has at most $L$ nonzero entries.

primaryStatements.label: encode:implementation
primaryStatements.text: Under the hypotheses and definitions of Section \ref{sec:fields}, there are exact-slot unitaries $\mathsf U_E,\mathsf U_R$ such that \begin{equation} \norm{\mathsf U_E\iota-\jmath\mathcal E_L}\le5r^{2L}, \qquad \norm{\mathsf U_R\iota-\jmath\mathcal R_L}\le5r^{2L}. \end{equation} Each uses $O\bigl(L(K+n+h)+K\bigr)$ slots and $K+n+h+2$ fresh qubits, with slot structure independent of $V$. The construction works coherently with any additional label register.

primaryStatements.name: Uniform programmable synthesis
primaryStatements.label: rec:skeleton
primaryStatements.text: Let $n\geq1$, $1\leq d\leq2^n$, and $t\geq0$. There is a programmable-slot circuit structure, determined by $n,d,t$, with the following property. For every family $(U_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\{0,1\}^t}$ of unitaries on $\C^d$, its slot tables can be chosen so that the circuit implements the controlled unitary $U_\lambda$, preserves the labels, and has clean-workspace operator norm error less than $1/100$ in the sense of \eqref{slot:clean-error}. The circuit uses \begin{equation} t+O((n+1)^{10})\quad\text{qubits}, \qquad O((n+1)^{13})\quad\text{slots}. \end{equation} Its structure, including each slot's ordered control list, is generated deterministically in time polynomial in $n+t$ from $n,d,t$.

primaryStatements.name: Compilation of slots
primaryStatements.label: compile:slots
primaryStatements.text: Let a skeleton have $S$ slots on $Q$ qubits, and put $\eta=1/h$ for an integer $h\ge2$. There is a deterministic procedure, polynomial in $Q,S,1/\eta$, that produces a circuit over $H,T,T^\dagger,\mathrm{CNOT}$ and one Boolean oracle, with polynomially many qubits, gates, calls, and address bits. For every assignment of the slot tables, some contents of that oracle make the circuit differ from the prescribed skeleton by at most $S\eta$ on inputs with its added scratch qubits zero, with the comparison circuit keeping those scratch qubits zero.

papers.title: A Nearly Quartic Separation Between Randomized and Quantum Query Complexity
papers.abstract: We construct total Boolean functions with a nearly quartic separation between bounded-error randomized and quantum query complexity. Writing these complexities as $\mathrm R(f)$ and $\mathrm Q(f)$, the examples rule out every universal bound $\mathrm R(f)=O((1+\mathrm Q(f))^\alpha)$ with α < 4. Thus the known quartic upper bound has the optimal exponent, disproving the conjectured cubic bound. Both complexities count worst-case bit queries with error at most 1/3 on every input.
papers.familySummary: Shows that the universal bound $R(f)=O((1+Q(f))^4)$ for total Boolean functions is sharp in its exponent, ruling out every smaller power and disproving the conjectured cubic relation. Here R and Q are randomized and quantum worst-case bit-query complexities with error at most 1/3; computation between queries is unrestricted.

primaryStatements.text: The optimal power is $\alpha_{\mathrm{tot}}=4$. More precisely, $\R(f)=O((1+\Q(f))^4)$ for every total Boolean function. primaryStatements.name: A tournament for probabilistic comparisons
primaryStatements.label: prop:tournament
primaryStatements.text: For $m\ge2$, put \[ T=\lceil\log(1000m)\rceil, \qquad \epsilon=\frac{1}{1000T}. \] Suppose a coherent comparison circuit, controlled by two candidate indices and reversible with all workspace retained, uses at most $c\ge1$ bit queries. Let $a_{ij}$ be the probability that it reports $i$ defeating $j$, and assume \eqref{eq:complementarity}. There is a quantum algorithm making \[ O\bigl(c\sqrt m\,T^2\log T\bigr) \] queries on every branch and returning a list of at most $T$ candidates with the following guarantee. If $i_\ast\in[m]$ satisfies \begin{equation} a_{i_\ast j}\ge1-\epsilon\qquad(j\ne i_\ast), \end{equation} then the list contains $i_\ast$ with probability at least $1-2m/2^T-T\epsilon$.

papers.abstract: We disprove rational injectivity of the coefficient-free reduced Baum–Connes assembly map for torsion-free groups. Specifically, we construct a finitely generated torsion-free discrete group whose degree-zero assembly map has a kernel class of infinite order.

primaryStatements.name: Simultaneous disjoint domains
primaryStatements.label: prop:domains
primaryStatements.text: There are sets $R_Q\subseteq V(Q)$, one for each sheet, such that each $R_Q$ is empty, an old-centered ball $B_Q(v)$, or a private singleton, and the sets $D_Q=V(Q)\setminus R_Q$ have the following properties. \begin{enumerate} \item The physical vertex sets $D_Q$ are pairwise disjoint. \item Put \[ E_{\mathrm{int}}= \bigcup_{Q\in\mathcal Q} \{e\in E(Q):\text{both endpoints of }e\text{ lie in }D_Q\}. \] Every edge in this union has a unique such sheet, and $(V(\mathcal C),E(\mathcal C)\setminus E_{\mathrm{int}})$ is a forest. \item $\operatorname{Star}_Q(R_Q)$ is a forest. If $R_Q$ contains an old vertex of layer $i$, then $\abs{R_Q}\leq2^{10H_i}$. A private singleton removes no old coordinate. \end{enumerate} No equivariance of the choices $R_Q$ is asserted or needed.

primaryStatements.name: The deterministic labeled tower
primaryStatements.label: prop:tower-labels
primaryStatements.text: For every fixed finite type set and every sufficiently large $s$ as above, the construction has the following properties. \begin{enumerate} \item The auxiliary state sizes are \eqref{eq:state-sizes}. In a fixed extra slice an incidence has degrees $d,D$. Without slicing, its smaller side acquires the extra factor $2^b$ and its larger side does not. The total degrees are at most $T2^b d$ on A and $T2^bD$ on B. \item The labeling is folded: no two outgoing oriented edges at a vertex have the same label. Its signed alphabet satisfies \begin{equation} |\mathcal S|\le 2TM2^b d2^r, \qquad \frac{\sqrt{|\mathcal S|}}q \le 2^{-.000025s+O(\log s)+O_{T,b}(1)}\longrightarrow0. \end{equation} \item At every height the fraction of removed vertices on each side is at most $\varepsilon_{\rm gate}+\varepsilon_{\rm sep}$. This bound can be made arbitrarily small, uniformly over heights and all table choices. The separate-parity and terminal gate conclusions of Lemma \ref{lem:gate-deletions} hold. \item Every immersed path in $X^{\rm good}$ starting at height $i$ and having length at least $\lceil1.002m_i\rceil$ is the unique immersed path with that oriented word anywhere in $X^{\rm good}$. This is a global assertion over all heights and components. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.name: Sequential selection
primaryStatements.label: prop:sequential-law
primaryStatements.text: There is a probability law on all the permutation tables such that every auxiliary incidence has centered singular norm at most the fixed number $\rho<1$ in \eqref{eq:uniform-incidence-gap}. At each individual source-block update, conditional on all earlier updates, any joint test of $k$ specified current tables has its probability increased by at most $e^{\varepsilon_s k}$ relative to independent uniform current tables. The bound is uniform in the earlier history and the height, with $\varepsilon_s\to0$.

primaryStatements.name: Pruned old graph
primaryStatements.label: prop:pruning
primaryStatements.text: Given any $\varepsilon>0$, the allowed parameters and the universal tables can be chosen so that the additional two deletions in this Section remove less than an $\varepsilon$ fraction of each $\mathscr A_i$ and $\mathscr B_i$. In the surviving induced old graph $X_{\mathrm{old}}$: \begin{enumerate} \item the folded labeling, padded-prefix recovery of Lemma \ref{lem:tower-recovery}, and global word uniqueness of Proposition \ref{prop:tower-labels} remain valid; \item a nonempty cyclically reduced closed path based at height $i$ has length greater than $.93m_i$; \item every bicycle containing a vertex of height $i$ has length at least $1.52m_i$; \item every nonempty cyclically reduced closed path based at height $i$ with length at most $6.04m_i$ is not a law in the independent edge variables of $\HH$. \end{enumerate} The expansion conclusions for the undeleted incidences hold simultaneously, and the degrees remain fixed along the tower.

primaryStatements.name: Simultaneously sampled symbols
primaryStatements.label: prop:sampled-symbols
primaryStatements.text: Fix b, a finite matrix dimension, a positive accuracy \(\eta\), and a finite list of compact smooth symbol profiles and height selections as above. The list may include cutoffs, both parities, the initial-height selection, and any finite mesh of the adjacent rescaling and rotation families. Allocate a prescribed incidence type for every required same or adjacent layer symbol. For sufficiently large s and then sufficiently large initial height, the surviving base graph admits a voltage on every edge and finite-net matrix weights such that the following hold simultaneously. \begin{enumerate} \item The voltage cover has no nontrivial cyclically reduced closed walk of length at most \(6.03m_i\) based at an old vertex of height i. \item All weighted blocks may use the common denominator q. If \(\mathcal V_{\tau,ik}\) is that normalized weighted convolution block and the prescribed symbol is \(S_{\tau,ik}=T_if_{\tau,ik}T_k^*\), then \[ \norm{\mathcal V_{\tau,ik} -U_{\tau,ik}\otimes S_{\tau,ik}}\leq\eta \] in the full regular operator norm, at every height. The tensor notation here means that each scalar incidence entry multiplies the same matrix-valued deck convolution symbol. \item Weights are read from one finite set, independent of height. Appending their net indices to the existing edge labels preserves the labelled-graph uniqueness properties and gives \[ \log_2\abs{\mathcal A} \leq1.00005s+O(\log s)+O_{b,\eta,\mathrm{profiles}}(1) <\log_2(q^2) \] for sufficiently large s. In particular \(\sqrt{\abs{\mathcal A}}/q\) tends to zero as s increases after the fixed data. Zero-weight edges are retained in the voltage cover. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.name: Graphical realization
primaryStatements.label: prop:graphical-realization
primaryStatements.text: There is an injective map of vertices and formal oriented edges \[ j\colon\widetilde X\longrightarrow\operatorname{Cay}(\Gamma,S) \] preserving labels and sending $(v_*,1)$ to the identity. The subgroup of vertices over $v_*$ defines an injective homomorphism $\phi\colon\HH\hookrightarrow\Gamma$. If $t_v=j(v,1)$, then \begin{equation} j(v,h)=\phi(h)t_v. \end{equation} The full group of label-preserving automorphisms of $\widetilde X$ is its deck group. Consequently the distinct translated images, called sheets, are indexed by $\Gamma/\phi(\HH)$, and the stabilizer of $g j(\widetilde X)$ under left translation is $g\phi(\HH)g^{-1}$.

primaryStatements.name: Torsion-freeness and the integral detector
primaryStatements.label: prop:torsion-detector
primaryStatements.text: The graphical group $\Gamma$ is torsion-free. The map $i_\Gamma:\Z^2\to\Gamma$ sending the ordered basis to $(z,x)$ is injective, and there is a class $c_\Gamma\in H^2(B\Gamma;\Z)$ such that \begin{equation} \bigl\langle(Bi_\Gamma)^*c_\Gamma,[T^2]\bigr\rangle=-1. \end{equation}

definitions.name: Coherent return
definitions.label: def:coherent-return
definitions.text: In band $k$, a coherent return is a positive-length nonbacktracking path \[ v_0,e_1,v_1,\ldots,e_p,v_p \] in $X^{\mathrm{good}}$, entirely in that band, whose endpoints are on the same side and agree through an available aligned depth \begin{equation} h\geq ps/2+M_k, \qquad h\leq\min\{D(v_0),D(v_p)\}. \end{equation} It is minimal if no proper positive-length contiguous subpath is a coherent return for the same band and the same $M_k$. An exact closed nonbacktracking path is included whenever it satisfies the available-depth condition.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: There exist a finitely generated torsion-free discrete group \(\Gproj\) and a projection \(e\in C_r^*(\Gproj)\) such that \[ 0<\tau_{\Gproj}(e)<\frac12. \] In particular, \(e\) is neither zero nor the identity.

primaryStatements.name: Geometric conclusion
primaryStatements.label: geo:main
primaryStatements.text: There are absolute constants $C_*,C_\bullet$ such that, for sufficiently large $\ell$, the preceding hypotheses have the following consequences. Every component map $\phi:C\to X$ is an embedding. Index copies by pairs $(C,\phi)$ modulo the equivalence \[ (C,\phi)\sim (\delta_a C,\phi\delta_a^{-1}),\qquad a\in F. \] Thus an indexed copy $Q$ remembers its source component and source vertices up to this deck alignment, in addition to its embedded image. There is a well-order of these copies and an induced intrinsic ball $B(Q)$ in each $Q$ such that \begin{enumerate} \item every vertex of $Q$ shared with an earlier copy belongs to $B(Q)$; \item the subgraph of $Q$ consisting of all edges with at least one endpoint in $B(Q)$ is a forest; \item for every vertex of $B(Q)$ lying over layer $i$, \begin{equation} |V(B(Q))|\le\mathfrak w_i, \qquad \mathfrak w_i=2^{C_\bullet H_i}; \end{equation} \item if $D_Q$ is $V(Q)$ minus its vertices shared with earlier copies, the domains $D_Q$ are pairwise disjoint, and deleting every edge of $Q$ whose two endpoints lie in $D_Q$, for all $Q$, leaves a forest in $X$. \end{enumerate} Furthermore $\Gbase$ is torsion-free. None of the constants depends on $F$, the voltage values, the number of components of $P$, or $|S|$.

primaryStatements.name: Assigned domains and the remaining forest
primaryStatements.label: geo:forest
primaryStatements.text: Put \[ D_Q=V(Q)\setminus\bigcup_{R<Q}V(R),\qquad E_{\mathrm{int}}=\bigcup_Q \{e\in E(Q):\text{ both endpoints of }e\text{ lie in }D_Q\}. \] The $D_Q$ are pairwise disjoint, $V(Q)\setminus D_Q\subseteq V(B(Q))$, and the formal graph $(V(X),E(X)\setminus E_{\mathrm{int}})$ is a forest. Each edge in $E_{\mathrm{int}}$ belongs to the displayed set for exactly one $Q$.

primaryStatements.name: Scalar compression after a free product
primaryStatements.label: scalar:compression
primaryStatements.text: Let \(\Lambda\) be a discrete group and \(p\in M_N(C_r^*(\Lambda))\) a projection with \[ 0<a:=\tau_{\Lambda,N}(p)<\frac12. \] Put \(K=\Lambda*\mathbb F_N\), where \(t_1,\ldots,t_N\) freely generate \(\mathbb F_N\), and regard \(p\) as a matrix over \(C_r^*(K)\) by Lemma \ref{scalar:subgroup}. Set \[ U=(\lambda_K(t_1),\ldots,\lambda_K(t_N)),\qquad A=pU^*Up. \] Then \(A\) is invertible in the unital corner \(pM_N(C_r^*(K))p\), and \begin{equation} e=(Up)A^{-1}(Up)^* \end{equation} is a projection in the scalar algebra \(C_r^*(K)\) with \(\tau_K(e)=a\). If \(\Lambda\) is finitely generated and torsion-free, then so is \(K\).

primaryStatements.name: Matrix construction
primaryStatements.label: setup:matrix-target
primaryStatements.text: There exist a finitely generated torsion-free discrete group \(\Gbase\), a finite integer \(N\ge1\), and a self-adjoint element \(T\in M_N(\mathbb C[\Gbase])\), in its regular representation, with a nonempty separated spectral subset whose spectral projection \(p_0\) satisfies \[ p_0\in M_N(C_r^*(\Gbase)),\qquad 0<\tau_{\Gbase,N}(p_0)<\frac12. \]

primaryStatements.name: Expansion of the realized incidence
primaryStatements.label: exp:realized-gap
primaryStatements.text: For all sufficiently large $\ell$, independently of the height pair and of its previously fixed lower tables, its current tables can be chosen so that \eqref{exp:actual-cut} holds. For this choice, the incidence operator of the actual $Y^0$ block, with each entry normalized by $\sqrt{dD'}$ in counting Hilbert spaces, sends normalized constants to normalized constants, as does its adjoint, and has norm at most $1-\chi$ between their orthogonal complements, where \[ \chi=\frac1{800}. \]

primaryStatements.name: Few short cyclic paths at one layer
primaryStatements.label: prune:cycle-count
primaryStatements.text: Fix a layer and a side. A nonempty cyclically reduced oriented label word is the word of at most one based cyclically nonbacktracking closed path with its base on that layer and side. Consequently the number of vertices of \(A_i\), or of \(B_i\), supporting such a closed path of length at most \(g_i\) is at most \[ \sum_{a=1}^{\lfloor g_i\rfloor}(2m_\ell)^a. \] For all sufficiently large \(\ell\), this is a fraction at most \(2^{-0.9H_i}\) of either vertex set, uniformly in \(i\).

primaryStatements.name: The tower properties
primaryStatements.label: prune:tower-properties
primaryStatements.text: For all sufficiently large \(\ell\), the preceding choices give a graph \(Y^0\) on sets of sizes \(|A_i|=d2^{H_i}\) and \(|B_i|=2^{H_i}\), and its induced subgraph \(Y\), with these properties. \begin{enumerate} \item For every \(|i-k|\leq1\), the \(Y^0\)-block between \(A_i\) and \(B_k\) has degrees \(d,D_{ik}\) with \(D_{ik}=D2^{|i|-|k|}\). Its counting incidence divided by \(\sqrt{dD_{ik}}\) maps normalized constants to normalized constants, as does its adjoint. On their orthogonal complements its norm is at most \(1-\chi\), with the absolute constant \(\chi\) of Proposition \ref{exp:realized-gap}. \item The fraction removed from any \(A_i\) or \(B_i\) is at most \(\varepsilon_\ell\) of \eqref{prune:total-budget}. \item The labels of \(Y\) are folded, with positive alphabet size at most \(m_\ell=O(d2^r(1+s)^2)\). \item Every nonbacktracking path in \(Y\) beginning at layer \(i\) and having length at least \(L_i\) is determined by its oriented word among all paths in \(Y\), including paths beginning in other layers. \item There is no nonempty cyclically nonbacktracking closed path in \(Y\), based at layer \(i\), of length at most \(g_i\). \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: There exist a finitely generated discrete group \(\Gsur\) and a projection \(b_0\in C_r^*(\Gsur)\) with irrational canonical trace. Moreover, \[ [b_0]\notin\mu_0^{\Gsur}\bigl(K_0^{\Gsur}(\underline E\Gsur)\bigr). \] In particular, the coefficient-free reduced Baum--Connes conjecture for countable discrete groups is false.

primaryStatements.name: L\"uck
primaryStatements.label: thm:trace-image
primaryStatements.text: For every countable discrete group \(G\), \[ \tau_{G*}\!\left(\mu_0^G(K_0^G(\underline EG))\right)\subseteq\Q. \]

primaryStatements.label: prop:cone-geometry
primaryStatements.text: There is an integer \(D_0\), independent of all the above data, such that every vertex on a geodesic triangle in \(\widehat X\) is within \(D_0\) of a vertex on another side. Moreover: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item If an edge path of length \(L\) joins \(x,a\in P\) while avoiding \(c_P\), then \begin{equation} d_P(x,a)\le12(L+1)\lambda\sigma(P). \end{equation} \item If \(\lambda<1/12\), the graph \(X\) is simple: no nonfreely-trivial closed label word in \(X\) has length at most two. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.name: Choice of data
primaryStatements.label: prop:data
primaryStatements.text: There are labelled graphs \((\Theta_i)_{i\ge1}\) satisfying all the hypotheses of Section \ref{sec:geometry}, with the following additional properties. Write \(n_i=|\operatorname{Vert}(\Theta_i)|\), \(k_i=\lfloor n_i/2\rfloor\), and let \(\sigma_i\) be the girth. There are constants \(\rho,\kappa>0\), independent of \(i\), such that: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item On the orthogonal complement of constants in \(\ell^2(\operatorname{Vert}(\Theta_i))\), \(dI-\Adj_{\Theta_i}\ge\rho I\), and for every vertex subset \(W\), \begin{equation} |\partial W|\ge\kappa\min\{|W|,n_i-|W|\}. \end{equation} Here \(\partial W\) is the unoriented edge boundary in \(\Theta_i\). \item With \begin{equation} c=\frac\eta2\min\{\kappa,1\}, \end{equation} we have \(n_i>100\), \(\sigma_i>\max\{16,20/c\}\), \(\lambda\sigma_i>3\), and \(1<\lfloor\lambda\sigma_i\rfloor<\lfloor\lambda\sigma_{i+1}\rfloor\). \item Every induced intrinsic ball of radius at most \(\sigma_i/16\) is a tree with fewer than \(\eta n_i\) vertices. \item The integers \(k_i\) strictly increase and \(k_{i+1}-k_i\to\infty\). \end{enumerate} Consequently every ball \(B_P\) in Lemma \ref{lem:overlap}, for every permitted root and chosen root geodesic, is an induced tree satisfying \begin{equation} r_P\le\sigma(P)/16,\qquad |B_P|<\eta|P|. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: A projection in the reduced group algebra
primaryStatements.label: prop:projection
primaryStatements.text: There exists a projection $b_0\in C_r^*(\Gsur)$ such that, for every $\omega\in\Omega$, $\pi_\omega(b_0)$ is the orthogonal projection onto $\ker\pi_\omega(T)$. Explicitly, it is projection onto constants on each valid copy and is zero on $\ell^2(U_\omega)$. In particular, \begin{equation} \langle\pi_\omega(b_0)\delta_1,\delta_1\rangle = \begin{cases} 1/n_i,&\text{if $1$ belongs to a valid copy of type $i$},\\ 0,&\text{if $1\in U_\omega$}. \end{cases} \end{equation} The valid copy in the first case is unique.

primaryStatements.label: prop:irrational-trace
primaryStatements.text: The projection \(b_0\in C_r^*(\Gsur)\) satisfies \begin{equation} \tau_{\Gsur}(b_0)=\sum_{i\ge1}p^{-k_i}\notin\Q. \end{equation}

definitions.text: Define the discrete additive group and distinguished element \[ V=\F_p^{(\Gamma)}/W_0,\qquad v_*=[\mathbf e_1]\in V, \] with the induced \(\Gamma\)-action, and put \[ \Gsur=V\rtimes\Gamma. \] We use the multiplication \((v,g)(v',g')=(v+gv',gg')\) in \(\Gsur\).

For $\omega\in\Omega$, its enabled graph $G_\omega$ has vertex set $\Gamma$. At $h\in\Gamma$ the allowed outgoing labels are $\mathcal J(X_\omega(h))$. The Cayley edge from $h$ to $hs$ is enabled precisely when $s$ is allowed at $h$ and $s^{-1}$ is allowed at $hs$. A copy $P$ is valid for $\omega$ if $X_\omega|_P=w_P$. Let $U_\omega$ be the complement in $\Gamma$ of the union of all valid copies.

papers.title: Arithmeticity of twisted finite correspondences for lattices over local fields
papers.abstract: We prove arithmetic exhaustion for bifinite correspondences between arbitrarily scalar-twisted group factors of ICC groups commensurable with property-$(T)$ lattices over characteristic-zero local fields and twisted group factors of arbitrary countable ICC groups. Every such correspondence is a closed summand of a finite direct sum of models obtained from actual finite-index subgroup isomorphisms and finite-dimensional projective representations of the matched cocycle ratio. The proof includes reducible products, mixed real and finite places, and quaternionic and Cayley rank-one factors.
papers.familySummary: Classifies finite-index bimodules between scalar-twisted group factors of ICC groups commensurable with property-$(T)$ lattices over characteristic-zero local fields and arbitrary ICC group factors. Every such bimodule is a summand of finite sums of models arising from finite-index subgroup isomorphisms and finite-dimensional projective representations. The classification also recovers the group, scalar cocycle and amplification scale up to the stated stable equivalence.

primaryStatements.name: Arithmetic exhaustion
primaryStatements.label: thm:arithmetic-exhaustion
primaryStatements.text: Let $\Gamma\in\mathscr K$, let $\Lambda$ be any countably infinite ICC group, and let $\mu\in Z^2(\Gamma,\mathbb T)$ and $\omega\in Z^2(\Lambda,\mathbb T)$ be normalized scalar cocycles. Every bifinite $L_\mu(\Gamma)$--$L_\omega(\Lambda)$ correspondence is unitarily isomorphic to a closed bimodule summand of a finite direct sum of the models $E(A,B,\delta,\sigma)$ in Equation \eqref{eq:intro-model}, where $A\leq\Gamma$ and $B\leq\Lambda$ have finite index, $\delta:A\to B$ is an actual group isomorphism, and $\sigma$ is a finite-dimensional projective unitary representation satisfying Equation \eqref{eq:intro-multiplier}. Conversely, every such model, finite direct sum, and closed bimodule summand is a normal bifinite correspondence. If $n=\dim_{\mathbb C}V_\sigma$, the elementary model has dimensions \[ \dim_{L_\mu(\Gamma)}E(A,B,\delta,\sigma)=n[\Lambda:B],\qquad \dim E(A,B,\delta,\sigma)_{L_\omega(\Lambda)}=n[\Gamma:A]. \]

primaryStatements.name: Elementary normality and dimensions
primaryStatements.label: cor:models-dimensions
primaryStatements.text: The correspondence $E(A,B,\delta,\sigma)$ is normal and bifinite. If $n=\dim_{\mathbb C}V_\sigma$, then \[ \dim_M E(A,B,\delta,\sigma)=n[\Lambda:B],\qquad \dim E(A,B,\delta,\sigma)_N=n[\Gamma:A]. \]

primaryStatements.name: Induced finite algebras
primaryStatements.label: prop:setup-induced-algebras
primaryStatements.text: The transports $U_a$ are strongly continuous in $a$, and $\sigma$ preserves the trace on $\mathcal N$. For $1\leq j\leq m$, let $R'_j$ be $R$ with $\Gamma_j$ omitted, put $\beta_j=\Ad W_{\Gamma_j}$, and let $\mathcal A_j$ be the commutant of the base multipliers and $W|_{R'_j}$. Then \[ (\mathcal A_j)^{\beta_j}=\mathcal N, \qquad (\mathcal A_j)^\sigma \ \text{has a faithful finite $\beta_j$-invariant trace}, \qquad \mathcal N^G=\mathbb C1. \]

primaryStatements.name: Link identities
primaryStatements.label: prop:links-link
primaryStatements.text: The one-column measurements and the forms \eqref{eq:input-1} have the following properties. \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item The image measurement in one measured copy lies in \(\mathcal A_j\), is \(\beta_j\)-equivariant, and is invariant under the source face parabolic. Its gap-stratum masses belong to \(\mathcal N\) and are scalar. Conjugating the source split frame transports the measurement by \(\sigma\). \item If the path escapes in every simple component, the link is an isometry \(\overline{\mathcal H}\otimes\mathcal H\to\mathcal K\). Its output forms are decomposable at the two bases, covariant under the two independent target shifts, invariant under the independently contracted source radicals, and invariant under simultaneous source centralizers. An image-and-stratum effect depends only on the start input and is \(1\otimes\Phi(A)\); the reverse rule is symmetric. \item If the path is active precisely in a subproduct \(G_0\), put \(N_0=\mathcal N^{G_0}\), and let \(E_{N_0}:\mathcal N\to N_0\) be the trace-preserving conditional expectation. On bounded columns the link instead has the form \begin{equation} \|J(\overline b,f)\|^2 =d^2\tau_{\mathcal N} \bigl(E_{N_0}(ff^*)E_{N_0}(bb^*)\bigr). \end{equation} Its polarized extension on finite sums is a positive semidefinite form. The same Gram covariances hold on this form space; they do not assert a tensor-product isometry. The precise Hilbert-input extensions are given in Lemma \ref{lem:links-relative-boundedness}. \item For any Borel event \(A\) determined by a gap stratum and its image flag, the finite-frame identity is \begin{equation} \langle f,\Phi(A)f\rangle =\frac1d\sum_{r=1}^k \|E(A)J(\overline{b_r},f)\|^2. \end{equation} It holds on mixed and nonmixed paths. More generally it holds for events in additional limiting coordinates which are unchanged by the ignored left Fourier shifts. When a proof starts with windows that also constrain the reverse flag or residual projectivity, those windows must first be exhausted to such an invariant event. \item The image measurements are independent of the finite regular embedding. Adding another original tensor slot gives their normal copies, tensored with the identity on that slot. This assertion concerns these compressed measurements and operators determined by their stated one-ended covariance and uniqueness. \end{enumerate} All statements use the specified order of successive limits. A contracted translate must tend to the identity in that order.

primaryStatements.name: Gap count and vertex quotients
primaryStatements.label: prop:links-gap-count
primaryStatements.text: In one measured copy, every positive stratum of a source path toward a face of type \(I\) has at most \(|I|\) infinite gaps. A vertex path has exactly one infinite gap. In a successive single-gap lex chain starting at a vertex, the stage with \(k\) source gaps has exactly \(k\) target gaps; in particular each such extension adds exactly one. For a quotient of a faster and a slower vertex translation in a common apartment, there is exactly one target gap if the two source vertices are coaxial, and at least two if they are not. Here coaxial means equal or opposite vertices on the same translation axis.

primaryStatements.name: Transverse products
primaryStatements.label: prop:transfer-transverse
primaryStatements.text: Fix face types, a thickness bound, and sufficiently small compact transverse face patches at the basepoint $o$. Suppose the supports of $f$ and $g$ lie within that thickness of the respective positive cones, with all specified positive gaps sufficiently large, and that the ideal directions of $po$ and $q^{-1}o$ belong to the fixed transverse patches. Then \[ \mu(qp)=\mu(q)+\mu(p)+O(1), \] where the error is uniform on the supports. The product in \eqref{eq:input-2} has a uniform tracial $L^2$ bound in either of the following situations: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item For each coordinate contributed by both cones, one of its two supports is restricted to a moving interval of a fixed bounded width. The separate cutoff factors may be arbitrary uniformly bounded functions. \item One of the face types is a single vertex. The cutoff factors are smooth with uniformly bounded sufficiently high seminorms in fixed compact normalized matrix charts; at finite places this means locally constant with a uniformly bounded level. \end{enumerate} To specify the retained cutoffs in the estimate, write $f=h_Af_1$ and $g=h_Bg_1$. In case \textup{(i)}, these four factors may be arbitrary uniformly bounded scalar functions. In case \textup{(ii)}, each factor has the smooth seminorm bounds or fixed clopen level just specified. Then \begin{equation} \big\|(D_gB_0)(D_fA_0)\big\|_2^2 \leq C\|A_0\|_\infty\|B_0\|_\infty \|D_{h_A}A_0\|_2\|D_{h_B}B_0\|_2. \end{equation} The constant includes the stated bounds on the scalar factors. The same estimate holds for a joint symbol, meaning the bilinear Fourier sum \[ \sum_{q,p}h_B(q)h_A(p)m(q,p)b_qa_p\,w_qw_p, \] where $w_qw_p$ is the actual twisted monomial product and $m$ is a smooth joint function on the fixed compact normalized charts, with sufficiently many uniformly bounded derivatives. At finite places use a fixed clopen level. The support and transverse restrictions remain in force. Consequently an additional smooth cutoff factor whose one-column Hilbert norm tends to zero makes the product tend to zero, provided the other bounds and the other cut Hilbert norm remain bounded. In particular, for a fixed finite trace of mass $t$, \[ \big\|(D_gB_0)(D_fA_0)\big\|_2 \leq C\sqrt t\,\|A_0\|_\infty\|B_0\|_\infty. \]

primaryStatements.name: Type comparison
primaryStatements.label: prop:transfer-types
primaryStatements.text: There is a unique permutation $p$ of the full relative type list $\Pi$ such that every candidate at source type $i$ takes values in target type $p(i)$. It preserves opposition: $p(i^*)=p(i)^*$. For noncoaxial source vertices of dual types, all ordered products of candidates vanish on transverse target patches. The permutation preserves the collection of isolated types.

primaryStatements.name: Sharpness at isolated types
primaryStatements.label: prop:transfer-isolated-sharpness
primaryStatements.text: At an isolated source vertex, every candidate is sharp, and all candidate choices agree.

definitions.label: def:class
definitions.text: Let $\mathscr K$ be the class of countably infinite ICC groups abstractly commensurable with a lattice in a finite nonempty product \[ G=\prod_{i=1}^r G_i,\qquad G_i=\mathbf H_i(k_i)^+. \] Here $k_i$ is $\mathbb R$, $\mathbb C$, or a finite extension of $\mathbb Q_p$; the primes may differ. The algebraic group $\mathbf H_i$ is connected, adjoint, and absolutely simple over $k_i$. The superscript $+$ denotes the subgroup generated by the $k_i$-points of the unipotent radicals of proper $k_i$-parabolic subgroups. Each $G_i$ is required to be noncompact and to have Kazhdan's property $(T)$. A lattice is discrete and has finite Haar covolume. Abstract commensurability means an actual isomorphism between finite-index subgroups. ICC means that every nonidentity conjugacy class is infinite. No irreducibility, cocompactness, product decomposition, or torsion hypothesis is imposed on the lattice.

definitions.label: def:ray-admissible
definitions.text: An admissible representation for \(T\) consists of a finite factor \[ D=B\bar\otimes L_\eta(\Gamma) \] and a normalized projective representation \(\Theta:\Gamma\to\mathcal U(D)\) such that \[ D\cap\Theta(\Gamma)'=\mathbb C1 \] and the representation \begin{equation} \gamma\longmapsto\Ad\Delta_T(\Theta(\gamma)) \quad\hbox{on}\quad L^2\bigl(B(L^2(X_T))\bar\otimes D,\Tr\otimes\tau\bigr) \end{equation} has no invariant vector. Here \(\Delta_T(u_h)=\lambda_{X_T}(h_T)\otimes u_h\), with the identity action on \(B\). The scalar multiplier of \(\Theta\) is not required to equal \(\eta\).

definitions.name: Controlled angular masks
definitions.label: def:scale-mask-controls
definitions.text: Fix an integer $m\ge1$ and positive constants specifying support diameter, separation, and overlap. A controlled family at scale $0<\delta\le\delta_0$ consists of smooth functions $\{f_A\}_A,\{g_D\}_D$ on $B_T$ and a set $\mathscr R$ of ordered pairs $(A,D)$. Each support lies in a ball of radius $a\delta$; each family of centers has boundedly many points in every ball of radius $b\delta$, for each fixed $b$; and \[ \operatorname{dist}_T(\supp f_A,\supp g_D)\ge c\delta \quad ((A,D)\in\mathscr R). \] After translation and graded dilation to a unit chart, derivatives through order $m$ are bounded by one. Changing this last bound only changes the constants by scalar rescaling. We permit any fixed enlargement of the diameter, overlap, or separation parameters. Set \[ p_\delta(x,y) =\sum_{(A,D)\in\mathscr R} P_x(f_A)^*P_y(|g_D|^2)P_x(f_A). \] This is a positive operator. Bounded overlap and spectral calculus give $0\le p_\delta(x,y)\le C_0 1$, with $C_0$ depending only on the controls, without any commutation assumption between $P_x$ and $P_y$.

definitions.label: def:scale-ordered-kernel
definitions.text: For $F\in C^\infty(B_T\times B_T)$, its ordered evaluation is \[ \mathcal K_{x,y}(F) =\iint F(w,v)\,P_y(dw)P_x(dv). \] More explicitly, on finitely many coordinate rectangles expand $F$ as an absolutely summable series of products of smooth functions; replace $g(w)f(v)$ by $P_y(g)P_x(f)$ and sum in operator norm. Smooth Fourier expansion with sufficiently many derivatives gives absolute summability, with the sum bounded by a fixed sufficiently high smooth seminorm of $F$. Approximation in that seminorm by finite separated smooth sums proves independence of the coordinate expansion. A smooth kernel has horizontal order at least one if it vanishes on the diagonal. It has horizontal order at least two if, in addition, its derivative in the second variable vanishes there on $\mathcal V_T$. These conditions are invariant under the coordinate changes used below.

papers.title: The arithmetic category and stable recovery of lattice factors
papers.abstract: We prove stable canonical recovery for scalar-twisted group factors of ICC groups commensurable with property-$(T)$ lattices over characteristic-zero local fields. Every specified stable isomorphism to a scalar-twisted factor of any countably infinite ICC group recovers the group, the cocycle up to a normalized cochain, and equal amplification scales, with an implementing partial isometry in the given matrix corners. We compute the arithmetic correspondence subcategory for arbitrary countable ICC groups, including all bounded maps, summands, conjugates, and Connes fusion, and combine it with the companion's arithmetic exhaustion theorem. Multiplication also recovers arbitrary finite-index factor neighbors, with the exact projective condition on the matched cocycle ratio.
papers.familySummary: Classifies finite-index bimodules between scalar-twisted group factors of ICC groups commensurable with property-$(T)$ lattices over characteristic-zero local fields and arbitrary ICC group factors. Every such bimodule is a summand of finite sums of models arising from finite-index subgroup isomorphisms and finite-dimensional projective representations. The classification also recovers the group, scalar cocycle and amplification scale up to the stated stable equivalence.

primaryStatements.name: Presentation equivalence and stable canonical recovery
primaryStatements.label: thm:stable
primaryStatements.text:
Let $\Lambda\in\mathscr K$ and let $\Pi$ be any countably infinite ICC group. Let $\omega,
u$ be arbitrary normalized scalar cocycles on them, and let $t,s>0$. Then \[ L_\omega(\Lambda)^t\cong L_
u(\Pi)^s \] if and only if $t=s$ and there are an isomorphism $\delta:\Lambda	o\Pi$ and a normalized cochain $b:\Lambda	o\mathbb T$ such that  egin{equation} \omega(g,h)=b(g)b(h)b(gh)^{-1}
u(\delta(g),\delta(h)). \end{equation} Every specified isomorphism at unit scale has the form \[ 	heta(u_g)=w\,b(g)v_{\delta(g)}w^* \] for a unitary $w$ in the target. More explicitly, put $M=L_\omega(\Lambda)$ and $N=L_
u(\Pi)$, and let \[ 	heta:pM_n(M)p\longrightarrow qM_m(N)q \] be a specified isomorphism, where the unnormalized traces of $p$ and $q$ are $t$ and $s$. Then $t=s$, and one may choose $\delta,b$ as above and $z\in M_{m,n}(N)$ so that, for the canonical map $\varphi(u_g)=b(g)v_{\delta(g)}$, \[ z^*z=\varphi^{(n)}(p),\qquad zz^*=q, \qquad 	heta(x)=z\varphi^{(n)}(x)z^*. \] Whenever such an isomorphism exists, the recovered comparison group $\Pi$ belongs to $\mathscr K$. In particular every factor $L_\omega(\Lambda)$ in this class has trivial fundamental group.

primaryStatements.name: All factor endpoints
primaryStatements.label: thm:endpoints
primaryStatements.text: Let $\Gamma\in\mathscr K$, let $\mu$ be any normalized scalar cocycle on $\Gamma$, and let $P$ be a $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor with separable predual. There is a nonzero bifinite $L_\mu(\Gamma)$--$P$ correspondence if and only if \[ P\cong L_\omega(\Lambda)^t \] for a countably infinite ICC group $\Lambda$, a normalized scalar cocycle $\omega$ on $\Lambda$, and $t>0$, for which there are finite-index subgroups $A\leq\Gamma$ and $B\leq\Lambda$, an actual isomorphism $\delta:A\to B$, and a nonzero finite-dimensional projective unitary representation of $A$ with multiplier \[ \frac{\mu|_{A\times A}}{\delta^*(\omega|_{B\times B})}. \] In particular, the reconstructed group $\Lambda$ belongs to $\mathscr K$.

primaryStatements.name: All finite correspondences
primaryStatements.label: thm:correspondences
primaryStatements.text: Let $\Gamma\in\mathscr K$, let $\Lambda$ be any countably infinite ICC group, and let $\mu$ and $\omega$ be arbitrary normalized scalar cocycles on these groups. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item Every nonzero bifinite $L_\mu(\Gamma)$--$L_\omega(\Lambda)$ correspondence is a closed bimodule summand of a finite direct sum of the models in Equation \eqref{eq:intro-model}. \item Every such correspondence has a finite orthogonal decomposition into full-germ orbit bundles. After choosing distinct germ orbits and allowing zero fibres, all bounded bimodule maps are \begin{equation} \Hom_{M\text{--}N}\!\left(\bigoplus_d H(d,\sigma_d), \bigoplus_d H(d,\tau_d)\right) =\bigoplus_d\Hom_{C_d,\alpha}(\sigma_d,\tau_d). \end{equation} Norm, adjoint, and composition are fibrewise. Projection summands are exactly projective-representation summands in the fibres. A correspondence $K=\bigoplus_d H(d,\sigma_d)$ has dimensions \[ \dim_M K=\sum_d\dim_{\mathbb C}(\sigma_d)[\Lambda:B_d],\qquad \dim K_N=\sum_d\dim_{\mathbb C}(\sigma_d)[\Gamma:A_d]. \] Both are positive integers when $K\ne0$. \item Conjugation and Connes fusion correspond to conjugation and balanced tensor product of these bundles. They are equivalently computed by finite double-coset induction. The scalar transports are given explicitly in Equations \eqref{eq:input-A1} and \eqref{eq:input-A2} and Section \ref{sec:calculus}. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.name: Arithmetic exhaustion, companion Theorem 1.2
primaryStatements.label: prop:recovery-exhaustion
primaryStatements.text: Let $\Gamma\in\mathscr K$, let $\Lambda$ be any countably infinite ICC group, and let $\mu,\omega$ be arbitrary normalized scalar cocycles. Every nonzero separable bifinite $L_\mu(\Gamma)$--$L_\omega(\Lambda)$ correspondence is a closed bimodule summand of a finite direct sum of the models $E(A,B,\delta,\sigma)$ in Equation \eqref{eq:intro-model}, with the exact multiplier in Equation \eqref{eq:intro-multiplier}.

primaryStatements.name: Dimensions of the actual orbit modules
primaryStatements.label: prop:calculus-dimensions
primaryStatements.text: For a finite-dimensional $\alpha|_{C_d}$-projective representation $\gamma$, \begin{equation} \dim_M H(d,\gamma) =\dim_{\mathbb C}(\gamma)[\Lambda:B_d], \qquad \dim H(d,\gamma)_N =\dim_{\mathbb C}(\gamma)[\Gamma:A_d]. \end{equation} For the original model these formulas read \[ \dim_M E(A,B,\delta,\sigma) =\dim_{\mathbb C}(\sigma)[\Lambda:B], \qquad \dim E(A,B,\delta,\sigma)_N =\dim_{\mathbb C}(\sigma)[\Gamma:A]. \] Zero fibres may be omitted. Dimensions add under finite orthogonal sums.

primaryStatements.name: Full-germ intertwiner formula
primaryStatements.label: thm:calculus-hom
primaryStatements.text: Choose finitely many distinct $D$-orbits of germs and a representative $d$ in each orbit. Let $\gamma_d,\tau_d$ be finite-dimensional projective representations of $C_d$, with multiplier $\alpha|_{C_d}$; either may be zero. Then \begin{equation} \Hom_{M\text{--}N} \left(\bigoplus_dH(d,\gamma_d),\, \bigoplus_dH(d,\tau_d)\right) =\bigoplus_d\Hom_{C_d,\alpha}(\gamma_d,\tau_d). \end{equation} The equality is implemented by restriction to the representative fibres and extension by transport. Norm is the maximum of the fibre norms, and adjoints and composition are fibrewise. In particular all closed bimodule summands are obtained by taking invariant subspaces of these finite-dimensional fibre representations.

primaryStatements.name: Fusion as a counting tensor-fibre bundle
primaryStatements.label: prop:calculus-fusion
primaryStatements.text: There is a unitary correspondence identification \begin{equation} \mathcal H_X\mathbin{\bar\otimes}_{N}\mathcal H_Y \cong\mathcal H_Z \end{equation} under which outer transport is Equation \eqref{eq:input-A2}. The space $Z$ has finitely many outer-group orbits. For each $z=[(x,y)]$, its stabilizer is a finite-index subgroup-isomorphism graph with germ $d_y d_x$. Regrouping these orbits over full stabilizers by Equation \eqref{eq:calculus-regrouping} gives the full-germ decomposition of the fusion.

primaryStatements.name: Arithmetic constraints on the corner
primaryStatements.label: prop:endpoints-corner-constraints
primaryStatements.text: For the corner in Lemma \ref{lem:endpoints-minimal-corner}, the group \(\Lambda\) is countably infinite and ICC. There are finite-index subgroups \(A\leq\Gamma\), \(B\leq\Lambda\), an actual group isomorphism \(\delta:A\to B\), and a finite-dimensional projective representation with multiplier \(\mu|_A/\delta^*(\omega|_B)\).

definitions.text: Let $\mathscr K$ be the class of countably infinite ICC groups abstractly commensurable with a lattice in a finite nonempty product \[ G=\prod_{i=1}^r G_i,\qquad G_i=\mathbf H_i(k_i)^+. \] Here $k_i$ is $\mathbb R$, $\mathbb C$, or a finite extension of $\mathbb Q_p$; the primes may differ. The algebraic group $\mathbf H_i$ is connected, adjoint, and absolutely simple over $k_i$. The superscript $+$ denotes the subgroup generated by the $k_i$-points of the unipotent radicals of proper $k_i$-parabolic subgroups. Each $G_i$ is required to be noncompact and to have Kazhdan's property $(T)$. A lattice is discrete and has finite Haar covolume. Abstract commensurability means an actual isomorphism between finite-index subgroups. ICC means that every nonidentity conjugacy class is infinite. No irreducibility, cocompactness, product decomposition, or torsion hypothesis is imposed on the lattice.

papers.title: An isomorphism of the free group factors
papers.abstract: We solve the free group factor isomorphism problem affirmatively by proving that $L(\mathbb F_2)$ and $L(\mathbb F_3)$ are isomorphic as tracial von Neumann algebras. The classical free group factor alternative then implies that all interpolated free group factors, including $L(\mathbb F_\infty)$, are isomorphic and have fundamental group $\mathbb R_{\gt 0}$.
papers.familySummary: Resolves the free group factor isomorphism problem: $L(\mathbb F_2)\cong L(\mathbb F_3)$, and hence all interpolated free group factors, including $L(\mathbb F_\infty)$, are isomorphic. Their common factor has fundamental group $\mathbb R_{\gt 0}$.

The classical free group factor alternative then implies that all interpolated free group factors, including $L(\F_\infty)$, are isomorphic and have fundamental group $\R_{>0}$.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: There exists a unital normal trace-preserving $*$-isomorphism \[ \Phi:L(\F_2)\longrightarrow L(\F_3). \]

primaryStatements.name: Isomorphism of consecutive ranks
primaryStatements.label: thm:rank-step
primaryStatements.text: For every integer $n\geq3$ there is a unital trace-preserving normal $*$-isomorphism \[ L(\F_n)\cong L(\F_{n+1}). \]

primaryStatements.name: Polynomial flow and displacement bounds
primaryStatements.label: prop:flow
primaryStatements.text: There is a one-parameter group $(\beta_t)_{t\in\R}$ of unital trace-preserving normal $*$-automorphisms of $M$ that fixes $S$ and whose restriction to \[ B=C^*(A_1,\ldots,A_n,S) \] is point-norm continuous. Writing $A_j(t)=\beta_t(A_j)$ and evaluating group words at this tuple, the paths satisfy \begin{equation} \frac{d}{dt}A_j(t)=\ii s_t(h_j)A_j(t),\qquad s_t(k)=\sum_{g\in\Gamma}k(g)A_g(t)SA_g(t)^*,\qquad A_j(0)=A_j. \end{equation} The derivatives here are in operator norm. With $K=3\pi$ as in \eqref{eq:free-sum}, for every $t\in\R$, \begin{align} \norm{\beta_t(A_j)-A_j} &\leq |t|K\|h_j\|_{\ell^2}, \\ \norm{\beta_t(A_w)-\exp(\ii tS)A_w} &\leq |t|K\|D_w-\e\|_{\ell^2} \qquad(w\in\Gamma). \end{align} In particular, at $t=1$ the target in \eqref{eq:word-displacement} is $CA_w$.

primaryStatements.name: Approximating the extra generator in one step
primaryStatements.label: prop:perturbation
primaryStatements.text: Let $n\geq 3$, and let $(A_1,\ldots,A_n,C)$ be a freely generating Haar tuple in a finite von Neumann algebra $(M,\tau)$. For every $\varepsilon>0$ there are a trace-preserving normal automorphism $\alpha$ of $M$ and a word $w\in\F_n$ such that, with $A_j'=\alpha(A_j)$, \begin{equation} \max_{1\leq j\leq n}\norm{A_j'-A_j}<\varepsilon, \qquad \norm{A_w'-C}<\varepsilon. \end{equation} The tuple $(A_1',\ldots,A_n',C')$, where $C'=\alpha(C)$, is again freely generating Haar. Here the target in the second estimate is the original $C$; the new completion is \[ C'=C A_w^*, \] where $A_w$ is evaluated on the original $n$-tuple.

primaryStatements.label: cor:all-interpolated
primaryStatements.text: For all $1<r,s\leq\infty$ there is a unital normal trace-preserving $*$-isomorphism $L(\F_r)\cong L(\F_s)$. Moreover, \[ \mathcal F\bigl(L(\F_r)\bigr)=\R_{>0} \qquad(1<r\leq\infty). \]

primaryStatements.name: Dependence on von Neumann generators
primaryStatements.label: cor:entropy-dimensions
primaryStatements.text: Let $M=L(\F_2)$ with its canonical trace. For every integer $n\geq2$ there are a self-adjoint $n$-tuple $X^{(n)}$ and a self-adjoint $2n$-tuple $Y^{(n)}$ such that \[ W^*(X^{(n)})=W^*(Y^{(n)})=M \] and \[ \delta(X^{(n)})=\delta_0(X^{(n)})=n, \qquad \delta^*(Y^{(n)})=\delta^\star(Y^{(n)})=n. \] Consequently, none of $\delta,\delta_0,\delta^*,\delta^\star$ is invariant under changing a finite self-adjoint $W^*$-generating tuple of a tracial von Neumann algebra. Each takes unbounded values on such generating tuples of the single factor $L(\F_2)$.

definitions.text: A freely generating Haar $d$-tuple in $M$ is a tuple of unitaries $U=(U_1,\ldots,U_d)$ such that $W^*(U)=M$ and \[ \tau(U_g)=0\qquad(g\in\F_d\setminus\{e\}). \] Here $U_g$ is the evaluation of the reduced group word $g$ in $U$, with inverse letters evaluated as adjoints.

lean.scopeText: The free group factor problem asks whether the von Neumann algebras of free groups of different ranks are isomorphic. The formalization proves that interpolated free group factors with any parameters $r,s>1$, including the infinite parameter, are normally trace-preservingly isomorphic. The paper's fundamental-group conclusion is a further consequence rather than a separate selected statement here.

papers.title: Kadison's similarity theorem through uniform derivation estimates
papers.abstract: We prove that every bounded complex-linear unital algebra homomorphism from a unital complex C∗-algebra into the bounded operators on an arbitrary Hilbert space is similar to a $*$-homomorphism. This resolves Kadison's similarity conjecture positively. We also obtain one universal hyperreflexivity constant for all unital von Neumann algebras on arbitrary complex Hilbert spaces.
papers.familySummary: Proves Kadison's similarity conjecture: every bounded complex-linear unital algebra homomorphism from a unital complex C∗-algebra to operators on a Hilbert space becomes a $*$-homomorphism after conjugation by a bounded invertible operator.
papers.subject: Operator algebras
papers.sourceAbstract: We prove that every bounded complex-linear unital algebra homomorphism from a unital complex $C^*$-algebra into the bounded operators on an arbitrary Hilbert space is similar to a $*$-homomorphism. This resolves Kadison's similarity conjecture positively. We also obtain one universal hyperreflexivity constant for all unital von Neumann algebras on arbitrary complex Hilbert spaces.

primaryStatements.name: Similarity
primaryStatements.label: thm:similarity
primaryStatements.text: Let \(A\) be any unital complex \(C^*\)-algebra, let \(H\) be any complex Hilbert space, and let \(\pi:A\to\mathcal B(H)\) be a bounded, complex-linear, unital algebra homomorphism. There exists an operator \(S\in\mathcal B(H)\), invertible with bounded inverse, such that \[ \rho(a)=S\pi(a)S^{-1}\qquad(a\in A) \] is a \(*\)-homomorphism. In particular, \(\rho(a^*)=\rho(a)^*\) for every \(a\in A\).

primaryStatements.name: Uniform commutator estimate
primaryStatements.label: thm:universal
primaryStatements.text: There is an absolute constant \(C<\infty\) such that, for every complex Hilbert space \(K\), every unital von Neumann algebra \(P\subset\mathcal B(K)\), every \(Y\in\mathcal B(K)\), every integer \(h\ge1\), and every \(X\in M_h(P)\), \begin{equation} \|[Y^{(h)},X]\|\le C\,g_P(Y)\,\|X\|. \end{equation} Here \(M_h(P)\) acts naturally on \(K^h\), and \([T,U]=TU-UT\).

primaryStatements.name: Universal hyperreflexivity
primaryStatements.label: cor:hyperreflexivity
primaryStatements.text: Let \(H\) be any complex Hilbert space and let \(M\subset\mathcal B(H)\) be a unital von Neumann algebra. For \(T\in\mathcal B(H)\), set \[ \alpha_M(T)=\sup\{\|(1-e)Te\|:e\in M',\ e=e^*=e^2\}. \] Then, with the absolute constant \(C\) from Theorem \ref{thm:universal}, \begin{equation} \dist(T,M)\le 2C\,\alpha_M(T)\qquad(T\in\mathcal B(H)). \end{equation} Thus every such \(M\) is hyperreflexive with constant at most \(2C\), independently of the algebra, its representation, and the Hilbert space. No optimality of this constant is asserted.

primaryStatements.name: Kirchberg's similarity--derivation equivalence
primaryStatements.label: thm:kirchberg
primaryStatements.text: For a unital \(C^*\)-algebra \(A\), the following properties are equivalent. \begin{enumerate} \item Every bounded unital homomorphism \(\pi:A\to\mathcal B(H)\), on any Hilbert space \(H\), is similar by a bounded invertible operator to a \(*\)-homomorphism. \item For every faithful unital \(*\)-representation \(\sigma:A\to\mathcal B(K)\), on any Hilbert space \(K\), every bounded linear map \(\Delta:A\to\mathcal B(K)\) satisfying \[ \Delta(ab)=\Delta(a)\sigma(b)+\sigma(a)\Delta(b) \] has the form \(\Delta(a)=V\sigma(a)-\sigma(a)V\) for some \(V\in\mathcal B(K)\). \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.name: Free-product corner estimate
primaryStatements.label: thm:free-corner
primaryStatements.text: Let $\mathcal L=D*A_0$ be as above, let $t=1/N$ for an integer $N\geq2$, and suppose that $G\in\mathcal B(L^2(\mathcal L))$ commutes with $L_D$. Suppose that $\epsilon\geq0$ and \begin{equation} \|[G,L_x]\|\leq\epsilon\|x\| \qquad (x\in e\mathcal L e, \ e\in D\text{ a projection with }\tau(e)=t). \end{equation} If $s=s^*=s^{-1}\in A_0$ and $\tau(s)=0$, then \begin{equation} \left\|P_{L^2(A_0)}[G,L_s]\big|_{L^2(A_0)}\right\| \leq c_1\epsilon, \qquad c_1=6\pi^2(1+4c_0). \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Finite standard multiplicities
primaryStatements.label: prop:finite-copies
primaryStatements.text: Let \(M\) be a separable-predual \(\mathrm{II}_1\) factor, and let \(M\) act on \(H_r=L^2(M)^r\) by common left multiplication, where \(r\geq1\) is finite. For every \(Y\in\mathcal B(H_r)\), every finite \(h\geq1\), and every \(X\in M_h(M)\), \[ \norm{[Y^{(h)},X]} \leq (3c_1+2)\,g_M(Y)\,\norm{X}. \] Here \(X\) denotes its entrywise action on \(H_r^h\); the constant is independent of \(M,r,h\).

primaryStatements.label: prop:factor-representations
primaryStatements.text: Let $P\subset\B(K)$ be a unital factor acting on a separable Hilbert space. For every $Y\in\B(K)$, every $h\ge1$, and every $X\in M_h(P)$, \[ \norm{[Y^{(h)},X]} \le C_{\mathrm{fac}}\,g_P(Y)\,\norm{X}. \]

primaryStatements.label: prop:separable-estimate
primaryStatements.text: Let $P\subset\B(K)$ be any unital von Neumann algebra on a separable Hilbert space. Then \[ \norm{[Y^{(h)},X]}\le C\,g_P(Y)\,\norm{X} \qquad(Y\in\B(K),\ X\in M_h(P),\ h\ge1). \]

lean.scopeText:
Kadison's similarity problem asks whether every bounded unital homomorphism from a unital complex $C^*$-algebra into operators on a Hilbert space is similar to a $*$-homomorphism. The formalization proves this for arbitrary Hilbert spaces. It also gives one universal hyperreflexivity constant for all unital von Neumann algebras.

The linked commutator estimate is uniform over all finite matrix amplifications: its constant is independent of the algebra, Hilbert space, and amplification size. This is the quantitative derivation estimate supporting the similarity result.

papers.title: Universal strong Kadison–Kastler stability
papers.abstract: We prove that sufficiently close unital von Neumann algebras are conjugate by a unitary arbitrarily close to the identity. The tolerance depends only on the prescribed distance of that unitary from the identity, uniformly over all algebras, representations, and Hilbert spaces. This resolves the strong Kadison–Kastler conjecture.

primaryStatements.name: Strong Kadison--Kastler stability
primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: For every $\eps>0$ there is $\delta=\delta(\eps)>0$ such that the following holds. If $H$ is any complex Hilbert space and $M,N\subseteq\B(H)$ are unital von Neumann algebras with identity $I_H$ and $d(M,N)<\delta$, there is a unitary $u\in\B(H)$ satisfying \[ uMu^*=N,\qquad \norm{u-I_H}<\eps. \]

primaryStatements.name: Amenable near inclusions
primaryStatements.label: thm:amenable
primaryStatements.text: Let $R,Q\subseteq\B(H)$ be von Neumann algebras with identity $I$, with $R$ amenable. If $R\subset_\gamma Q$ and $\gamma<1/100$, there is a unitary $v\in(R\cup Q)”$ such that \[ vRv^*\subseteq Q,\qquad \norm{v-I}\le150\gamma. \] If also $Q\subset_\gamma R$ and $\gamma<1/101$, the same conclusion holds with $vRv^*=Q$.

primaryStatements.name: UCP criterion
primaryStatements.label: prop:ucp
primaryStatements.text:
Let $P,Q$ be von Neumann algebras, let $ho:P	o\B(H)$ be a faithful normal unital representation, and let $Q\subseteq\B(H)$ have the same identity. Suppose that $F:P	o Q$ is UCP and \[ 
orm{F-ho}_{\cb}\le e<10^{-3},\qquad \sup_{y\in Q_1}\dist(y,ho(P)_1)\le g,\qquad g+e<1. \] Then there is a normal unital $*$-isomorphism $	heta:P	o Q$ and a unitary $u\in\B(H)$ such that \[ 
orm{	heta-ho}_{\cb}\le32e,\qquad uho(x)u^*=	heta(x)\ (x\in P),\qquad 
orm{u-I}\le128e. \] The map $F$ need not be normal.

primaryStatements.name: Uniform amplification
primaryStatements.label: thm:amplification
primaryStatements.text: There is an absolute constant \(C_{\mathrm{amp}}\) such that, for every type \(\II_1\) factor \(M\subseteq\B(H)\) on a separable Hilbert space and every selfadjoint \(h\in\B(H)\), \[ \norm{\ad_h|_M}_{\cb}\le C_{\mathrm{amp}}\norm{\ad_h|_M}. \] The constant is independent of \(M\), its representation, and \(H\).

primaryStatements.name: Sum of squared word bounds through one label
primaryStatements.label: cor:through-label
primaryStatements.text: For every integer $N\geq1$ there is an integer $d_0(N)$ such that, whenever $d\geq d_0(N)$, the constants \eqref{eq:fw-beta} satisfy \begin{equation} \max_{1\leq a\leq d} \sum_{\substack{W\text{ a multiset from }\{1,\ldots,d\}\\ |W|=r,\ a\in W}} \beta_W^2\leq64 \qquad(1\leq r\leq N). \end{equation} Membership $a\in W$ here means that $a$ occurs at least once; each multiset is counted once, regardless of that multiplicity. In particular, for free copies as in \cref{lem:free-words}, the norm bounds and \eqref{eq:fw-through-label} hold simultaneously through length $N$ after choosing this one threshold for $d$.

primaryStatements.name: Uniform stability of finite factors
primaryStatements.label: thm:finite
primaryStatements.text: There are a number $t_{\mathrm{fin}}>0$ and a nondecreasing function $\eta_{\mathrm{fin}}:(0,t_{\mathrm{fin}})\to(0,\infty)$, with $\eta_{\mathrm{fin}}(t)\to0$ as $t\downarrow0$, having the following property. Let $H$ be a separable nonzero Hilbert space, let $M\subseteq\B(H)$ be a unital finite factor, and let $N\subseteq\B(H)$ be a von Neumann algebra with the same identity. If $d(M,N)<t<t_{\mathrm{fin}}$, then $N$ is a finite factor and there is a unitary $u\in\B(H)$ such that \[ uMu^*=N,\qquad \norm{u-I_H}\le\eta_{\mathrm{fin}}(t). \] The threshold and function are independent of $M,N$ and their representations.

primaryStatements.name: Common-position theorem
primaryStatements.label: prop:finite-common-position
primaryStatements.text: Let $M,N$ be separable-predual $\II_1$ factors acting nondegenerately on one Hilbert space, with mutual strict $g$-near inclusions, where $0<g<1.74\cdot10^{-13}$. Suppose that an amenable von Neumann subalgebra $R\subseteq M\cap N$ satisfies $R'\cap M\subseteq R$. There are faithful normal representations $\pi:M\to\B(K)$ and $\rho:N\to\B(K)$, a common unit vector $\Omega$, and a number $\beta<50948\sqrt g$ such that: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=*] \item both images are in standard tracial position with vector $\Omega$; \item $\pi|_R=\rho|_R$, and the images have mutual strict $\beta$-near inclusions; \item for original contractions $x\in M$, $y\in N$, \[ \norm{\pi(x)-\rho(y)}\le\beta+\norm{x-y}; \] \item if $e_R$ is the projection onto $\overline{\pi(R)\Omega}$, then $(\pi(M)\cup\{e_R\})”=(\rho(N)\cup\{e_R\})”$. \end{enumerate} The space $K$ can be taken separable.

primaryStatements.label: prop:finite-standard-isomorphism
primaryStatements.text: There are absolute constants $b_0>0$ and $C_{\mathrm{st}}>0$ such that the following holds. Let $M,N\subseteq\B(K)$ be type $\II_1$ factors on a separable Hilbert space in common standard tracial position with vector $\Omega$. Suppose they contain a common hyperfinite $\II_1$ subfactor $R$, irreducible in $M$ and generated by increasing matrix algebras, and that $J_MrJ_M=J_NrJ_N$ for every $r\in R$. If $d(M,N)<b<b_0$, then there is a normal unital star-isomorphism $\vartheta:M\to N$ satisfying \[ \sup_{x\in M_1}\norm{\vartheta(x)-x}\le C_{\mathrm{st}}b. \]

definitions.name: Prepared pair
definitions.label: def:prepared-pair
definitions.text: A prepared pair consists of type $\III_1$ factors $M,N\subseteq\B(H)$ on a separable Hilbert space, a common cyclic separating unit vector $\Omega$, and a hyperfinite $\II_1$ factor $R\subseteq M\cap N$ such that \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item $R'\cap M=R'\cap N=\C1$; \item the vector state $\varphi(x)=\ip{x\Omega}{\Omega}$ centralizes $R$ when restricted to either algebra; \item $J_MrJ_M=J_NrJ_N$ for every $r\in R$, where $J_M,J_N$ are the modular conjugations associated with $\Omega$. \end{enumerate}

lean.scopeText: The formalization proves the strong Kadison–Kastler conjecture uniformly. For every $\varepsilon>0$, there is a $\delta>0$ such that any two unital von Neumann algebras on the same complex Hilbert space at Kadison–Kastler distance below $\delta$ are conjugate by a unitary $u$ with $\lVert u-1\rVert<\varepsilon$. The tolerance depends only on $\varepsilon$, uniformly over the algebras, their representations, and the Hilbert space.

papers.title: Near Inclusions of von Neumann Algebras Without Small Spatial Embeddings
papers.abstract: We give a negative answer to the unrestricted small-spatial-embedding problem for one-sided near inclusions of von Neumann algebras. On separable complex Hilbert spaces, we construct pairs of unital von Neumann algebras with common identity whose one-sided gaps tend to zero. Spatial embeddings of the source into the target exist, but every implementing unitary stays a fixed positive distance from the identity. The obstruction therefore concerns small implementing unitaries, rather than the existence of spatial embeddings.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: There exist $\varepsilon_0>0$, separable complex Hilbert spaces $H_n$, and von Neumann algebras $M_n,N_n\subseteq\mathcal B(H_n)$ with common identity $I_{H_n}$ such that \[ \gamma(M_n,N_n)\longrightarrow 0, \] but, for all sufficiently large $n$, every unitary $u\in\mathcal B(H_n)$ satisfying $uM_nu^*\subseteq N_n$ obeys \[ \|u-I_{H_n}\|\geq\varepsilon_0. \]

primaryStatements.label: prop:circle
primaryStatements.text: There are unitary representations $\pi_z:F\to\B(K)$, indexed by $z\in\mathbb T$, and operators $A_k(g)\in\B(K)$, indexed by $k\in\mathbb Z$ and $g\in F$, such that \begin{align} \pi_z(g)&=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}z^kA_k(g), &\sup_{g\in F}\|A_k(g)\|&\leq c_k, &c_k&=\mathbf 1_{\{k=0\}}+\frac{2t^{|k|}}{1-t}, \\ \pi_z(s_j)&\xrightarrow[j\to\infty]{\WOT}tzp_e. \end{align} The series in \eqref{eq:fourier} converges absolutely in operator norm, uniformly in $g$ and $z$, and \begin{equation} S_0:=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}c_k<\infty, \qquad S_1:=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}|k|c_k<\infty. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.label: prop:near
primaryStatements.text: For the algebras in \eqref{eq:algebras}, \begin{equation} \gamma(M,N)\leq C\|UV-VU\|, \qquad C:=\sum_{k,m,p,h\in\mathbb Z} c_kc_mc_pc_h|m-p|\,|h|<\infty. \end{equation} Moreover, for every $g\in G$, \begin{equation} \bigl\|W(\lambda(g)\otimes I_L)W^* -\lambda(g)\otimes f(g)\bigr\| \leq C\|UV-VU\|. \end{equation} The constant is independent of $D,U,V$.

papers.title: Close Separable C*-Algebras Without Spatial Conjugacy
papers.abstract: We disprove the separable C∗-algebraic spatial form of the Kadison–Kastler conjecture. For every ε > 0, we construct unital, norm-separable C∗-algebras on a common separable complex Hilbert space, with the same identity and Kadison–Kastler distance less than ε, that are not conjugate by any unitary. The two algebras have the same von Neumann closure.
