sections.title: Close inclusions distinguished by a tensor norm

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: For every $\varepsilon>0$ there are a separable complex Hilbert space $H$ and unital, norm-separable $C^*$-algebras $A,B\subseteq\B(H)$ with common identity $\id_H$ such that \[ \KK(A,B)<\varepsilon,\qquad A”=B”, \] but no unitary $u\in\B(H)$ satisfies $uAu^*=B$.

primaryStatements.label: prop:sequences
primaryStatements.text: Let $L$ be a nonzero separable Hilbert space, let $D\subseteq\B(L)$ be a unital norm-separable $C^*$-algebra with $Z(D)=\C\id_L$, and let $P,Q\subseteq D$ be unital $C^*$-subalgebras containing $\id_L$. On $H=\bigoplus_{n\ge1}L$, define \begin{equation} \E_D(P)=\{(x_n)_{n\ge1}:x_n\in D,\ x_n\to p\in P\text{ in norm}\}, \end{equation} and define $\E_D(Q)$ similarly. Then: \begin{enumerate} \item These are unital norm-separable $C^*$-algebras with common identity, and \begin{equation} \KK(\E_D(P),\E_D(Q))=\KK(P,Q). \end{equation} \item If a unitary conjugates $\E_D(P)$ onto $\E_D(Q)$, there are unitaries $U_n\in\B(L)$ with $U_nDU_n^*=D$ such that, for every $b\in Q$, some $p_b\in P$ satisfies \begin{equation} \norm{b-U_np_bU_n^*}\longrightarrow0. \end{equation} The same sequence $(U_n)$ works for every $b$. \item The two algebras have the same commutant, and hence the same von Neumann closure. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.label: cor:obstruction
primaryStatements.text: Under the hypotheses of Proposition \ref{prop:sequences}, suppose that $P$ has the spatial tensor-norm identity relative to $D$, whereas $Q$ does not. Then $\E_D(P)$ and $\E_D(Q)$ are not spatially conjugate. If $W\in\B(L)$ is unitary and $WPW^*=Q$, then nevertheless \[ \KK(\E_D(P),\E_D(Q))\le2\norm{W-\id_L}. \]

definitions.label: def:tensor
definitions.text: For a unital inclusion $P\subseteq D\subseteq\B(L)$, say that $P$ has the spatial tensor-norm identity relative to $D$ if \begin{equation} \norm{\sum_{i=1}^m p_i z_i}_{\B(L)} =\norm{\sum_{i=1}^m p_i\otimes z_i}_{\B(L\otimes L)} \end{equation} for every positive integer $m$, all $p_1,\ldots,p_m\in P$, and all $z_1,\ldots,z_m\in D'$.

papers.title: Bounded recovery for modular spectral averages
papers.abstract: We prove a bounded spectral recovery theorem for a von Neumann algebra with a faithful normal state whose centralizer consists only of scalars. A positive averaged squared norm for an arbitrary bounded Hilbert-space operator on shrinking modular spectral bands can be recovered on uniformly bounded algebra elements with shrinking spectral support. We apply this theorem to spectral intertwining rigidity and obtain an alternative proof of bicentralizer triviality for type III1 factors with separable predual.

papers.title: Equivariant Jiang–Su Stability for Amenable Actions in the Unital Stably Finite Case
papers.abstract: Every action of a countable discrete amenable group on a simple, separable, unital, infinite-dimensional, nuclear, stably finite complex C∗-algebra that is already Jiang–Su stable absorbs the trivial action on the Jiang–Su algebra up to cocycle conjugacy. No restriction is imposed on the action on the tracial-state simplex. This proves the unital, stably finite case of Szabó's Conjecture A on automatic equivariant Jiang–Su stability.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let \(A\) be a simple, separable, unital, infinite-dimensional, nuclear, stably finite complex \(\mathrm C^*\)-algebra satisfying \(A\cong A\otimes\Zalg\). Let \(G\) be a countable discrete amenable group and let \(\alpha:G\to\Aut(A)\) be any action. Put \[ B=A\otimes\Zalg,\qquad \beta_g=\alpha_g\otimes\operatorname{id}_{\Zalg}. \] There are a unital \(*\)-isomorphism \(\Phi:A\to B\) and unitaries \(u_g\in B\), \(g\in G\), such that \begin{align} u_e&=1,& u_{gh}&=u_g\beta_g(u_h),\\ \Phi(\alpha_g(a))&=u_g\beta_g(\Phi(a))u_g^* &&(g\in G,\ a\in A). \end{align}

primaryStatements.name: Szab\'o--Wouters
primaryStatements.label: thm:absorption
primaryStatements.text: Let a countable discrete amenable group act on a separable, unital, simple, nuclear, \(\Zalg\)-stable \(\mathrm C^*\)-algebra with nonempty tracial-state space. If the action has equivariant uniform property Gamma, it is cocycle conjugate to its tensor product with the trivial action on \(\Zalg\).

primaryStatements.name: Commuting orbit rows
primaryStatements.label: prop:rows
primaryStatements.text: There are unital embeddings \(\iota_i\colon\Zalg\to A^\omega\), \(i\geq 1\), for which the unital orbit algebras \[ C_i=C^*\bigl(\bar\alpha_g(\iota_i(\Zalg)):g\in G\bigr) \] commute with \(A\) and commute pairwise. In particular, \[ C=C^*\Bigl(\bigcup_{i\geq 1}C_i\Bigr) \subseteq A^\omega\cap A' \] is unital, separable, and \(\bar\alpha\)-invariant, and \(\T(C)\neq\varnothing\). Moreover, there are self-adjoint elements \(x_{i,g}\in C_i\), \(i\geq 1\), \(g\in G\), and a constant \(M<\infty\), such that \begin{equation} \|x_{i,g}\|\leq M,\qquad \varphi(x_{i,g})=0,\qquad \varphi(x_{i,g}^2)=1 \quad\bigl(\varphi\in\T(C)\bigr), \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \bar\alpha_h(x_{i,g})=x_{i,hg} \qquad(i\geq1,\ g,h\in G). \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Joint ordered moment limit
primaryStatements.label: prop:joint-clt
primaryStatements.text: Let \(J\subseteq G\) be nonempty and finite. Let \(N_j\to\infty\) be a sequence of positive integers, and let \(\varphi_j\in\partial_{\mathrm e}\T(C)\). Suppose that \begin{equation} \varphi_j(k_{N_j;g,h})\longrightarrow R_{g,h} \qquad(g,h\in J). \end{equation} Then \(R=(R_{g,h})_{g,h\in J}\) is a real positive semidefinite matrix with diagonal entries one. Choose unit vectors \(v_g\), \(g\in J\), spanning a finite-dimensional real Euclidean space \(L\), with \(\langle v_g,v_h\rangle=R_{g,h}\). If \(W\) is a standard Gaussian vector in \(L\) and \(\xi_g=\langle v_g,W\rangle\), then \[ \bigl((z_{N_j,g})_{g\in J},(k_{N_j;g,h})_{g,h\in J}\bigr) \longrightarrow \bigl((\xi_g)_{g\in J},(R_{g,h})_{g,h\in J}\bigr) \] in all ordered joint moments under \(\varphi_j\). Equivalently, for every noncommutative \(*\)-polynomial \(P\) in these self-adjoint variables, \begin{equation} \varphi_j\!\left( P\bigl((z_{N_j,g})_g,(k_{N_j;g,h})_{g,h}\bigr)\right) \longrightarrow \mathbb E\,P\bigl((\xi_g)_g,(R_{g,h})_{g,h}\bigr). \end{equation} For every sequence \((N_j,\varphi_j)\) as above, a subsequence satisfying Equation \eqref{eq:covariance-convergence} exists.

primaryStatements.name: Uniform approximately invariant unitaries
primaryStatements.label: prop:uniform-unitaries
primaryStatements.text: For every finite set \(H\subset G\), every \(\eps>0\), and every integer \(m\geq1\), there are \(t>0\) and a self-adjoint element \(Q\in C\) such that \(V=\exp(\iu tQ)\) satisfies \begin{align} \sup_{\varphi\in\T(C)} \|\bar\alpha_h(V)-V\|_{2,\varphi} &<\eps &&(h\in H), \\ \sup_{\varphi\in\T(C)}|\varphi(V^\ell)| &<\eps &&(1\leq\ell\leq m). \end{align}

primaryStatements.name: A weighted Haar unitary
primaryStatements.label: prop:haar
primaryStatements.text: There is a unitary \(w\in(A^\omega\cap A')^{\bar\alpha}\) such that, for every \(a\in A\), \(\tau\in\T_\omega(A)\), and \(f\in C(\mathbb T)\), \begin{equation} \tau(af(w))=\tau(a)\int_{\mathbb T}f\,d\mu, \end{equation} where \(\mathbb T=\{z\in\C:|z|=1\}\) and \(\mu\) is normalized Haar measure.

primaryStatements.name: Equal trace projections
primaryStatements.label: prop:gamma
primaryStatements.text: The action \(\alpha\) has equivariant uniform property Gamma. The projections in Definition \ref{def:gamma} can be chosen to sum to \(1\).

definitions.label: def:gamma
definitions.text: The action \(\alpha\) has equivariant uniform property Gamma if, for every integer \(k\geq2\), there are pairwise orthogonal projections \(p_1,\ldots,p_k\in(A^\omega\cap A')^{\bar\alpha}\) with \begin{equation} \tau(ap_i)=\frac{\tau(a)}{k} \qquad(a\in A,\ \tau\in\T_\omega(A),\ 1\leq i\leq k). \end{equation}

papers.title: Cuntz comparison and Jiang–Su absorption
papers.abstract: We prove that strict comparison in the extended-functional sense implies Jiang–Su absorption for separable simple nuclear non-elementary C∗-algebras. This resolves the corresponding implication of the Toms–Winter regularity problem, including nonunital algebras and allowing unbounded traces. More generally, every separable nuclear C∗-algebra whose Cuntz semigroup is almost unperforated and fully almost divisible absorbs the Jiang–Su algebra.
papers.familySummary: Proves equivariant Jiang–Su stability for every countable discrete amenable group action on a simple separable unital infinite-dimensional nuclear stably finite Jiang–Su-stable C∗-algebra, resolving this case of Szabó's conjecture without restrictions on trace dynamics. The family also proves the unital Toms–Winter conjecture, equating strict comparison, finite nuclear dimension and Jiang–Su stability in the simple separable unital infinite-dimensional nuclear setting.

primaryStatements.name: Simple comparison and absorption
primaryStatements.label: ext:thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let $A$ be a separable simple nuclear non-elementary $C^*$-algebra. If $A$ has strict comparison in the sense of Equation \eqref{ext:eq:comparison}, then $A\cong A\otimes_{\min}\Z$.

primaryStatements.name: Absorption from condition \textup{(C)}
primaryStatements.label: thm:condition-C
primaryStatements.text: Let $A$ be a nonzero separable nuclear $C^*$-algebra satisfying \textup{(C)}. For every fixed free ultrafilter $\omega$ on $\mathbb N$, there is a unital $*$-homomorphism $\Z\to F_\omega(A)$. Consequently $A\cong A\otimes_{\min}\Z$.

primaryStatements.name: The canonical Cuntz-semigroup map
primaryStatements.label: cor:canonical
primaryStatements.text: Let $A$ be a separable nuclear $C^*$-algebra, and let $\iota:A\to A\otimes_{\min}\Z$ be $\iota(a)=a\otimes1_\Z$. If $\Cu(\iota):\Cu(A)\to\Cu(A\otimes_{\min}\Z)$ is an isomorphism, then $A\cong A\otimes_{\min}\Z$.

primaryStatements.name: An abstract Cuntz-semigroup criterion
primaryStatements.label: cor:abstract-cu
primaryStatements.text: Let $A$ be a separable nuclear $C^*$-algebra. Then \[ A\cong A\otimes_{\min}\Z \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \Cu(A)\cong\Cu(A\otimes_{\min}\Z) \text{ in the category }\mathbf{Cu}. \] The isomorphism on the right is abstract: it is not required to be induced by the first-factor embedding, or by any $*$-homomorphism.

primaryStatements.label: ext:thm:divisibility
primaryStatements.text: Let $A$ be a simple exact non-elementary $C^*$-algebra with strict comparison as in Equation \eqref{ext:eq:comparison}. For every $x\in\Cu(A)$ and integer $N\ge1$, there exists $u\in\Cu(A)$ such that $Nu\le x\le(N+1)u$.

primaryStatements.name: Condition (C) from comparison
primaryStatements.label: ext:cor:condition-C
primaryStatements.text: Let $A$ be a simple exact non-elementary $C^*$-algebra with strict comparison in the sense of Equation \eqref{ext:eq:comparison}. Then $\Cu(A)$ satisfies condition \textup{(C)}.

primaryStatements.name: Uniform approximation from below
primaryStatements.label: prop:unital-approx
primaryStatements.text: Let $A$ be a unital simple infinite-dimensional $C^*$-algebra with nonempty tracial state space $T(A)$. For every $p\in A_+$ and $\eta>0$, there are a finite integer $L$ and $w\in M_L(A)_+$ such that \[ 0\le\tau(p)-d_\tau(w)\le\eta \qquad(\tau\in T(A)), \] where matrix traces are unnormalized. No exactness, nuclearity, or comparison assumption is required.

definitions.label: loc:relative-ideal
definitions.text: For $b\in A_+$ define $J_b\subseteq A_\omega$ as follows. An element $z=(z_n)$ belongs to $J_b$ if, for every $s>0$ and $\eta>0$, there is $E\in\omega$ such that \begin{equation} d_\tau((|z_n|-s)_+)\le\eta d_\tau(b) \quad\text{for every }n\in E\text{ and every }\tau \text{ with }d_\tau(b)<\infty. \end{equation} For $d_\tau(b)=0$ this means exact zero on the left. The set $E$ is common to the entire indicated trace family. It is enough to test positive rational $s,\eta$.

papers.title: Nuclear dimension and Jiang–Su stability without elementary subquotients
papers.abstract: For separable nuclear C∗-algebras with no nonzero elementary ideal subquotients, finite nuclear dimension is equivalent to Jiang–Su stability. primaryStatements.name: Nonsimple nuclear regularity
primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let $A$ be a separable nuclear complex $C^*$-algebra with no nonzero elementary ideal subquotients. The following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $\nucdim(A)<\infty$; \item $A\cong A\otimes\Z$; \item $\nucdim(A)\le1$. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.name: Sharp bound after Jiang--Su absorption
primaryStatements.label: intro:main
primaryStatements.text: For every separable nuclear complex $C^*$-algebra $A_0$, \[ \nucdim(A_0\otimes\Z)\le1. \]

primaryStatements.name: Regularity and Cuntz-semigroup criteria
primaryStatements.label: cor:regularity-cu
primaryStatements.text: Under the hypotheses of Theorem \ref{thm:main}, let $\iota_A:A\to A\otimes\Z$ be $\iota_A(a)=a\otimes1_\Z$. The conditions of that theorem are also equivalent to each of the following: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item the canonical map $\Cu(\iota_A):\Cu(A)\to\Cu(A\otimes\Z)$ is an isomorphism in $\mathbf{Cu}$; \item there is an abstract isomorphism $\Cu(A)\cong\Cu(A\otimes\Z)$ in $\mathbf{Cu}$. \end{enumerate} The abstract isomorphism need not be induced by a $*$-homomorphism.

primaryStatements.name: Full signs in a finite maximal tensor power
primaryStatements.label: thm:tensor-intro
primaryStatements.text: For every nonzero unital complex $C^*$-algebra $D$ with no characters, there is a finite integer $n\ge1$ such that $D^{\otimes_{\max}n}$ contains two full orthogonal positive elements.

primaryStatements.name: Brown--Carri\'on--White
primaryStatements.label: prelim:bcw
primaryStatements.text: For every separable nuclear $D$ there are finite-dimensional algebras $F_n$ and c.p.c. maps \[ D\xrightarrow{\alpha_n}F_n\xrightarrow{\beta_n}D \] such that $\beta_n\alpha_n\to\id_D$ in point-norm, $\|\alpha_n(a)\alpha_n(b)\|\to0$ for orthogonal $a,b\in D_+$, and each $\beta_n$ is a finite convex combination of c.p.c. order-zero maps $F_n\to D$.

primaryStatements.name: R\o rdam's comparison criterion
primaryStatements.label: prelim:comparison
primaryStatements.text: If $D\cong D\otimes\Z$, then $W(D)$ is almost unperforated. More generally, if $W(D)$ is almost unperforated, $u,v\in D_+$, $u\in\Ideal_D(v)$, and \[ d([u])<d([v])\quad\text{for every dimension function $d$ with }d([v])=1, \] then $u\precsim v$.

primaryStatements.name: Gabe's approximate domination theorem
primaryStatements.label: prelim:domination
primaryStatements.text: Let $D$ be exact and let $\Phi,\Psi:D\to E$ be nuclear completely positive maps, with $\Psi$ of order zero. Suppose \[ \Phi(a)\in\Ideal_E(\Psi(a))\qquad(a\in D_+). \] For every finite $\mathcal F\subset D$ and $\varepsilon>0$ there are $y_1,\ldots,y_N\in E$ such that \[ \left\|\Phi(a)-\sum_{l=1}^Ny_l^*\Psi(a)y_l\right\|<\varepsilon \qquad(a\in\mathcal F). \]

primaryStatements.name: Localized comparison
primaryStatements.label: trace:comparison
primaryStatements.text: There is a sequence $m(n)\geq2$ with $m(n)\to_\omega\infty$ such that, on putting \[ P_n=D_{m(n)}\in\Z_2,\qquad P=(P_n)_\omega\in B, \qquad \Psi(a)=P(q-1/2)_+\pi(a), \] the map $\Psi\colon A\to B$ is c.p.c. order zero and, for every $j\geq1$, \begin{equation} e\pi(x_j),\ e\theta(x_j) \precsim (\Psi(a_j)-c_j)_+ \quad\text{in }B, \qquad c_j=\gamma_j/64. \end{equation}

definitions.name: Winter--Zacharias {\cite[Definition 2.1
definitions.label: prelim:nuclear-dimension
definitions.text: {WZNuclear}}] For an integer $d\ge0$, a $C^*$-algebra $D$ has nuclear dimension at most $d$, written $\nucdim(D)\le d$, if for every finite $\mathcal F\subset D$ and $\varepsilon>0$ there are finite-dimensional algebras $E_0,\ldots,E_d$, a c.p.c. map $\psi:D\to\bigoplus_{j=0}^dE_j$, and c.p.c. order-zero maps $\varphi_j:E_j\to D$ such that \[ \left\|\sum_{j=0}^d\varphi_j\psi_j(a)-a\right\|<\varepsilon \qquad(a\in\mathcal F). \] The $d+1$ summands are called colours. The sum of the return maps need not be contractive; each coloured return map must be contractive.

papers.title: Tracial projection methods and uniform property Gamma
papers.abstract: For a simple, separable, unital, infinite-dimensional, nuclear, stably finite C∗-algebra with traces, real rank zero of the uniform tracial ultrapower of its uniform tracial completion implies uniform property Γ. This answers Problem XXI of Schafhauser, Tikuisis and White affirmatively. Independently, strict comparison implies Jiang–Su absorption for simple, separable, unital, infinite-dimensional nuclear algebras, resolving the unital Toms–Winter conjecture. Under comparison tested on traces of finite target rank, we also obtain uniform property Γ and absorption for simple, separable, nuclear, stably projectionless algebras whose densely finite traces are all bounded and have a nonempty compact normalized base.

primaryStatements.name: Real rank zero and uniform property $\Gamma$
primaryStatements.label: r:thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let $A$ be a unital, separable, simple, infinite-dimensional, nuclear, stably finite $C^*$-algebra with $T(A)\ne\varnothing$, and let $B=\overline A^{T(A)}$. Fix any free ultrafilter $\omega$ on $\N$. If $B^\omega$ has real rank zero in its quotient $C^*$-norm, then there is a projection $p\in B^\omega\cap B'$ such that \[ \lambda(px)=\tfrac12\lambda(x) \qquad(x\in B,\ \lambda\in\Lambda_\omega). \] In particular, $A$ has uniform property $\Gamma$.

primaryStatements.name: The direct unital comparison route
primaryStatements.label: u:thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let $A$ be a simple, separable, unital, infinite-dimensional nuclear $C^*$-algebra with strict comparison in the preceding sense. Then $A\cong A\otimes\Z$. When $T(A)\ne\varnothing$, the proof constructs uniform property $\Gamma$ directly.

primaryStatements.name: The direct stably projectionless route
primaryStatements.label: n:thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let $A$ be a nonzero simple, separable, nuclear $C^*$-algebra such that $A\otimes\K$ has no nonzero projections. Suppose that every trace in $T_{\mathrm{lsc}}(A)$ is bounded on the positive unit ball and that $T_1(A)$ is nonempty and weak-$*$ compact. Assume that, for $a,b\in(A\otimes\K)_+$ with $b\ne0$, \[ d_\tau(a)<1\quad \text{for every }\tau\in T_{\mathrm{lsc}}(A) \text{ with }d_\tau(b)=1 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad a\precsim b. \] Then $A$ has uniform property $\Gamma$ and $A\cong A\otimes\Z$.

primaryStatements.name: Traces on the completion
primaryStatements.label: r:cor:completion-traces
primaryStatements.text: Under the hypotheses of Theorem \ref{r:thm:main}, including real rank zero of $B^\omega$ in its quotient $C^*$-norm, every tracial state of $B$ is the designated extension of a unique trace in $T(A)$. Thus restriction is an affine homeomorphism $T(B)\to T(A)$, with inverse $\tau\mapsto\bar\tau$. Moreover, \[ |\sigma(b)|\le\|b\|_{2,T(A)} \qquad(b\in B,\ \sigma\in T(B)), \] so every tracial state of $B$ is continuous for the designated uniform $2$-norm.

primaryStatements.name: Finite-set central splitting
primaryStatements.label: r:thm:finite
primaryStatements.text: Let $A\subseteq D$ be a unital inclusion of $C^*$-algebras, with $A$ nuclear, $D$ of real rank zero, and $T(D)\ne\varnothing$. Suppose that for every $\delta>0$ there is a full projection $g\in D$ with $\sup_{\tau\in T(D)}\tau(g)<\delta$. For every finite $K\subseteq\mathcal U(A)$ and $\varepsilon>0$ there is a projection $P\in D$ such that, for every $x\in K$, \[ \sup_{\tau\in T(D)}\|[P,x]\|_{2,\tau}<\varepsilon, \qquad \sup_{\tau\in T(D)}|\tau(Px)-\tfrac12\tau(x)|<\varepsilon. \]

primaryStatements.name: Uniform proportional subprojections
primaryStatements.label: r:proj:split
primaryStatements.text: Assume that for every $\delta>0$ there is a full projection $g\in D$ with $\sup_{\tau\in\T(D)}\tau(g)<\delta$. For every projection $f\in D$, every $s\in[0,1]$, and every $\eps>0$, there is a projection $e\le f$ such that \begin{equation} \sup_{\tau\in\T(D)}|\tau(e)-s\tau(f)|<\eps. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Splitting finite linear tests
primaryStatements.label: r:proj:tests
primaryStatements.text: Under the small-full-projection hypothesis of Proposition \ref{r:proj:split}, let $q\in D$ be a projection, $s\in[0,1]$, and $\mathcal F\subset D$ a finite set. For every $\eps>0$, there is a projection $e\le q$ such that \begin{equation} |\tau(eh)-s\tau(qh)|<\eps \qquad(h\in\mathcal F,\ \tau\in\T(D)). \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Weighted matrix blocks
primaryStatements.label: r:weighted:family
primaryStatements.text: Let \(K\subseteq\U(A)\) be finite and \(0<\eta<1\). There are contractions \(v_1,\ldots,v_m\in A\) and nonnegative numbers \(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_m\) summing to one, chosen using only \(K,\eta\), such that the map \begin{equation} \Phi:D\longrightarrow D,\qquad \Phi(b)=\sum_{l=1}^m\lambda_l v_lbv_l^*, \end{equation} satisfies \eqref{r:eq:diagonal-mass} with \(\mu=\eta^2\). For every projection \(r\in D\), there is a finite family consisting of weights \(0<w_j\leq1\), nonzero projections \(q_j\leq r\), integers \(k_j\geq1\), and rows \(U_j\in M_{1,k_j}(D)\), such that, with \(p_j=U_jU_j^*\), \begin{align} U_j^*U_j&=1_{k_j}\otimes q_j,\\ \dist\big(U_j^*xU_j,M_{k_j}(\C)\otimes q_j\big)&<\eta &&(x\in K),\\ \normone{\sum_jw_jp_j-\Phi(r)}{\tau}&\leq\eta^2, \\ \sum_jw_j\normtwo{[x,p_j]}{\tau}^2&\leq6\eta &&(x\in K). \end{align} The last two estimates hold for every \(\tau\in\T(D)\). The family may be empty; the base projections \(q_j\) may repeat, and the projections \(p_j\) need not be mutually orthogonal.

definitions.name: Strict comparison
definitions.label: u:def:strict-comparison
definitions.text: The algebra $A$ has strict comparison if, whenever $a,b\in(A\otimes_{\min}\K)_+$ and $b\ne0$, the inequalities \[ d_\tau(a)<d_\tau(b)\qquad(\tau\in T(A)) \] imply $a\precsim b$. When $T(A)=\varnothing$, this requires $a\precsim b$ for every positive $a$ and every nonzero positive $b$ in the stabilization.

definitions.name: Uniform property $\Gamma$
definitions.label: u:def:uniform-gamma
definitions.text: For a simple separable unital $A$ with $T(A)\ne\varnothing$, uniform property $\Gamma$ means that for every $m\ge1$ there are projections $p_1,\ldots,p_m\in D\cap A'$ satisfying \[ \sum_{i=1}^m p_i=1, \qquad \tau(ap_i)=\frac{1}{m}\tau(a) \quad(a\in A,\ \tau\in\Lambda,\ 1\le i\le m). \] This is \cite[Definition 2.1 and Equation (2.1)]{CETW}, in the uniform tracial ultrapower notation used here.

lean.scopeText:
The formalization proves that real rank zero of the uniform tracial ultrapower of the uniform tracial completion implies uniform property $\Gamma$ for a simple separable unital infinite-dimensional nuclear stably finite $C^*$-algebra with traces. The conclusion holds at every specified free ultrafilter under the corresponding real-rank-zero hypothesis.

The linked comparison results also prove Jiang–Su absorption and uniform property $\Gamma$ for simple separable unital infinite-dimensional nuclear algebras with strict comparison, and for the stated stably projectionless nuclear algebras with bounded densely finite traces, a nonempty compact normalized trace base, and the prescribed finite-target-rank comparison condition.

papers.title: An explicit obstruction to nuclear norm-ultrapower embeddings
papers.abstract: We give a negative answer to Kirchberg's norm-ultrapower embedding problem. We construct an explicit separable unital full group C∗-algebra that admits no unital embedding into Bω, for any nonzero unital nuclear C∗-algebra B and any free ultrafilter ω on ℕ. In particular, it does not embed unitally into $\mathcal O_2^\omega$.

primaryStatements.text: Let \[ G=\Z[1/2]^3\rtimes\bigl(\SL_3(\Z)\times\Z\bigr), \qquad (M,k)\cdot v=2^kMv, \] and let $A=C^*(G)$ be its full group $C^*$-algebra. Then $A$ is separable and unital. primaryStatements.name: Consequences of negative KEP
primaryStatements.label: cor:kep-consequences
primaryStatements.text: Neither $\Otwo$ nor any exact or nuclear unital $C^*$-algebra is existentially closed among unital $C^*$-algebra extensions. For every free ultrafilter $\omega$ on $\N$, there are a separable unital $C^*$-algebra $D$ and $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(D)$ such that $D$ embeds unitally into $\Otwo^\omega$ but $D\rtimes_\alpha\Z$ does not embed unitally there. primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: For every irrational $\theta\in(0,1)$ there exists a continuous function $f:\T\to[0,1]$ such that \[ f^{-1}(\{0\})=\{1\},\qquad \int_\T\log f\,dm=-\infty, \] and every projection $p\in R_\theta$ satisfying $(1-p)Uf(V)p=0$ is either $0$ or $1$.

primaryStatements.label: cor:transitive-commutant
primaryStatements.text: Every separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space carries a nonzero norm-quasinilpotent operator with no nontrivial hyperinvariant subspace. Its commutant is a proper strongly closed transitive unital algebra.

primaryStatements.label: prop:parameters
primaryStatements.text: For the fixed $\theta$ there are positive integers $m_j,K_j,G_j,q_i$, positive real numbers $L_j,C_j,\varepsilon_j$, and consecutive blocks $J_j=\{d_{j-1}+1,\ldots,d_j\}$ of size $m_j$, with $d_0=0$, having the following properties. Set \begin{gather*} q_0=1,\qquad u_i(x)=\{q_ix\},\qquad\alpha_i=\{q_i\theta\},\\ \kappa_j=(100j)^{-1},\qquad N_j=m_jK_j,\\ a_j=G_j/m_j,\qquad b_j=m_j^{-19/20},\qquad Q_j=m_j^{(7/10)m_j}. \end{gather*} The frequencies are strictly increasing and divisible, and \begin{equation} \frac1{N_j}<\alpha_i<\frac2{N_j},\qquad q_i\mid q_{i+1},\qquad \frac{q_{i+1}}{q_i}\ge N_j \quad(i\in J_j). \end{equation} For every integer $k$ with $N_j/4\le |k|\le m_j^{(4/5)m_j}$, at least $m_j/20$ indices in $J_j$ satisfy \begin{equation} 1-\{k\alpha_i\}\in[b_j,1-b_j]. \end{equation} If $G_jK_j\le |k|\le N_j/4$, every index in $J_j$ has $1-\{k\alpha_i\}\in[a_j,1-a_j]$. The initial values are $K_1=100,G_1=1$. The numbers $L_j\ge1$ are nondecreasing, $C_j=\max(L_j,K_j^2)$, and the sizes satisfy \begin{align} &m_j\ge\max(K_j,2^j,4G_j,200),\qquad K_{j+1}=\lceil m_j^{(3/4)m_j}\rceil>2K_j,\notag\\ &G_{j+1}K_{j+1}<m_j^{(4/5)m_j},\qquad \kappa_jm_j^{1/40}\ge L_j,\qquad \kappa_{j+1}\sqrt{G_{j+1}}\ge L_j,\notag\\ &h_{j+1}^*/K_{j+1}\le2^{-j}. \end{align} Put $D_j=\exp((K_j+1)\sum_{s<j}C_sm_s)$. If $A,B$ are Laurent polynomials supported in $[-K_j,K_j]$, every coefficient has modulus at most $D_j$, and $|A_0|,|B_0|\ge1/j$, then \begin{equation} \max_{0\le n\le2K_j}|(AB)_{-n}|\ge\varepsilon_j, \qquad (2K_j+1)3e^{-L_j/10000}\le\varepsilon_j/j. \end{equation} Finally put $p_*=d_{j-1}$ and $\ell_j=((j+1)^2(1+p_*)q_{p_*})^{-1}$. For every $t=r/q_{p_*}$ with $r\in\Z$, $0\le r<q_{p_*}$, there is a finite nonempty set $\mathcal N_{j,t}$ of positive integers in $[Q_j/2,Q_j]$, with $\{n\theta-t\}\in(0,\ell_j)$, such that for $r'=1,2$, \begin{equation} \left\|\frac1{|\mathcal N_{j,t}|}\sum_{n\in\mathcal N_{j,t}} \prod_{i\in J_j}w_{m_j}^{(r')}(u_i(x),\{n\alpha_i\})-1 \right\|_{L^2(\mu)}<\frac1j. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Invariance on the ordered pairs
primaryStatements.label: prop:ordered-couplings
primaryStatements.text: Let $p\in M$ be a projection satisfying $(1-p)T_*p=0$. For every $j$, \begin{equation} (1-p(y))\operatorname{diag}_{k\in\Z}\bigl(R_{x,y}(k)\bigr)p(x)=0 \quad\text{for }\mathbb P_j\text{-almost every pair}. \end{equation} Moreover $0<R_{x,y}(k)\le1$ for all $k\in\Z$ almost surely.

primaryStatements.label: thm:measurable
primaryStatements.text: The bounded operator $T_*=U\pi(f_*)$ has no projection $p\in M$ satisfying $0<\tau(p)<1$ and $(1-p)T_*p=0$.

primaryStatements.label: cor:quasinilpotent
primaryStatements.text: The constructed operator $T_f$ is nonzero and quasinilpotent.

primaryStatements.name: Product realization
primaryStatements.label: p:thm:model
primaryStatements.text: There are angles $0<\theta_i<1$ and costs $c_i>0$, with $\sum_i\theta_i<\infty$ and $1,\theta_1,\theta_2,\ldots$ rationally independent, such that the measurable weight \[ f(x)=\exp\left(-\sum_{i\ge1}c_i\lfloor x_i+\theta_i\rfloor\right) \] is positive almost everywhere and has $\int_X\log f\,d\mu=-\infty$. The algebra $M$ is a type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor with separable predual, and $T=U\pi(f)$ is nonzero and norm-quasinilpotent, with $\Delta(T)=0$. Every projection $p\in M$ satisfying $(1-p)Tp=0$ is $0$ or $1$. Moreover, $|T|$ has pure-point spectral type. The abelian algebra generated by any finite family of polar conjugates $U^n|T|U^{-n}$ is atomic, whereas $W^*(U^n|T|U^{-n}:n\in\Z)$ is diffuse.

primaryStatements.name: Phase ranges
primaryStatements.label: p:prop:phases
primaryStatements.text: Almost surely, for every sufficiently large $j$ the following hold simultaneously for all integers $k$ in the indicated ranges, with $m=m_j$: \begin{enumerate} \item If $G_jK_j\le |k|\le N_j/4$, then every $i\in J_j$ satisfies \[ 1-\{k\theta_i\}\in[a_j,1-a_j]. \] \item If $N_j/4\le |k|\le m^{(4/5)m}$, then at least $m/20$ coordinates $i\in J_j$ satisfy \[ 1-\{k\theta_i\}\in[b_j,1-b_j]. \] \end{enumerate} The first assertion in fact holds at every stage and for every realization of the angles in their prescribed intervals.

lean.scopeText:
For every irrational rotation angle $\theta\in(0,1)$, the formalization constructs a continuous nonnegative circle weight with a single zero and logarithmic integral $-\infty$ whose weighted rotation is nonzero and quasinilpotent. In its associated hyperfinite type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor, the operator has no nontrivial invariant projection: $(1-p)Tp=0$ forces $p=0$ or $p=1$. The linked statements also include an earlier existence construction, a product realization, and the selected product model's Brown measure $\delta_0$.

The formalization for the companion paper [Backward intertwiners and a transitive commutant](../../preprints/Backward-intertwiners-and-a-transitive-commutant-September-27-2026/paper.pdf) gives, on every separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space, a nonzero quasinilpotent operator whose commutant is transitive, proper, and closed in the strong operator topology. Thus no nontrivial closed subspace is invariant under every operator in the commutant.

The hyperinvariant-subspace problem asks whether every bounded operator on a complex Hilbert space has a nontrivial closed subspace invariant under every operator that commutes with it. The formalization gives a negative answer on every separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space: there is a nonzero quasinilpotent operator with a transitive commutant. Its commutant is a proper unital operator algebra closed in the strong operator topology. The construction therefore has no nonzero proper closed hyperinvariant subspace.

papers.abstract: We refute Kaplansky's quasitrace conjecture by constructing a separable unital complex C∗-algebra that admits normalized 2-quasitraces but has no tracial state. As a consequence, we show that the minimal tensor product of two unital simple stably finite complex C∗-algebras can be properly infinite, even when one factor is the reduced free-group algebra $C_r^*(\mathbb F_2)$.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: There exist a separable unital complex \(C^*\)-algebra \(A\), admitting a normalized \(2\)-quasitrace, and positive contractions \(a,b\in A\) such that every normalized \(2\)-quasitrace \(\tau\) on \(A\) satisfies \[ \tau(a+b)-\tau(a)-\tau(b)\ge\frac1{144}. \]

primaryStatements.name: Tensor products and stable finiteness
primaryStatements.label: cor:stable-finiteness
primaryStatements.text: \leavevmode \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item There are two unital simple stably finite complex \(C^*\)-algebras whose minimal tensor product is properly infinite. One factor can be taken to be \(C_r^*(\mathbb F_2)\). \item There is a separable unital complex \(C^*\)-algebra \(B\) admitting a normalized \(2\)-quasitrace such that \(B\otimes_{\min}C_r^*(\mathbb F_2)\) is properly infinite and admits no normalized \(2\)-quasitrace. \item There is a separable unital stably finite complex \(C^*\)-algebra with no tracial state. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.name: Quasitrace existence
primaryStatements.label: thm:existence
primaryStatements.text: A unital \(C^*\)-algebra \(C\) admits a normalized \(2\)-quasitrace if and only if \(M_m(C)\) is not properly infinite for every positive integer \(m\).

primaryStatements.label: prop:bundle-test
primaryStatements.text: For every pair of integers $m,R\geq 1$, set \begin{equation} d_0=64m4^R,\qquad d_j=4^j d_0\quad(0\leq j\leq R). \end{equation} There are a compact smooth manifold $Y$, Hermitian complex vector bundles $E_j\to Y$ for all $j\geq0$, and continuous bundle maps $X_i^{(j)}:E_j\to E_{j+1}$, for $1\leq i\leq24$ and $j\geq0$, such that $E_0$ is trivial of rank $d_0$, the rank of $E_j$ is $d_j$ for $0\leq j\leq R$, and \begin{equation} \sum_{i=1}^{24}(X_i^{(j)})^*X_i^{(j)}=I_{E_j}, \qquad \sum_{i=1}^{24}X_i^{(j)}(X_i^{(j)})^* \leq\frac23 I_{E_{j+1}}. \end{equation} Moreover, \begin{equation} \begin{gathered} \left(\bigoplus_{j=0}^R E_j\right)^{\oplus m}\\ \text{contains no trivial subbundle of rank }2md_0. \end{gathered} \end{equation}

primaryStatements.label: thm:construction
primaryStatements.text: There is a separable unital complex $C^*$-algebra $B=C^*(1,x_1,\ldots,x_{24})$ such that \begin{equation} \sum_{i=1}^{24}x_i^*x_i=1, \qquad \sum_{i=1}^{24}x_ix_i^*\le\frac23\,1, \end{equation} and $M_m(B)$ is not properly infinite for every integer $m\ge1$.

lean.scopeText:
Kaplansky's quasitrace conjecture predicts that every $2$-quasitrace on a $C^*$-algebra is a trace. The formalization constructs a separable $C^*$-algebra with normalized $2$-quasitraces and fixed positive contractions $a,b$ for which every such quasitrace satisfies $\mathrm{Re}(\tau(a+b)-\tau(a)-\tau(b))\ge1/144$. Thus none is additive on this pair.

The formalization also gives simple stably finite $C^*$-algebras whose spatial tensor product is properly infinite, a separable stably finite algebra with no tracial state, and a tensor-product example in which normalized $2$-quasitraces are lost. These are the stable-finiteness consequences named in the paper's title.

primaryStatements.text: Let \(M\) be a complex von Neumann algebra and let \(k\geq2\). Every \(f\in C_b^k(M,M)\) satisfying \(df=0\) has the form \(f=dg\) for some \(g\in C_b^{k-1}(M,M)\). Consequently \(H_b^k(M,M)=0\).

primaryStatements.text: Let \(M\) be a von Neumann algebra and \(k\geq2\). \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item If \(f\in C_b^k(M,M)\) is a cocycle, there are a separately normal bounded cocycle \(f_0\) and a bounded \((k-1)\)-cochain \(b\) such that \(f=f_0+db\). \item If \(M\) has no type \(\mathrm{II}_1\) central summand, then \(H_b^k(M,M)=0\). \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.label: thm:walk
primaryStatements.text: Let $M$ be a finite type $\mathrm{II}_1$ von Neumann algebra with separable predual and faithful normal tracial state $\tau$. There exist a symmetric, countably supported probability measure $\mu$ on $\U(M)$ and a strictly increasing sequence $n_\ell\to\infty$ with the following properties. The positive-mass atoms of $\mu$ contain a countable $2$-norm dense subset of $\U(M)$, and hence generate $M$ as a von Neumann algebra. For every $r\in\N$, every nonempty finite set $\mathcal W\subset\mathbb F_r\setminus\{e\}$, and every $\eta>0$, if $G_1^{(\ell)},\ldots,G_r^{(\ell)}$ are independent with law $\mu^{*n_\ell}$, then \[ \Pr\left( \max_{w\in\mathcal W} \left|\tau\bigl(w(G_1^{(\ell)},\ldots,G_r^{(\ell)})\bigr)\right| \geq\eta \right)\longrightarrow0. \] Thus these products have joint free Haar moments in probability.

primaryStatements.label: thm:liouville
primaryStatements.text: Let $(M,\tau)$ be a type $\mathrm{II}_1$ von Neumann algebra with separable predual and a faithful normal tracial state, and let $\mu$ be the measure supplied by Theorem \ref{thm:walk}. Suppose that $T:M\to M$ is bounded, linear, and bounded-ball $2$-continuous, and that \begin{equation} T(x)=\E_{U\sim\mu}\bigl[T(xU)U^*\bigr] \qquad(x\in M). \end{equation} Then \begin{equation} T(x)=T(1)x\qquad(x\in M). \end{equation}

papers.title: Relative generation and the generator problem for finite factors
papers.abstract: We prove that every type II1 factor with separable predual is generated by one operator, equivalently by two self-adjoint operators. Combined with the established direct-integral reduction to this case, this gives an affirmative solution of the generator problem for von Neumann algebras with separable predual.
papers.familySummary: Proves that every type II1 factor with separable predual is generated by a single operator, equivalently by two self-adjoint operators, resolving the generator problem. More strongly, for every irreducible inclusion $P\subset M$ of such factors, the unitaries u with $M=W^*(P,u)$ form a dense Gδ subset in the trace 2-norm topology.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Every type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor $M$ with separable predual is generated by two self-adjoint elements. Equivalently, there is an $x\in M$ such that $M=W^*(x)$.

primaryStatements.label: thm:relative-generation
primaryStatements.text: Let $P\subset M$ be an irreducible inclusion of type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors, with $M$ of separable predual. The set \[ \{u\in\mathcal U(M):W^*(P,u)=M\} \] is a dense $G_\delta$ subset of the unitary group $\mathcal U(M)$ for the trace $2$-norm topology.

primaryStatements.name: Popa's independence theorem
primaryStatements.label: thm:popa-independence
primaryStatements.text: Let $P\subset M$ be an irreducible inclusion of $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors, and put $\mathbf Q=P^\omega\subset M^\omega=\mathbf M$. For every linear subspace $X\subset\mathbf M$ that is separable in $2$-norm and satisfies $\tau(x)=0$ for all $x\in X$, there is a diffuse abelian von Neumann algebra $A\subset\mathbf Q$ such that \begin{equation} \tau(x_0a_1x_1\cdots a_mx_m)=0 \end{equation} whenever $m\geq1$, $x_0\in X\cup\{1\}$, $x_1,\ldots,x_m\in X$, and $a_1,\ldots,a_m\in A$ have trace zero.

primaryStatements.label: prop:perturbation
primaryStatements.text: Let $P\subset M$ be an irreducible inclusion of $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors. Given $u,z\in\mathcal U(M)$, $\xi\in M$, and $0<\alpha<1/2$, for every integer $\ell\ge1$ there are $\widetilde u\in\mathcal U(M)$ and $\widetilde t_0,\ldots,\widetilde t_\ell\in\mathcal U(P)$ such that, with \[ \widetilde W=\widetilde t_0 \prod_{k=1}^{\ell}(\widetilde u\,\widetilde t_k), \] one has \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \norm{\widetilde u-u}_2 &\le \frac{\alpha}{\sqrt{2\ell}}+\frac1\ell,\\ \left|\tau(\xi^*\widetilde W) -\frac\alpha2\tau(\xi^*z)\right| &\le \norm{\xi}_2\frac{4\alpha^2}{1-2\alpha}+\frac1\ell. \end{aligned} \end{equation} All products indexed by $k$ are taken in increasing order from left to right. The unitaries may depend on $\ell$.

primaryStatements.name: Popa
primaryStatements.label: thm:irreducible-hyperfinite
primaryStatements.text: Let $N\subset M$ be an irreducible inclusion of $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors with separable preduals. There is a hyperfinite $\mathrm{II}_1$ subfactor $R\subset N$ such that $R'\cap M=\mathbb C1$.

primaryStatements.label: prop:four-generators
primaryStatements.text: Every $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor with separable predual is generated by four self-adjoint elements.

primaryStatements.label: cor:entropy-generators
primaryStatements.text: For every integer $n\geq3$, the factor $L(\mathbb F_n)$ with its canonical trace has two finite self-adjoint generating tuples on which both $\delta$ and $\delta_0$ take different values. In particular, neither dimension is determined by the generated tracial von Neumann algebra.

lean.scopeText:
The formalization answers the generator problem affirmatively for type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors with separable predual: one bounded operator generates the factor under adjoints and weak-operator closure. It imposes no separability assumption on the representing Hilbert space or on the operator-norm topology.

It also proves the paper's relative-generation result. For an irreducible inclusion of type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors with separable predual for the larger factor, the unitaries that generate the larger factor together with the smaller one form a dense $G_\delta$ set in the normalized trace two-norm topology. The normalized faithful normal trace is included in the assertion.

papers.title: A counterexample to Naimark's problem in ZFC
papers.abstract: We construct in ZFC a unital infinite-dimensional simple complex C∗-algebra with a faithful tracial state whose nonzero irreducible representations are all unitarily equivalent. This gives a negative answer to Naimark's problem without additional set-theoretic assumptions.
papers.familySummary: Gives an alternative to [Tanaka's ZFC construction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.26930v1) of a unital infinite-dimensional simple complex C∗-algebra with a faithful tracial state and exactly one nonzero irreducible representation up to unitary equivalence. Thus the unrestricted compact-operator characterization fails without additional set-theoretic assumptions; the counterexample is nonseparable.

primaryStatements.label: na:main
primaryStatements.text: There exists a unital infinite-dimensional simple complex $C^*$-algebra $A$ with a faithful tracial state such that all its nonzero irreducible representations are unitarily equivalent. In particular, $A$ is not isomorphic to $K(H)$ for any complex Hilbert space $H$.

primaryStatements.label: na:hnn
primaryStatements.text: Let $(A,\tau)$ be a unital $C^*$-algebra with faithful tracial state, let $D_1,D_2\subset A$ be unital subalgebras with trace-preserving conditional expectations $E_i:A\to D_i$, and let $\theta:D_1\to D_2$ be a trace-preserving isomorphism. There is a unital extension with a faithful tracial state extending $\tau$, \[ H(A)=C^*(A,v),\qquad vdv^*=\theta(d)\quad(d\in D_1), \] where $v$ is called the stable unitary, and a trace-preserving conditional expectation $E_A:H(A)\to A$ annihilating every nonempty reduced word \eqref{na:hnn-word}. Among faithfully tracial extensions generated by $A$ and such a unitary, the relation and vanishing of the trace on nonempty reduced words determine $H(A)$ uniquely, by an isomorphism fixing $A$ and $v$.

primaryStatements.label: na:hnn-restriction
primaryStatements.text: With the hypotheses of Proposition \ref{na:hnn}, let $A'\subset A$ be a unital subalgebra containing $D_1$ and $D_2$. Then $C^*(A',v)\subset H(A)$ is the reduced adjunction $H(A')$ formed with the restricted trace and expectations $E_i|_{A'}$. The expectation $E_A$ restricts to the expectation $H(A')\to A'$.

primaryStatements.label: na:reorder
primaryStatements.text: Let $O$ be a unital faithfully tracial $C^*$-algebra. For each $t\in\{j,k\}$, let $D_1^t,D_2^t\subset O$, $E_i^t:O\to D_i^t$ and $\theta_t:D_1^t\to D_2^t$ satisfy the hypotheses of Proposition \ref{na:hnn}. When forming an adjunction over $H_j(O)$ or $H_k(O)$, extend the other data expectations by composition with the expectation onto $O$. There is a trace-preserving isomorphism \begin{equation} H_k(H_j(O))\ \cong\ H_j(H_k(O)) \end{equation} fixing $O$ and the named stable unitaries $v_j,v_k$.

primaryStatements.name: The bridge
primaryStatements.label: na:bridge
primaryStatements.text: Let $A$ be a unital $C^*$-algebra with a faithful tracial state $\tau$ and no finite-dimensional irreducible representations. For $i=1,2$, let $(p_n^i)_{n\geq0}$ be a decreasing sequence of projections, with $p_0^i=1$, peaking to a pure state $f_i$. Suppose that $f_1\not\sim f_2$ and \[ \tau(p_n^1)=\tau(p_n^2)=t_n, \qquad 1=t_0>t_1>\cdots>0, \qquad t_n\longrightarrow0. \] Put $D_i=C^*(p_n^i:n\geq0)$ and let $\theta:D_1\to D_2$ be determined by $\theta(p_n^1)=p_n^2$. Form the reduced HNN extension $H(A)$ of Proposition \ref{na:hnn} using these data and their trace-preserving conditional expectations. Then every pure state $h$ of $A$ has a unique state extension $\widetilde h$ to $H(A)$. These extensions are pure, and for all pure states $h,k$ of $A$, \[ \widetilde h\sim\widetilde k \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad h\sim k \quad\text{or}\quad \{[h],[k]\}=\{[f_1],[f_2]\}. \] The extension has a faithful tracial state extending $\tau$ and a faithful trace-preserving conditional expectation onto $A$. If $A$ is simple, then $H(A)$ is simple.

primaryStatements.label: na:closed-extension
primaryStatements.text: For every dependency-closed $S\subset\delta$, the inclusion $A[S]\subset X_\delta$ has property \textup{(U)}.

primaryStatements.label: na:state-count
primaryStatements.text: Put $\mathfrak c=2^{\aleph_0}$. If $|\delta|\le\mathfrak c$, then $X_\delta$ has at most $\mathfrak c$ pure states.

primaryStatements.name: Kishimoto--Ozawa--Sakai
primaryStatements.label: na:homogeneity
primaryStatements.text: Let $B$ be a separable $C^*$-algebra. If pure states $h,k$ of $B$ have GNS representations with the same kernel, there is an automorphism $\gamma$ of $B$ such that $h\circ\gamma=k$. In particular, this holds for every pair of pure states of a separable simple $C^*$-algebra.

lean.scopeText: Naimark's problem asks whether a $C^*$-algebra whose nonzero irreducible representations are all unitarily equivalent must be an algebra of compact operators. The formalization gives a counterexample in ZFC: a unital infinite-dimensional simple complex $C^*$-algebra with a faithful tracial state has that uniqueness property for irreducible representations but is not isomorphic to the compact operators on any Hilbert space. No additional set-theoretic assumption is used.

papers.title: A finite-entropy separation of microstates and nonmicrostates free entropy
papers.abstract: We answer the finite-entropy equality question for microstates and nonmicrostates free entropy negatively. We construct a bounded self-adjoint tuple X in a von Neumann algebra with faithful normal tracial state such that $-\infty\lt \chi(X)\leq\chi^*(X)-\tfrac12\lt \infty$. Here χ is the original microstates entropy with an operator-norm cutoff and a limsup over matrix sizes. The counterexample uses a large but fixed number of variables.
papers.familySummary: Constructs a bounded self-adjoint tuple in a tracial von Neumann algebra whose microstates and nonmicrostates free entropies satisfy $-\infty\lt \chi\lt \chi^*\lt \infty$. This answers Voiculescu’s finite-entropy equality question negatively: the matrix-approximation and free-Fisher-information definitions differ even when both are finite.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: There exist an integer $n\geq2$ and a bounded self-adjoint tuple $X=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$ in a von Neumann algebra with faithful normal tracial state such that \[ -\infty<\chi(X)\leq\chi^*(X)-\tfrac12<\infty. \] Here $\chi$ is the original microstates entropy using an operator-norm cutoff and a limsup over matrix sizes.

primaryStatements.name: Squared-cumulant Fisher bound
primaryStatements.label: prop:fisher
primaryStatements.text: Let $C$ be a centered bounded self-adjoint $n$-tuple with diagonal covariance $\tau(C_iC_j)=\delta_{ij}c_i$, where $c_i\geq0$, and let $S$ be a standard semicircular family free from $C$. Put $V_u=C+\sqrt u S$ and $v_i(u)=u+c_i$ for $u>0$. For every $u>0$, \[ \sum_i\frac1{v_i(u)}\leq\Phi^*(V_u)\leq\frac n u. \] Whenever $\sum_{r\geq2}u^{-r}\|\kappa_{r+1}(C)\|_2^2<\infty$, \begin{equation} 0\leq\Phi^*(V_u)-\sum_i\frac1{v_i(u)} \leq\frac1{u^2}\sum_{r\geq2}u^{-r}\|\kappa_{r+1}(C)\|_2^2. \end{equation}

lean.scopeText: The formalization disproves equality of microstates and nonmicrostates free entropy even when both quantities are finite. It constructs a bounded self-adjoint tuple $X$ in a von Neumann algebra with a faithful normal tracial state such that $-\infty<\chi(X)\le\chi^*(X)-1/2<\infty$. Here $\chi$ is the microstates entropy with an operator-norm cutoff and a limsup over matrix sizes, and $\chi^*$ is the nonmicrostates entropy defined using free semicircular noise. The example has a fixed finite number of variables.

papers.title: The Kirchberg–Rørdam character criterion
papers.abstract: We prove the Kirchberg–Rørdam character criterion: for every free ultrafilter on ℕ, a nonzero unital separable complex C∗-algebra absorbs the Jiang–Su algebra if and only if its norm central-sequence algebra has no characters. We also prove that the infinite minimal tensor power of every nonzero unital separable complex C∗-algebra without characters is $\mathcal Z$-stable and contains a unital copy of $\mathcal Z$.
papers.familySummary: A nonzero unital separable complex C∗-algebra is Jiang–Su stable exactly when its norm central-sequence algebra has no characters, for every free ultrafilter. This answers the Kirchberg–Rørdam character question. Also, the infinite minimal tensor power of every such algebra without characters is Jiang–Su stable, answering the Dadarlat–Toms question.

papers.sourceAbstract: We prove the Kirchberg--R\o rdam character criterion: for every free ultrafilter on $\N$, a nonzero unital separable complex $C^*$-algebra absorbs the Jiang--Su algebra if and only if its norm central-sequence algebra has no characters. We also prove that the infinite minimal tensor power of every nonzero unital separable complex $C^*$-algebra without characters is $\Z$-stable and contains a unital copy of $\Z$.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let $A$ be a nonzero unital separable complex $C^*$-algebra, and let $\omega$ be any free ultrafilter on $\N$. Then \[ F_\omega(A)\text{ has no characters} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad A\cong A\otmin\Z. \]

primaryStatements.label: thm:finite
primaryStatements.text: Let $D$ be a nonzero unital complex $C^*$-algebra without characters. There is an integer $m\ge1$ and a unital $*$-homomorphism \[ I(2,3)\longrightarrow D^{\otimes_{\max}m}, \] where \[ I(2,3)=\{f\in C([0,1],M_2\otimes M_3): f(0)\in M_2\otimes1_3,\ f(1)\in1_2\otimes M_3\}. \]

primaryStatements.name: Infinite minimal tensor powers
primaryStatements.label: cor:infinite-tensor
primaryStatements.text: Let $D$ be a nonzero unital separable complex $C^*$-algebra without characters, and write \[ B=D^{\otimes_{\min}\infty} :=\varinjlim_{n\ge1} \bigl(D^{\otimes_{\min}n},\,x\longmapsto x\otimes1_D\bigr). \] Then $B\cong B\otmin\Z$, and $B$ contains a unital copy of $\Z$.

primaryStatements.name: R\o rdam--Winter
primaryStatements.label: prop:rw
primaryStatements.text: Let $B$ be a unital $C^*$-algebra. Suppose that $a_1,a_2\in B$ are orthogonal positive contractions with $a_1=v^*v$, $a_2=vv^*$ for some $v\in B$, and that, for some $\varepsilon>0$, \[ 1_B-a_1-a_2\precsim(a_1-\varepsilon)_+. \] Then there is a unital $*$-homomorphism $I(2,3)\to B$.

primaryStatements.name: Kirchberg--R\o rdam
primaryStatements.label: prop:kr
primaryStatements.text: Let $A$ be a nonzero unital separable $C^*$-algebra. \begin{enumerate} \item If $D\subset F_\omega(A)$ is separable and contains the ambient unit, then for every $m\ge1$ there is a unital $*$-homomorphism $D^{\otimes_{\max}m}\to F_\omega(A)$. \item $A\cong A\otmin\Z$ if and only if $F_\omega(A)$ contains, with the ambient unit, a separable subhomogeneous $C^*$-algebra without characters. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.label: cor:tensor-represented-labels
primaryStatements.text: Let \(D\) and \(V\) be as in Lemma \ref{lem:tensor-detecting-space}. For each \(r\ge1\), there are \(n\ge1\) and selfadjoint elements \(x_1,\ldots,x_r\in D^{\otimes n}\) whose images are complex linearly independent under every irreducible representation of \(D^{\otimes n}\otmax B\), for every nonzero unital \(C^*\)-algebra \(B\). Here the elements \(x_i\) occupy the first \(n\) tensor legs.

primaryStatements.label: prop:full-cone
primaryStatements.text: For every nonzero unital \(C^*\)-algebra \(D\) without characters, there are an integer \(m\ge1\), the maximal tensor power \(P=D^{\otimes m}\), and a unital \(*\)-homomorphism \(\eta:C\to P\) such that \(\eta(\iota e_{11})\) is full in \(P\).

primaryStatements.label: prop:cone-drop
primaryStatements.text: Let \(P\) be a nonzero unital \(C^*\)-algebra. Suppose that there is a unital \(*\)-homomorphism \(\eta:C\to P\) such that \(\eta(\iota e_{11})\) is full in \(P\). Then, for some finite \(m\ge1\), the maximal tensor power \(B=P^{\otimes m}\) contains orthogonal positive contractions \(b_1,b_2\) and an element \(v_B\) such that \[ b_1=v_B^*v_B,\qquad b_2=v_Bv_B^*,\qquad 1_B-b_1-b_2\precsim(b_1-1/2)_+. \] Consequently there is a unital \(*\)-homomorphism \[ I(2,3)\longrightarrow P^{\otimes m}. \]

lean.scopeText: The Kirchberg–Rørdam criterion relates Jiang–Su absorption to characters of the central-sequence algebra. The formalized result proves that, for every nonzero unital separable complex $C^*$-algebra $A$ and every free ultrafilter on $\mathbb N$, the norm central-sequence algebra has no nonzero character exactly when $A\cong A\otimes_{\min}\mathcal Z$. No nuclearity, simplicity, trace, or comparison hypothesis is imposed.

papers.title: Approximation Paving over Arbitrary Maximal Abelian Subalgebras
papers.abstract: We prove the approximation-paving conjecture of Popa and Vaes for every maximal abelian subalgebra of a complex von Neumann algebra. For each $0\lt \varepsilon\lt 1$, every self-adjoint operator is a strong limit of self-adjoint operators of norm at most three times its norm, each admitting a norm paving with error at most ε times the approximant's own norm. The number of projections is at most $C\varepsilon^{-6}$ for a universal constant C. No separability or conditional-expectation hypothesis is required.
papers.familySummary: Proves that every self-adjoint element of a complex von Neumann algebra admits strong-operator paving relative to any maximal abelian subalgebra with $O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ blocks. The norm bound holds after compression by a projection arbitrarily close to the identity in the strong topology, resolving the Popa–Vaes quadratic paving conjecture.

papers.sourceAbstract: We prove the approximation-paving conjecture of Popa and Vaes for every maximal abelian subalgebra of a complex von Neumann algebra. For each \(0<\varepsilon<1\), every self-adjoint operator is a strong limit of self-adjoint operators of norm at most three times its norm, each admitting a norm paving with error at most \(\varepsilon\) times the approximant's own norm. The number of projections is at most \(C\varepsilon^{-6}\) for a universal constant \(C\). No separability or conditional-expectation hypothesis is required.

primaryStatements.name: One-sided measured paving
primaryStatements.label: thm:measured-paving
primaryStatements.text: There is a universal constant $K\geq1$ with the following property. Suppose $T$, $\mathcal R$, $\mathcal G$, and $\omega$ satisfy the preceding assumptions. Let $b>0$, and choose a positive integer $r$ such that \begin{equation} 2\sqrt{2/r}+2/r<b. \end{equation} For every $\sigma>0$ and $\rho>0$, there is a measurable coloring of $V$ with $r+1$ colors for which \begin{equation} \int_V \bigl((T_{\mathrm{pav}}-(Kb+\sigma)\one)_+^2\bigr)_{vv} \,d\mu(v)<\rho. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.label: prop:sparse-pinning
primaryStatements.text: For every $\zeta,\eta>0$ and $L_0\geq1$, there are an integer $L\geq L_0$ and a measurable partition \[ V=\mathcal U\sqcup V_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup V_r \] such that $\mu(\mathcal U)<\eta$ and the following holds. On the surviving lifted vertices $(V\setminus\mathcal U)\times[0,L]$, let $T_{\mathrm{col}}^L$ be the restriction of $T$, keeping only entries between vertices whose basepoints belong to the same $V_i$, and put \begin{equation} A_L=d^{1/2}(T_{\mathrm{col}}^L-Kb\one)d^{1/2}, \qquad d_{(v,s)}=e^s. \end{equation} Extend $m_u^{\mathrm{surv}}=((A_L)_+)_{uu}$ by zero on the deleted vertices. Then \begin{equation} \frac1L\int_{V\times[0,L]}m_u^{\mathrm{surv}}\, d\widetilde\mu(u)<\zeta. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: For every $0<\eps<1$, set \[ r_\eps=\left\lceil400000000\eps^{-2}\right\rceil +\left\lceil4/\eps\right\rceil+1 \le500000000\eps^{-2}. \] For every masa $A\subseteq M\subseteq\mathcal B(H)$ and every $x=x^*\in M$, the element $x$ is $(\eps,r_\eps)$ so-pavable over $A$. In particular, the number of projections is fixed before the inclusion, operator, and strong neighborhood. No separability or conditional-expectation assumption is imposed on the inclusion.

primaryStatements.name: Quadratic norm paving in Ocneanu ultrapowers
primaryStatements.label: cor:ultrapower-paving
primaryStatements.text: Let $A\subseteq M$ be a masa. Suppose that $A$ is countably decomposable and is the range of a normal conditional expectation from $M$. Let $\omega$ be a free ultrafilter on $\mathbb N$, and let $A^\omega\subseteq M^\omega$ be the associated inclusion in the Ocneanu von Neumann ultrapower. For every $0<\eps<1$ and every $x=x^*\in M^\omega$, there are a partition $p_1,\ldots,p_{r_\eps}\in A^\omega$ and an element $a=a^*\in A^\omega$ such that \[ \|a\|\le\|x\|, \qquad \left\|\sum_{i=1}^{r_\eps}p_i x p_i-a\right\|\le\eps\|x\|. \] Here $r_\eps$ is the same integer as in Theorem \ref{thm:main}.

primaryStatements.label: prop:state-reduction
primaryStatements.text: Fix $0<\eps<1$ and an integer $R\geq1$. Suppose that for every masa $A\subseteq M$ admitting a faithful $A$-central normal state $\varphi$, every self-adjoint contraction $x\in M$, and every $\rho>0$, there exist a partition of $1$ into $R$ projections of $A$, a self-adjoint $a\in A$ of norm at most one, and a projection $q\in M$ with $\varphi(1-q)<\rho$ and \[ \left\|q\left(\sum_{i=1}^R p_i x p_i-a\right)q\right\|\leq\eps. \] Then every masa in every represented von Neumann algebra has the strong-operator paving property of Theorem \ref{thm:main} at error $\eps$, with \[ r=R+\lceil4/\eps\rceil+1. \] In particular this number is chosen before the finite vector set and the strong-neighborhood tolerance.

primaryStatements.label: prop:atomless-kernels
primaryStatements.text: In the setting of this section, for every $y\in M^\circ$ the map \[ K_y(f)=E_A(y^*fy),\qquad f\in A, \] has a positive kernel whose mass is at most $\|y\|^2$ and which is atomless for almost every output point $v\in X$. For $k\geq1$ and $y_1,\ldots,y_k\in M^\circ$, the composition $K_{y_1}\circ\cdots\circ K_{y_k}$ has a positive kernel whose mass is at most $\prod_{j=1}^k\|y_j\|^2$ and which is atomless almost everywhere. If $p_{\rm at}\in A$ is the projection of the atomic part of $A$, then \[ p_{\rm at}y=yp_{\rm at}=0\qquad(y\in M^\circ). \]

primaryStatements.name: Bernoulli coloring
primaryStatements.label: thm:bernoulli-coloring
primaryStatements.text: Let $(X,\mu,\mathcal R)$, $G$, $\Delta$, and $T$ satisfy the assumptions above: $\mathcal R$ is countable and nonsingular on a standard probability space, $G$ is undirected, has no loops, has degree at most $D_0<\infty$, and satisfies Equation \eqref{eq:coloring-edge-ratios}, and $T$ is a measurable Hermitian contraction with zero diagonal and support on $G$, allowing diagonal unitary conjugacy under a change of root. Fix an integer $r\geq1$ and a real number $t>3/\sqrt r$, and put $\beta=80$. For every integer $m\geq1$ and every $\alpha,\eta>0$, there is a measurable coloring $c:\widetilde X\to\{1,\ldots,r\}$ on the relative Bernoulli extension such that \begin{equation} \kappa_v\{\omega:c(v,\omega)=i\}=\frac1r \quad\text{for every }i\in\{1,\ldots,r\} \quad\text{and almost every }v\in X, \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \widetilde\mu\left\{(v,\omega): \|T_{B_G(v,m),c}\|\leq2\beta t+\alpha\right\}>1-\eta. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Transfer of fixed scalar moments
primaryStatements.label: prop:moment-transfer
primaryStatements.text: Let $A\subset M$, $\varphi$, and $\mathcal K$ be as in Lemma \ref{lem:bernoulli-model}. Fix a finite symbol size $s$, the corresponding cylinder algebra $\mathcal Y$, and the generating partition sequence $(\mathcal P_j)$ just described. For any fixed integer $k\ge1$ and fixed factors $Z_1,\ldots,Z_k$, each chosen in $M$ or in $\mathcal Y$, define $Z_h^{(j)}=Z_h$ for a factor chosen in $M$ and $Z_h^{(j)}=\mathrm{ev}_{\mathcal P_j}(Z_h)$ for a factor chosen in $\mathcal Y$. Use the same independent symbols for all evaluations in a word. Then \begin{equation} \lim_{j\to\infty} \mathbb E_{\{z_a\}} \varphi\bigl(Z_1^{(j)}\cdots Z_k^{(j)}\bigr) =\Phi(Z_1\cdots Z_k). \end{equation}

primaryStatements.label: prop:expected
primaryStatements.text: Let $A\subseteq M$ be a masa and let $\varphi$ be a faithful normal state on $M$ with $A$ in its centralizer. For $0<\eps<1$, put \[ r_{\mathrm e}=\left\lceil 20000^2\eps^{-2}\right\rceil. \] For every self-adjoint contraction $x\in M$ and every $\rho>0$, there are a partition $P=(p_1,\ldots,p_{r_{\mathrm e}})$ in $A$ and a projection $q\in M$ such that \[ \varphi(1-q)<\rho, \qquad \|q(S_P(x)-E_Ax)q\|\le\eps. \] Here $E_A$ is the $\varphi$-preserving conditional expectation onto $A$.

definitions.name: Strong-operator paving
definitions.label: def:so-paving
definitions.text: Let $x=x^*\in M$, $\eps>0$, and $r\ge1$ be an integer. We say that $x$ is $(\eps,r)$ so-pavable over $A$ if for every finite $F\subset H$ and every $\delta>0$ there are a partition $P=(p_1,\ldots,p_r)$ in $A$, an element $a=a^*\in A$ with $\|a\|\le\|x\|$, and a projection $q\in M$ such that \[ \|(1-q)\xi\|<\delta\quad(\xi\in F), \qquad \|q(S_P(x)-a)q\|\le\eps\|x\|. \] The integer $r$ is fixed before $F$ and $\delta$ are chosen.

papers.title: The trace cone classifies Razak–Jacelon stabilizations
papers.abstract: We prove that the canonical topological cone of all extended lower-semicontinuous tracial weights determines a separable nuclear C∗-algebra after tensoring with the Razak–Jacelon algebra and the compact operators, answering Robert's trace-cone classification question positively. The isomorphism realizes the prescribed cone map, with arbitrary ideal structure and without a density assumption on the finite domains of the weights.

This answers Robert’s trace-cone question, including algebras with arbitrary ideal structure and both finite and infinite subquotients.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let \(A\) and \(B\) be separable nuclear complex \(C^*\)-algebras. If \(T(A)\) and \(T(B)\) are isomorphic as topological cones, then \[ A\otimes\W\otimes\K\ \cong\ B\otimes\W\otimes\K, \] where \(\K=\K(\ell^2(\N))\) and all tensor products are spatial.

primaryStatements.name: Trace realification
primaryStatements.label: st:realification
primaryStatements.text: For every \(C^*\)-algebra \(C\), the trace cone with topology \eqref{intro:trace-topology} is compact Hausdorff, and it is second countable when \(C\) is separable. If \(C\) is exact, the assignment \(\tau\mapsto d_\tau\) identifies this cone with the topological cone of functionals on \(\Cu(C)\). For every \(C^*\)-algebra \(C\), \[ \Cu(C\otimes\W)\cong\Cu(C)_{\R}. \] Realification is determined functorially by the topological functional cone. Its realization as functions on that cone has pointwise order, pointwise addition, and multiplication by positive real scalars. It has the same functional cone as \(\Cu(C)\). Consequently the given trace-cone isomorphism induces isomorphisms \begin{equation} F:T(Q)\longrightarrow T(P),\qquad G:\Cu(P)\longrightarrow\Cu(Q),\qquad d_\tau(Gx)=d_{F\tau}(x). \end{equation} In particular, for \(x,y\in\Cu(Q)\), \begin{equation} x\leq y \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad d_\tau(x)\leq d_\tau(y)\quad\hbox{for every }\tau\in T(Q). \end{equation} Multiplication by every positive real scalar is an order automorphism preserving increasing suprema and compact containment.

primaryStatements.name: Transport of ideals
primaryStatements.label: st:ideals
primaryStatements.text: The maps \(F,G\) identify the complete ideal lattices of \(P\) and \(Q\), and these identifications agree. They identify the finite and zero ideals of corresponding weights. The resulting homeomorphism of primitive ideal spaces will be used to regard \(\Prim(P)=\Prim(Q)=X\). For an open \(U\subseteq X\), write \(P(U)\) and \(Q(U)\) for the corresponding ideals. Then \[ G(\Cu(P(U)))=\Cu(Q(U)), \] and \[ \Fin(\tau)=Q(U)\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \Fin(F\tau)=P(U), \qquad \Ker(\tau)=Q(U)\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \Ker(F\tau)=P(U). \]

primaryStatements.name: Regularized limits
primaryStatements.label: seq:regularized
primaryStatements.text: Let \(\omega\) be a free ultrafilter on \(\N\), and let \(\tau_n\in T(Q)\) be arbitrary. For a bounded positive sequence \((x_n)\), the formula \begin{equation} \rho([(x_n)])= \sup_{\eps>0}\lim_{n\to\omega}\tau_n((x_n-\eps)_+) \end{equation} defines a lower-semicontinuous tracial weight on \(D\). Its rank functional is \begin{equation} d_\rho([(x_n)])= \sup_{\eps>0}\lim_{n\to\omega}d_{\tau_n}((x_n-\eps)_+). \end{equation} If \(\sigma=\lim_{n\to\omega}\tau_n\) in the canonical topology on \(T(Q)\), then \(\rho|_Q=\sigma\).

primaryStatements.name: Sandwich comparisons
primaryStatements.label: seq:sandwich
primaryStatements.text: Let \(p:S_Y\to D\) be a model, let \(s=f\otimes a\geq0\), and suppose that \(0<m_0:=m(f>0)<\infty\). For \(r>0\), choose \(c_r\in Q_+\) representing \(rG[a]\). Then \begin{equation} c_r\precsim p(s)\quad(0<r<m_0), \qquad p(s)\precsim c_r\quad(r>m_0). \end{equation} The following versions have fixed target cuts. If \(\eta,\delta>0\), \(0<r<m(f>\eta)\), and \(c\) represents \(rG[(a-\delta)_+]\), then, for every \(0<\kappa<\eta\delta\), \begin{equation} c\precsim(p(f\otimes a)-\kappa)_+. \end{equation} If \(r'>m_0\) and \(\eps>0\), then a representative \(b\) of \(r'G[a]\) has a positive cut \((b-\kappa)_+\) such that \begin{equation} (p(f\otimes a)-\eps)_+\precsim(b-\kappa)_+. \end{equation} The choices in these two displays can be made independently of the model \(p\). The complete collection of such comparisons on the countable compact tests characterizes the model equation.

primaryStatements.name: Constant ideals and all traces
primaryStatements.label: seq:all-traces
primaryStatements.text: For a model \(p\) and every \(s\in S\), \begin{equation} \Ideal_D(p(s))=\Ideal_D(Q(U_s)). \end{equation} Given countably many models \(p_i:S\to D\), there is a separable subalgebra \(D_0\subseteq D\) containing their ranges and the constants \(Q\), such that, for every \(\gamma\in T(D_0)\), \begin{equation} \gamma\circ p_i=m\otimes F(\gamma|_Q) \quad\hbox{for every }i. \end{equation} It may also contain any prescribed countable subset of \(D\).

primaryStatements.name: Properties of the local error ideals
primaryStatements.label: seq:smallideal-properties
primaryStatements.text: The definition of \(J(U)\) is independent of representatives and makes it a closed two-sided ideal of \(D\). The assignment is order preserving, and \begin{equation} J(U)\subseteq\Ideal_D(Q(U)). \end{equation} If \(\rho\) is a regularized limit and its restriction \(\sigma=\rho|_Q\) is densely finite on \(Q(U)\), then \begin{equation} \rho|_{J(U)}=0. \end{equation} All assertions use the same conventions in finite matrix algebras.

primaryStatements.name: Small stabilizers
primaryStatements.label: sm:stabilizers
primaryStatements.text: Let \(S=C_0(Y)\otimes P\), and prescribe countably many pairs \[ x_l\in S_+, \qquad e_l\in J(U_{x_l}), \qquad l\in\N. \] There is a homomorphism \(\theta:S\to D\) satisfying \begin{equation} \theta(S(U))\subseteq J(U), \qquad e_l\in\Ideal_D(\theta(x_l)) \quad(U\subseteq X\text{ open},\ l\in\N), \end{equation} in either of the following situations. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item An existing model \(\chi:S\to D\) is given. In this case \(\theta\) can be a slowly vanishing rational UHF fraction of \(\chi\), and it also satisfies \begin{equation} \theta(S(U_x))\subseteq\Ideal_D(\theta(x)) \qquad(x\in S_+). \end{equation} For every fixed \(N\), \(N\) copies of its defining fraction fit in the defining copy of \(\chi\) at all sufficiently late coordinates. \item \(Y=(0,1]\). No model is needed in this case, and \eqref{sm:coarse-fullness} is not asserted. \end{enumerate} In both cases, for every \(l\) and \(\eps>0\) there is \(\delta_{l,\eps}>0\) such that \begin{equation} [ (|e_l|-\eps)_+] \leq[(\theta(x_l)-\delta_{l,\eps})_+] \quad\text{in }\Cu(D). \end{equation} The construction permits the prescribed errors and the stabilizer to occupy separate matrix corners.

definitions.name: Model
definitions.label: seq:model
definitions.text: A model for \((Y,m,F)\) is a homomorphism \(p:S_Y\to D\) such that \begin{equation} \rho\circ p=m\otimes F(\sigma),\qquad \sigma=\rho|_Q, \end{equation} for every regularized limit \(\rho\).

definitions.name: Local error ideal
definitions.label: seq:smallideal
definitions.text: For an open \(U\subseteq X\), an element \(x=[(x_n)]\in D\) belongs to \(J(U)\) if, for every \(\eps>0\), there are a positive element \(c\) compactly Cuntz supported in \(Q(U)\), a sequence \(r_n>0\) tending to zero, and an index \(N\), such that \begin{equation} d_\tau((|x_n|-\eps)_+) \leq r_n d_\tau(c) \qquad(n\geq N,\ \tau\in T(Q)). \end{equation} The controller \(c\), the decay sequence, and \(N\) may depend on \(x,U,\eps\). Once these have been chosen, the same bound holds for all traces and all coordinates in the tail.

lean.scopeText:
The paper classifies separable nuclear complex $C^*$-algebras after tensoring with the Razak–Jacelon algebra and the compact operators, using their cones of extended lower-semicontinuous traces. The linked formalization proves the ideal-transport part: a trace-cone equivalence induces an order isomorphism of closed two-sided ideals, carrying the ideals determined by finiteness and vanishing of each trace to those of its image.

For each closed ideal $I$, it also constructs the trace that is zero on positive elements of $I$ and infinite elsewhere. These traces are exactly the additive idempotents, meaning $\tau+\tau=\tau$, and their addition recovers ideal inclusion. Spatial classification, existence of the stabilization models, norm uniqueness, and final intertwining are outside this supporting comparison.

papers.title: Filtered products and boundary-preserving compression in complex cobordism
papers.abstract: We prove that, in sufficiently large smash powers, an $MU$-null restriction to a finite pointed subcomplex becomes stably null on the entire union of products with a fixed positive proportion of restricted factors. This coherent vanishing theorem yields boundary-preserving compression of cube-valued maps on every compact metrizable input space. When the torus slot bundle embeds continuously into a trivial bundle of rank less than twice the source rank, the compression places a positive proportion of slots on their boundaries in arbitrarily large powers and fixes every original boundary slot exactly. An example at equality shows that the strict rank inequality cannot be removed.
papers.familySummary: For every minimal homeomorphism h of an infinite compact metrizable space X, the radius of comparison of $C(X)\rtimes_h\mathbb Z$ equals $\tfrac12\mathrm{mdim}(X,h)$, including infinite values. Zero mean dimension is equivalent to the small boundary property, Jiang–Su stability and finite nuclear dimension; in this case nuclear dimension is at most one.

primaryStatements.name: Filtered products
primaryStatements.label: thm:filtered-product
primaryStatements.text: Let $G\subset E$ be a finite pointed CW pair, let $d\geq0$ be an integer, and let $v:E\to S^d$ be a based map. Suppose that the composite \[ \Sigma^\infty G\longrightarrow\Sigma^\infty E \xrightarrow{\Sigma^\infty v}\Sigma^d\mathbb S \longrightarrow\Sigma^d MU \] is nullhomotopic. For $\ell\geq1$, let $U_\ell\subset E^{\wedge\ell}$ be the union of the subcomplexes in which at least $\lceil\ell/2\rceil$ factors are required to belong to $G$. Then, for every sufficiently large $\ell$, the restriction \[ v^{\wedge\ell}|_{U_\ell}:U_\ell\longrightarrow S^{d\ell} \] is stably nullhomotopic.

primaryStatements.name: Torus compression
primaryStatements.label: thm:torus-compression
primaryStatements.text: Let $p,n\ge1$ be integers, put $t=2p+1$, and choose $L,H$ as above. Let $0<a<1/16$, let $Y$ be any compact metrizable space, and let $f:Y\to C(t,n)$ be continuous. Suppose there is one continuous complex bundle monomorphism \[ E_f\longrightarrow\mathcal T(f,Z_{an}(t,n))\times\mathbb C^K \] over the entire locus $\mathcal T(f,Z_{an}(t,n))$, for a nonnegative integer $K<2pn$. Then for every integer $U\ge1$ there are an integer $u\ge U$ and a continuous map \[ G:Y^u\longrightarrow C(t,un) \] such that at least $(a/8)un$ slots of $G(\mathbf y)$ lie in $\partial[-1,1]^t$ for every $\mathbf y=(y_0,\ldots,y_{u-1})$. Moreover, for $0\le b<u$ and $1\le j\le n$, \[ f_j(y_b)\in\partial[-1,1]^t \quad\Longrightarrow\quad G_{b,j}(\mathbf y)=f_j(y_b). \]

primaryStatements.name: Compatible Adams lift
primaryStatements.label: prop:compatible-adams-lift
primaryStatements.text: Let $R$ be a commutative ring spectrum, let $G\subset E$ be a finite pointed CW pair, let $d\in\mathbb Z$, and let $v:\Sigma^\infty E\to\Sigma^d\mathbb S$ be a stable map whose restriction to $\Sigma^\infty G$ becomes null in $\Sigma^dR$. For integers $1\leq n\leq\ell$, let $U_{\ell,n}\subset E^{\wedge\ell}$ be the union requiring at least $n$ factors in $G$. Then the restriction of $v^{\wedge\ell}$ admits a lift \[ \Sigma^\infty U_{\ell,n}\longrightarrow\Sigma^{d\ell}I_R^{\wedge n} \] through $\Sigma^{d\ell}\varphi_{R,n}$.

primaryStatements.name: Quantitative nilpotence
primaryStatements.label: thm:quantitative-nilpotence
primaryStatements.text: Fix a prime $p$, and let $R$ be either $MU_{(p)}$ or the Brown--Peterson spectrum $BP$ at that prime. For $k\geq1$, let $f_R(k)$ be the least integer $n\geq0$ for which \begin{equation} I_R^{\wedge n}\wedge\tau_{<k}\mathbb S_{(p)} \xrightarrow{\varphi_{R,n}\wedge\operatorname{id}} \tau_{<k}\mathbb S_{(p)} \end{equation} is nullhomotopic. These integers exist and satisfy \[ \lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{f_R(k)}{k}=0. \] Equivalently, $f_R(k)$ is the least $n$ such that, for every connective $p$-local spectrum $X$ and every $i<k$, a class in $\pi_iX$ of $R$-Adams filtration at least $n$ is zero.

primaryStatements.name: Boundary compression
primaryStatements.label: thm:boundary-compression
primaryStatements.text: Let $P$ be a finite polyhedron, let $f:P\to C(t,n)$ be PL, and fix $0<a<1/16$. If \[ \omega_{MU}\bigl(f,Z_{an}(t,n)\bigr)=0, \] then for arbitrarily large positive integers $u$ there is a continuous map \[ G:P^u\longrightarrow C(t,un) \] with the following properties. At every point of $P^u$, at least $(a/8)un$ output slots are on their cube boundaries. Moreover, if any slot of $f^{\times u}$ is on its boundary, the corresponding slot of $G$ equals that original slot exactly.

definitions.name: Torus locus and slot bundle
definitions.label: not:torus-bundle
definitions.text: On $L^n$ put \[ H_n=\bigoplus_{j=1}^n\operatorname{pr}_j^*H \subset L^n\times\mathbb C^{2pn}. \] For $f:Y\to C(2p+1,n)$ and $Z\subset T(2p+1,n)$, let \[ \mathcal T(f,Z)=\{(y,z)\in Y\times Z:f(y)-z\in L^n\}, \qquad d_f(y,z)=f(y)-z. \] The slot bundle on this locus is $E_f=d_f^*H_n$, of complex rank $pn$, with its fixed embedding in the trivial bundle of rank $2pn$.

definitions.name: Point test
definitions.label: def:point-test
definitions.text: Recall $c=1/32$. Let $P$ be a finite polyhedron, let $f:P\to C(t,n)$ be PL, and let $Z\subseteq T(t,n)$ be a subpolyhedron. Define \begin{align*} A_c(f,Z)&=\{(x,z)\in P\times Z:\|f(x)-z\|_\infty\ge c\},\\ Q_c(f,Z)&=(P\times Z)/A_c(f,Z). \end{align*} For $0<\rho<c$, take the oriented collapse $\kappa_\rho:\R^M\to S^M$ of the complement of $(-\rho,\rho)^M$. The point test is the based map \begin{equation} \varphi_\rho(f,Z):Q_c(f,Z)\longrightarrow S^M, \qquad [x,z]\longmapsto\kappa_\rho(f(x)-z). \end{equation} Its stable class is denoted by \[ \omega_{\mathbb S}(f,Z)\in [\Sigma^\infty Q_c(f,Z),\Sigma^M\mathbb S]. \] Composing with the unit $\mathbb S\to MU$ gives $\omega_{MU}(f,Z)\in\widetilde{MU}^{M}(Q_c(f,Z))$.

papers.title: Radius of comparison equals half the mean dimension
papers.abstract: We prove the integer-action case of the Phillips–Toms conjecture: for every minimal homeomorphism of an infinite compact metrizable space, the radius of comparison of its crossed product equals one half of its mean dimension, including equality at infinity. For these systems, zero mean dimension and the small boundary property are equivalent to Jiang–Su stability and to finite nuclear dimension of the crossed product; in this case its nuclear dimension is at most one.
