primaryStatements.name: Zero mean dimension and crossed-product regularity
primaryStatements.label: cor:regularity
primaryStatements.text: Let \(h\) be a minimal homeomorphism of an infinite compact metrizable space \(X\), and put \(A=C(X)\rtimes_h\Z\). The following conditions are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item \(\mdim(X,h)=0\); \item \((X,h)\) has the small boundary property; \item \(A\cong A\otimes\mathcal Z\); \item \(\dim_{\mathrm{nuc}}(A)<\infty\); \item \(\dim_{\mathrm{nuc}}(A)\le1\). \end{enumerate} In particular, if \(\mdim(X,h)\in(0,\infty]\), then \(A\not\cong A\otimes\mathcal Z\) and \(\dim_{\mathrm{nuc}}(A)=\infty\).

primaryStatements.name: Torus compression {\cite[Theorem 1.3
primaryStatements.label: thm:torus-compression
primaryStatements.text: {OpenAICompression2026}}] Let $p,n\ge1$ be integers, put $t=2p+1$, and use the fixed framed torus $L$ and rank-$p$ bundle $H$ specified above. Let $0<a<1/16$, let $Y$ be any compact metrizable space, and let $f:Y\to C(t,n)$ be continuous. Suppose there are a nonnegative integer $K<2pn$ and one continuous complex bundle monomorphism \[ d_f^*H_n\longrightarrow \mathcal T(f,Z_{an}(t,n))\times\C^K \] over the full compact locus $\mathcal T(f,Z_{an}(t,n))$. Then, for every integer $U\ge1$, there are an integer $u\ge U$ and a continuous map \[ G:Y^u\longrightarrow C(t,un) \] such that for every $\mathbf y=(y_0,\ldots,y_{u-1})\in Y^u$: \begin{enumerate} \item at least $(a/8)un$ slots of $G(\mathbf y)$ lie in $\partial C_t$; \item for every $0\le b<u$ and $1\le j\le n$, \[ f_j(y_b)\in\partial C_t \quad\Longrightarrow\quad G_{b,j}(\mathbf y)=f_j(y_b). \] \end{enumerate} The slots of $f^{\times u}$ and $G$ are ordered first by copy $b$ and then by original slot $j$.

primaryStatements.name: Niu's open tower theorem
primaryStatements.label: thm:niu-open-tower
primaryStatements.text: For every integer $L\geq1$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, there is an open set $V\subset X$ such that $V,hV,\ldots,h^{L-1}V$ are pairwise disjoint and, writing $\mathcal T=\bigcup_{j=0}^{L-1}h^jV$, \[ \lim_{m\to\infty}\frac1m\sup_{x\in X} \sum_{s=0}^{m-1}\mathbf 1_{X\setminus\mathcal T}(h^sx) <\varepsilon. \] In particular, $\mu(\mathcal T)>1-\varepsilon$ for every $\mu\in\mathcal M_h(X)$.

primaryStatements.name: Comparison gives a parametrized bundle embedding
primaryStatements.label: prop:comparison-bundle
primaryStatements.text: Let $r$ be a comparison bound for $A$. Fix positive integers $p,g,k,H_0$ with $H_0\geq2$, numbers $0<a<1/16$ and $b_0>0$, and an integer $R$ such that \begin{equation} \frac{RH_0}{pg(H_0-1)}+2(a+b_0)<2, \qquad \frac{R-pg}{k}>r. \end{equation} Let $F_1,\ldots,F_g:X\to[-1,1]^t$ be arbitrary continuous maps. Choose $B,(O_i)_{i=0}^{k-1},w,K$ as in \Cref{lem:uniform-block-allocation}, with $\gamma=R-pg$ and $e=kH_0$. For all sufficiently large integers $J$, put \[ N=eJ,\qquad n=J(H_0-1)g. \] There is a continuous map $f_J:X\to[-1,1]^{tn}$, with slots indexed by \[ (q,D,j),\qquad 0\leq q<J,\quad 0\leq D\leq H_0-2,\quad 1\leq j\leq g, \] such that \begin{equation} (f_J)_{q,D,j}(x)=F_j(h^{qe+i+Dk}x) \quad\text{when }h^{qe}x\in O_i \text{ and }w(h^{qe}x)>0. \end{equation} The agreement holds, more strongly, on a neighborhood of each compact set $h^{-qe}(\operatorname{supp}(w)\cap O_i)$. Over the compact space \begin{equation} \mathcal L_J= \{(x,z)\in X\times Z_{an}(t,n): f_J(x)-z\in L^n\}, \end{equation} the direct sum of the $n$ pullbacks of $H$, by the slot maps $(x,z)\mapsto(f_J)_\alpha(x)-z_\alpha$, embeds continuously in a trivial complex bundle of rank strictly less than $2pn$. The same allocation $B,(O_i),w,K$ works for every such $J$.

primaryStatements.label: thm:cover-bound
primaryStatements.text: Let $h$ be a minimal homeomorphism of an infinite compact metrizable space $X$, and let $A=C(X)\rtimes_h\Z$. For every finite comparison bound $r$ for $A$ and every finite open cover $\mathcal U$ of $X$, \[ \lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{D(\mathcal U^{[0,k)})}{k}\le2r. \]

papers.title: Weak pure infiniteness and O-infinity absorption
papers.abstract: We prove that every complex C∗-algebra in which each positive element is properly infinite is strongly purely infinite. This answers the ordinary-to-strong part of Kirchberg–Rørdam's comparison question. For exact algebras, we also prove that proper infiniteness of one fixed finite amplification of every positive element implies proper infiniteness of each positive element. Consequently, every separable nuclear algebra with this fixed-amplification property absorbs $\mathcal O_\infty$, without assumptions of unitality or simplicity.
papers.familySummary: Resolves the ordinary-to-strong pure-infiniteness question of Kirchberg and Rørdam for complex C∗-algebras. For exact algebras, proper infiniteness of one fixed finite amplification of every positive element also suffices. Consequently, every separable nuclear algebra with this property absorbs $\mathcal O_\infty$, without unitality or simplicity assumptions.

papers.sourceAbstract: We prove that every complex \(C^*\)-algebra in which each positive element is properly infinite is strongly purely infinite. This answers the ordinary-to-strong part of Kirchberg--R{\o}rdam's comparison question. Consequently, every separable nuclear algebra with this fixed-amplification property absorbs \(\Oinf\), without assumptions of unitality or simplicity.

primaryStatements.label: thm:individual-to-strong
primaryStatements.text: Let \(C\) be a complex \(C^*\)-algebra satisfying \(\propP\). For all \(a,b\in C_+\), \(c\in C\), and \(\varepsilon>0\), there are \(s,t\in C\) such that \begin{equation} \|s^*as-a\|<\varepsilon,\qquad \|t^*bt-b\|<\varepsilon,\qquad \|s^*ct\|<\varepsilon. \end{equation} Consequently \(C\) is strongly purely infinite.

primaryStatements.label: thm:exact-infiniteness
primaryStatements.text: Let \(C\) be an exact complex \(C^*\)-algebra. Suppose that there is one integer \(n\ge1\) such that \(h^{\oplus n}\) is properly infinite for every \(h\in C_+\). Then every positive element of \(C\) is properly infinite. Consequently \(C\) is strongly purely infinite.

primaryStatements.label: cor:absorption
primaryStatements.text: Let \(A\) be a separable nuclear complex \(C^*\)-algebra. If there is one integer \(n\ge1\) such that \(h^{\oplus n}\) is properly infinite for every \(h\in A_+\), then \[ A\cong A\otimes_{\min}\Oinf. \]

primaryStatements.name: Fixed measurements of a graph
primaryStatements.label: prop:graph
primaryStatements.text: Let \(C\) be a \(C^*\)-algebra, let \(a,y\in C_+\) be contractions with \(a\) rich, and let \(c\in\widetilde C\) be a contraction. For an integer \(k\ge1\) and fixed positive \(\gamma_g,\sigma_g\) satisfying \eqref{eq:graph-constants}, there are \[ X\in\Her((a-1/8)_+)_+,\qquad B_1,\ldots,B_k\in\Her((a-1/8)_+) \] with the following property. For any contractions \[ S_i\in\Her((X-\alpha_0)_+),\qquad 1\le i\le k, \] one can form a rich positive contraction \(p\in\Her(a)\) such that, for every representation \(\pi\) of \(C\), \(\|\pi(a)\|>1/2\) implies \(\|\pi(p)\|=1\). If a representation \(\pi\) of \(C\) satisfies \[ \pi\bigl(y(1-c^*p^2c)y\bigr)=0,\qquad \|\pi(y)\|>s, \] then, in that same representation, \begin{equation} \|\pi(X)\|>s,\qquad \pi(B_i)=\pi(S_i)\quad(1\le i\le k). \end{equation} The elements \(X,B_1,\ldots,B_k\) are fixed before the \(S_i\) are chosen.

primaryStatements.name: Four entries avoid the fixed measurements
primaryStatements.label: prop:four-avoidance
primaryStatements.text: Suppose \(C\) satisfies \(\propP\). Let \(X\in C_+\) and \(B_1,B_2,B_3,B_4\in C\). With \[ \alpha_0=\frac1{32}<\alpha=\frac1{16} <\beta=\frac18<s=\frac14,\qquad h=\frac12, \] there exist contractions \(T_1,\ldots,T_4\) in \(\Her((X-\alpha_0)_+)\) for which no representation \(\pi\) of \(C\) satisfies \begin{equation} \|\pi(X)\|>s,\qquad \pi(B_i)=\pi(T_i)\quad(1\le i\le4). \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Shrinking under individual proper infiniteness
primaryStatements.label: prop:shrinking-P
primaryStatements.text: Suppose \(C\) satisfies \(\propP\). Let \(a,y\in C\) be positive contractions and let \(c\in\widetilde C\) be a contraction. There are positive contractions \(p_1\in\Her(a)\) and \(q_1\in\Her(y)\), with \(p_1\) rich, such that for every representation \(\pi\) of \(C\), \begin{equation} \|\pi(a)\|>1/2\ \Longrightarrow\ \|\pi(p_1)\|=1, \qquad \|\pi(y)\|>1/2\ \Longrightarrow\ \|\pi(q_1)\|=1, \end{equation} and, in the universal bidual, \begin{equation} \|e_{p_1}c e_{q_1}\|<1. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Arbitrarily small support compression
primaryStatements.label: prop:iterated-separation
primaryStatements.text: Suppose \(C\) satisfies \(\propP\). For positive contractions \(a_*,b_*\in C\), a contraction \(c_*\in C\), and \(\zeta>0\), there are positive contractions \(p\in\Her(a_*)\), \(q\in\Her(b_*)\) such that \[ \|e_p c_*e_q\|<\zeta \] and, for every representation \(\pi\), \[ \|\pi(a_*)\|>1/2\ \Longrightarrow\ \|\pi(p)\|=1, \qquad \|\pi(b_*)\|>1/2\ \Longrightarrow\ \|\pi(q)\|=1. \]

primaryStatements.name: Comparison with bounded coefficients
primaryStatements.label: prop:bounded-diagonalization
primaryStatements.text: Suppose \(C\) satisfies \(\propP\). Let \(a,b\in C_+\) be contractions and let \(c\in C\). Given \[ 0<\delta<1/2,\qquad 0<\rho\le2\delta,\qquad \zeta>0, \] there exist \(s,t\in C\) such that \begin{align} \|s^*as-a\|,\ \|t^*bt-b\|&<2\delta+\rho, \\ \|s^*ct\|&<\zeta,\qquad \|s\|,\ \|t\|\le\delta^{-1/2}. \end{align}

definitions.label: def:rich
definitions.text: A positive contraction \(a\) is rich if \((a-\varepsilon)_+\) is properly infinite for every \(\varepsilon\ge0\).

lean.scopeText:
The formalization proves that a complex $C^*$-algebra in which every positive element is properly infinite is strongly purely infinite, with the full positive-element diagonalization property. No exactness, nuclearity, unitality, or simplicity assumption is needed for this implication.

For exact algebras, proper infiniteness of one fixed finite amplification of every positive element already implies individual proper infiniteness and strong pure infiniteness.

papers.title: The Hilbert–Smith conjecture in every finite dimension
papers.abstract: We prove the Hilbert–Smith conjecture in every finite dimension: every locally compact second-countable Hausdorff group acting faithfully and jointly continuously on a connected Hausdorff second-countable finite-dimensional topological manifold without boundary is a Lie group.
papers.familySummary: Every locally compact second-countable Hausdorff group acting faithfully and jointly continuously on a connected finite-dimensional topological manifold is a Lie group. This proves the Hilbert–Smith conjecture in all finite dimensions, for Hausdorff second-countable manifolds without boundary.

primaryStatements.name: $p$-adic exclusion
primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let \(n\geq1\) be an integer and \(p\) a prime. Every jointly continuous action of \(\Zp\) on a connected Hausdorff second-countable topological \(n\)-manifold without boundary has nonzero kernel. Consequently the action factors through a finite quotient of \(\Zp\).

primaryStatements.name: The Hilbert--Smith conjecture
primaryStatements.label: cor:lie
primaryStatements.text: Let \(n\geq1\). A locally compact second-countable Hausdorff group acting faithfully and jointly continuously on a connected Hausdorff second-countable topological \(n\)-manifold without boundary is a Lie group.

primaryStatements.name: Duality and compact support
primaryStatements.label: prop:test-duality
primaryStatements.text: The Verdier operation restricts to a triangulated duality on each of $\Tzero(X)$, $\T(X)$, $\Pzero(X)$, and $\Pcat(X)$. In particular, for every object $A$ in one of these categories, $\D_X A$ belongs to the same category and the canonical map \[ \eta_A:A\xrightarrow{\sim}\D_X^2A \] is an isomorphism. There is a compact $K\subset X$ outside which both $A$ and $\D_X A$ vanish.

primaryStatements.name: Direct images and open extension
primaryStatements.label: prop:test-pushforward
primaryStatements.text: For an allowed map $g:X\to Y$, direct image induces exact functors \[ g_*:\Tzero(X)\longrightarrow\Tzero(Y), \qquad g_*:\T(X)\longrightarrow\T(Y), \] and the analogous functors for $\Pzero,\Pcat$. They are given by $Rg_!\simeq Rg_*$ on these categories, commute coherently with Verdier duality and its shifts, and are compatible with composition. For an open inclusion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, this functor is $j_!$ and is fully faithful.

primaryStatements.name: Homotopy invariance
primaryStatements.label: thm:homotopy
primaryStatements.text: If $h:I\times X\to Y$ is a continuous homotopy of maps of test spaces, its endpoint maps induce equal homomorphisms \[ h_{0*}=h_{1*}:E_r(X)\longrightarrow E_r(Y) \qquad(r\in\Z). \] The same assertion holds for $W_r(\Pcat(-))$ under the allowed semialgebraic homotopies. In particular, homotopy equivalences induce isomorphisms, and a nonempty contractible test space has the Witt groups of a point. The semialgebraic assertion uses a contraction in the allowed semialgebraic category.

primaryStatements.name: Objects supported in an open set
primaryStatements.label: prop:compact-support
primaryStatements.text: For an open inclusion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, the essential image of $j_!: \Bcat(U)\to\Bcat(X)$ consists exactly of those objects whose cohomology vanishes outside some compact subset of $U$. This image is a thick, duality-stable subcategory.

primaryStatements.name: Germ description
primaryStatements.label: thm:germs
primaryStatements.text: Restriction induces natural isomorphisms \[ \Hom_{\Bcat(X)/\Bcat(U)}(A,B) \simeq \operatorname*{colim}_{N\supset X\setminus U} \Hom_{\mathsf D(N)}(A|_N,B|_N) \] for every $A,B\in\Bcat(X)$. These isomorphisms respect composition, open restriction of duality, and restriction of distinguished triangles. The quotient here is the Verdier quotient itself.

primaryStatements.name: Witt localization
primaryStatements.label: thm:witt-localization
primaryStatements.text: For every open $U\subset X$ and every $r\in\Z$, there is a natural long exact sequence \begin{equation} \cdots\longrightarrow W_r(\Bcat(U)) \longrightarrow W_r(\Bcat(X)) \longrightarrow W_r(\Bcat(X)/\Bcat(U)) \xrightarrow{\partial}W_{r-1}(\Bcat(U)) \longrightarrow\cdots. \end{equation} The sequence is natural for $\Pcat\to\T$ and for the pushforwards of \Cref{prop:test-pushforward}: a map $g:X\to X'$ with $g(U)\subset U'$ induces a morphism from the sequence for $(X,U)$ to the sequence for $(X',U')$.

definitions.name: The test categories
definitions.label: def:test-categories
definitions.text: Let $\Tzero(X)$ be the smallest full replete triangulated subcategory of $\mathsf D(X)$ containing \begin{equation} Rf_*\const{\R}{B}, \qquad f:B\longrightarrow X, \qquad B\text{ a compact finite polyhedron}, \end{equation} where $f$ is any continuous map. Let $\T(X)$ be its closure under direct summands in $\mathsf D(X)$. When $X$ has a specified semialgebraic model, define $\Pzero(X)$ and $\Pcat(X)$ in the same manner, requiring $B$ to be a compact polyhedron in a Euclidean space and $f$ to be continuous semialgebraic in the specified models. For an arbitrary open subset $U$ of a semialgebraic model, the condition on $f:B\to U$ is that its composite into that model be semialgebraic. The open subset itself need not be semialgebraic. An allowed map for $\T$ is a continuous map of test spaces. For $\Pcat$ we use continuous semialgebraic maps in the models, their restrictions to the open subsets under consideration, and inclusions of such open subsets. The condition on a map used in the arguments below is that composition carry every allowed compact-source generator to an allowed compact-source generator. Homotopies for $\Pcat$ satisfy this condition in their two variables; the continuous semialgebraic homotopies used below do so.

definitions.name: Character classes
definitions.label: def:character-classes
definitions.text: Let \[ \ell_U:E_d(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}W_d(\mathcal Q_U(X)) \] be the integral isomorphism of \Cref{prop:contractible-quotient}. For $0\leq i<m$ define $z_i(t)\in E_d(X)$ uniquely by \begin{equation} \ell_U(z_i(t))= [A_t,\alpha_t]+[A_t,\alpha_t\circ(2e_i-\id)]. \end{equation}

papers.title: A boundary-only obstruction to four-dimensional disk embedding
papers.abstract: We disprove the four-dimensional disc embedding conjecture without a fundamental-group hypothesis, even when no homotopy classes or output framings are prescribed. We construct a compact oriented smooth four-manifold containing finitely many disc maps with framed algebraic dual spheres whose boundary circles bound no disjoint locally flat discs. Consequently, the free group on two generators is not good in the sense of Freedman–Quinn, and neither is any group containing it as a subgroup.
papers.familySummary: The unrestricted four-dimensional disk-embedding conjecture fails: framed algebraic dual spheres do not suffice to obtain disjoint locally flat spanning disks. In particular, the free group F2 is not good in the sense of Freedman–Quinn. Also constructs a finitely presented integral Poincaré duality group of dimension four with a finite classifying space but no realization as the fundamental group of a closed aspherical topological four-manifold, disproving Wall's conjecture.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: There exist a compact connected oriented smooth four-manifold $M$ with nonempty boundary, an integer $k\geq1$, proper generically immersed discs \[ f_i\colon(D^2,S^1)\longrightarrow(M,\partial M),\qquad 1\leq i\leq k, \] whose boundary restrictions form an embedding of $\coprod_iS^1$, and framed sphere maps $g_i\colon S^2\to M$ such that \begin{equation} \lambda(f_i,g_j)=\delta_{ij}\,1,\qquad \lambda(g_i,g_j)=0,\qquad \widetilde\mu(g_i)=0 \quad(1\leq i,j\leq k), \end{equation} but the given boundary circles do not bound pairwise disjoint proper locally flat embedded discs in $M$. Each $g_i$ can be chosen to be a smooth embedded sphere; different $g_i$ are allowed to intersect.

primaryStatements.name: Nongoodness of the free group
primaryStatements.label: cor:nongood
primaryStatements.text: The free group $F_2$ on two generators is not good in the sense of Freedman--Quinn. Every group containing a subgroup isomorphic to $F_2$ is likewise not good.

primaryStatements.label: cor:surgery-conjunction
primaryStatements.text: The unrestricted topological surgery and $s$-cobordism assertions cannot both hold.

primaryStatements.name: The exact algebraic input
primaryStatements.label: geo:input-invariants
primaryStatements.text: There are orientations and whiskers for the discs and spheres such that, for all $r,s\in\mathcal R$ and $R=\mathbb Z[\pi_1(M)]$, \begin{equation} \lambda(f_r,g_s)=\delta_{rs}\,1\in R, \qquad \lambda(g_r,g_s)=0\in R, \qquad \widetilde\mu(g_r)=0. \end{equation} In particular the normal second Stiefel--Whitney number of every $g_r$ is zero. These data satisfy all algebraic and boundary hypotheses of the unrestricted disc-embedding assertion.

primaryStatements.name: The geometric input and the forced cut data
primaryStatements.label: geo:construction
primaryStatements.text: For every $d\geq5$, with the finite word set $\mathcal H$ defined above, the preceding construction produces a compact connected oriented smooth four-manifold $M$ with nonempty boundary, a finite family $F=(f_r)_{r\in\mathcal R}$ of smooth proper disc maps with disjoint embedded boundary, and individually embedded framed sphere maps $(g_r)_{r\in\mathcal R}$ satisfying \eqref{geo:invariants}. If the circles $\partial F$ bound pairwise disjoint proper locally flat embedded discs in $M$, the following data exist: \begin{enumerate} \item The compact oriented smooth four-manifold $G$ has a homotopy equivalence $p:G\longrightarrow\Gamma$, where $\Gamma$ is the rose on $h_0,h_+,h_-,q_1,\ldots,q_d$. The boundary is $Q\cup\bigcup_e C_e$, with the free group and peripheral coordinates of Lemma \ref{geo:graph} and the longitude--meridian interchange \eqref{geo:hopf-collar}. \item There are disjoint cooriented smooth cuts $J_1,\ldots,J_d$, each a compact oriented three-manifold with one boundary torus and possibly additional closed components. Their boundary tori are the fixed product cuts in the $C_e$. \item Cutting $G$ along all $J_e$ gives a compact oriented smooth four-manifold $X$, possibly disconnected. With half collars absorbed into $Q$, its boundary is obtained by gluing $Q$ to the two oppositely oriented copies of each $J_e$ along their boundary tori. Every torus-bearing wall component has just that one torus; closed wall components remain separate. Regluing the paired cuts recovers $G$. \item The map on $X$ lands in the graph cut open at the chosen $q_e$ points, namely $\Gamma_h$ with the resulting half-edges; it is constant on every copy of a cut at its endpoint value. All words \eqref{geo:relations} are trivial in the fundamental group of the component $X_Q$ containing $Q$, with the original basings in $Q$. \item Extend \eqref{geo:matrices} to $\pi_1(\Gamma)$ by $\rho(q_e)=1$. The associated adjoint local system on $G$ restricts to $\rho$ on the $h$ generators, to the identity on all $z_a$, and to a trivial system on each $J_e$, with matching reference frames on its two copies induced by the graph point. \end{enumerate} The implication uses only the asserted embedded discs. It imposes neither output-dual conditions nor an additional framing or relative homotopy condition on those discs.

primaryStatements.name: Wall and vertex coordinates
primaryStatements.label: def:restriction-charts
primaryStatements.text: There are wall charts with parameters \[ (a_i,y_i)\in\mathbb C^3\oplus\mathbb C^{n_i}, \] vertex parameters \((a,t)\in\mathbb C^{3d}\oplus\mathbb C^D\), a vertex defect ideal \(\mathfrak r\subset\mathbb C[[a,t]]\), and algebraic maps \begin{equation} \iota_i^+(a,t)=(a_i,Y_i^+(a,t)),\qquad \iota_i^-(a,t)=(0,Y_i^-(a,t)), \end{equation} with the following properties. The maps give the actual based restrictions of the flat vertex family modulo \(\mathfrak r\). The \(a_i\) are algebraic group coordinates for the first-slope holonomy, centered at the identity. The two maps \[ t\longmapsto Y(0,t),\qquad t\longmapsto \sigma Y(0,t), \quad Y=(Y_i^+,Y_i^-)_{i=1}^d, \] have injective and complementary tangent images in \(\mathcal Y\).

primaryStatements.name: Cubic nilpotence
primaryStatements.label: def:cubic-nilpotence
primaryStatements.text: In \(B/\mathfrak r\), where \(B=\mathbb C[[a,t]]\), let \(\mathfrak n\) be generated by all matrix entries of the end holonomies minus \(1\). Then \begin{equation} \mathfrak n^3=0. \end{equation} In particular, for either restriction map in \eqref{def:restriction-maps}, \begin{equation} (\iota_i^\pm)^*(\mathfrak k_i)^3\subset\mathfrak r . \end{equation} The same conclusion holds for the cube of the sum of all these pulled-back ideals.

primaryStatements.name: Generation of the full defect ideal
primaryStatements.label: conn:derivative-ideal
primaryStatements.text: In \(B=\mathbb C[[a,t]]\), \begin{equation} \bigl(\partial_C\Psi(a,Y(a,t))\bigr)=\mathfrak r. \end{equation}

definitions.name: Scalar rings and formal coefficients
definitions.label: def:coefficient-convention
definitions.text: An algebraic parameter chart will mean a local \(\mathbb C\)-algebra essentially of finite type and etale over an affine coordinate space at the designated origin. Its completion is \(B=\mathbb C[[v_1,\ldots,v_N]]\), with maximal ideal \(\mathfrak m\). Finite collections of algebraic germs obtained by an implicit equation with invertible Jacobian can always be placed in one such chart, after replacing it by a common etale neighborhood. For a smooth manifold \(Z\), smooth forms with formal coefficients mean \[ \Omega^j(Z)\widehat\otimes B =\varprojlim_k\bigl(\Omega^j(Z)\otimes_{\mathbb C} B/\mathfrak m^k\bigr). \] For quotients of \(B\), use the analogous inverse limit. The extension of a scalar ideal \(I\) to this space always means its closed extension. Differential operations in the \(Z\)-variables preserve that extension; multiplication respects its powers. Integration over a compact manifold is defined at each finite parameter quotient and then by inverse limit.

definitions.name: The polarized wall function
definitions.label: conn:potential-definition
definitions.text: Use the global frame in Lemma \ref{conn:wall-collar}, and denote the fiber connection form by \(A_i\). With \(\epsilon_i=\int_{\partial J_i}d\theta_i\wedge d\eta_i\), put \begin{align} \operatorname{CS}_{J_i}(A_i) &=\int_{J_i}\operatorname{tr} \left(A_i\wedge dA_i+\frac23 A_i\wedge A_i\wedge A_i\right), \notag\\ P_i(a_i,y_i) &=\operatorname{CS}_{J_i}(A_i) +\epsilon_i\operatorname{tr}(U_iV_i). \end{align} The differential in this integral is fiberwise. Integrals over all closed components are included with their chosen orientations.

definitions.name: The algebraic input
definitions.label: alg:input-data
definitions.text: Fix finitely many labels $1\leq i\leq d$, integers $n_i\geq0$, and $D=\sum_i n_i$. Write \[ a_i=(a_{i,1},a_{i,2},a_{i,3}),\qquad y_i\in\mathbb C^{n_i},\qquad C=(C_i^+,C_i^-)_{i=1}^d\in\mathbb C^{2D},\qquad z=(a,t),\quad t\in\mathbb C^D. \] An algebraic germ in specified coordinates means a regular germ at the specified complex point of an \'etale neighborhood of their affine coordinate space, expanded in those coordinates. Finitely many such germs can be placed in a common neighborhood. The following are the input data established by the preceding geometric and connection constructions. \begin{enumerate} \item For each $i$ there is a local \'etale complex ring $A_i$ in coordinates $(a_i,y_i)$, with completion $B_i=\mathbb C[[a_i,y_i]]$, maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_i$, and an ideal $\mathfrak k_i\subset\mathfrak m_i$. The formal potential $P_i^{\mathrm{o}}\in\mathfrak m_i^3B_i$ satisfies, for every wall coordinate $x$, \[ \partial_xP_i^{\mathrm{o}}\in\mathfrak k_iB_i,\qquad \partial_xP_i^{\mathrm{o}}\in A_i+\mathfrak k_i^bB_i \quad(b\geq1). \] The second assertion means that a representative in the same ring $A_i$ exists at every indicated ideal order; it does not assert that the full gradient is algebraic. \item There are centered algebraic germs $Y_i^\pm(z)$ and an algebraic ideal $\mathfrak r$ in a local \'etale chart in $z$. All ideals in the following identities are extended to $B_X=\mathbb C[[z]]$, whose maximal ideal is $\mathfrak m$. Put \[ \phi_i^+(z)=(a_i,Y_i^+(z)),\qquad \phi_i^-(z)=(0,Y_i^-(z)),\qquad L_i^\pm=\phi_i^{\pm *}(\mathfrak k_i)B_X. \] Then $L_i^\pm\subset\mathfrak m$ and \begin{equation} (L_i^\pm)^3\subset\mathfrak r. \end{equation} \item With $Y=(Y_i^+,Y_i^-)_{i=1}^d$, define \[ \Psi^{\mathrm{o}}(a,C) =\sum_{i=1}^d\bigl(P_i^{\mathrm{o}}(a_i,C_i^+) -P_i^{\mathrm{o}}(0,C_i^-)\bigr), \qquad p_i^{\mathrm{o}}(y_i)=\partial_{a_{i,1}}P_i^{\mathrm{o}}(0,y_i). \] Differentiation with respect to $C$ is performed before substitution. The following identities hold in $B_X$: \begin{equation} \bigl((\partial_C\Psi^{\mathrm{o}})(a,Y)\bigr)=\mathfrak r, \qquad \Psi^{\mathrm{o}}(a,Y)\in\mathfrak r^2, \end{equation} and, for every ordered triple $(i,j,k)$, with repetitions allowed, \begin{equation} a_{i,1}a_{j,1}a_{k,1}\in\mathfrak r,\qquad p_i^{\mathrm{o}}(Y_i^-) p_j^{\mathrm{o}}(Y_j^-) p_k^{\mathrm{o}}(Y_k^-)\in\mathfrak r. \end{equation} Here the original triple memberships and \eqref{alg:cube-input} are consequences of the end-deviation cube law on the original restriction graph. \item Let $\sigma$ exchange $C_i^+$ and $C_i^-$ for every $i$, and set $J=\partial_tY(0,0)$, a $2D$-by-$D$ matrix. The two tangent images are complementary: \begin{equation} \Delta=\det[\,J\ \ \sigma J\,]\ne0. \end{equation} \end{enumerate}

papers.title: A marked tensor obstruction to four-dimensional disk embedding
papers.abstract: We disprove the unrestricted four-dimensional disk-embedding conjecture. We construct immersed disks in a compact oriented smooth four-manifold with framed algebraic dual spheres satisfying the usual equivariant intersection and reduced self-intersection conditions, but with no pairwise disjoint locally flat replacements that preserve the boundary maps and induced normal framings. The obstruction holds even when the replacement disks' relative homotopy classes are not prescribed.
papers.familySummary: The unrestricted four-dimensional disk-embedding conjecture fails: framed algebraic dual spheres do not suffice to obtain disjoint locally flat spanning disks. In particular, the free group F2 is not good in the sense of Freedman–Quinn. Also constructs a finitely presented integral Poincaré duality group of dimension four with a finite classifying space but no realization as the fundamental group of a closed aspherical topological four-manifold, disproving Wall's conjecture.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: There exist a compact connected oriented smooth four-manifold \(M\) with boundary, an integer \(k\geq1\), generically immersed proper disks \[ f_1,\ldots,f_k:(D^2,S^1)\longrightarrow(M,\partial M) \] with disjoint embedded boundary circles, and generically immersed framed spheres \(g_1,\ldots,g_k:S^2\longrightarrow M\), such that \[ \lambda(f_i,g_j)=\delta_{ij},\qquad \lambda(g_i,g_j)=0\quad\text{for all }i,j,\qquad \widetilde\mu(g_i)=0\quad\text{for all }i, \] but there are no pairwise disjoint locally flat embedded disks in \(M\) with the same boundary maps and the boundary normal framings induced by the \(f_i\).

primaryStatements.name: Geometric reduction
primaryStatements.label: prop:geometric-reduction
primaryStatements.text: For the integers \(m,p\) and the finite list just specified, there is a compact connected oriented smooth four-manifold \(X\), constructed without Assumption \ref{ass:disk}, with the following properties. It has a regular cover with deck group \(F_m\), whose block graph is the Cayley tree of \(F_m\). Each block is a four-dimensional one-handlebody on the \(p\) extra letters. Its exposed boundary piece is \[ K_v\cong \bigl(\#^p(S^1\times S^2)\bigr) \setminus\operatorname{int}\nu(L_{2m}), \] where \(L_{2m}\) is a \(2m\)-component unlink in a ball. The port meridians and the extra letters freely generate \(\pi_1K_v\). At every join, the meridian on one side is the longitude on the other. There is a finite family of framed grope bodies with boundary in these pieces, equivariant in the cover, realizing the list \eqref{eq:three-slot-inputs}. If Assumption \ref{ass:disk} holds, there are equivariant cuts, with compact quotient, having connected vertex pieces \(V_v\) and connected edge three-manifolds \(Y_e\). Each \(Y_e\) has as its entire boundary the prescribed join torus. Every corresponding three-slot grope word is trivial in \(\pi_1V_v\). In the index-two parity quotient, these cuts give two connected vertex pieces \(A,B\) and \(2m\) connected oriented edge pieces \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_{2m}\). Their ambient manifold \(X_2\) is homotopy equivalent to the graph with two vertices and \(2m\) edges, with \(p\) additional circles at each vertex. For any characteristic-zero field \(k\), difference of restrictions gives \begin{equation} H^2(A;k)\oplus H^2(B;k) \xrightarrow{\;\cong\;} \bigoplus_{i=1}^{2m}H^2(Y_i;k). \end{equation} In degree one it is surjective, and restricts to an isomorphism on the kernel of evaluation on the \(p\) extra loops at each vertex. At each boundary torus choose the two original coordinate loops \(\alpha_i,\beta_i\) so that \(\alpha_i\) has nonzero image in \(H_1(Y_i;k)\) and \(\beta_i\) has zero image. Such a choice is possible: one of the original coordinate directions, not just an arbitrary slope, is killed. Call the endpoint where \(\beta_i\) is a longitude the plus endpoint; there \(\alpha_i\) is the port meridian. There are exactly \(m\) edges with plus endpoint \(A\). After numbering these as \(1,\ldots,m\), the finite relation list includes, at \(A\), all the required three-slot relations on any three distinct \(\alpha_i\), and, at \(B\), those on the corresponding \(\beta_i\), with independent conjugations by \(\mathcal C\).

primaryStatements.label: thm:tensor-obstruction
primaryStatements.text:

Let \(I\subset\{1,\ldots,n\}\) have cardinality \(m\geq5\), and let \[ F_i\in K\langle h_iangle\quad(1\leq i\leq n), \qquad b_i\in K\langle h_iangle\quad(i\in I). \] Put \[ T=K[t_i:i\in I]/(t_i^2:i\in I),\qquad S_0(h)=\sum_{i=1}^nF_i(h_i),\qquad S_t(h)=S_0(h)+\sum_{i\in I}t_i b_i(h_i). \] Suppose there are formal parametrizations \[ H_L(x,t)\in (x,t)\,T[[x]]^N,\qquad H_R(y)\in (y)\,K[[y]]^N, \] where \(x\) has \(a\) coordinates and \(y\) has \(N-a\) coordinates, with the following properties.  egin{enumerate}[label=	extup{(oman*)}] \item The central tangent maps \[ \partial_xH_L(0,0):K^a\longrightarrow K^N,\qquad \partial_yH_R(0):K^{N-a}\longrightarrow K^N \] are injective and have complementary images. \item The identities \[ S_t(H_L(x,t))=0,\qquad S_0(H_R(y))=0 \] hold in \(T[[x]]\) and \(K[[y]]\), respectively. \item For every three distinct \(i,j,k\in I\),  egin{align} t_i t_j t_k &\in igl((\partial_{h_

u\leq N igr)\subset T[[x]], \ (b_i b_j b_k)(H_R(y)) &\in igl((\partial_{h_

primaryStatements.name: The marked edge potential
primaryStatements.label: prop:edge-potential
primaryStatements.text: With the boundary polarization fixed above, there is a formal potential $f\in\mathbb C[[h_1,\ldots,h_N]]$, where $N=3(b_1(Y)-1)$, and a slice $s(h)$ such that: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item $f=\mathcal C(s)$ has order at least three. Its full Jacobian ideal equals the curvature ideal of $s$. The formal critical scheme $\Crit(f)=\Spf(S/\Jac(f))$ is the based flat-representation scheme with $G_\alpha=1$, and carries its marked based matrix $G_\beta$. \item For each fixed $T_0\in\g$ there is an affine slice with boundary $\tau T_0\zeta+v(h,\tau)\xi$ and adjusted potential \[ f_\tau=f+\tau b =\mathcal C(s(h,\tau)) +\tfrac{\epsilon}{2}\tr(\tau T_0v(h,\tau)), \qquad \tau^2=0. \] Its internal Jacobian ideal equals its full curvature ideal. Accordingly $\Crit_h(f_\tau)$ is the based flat-representation scheme with $G_\alpha=\exp(-\tau T_0)$. No derivative with respect to $\tau$ is imposed in this relative critical scheme. \item On the entire, possibly nonreduced, central critical scheme, \begin{equation} b=\epsilon\tr(T_0v(h,0)) =-\epsilon\tr\bigl(T_0\log G_\beta\bigr) \quad\bmod\Jac(f). \end{equation} The function $b$ has order at least two. Every flat connection with the indicated normalized boundary value is carried uniquely to the corresponding slice by gauge transformations equal to the identity on $T$. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.name: Algebraic edge potential with markings
primaryStatements.label: thm:edge-algebraicity
primaryStatements.text: Put \(N=\dim(H^1(C)\otimes\mathfrak{sl}_2)\), \(R=\mathbb C[[h_1,\ldots,h_N]]\), and \(J=\Jac(f)\). There are an invertible formal coordinate change \(x=\varphi(h)\) and an algebraic power series \(F(x)\in(x)^3\) such that \[ f(h)=F(\varphi(h)). \] Fix a torus basepoint and any finite collection of based loops in \(Y\). For every matrix entry of their holonomies on the central critical scheme \(\Spf(R/J)\), there is an algebraic power series in the \(x\)-coordinates whose pullback is that entry. In particular this holds for the based \(\beta\)-holonomy. The coordinate change can be chosen to identify these markings on the entire, possibly nonreduced, critical scheme.

primaryStatements.name: Formal trace comparison
primaryStatements.label: prop:formal-trace-comparison
primaryStatements.text: Let \(X\) be a finite triangulated space, and let \[ a_X\in \bigl(A_X\otimes\mathfrak g\widehat\otimes\mathfrak m_R\bigr)^1, \qquad (d_X+Q)a_X+\tfrac12[a_X,a_X]=0, \] represent a family of local systems formally near the trivial one. For its evaluation map \(\operatorname{ev}_{a_X}:X_B\times\Spf R\to BG\), the image of \(\operatorname{ev}_{a_X}^*\omega_\kappa\) under the Betti coefficient map of \cite[\S2.1]{PTVV2013} is the class of \begin{equation} \Theta_X=\tfrac12\kappa(\delta_Ra_X,\delta_Ra_X), \qquad (d_X+\mathcal L_Q)\Theta_X=0,\qquad \delta_R\Theta_X=0, \end{equation} in the full complex \(\operatorname{Cl}^2_R(A_X)\). This identification is natural for source restrictions, derived coefficient changes, and integration of source cochains. For an oriented compact three-manifold \(Z\) with boundary \(S\), it also identifies the relative-orientation isotropic homotopy with integration of \(\Theta_Z\) over \(Z\). If \(S=S^2\) and the sphere condition is represented by \(a_S=\nu b\), where \(\nu\) is a two-form and \(b\) has internal degree \(-1\), then \(\Theta_S=0\) strictly. Using the zero isotropic path on this sphere model, the resulting intersection form is represented by \[ \tfrac12\int_Z \kappa(\delta_Ra_Z,\delta_Ra_Z) \] as a closed two-form of degree \(-1\).

primaryStatements.name: Vertex data
primaryStatements.label: prop:vertex-data
primaryStatements.text: Suppose that the data of Proposition \ref{prop:geometric-reduction} exist, with $m\geq 5$, $p\geq9$ extra letters, and the finite family of independently conjugated boundary laws described there. Their Brunnian property means that omitting any slot makes the law the identity, as in Equation \eqref{eq:grope-word-properties}. There are a characteristic-zero field $K$, internal coordinate blocks $h_i$ for the $2m$ edges, and algebraic power-series germs $F_i(h_i)$ and $b_i(h_i)$, the latter for the $m$ active edges, with the following properties. Put \[ T=K[t_i:i\text{ active}]/(t_i^2:i\text{ active}),\qquad S_0=\sum_i F_i, \qquad S_t=S_0+\sum_{i\text{ active}}t_i b_i. \] There are formal parametrizations $H_L(x,t)$ over $T$ and $H_R(y)$ over $K$ whose central tangent maps are injective and have complementary images in the full internal coordinate space. They are smooth graph germs over $T$ and $K$, respectively, and \begin{equation} S_t(H_L)=0,\qquad S_0(H_R)=0. \end{equation} For every three distinct active indices $i,j,k$, \begin{align} t_i t_j t_k &\in\left((\partial_{h_a}S_t)(H_L):a=1,\ldots,N\right) \subset T[[x]], \\ (b_i b_j b_k)(H_R) &\in\left((\partial_{h_a}S_0)(H_R):a=1,\ldots,N\right) \subset K[[y]], \end{align} where $N$ is the total number of internal coordinates. The field can be taken to be $K=\mathbb C((\sigma))$. The individual functions can be normalized so that $F_i(0)=b_i(0)=0$.

primaryStatements.label: cor:vertex-tensor-interface
primaryStatements.text: The cut data of Proposition \ref{prop:geometric-reduction}, with $m\geq5$ and the indicated finite law list, supply all the hypotheses of Theorem \ref{thm:tensor-obstruction}.

definitions.name: Universal framed disk replacement
definitions.label: ass:disk
definitions.text: Let \(M\) be a compact connected oriented smooth four-manifold with boundary. Suppose that a finite collection of proper generic immersions \[ f_i\colon(D^2,S^1)\longrightarrow(M,\partial M),\qquad 1\leq i\leq k, \] has pairwise disjoint embedded boundary circles, and admits generically immersed framed spheres \(g_1,\ldots,g_k\) such that \[ \lambda(f_i,g_j)=\delta_{ij},\qquad \lambda(g_i,g_j)=0,\qquad \widetilde\mu(g_i)=0 \quad\text{for all }i,j. \] Here intersections are counted in \(\mathbb Z[\pi_1M]\), with fixed whiskers, the diagonal equations are included, and \[ \widetilde\mu(g_i)\in \mathbb Z[\pi_1M]\big/ \big\langle h-h^{-1},\,\mathbb Z\cdot1\big\rangle \] uses the additive quotient. Then the \(f_i\) can be replaced by pairwise disjoint locally flat embedded disks with the same boundary maps and the same induced normal framings on those boundary circles.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: There is a finitely presented group $G$ with a finite, oriented, four-dimensional aspherical Poincar\'e complex $Q$ such that \[ H^i(G;\Z G)=0\quad(i\ne4),\qquad H^4(G;\Z G)\cong\Z \] with trivial right $G$-action on the last group, but no closed aspherical topological four-manifold has fundamental group $G$. In particular the trivial left $\Z G$-module $\Z$ has a finite resolution by finitely generated free modules.

primaryStatements.name: Removal of the remaining planes
primaryStatements.label: ct:removal
primaryStatements.text: The compact manifold $Z$ admits interior surgeries producing a compact oriented topological four-manifold $V$ with boundary $S$, fundamental group $H$, and contractible universal cover. The boundary map to $BH$ is the original central marking.

primaryStatements.name: The marked chamber
primaryStatements.label: ch:chamber
primaryStatements.text: There are a compact connected oriented smooth four-manifold $D$, its connected boundary $S$, a finitely generated free group $H$, and a map $c:D\to BH$ with the following properties. \begin{enumerate} \item The map $c$ induces an isomorphism on fundamental groups, and $D$ has the homotopy type of a finite graph with $2k$ two-spheres attached at its basepoint. Its module $\pi_2D$ has a specified hyperbolic basis over $\Z H$, represented by framed immersed spheres with vanishing quadratic self-intersection obstructions. \item Attach a three-cell to each basis sphere, and denote the resulting space by $P$. Then $(P,S)$ is an oriented Poincar\'e pair of formal dimension four, and $P\simeq BH$. The boundary marking is $c|_S:S\to BH$. \item There is no compact oriented topological four-manifold $D'$ with boundary identified with $S$ and a homotopy equivalence $c':D'\to BH$ whose restriction to $S$ is homotopic to $c|_S$. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.label: ch:boundary-homology
primaryStatements.text: The map $\pi_1S\to H$ is onto. If $r=\operatorname{rank}H$, then $H_1(S;\Z)\to H_1(P;\Z)$ is an isomorphism and $H_2(S;\Z)\cong\Z^r$.

primaryStatements.name: The reflected pair
primaryStatements.label: rf:development
primaryStatements.text: The space $Q$ is a finite oriented Poincar\'e complex of dimension four. The natural map $f:N\to Q$ has degree one and induces an isomorphism on fundamental groups, identifying both with the group $G$ in \eqref{rf:group}. If $b$ is the total number of chamber hyperbolic planes in $N$, then \[ \pi_2(N)\cong(\Z G)^{2b} \] has the specified orthogonal hyperbolic basis, and $\widetilde H_i(\widetilde N;\Z)=0$ for $i\ne2$. The group $G$ is finitely presented, is torsion-free, and satisfies \begin{equation} H^i(G;\Z G)=0\quad(i\ne4),\qquad H^4(G;\Z G)\cong\Z \end{equation} with trivial right $G$-action.

primaryStatements.label: st:marked-equivalence
primaryStatements.text: There is an orientation-preserving homotopy equivalence \[ f\colon N\longrightarrow L \] inducing the specified isomorphism on $\pi_1$ and the prescribed isometry $A\to\pi_2(L)$.

primaryStatements.label: st:stable-product
primaryStatements.text: For some integer $k\ge0$ there is a homeomorphism \[ h\colon N\mathbin{\#}\,k(S^2\times S^2) \longrightarrow L\mathbin{\#}\,k(S^2\times S^2) \] which induces the prescribed original marking and matches every added standard pair with its specified added standard pair. In particular, on the left, all the prescribed original hyperbolic pairs and all new standard pairs have simultaneous geometric representatives with pairwise disjoint punctured $S^2\times S^2$ neighborhoods.

primaryStatements.label: st:periodic-data
primaryStatements.text: The manifold $Y$ has two $\Delta$-periodic systems of sphere pairs, with the same chamber labels: \begin{enumerate} \item framed immersed hyperbolic pairs in the interiors of the chambers $D_v$, including the added standard pairs, with their equivariant products already correct over the individual chamber group; \item geometrically standard pairs with pairwise disjoint punctured $S^2\times S^2$ neighborhoods, based-homotopic sphere by sphere to the correspondingly labelled pairs in the first system. \end{enumerate} There is an integer $d_0$ such that the drawing of each pair, its standard neighborhood, and the homotopies relating the two systems are contained in the chambers at gallery distance at most $d_0$ from that pair's label. Basings in this statement are local basings transported with the chamber; no bound is asserted for whiskers drawn from one global base point to all chambers.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth nontrivial knot. For any $r,s\in\Q\cup\{\infty\}$, an orientation-preserving homeomorphism \[ S^3_r(K)\cong S^3_s(K) \] implies $r=s$.

primaryStatements.name: Cosmetic surgery reduction
primaryStatements.label: prop:introduction:reduction
primaryStatements.text: If a smooth nontrivial knot $K\subset S^3$ has distinct purely cosmetic slopes, then $g(K)=2$ and the two slopes are $-2$ and $2$.

primaryStatements.name: Ordinary handle units
primaryStatements.label: thm:ordinary:units
primaryStatements.text: Let $C(Y_j;\Z)$ be the irreducible, unframed instanton complex with the determinants just specified. Compatible small perturbations and coherent orientations can be chosen so that the rigid counts define integral chain maps, and the rigid and interval counts have the following properties over $\F_2$. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item Each rigid meridional handle map $Y_r\longrightarrow Y_{r+1}$, for $r=0,1$, is a unit whenever its determinant has the specified end restrictions. The rigid count on their composite is their composition up to chain homotopy. Denote this composite by $f_+:C(Y_0)\longrightarrow C(Y_2)$. \item On the path $2\longrightarrow\infty\longrightarrow0$, let $F_l,A$ be the capped Seifert classes of squares $-2,0$, respectively, with $F_l\cdot A=0$, and let $S_l=A-F_l$. Choose the base determinant $c(F_l,A)=(0,1)$ and the two determinants $c+e\PD(S_l)$, $e=0,1$, identified off $S_l$. The sum modulo two of the interval counts of actual index $-1$ is a unit $g_+:C(Y_2;\F_2)\longrightarrow C(Y_0;\F_2)$. \item The mirror construction, read backwards, gives units $f_-:C(Y_{-2})\longrightarrow C(Y_0)$ on the rigid path through $-1$, and $g_-:C(Y_0;\F_2)\longrightarrow C(Y_{-2};\F_2)$ on $0\longrightarrow\infty\longrightarrow-2$. For $g_-$ the base evaluations are $(1,0)$ and the second determinant differs by the Poincar\'e dual of the intervening $(-2)$-sphere. \end{enumerate} For the summed interval maps, each summand has an integral orientation; the assertion that the sum is a chain map and a unit is required only after reduction modulo two. End identifications, including any tensor automorphisms, are fixed before composing the maps.

primaryStatements.name: The ordinary bridge
primaryStatements.label: cor:ordinary:bridge
primaryStatements.text: Fix an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism $\phi:Y_{-2}\longrightarrow Y_2$, with fixed bundle and collar identifications. The stacked cobordism and its rigid count \begin{equation} T=f_-\,\phi^{-1}\,f_+:Y_0\longrightarrow Y_0 \end{equation} define an integral chain map inducing a unit over $\F_2$ and an isomorphism over $\Q$. The cobordism has \begin{equation} H_1(T;\Z)=0,\qquad \chi(T)=4,\qquad \sigma(T)=-2. \end{equation} Its two increasing-handle halves are simply connected.

primaryStatements.name: Negative interval unit
primaryStatements.label: thm:negative:unit
primaryStatements.text: The counts defining $B$ can be chosen coherently so that \[ B\colon C(Y_2;\Z)\longrightarrow C(Y_{-2};\Z) \] is an integral chain map. Its reduction modulo two induces an isomorphism on Floer homology. Its integral chain-homotopy class is unchanged by compatible changes of the interval data and sphere sweep. The relative sign of the two determinant lifts is local at $N'$, is independent of the exterior solution, and is preserved under composition with other cobordisms.

primaryStatements.name: Local relative signs
primaryStatements.label: prop:negative:local-sign
primaryStatements.text: There is a relative orientation convention for the two lifts in \eqref{eq:negative:lifts} under which their minimal lens ends cancel over $\Z$. The comparison uses identical exterior data, including relative bundle degree, and is independent of the exterior field. It commutes with gluing on other seams and is multiplicative for disjoint sphere caps. Adding a coupled complex Dirac determinant preserves this convention.

primaryStatements.name: Chain property and invariance
primaryStatements.label: prop:negative:invariance
primaryStatements.text: With the signs of Proposition \ref{prop:negative:local-sign}, $B$ is an integral chain map. Compatible homotopies of equation data and incidence representatives give integral chain homotopies. The allowed representative homotopies include smooth conjugation-equivariant homotopies of the normalized based holonomy paths, relative to their collapsed endpoints, under the following requirements. Their exact compact supports remain in the specified parts, they persist under ideal convergence away from a support hit, and the equation data do not depend on the incidence mark. At the lens endpoint the test is supported in $N'$, its two lifts are tensor-paired with the same exterior, and its flat-cap and collapsed-endpoint avoidance holds throughout. The data admit regularization preserving these requirements. The homotopy of the incidence representative need not be small. Near the primary $J$ endpoint the unconstrained equation exclusion requires no additional behavior of the representative.

primaryStatements.name: Fixed caps with a nonzero pairing
primaryStatements.label: thm:caps:pairing
primaryStatements.text: There are two fixed compact caps $C_-$ and $C_+$ with common rational boundary $Y_2$, fixed determinant data trivialized at that boundary, and finite collections of integral point and surface probes in their interiors with the following properties. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item Each cap has $H_1(C_\pm;\Z)=0$ and $b^+(C_\pm)>0$. Each contains a square-zero copy of $A$ on which the determinant class evaluates as $1$, and a tight genus-two surface of square two. \item Each cap has one additional, separate exceptional summand. The determinant evaluates as zero on its exceptional sphere, and every probe is supported in the old part of the cap. \item For suitable generic cap data and small ordinary Floer data at the rational boundary, the cut counts give a rational cycle $x$ and a rational cocycle $y$ on the irreducible determinant-one Floer complex, with \begin{equation} yx\ne0. \end{equation} Fixed integral multiples of these are an integral cycle and cocycle. \item The total real degree $z$ of all cap probes is fixed. Reducible cap limits in any of the bounded charge ranges used below are excluded by the cap period choices. The period choices admit the finite isolation extensions of Proposition \ref{prop:estimates:cap}. \end{enumerate} The cycle and cocycle can be recomputed with the final cap data used in Section \ref{sec:stack}; their pairing is the same nonzero closed Donaldson count, up to the fixed normalization and orientation sign.

definitions.label: def:indices:types
definitions.text: The phase circle $\mathbb T$ acts by multiplying $\Phi$. On the quotient by determinant-one gauge, its kernel at a free orbit is $\{1,-1\}$. A main component has type $A$ when $\Phi=0$ and the connection is irreducible, type $R$ when $\Phi=0$ and the connection has continuous stabilizer, type $S$ when $\Phi\ne0$ lies in one summand of a parallel splitting, and type $P$ otherwise. A fixed-type tuple has no component of type $P$. The letters here denote field types; in particular $A$ is not the capped Seifert surface, and $P$ is not the positive bridge cell. For a split connection write $E=L_1\oplus L_2$ and $v=c_1(L_1)-c_1(L_2)$, placing the active spinor line first in type $S$. Then \begin{equation} v\equiv c\pmod2,\qquad K=l+2c_1(L_1)=\Lambda+v. \end{equation} At type $R$ choose either ordering, including an ordering at a central connection. Actual separated lens caps are not counted as main components when assigning these types.

definitions.label: def:indices:analytic-hypotheses
definitions.text: Call a choice of equations and representatives admissible for the exclusion calculation if it has the following properties, for all ideal main-part tuples in the fixed total charge budget, including the enlarged candidate class described in Section \ref{subsec:analysis:candidates}. In this class the completed main fields satisfy their equations and retained nonphase cuts, together with the phase cuts when imposed. Matching across true cuts and the actual lens-cap and connector fields are omitted. The assigned lens-cap and connector charges obey their permitted nonnegative ranges and the total charge constraint; the omitted fields need not be realizable. \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)] \item On a fixed-type tuple, the restricted ASD equations with retained nonphase cuts on type $A$ components, and the pure tangential equations on type $S$ components, are transverse. In particular a type $A$ component has $q_i\ge0$, with strict inequality if it has any lens end, main particle, or allocated nonconstant $J$-trajectory loss. A type $S$ component satisfies \begin{equation} d_s+p_i+4\ell_i\ge0. \end{equation} These are componentwise assertions using only parameters retained on the component. \item For types $R,S$, an assigned whole sphere test with $v(S_j)=0$ requires a unit of $\ell_i$. This includes a separated lens test. During switching to the $J$ prescription the unit is required if both half values vanish; at a true $J$ the assigned test requires the unit if its own half value vanishes. Different sphere tests so charged on the same component require distinct units. Type $S$ is needed in this assertion only for a tuple with no $P$. \item For a tuple containing $P$, project away all type $R$ fields, positions, and tests, retaining their parameters. The equations and retained cuts on the other components are independent of the discarded data. Before diagonal phase quotient and phase cuts, the necessary projected problem has dimension at most \begin{equation} \sum_{i\notin R} \left(i_i-\sum_{\text{lens ends of }i}(\delta_{\rm sp}-1)-2w_i\right) +\sum_{i\in R}p_i, \end{equation} where $w_i$ is the total main-particle weight and other allocated integer loss outside lens caps on that component. The $\eta$ phase sections subtract $2\eta$, and the phase quotient subtracts one. Regularity is required only near the projections of candidate tuples in the stated overcount, with all $R$ fields still present before projection. At those candidate projections, a negative dimension excludes a zero. No assertion is made about other zeros of the enlarged equations after the $R$ fields are discarded. This permits finite rational multisections on free strata without changing the integral instanton maps at zero spinor. \end{enumerate}

papers.abstract: We construct a uniformly discrete bounded-geometry space whose maximal coarse assembly map has an infinite-order element in its kernel. primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: There exist finite connected graphs $(X_j)_{j\geq1}$ with a common finite bound on vertex degree, a coarse disjoint union $X=\bigsqcup_{j\geq1}X_j$, and an infinite-order class $\alpha\in\KX_1(X)$ such that \[ \mu_X^{\max}(\alpha)=0. \] Consequently, $\mu_X^{\max}\otimes\Q$ is not injective.

primaryStatements.label: top:infinite-order
primaryStatements.text: The class $\alpha\in\KX_1(X)$ defined in \eqref{top:alpha} has infinite order. In particular, $\alpha\otimes1\neq0$ in $\KX_1(X)\otimes\mathbb Q$.

primaryStatements.name: Coarse functoriality
primaryStatements.label: ana:functoriality
primaryStatements.text: Conjugation by an exact covering isometry defines a $*$-homomorphism \[ h_A=\Ad(V_h):A_Z\longrightarrow A_W. \] Its induced map on $K$-theory is independent of the covering isometry. These induced maps respect composition, and an exact covering isometry over $\id_Z$ induces the identity on $K_*(A_Z)$.

primaryStatements.name: Naturality for the end classes
primaryStatements.label: ana:naturality
primaryStatements.text: For the classes $\beta\in\KX_1(B)$ and $\alpha=(i_+)_*\beta-(i_-)_*\beta\in\KX_1(X)$ constructed above, \begin{equation} \mu_X^{\max}(\alpha) =(i_{+,A})_*\mu_B^{\max}(\beta) -(i_{-,A})_*\mu_B^{\max}(\beta). \end{equation}

primaryStatements.label: ana:transfer
primaryStatements.text: For the projection $f:Y\to B$ there is a $*$-homomorphism \[ \Phi:A_B\longrightarrow A_Y \] such that $(f_A\Phi)_*=\id$ on $K_*(A_B)$. In particular, \[ (f_A)_*:K_1(A_Y)\longrightarrow K_1(A_B) \] is surjective.

primaryStatements.label: ana:endpoints
primaryStatements.text: The endpoint maps induce the same homomorphism \[ (i_{+,A}f_A)_*=(i_{-,A}f_A)_*: K_1(A_Y)\longrightarrow K_1(A_X). \]

papers.title: A counterexample to the coarse Novikov conjecture
papers.abstract: We disprove the coarse Novikov conjecture: ordinary coarse assembly need not be rationally injective for uniformly discrete spaces of bounded geometry. We construct a coarse disjoint union of finite graphs of uniformly bounded degree and an infinite-order class in its degree-one coarse K-homology whose image under ordinary coarse assembly in the K-theory of the reduced, locally compact Roe algebra vanishes.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: There is a uniformly discrete bounded-geometry metric space $X$, which is a coarse disjoint union of finite connected graphs of uniformly bounded degree, and an infinite-order element $\alpha\in KX_1(X)$ such that \[ \mu_X(\alpha)=0\quad\text{in }K_1(C^*(X)). \] Consequently, ordinary coarse assembly for $X$ fails to be injective both integrally and after tensoring its domain and target with $\Q$.

primaryStatements.label: prop:persistence
primaryStatements.text: For every integer $r\ge1$ there is a homomorphism \[ \lambda_r:K_1^{\lf}(P_r(X))\longrightarrow\Z \quad\text{such that}\quad \lambda_r(\alpha_r)=1. \] Consequently, every nonzero integer multiple of $\alpha$ is nonzero in $KX_1(X)$.

primaryStatements.name: Transfer through finite fibers
primaryStatements.label: prop:transfer
primaryStatements.text: Let $D$ and $X$ be countable uniformly discrete bounded-geometry spaces. Suppose $X=\coprod_{u\in D}F_u$ is a partition into nonempty finite sets. Write $\xi_u=\abs{F_u}^{-1/2}\sum_{x\in F_u}\delta_x$ and let $P$ be the orthogonal projection on $\ell^2(X)$ onto the span of the $\xi_u$. Assume: \begin{enumerate} \item $P$ is an operator-norm limit of finite-propagation contractions $P_n$ on $\ell^2(X)$; \item for every $R<\infty$ there is $s_R<\infty$ such that, whenever $d_D(u,v)\le R$, there is a contraction $O_{uv}:\ell^2(F_v)\to\ell^2(F_u)$ of propagation at most $s_R$ with $O_{uv}\xi_v=\xi_u$. \end{enumerate} For the isometry \[ V:\ell^2(D)\otimes\HH_0\longrightarrow\ell^2(X)\otimes\HH_0, \qquad V(\delta_u\otimes h)=\xi_u\otimes h, \] conjugation defines a $*$-homomorphism $\Ad V:C^*(D)\to C^*(X)$ between the reduced, locally compact Roe algebras.

lean.scopeText: The coarse Novikov conjecture predicts rational injectivity of the ordinary coarse assembly map for uniformly discrete spaces of bounded geometry. The formalization constructs a counterexample from a coarse disjoint union of finite connected graphs with uniformly bounded degree. Its degree-one coarse $K$-homology contains an infinite-order class whose image under ordinary coarse assembly into the reduced locally compact Roe algebra vanishes. The class remains nonzero after tensoring with $\mathbb Q$, so rational injectivity fails.

papers.title: Finite Smith–Toda Complexes at Varying Primes
papers.abstract: For every nonnegative integer n, we construct a Smith–Toda complex $V(n)$ at some prime p depending on n. It is a finite p-local spectrum whose Brown–Peterson homology is $\mathrm{BP}_*/(p,v_1,\ldots,v_n)$ with its canonical comodule structure and generator in degree zero. Each listed generator is killed to its first power.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: For every integer $n\geq0$, there exist a prime $p$ and a finite $p$-local spectrum $X$ such that \[ \BP_*X\cong\BP_*/(p,v_1,\ldots,v_n) \] as graded $\BP_*\BP$-comodules, with the canonical quotient coaction and generator in degree zero.

primaryStatements.label: found:ultraproduct
primaryStatements.text: The category $\cC$ is stable and symmetric monoidal, with finite stable constructions and tensor products computed primewise. If $X=[(X_p)]$ and $Y=[(Y_p)]$, then \begin{equation} \map_{\cC}(X,Y) \simeq\colim_{U\in\U}\prod_{p\in U} \map_{\Sp_{(p)}}(X_p,Y_p). \end{equation} Every mapping spectrum is rational, and the endomorphism algebra of the tensor unit is $HD$. The ring $D$ contains $\Q$, and $\varpi$ is a nonzerodivisor. Objects, arrows, and homotopies forming a diagram indexed by a finite simplicial set can be represented simultaneously on a large set of primes. The same holds for specified finite cofiber diagrams. Sequence objects become compact in $\Ind(\cC)$.

primaryStatements.label: found:finite-cell-morita
primaryStatements.text: The functor $h_\Omega$ induces a symmetric monoidal equivalence between $\cC_{\mathrm{cell}}$ and the category of finite-cell graded $A$-modules. For $X,Y\in\cC$, the natural comparison \begin{equation} h_\Omega(X)\otimes_A h_\Omega(Y) \longrightarrow h_\Omega(X\otimes Y) \end{equation} is an equivalence whenever either input is in $\cC_{\mathrm{cell}}$. These comparisons preserve units, compositions, and symmetric multi-input products. In particular, a commutative $A$-algebra whose underlying module is finite-cell determines a commutative algebra in $\cC$.

primaryStatements.label: found:koszul-realization
primaryStatements.text: Fix $0\leq r\leq n$. Suppose cycles $b_h$ of chain degree zero and weight $w_h$, for $0\leq h\leq r$, have been chosen successively in the strict algebras \begin{equation} \begin{gathered} A[e_0,\ldots,e_{j-1}],\qquad |e_h|_{\mathrm{chain}}=1,\quad \wt(e_h)=w_h,\\ \partial e_h=b_h\in A[e_0,\ldots,e_{h-1}], \qquad b_0=\varpi u_0. \end{gathered} \end{equation} For $0\leq j\leq r+1$, these algebras determine commutative algebras $Y_j\in\cC$, with $Y_0=\one$. For $0\leq j\leq r$, the cycle $b_j$ represents a map $S(w_j)\to Y_j$, and there is a cofiber sequence \begin{equation} S(w_j)\otimes Y_j\xrightarrow{\,b_j\cdot-\,}Y_j \longrightarrow Y_{j+1}, \end{equation} whose second map is the algebra map adjoining the null $e_j$. For $M=[(\MU_{(p)})_p]$ and $0\leq j\leq r+1$, there are compatible equivalences \begin{equation} h_\Omega(M\otimes Y_j) \simeq h_\Omega(M)\otimes_A A[e_0,\ldots,e_{j-1}]. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: The unnormalized power
primaryStatements.label: power:operation
primaryStatements.text: For a sequence of actual primewise $\Lambda$-graded commutative algebras, there is a natural map of graded commutative algebras over rational spectra \begin{equation} P_X:h_\Lambda(X)\longrightarrow B(X)[t^{-1}]_{*,0,0}. \end{equation} On a represented degree-zero class, its value is obtained by taking the permuted $p$-fold smash and then multiplying the $p$ factors. In particular, that value has this represented class in $B(X)$ before Euler inversion. No $D$-linearity is asserted for $P_X$.

primaryStatements.name: The multiplicative Euler layer
primaryStatements.label: layer:comparison
primaryStatements.text: For every sequence of graded commutative algebras $X$, there are natural product-compatible equivalences \begin{equation} B(X)//t\xrightarrow{\simeq}\Phi(X) \xleftarrow{\simeq}Q(X)\otimes_D(D//\varpi). \end{equation} The right-hand comparison applies to arbitrary spectrum inputs as well. The scalar action in the $\delta$ direction agrees with ordinary evaluation on $Q(X)$ followed by reduction. The comparisons are compatible with algebra units and maps of inputs. The first map uses the tautological Euler null on $S(2V)$, restricted to $S(V)$.

primaryStatements.name: The first Koszul layer
primaryStatements.label: layer:first-koszul
primaryStatements.text: For constant input $\one$, the comparison identifies \[ B(\one)//t\simeq F^*h_\Omega(Y_1) \] as graded algebras. For $M=(\MU_{(p)})_p$ there is a compatible identification \[ B(M)//t\simeq F^*h_\Omega(M\otimes Y_1). \] These identifications preserve the algebra maps induced by the unit and the scalar action in the $\delta$ direction.

primaryStatements.label: universal:primewise-models
primaryStatements.text: For the chosen cycles through $b_a$, there exist the following data as germs along $\U$: \begin{enumerate} \item Filtered $\Lambda$-graded commutative ring spectra $R_p^a$, with an equivalence $R^a\simeq h_\Lambda(R_p^a)$ at every filtration order, compatible with the filtered algebra structures. \item Maps of whole unfiltered graded commutative algebras $R_p^a\to S_{(p)}$, where the sphere is constant in the weight grading, together with a homotopy identifying their normalized evaluation with Equation \eqref{universal:evaluation}. \item Filtered finite-cell $R_p^a$-modules $K_p^a$, with an equivalence $K^a\simeq h_\Lambda(K_p^a)$ of filtered modules. \end{enumerate} The algebra models, their comparisons, and the evaluation homotopies may be chosen relative to the preceding stage. Thus the maps $R^{a-1}\to R^a$ and $R_p^{a-1}\to R_p^a$ and their evaluations form compatible diagrams of algebras. No algebra structure is required on $K_p^a$.

definitions.label: universal:coefficients
definitions.text: The graded algebra underlying $R^a$ is the free graded-commutative $D$-algebra on variables \[ z_{j,S},\qquad 0\leq j\leq a,\quad S\subseteq[j), \qquad |z_{j,S}|_{\mathrm{chain}}=-|S|, \qquad \wt(z_{j,S})=\gamma_{j,S} :=w_j-\sum_{h\in S}w_h. \] Set \[ b_j^u=\sum_{S\subseteq[j)}z_{j,S}e_S, \qquad \partial e_j=b_j^u. \] The differential on $R^a$ is determined by $\partial b_j^u=0$, with coefficients compared in the exterior basis. Define \[ K_-^a=R^a[e_j:j<a],\qquad K^a=R^a[e_j:j\leq a]. \] The superscript $u$ indicates these universal cycles.

primaryStatements.label: intro:main
primaryStatements.text: At $p=1009$ there is a finite $p$-local spectrum $X$ and an isomorphism \[ BP_*X\ \cong\ BP_*/(p,v_1,v_2,v_3,v_4) \] of graded $BP_*BP$-comodules, with the canonical quotient comodule on the right and its generator in degree zero.

primaryStatements.name: All later obstruction candidates
primaryStatements.label: may:remaining-list
primaryStatements.text: For $k\geq2$ the complete initial May page in \eqref{may:obstruction-degrees} is Table \ref{may:remaining-table}; all other values of $k$ give an empty page. Put $N_0=(p-1)^2$ and $N=p(p-1)-2$. \begin{table}[htbp] \centering \begin{tabular}{c l} \toprule $k$ & Initial May monomials\\ \midrule $2$ & $xac B A^{p-2}C^{p-2}$, $\quad xacyz A^{p-2}C^{p-2}$\\[2pt] $p-1$ & $y B^3 A^{N_0-3}$, $\quad b B^2 A^{N_0-2}$, $\quad ybz B A^{N_0-2}$\\[2pt] $p$ & $cyb A^{N+1}$, $\quad ayb B A^N$\\ \bottomrule \end{tabular} \caption{Every initial May monomial for the later $v_4$ obstruction bidegrees.} \end{table}

primaryStatements.name: The bounded-below Adams--Novikov resolution
primaryStatements.label: fw:anss
primaryStatements.text: For every bounded-below $p$-local spectrum $Z$, the sphere-source Adams--Novikov spectral sequence has \[ E_2^{s,t}(Z)=H^{s,t}\bigl(C^\bullet_\Gamma(BP_*Z)\bigr) \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \pi_{t-s}Z. \] It converges strongly, and the induced filtration in each stem is finite. The differential $d_r$ changes $(s,t)$ by $(r,r-1)$. The filtration-zero edge identifies $E_\infty^{0,*}$ with the image of the $BP$-Hurewicz map $\pi_*Z\longrightarrow BP_*Z$.

primaryStatements.name: Binary pairings of the resolution
primaryStatements.label: fw:anss-pairing
primaryStatements.text: For bounded-below $p$-local spectra $Z_1,Z_2,Z_3$, an actual map $f:Z_1\wedge Z_2\to Z_3$ induces pairings of the Adams--Novikov spectral sequences, with the Leibniz rule on every page. The $E_2$ pairing is the cobar cup pairing induced by the exterior $BP$-homology pairing, and the $E_\infty$ pairing is the associated-graded pairing of the actual homotopy map $f$. No associativity of $f$ is needed. If $Z_1=Z_2=Z_3=Z$ has a binary two-sided unital multiplication and $BP_*Z=R/I$ is cyclic on its unit, the $E_2$ pairing is the ordinary multiplication on cobar cohomology with quotient-ring coefficients.

primaryStatements.name: Sparsity
primaryStatements.label: fw:sparsity
primaryStatements.text: If $BP_*Z$ is concentrated in internal degrees divisible by $q$, then all pages of its Adams--Novikov spectral sequence have that same internal sparsity. Every possibly nonzero positive differential has length $r=qk+1$ for an integer $k\geq1$. In weight notation it changes $(s,w)$ to $(s+qk+1,w+k)$. In particular, a primitive coefficient of weight $u_n$ in filtration zero can have only targets \begin{equation} (s,w)=(qk+1,u_n+k),\qquad k\geq1. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Construction through $V(3)$
primaryStatements.label: low:V3
primaryStatements.text: For $0\leq n\leq3$ there is a finite $p$-local cell spectrum $V(n)$ with a bottom-cell unit $\eta_n:S_{(p)}\to V(n)$ and a binary multiplication \[ \mu_n:V(n)\wedge V(n)\longrightarrow V(n) \] whose two unit identities hold. Its cells are indexed by subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n\}$, in dimensions \begin{equation} \sum_{i\in S}(qu_i+1), \end{equation} and its $BP$-homology is the canonical quotient comodule $R/I_{n+1}$, generated in degree zero by the bottom unit. In particular, we may fix \begin{equation} Y=V(3),\qquad BP_*Y=R/I_4, \end{equation} with such a binary two-sided unital multiplication.

primaryStatements.name: The action of $p$ on $Y$
primaryStatements.label: low:p-null
primaryStatements.text: For the spectrum $Y$ of Proposition \ref{low:V3}, $\pi_0Y=\mathbb F_p$ and $p\operatorname{id}_Y$ is nullhomotopic.

primaryStatements.name: An injective multiplication
primaryStatements.label: may:injectivity
primaryStatements.text: Multiplication by the primitive class $h_{1,4}$ is injective on actual cobar cohomology in bidegree $(q+1,u_4+1)$: \[ H^{q+1,u_4+1}(P)\xrightarrow{\ h_{1,4}\ } H^{q+2,u_5+1}(P). \]

papers.title: The Kervaire invariant problem at the prime three
papers.abstract: We solve the Kervaire invariant problem at the prime three for the standard Kervaire classes in the mod-three Adams spectral sequence. These classes survive precisely at indices 0, 2, and 3, and each surviving detection coset contains an element of additive order three. In particular, there is an order-three Kervaire element in stem 322.

primaryStatements.label: thm:classification
primaryStatements.text: At the prime three, \[ K=K_3=\{0,2,3\}. \] Thus the surviving classes occur in stems $10$, $106$, and $322$, and each admits an additive-order-three representative. The class $b_1$ and every $b_j$ with $j\geq4$ fail to survive.

primaryStatements.label: intro:unstable-consequences
primaryStatements.text: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item There are homotopy equivalences of H-spaces \[ \Omega S^{163}\{3\}\simeq T^{163}(3)\times\Omega T^{487}(3), \qquad BW_{81}\simeq\Omega T^{487}(3). \] Consequently, $W_{81}\simeq\Omega^2T^{487}(3)$. \item For every integer $n>1$, the underlying space $\Omega S^{2n+1}\{3\}$ has a nontrivial product decomposition if and only if $n\in\{3,27,81\}$. For every other $n>1$ it is mod-three atomic, hence indecomposable. Here a product is nontrivial when both factors are noncontractible. \item For every integer $n>1$, the homotopy type $T^{2n+1}(3)$ admits a homotopy-associative H-space multiplication if and only if $n\in\{3,27,81\}$. The multiplication on $T^{163}(3)$ supplied by the displayed product is homotopy associative and homotopy commutative. For this multiplication, the third-power map on $T^{163}(3)$ is null-homotopic, as is the third-power map on the loop H-space $\Omega T^{487}(3)$. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.name: Detection of actual sphere classes
primaryStatements.label: det:actual-detector
primaryStatements.text: Let \(j\geq2\), and let \(\alpha\in\pi_{4\cdot3^{j+1}-2}S_{(3)}\) be detected by \(b_j\) in the mod-\(3\) Adams spectral sequence. Its image under the unit \[ \pi_{4\cdot3^{j+1}-2}S_{(3)} \longrightarrow \pi_{4\cdot3^{j+1}-2}(E^{hG}) \] is nonzero and has finite additive order. Its filtration-two symbol is the nonzero image of the Adams--Novikov representative in Lemma \ref{det:filtration-comparison}.

primaryStatements.label: det:full-gap
primaryStatements.text: For every \(n\in\Z\), the group \(\pi_{-2n}(E^{hG})\) contains an element of infinite additive order. In particular, \(\pi_{-2}(E^{hG})\ne0\).

primaryStatements.name: The torsion-free repair
primaryStatements.label: det:conditional-repair
primaryStatements.text: Suppose that the graded groups \(\pi_*(E^{hG})\) are \(972\)-periodic and that \(\pi_{-2}(E^{hG})\) is torsion-free. Then \(b_j\) does not survive for any \(j\geq4\).

primaryStatements.name: Finite Euler bound
primaryStatements.label: det:euler-bound
primaryStatements.text: In the cofree genuine spectra associated to \(E\), the actual faithful Euler classes satisfy \[ a_{\lambda|H}^{79}=0,\qquad a_\lambda^{235}=0. \] Consequently, the \(H\)-Tate pages kill the unit by a differential of length at most \(157\), and the \(G\)-Tate pages kill it by a differential of length at most \(469\).

primaryStatements.name: Integral obstruction calculation
primaryStatements.label: coef:integral-lift
primaryStatements.text: After compatible nonzero scalar normalizations, the auxiliary coefficient spectral sequence has \[ d_1(u)=uz_0,\qquad d_1(e)=ez_0,\qquad d_1(z_i)=z_i z_0\ (i=1,2),\qquad d_1(z_0)=0. \] Consequently \begin{equation} \mathcal E_2 =k[b^{\pm1},u^{\pm3},N_0,N_1,N_2] \otimes\Lambda(eu,z_1u,z_2u,z_0). \end{equation} Its only nonzero differential on these generators is \[ d_2(z_0)=c\,bN_0,\qquad c\in k^\times. \] There are no further differentials. In particular the leading cohomology class \(eu\) is represented by an actual element \(x_0\in E_{-2}\) satisfying \[ x_0/u\equiv1\pmod{\m},\qquad \Tr_H(x_0)=0. \] The element \(x_0\) may be chosen of \(T\)-weight one.

primaryStatements.name: The exact cyclic coefficient model
primaryStatements.label: coef:model
primaryStatements.text: Set \(x_i=g^i x_0\), with indices read modulo nine. Then \begin{equation} \left( \frac{W(k)[x_0,\ldots,x_8,(x_0\cdots x_8)^{-1}]} {(x_i+x_{i+3}+x_{i+6}:0\le i<3)} \right)^{\wedge}_{(3,x_i/x_0-1)} \xrightarrow{\ \cong\ } E_* \end{equation} is an isomorphism of \(W(k)\)-linear graded \(G\)-rings, with \(|x_i|=-2\) and \(g(x_i)=x_{i+1}\).

papers.title: Rational homology and Quillen's conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove Quillen's conjecture for all finite groups and all primes. More precisely, if a finite group G has trivial largest normal p-subgroup $O_p(G)$, then the poset of nontrivial elementary abelian p-subgroups of G has nonzero augmented reduced rational homology. This establishes the stronger rational-homology form of the conjecture.
papers.familySummary: Proves the rational-homology form of Quillen's conjecture for every finite group and every prime. If the largest normal p-subgroup of G is trivial, the poset of nontrivial elementary abelian p-subgroups has nonzero augmented reduced rational homology and is therefore not contractible.
