papers.title: Positive scalar curvature forces rational inessentiality
papers.abstract: We prove that every closed connected oriented smooth manifold admitting strictly positive scalar curvature is rationally inessential: its rational fundamental class maps to zero under the classifying map. No spin or fundamental-group hypothesis is needed, and there is no upper dimension bound. This proves the Gromov–Lawson aspherical conjecture; moreover, every nonnegative-scalar-curvature metric on a closed aspherical manifold is flat. We also show that every closed oriented smooth manifold of positive dimension with nonnegative scalar curvature has zero real simplicial volume, proving the qualitative vanishing consequence of Gromov's conjectural comparison.

Here $\mathrm{Scal}_g^-=\max\{0,-\mathrm{Scal}_g\}$ and $\lVert M\rVert$ is real simplicial volume. Also proves rational inessentiality under positive scalar curvature, resolving the Gromov–Lawson conjecture; every nonnegative-scalar-curvature metric on a closed aspherical manifold is flat.

primaryStatements.name: Rational inessentiality
primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let $M^n$ be a closed connected oriented smooth manifold of dimension $n\ge2$. If $M$ admits a Riemannian metric of strictly positive scalar curvature, then \[ (c_M)_*[M]=0\qquad\text{in }H_n(B\pi_1(M);\Q). \]

primaryStatements.name: The Gromov--Lawson aspherical conjecture
primaryStatements.label: cor:aspherical
primaryStatements.text: No closed smooth aspherical manifold, whether orientable or not, admits a Riemannian metric of strictly positive scalar curvature.

primaryStatements.name: Aspherical nonnegative-scalar-curvature rigidity
primaryStatements.label: cor:aspherical-flat
primaryStatements.text: Let $g$ be a Riemannian metric of nonnegative scalar curvature on a closed smooth aspherical manifold $M$, not necessarily oriented. Then $g$ is flat.

primaryStatements.name: Oriented target-map obstruction
primaryStatements.label: cor:degree-aspherical
primaryStatements.text: Let $M^n$ and $N^n$ be closed connected oriented smooth manifolds of dimension $n\ge2$, with $N$ aspherical. If a continuous map $f:M\to N$ has nonzero ordinary oriented degree $d\in\Z\setminus\{0\}$, then $M$ admits no Riemannian metric whose scalar curvature is strictly positive everywhere. In particular, if $P^n$ is any closed connected oriented smooth manifold, the oriented connected sum $N\#P$ admits no such metric.

primaryStatements.name: Simplicial-volume vanishing
primaryStatements.label: cor:simplicial
primaryStatements.text: Every closed oriented smooth manifold of positive dimension admitting a Riemannian metric of nonnegative scalar curvature has zero real simplicial volume.

Let $(M^n,g_M)$ be a closed connected oriented Riemannian manifold, $n\ge2$, let $\Gamma=\pi_1(M)$, and suppose that its classifying map $c_M:M	o B\Gamma$ satisfies \[ (c_M)_*[M]

The diagonal cover \[ Z=(\widetilde M	imes\widehat A)/\Gamma\longrightarrow M	imes A \] is oriented and has dimension $q$. There are a smooth compactly supported map $G:Z	o\R^q$ and a relatively compact open set $\Omega\subset Z$ such that  egin{equation} \deg(G,\Omega,0)
e0, \qquad 
orm{G}_\infty>3\quad	ext{on }\partial\Omega, \end{equation} and  egin{equation} \max_{1\le i\le q}\sup_Z\abs{d_{\widetilde M}G_i}_{g_M} \le rac JR, \qquad \log q\le JR. \end{equation} Write $\pi_Z:Z	o M	imes A$ for the covering projection. Its differential gives a global splitting \[ TZ=E_M\oplus E_A,\qquad E_M=(d\pi_Z)^{-1}(TM\oplus0),\qquad E_A=(d\pi_Z)^{-1}(0\oplus TA). \] The bundle $E_M$ is tangent to the $\widetilde M$ fibres of $Z	o A$, and $E_A$ is the flat lift of the parameter directions. primaryStatements.name: Compact diagonal pairing
primaryStatements.label: prop:compact-pairing
primaryStatements.text: There are a compact set $K_*\subset D_L$ and a class \[ u\in H^{n+d}(D_L,D_L\setminus K_*;\Q) \] such that \begin{enumerate} \item if $[t,o]\in K_*$, every label of $t$ is within $7L$ of every label of $r(o)$; \item the compactly supported evaluation \begin{equation} \ip{\Phi_h^*u,[X]_{\mathrm{lf}}}\ne0 \end{equation} is nonzero. \end{enumerate} Here $[X]_{\mathrm{lf}}$ is the locally finite fundamental class.

primaryStatements.name: Exact scalar-curvature identity
primaryStatements.label: prop:scalar-update
primaryStatements.text: At a point where $t>0$, choose a $g$-orthonormal frame $e_1=\nabla f/t,e_2,\ldots,e_{\dim B}$, and put \[ \mathfrak p=\frac{tN'(t)}{N(t)},\qquad A=d\log t,\qquad C_{jk}=t^{-1}\Hess_g f(e_j,e_k)\quad(j,k>1). \] Then \begin{equation} \begin{split} \Scal_{g^+}-\Scal_g ={}&D^2-2U(D)+r^2\abs{C}^2+(e_1r)^2\\ &+2r^2(1+\mathfrak p)(v^2-\mathfrak p r^2) \sum_{j>1}A(e_j)^2. \end{split} \end{equation} In particular, the final term is nonnegative whenever $\mathfrak p\ge0$ and $\mathfrak p N(t)^2t^2\le1$. For $N\equiv1$, one also has, everywhere, \begin{equation} \Scal_{g^+}-\Scal_g=\abs{II}^2+D^2-2U(D), \end{equation} where $II$ is the second fundamental form of the ordinary product graph. The inverse graph metric on base covectors and the volume form of $g^+$ are \begin{equation} P=g^{-1}-U\otimes U, \qquad dV_{g^+}=dV_g\,d\theta. \end{equation}

papers.title: Spectral scalar curvature and uniform Urysohn width
papers.abstract: For every n ≥ 4, a complete connected smooth Riemannian n-manifold without boundary satisfying $-4\Delta+\mathop{\mathrm{Scal}}\nolimits \ge1$ as a quadratic-form inequality admits a continuous map to a simplicial complex of dimension at most $n-2$ whose entire fibers have diameter bounded only in terms of n. The bound is measured in the original metric. This extends the uniform Urysohn width theorem from a pointwise scalar-curvature lower bound to a spectral lower bound.
papers.familySummary: Every complete connected smooth boundaryless n-manifold, n ≥ 3, satisfying $-4\Delta+\mathrm{Scal}\ge1$ as a quadratic-form inequality admits a continuous map to a simplicial complex of dimension at most $n-2$ whose entire fibers have diameter bounded only by n in the original metric. This strengthens Gromov's width conclusion to spectral scalar curvature. Universal covers of closed positive-scalar-curvature manifolds also have continuous macroscopic dimension at most $n-2$ for every n ≥ 2.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: For every integer $n\ge4$ there is a finite constant $C_n$ with the following property. Every connected complete smooth Riemannian $n$-manifold $(M,g)$ without boundary satisfying \eqref{eq:spectral-bound} admits a continuous map $f:M\to K$ to a simplicial complex of dimension at most $n-2$ such that \[ \diam_g f^{-1}(y)\le C_n\qquad(y\in K). \] In particular, $\UW_{n-2}(M,g)\le C_n$.

primaryStatements.name: Partition theorem for stretched data {\cite{OpenAIWidth}}
primaryStatements.label: interface:width
primaryStatements.text: For each integer $n\ge4$, there is a finite number $D_{\mathrm{nat}}(n)>0$ with the following property. Let $(M^n,g)$ be a connected complete smooth Riemannian manifold without boundary, and let $D\ge D_{\mathrm{nat}}(n)$. Choose a maximal $D$-separated set of centers $(x_i)_{i\in I}$, where $I=\{1,\ldots,N\}$ or $I=\mathbb N$, and put \[ A_i=\overline B_g(x_i,D),\qquad B_i=M\setminus B_g(x_i,2D). \] Suppose every $B_i$ is nonempty. Choose positive numbers $p_i^*$ for $i\in\{0\}\cup I$ such that \[ \sum_{i\in\{0\}\cup I}p_i^*=\frac1{20}. \] Assume there are a complete smooth metric $h\ge g$ and a finite or countable family of smooth real functions $(p_\alpha)$ with locally finite compact supports such that \begin{equation} \dist_h(A_i,B_i)>10+2\pi\sqrt{2/p_i^*}\quad(i\in I), \qquad R(h,(p_\alpha))\ge\frac25\quad\hbox{on }M. \end{equation} Then there is a continuous map $f:M\to K$ to a simplicial complex of dimension at most $n-2$, with its usual polyhedral topology, such that \[ \sup_{y\in K}\diam_g f^{-1}(y)\le4D+2. \] The diameter bounds the entire fiber, including all its components.

primaryStatements.name: Quadratic reserve
primaryStatements.label: pre:reserve
primaryStatements.text: For every integer $n\ge4$ there is a constant $C(n)<\infty$ with the following property. If $h$ is a complete smooth metric on a connected boundaryless $n$-manifold $M$ and $w\in C^\infty(M)$, there are a smooth complete metric $h^+\ge h$ and a smooth real-valued function $t^+$ such that \begin{equation} \Dcal(h^+,t^+)\ge \Dcal(h,w)+(t^+)^2-C(n) \quad\hbox{on }M. \end{equation} One may take $C(n)=100n+203$.

primaryStatements.name: Signed pressure law
primaryStatements.label: pressure:law
primaryStatements.text: For every \(A_0,P_0,\epsilon,b_0>0\), there are constants \(S_0\in(0,1]\), \(T\ge10\), and a smooth function \[ F:(-S_0,S_0)\times\R\longrightarrow\R \] that is odd in its first variable and has the following properties. Set \begin{equation} N(t)=\sqrt{t^2+T^2},\qquad V(t)=N(t)^2=t^2+T^2. \end{equation} At every \((x,t)\in(-S_0,S_0)\times\R\), \begin{equation} \begin{gathered} F_x\ge A_0N(t),\qquad |F_t|\le\epsilon|F|, \qquad FF_t\le\epsilon F_x,\\ F_x\le b_0N(t)^2\quad\text{or}\quad -FF_t\ge P_0F_x,\\ F_x\le b_0N(t)^2+\epsilon F^2. \end{gathered} \end{equation} Moreover, \(F(x,t)\to+\infty\) as \(x\uparrow S_0\) and \(F(x,t)\to-\infty\) as \(x\downarrow-S_0\), uniformly for \(t\) in each compact subset of \(\R\).

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let $(M^3,g)$ be a connected complete smooth Riemannian three-manifold without boundary. Suppose that $\lambda>0$ and \begin{equation} \int_M\bigl(4|\nabla_g\phi|_g^2+\Scal_g\phi^2\bigr)\,d\vol_g \ge \lambda\int_M\phi^2\,d\vol_g \qquad\bigl(\phi\in C_c^\infty(M;\R)\bigr). \end{equation} Then there exist a simplicial complex $K$ of dimension at most one and a continuous map $f:M\to K$ such that \[ \diam_g f^{-1}(y)\le \frac{500}{\sqrt\lambda} \qquad(y\in K). \] The complex has its usual polyhedral topology. No orientability, spin, compactness, or bounded-geometry assumption is imposed on $M$.

primaryStatements.name: Closed stable surfaces
primaryStatements.label: prop:stable-surface
primaryStatements.text: Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth closed connected two-sided surface in a Riemannian three-manifold $(X,h)$. Let $T,\mu$ be smooth ambient functions. Suppose that $\Sigma$ satisfies $H-\nu T=\mu$, is stable for weighted area with pressure $\mu$, and satisfies \eqref{eq:pressure-curvature-condition} for a constant $c>0$. Then, in the induced metric $k=h|_\Sigma$, \[ \diam_k\Sigma\le\frac{2\pi}{\sqrt c}. \] Moreover, $\Sigma$ is diffeomorphic to $S^2$ or $\R P^2$.

primaryStatements.label: prop:separating-cut
primaryStatements.text: There is a locally finite family $\mathcal S$ of pairwise disjoint closed connected embedded two-sided stable weighted minimal surfaces in $M$ such that the following statements hold. Let $N$ be the manifold obtained by cutting $M$ along $\mathcal S$, and let $q:N\to M$ be the natural gluing map. \begin{enumerate} \item The map $q$ is proper and is a quotient map. Each connected component $P$ of $N$, with the intrinsic length metric of the pulled-back metric $g$, is proper. \item Each boundary component of $P$ is a sphere or a real projective plane, is stable weighted minimal, and has intrinsic $g$-diameter at most $2\pi$. Each surface of $\mathcal S$ gives two boundary copies in $N$. \item Every compact connected neatly embedded two-sided hypersurface in $P$ separates $P$. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.name: Separating interfaces
primaryStatements.label: prop:separating-interfaces
primaryStatements.text: Let $\ell\ge100$, and suppose that $\{r>\ell\}$ is nonempty. There are finitely many disjoint smooth compact connected two-sided neat hypersurfaces $F_1,\ldots,F_m$ in $P$ such that \begin{equation} F_i\subset\{\ell-91<r<\ell-18\},\qquad \diam_d F_i\le4\pi. \end{equation} Each $F_i$ separates $P$. Moreover, $P\setminus\bigcup_iF_i$ is the disjoint union of two open sets $U_+,U_-$, with $o\in U_+$ and $\{r>\ell\}\subset U_-$.

primaryStatements.name: Slab diameter bound
primaryStatements.label: prop:slab-diameter
primaryStatements.text: For $\ell<u\le\ell+2$, every connected component $C$ of \[ \{x\in P:\ell<r(x)<u\} \] has $d$-diameter at most $220$.

papers.title: Positive scalar curvature and uniform codimension-two width
papers.abstract: We prove the quantitative continuous form of Gromov's scalar-curvature conjecture in every dimension n ≥ 4. Every complete connected smooth boundaryless n-manifold with scalar curvature at least one admits a continuous map to a simplicial complex of dimension at most $n-2$ whose entire fibers have diameter bounded only in terms of n. We also obtain the continuous macroscopic-dimension conclusion for universal covers of closed manifolds with positive scalar curvature in every dimension n ≥ 2.

This strengthens Gromov's width conclusion to spectral scalar curvature. Universal covers of closed positive-scalar-curvature manifolds also have continuous macroscopic dimension at most $n-2$ for every n ≥ 2.

Every complete connected smooth boundaryless $n$-manifold with scalar curvature at least one admits a continuous map to a simplicial complex of dimension at most $n-2$ whose entire fibers have diameter bounded only in terms of $n$. primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: For every integer \(n\ge4\), there is a finite constant \(C_n\) such that every connected complete smooth Riemannian \(n\)-manifold \((M,g)\), without boundary and with \(\Scal_g\ge1\), admits a continuous map \(f:M\to K\) to a simplicial complex of dimension at most \(n-2\) satisfying \[ \diam_g f^{-1}(y)\le C_n\qquad(y\in K). \] In particular, \(\UW_{n-2}(M,g)\le C_n\).

primaryStatements.name: Continuous macroscopic dimension of universal covers
primaryStatements.label: cover:main
primaryStatements.text: Let $(M,h)$ be a closed connected smooth Riemannian manifold of dimension $n\ge2$ with positive scalar curvature. Its universal cover, with the lifted original metric $\widetilde h$, satisfies \[ \dim_{\mathrm{mc}}(\widetilde M,\widetilde h)\le n-2. \]

primaryStatements.name: Local stretching
primaryStatements.label: step:main
primaryStatements.text: Fix $n\ge2$ and $0<\delta<1/10$, and put $L_*=1.004$. There are constants $W,T\ge1$, depending only on $n,\delta$, with the following property. Let $h_0$ be a complete smooth metric on a manifold $M^n$ without boundary, let $h\ge h_0$ be smooth, and let $t\ge T$ be smooth. Let $A$ be a nonempty compact set and $B$ a nonempty closed set such that \[ \dist_{h_0}(A,B)\ge W. \] For every $0<d<\delta$ there are smooth $h'\ge h$ and $t'\ge t$ such that the changes have compact support in $\{\dist_{h_0}(A,\cdot)<W\}$, \begin{equation} \mathcal D(h',t')\ge \mathcal D(h,t)+(t'^2-t^2) -\delta\bigl(\tr_h h_0-\tr_{h'}h_0\bigr)t'^2-dt'^2, \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \dist_{h'}(A,B)\ge L_*W. \end{equation} In particular, $h'$ is complete. Neither $W$ nor $T$ depends on $d$, the geometry of $M$, or the sets $A,B$.

primaryStatements.name: Closed-manifold filling-radius bound
primaryStatements.label: cor:filling-radius
primaryStatements.text: Let \((M,g)\) be a closed connected smooth Riemannian \(n\)-manifold with \(n\ge4\) and \(\Scal_g\ge\sigma^2\) for some \(\sigma>0\). Then \[ \operatorname{FillRad}(M,g)\le \frac{C_n}{2\sigma}, \] where \(C_n\) is the constant in Theorem \ref{thm:main}.

primaryStatements.name: Aspherical obstruction
primaryStatements.label: cor:aspherical
primaryStatements.text: No closed smooth aspherical manifold of dimension \(n\ge4\) admits a Riemannian metric of strictly positive scalar curvature.

primaryStatements.name: Pressure law
primaryStatements.label: pressure:law
primaryStatements.text: For every $A_0,P_0,\eps,b_0>0$ there exist $0<S_0\le1$, $T\ge1$, and a smooth function \[ F:(-S_0,S_0)\times[T,\infty)\longrightarrow\R \] which is odd in $x$, has $F_x>0$, and satisfies \begin{equation} \begin{gathered} F_x\ge A_0t,\qquad |F_t|\le\eps|F|,\qquad FF_t\le\eps F_x,\\ F_x\le b_0t^2\quad\text{or}\quad -FF_t\ge P_0F_x,\\ F_x\le b_0t^2+\eps F^2. \end{gathered} \end{equation} For each fixed $t\ge T$, \[ \lim_{x\to-S_0}F(x,t)=-\infty, \qquad \lim_{x\to S_0}F(x,t)=+\infty. \] These limits are uniform when $t$ ranges over a compact subinterval of $[T,\infty)$. The choices depend only on $A_0,P_0,\eps,b_0$ and fixed numerical constants. In particular, they are independent of any manifold, metric, local cutoff, or subsequent deformation parameter. The lower bound $T$ may be increased after the construction.

primaryStatements.name: Prescribed widths for a locally finite family
primaryStatements.label: rounds:wide
primaryStatements.text: Let \((M,g)\) be complete, connected and smooth, with \(\Scal_g\ge1\). There is a countable set of centers \((x_i)\) such that \[ A_i=\overline B_g(x_i,D),\qquad B_i=M\setminus B_g(x_i,2D) \] have the following properties: the \(A_i\) cover \(M\), and the closed balls \(\overline B_g(x_i,2D)\) are locally finite. Suppose that every \(B_i\) is nonempty. Given arbitrary finite numbers \(L_i>0\), there exist a complete smooth metric \(h\ge g\) and a countable family of smooth functions \((p_\alpha)\), whose supports form a locally finite family of compact sets, for which \begin{align} \dist_h(A_i,B_i)&>L_i \quad(i\ge1),\\ \Scal_h-2\Delta_h\sum_\alpha p_\alpha -\left|\dd\sum_\alpha p_\alpha\right|_h^2 -\sum_\alpha|\dd p_\alpha|_h^2&\ge\frac25. \end{align} Every sum in \eqref{rounds:stabilized} is locally finite. If some \(B_i\) is empty, then \(\diam_g M\le4D\).

primaryStatements.name: Finite compatible cutting
primaryStatements.label: finite:cut
primaryStatements.text: Fix a finite number $N_*$ of labels and the stage constants in \eqref{packet:constants}. Suppose a stage-$r$ packet diagram is obtained by the regular splitting construction of \cref{packet:split}, with compatible smooth base metrics and a finite common list of positive circle warps, and satisfies \cref{packet:invariant}. After the radial stage, require the complete compact-part/product-end geometry of \cref{packet:category,packet:geometry}. Let $j_0$ be the next label, and suppose every nonempty parent packet has base dimension at least two. Then $j_0$ can be processed as follows. On every parent there is a compatible smooth regular defining function with the prescribed signs on the current forced core closures. Keep its zero wall as the new hit space. To each closed sign side attach the full product cylinder over its boundary. These pieces form a compatible smooth stage-$(r+1)$ packet diagram with the continuous projections described above. The wall on a parent $E$ lies in $\operatorname{int}G_{j_0}$. The remaining profiles may first be modified, their cores enlarged, and their potentials increased in the parents; these data are then carried to the new pieces by restriction and cylinder projection. There are compatible smooth metrics and potentials, and exactly $399$ new positive circle factors on each new packet, for which the entire stage-$(r+1)$ invariant holds. Earlier forced signs are preserved. The new packets have complete compact-part/product-end geometry. This assertion includes a possible one-dimensional output, on which its scalar lower bound holds everywhere. The operation fixes every old warp identically equal to $1$. For a remaining label that is passive on the finite downward source diagrams and the face copies used in their comparisons---constant pole profile, full corresponding core, and spatially constant potential $c_j$ agreeing on compared faces---the construction can preserve the pole and core and choose its new potential to be exactly $(1+3\eta_r/2)c_j$, where $\eta_r=1/(200N_*)$. At stage zero the single parent may instead be an arbitrary complete smooth manifold with no product-end or bounded-geometry assumption. Subject to the same scalar and separation assumptions, if its data are the radial initialization of \cref{packet:initialization}, the same conclusion holds for the first split. Every resulting wall component and every closed-side component is compact before the cylinders are attached, and these components form locally finite families.

definitions.name: Packet diagram
definitions.label: packet:category
definitions.text: At stage $r$, a status is $\alpha\in\{+,-,*\}^{r}$. Its entries record the first $r$ processed cuts. A sign $+$ or $-$ selects the corresponding retained side of a cut, and a star $*$ selects the wall, called a hit. The space $E_\alpha$ is a smooth second countable manifold without boundary, possibly empty or disconnected; when nonempty its base dimension is $m(\alpha)=n-\#\{i:\alpha_i=*\}$. Its connected components are called packets. Replacing signs by stars gives the face order. If $B$ is a packet with $d$ additional stars relative to a coarser status, then for that coarser status it has exactly one incident packet $E$ and one corresponding occurrence of a full product tail \begin{equation} \iota_{BE}:B\times(T_1,\infty)\times\cdots\times(T_d,\infty) \longrightarrow E. \end{equation} The normal coordinates are labelled by the changed status entries. Thresholds may depend on the incidence. For a single entry, tails from distinct face components are disjoint. Intersections of sufficiently far tails for different entries are exactly the tails over their common further faces. The identifications commute: composing face maps in any order gives the same occurrence and the same individually labelled normal coordinates. After slightly raising the entry thresholds, each closed tail is properly embedded. Each packet $E$ is equipped with a continuous map $q_E:E\to X$. After the radial stage we require the following additional properties. Every packet has only finitely many incident faces and cofaces, including through chains; the complement of its sufficiently far elementary tails is compact. On each sufficiently far face product these maps satisfy $q_E(\iota_{BE}(b,\mathbf t))=q_B(b)$. A metric, scalar function, warp, or set is compatible if, in every sufficiently far tail, it is exactly the product or pullback of the corresponding face datum. For metrics the normal factors are $\dd t_1^2+\cdots+\dd t_d^2$; all warps are independent of the normal coordinates there. The thresholds for different data may differ.

definitions.name: Analytic invariant
definitions.label: packet:invariant
definitions.text: At stage $r$, write $J_r$ for the unprocessed labels. On a packet $E$ of base dimension $m$, retain its base metric and all circle warps. Write $R_E$ for the scalar curvature of that full warped metric and $\omega_E$ for the product of its circle lengths, suppressing fixed circle-volume constants. Gradients of invariant functions are base gradients; their integrals use $\omega_E\,\dd\vol_E$, and their Laplacian is the corresponding weighted base Laplacian. For every $j\in J_r$ the data comprise a compatible continuous profile $\mu_j:E\to[-\infty,\infty]$ with locally Lipschitz finite truncations, a compatible smooth potential $\Pi_j\ge\pi_0$, and compatible open cores $U_j^+,U_j^-$ satisfying \begin{equation} \overline{U_j^\pm}\subset \operatorname{int}_E\{\mu_j=\pm\infty\}. \end{equation} On the open finite band the profile obeys, almost everywhere, \begin{equation} 2|\grad\mu_j|\le a_r\mu_j^2+\Pi_j. \end{equation} Set \begin{equation} G_j=E\setminus(U_j^+\cup U_j^-),\qquad D_E=\bigl\{x:\#\{j\in J_r:x\in G_j\}\ge m-1\bigr\}. \end{equation} The required scalar bound is \begin{equation} R_E\ge\lambda_r+b_r\sum_{j\in J_r}\Pi_j \quad\hbox{on }D_E. \end{equation} For an unprocessed color $i$, the cores contain $q_E^{-1}(A_i)\subset U_i^+$ and $q_E^{-1}(B_i)\subset U_i^-$. Enlarging cores must preserve these conditions. The sets $D_E$ are closed: they are finite unions of finite intersections of the closed sets $G_j$ (and equal $E$ when the count threshold is nonpositive). All data are exact products in the sense of \cref{packet:category}; at stage zero the single space is $X$, with no product-end requirement.

definitions.name: Finite exceptional data
definitions.label: countable:finite-data
definitions.text: At stage $r\ge1$, on each whole packet $E$ there are finite sets $I_E\subset J_r$ of label indices and $F_E$ of old warp indices such that, for $j\notin I_E$, \begin{equation} \mu_j\equiv-\infty,\qquad U_j^-=E,\qquad U_j^+=\varnothing, \qquad \Pi_j\equiv c_rp_j^*. \end{equation} For every old warp index outside $F_E$, its length is identically one. The number $c_r$ is the same on all packets and is prescribed by \begin{equation} c_0=1,\qquad c_{r+1}=(1+3\eta_r/2)c_r. \end{equation} For any finite diagram used in a comparison, take the union of its finite exceptional sets, adding the current label explicitly. This one finite union then works simultaneously on all its whole packets. At stage zero the analogous property is required on every compact radial block and buffer, with $c_0=1$.

definitions.name: Local absolute minimizer
definitions.label: cut:minimizer-definition
definitions.text: For smooth $p$ a phase $A$ is a local absolute minimizer if for every relatively compact open $U\subset E$ and every locally finite-perimeter set $B$ with $A\mathbin\triangle B\Subset U$, \begin{equation} P_\omega(A;U)-\int_{A\cap U}p\,\dd\mu \le P_\omega(B;U)-\int_{B\cap U}p\,\dd\mu. \end{equation} The notation $A\mathbin\triangle B\Subset U$ means that the discrepancy is contained, modulo null sets, in a compact subset of $U$.

definitions.name: Reserved form and test completion
definitions.label: cut:reserve
definitions.text: For the wall or a joined side define, respectively, \begin{align*} \mathcal N_S(v)&=1.7\int_S|\grad v|^2\,\dd\mu_S,\\ \mathcal N_\Omega(v) &=.8\int_\Omega|\grad v_b|^2\,\dd\mu +1.7\int_0^\infty\!\int_S|\grad v_c|^2 \,\dd\mu_S\,\dd t. \end{align*} We write $\mathcal N$ when the tested space is understood. The squared norm $\|v\|_2^2$ is the sum of the corresponding piecewise weighted integrals. With \[ e_0=(\lambda_r-\lambda_{r+1})/100>0, \qquad \mathfrak h(v)=\mathcal N(v)+e_0\|v\|_2^2, \] the test completion means completion of the admissible compact tests just specified in the norm $\mathfrak h^{1/2}$. In particular its seam condition is matching traces, with no zero trace imposed there.

definitions.name: The matching form domain
definitions.label: shield:domain
definitions.text: Let $E$ be a parent packet of dimension $m$, with true wall $S$ and singular set $\Sigma$. A raw piece $Z$ means either $S_{\rm reg}$ or one of the two joined spaces \[ Z=\Omega\mathbin{\cup}_{S_{\rm reg}} (S_{\rm reg}\times[0,\infty)). \] The tests on a joined space are compactly supported, piecewise smooth functions whose two traces agree at the regular seam and whose support avoids $\Sigma$ and the cylinders over $\Sigma$. The wall has the corresponding compact tests away from $\Sigma$. All measures include the old warp weight. Put \begin{equation} \mathfrak h_Z(v)=\mathcal N_Z(v)+e_0\norm{v}_{L^2(Z)}^2, \qquad e_0=\frac{\lambda_r-\lambda_{r+1}}{100}>0, \end{equation} where $\mathcal N$ is the reserved gradient form in \cref{cut:reserve}: its gradient coefficients are $.8$ on the bulk and $1.7$ on the wall or cylinder. Write $\mathcal H_Z$ for the completion of these tests in $\mathfrak h_Z^{1/2}$. Pure cylinders $S_{\rm reg}\times\R$ use the coefficient $1.7$ throughout. The definitions also apply after adjoining finitely many Euclidean product coordinates, with the same coefficients and $e_0$. Such products are used only to identify limits on translated windows; they do not append further circle warps or change the weight. A compact window means a fixed compact ambient base window together with a bounded cylinder interval, when a cylinder is present.

papers.title: Generalized Cartan–Hadamard isoperimetry and Euclidean equality rigidity
papers.abstract: We resolve the generalized Cartan–Hadamard isoperimetric conjecture in every dimension. In a complete simply connected smooth manifold with sectional curvature at most κ ≤ 0, every finite-volume set of finite ambient perimeter has perimeter at least that of the equal-volume ball in curvature κ. For bounded positive-volume sets, equality in the Euclidean comparison holds precisely when the set agrees up to null sets with an open region isometric, with its induced metric, to a round Euclidean ball.
papers.familySummary: Proves generalized Cartan–Hadamard isoperimetry in every dimension: in a complete simply connected manifold with sectional curvature at most κ ≤ 0, every finite-volume finite-perimeter set satisfies the sharp comparison with the equal-volume model ball. Bounded positive-volume equality regions for κ = 0 are Euclidean balls. Also proves sharp Euclidean filling bounds for compactly supported integral n-cycles, n ≥ 2, in arbitrary proper CAT$(0)$ spaces.
papers.subject: Differential geometry
papers.sourceAbstract: We resolve the generalized Cartan--Hadamard isoperimetric conjecture in every dimension. In a complete simply connected smooth manifold with sectional curvature at most $\kappa\le0$, every finite-volume set of finite ambient perimeter has perimeter at least that of the equal-volume ball in curvature $\kappa$. For bounded positive-volume sets, equality in the Euclidean comparison holds precisely when the set agrees up to null sets with an open region isometric, with its induced metric, to a round Euclidean ball.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let $n\ge2$, let $\kappa\le0$, and let $(M^n,g)$ be a complete simply connected smooth Riemannian manifold with $\Sec_g\le\kappa$. Every measurable set $E\subset M$ with $\vol_g(E)<\infty$ and $P_g(E)<\infty$ satisfies \[ P_g(E)\ge \mathcal I_{\sqrt{-\kappa}}\bigl(\vol_g(E)\bigr). \]

primaryStatements.name: Euclidean equality rigidity
primaryStatements.label: thm:equality
primaryStatements.text: Let $(M^n,g)$ be complete, simply connected and smooth, with $n\ge2$ and $\Sec_g\le0$. Let $E\subset M$ be bounded and measurable, with $0<\vol_g(E)<\infty$ and $P_g(E)<\infty$. Then \[ P_g(E)=n\omega_n^{1/n}\vol_g(E)^{(n-1)/n} \] if and only if $E$ agrees up to ambient volume zero with an open region whose induced Riemannian metric is isometric to a round Euclidean ball.

primaryStatements.name: Model-ball Faber--Krahn and Saint--Venant comparisons
primaryStatements.label: cor:model-ball-spectral
primaryStatements.text: Let $n\ge2$, $\kappa\le0$ and $1<p<\infty$. Let $(M^n,g)$ be complete, simply connected, smooth and without boundary, with $\Sec_g\le\kappa$. For a nonempty smooth domain $D\Subset M$, let $B_\kappa(|D|)$ be a geodesic ball of volume $|D|=\vol_g(D)$ in the simply connected $n$-dimensional space form of curvature $\kappa$. Then \[ \lambda_{1,p}(D)\ge\lambda_{1,p}\bigl(B_\kappa(|D|)\bigr), \qquad T_p(D)\le T_p\bigl(B_\kappa(|D|)\bigr). \]

primaryStatements.name: Distance and metric comparison
primaryStatements.label: lem:distance-comparison
primaryStatements.text: Let $(M^n,g)$ be complete and simply connected with $\Sec_g\le0$. For $p\in M$, write $\log_p=\exp_p^{-1}$, $r_p(x)=d(p,x)$, and $D_p=r_p^2/2$. Then \begin{equation} \Hess_gD_p\ge g,\qquad (\exp_p)^*g\ge g_p, \qquad |d\log_p(X)|_{g_p}\le |X|_g. \end{equation} Here $g_p$ on $T_pM$ denotes its constant Euclidean metric.

primaryStatements.name: Hypersurface Sobolev inequality
primaryStatements.label: thm:extrinsic-sobolev
primaryStatements.text: For every Lipschitz function $v$ with compact support in $\Sigma^\circ$, \begin{equation} Q_\Sigma(v)\ge Y_m\left(\int_\Sigma |v|^q\,d\sigma\right)^{2/q}. \end{equation} The inequality also holds for the zero extension of every $v\in H^1_0(U)$, where $U\Subset\Sigma^\circ$ is open.

primaryStatements.name: Confined minimizers and their regularity
primaryStatements.label: prop:confined-regularity
primaryStatements.text: For each $v\in(0,|B|)$ there is a minimizer $E$ in \eqref{eq:confined-profile}. It has a regular representative for which $\Gamma=\partial E$ is the support of its perimeter measure and is contained in $\overline B$. There is a compact set $S\subset B$ such that \begin{enumerate} \item $\dim_{\mathcal H}S\le n-8$, with $S=\varnothing$ if $n<8$; \item $\Sigma=\Gamma\setminus S$ is a boundaryless $C^{1,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ hypersurface, smooth on $\Sigma\cap B$; \item $\Gamma$ is $C^{1,1}$ in an ambient neighborhood of $\partial B$, and $S$ is disjoint from a collar of $\partial B$; \item with $d\sigma$ denoting area on $\Sigma$, for every Borel set $A\subset M$ one has \begin{equation} |D\chi_E|(A)=\int_{A\cap\Sigma}d\sigma, \qquad P(E)=\int_\Sigma d\sigma=I(v). \end{equation} \end{enumerate} The unit normal on $\Sigma$ is the outward normal of $E$.

primaryStatements.name: Profile differential inequality
primaryStatements.label: prop:profile-ode
primaryStatements.text: For almost every $v\in(0,\vol(B))$, \begin{equation} I'(v)\ge m\sqrt{b^2+\left(\frac{s_m}{I(v)}\right)^{2/m}}. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Comparison in the normalized curvatures
primaryStatements.label: thm:normalized-comparison
primaryStatements.text: Let $n\ge4$ and $b\in\{0,1\}$. If $M^n$ is complete, simply connected and smooth, with $\Sec_M\le-b^2$, then every bounded measurable set $E\subset M$ of finite perimeter and positive volume satisfies \[ P(E)\ge\mathcal I_b(\vol(E)). \]

papers.title: Sharp integral fillings in CAT(0) spaces
papers.abstract: Every compactly supported integral n-cycle, n ≥ 2, in a proper CAT(0) space bounds a compactly supported integral current with the sharp Euclidean mass bound. The theorem allows arbitrary integer multiplicities and unrestricted ambient dimension. In particular, we prove the Euclidean Cartan–Hadamard isoperimetric conjecture in dimensions at least three.
papers.familySummary: Proves generalized Cartan–Hadamard isoperimetry in every dimension: in a complete simply connected manifold with sectional curvature at most κ ≤ 0, every finite-volume finite-perimeter set satisfies the sharp comparison with the equal-volume model ball. Bounded positive-volume equality regions for κ = 0 are Euclidean balls. Also proves sharp Euclidean filling bounds for compactly supported integral n-cycles, n ≥ 2, in arbitrary proper CAT$(0)$ spaces.

primaryStatements.name: Sharp integral filling
primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let $X$ be a proper CAT(0) space and $n\ge2$ an integer. Every compactly supported $T\in\I_n(X)$ with $\partial T=0$ admits a compactly supported $S\in\I_{n+1}(X)$ such that \begin{equation} \partial S=T,\qquad \M(S)\le c_n\M(T)^{(n+1)/n} =\frac{\M(T)^{(n+1)/n}} {(n+1)^{(n+1)/n}\omega_{n+1}^{1/n}}. \end{equation} There is no restriction on the dimension of $X$ or on the integer multiplicities of the currents. The coefficient is optimal.

primaryStatements.label: cor:cartan-hadamard
primaryStatements.text: Let $M$ be a Cartan--Hadamard manifold of dimension $d\ge3$. For every bounded domain $\Omega\subset M$ with smooth boundary, \begin{equation} \operatorname{area}(\partial\Omega) \ge d\omega_d^{1/d}\vol(\Omega)^{(d-1)/d}. \end{equation} The same inequality holds for relatively compact sets of finite perimeter, with ambient perimeter in place of boundary area.

primaryStatements.name: Current background in a compact \(\operatorname{CAT}(0)\) space
primaryStatements.label: thm:current-background
primaryStatements.text: Let \(Y\) be compact and \(\operatorname{CAT}(0)\), and let \(k\ge1\). The following statements hold. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item Lipschitz pushforward preserves integral currents, commutes with boundary, and satisfies the Lipschitz mass bound. Restrictions by bounded Borel coefficients have the usual mass-measure bound; for a Borel set \(E\subset Y\), \[ \|C\restr E\|=\|C\|\restr E. \] The restricted current need not be normal. If \(u:Y\to\R\) is Lipschitz and \(C\in\I_k(Y)\), then \(C\restr\{u>t\}\) is integral for almost every \(t\). In particular its boundary is an integral \((k-1)\)-cycle. \item If \(C_j\in\I_k(Y)\) and \(\sup_j(\M(C_j)+\M(\partial C_j))<\infty\), a subsequence converges weakly to an integral current. Boundary commutes with weak convergence, and mass is lower semicontinuous. \item Every \(C\in\I_k(Y)\) admits a representation by bi-Lipschitz maps \(\phi_i:E_i\to Y\), where \(E_i\subset\R^k\) are bounded Borel sets and the images \(Z_i=\phi_i(E_i)\) are pairwise disjoint Borel sets, and by signed integer multiplicities \(\theta_i\in L^1(E_i)\), such that \begin{equation} C(b,\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_k) =\sum_i\int_{E_i}\theta_i(z)b(\phi_i(z)) \det D\bigl((\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_k)\circ\phi_i\bigr)(z)\dd z. \end{equation} The chart summands have summable masses. Zero multiplicities may be discarded. Scalar functions on a Borel chart domain are differentiated by Lipschitz extension to \(\R^k\); their derivatives are independent of that extension at almost every density point of the domain. \item For \(h>0\), the whole-current product \([0,h]\times C\), with the Euclidean product metric, is an integral \((k+1)\)-current and obeys \begin{equation} \partial([0,h]\times C) =[h]\times C-[0]\times C-[0,h]\times\partial C. \end{equation} Writing \(b_t(x)=b(t,x)\) and \(\pi_{a,t}(x)=\pi_a(t,x)\), its action is \begin{equation} \begin{split} &([0,h]\times C)(b,\pi_1,\ldots,\pi_{k+1})\\ &\quad=\sum_{a=1}^{k+1}(-1)^{a+1}\int_0^h C\bigl(b_t\,\partial_t\pi_a(t,\cdot), \pi_{1,t},\ldots,\widehat{\pi_{a,t}},\ldots, \pi_{k+1,t}\bigr)\dd t. \end{split} \end{equation} The hat indicates omission. The time derivative is interpreted almost everywhere and as a bounded Borel first coefficient in the current action. \item There are finite constants \(K_k,L_k\), independent of the cycle, such that every integral \(k\)-cycle \(B\) in \(Y\) satisfies \begin{equation} V(B)\le K_k\M(B)^{(k+1)/k},\qquad V(B)\le L_k\M(B). \end{equation} Every such \(B\) has a mass-minimizing integral filling in \(Y\). If integral \(k\)-cycles \(B_j\) have bounded masses and converge weakly to an integral cycle \(B\), then \begin{equation} V(B_j-B)\longrightarrow0, \qquad V(B_j)\longrightarrow V(B). \end{equation} \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.name: Exact chart mass
primaryStatements.label: prop:chart-mass
primaryStatements.text: For the representation \eqref{eq:chart-action}, let \(G_i,J_i\) be as in \eqref{eq:chart-metric}. Then \begin{equation} \|C\|=\sum_i(\phi_i)_\#\bigl(|\theta_i|J_i\dd z\bigr). \end{equation} Thus, with \(\rho_i=|\theta_i|J_i\), integration against the current mass is integration against \(\rho_i\dd z\) on the disjoint charts.

primaryStatements.name: Radial first variation
primaryStatements.label: prop:radial
primaryStatements.text: For every center $y\in Y$, write $r(x)=d(y,x)$. Every nonnegative Lipschitz function $g:Y\to\R$ satisfies \begin{equation} \int_Y \bigl(ng+r\,Dr\cdot Dg\bigr)\dd\mu \leq n\int_Y rg\sqrt{1-|Dr|^2}\dd\mu. \end{equation} The square root is defined $\mu$-almost everywhere by $|Dr|\leq 1$.

primaryStatements.name: Sharp filling in cycle dimension two
primaryStatements.label: prop:base
primaryStatements.text: Let $Y$ be a compact CAT(0) space. Every integral two-cycle $T\in\I_2(Y)$ admits $S\in\I_3(Y)$ with \[ \partial S=T,\qquad \M(S)\leq c_2\M(T)^{3/2} =\frac{\M(T)^{3/2}}{6\sqrt{\pi}}. \]

primaryStatements.name: Uniform small-set isoperimetry
primaryStatements.label: prop:small-set
primaryStatements.text: For every $\eta\in(0,1)$ there is a number $\delta\in(0,m/2)$, independent of the Lipschitz function $u\colon Y\to\R$, with the following property. Put \[ a(t)=\mu\{u>t\},\qquad U_t=A\restr\{u>t\},\qquad P(t)=\M(\partial U_t), \] where $U_t$ and its boundary are integral for almost every $t$. At almost every level for which $a(t)\le\delta$, \begin{equation} P(t)\ge(1-\eta)n\omega_n^{1/n}a(t)^{(n-1)/n}. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Almost Euclidean critical Sobolev bound
primaryStatements.label: prop:almost-sobolev
primaryStatements.text: For every $\epsilon\in(0,S_*)$ there is a finite constant $C_\epsilon\ge0$ such that every real Lipschitz function $u$ on $Y$ satisfies \begin{equation} (S_*-\epsilon)\|u\|_p^2 \le4\beta E(u)+C_\epsilon\|u\|_2^2. \end{equation} The constant is independent of $u$.

primaryStatements.label: thm:uniformization
primaryStatements.text: Let $M$ be a connected noncompact complex manifold of complex dimension $n\geq1$. If $M$ admits a smooth complete K\"ahler metric with strictly positive holomorphic bisectional curvature, then $M$ is biholomorphic to $\C^n$.

primaryStatements.name: Initial analytic data
primaryStatements.label: prop:initial-data
primaryStatements.text: The following objects and estimates are available. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item There is a smooth strictly plurisubharmonic function $\psi$ with $\psi\le C(1+r)$. \item Holomorphic functions and holomorphic tangent fields interpolate arbitrary finite jets at a finite set of points. There are finitely many holomorphic functions defining an injective immersion $F:M\longrightarrow\C^N$, and finitely many global holomorphic tangent fields spanning $T^{1,0}M$ at every point. \item At every point $x$ there is a global holomorphic canonical section $S$ with $S(x)\ne0$ and $\log|S|_g^2\le C_S(1+r)$. There is also a smooth function $\Xi$ such that \begin{equation} \dd\Xi\ge\Ric(g),\qquad \Xi\le C(1+r^{3/2}). \end{equation} \item There is a smooth exhaustion $u\ge1$ such that \begin{equation} C^{-1}(1+r)\le u\le C(1+r),\qquad |\partial u|_g\le C,\qquad |\dd u|_g\le C/u. \end{equation} \item If $S(o)\ne0$ is chosen as in \textup{(iii)}, then, for $L\ge1$, \begin{equation} \frac{1}{\Vol B(o,L)}\int_{B(o,L)} \bigl|\log|S|_g^2\bigr|\,dV_g\le CL, \qquad \frac{1}{\Vol B(o,L)}\int_{B(o,L)}R_g\,dV_g\le C/L. \end{equation} \end{enumerate} Neither $F$ nor $\psi$ is asserted to be proper. The exhaustion in \textup{(iv)} has a two-sided complex Hessian bound.

primaryStatements.name: Localized flow
primaryStatements.label: thm:localized-flow
primaryStatements.text: There is a smooth K\"ahler--Ricci flow $h_t$ on $M$, for $0\le t<\infty$, with $h_0=g$. There are smooth real functions $U,P$ and $\rho$ such that \begin{equation} \begin{gathered} 0<h_t\le g,\qquad h_t=g-t\Ric(g)+\dd U,\qquad U(\cdot,0)=0,\\ P=U_t=\log\frac{\det h_t}{\det g},\qquad \rho=-P\ge0,\qquad R_{h_t}=-P_t\ge0. \end{gathered} \end{equation} For each finite $T$, there is $C_T$ such that \begin{equation} \sup_{0\le t\le T} \frac{1}{\Vol_gB_g(o,L)}\int_{B_g(o,L)}\rho(x,t)\,dV_g(x) \le C_TL\qquad(L\ge1). \end{equation} At every fixed $x$, $\rho(x,t)\le C_x(1+t)$ for all $t\ge0$. Furthermore, on each finite time interval there is a smooth positive function $Q$ and a constant $c>0$ with \begin{equation} Q\ge c(1+r^2),\qquad (\partial_t-\Delta_{h_t})Q\ge c\tr_{h_t}g. \end{equation} Smoothness at $t=0$ means smoothness with all one-sided time derivatives.

primaryStatements.name: Scalar comparisons
primaryStatements.label: prop:scalar-comparison
primaryStatements.text: Fix a finite $T>0$. The following conclusions hold for the flow of Theorem \ref{thm:localized-flow}. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item The function $\rho$ is the minimal nonnegative solution with zero initial values of \begin{equation} (\partial_t-\Delta_{h_t})\rho =\tr_{h_t}\Ric(g). \end{equation} There are nonnegative smooth supercaloric functions $\rho_j$ on $M\times[0,T]$ such that \begin{equation} 0\le\rho_j\le\rho,\qquad \rho_j\ge\rho-C_j,\qquad \rho_j\longrightarrow0 \text{ locally uniformly on }M\times[0,T]. \end{equation} Each fixed $\rho_j$ has all spatial and one-sided time derivatives smooth at $t=0$ and bounded on compact spacetime sets. \item Suppose $v$ is upper semicontinuous, bounded on compact spacetime sets, $0\le v\le\rho$, and satisfies, in the upper viscosity sense on $0<t<T$, \begin{equation} \partial_tv\le e^{-v}\Delta_{h_t}v+(1-e^{-v})R_{h_t}. \end{equation} Then $v=0$ on $M\times[0,T)$. \end{enumerate} Neither assertion requires completeness of $h_t$.

primaryStatements.name: Compactness of discs
primaryStatements.label: prop:disc-compactness
primaryStatements.text: For each compact $K\subset M$ and each $A_0<\infty$, there is a compact $K'\subset M$ such that every holomorphic disc $f:\overline\Delta\to M$, smooth up to the circle, satisfying \[ f(\partial\Delta)\subset K,\qquad \int_\Delta f^*\omega_g\le A_0 \] has $f(\overline\Delta)\subset K'$. Every sequence of such discs has a subsequence converging holomorphically on compact subsets of $\Delta$. The same statements hold for discs in $Y$ with compact boundary in $Y$ and with $\int_\Delta(\pi\circ f)^*\omega_g\le A_0$. The resulting compact may depend on $K$ and $A_0$.

primaryStatements.name: Differential inequality for the envelope
primaryStatements.label: prop:disc-inequality
primaryStatements.text: Suppose that a smooth real function $\varphi$ touches $v$ from below at $(y_*,s_*)$, where $0<s_*<T$. In holomorphic cotangent coordinates write \[ W=\dd_Y\varphi(y_*,s_*)= \begin{pmatrix} A&B\\ B^*&C\end{pmatrix},\qquad C>0. \] There is a Hermitian form $K$ on the horizontal coordinate space such that \begin{equation} K\ge0,\qquad K\ge A-BC^{-1}B^*,\qquad \partial_s\varphi(y_*,s_*)\ge\tr(C^{\mathsf T}K). \end{equation} The transpose is the tangent--cotangent contraction in these coordinates. In particular the statement applies to lower tests translated in a fixed cotangent coordinate chart; its contraction has constant coefficients.

primaryStatements.label: prop:ellipsoid-comparison
primaryStatements.text: For the optimizer in \eqref{ell:optimizer}, every smooth lower test $\lambda$ of $\mathcal L$ at an interior point $(x_0,t_0)$ satisfies \begin{equation} \partial_t\lambda(x_0,t_0) \ge e^{-F_0(x_0,t_0)}\Delta_{h_{t_0}}\lambda(x_0,t_0). \end{equation} Thus $\mathcal L$ satisfies this inequality in the lower viscosity sense on $M\times(0,T)$.

primaryStatements.label: thm:joint-positivity
primaryStatements.text: For the flow in Theorem \ref{thm:localized-flow}, the function \[ (x,\xi,w)\longmapsto N(x,\xi,e^{w+\bar w}) \] is plurisubharmonic on $T^{*(1,0)}M\times\C$. For every finite $T$, its disc envelope satisfies $v=N$ on $T^{*(1,0)}M\times(0,T)$.

papers.title: Entropy equality and local symmetry in negative curvature
papers.abstract: For every closed connected smooth Riemannian manifold of dimension at least three with strictly negative sectional curvature, we prove that normalized Liouville measure has maximal entropy for the unit-speed geodesic flow if and only if the metric is locally symmetric. This resolves Katok's entropy rigidity conjecture positively in these dimensions, including all rank-one symmetric types at arbitrary scale.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Suppose $n\ge3$ and every sectional curvature of $g$ is strictly negative. Then \[ h_{m_L}(\phi_1)=\htop(\phi_1) \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \nabla^gR_g=0. \] Equivalently, equality holds precisely when the universal Riemannian cover is a rank-one symmetric space of noncompact type, at an arbitrary overall scale.

primaryStatements.name: The two formal affine fields
primaryStatements.label: hull:main
primaryStatements.text: At every point of a conull invariant set there are formal affine fields $\mathcal A^u,\mathcal A^s$ of horizontal $m$-covectors with the following properties. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item Their values contain $u$ and $w$, respectively. At the center, the exterior product of any element of $\mathcal A^u$ with any element of $\mathcal A^s$ equals the fixed nonzero exterior product $u\wedge w$. \item The fields are equivariant under $f$, changes of section, and flip, with the same constant and height multipliers as $u,w$. In a flow box their height dependences are $e^{-h\tau}$ and $e^{h\tau}$. \item On each entire typical strong stable or strong unstable leaf, every ambient Taylor coefficient has a smooth representative agreeing almost everywhere with the regular construction. These representatives are holonomic: differentiating along the leaf gives the corresponding higher ambient coefficients. The analogous assertion holds on typical weak leaves, using flow transport. \item At every finite order the local representatives, their bounds, and positive radii can be chosen measurably. On compact plaque subboxes one may restrict to positive-measure families with uniform finite-order bounds. No common convergence radius for all orders is asserted. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.label: pre:entropy-forms
primaryStatements.text: The potential $-J$ has pressure zero and Liouville volume is an equilibrium state for it. If $h_{m_L}(\phi_1)=\htop(\phi_1)=h$, there is a Hölder function $F$ with flow derivative satisfying \begin{equation} J=h+XF. \end{equation} The function $F$ is smooth on weak unstable plaques, with uniform bounds at each finite leaf order. There are continuous horizontal $m$-forms $u,w$, with $u$ annihilating $\Eu$ and $w$ annihilating $\Es$, such that \begin{equation} \phi_t^*u=e^{-ht}u, \qquad \phi_t^*w=e^{ht}w, \qquad u\wedge w=c_*(d\alpha)^m, \quad c_*\ne0. \end{equation} The form $u$ has smooth uniformly bounded finite jets on weak unstable plaques, and $w$ has the analogous property on weak stable plaques. These leaf jets vary continuously in uniform plaque charts.

primaryStatements.label: pre:smooth-rigidity
primaryStatements.text: If $\Es$ and $\Eu$ are smooth on $SM$, then $(M,g)$ is locally symmetric.

primaryStatements.name: Finite arrays and higher kernels
primaryStatements.label: nf:finite-weight
primaryStatements.text: In either normalized tower, the independent coordinates introduced at level $j$ have weights at least $j\chi_*$ for a fixed $\chi_*>0$. A prescribed upper weight bound consequently uses only finitely many independent tower coordinates and finitely many monomials. On the array of monomials of a fixed weight $d$, normal substitution has the single exponent $-d$, and inverse substitution has exponent $d$, with two-sided estimates and arbitrarily small exponential slack. These estimates continue to hold for finite tensor arrays and their invariant subquotients, with the corresponding sums and differences of weights.

primaryStatements.label: hull:pairing
primaryStatements.text: Every sufficiently small unstable alternative and stable alternative through the center have the same wedge as the actual pair. This remains true for their affine spans.

primaryStatements.name: Dilation in the symmetry algebra
primaryStatements.label: sym:dilation
primaryStatements.text: In the coordinates of Lemma \ref{sym:graded-contact}, \begin{equation} H=-T+\theta_0(D),\qquad Z_H=D-T\partial_\tau \end{equation} belongs to $\mathfrak k\subset\mathfrak h$. The operator $\ad H$ on formal Hamiltonians is $D$ and is semisimple on every finite Taylor quotient, with real weights. Every closed $\ad H$-invariant linear subspace admits the continuous projections onto each individual weight. On a finite-dimensional continuous invariant subquotient, weight-zero vectors have weight-zero lifts. Moreover $\mathfrak h_0\subset\mathfrak k$, and $\xi$ vanishes on every nonzero weight space.

primaryStatements.name: Transitivity
primaryStatements.label: sym:transitivity
primaryStatements.text: At every regular center the map \[ \mathfrak h\longrightarrow T_0\R^{2m},\qquad p\longmapsto Y_p(0) \] is onto. It remains onto at every point of the smooth formal extensions on either entire typical axis.

definitions.label: nf:tempered
definitions.text: A measurable function $C\geq1$ on the regular set is tempered if \[ \lim_{|n|\to\infty}\frac{\log C(f^n v)}{|n|}=0. \] A positive radius is tempered when its reciprocal, increased to at least one, is tempered. An estimate with arbitrarily small exponential slack means that for every $\epsilon>0$ its prefactor can be chosen tempered, while its exponential rate increases by at most $\epsilon$.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: For some sufficiently large even integer $N$, the manifold $Q=S^9\times S^{N-1}$ admits a closed exact smoothly embedded Lagrangian $L\subset T^*Q$ such that $L$ is diffeomorphic to $Q$ and no compactly supported Hamiltonian isotopy carries the zero section to $L$.

primaryStatements.name: Waldhausen's tube fibration
primaryStatements.label: thm:tube-fibration
primaryStatements.text: For the stable smooth tube space \eqref{eq:stable-tubes} there is a homotopy fiber sequence \begin{equation} \Hs(*)\longrightarrow\T\xrightarrow{\gamma}BG. \end{equation} The rigid tube map $\iota:BO\to\T$, defined by nondegenerate quadratic forms, satisfies $\gamma\circ\iota\simeq BJ$, where $BJ:BO\to BG$ is the stable spherical fibration map.

primaryStatements.label: prop:kernel-class
primaryStatements.text: There exists \begin{equation} 0\ne a\in\pi_9\T,\qquad \gamma_*a=0. \end{equation} Moreover, $(BJ)_*:\pi_9BO\to\pi_9BG$ is injective.

primaryStatements.label: prop:one-critical
primaryStatements.text: Let $B=S^9$ and let $p\geq20$. Suppose that $f_b:\R^{2p}\to\R$, $b\in B$, is a smooth family satisfying the following conditions: \begin{enumerate} \item it is homogeneous at infinity, with smooth homogeneous data in $T_{p,p}$; \item each $f_b$ has exactly one critical point, which is nondegenerate and varies smoothly with $b$; \item the stable spherical class of the family at infinity is zero in $[B,BG]$. \end{enumerate} Then its stable tube class is zero in $[B,\T]$.

primaryStatements.label: prop:hcob-injectivity
primaryStatements.text: Let $k,l\geq20$, and put \[ Y=S^{k+l-1},\qquad \Sigma=\{q_{k,l}=0\}\cap Y\cong S^{k-1}\times S^{l-1}. \] For a closed collar embedding $e:\Sigma\times J\hookrightarrow Y$, the composite \begin{equation} H(\Sigma)\xrightarrow{\sigma}H(\Sigma\times J) \xrightarrow{e_!}H(Y)\longrightarrow\Hs(Y) \end{equation} induces an isomorphism on $\pi_9$ in the product component. Consequently, if a sphere family in $H(\Sigma)$ has null image under this composite, the family is itself null.

primaryStatements.label: prop:embedded-realization
primaryStatements.text: On $Q=B\times S^{N-1}$ there is a smooth Morse family $F:Q\times\R^N\to\R$ which equals $g_b(w)$ outside a uniform vertical ball and whose generating map is a diffeomorphism from its critical locus onto a closed exact embedded Lagrangian $L\subset T^*Q$. Its critical locus, and hence $L$, is diffeomorphic to $Q$. The infinity class on each slice $B\times\{v_0\}$ is the chosen class $a$.

papers.title: Deforming hypersymplectic four-manifolds to hyperkähler triples
papers.abstract: Every smooth normalized positive triple of closed two-forms on a closed connected oriented four-manifold admits a smooth deformation, with each cohomology class fixed, to a hyperkähler triple. This resolves Donaldson's hypersymplectic deformation conjecture.
papers.familySummary: Proves Donaldson's hypersymplectic deformation conjecture in a cohomology-preserving form. Every positive triple of smooth closed two-forms on a closed connected oriented four-manifold, normalized by $\int\omega_i\wedge\omega_j=\delta_{ij}$, deforms through positive closed triples to a hyperkähler triple while preserving all three cohomology classes. Any positive triple can first be normalized by a constant linear change.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let $X$ be a closed connected oriented smooth four-manifold, and let $\omega=(\omega_1,\omega_2,\omega_3)$ be a smooth hypersymplectic structure normalized by \begin{equation} \int_X\omega_i\wedge\omega_j=\delta_{ij}. \end{equation} There is a smooth family of hypersymplectic structures $\omega(t)$, $0\le t\le1$, such that \[ \omega(0)=\omega,\qquad [\omega_i(t)]=[\omega_i] \quad (i=1,2,3), \] and a positive volume form $\mu_1$ with \begin{equation} \omega_i(1)\wedge\omega_j(1)=2\delta_{ij}\mu_1. \end{equation} The endpoint forms are parallel and self-dual for a hyperk\"ahler metric.

primaryStatements.name: Individual K\"ahler realizations
primaryStatements.label: cor:individual-kahler
primaryStatements.text: Let $X$ be a closed connected oriented smooth four-manifold with a smooth positive triple $\omega$ of closed real two-forms. For every fixed $c\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$, the form $\alpha_c=\sum_i c_i\omega_i$ is a K\"ahler form for a parallel integrable complex structure $J_c$ of some hyperk\"ahler metric $g_c$ on $X$: \[ \alpha_c(v,w)=g_c(J_cv,w). \] The compatible structure is chosen separately for each $c$; no simultaneous transport of the triple is asserted.

primaryStatements.name: Smooth type
primaryStatements.label: cor:smooth-type
primaryStatements.text: Let $X$ be a closed connected smooth four-manifold admitting a smooth positive triple of closed real two-forms. Then $X$ is diffeomorphic to the standard K3 manifold or to $T^4$.

primaryStatements.label: prop:topology
primaryStatements.text: If $X$ carries a positive closed triple, then \[ b^+(X)=3,\qquad (b_1(X),b^-(X))=(0,19)\ \text{or}\ (4,3). \] The free integral intersection lattice is respectively $3H\oplus2(-E_8)$ or $3H$, where $H$ is the hyperbolic plane. Every almost-complex structure obtained from a definite pair in the triple has vanishing integral first Chern class.

primaryStatements.name: Angular energy
primaryStatements.label: prop:angular-energy
primaryStatements.text: In setup \textup{(A)} or \textup{(B)}, the correction satisfies $Q\in L^2(X,E)$ and \begin{equation} \iint_{\dist(y,z)<s}|\ell-\tau_{z\to y}m|^2 \,\dd\lambda(y,\ell)\dd\lambda(z,m)\le Cs^4. \end{equation} The estimates in \Cref{lem:current-positive-pairing,lem:current-commutator} hold for all the indicated submeasures, and, for every such fixed submeasure current $N'$, \begin{equation} \lim_{s\downarrow0}\langle S_sN',S_sQ\rangle_2=0. \end{equation} In fact the convergence in \Cref{eq:current-mixed-vanishing} is uniform over $\lambda'\le\lambda$.

primaryStatements.name: From taming to compatibility
primaryStatements.label: thm:tamed-compatible
primaryStatements.text: Let \(X\) be a closed connected smooth four-manifold and let \(J\) be a smooth almost complex structure, with its complex orientation. If a smooth symplectic form tames \(J\), then there is a smooth symplectic form compatible with \(J\).

primaryStatements.name: A curve criterion for taming classes
primaryStatements.label: thm:taming-cone
primaryStatements.text: Let \(X\) be a closed connected oriented smooth four-manifold with \(b^+(X)=3\), and let \(J\) be a smooth almost complex structure inducing the given orientation. Suppose that smooth closed real two-forms \(A,C\) span a pointwise definite plane and form a basis of the \(J\)-anti-invariant two-forms at every point. Set \[ V=[A]^\perp\cap[C]^\perp\subset H^2(X;\R). \] Suppose \(U\in V\) has positive square and contains a smooth form taming \(J\). If \(H\in V\) has positive square, belongs to the same component of \(\{v\in V:v^2>0\}\) as \(U\), and satisfies \[ H\cdot d>0 \] for every irreducible closed \(J\)-holomorphic curve of class \(d\), then \(H\) contains a smooth symplectic form taming \(J\).

primaryStatements.name: Integrated transverse estimate
primaryStatements.label: cor:density-transverse
primaryStatements.text: With the plane projection taken in \(T_yX\), one has \begin{equation} \mathcal T_s:= \int d\lambda(y,\ell) \int_{B_s(y)} \left|\operatorname{pr}_{\ell^\perp} \exp_y^{-1}(z)/s\right|^2\,d\mu(z) =o(s^2). \end{equation}

definitions.text: A pair $(A,C)$ of real two-forms is definite if its wedge-product matrix is positive definite at every point. A two-form $B$ tames an almost-complex structure $J$ if $B(v,Jv)>0$ for every nonzero tangent vector $v$. It is compatible if, in addition, $B(Ju,Jv)=B(u,v)$. When these forms are called symplectic, closedness is included.

papers.title: Taming implies compatibility on four-manifolds
papers.abstract: We prove that every smooth almost complex structure on a closed four-manifold which is tamed by a symplectic form is compatible with a symplectic form. This gives a positive solution to Donaldson's tamed-to-compatible conjecture. We also characterize the compatible cone by strict intersection positivity on the closure of the invariant part of the taming cone.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Suppose that a smooth almost complex structure \(J\) on a closed connected smooth real four-manifold \(X\) is tamed by a symplectic form. Then there is a smooth symplectic form compatible with \(J\).

primaryStatements.name: Taming and compatible cones
primaryStatements.label: thm:taming-cones
primaryStatements.text: Let \(X,J\) satisfy the hypotheses of Theorem \ref{thm:main}, and give \(X\) the orientation induced by \(J\). Let \(\mathcal K_J^t,\mathcal K_J^c\subset H^2(X;\R)\) be the classes represented by taming and compatible symplectic forms, respectively. Let \(H_J^-\) be the subspace represented by smooth closed real anti-invariant two-forms. Set \[ \mathcal V=(H_J^-)^\perp,\qquad \mathcal C=\mathcal K_J^t\cap\mathcal V, \] where orthogonality is for the intersection pairing. Then \begin{align} \mathcal K_J^t&=\mathcal C+H_J^-,\\ \mathcal K_J^c&= \{a\in\mathcal C:\ a\cdot y>0 \text{ for every }0\ne y\in\overline{\mathcal C}\}. \end{align} The closure is taken in \(\mathcal V\), and the sum in \eqref{eq:tame-decomposition} is a Minkowski sum.

primaryStatements.label: cor:taming-cones
primaryStatements.text: Under the same hypotheses, write \(h_J^-=\dim H_J^-\) and let \(b_2^+(X)\) be the positive index of the intersection form. If \(h_J^-=b_2^+(X)-1\), then \[ \mathcal K_J^t=\mathcal K_J^c+H_J^-. \] In particular, if \(b_2^+(X)=1\), then \(\mathcal K_J^t=\mathcal K_J^c\): every taming class has a smooth compatible symplectic representative.

primaryStatements.label: prop:separation
primaryStatements.text: If \(J\) admits no compatible symplectic form, there are currents \(P,Q,T\) and a finite positive measure \(\lambda\) on \(\mathscr C\) such that \begin{align} P(\alpha)&=\int_{\mathscr C}\alpha_x(\ell)\dd\lambda(x,\ell), &\lambda(\mathscr C)&=1,\\ T&=P+Q, &RP&=0,\quad RQ=Q,\quad *Q=Q,\\ T(\alpha)&=0&&\text{for every smooth closed two-form }\alpha. \end{align} The current \(P\) annihilates every closed invariant two-form. The projection \(\mu\) of \(\lambda\) to \(X\) is the trace measure of \(P\): for every smooth function \(b\), \(P(bF)=\int_Xb\dd\mu\). Each of \(P,Q,T\) belongs to \(H^{-3}\).

primaryStatements.label: prop:growth
primaryStatements.text: There is a constant \(C\) such that \begin{equation} \mu(B_s(x))\le Cs^2 \end{equation} for all \(x\in X\) and \(s>0\).

primaryStatements.label: prop:energy
primaryStatements.text: The correction \(Q\) belongs to \(L^2\), and \begin{equation} \ang_r:= \iint_{d_g(x,y)<r}|\ell-\tau_{yx}m|^2 \dd\lambda(x,\ell)\dd\lambda(y,m)\le Cr^4. \end{equation} For every positive current \(P'\) represented by \(\lambda'\le\lambda\), \begin{equation} \lim_{r\downarrow0}\ip{S_rP'}{*S_rQ}_{L^2}=0. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Closedness of the positive-density part
primaryStatements.label: thm:splitting
primaryStatements.text: Fix a smooth almost complex structure \(J\) and a \(J\)-Hermitian metric on a closed four-manifold. Suppose that \[ P(\alpha)=\int_{\mathscr C}\alpha_x(\ell)\dd\lambda(x,\ell) \] for a finite positive measure \(\lambda\), with projection \(\mu\). Suppose also that \(Q\in L^2\) is anti-invariant and that \(P+Q\) is a closed current. Assume the estimates \begin{align} \mu(B_r(x))&\le Cr^2,\\ \iint_{d_g(x,y)<r}|\ell-\tau_{yx}m|^2 \dd\lambda(x,\ell)\dd\lambda(y,m)&\le Cr^4 \end{align} for all sufficiently small \(r\), uniformly in \(x\). Then the limit \[ \theta(x)=\lim_{r\downarrow0}r^{-2}\mu(B_r(x)) \] exists at every point. If \(E=\{x:\theta(x)>0\}\), the current \(P_E=\ind_EP\) is closed.

primaryStatements.label: prop:class-estimates
primaryStatements.text: Suppose that \(P\ne0\) is positive, annihilates exact invariant forms, and \(T=P+Q\) is closed, where \(Q\in H^{-3}\) is anti-invariant. Write \(\lambda\) for a positive measure representing \(P\), and \(\mu\) for its trace. Then \begin{gather} \mu(B_s(x))\le Cs^2,\qquad Q\in L^2, \\ \iint_{d_g(x,y)<r}|\ell-\tau_{yx}m|^2 \dd\lambda(x,\ell)\dd\lambda(y,m)\le Cr^4. \end{gather} Consequently the positive-density restriction \(P_E\) is closed, where \(E=\{x:\lim_{s\downarrow0}s^{-2}\mu(B_s(x))>0\}\). If \(A\) is any positive current whose trace has quadratic growth, then \begin{equation} \lim_{r\downarrow0}\ip{S_rA}{*S_rQ}_{L^2}=0. \end{equation} Every closed positive current has quadratic trace growth.

papers.title: Symplectic Ball Packings in Higher Dimensions
papers.abstract: We prove that, for all integers n ≥ 3 and k ≥ 1 and all positive real capacities $R_1,\ldots,R_k$, the closed standard symplectic $2n$-balls of these capacities embed disjointly into the interior of a ball of capacity R > 0 if and only if $\displaystyle \sum_{i=1}^k R_i^n\lt R^n, \qquad R_i+R_j\lt R\quad(i\ne j).$ Capacity is π times the squared Euclidean radius, and each embedding is defined on a neighborhood of its closed source ball. This proves Siegel and Yao's Conjecture A.
papers.familySummary: Resolves the Siegel–Yao conjecture for arbitrary capacities in every dimension $2n\ge6$. Finitely many closed symplectic balls of capacities $R_1,\ldots,R_k$ embed disjointly into an open ball of capacity R exactly when $\sum_iR_i^n\lt R^n$ and $R_i+R_j\lt R$ for every distinct pair i, j.
papers.subject: Differential geometry
papers.sourceAbstract: We prove that, for all integers \(n\ge3\) and \(k\ge1\) and all positive real capacities \(R_1,\ldots,R_k\), the closed standard symplectic \(2n\)-balls of these capacities embed disjointly into the interior of a ball of capacity \(R>0\) if and only if \[ \sum_{i=1}^k R_i^n<R^n, \qquad R_i+R_j<R\quad(i\ne j). \] Capacity is \(\pi\) times the squared Euclidean radius, and each embedding is defined on a neighborhood of its closed source ball. This proves Siegel and Yao's Conjecture A.

primaryStatements.label: intro:main
primaryStatements.text: Let \(n\ge3\) and \(k\ge1\) be integers. For positive real numbers \(R,R_1,\ldots,R_k\), there exists a symplectic embedding \[ \bigsqcup_{i=1}^k B^{2n}(R_i) \hookrightarrow \Int B^{2n}(R) \] if and only if \begin{equation} \sum_{i=1}^k R_i^n<R^n, \qquad R_i+R_j<R\quad (1\le i<j\le k). \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Normal-cone transfer
primaryStatements.label: geo:transfer
primaryStatements.text: Let \(T\) be a smooth projective manifold, \(Z\subset T\) a smooth closed submanifold of positive codimension, possibly disconnected, and \(L\) an ample rational polarization. Let \[ T'=\Bl_ZT,\qquad Y=\PP_Z(\mathbf1\oplus N_{Z/T}),\qquad D_\infty=\PP_Z(N_{Z/T})\subset Y. \] Write \(E_Z\) for the exceptional divisor on \(T'\); when \(Z\) is a divisor, \(T'\simeq T\) and \(E_Z\) means \(Z\). Suppose \(d>0\) is rational and \[ \pi^*L-dE_Z\quad\hbox{on }T', \qquad L|_Z+dU\quad\hbox{on }Y \] are ample. Let \(F\subset T\) be a finite union of pairwise disjoint smooth closed complex submanifolds. Assume the inverse image of \(F\cap Z\) under \(Y\to Z\) is also a finite union of pairwise disjoint smooth complex submanifolds; the empty union is allowed. Let \(\omega_T\) be any K\"ahler form in class \(L\), and let \(\omega_Y\) be a K\"ahler form in class \(L|_Z+dU\), invariant under scalar rotation of the normal summand. Then every compact subset of \[ Y\setminus\bigl(D_\infty\cup\pi_Y^{-1}(F\cap Z)\bigr) \] has a neighborhood admitting a symplectic embedding into \((T\setminus F,\omega_T)\), with its given form \(\omega_Y\). In particular any compact packing there transfers with neighborhood embeddings.

primaryStatements.label: app:small
primaryStatements.text: Let $n\ge3$, and let $\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_k$ be positive real numbers with \[ \rho_i<\tfrac12\quad(1\le i\le k),\qquad \sum_{i=1}^k\rho_i^n<1. \] Then the closed balls of capacities $\rho_i$ admit a disjoint symplectic packing into $\Int B^{2n}(1)$, with embeddings defined on neighborhoods of the closed source balls.

primaryStatements.label: app:large
primaryStatements.text: Let $n\ge4$, let $A\ge1/2$, and let $\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_k>0$ satisfy \[ A^n+\sum_i\rho_i^n<1,\qquad A+\rho_i<1\quad(1\le i\le k). \] Then the closed ball of capacity $A$ and the closed balls of capacities $\rho_i$ admit a disjoint symplectic packing into $\Int B^{2n}(1)$, with embeddings on neighborhoods of all source balls.

primaryStatements.label: six:large
primaryStatements.text: Let \(R_0,R_1,\ldots,R_k>0\), with \(R_0\ge1/2\), satisfy \[ \sum_{i=0}^k R_i^3<1,\qquad R_i+R_j<1\quad(i\ne j). \] Then the disjoint union of their closed six-dimensional balls embeds symplectically into the open ball of capacity one, with each embedding defined on a neighborhood of its closed source.

lean.scopeText:
The formalization proves Siegel and Yao's ball-packing criterion in every symplectic dimension $2n$ with $n\ge3$. For $k\ge1$ closed standard balls of positive capacities $R_1,\ldots,R_k$, disjoint symplectic embeddings into the interior of a ball of capacity $R$ exist exactly when
$\sum_i R_i^n<R^n$ and $R_i+R_j<R$ for all $i\ne j$.
Capacity is $\pi$ times squared Euclidean radius, and each embedding is defined on a neighborhood of its closed source ball. The linked statements include both the full equivalence and the necessity direction.

primaryStatements.name: The metric Blaschke theorem
primaryStatements.label: thm:blaschke
primaryStatements.text: Let $(M,g)$ be a connected closed smooth Riemannian manifold of positive dimension. If $\inj(M,g)=\diam(M,g)$, then $(M,g)$ is isometric, up to multiplication of the metric by a positive constant, to a round sphere, a standard real, complex or quaternionic projective space, or the Cayley plane.

primaryStatements.name: Sharp volume comparison
primaryStatements.label: thm:comparison
primaryStatements.text: Every Blaschke manifold and its model at the same diameter satisfy \[ \Vol(M,g)\ge\Vol(M_0,g_0). \] Equality holds if and only if $(M,g)$ is isometric to $(M_0,g_0)$.

primaryStatements.name: Reduction to an upper volume bound
primaryStatements.label: thm:volume-reduction
primaryStatements.text: If a Blaschke manifold has volume at most that of its model at the same diameter, then it is isometric to that model.

primaryStatements.name: Classical Blaschke structure
primaryStatements.label: geom:structure
primaryStatements.text: Every unit-speed geodesic is simply closed with period $2D$. For each $p\in M$, the map $v\mapsto\exp_p(Dv)$ from $S_pM$ onto the cut locus is a smooth sphere fibration whose fibers are great spheres of one dimension $k$, independent of $p$. Its differential has nullity $k$. The model is determined as follows: \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item If $k=n-1$, the model is a sphere; if $k=0$, it is a real projective space. In these two cases the metric classification is known: the manifold is isometric to its equally scaled model. \item If $0<k<n-1$, the manifold is simply connected and its integral cohomology ring has one generator of degree $k+1$. The possibilities are complex-projective type, quaternionic-projective type, and Cayley-plane type, with the dimensions listed below. \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.name: Jacobi determinant normalization
primaryStatements.label: lag:determinant
primaryStatements.text: Choose $G_x$- and $G_y$-orthonormal frames $Z_x=(Z_{x,1},\ldots,Z_{x,d})$ and $Z_y=(Z_{y,1},\ldots,Z_{y,d})$ of $L_x$ and $L_y$. Then \begin{equation} f(x,y)=\left|\det\bigl(\omega(Z_{x,a},Z_{y,b})\bigr)_{a,b=1}^d\right| \end{equation} is independent of these choices. It is continuous, symmetric in its arguments, and separately $T$-periodic. It is the absolute normal Jacobi determinant at $y$ of fields vanishing at $x$ with orthonormal initial derivatives there. In particular, for $0<y-x<D$ it is the polar volume density with respect to $dt$ and ordinary sphere area at $\gamma(x)$. Use the same orthonormal basis of $\dot\gamma(0)^\perp$ for the coordinates \[ (q,p)=(J(0),J'(0))\in\R^d\oplus\R^d, \] choosing its first $k$ vectors to be the initial derivatives of a basis of $L_0\cap L_D$. On \[ \mathcal I=(0,D)\cup(D,T) \] there is a smooth symmetric matrix $A(t)$ such that $L_t=\{(q,A(t)q):q\in\R^d\}$, and $A'(t)>0$. For $x,y\in\mathcal I$, \begin{equation} f(x,y)= \frac{|\det(A(y)-A(x))|} {\sqrt{\det A'(x)\det A'(y)}}. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Scalar profiles
primaryStatements.label: lag:profiles
primaryStatements.text: Define \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} h(t)&=\det(H'(t))^{1/m} &&(0<t<T),\\ s(t)&=\det(S(t))^{1/k} &&(t\in\mathcal I),\\ s_i(t)&=s(t+iD) &&(0<t<D,\ i=0,1). \end{aligned} \end{equation} The function $h$ is smooth and positive across $D$. There are positive constants $c_H,C_H,c_i,C_i$, depending on the fixed geodesic and its chart, such that \begin{align} c_H&\le h(t)\sin^2t\le C_H &&(0<t<T), \\ c_i&\le \frac{s_i(t)\sin^2(2t)}4\le C_i &&(0<t<D,\ i=0,1). \end{align} Equivalently, the logarithms of the ratios of $h$ to $1/\sin^2t$ and of $s_i$ to $4/\sin^2(2t)$ are bounded.

primaryStatements.name: Two Schur-complement bounds
primaryStatements.label: lag:schur
primaryStatements.text: The matrix $Q(x,y)$ is symmetric and satisfies \begin{equation} \det(\Delta A)=\det(\Delta H)\det Q(x,y),\qquad Q(y,x)=-Q(x,y). \end{equation} It extends continuously by zero to $y=x\in\mathcal I$, and \begin{equation} Q(u,u+D)=Q(u+D,u)=0\qquad(0<u<D). \end{equation} Whenever its distinct endpoints remain in $\mathcal I$, it obeys the positive-semidefinite matrix inequalities \begin{equation} \partial_yQ(x,y)\ge S(y),\qquad -\partial_xQ(x,y)\ge S(x). \end{equation} Consequently, for every $0<u<v<D$ and $i,j\in\{0,1\}$, \begin{align} Q(u+iD,v+jD)&\ge\int_u^v S(t+jD)\,dt, \\ Q(u+iD,v+jD)&\ge\int_u^v S(t+iD)\,dt. \end{align} In particular, this $Q$ is positive definite for all four choices of $i,j$, including $i=1,j=0$.

primaryStatements.name: Scalar block bounds
primaryStatements.label: lag:block-bounds
primaryStatements.text: With the profiles of Proposition \ref{lag:profiles}, every pair of distinct chart endpoints satisfies \begin{equation} f_H(x,y)^{1/m}\ge \frac{\left|\int_x^y h(t)\,dt\right|}{\sqrt{h(x)h(y)}}. \end{equation} For $0<u<v<D$ and $i,j\in\{0,1\}$ one has \begin{equation} f_K(u+iD,v+jD)^{1/k}\ge \frac{ \left(\int_u^v s_i(t)\,dt\right)^{1/2} \left(\int_u^v s_j(t)\,dt\right)^{1/2}} {\sqrt{s_i(u)s_j(v)}}. \end{equation} Together with endpoint exchange, these bounds cover the full square $(0,T)^2$ except the chart, diagonal, and cut lines, a set of planar measure zero.

papers.title: Infinitely many closed geodesic images on every Riemannian sphere
papers.abstract: We resolve the sphere case of the closed-geodesic infinitude problem: every smooth Riemannian metric on the standard sphere Sn, n ≥ 2, has infinitely many prime closed geodesics with pairwise distinct images. The two-sphere case is classical; the result in higher dimensions includes degenerate metrics. Using finite covers and theorems of Perelman and Rademacher–Taimanov, we also obtain the same conclusion for every smooth Riemannian metric on a nonempty closed smooth three-manifold.
papers.familySummary: Proves that every smooth Riemannian metric on Sn, n ≥ 2, has infinitely many prime closed geodesics with pairwise distinct images. The same conclusion holds on every closed manifold admitting a finite smooth spherical cover and on every closed three-manifold, without orientability or nondegeneracy restrictions.

papers.sourceAbstract: We resolve the sphere case of the closed-geodesic infinitude problem: every smooth Riemannian metric on the standard sphere $S^n$, $n\ge2$, has infinitely many prime closed geodesics with pairwise distinct images. The two-sphere case is classical; the result in higher dimensions includes degenerate metrics. Using finite covers and theorems of Perelman and Rademacher--Taimanov, we also obtain the same conclusion for every smooth Riemannian metric on a nonempty closed smooth three-manifold.
