primaryStatements.name: Convexity of injectivity domains
primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: If $(M,g)$ satisfies \eqref{eq:weak-mtw}, then $I(x)$ is convex for every $x\in M$. More precisely, for every $v_0,v_1\in I(x)$ and $\theta\in[0,1]$, \[ (1-\theta)v_0+\theta v_1\in I(x). \]

primaryStatements.name: Convex injectivity domains
primaryStatements.label: geo:convexity
primaryStatements.text: For every $x$, both $G_x$ and $I(x)$ are convex.

primaryStatements.name: Global support and intermediate geometry
primaryStatements.label: thm:foundation
primaryStatements.text: Under \eqref{eq:weak-mtw}, every potential $u$, with its dual potential $v$, has the following properties. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item Every $p\in\partial u(x)$ belongs to $G_x$ and satisfies \[ u(x')\geq u(x)+c(x,\exp_xp)-c(x',\exp_xp) \qquad(x'\in M). \] For every $0<t<1$, the map $F_t:\Gamma_u\to M$, $F_t(x,p)=\exp_x(tp)$, is a homeomorphism; $tp\in I(x)$ and $x$ is the unique global minimizing pole of $Q_tu$ at $F_t(x,p)$. \item For every dual pair $(u,v)$, every $x$ and every $r$, the lifted section \[ \mathcal S_x(r)=\left\{p\in G_x: u(x)+\frac{|p|^2}{2}+v(\exp_xp)\leq r\right\} \] is compact and convex. If it is nonempty and $r\geq0$, then \[ \operatorname{diam}\mathcal S_x(r)^2 \leq8\left(r+\osc_{p\in\mathcal S_x(r)}v(\exp_xp)\right). \] \item For $0<t<1$, one has $Q_tu=-Q_{1-t}v\in C^{1,1}(M)$. Its $C^{1,1}$ seminorm and the Lipschitz constants of the pole and momentum maps $F_t^{-1}$ depend only on $M,g,t$. There are also $r_t,b_t>0$, depending only on $M,g,t$, such that, for $z=F_t(x,p)$, \[ u(x')+\frac{c(x',z)}t \geq u(x)+\frac{c(x,z)}t+b_t d(x,x')^2 \quad\text{if }d(x,x')<r_t. \] These constants can be chosen uniformly on compact subintervals of $(0,1)$. \end{enumerate} No density hypothesis is required.

primaryStatements.label: prop:segment-nonconjugacy
primaryStatements.text: Suppose that $[b_0,b_1]\subset G_x$ and that $b_0,b_1$ are nonconjugate. Then every velocity in $[b_0,b_1]$ is nonconjugate.

primaryStatements.name: Nonconjugacy of a minimizing convex hull
primaryStatements.label: geo:first-cut
primaryStatements.text: Let $a_1,\ldots,a_m\in T_xM$ be nonconjugate velocities, with $m\geq1$, and suppose \[ K=\operatorname{co}\{a_1,\ldots,a_m\}\subset G_x. \] Then every velocity in $K$ is nonconjugate.

primaryStatements.name: Global supporting property
primaryStatements.label: geo:support
primaryStatements.text: For every potential $u$, every $x\in M$, and every $p\in\partial u(x)$, one has $p\in G_x$ and \begin{equation} u(x')\geq u(x)+c(x,\exp_xp)-c(x',\exp_xp) \qquad\text{for all }x'\in M. \end{equation} For each $0<t<1$, the projection $F_t:\Gamma_u\to M$ is a homeomorphism; its vectors $tp$ lie in $I(x)$, and its poles are the unique global minimizers of $Q_tu$.

primaryStatements.name: Convex lifted gap sections
primaryStatements.label: geo:sections
primaryStatements.text: Let $(u,v)$ be a dual pair and define \[ \mathcal S_x(r)=\left\{p\in G_x: u(x)+\frac{|p|^2}{2}+v(\exp_xp)\leq r\right\}. \] Every such set is compact and convex, including its ordinary and conjugate cut endpoints. If it is nonempty and $r\geq0$, then \begin{equation} \operatorname{diam}\mathcal S_x(r)^2 \leq 8\left(r+ \osc_{p\in\mathcal S_x(r)}v(\exp_xp)\right). \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Intermediate regularity and pole control
primaryStatements.label: geo:intermediate
primaryStatements.text: Let $(u,v)$ be a dual pair and $0<t<1$. Then \begin{equation} Q_tu=-Q_{1-t}v\in C^{1,1}(M). \end{equation} The $C^{1,1}$ seminorm is bounded solely in terms of $M,g,t$. If $(x_t(z),p_t(z))=F_t^{-1}(z)$ and $\Phi_s$ denotes geodesic flow on $TM$, then \begin{equation} (x_t(z),p_t(z)) =\Phi_{-t}(z,\grad Q_tu(z)), \qquad x_t(z)=\exp_z(-t\grad Q_tu(z)). \end{equation} In particular the pole and momentum are Lipschitz, with constants depending only on $M,g,t$. There are also $r_t,b_t>0$, depending only on $M,g,t$, such that every projected pair $z=\exp_x(tp)$ satisfies \begin{equation} u(x')+c_t(x',z) \geq u(x)+c_t(x,z)+b_t d(x,x')^2 \qquad\text{if }d(x,x')<r_t. \end{equation} These assertions use no density hypothesis. On every compact subinterval of $(0,1)$, their constants can be chosen uniformly.

lean.scopeText:
On a compact connected smooth Riemannian manifold of dimension at least two, the formalized result proves that weak MTW curvature implies convexity of every open tangent injectivity domain. Prior convexity or nonfocality is not assumed. Additional formalized results give global support at ordinary subgradients, compact convex lifted gap sections with the stated diameter bound, and scale and local-injectivity estimates for finite target families. The latter finite-family result does not cover the paper's arbitrary-potential local-injectivity assertion.

The formalized result gives uniform bi-Hölder optimal transport for squared-distance cost on each fixed compact connected smooth Riemannian manifold of dimension at least two satisfying weak MTW. For probability densities between fixed positive lower and finite upper bounds, one exponent and constant work for every pair of densities. The optimal map is a homeomorphism, is unique almost everywhere, and both it and its inverse satisfy the global Hölder bound. The constants are uniform over the density class on the fixed manifold, not over varying metrics.

papers.title: Uniform Bi-Holder Transport from Weak MTW
papers.abstract: We prove that the weak Ma–Trudinger–Wang condition on a fixed smooth connected compact boundaryless Riemannian manifold of dimension at least two implies a common Hölder estimate for optimal transport maps and their inverses over the entire class of probability densities with fixed positive upper and lower bounds. The maps have homeomorphic representatives, conjugate cut points are allowed, and no density regularity is assumed.
papers.familySummary: On every closed connected Riemannian manifold of dimension at least two satisfying weak Ma–Trudinger–Wang curvature, all tangent injectivity domains are convex, resolving Villani’s conjecture in this setting. For squared-distance transport between measurable probability densities bounded above and away from zero, the optimal map and its inverse are Hölder continuous.

primaryStatements.name: Uniform bi-H\"older transport
primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Fix $(M,g)$ as above and $0<\lambda\leq\Lambda<\infty$ for which the following density class is nonempty. There are $\alpha\in(0,1]$ and $C<\infty$, depending only on $(M,g),\lambda,\Lambda$, such that the following holds for every pair of measurable densities satisfying \[ \int_M\rho_i\,d\vol=1,\qquad \lambda\leq\rho_i\leq\Lambda\quad\vol\text{-almost everywhere}, \qquad i=0,1. \] The almost-everywhere unique optimal map from $\rho_0\vol$ to $\rho_1\vol$ for the cost $c$ has a homeomorphic representative $\widetilde T:M\to M$, and \[ d(\widetilde T(x),\widetilde T(x'))\leq C d(x,x')^\alpha, \qquad d(\widetilde T^{-1}(y),\widetilde T^{-1}(y')) \leq C d(y,y')^\alpha \] for all $x,x',y,y'\in M$.

primaryStatements.name: Convex injectivity domains
primaryStatements.label: geo:convexity
primaryStatements.text: Both $G_x$ and $I(x)$ are convex for every $x\in M$.

primaryStatements.name: Global supporting property
primaryStatements.label: geo:support
primaryStatements.text: For every potential $u$, every $x\in M$, and every $p\in\partial u(x)$, one has $p\in G_x$ and \[ u(x')\geq u(x)+c(x,\exp_xp)-c(x',\exp_xp) \qquad(x'\in M). \] For each $0<t<1$, $F_t:\Gamma_u\to M$ is a homeomorphism, $tp\in I(x)$, and its poles are the unique global minimizers of $Q_tu$.

primaryStatements.name: Convex lifted gap sections
primaryStatements.label: geo:sections
primaryStatements.text: For a dual pair $(u,v)$, each set \[ \mathcal S_x(r)=\left\{p\in G_x: u(x)+\frac{|p|^2}{2}+v(\exp_xp)\leq r\right\} \] is compact and convex, including ordinary and conjugate cut endpoints. If it is nonempty and $r\geq0$, then \[ \operatorname{diam}\mathcal S_x(r)^2 \leq8\left(r+\osc_{p\in\mathcal S_x(r)}v(\exp_xp)\right). \]

primaryStatements.name: Intermediate regularity and pole control
primaryStatements.label: geo:intermediate
primaryStatements.text: Let $(u,v)$ be a dual pair and $0<t<1$. Then $Q_tu=-Q_{1-t}v\in C^{1,1}(M)$, with almost-everywhere bounds \[ -\frac{C_g}{1-t}g\leq\Hess Q_tu\leq\frac{C_g}{t}g. \] If $(x_t(z),p_t(z))=F_t^{-1}(z)$ and $\Phi_s$ is geodesic flow on $TM$, then \[ (x_t(z),p_t(z))=\Phi_{-t}(z,\grad Q_tu(z)). \] In particular, the pole and momentum maps are Lipschitz with constants depending only on $M,g,t$. There are also $r_t,b_t>0$, depending only on $M,g,t$, such that every $z=\exp_x(tp)$, $p\in\partial u(x)$, satisfies \[ u(x')+c_t(x',z)\geq u(x)+c_t(x,z)+b_t d(x,x')^2 \qquad\text{if }d(x,x')<r_t. \] All these constants are uniform when $t$ ranges in a compact subinterval of $(0,1)$.

primaryStatements.name: Radial comparison of exponential determinants
primaryStatements.label: spec:radial-determinants
primaryStatements.text: With a constant depending only on $(M,g)$, if $v\in G_x$ and $1/2\le\theta\le1$, then \begin{equation} \sigma_x(\theta v)\ge c\sigma_x(v). \end{equation} Suppose $y=\exp_xp$, $p\in G_x$, and $\bar p=-P_{x\to y}p$. If $l\in[1/2,1)$ and $\bar p/l\in G_y$, then \begin{equation} \sigma_y(\bar p/l)\le C\sigma_x(p). \end{equation} If $l_+\in[1,2]$, then \begin{equation} \sigma_y(\bar p/l_+)\ge c\sigma_x(p). \end{equation} Comparison \eqref{spec:center-true-det} permits the longer reversed vector $\bar p/l$ to have a conjugate endpoint.

primaryStatements.name: Barycentric configurations
primaryStatements.label: spec:outward
primaryStatements.text: Assume weak MTW and the convexity of $G_x$ established in Corollary \ref{geo:convexity}. Fix $\mu\in(0,1)$ and positive constants $\kappa,L_0$. Suppose \[ p=\sum_{i=1}^N m_i p_i,\qquad p_i\in G_x,\quad m_i>0,\quad\sum_i m_i=1, \] and for one index $i$ there are $D>0$, a unit vector $e$, and $t_i>0$ such that \begin{equation} p_i=p+t_i e,\quad h:=p\cdot e>0,\quad h^2\ge\kappa D,\quad |p_i|^2-|p|^2\le L_0D,\quad m_i\ge\mu. \end{equation} Then \begin{equation} \sigma_x(p)\ge c\sigma_x(p_i), \end{equation} where $c>0$ depends only on $(M,g),\mu,\kappa,L_0$.

primaryStatements.name: The limiting matrix configuration
primaryStatements.label: jet:determinants
primaryStatements.text: Fix the center template and the constants of Lemmas \ref{sc:excess}, \ref{sc:maximum}, \ref{sc:parameter}, and \ref{sc:outward}. Choose $K$, then an outer template with curvature less than $-K$ in the prescribed capped region. For all sufficiently small scales in the sequence of Lemma \ref{sc:plateau}, there are a parameter $b\in[b_-,b_+]$, a pole $x$, center and active logs $p,p_i\in G_x$, weights $m_i>0$ summing to one, and symmetric matrices $H,L,V,V_i$ on $T_xM$, with the following properties. For one selected index $i$, \begin{gather} p=\sum_jm_jp_j,\qquad E=\Span\{p_j-p\}=\R e,\qquad |e|=1,\quad q=p\cdot e>0,\quad q^2\ge cD, \\ m_i\ge m_*>0,\qquad p_i=p+d_ie,\quad d_i>0, \\ L\ge0,\qquad LE=0,\qquad H\le L,\qquad H\ge V+c\frac bD\Id-C\frac b{D^2}pp^*,\qquad V>0, \\ V_i\ge m_iL+cK\frac b{D^2}p_ip_i^*,\qquad V_i>0. \end{gather} The center modified log and the selected outer modified log are nonconjugate. Let $r$ and $r_i$ denote the reverse logs of these specified rays, let $y=\exp_xp$, $y_i=\exp_xp_i$, and set $l=\varphi_c'(v(y))$, $l_i=\varphi_o'(v(y_i))$. The chosen true limiting branches are also nonconjugate, and \begin{equation} \det V\ge c\,\frac{\sigma_x(p)^2}{\sigma_y(r/l)}, \qquad \det V_i\le C\,\frac{\sigma_x(p_i)^2}{\sigma_{y_i}(r_i/l_i)}. \end{equation} Here $c,C,m_*$ are independent of $K$ and the outer template. The level and norm-increment conclusions of Lemma \ref{sc:outward} hold as well.

lean.scopeText:
On a compact connected smooth Riemannian manifold of dimension at least two, the formalized result proves that weak MTW curvature implies convexity of every open tangent injectivity domain. Prior convexity or nonfocality is not assumed. Additional formalized results give global support at ordinary subgradients, compact convex lifted gap sections with the stated diameter bound, and scale and local-injectivity estimates for finite target families. The latter finite-family result does not cover the paper's arbitrary-potential local-injectivity assertion.

The formalized result gives uniform bi-Hölder optimal transport for squared-distance cost on each fixed compact connected smooth Riemannian manifold of dimension at least two satisfying weak MTW. For probability densities between fixed positive lower and finite upper bounds, one exponent and constant work for every pair of densities. The optimal map is a homeomorphism, is unique almost everywhere, and both it and its inverse satisfy the global Hölder bound. The constants are uniform over the density class on the fixed manifold, not over varying metrics.

papers.title: A counterexample to integer-degree harmonic dimension comparison
papers.abstract: For some even n ≥ 8 and integer k ≥ 2, we construct a complete smooth metric on ℝn with nonnegative Ricci curvature whose space of real harmonic functions of pointwise polynomial growth at most k has dimension larger than the Euclidean harmonic-polynomial dimension. The metric is Euclidean near the origin, has asymptotic volume ratio strictly between zero and one, and has nonunique tangent cones at infinity. This answers the integer-degree form of Yau's dimension comparison question in the negative.
papers.familySummary: Disproves Yau's proposed Euclidean dimension bound for harmonic functions of integer growth on manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature. For every sufficiently large integer k, a complete smooth metric on ℝ3 has at least $(k+2)^2$ independent harmonic functions of growth at most k, exceeding the Euclidean count $(k+1)^2$. The metric may depend on k.

The metric is Euclidean near the origin, has asymptotic volume ratio strictly between zero and one, and has nonunique tangent cones at infinity. This answers the integer-degree form of Yau's dimension comparison question in the negative.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: There are an even integer $n\geq8$, an integer $k\geq2$, and a complete smooth metric $g$ on $\mathbb R^n$ such that $\operatorname{Ric}_g\geq0$ and \[ h_k(\mathbb R^n,g)>h_k(\mathbb R^n,g_{\mathrm E}). \] The metric is Euclidean near the origin, and its asymptotic volume ratio satisfies \[ 0<\lim_{R\to\infty} \frac{\operatorname{vol}_g B_g(0,R)}{\omega_nR^n}<1, \] where $\omega_n$ is the volume of the Euclidean unit ball.

primaryStatements.name: Simultaneous control
primaryStatements.label: prop:control
primaryStatements.text: Fix positive numbers \(\kappa_l\), \(2\leq l\leq L\). As \(J\) ranges over all orthogonal complex structures on \(\mathbb R^{2s}\), the tuples \begin{equation} X_J=\bigl(\kappa_l(D_J^2|_{V_l})_{\mathrm{tf}}\bigr)_{l=2}^L \end{equation} generate, under real linear combinations and brackets, the full Lie algebra \[ \bigoplus_{l=2}^L\mathfrak{sl}(V_l). \]

primaryStatements.name: A finite word with invertible differential
primaryStatements.label: prop:word
primaryStatements.text: Let \(d=\sum_{l=2}^L(N_l^2-1)\). There exist finitely many orthogonal complex structures \(J_1,\ldots,J_R\), an open neighborhood \(U\) of zero in \(\mathbb R^d\), and smooth real functions \(c_1,\ldots,c_R\) on \(U\) such that \[ \mathcal W(h)= \exp(c_R(h)X_{J_R})\cdots\exp(c_1(h)X_{J_1}) \] satisfies \(\mathcal W(0)=\Pi\), and \[ D\mathcal W(0):\mathbb R^d\longrightarrow T_\Pi\mathcal G \] is an isomorphism. The same assertion holds for any prescribed target in \(\mathcal G\).

primaryStatements.label: prop:metric
primaryStatements.text: For the fixed spectral data above, there are a smooth function \(a:\R\to(0,1]\) and an index \(j_{\rm geom}\) such that, for every \(j_0\geq j_{\rm geom}\), every sequence \((h_j)_{j\geq j_0}\) in \(K\), used in the preceding scheme, defines a smooth complete metric on \(\R^{m+1}\) with nonnegative Ricci curvature: \[ g=dr^2+r^2\gamma(\log r),\qquad \gamma(t)=G(a(t),q(t),J(t)). \] The function \(a\) is identically \(1\) for \(t\leq2\), decreases to \(a_*\), and, for some \(\mu>0\), satisfies \begin{equation} b(t):=\frac{a'(t)}{a(t)} =-\mu(1+t)^{-5/4}\quad(t\geq4), \qquad \log\frac{a(t)}{a_*}=4\mu(1+t)^{-1/4}\quad(t\geq4). \end{equation} The metric is Euclidean near the origin, and its distance from the origin is exactly \(r\). Its volume form is \[ d\operatorname{vol}_g =r^m a(\log r)^m\,dr\,d\operatorname{vol}_{g_0}. \] The function \(a\) and the starting index \(j_0\) can be chosen independently of the sequence of control parameters.

primaryStatements.name: Exact full-period transmission
primaryStatements.label: prop:transmission
primaryStatements.text: For finite spectral data as specified at the end of Section \ref{sec:counting}, choose the word and compact pulse family above. There are a starting index \(j_0\) and parameters \(h_j\in K\), for every \(j\geq j_0\), such that the center-regular value transmissions of the resulting metric satisfy \begin{equation} \mathcal T_{l,j}=s_{l,j}D_{l,j}\Pi_l,\qquad s_{l,j}>0,\qquad |\log s_{l,j}|\leq C T_j \quad(2\leq l\leq L,\ j\geq j_0). \end{equation} The positive diagonal matrices \(D_{l,j}\) propagate the reference Cauchy data \((I,\theta_l I)\) over the entire leg following the pulse; they satisfy \eqref{eq:diagonal-growth}. The regular value equation has the bounds \eqref{eq:riccati-barriers}. All estimates used to choose \(j_0\) are uniform over preceding admitted controls for this fixed finite family.

primaryStatements.name: Cone geometry and the union of degrees
primaryStatements.label: prop:cone-consequences
primaryStatements.text: Let \(g\) be the metric constructed in the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:main}, with link parameters \(a_*,q_*\) and comparison integer \(k\). Every cone with link \(G(a_*,q,J_0)\), \(1\leq q\leq q_*\), occurs as a pointed tangent cone at infinity. In particular the tangent cone is not unique. The metric \(g\) is not locally conformally flat. If \(\mathcal D(M)\) denotes the union of nonnegative homogeneous harmonic degrees over all its tangent cones, then \(\mathcal D(M)\) contains a half-line and a neighborhood of \(k\).

lean.scopeText: The formalized result disproves the proposed Euclidean upper comparison for dimensions of harmonic functions with integer polynomial growth. It constructs one complete smooth metric with nonnegative Ricci curvature on an even-dimensional Euclidean space, Euclidean near the origin and with asymptotic volume ratio strictly between zero and one, admitting more independent harmonic functions of the prescribed growth degree than the Euclidean count. The construction uses dimension $16$ and degree $50000$. Separate tangent-cone and cone-spectrum conclusions are not included.

papers.title: A Three-Dimensional Counterexample to Integer-Degree Harmonic Dimension Comparison
papers.abstract: For every $4/9\lt v\lt 1$ and $1\lt c\lt 9v/4$, all sufficiently large integers k admit a complete smooth metric on ℝ3 with nonnegative Ricci curvature, asymptotic volume ratio v, and at least $c(k+1)^2$ linearly independent real harmonic functions of pointwise growth at most k. This answers Yau's integer-degree dimension comparison question negatively in dimension three, with a fixed-factor excess over the Euclidean count. For each $1\lt c\lt 9/4$, these metrics can be chosen arbitrarily close to the Euclidean metric in global bi-Lipschitz distance. The metric may depend on k.

primaryStatements.label: n:main
primaryStatements.text: For every \(v\in(4/9,1)\) and \(c\in(1,9v/4)\), there is an integer \(k_0(v,c)\) such that for every integer \(k\geq k_0(v,c)\) there is a complete smooth metric \(g_k\) on \(\mathbb R^3\), Euclidean near the origin, with \(\operatorname{Ric}_{g_k}\geq0\), \(\operatorname{AVR}(g_k)=v\), and \[ h_k(\mathbb R^3,g_k)\geq c(k+1)^2>(k+1)^2 =h_k(\mathbb R^3,g_{\mathrm E}). \] The Ricci curvature is positive outside a compact set. The metric has uncountably many pairwise nonisometric pointed tangent cones at infinity. There are points tending to infinity and planes containing the radial direction at those points whose sectional curvature is negative. The metric is chosen after \(k\) and may depend on it.

primaryStatements.label: n:near-euclidean
primaryStatements.text: For every \(\epsilon>0\) and \(1<c<9/4\), all sufficiently large integers \(k\) admit metrics with the conclusions of Theorem \ref{n:main} and \[ (1+\epsilon)^{-2}g_{\mathrm E}\leq g_k \leq(1+\epsilon)^2g_{\mathrm E} \qquad\text{on }\mathbb R^3. \] Their asymptotic volume ratio can be prescribed arbitrarily close to \(1\). In particular, the identity map is globally \((1+\epsilon)\)-bi-Lipschitz.

primaryStatements.name: Angular program
primaryStatements.label: n:prop-angular-program
primaryStatements.text: Fix \(2/3<a<1\), \(1<\vartheta<3a/2\), and \(a^2<\kappa_*<1\). Prescribe a sufficiently small conformal neighborhood \(\mathcal U\) for which the curvature and comparison bounds above hold. For every sufficiently large integer \(k\), with threshold allowed to depend on \(\mathcal U\), there are \(S>0\) and a smooth \(S\)-periodic path \(w(s)\) in \(\mathcal U\) such that \(H(s)=h(w(s))\) has the following properties, with \(M,p,L,I,N\) as in \eqref{n:eq-band}. The phase origin can be chosen so that \(w(s)=w(0)\) for \(|s|<\varepsilon_0\), for some \(\varepsilon_0>0\), and \(h(w(0))\) is simple through position \(p+1\). \begin{enumerate} \item The area form is \(d\operatorname{vol}_{H(s)}=4\pi\,d\mu\) pointwise, and the ordered outer gap \(\lambda_p(H(s))<\lambda_{p+1}(H(s))\) holds for every \(s\). \item Along the unwrapped path \(s\in\mathbb R\), the spectral subspace of the first \(p\) positions has a smooth real \(L^2(d\mu)\)-orthonormal frame \(e_1(s),\ldots,e_p(s)\) of continued eigenlines. Their only equalities are isolated double crossings at distinct phases, and at each crossing the traceless first derivative of its \(2\times2\) cluster matrix is nonzero. The return permutation after \(S\) fixes positions \(1,\ldots,B_L\) and is one cycle on \(I\). \item With \[ d(x)=\frac{-1+\sqrt{1+4x}}2, \] every label among the first \(p\) satisfies \begin{equation} \frac1{NS}\int_0^{NS}d\bigl(a^{-2}\lambda_i(s)\bigr)\,ds<k. \end{equation} Here \(NS\) is an eigenvalue period for every band label and also a period for every fixed lower label. \end{enumerate} At each crossing there is a smooth conformal direction \(\xi\) for which the off-diagonal entry \[ \left\langle e_h, \left.\frac{d}{d\varepsilon}\right|_{\varepsilon=0} (-\Delta_{h(w+\varepsilon\xi)})e_i \right\rangle_{L^2(d\mu)} \] is nonzero on the crossing pair. After \(k\) and the entire program are fixed, the outer gap, the absolute crossing slopes, and the separations between crossing phases have positive uniform lower bounds. For every fixed order, the smooth norms of the frame and metrics have a uniform upper bound. For each pair, its absolute eigenvalue gap has a positive lower bound on every compact subset of the full label-period phase circle \(\mathbb R/(NS\mathbb Z)\) disjoint from that pair's crossing set. A pair with no crossings has a uniform gap on that whole circle.

primaryStatements.name: Uniform radial realization
primaryStatements.label: n:prop-radial-realization
primaryStatements.text: Suppose the fixed reference program, including its negative-phase interpolation, is close enough to round that its Gauss curvature is uniformly greater than $\kappa_*$. There are a constant $C>0$ and, after $C$ is fixed, an integer $J_0$ such that for every integer $J\geq J_0$ there is a smooth function $f=f_J:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$, independent of $z$, such that \[ g_z=dr^2+f(r)^2H_z(\log r) \] extends to a complete smooth metric on $\mathbb R^3$ for every $z\in[-1,1]^{\mathbb N}$. The metric is Euclidean near zero, $\operatorname{Ric}_{g_z}\geq0$, with strictly positive Ricci curvature outside a compact set, and $d_{g_z}(0,(r,x))=r$. Moreover \[ a\leq f'(r)\leq1,\qquad f'(r)\to a,\qquad b(t):=e^{-t}f(e^t)\to a. \] For every $t\geq0.8J$ the following estimates are uniform over the entire product box of controls, also after any fixed number of angular differentiations: \begin{align} &\partial_tH_z=O(\eta),\qquad \partial_t^2H_z=O(\eta^2), \qquad \operatorname{tr}(H_z^{-1}\partial_tH_z)=0, \\ &b_{tt}+b_t=-C\eta^2,\qquad b_t=O(C\eta^2),\quad b_{tt}=O(C\eta^2),\quad b-a=O(Ct^{-1/2}). \end{align} In every fixed smooth angular norm, $H_z(t)-H(s(t))=O(\eta(t)^{3/4})$ in this range, where the reference $H(s)=h(w(s))$ includes the negative-phase interpolation. The controlled links stay in a fixed compact subset of a finite-dimensional smooth family and have $K_{H_z}>\kappa_*$. All implied constants may depend on $a$, $\kappa_*$, the fixed angular program, and the fixed $C$; they do not depend on $J\geq J_0$ or on the control sequence.

primaryStatements.name: Invariant spaces for the exact Dirichlet maps
primaryStatements.label: n:prop-exact-graphs
primaryStatements.text: After increasing \(J\), there is a fixed \(\kappa<1\) such that, uniformly in the controls, \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} T_{QL}&=O(\delta_j),& T_{LL}&=\operatorname{diag}(\alpha_i(j)^{-1})+O(\delta_j),\\ T_{LQ}&=o(1),& \|T_{QQ}\|&\leq\kappa\tau_j. \end{aligned} \end{equation} There is a unique family of graph maps \(V_j:\mathbb R^p\to Q_j\), among families in one fixed sufficiently small operator ball, such that \(T_j\) maps \[ \operatorname{graph}_{j+1}V_{j+1} =\{\iota_{j+1}c+V_{j+1}c:c\in\mathbb R^p\} \] isomorphically onto \(\operatorname{graph}_jV_j\). They satisfy \(\|V_j\|\leq C\delta_j\). For each fixed \(j\), \(V_j\) is continuous in operator norm as a function of the complete control sequence with its countable product topology. The outward matrix on these spaces is \begin{equation} A_j=(T_{LL}+T_{LQ}V_{j+1})^{-1} =\operatorname{diag}(\alpha_i(j))+O(\delta_j), \qquad T_{LQ}V_{j+1}=o(\delta_j). \end{equation} It too is continuous in the product topology.

papers.title: Global classical solutions of the three-dimensional relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell system
papers.abstract: We prove global existence and uniqueness for arbitrary smooth admissible initial data in the three-dimensional, one-species relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell system. The particle density is initially compactly supported, and the electromagnetic fields have finite energy and bounded derivatives of all orders. The solution remains smooth on every finite time interval. This resolves the large-data global classical regularity problem for this model, without size or symmetry restrictions on the data.

primaryStatements.label: thm:global
primaryStatements.text: Every smooth admissible datum \eqref{eq:data} generates a unique global classical solution of \eqref{eq:rvm}. For every finite $T$, this solution satisfies \[ f\in C^\infty([0,T]\times\R^3_x\times\R^3_v),\qquad E,B\in C^\infty([0,T]\times\R^3_x;\R^3), \] and $f$ has compact phase-space support on $[0,T]$. The two divergence constraints hold for all time.

primaryStatements.name: Signed momentum increments
primaryStatements.label: prop:increment
primaryStatements.text: For each smooth admissible datum and finite $T_0$, there are constants $M,A\ge1$ and $P_0$ with the following property. On every compact classical solution interval $[0,t_*]$ as above, for every dyadic $P\ge P_0$ satisfying \eqref{eq:P-range}, every supported receiver, every $w=2^k$, $k\ge0$, and every interval $[t_1,t_2]\subset[0,t_*]$ on which $w/8\le q_X(t)\le8w$ throughout, one has \begin{equation} |V_X(t_2)-V_X(t_1)| \le MP\sqrt{t_2-t_1}+A(t_2-t_1)S(w). \end{equation} The constants are independent of $t_*$ and $P$.

primaryStatements.name: Local theory and continuation
primaryStatements.label: prop:continuation
primaryStatements.text: Every smooth admissible datum has a unique maximal classical solution. It is smooth on each compact subinterval of its lifespan. If its maximal time $T_{\max}$ is finite and \[ \sup\{\,|v|:0\le t<T_{\max},\ (x,v)\in\supp f(t)\,\}<\infty, \] then the solution has a classical extension beyond $T_{\max}$.

primaryStatements.name: Retarded field representation
primaryStatements.label: ret:representation
primaryStatements.text: Let $E^{\rm fr},B^{\rm fr}$ be the homogeneous wave solutions with data \[ (E^{\rm fr},\partial_tE^{\rm fr})|_{t=0} =(E_0,\nabla\times B_0),\qquad (B^{\rm fr},\partial_tB^{\rm fr})|_{t=0} =(B_0,-\nabla\times E_0). \] For $t>0$, define initial boundary terms by \begin{equation} \begin{split} (E^{\rm bd},B^{\rm bd})(t,x) =\frac1{4\pi t}\int_{|x-y_0|=t}\int_{\R^3} \frac{f_0(y_0,v_0)}{d_0} \bigl(n_0-u_0,\ n_0\times(n_0-u_0)\bigr)\,dv_0\,dS_{y_0},\\ n_0=(x-y_0)/t,\qquad u_0=u(v_0),\qquad d_0=1-n_0\cdot u_0. \end{split} \end{equation} Set these terms to zero at $t=0$. Then \begin{equation} \begin{split} E(t,x)&=E^{\rm fr}(t,x)+E^{\rm bd}(t,x) +\frac1{4\pi}\int_{\mathcal L_{t,x}}f_0(z)\,\mathscr K\,dz,\\ B(t,x)&=B^{\rm fr}(t,x)+B^{\rm bd}(t,x) +\frac1{4\pi}\int_{\mathcal L_{t,x}}f_0(z)\,(n\times\mathscr K)\,dz, \end{split} \end{equation} where \begin{equation} \mathscr K=\frac{n-u}{r^2q^2d^3} +\frac{(n-u)(n\cdot b)-db}{rd^3}. \end{equation} All these integrals are well defined at the stated classical regularity. Moreover, \begin{equation} \sup_{0\leq t\leq T_0,\ x\in\R^3} (|E^{\rm fr}|+|B^{\rm fr}|+|E^{\rm bd}|+|B^{\rm bd}|) \leq C_{T_0,f_0,E_0,B_0}. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Baseline occupation with a joint energy budget
primaryStatements.label: occ:refined-proposition
primaryStatements.text: Suppose $h\leq I$, excluding only deficit bins with $h\leq\lambda$. Then \begin{equation} \mathsf M\leq C\frac{hk_1}{p} \left(1+\frac I\lambda\mathcal E\right), \qquad \mathcal E=\begin{cases} \mathcal E_{p\phi},&\text{small sector},\\ 1,&\text{remaining sector}. \end{cases} \end{equation} Consequently, with $R=1+\sqrt{I/\lambda}\sqrt{\mathcal E}$, \begin{equation} \mathsf M\leq C\frac{hk_1}{p}R^2 \end{equation} for all $h$, except deficit bins with $h\leq\min(I,\lambda)$.

primaryStatements.name: Integrated force bounds
primaryStatements.label: dir:direct
primaryStatements.text: Assume the bootstrap \eqref{eq:bootstrap}. The bounded data term, $T_r$, $T_\perp$, $S_b$, and the remaining-sector part of $S_g$ have combined integral at most \begin{equation} C\bigl[P\sqrt I+(M+\sqrt A)I S(w)\bigr]. \end{equation} The integral of the full force satisfies \begin{equation} \int_{\mathcal T}|K(t)|\,dt \le C\sqrt w\bigl[P\sqrt I+(M+\sqrt A)I S(w)\bigr]. \end{equation} The constant $C$ is independent of $P,w,I,M,A$.

primaryStatements.name: Weighted signed formula
primaryStatements.label: can:weighted-formula
primaryStatements.text: Let $J=[t_1,t_2]$ lie in a compact classical time interval. Let $0\leq\psi\leq1$ be Lipschitz on $J$, vanish at its endpoints, and be extended by zero outside $J$. Let $\chi$ be a selected sum as in Lemma \ref{can:cutoff-cancellation}. One may integrate \eqref{can:label-identity} labelwise against $\psi\chi$ and a bounded $C^1$ matrix $\Pi(t)$, including $\Pi=\Id$. More precisely, \begin{align} \int_J\!\int\psi\chi\Pi\mathcal K_t\,dy\,dv\,dt ={}&\mathcal B_0+\int_J\!\int \biggl[\psi\chi\Pi(\mathcal R+\mathcal A) +\psi_t\chi\Pi\frac{fk_0}{r}\notag\\ &\hspace{25mm}+\psi\chi\Pi_t\frac{fk_0}{r} +\psi\Pi\frac{fDk_0}{rd}\chi'_s\biggr]\,dy\,dv\,dt, \end{align} where the spatial integral has $r=|X(t)-y|<t$, all source quantities are evaluated at $s=t-r$, and $\mathcal B_0$ is the initial-cone boundary term. If $\|\Pi\|\lesssim1$, that boundary term is bounded in norm by \begin{equation} C\int_J|\psi(t_0)|\,dt_0. \end{equation} The constant in \eqref{can:initial-boundary-bound} depends only on the datum and fixed time horizon. For $\Pi=\Id$, and for $\Pi=wP_X/|V_X|$ when $|V_X|\asymp w$, the derivative kernels satisfy the bounds above, uniformly in the fixed selected index set. For a general $\Pi$, its derivative term retains the explicit bound $Cf\theta\|\Pi_t\|/(r\phi)$.

primaryStatements.label: sel:bulk-impulse
primaryStatements.text: For the weight $\psi$ above and $P\ge P_*(M,A)$, \begin{equation} \left|\int_J\psi(t)K(t)\,dt\right| \le C_\eta\big[P\sqrt I+(M+\sqrt A)I S(w)\big]. \end{equation} The constant $C_\eta$ is independent of $M,A$.

lean.scopeText: The formalized result gives global existence and uniqueness for the three-dimensional one-species relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell system. The initial particle density is nonnegative, smooth, and compactly supported; the initial fields have bounded derivatives of all orders, finite energy, and satisfy both Gauss constraints. The solution is smooth on every finite time interval, has compact particle phase support there, and is unique among classical solutions. No smallness, symmetry, or neutrality assumption is imposed.

papers.title: Nonuniqueness with local conservation for the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation
papers.abstract: We prove nonuniqueness for the three-dimensional periodic hard-sphere Boltzmann equation among global entropy solutions satisfying exact local conservation of mass, momentum, and kinetic energy. We construct one nonnegative initial density with bounded velocity support and finite mass, energy, and absolute entropy that gives rise to two distinct such solutions. Both are strongly continuous in L1, and their collision gain and loss terms are integrable with every polynomial velocity weight on every bounded time interval.

Both are strongly continuous in L1 and satisfy exact local conservation of mass, momentum and kinetic energy.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: There exist \(R<\infty\) and a nonnegative datum \(F_0\) with \[ \supp_vF_0\subset B_R(0),\qquad \int_\Omega F_0(1+|v|^2+|\log F_0|)\dd x\dd v<\infty, \] for which \eqref{eq:collision} has two global entropy solutions with local conservation in the sense of Definition \ref{def:admissible}, differing on a set of positive \((t,x,v)\)-measure. Both solutions belong to \(C([0,\infty);L^1(\Omega))\). Moreover, for every finite \(T\) and every \(k\ge0\), they satisfy \begin{equation} \int_0^T\!\!\int_\Omega \langle v\rangle^k\bigl[Q^+(F,F)+Q^-(F,F)\bigr] \dd x\dd v\dd t<\infty, \qquad \langle v\rangle=(1+|v|^2)^{1/2}. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Finite evolution and its identities
primaryStatements.label: con:finite-evolution
primaryStatements.text: For fixed \(N,b,T,\lambda\), the colored equations have a unique nonnegative local mild solution with bounded total \(H\)-norm. It continues while that norm remains bounded, with the prescribed transfers at retirement times, and depends continuously in this norm on its initial data on every common bounded interval of existence. The norm of each component is continuous between transfers. On every such interval, total mass, momentum, and energy are conserved. The exact local collision-invariant balances hold, with all polynomial velocity fluxes integrable. For \(\rho=M\) or \(\rho=\mu\), one has at every time of existence \begin{equation} \mathcal H_\rho(F(t))+ \int_0^t\mathcal D^b(F(s))\dd s \le\mathcal H_\rho(F(0)), \end{equation} where \(\mathcal D^b\) is the entropy dissipation with the same cutoff.

primaryStatements.name: Control of every active color
primaryStatements.label: cold:control
primaryStatements.text: There is a fixed constant \(C_*\) such that, with \[ \epsilon_s=C_*L_sd_s/s,\qquad \mathcal U_i=f_i+\epsilon_s m_i, \] and sufficiently small \(s_0\), every finite colored evolution obeys \begin{equation} 0\le c_i(t,x,v)\le\mathcal U_i(t,x,v)\qquad (0\le t\le L_{s_i}) \end{equation} as long as that color is active and the solution exists. If, on an interval beginning at \(t_1\), one also has \(\nu_F^b\ge\kappa>0\), then \begin{equation} c_i(t,x,v)\le e^{-\kappa(t-t_1)}\mathcal U_i(t,x,v)\qquad (t_1\le t\le L_{s_i}) \end{equation} throughout that interval. None of the constants in \eqref{cold:upper} uses a bound on the bath or hot density.

primaryStatements.name: Cap selection
primaryStatements.label: early:cap-selection
primaryStatements.text: For fixed $\delta>0$, there are $\bar s_0,T_0>0$, uniform in $N$ and the collision cutoff, with the following property. For each $0<s_0\le\bar s_0$, each $0<T\le T_0$, and each finite approximation, a seed parameter $\lambda\in(0,L_0)$ gives a solution on $[0,T]$ satisfying \begin{equation} Z(t)\le m_T(t+s_N)\quad(0\le t\le T), \qquad \max_{0\le t\le T}\frac{Z(t)}{m_T(t+s_N)}=1. \end{equation} The dormant solution exists on a fixed initial interval and satisfies \begin{equation} Z(t)\le C'_{A,\delta}t^A. \end{equation} The interval and constant in \eqref{early:dormant-bound} are independent of $N$, the collision cutoff, and sufficiently small $s_0$.

primaryStatements.name: Uniform early continuation
primaryStatements.label: early:continuation
primaryStatements.text: Fix $\delta>0$ and $\zeta\in(0,1)$. There are $\bar s_0>0$ and $T_0\in(0,t_1)$, depending on $\delta$ and $\zeta$ and on the fixed jet parameters, such that for every $0<s_0\le\bar s_0$, every finite approximation, and every $0<T\le T_0$, the dormant solution and every solution selected in Proposition \ref{early:cap-selection} continue to $t_1$ and satisfy \begin{equation} \sup_{0\le t\le t_1}\|h(t)\|_H\le\zeta. \end{equation} The choices are uniform in $N$, the collision cutoff, $R_\mu$, and $T$. For dormant solutions, \eqref{early:dormant-bound} also holds on an initial interval independent of these indices, with the fixed exponent $A>p+1$ chosen in \eqref{early:exponents}.

primaryStatements.name: Uniform global continuation
primaryStatements.label: prop:global-control
primaryStatements.text: The construction parameters can be fixed so that every dormant finite evolution and every cap solution with $0<T\le T_0$ continues globally. There are constants $B<\infty$ and $\kappa>0$, independent of $N$, $b_N\ge1$, and $T$, such that \begin{equation} \|w(t)\|_H\le B,\qquad \nu_F^{b_N}(t,x,v)\ge\kappa, \qquad t\ge t_1. \end{equation} Every active jet satisfies \eqref{global:cold-decay} through its retirement, the total retirement increment is bounded by \eqref{global:retirement}, and the hot component satisfies the small bound of \cref{early:continuation} on $[0,t_1]$.

primaryStatements.label: prop:global-limits
primaryStatements.text: Fix the construction parameters supplied by Proposition \ref{prop:global-control}, and let $b_N\to\infty$. Either the dormant family, or a family of cap solutions at one fixed horizon $T\in(0,T_0]$, has a subsequence of total densities $F_N$ converging weakly in $L^1([0,\tau]\times\Omega)$ for every $\tau<\infty$ to a nonnegative density $F$. This subsequence can be chosen so that $F_N(t)\rightharpoonup F(t)$ in $L^1(\Omega)$ at every $t\ge0$, with uniformly small polynomially weighted velocity tails on each bounded time interval. The limit has initial datum $F_0$ and is a global entropy solution obeying local conservation in the sense of Definition \ref{def:admissible}. More precisely, \begin{equation} F\in C([0,\infty);L^1(\Omega)),\qquad \int_0^\tau\!\int_\Omega \langle v\rangle^k\bigl(F+Q^+(F,F)+Q^-(F,F)\bigr) \dd x\dd v\dd t<\infty \quad(k\ge0,\ \tau<\infty). \end{equation} Total mass, momentum, and energy are conserved at every time. The common early-time pointwise majorant of the dormant approximations also bounds any dormant limit.

primaryStatements.label: prop:blowup-limit
primaryStatements.text: Every sequence \eqref{eq:rescaling} has a subsequence for which \(h_{r_N}\rightharpoonup g\) in local spacetime \(L^1\) on \((0,U)\times\R^3_x\times\R^3_v\), where \begin{equation} 0\leq g(t,x,v)\leq(t+l)H(v),\qquad \D g=2P(B,g)-g\nu_B. \end{equation} Here \(B\) is \eqref{eq:background}; its gain and loss are defined by integration against the velocity measure. Both terms on the right are locally integrable, with a velocity majorant uniform in position on each compact positive-time interval. Compactly supported velocity averages of \(h_{r_N}\) converge strongly in local \(L^1_{t,x}\). The limit has a locally strongly continuous \(L^1\) representative at positive times and obeys the integrating-factor formula \eqref{dil:mild} below. If \(l>0\), pass also to a limit \(\lambda_N\to\lambda_0\) of the seed parameters. The conclusion and its local continuity extend to time zero, with \begin{equation} g(0,x,v)=\lambda_0 l\,\chi(x/l,v). \end{equation}

definitions.name: Entropy solution with local conservation
definitions.label: def:admissible
definitions.text: Let \(F_0\ge0\) have finite mass, energy, and absolute entropy. A global entropy solution with local conservation is a nonnegative function \(F\) satisfying the following conditions. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item \(F\in C_w([0,\infty);L^1(\Omega))\), \(F(0)=F_0\), with continuity against every bounded measurable test. For every finite \(T\), \[ \sup_{0\le t\le T}\int_\Omega F(t)(1+|v|^2+|\log F(t)|)\dd x\dd v<\infty. \] \item The two functions \(Q^\pm(F,F)/(1+G)\) belong to \(L^1([0,T]\times\Omega)\) for every finite \(T\). For every \(\beta\in C^1([0,\infty))\) with \(\beta(0)=0\) and \(|\beta'(z)|\le C_\beta/(1+z)\), and every smooth \(\varphi\) periodic in \(x\) and compactly supported in \([0,\infty)\times\R^3_v\), \begin{equation} \begin{split} &\int_0^\infty\!\!\int_\Omega \left[M\beta(G)\D\varphi+\beta'(G)Q(F,F)\varphi\right] \dd x\dd v\dd t\\ &\hspace{15mm} +\int_\Omega M\beta(F_0/M)\varphi(0,x,v)\dd x\dd v=0. \end{split} \end{equation} \item Total momentum is conserved. At every \(t\ge0\), \[ \int_\Omega |v|^2F(t)\dd x\dd v\le\int_\Omega |v|^2F_0\dd x\dd v, \qquad \mathcal H_M(F(t))+\int_0^t\mathcal D(F(s))\dd s \le\mathcal H_M(F_0). \] \item For every finite \(T\), \[ \int_0^T\!\!\int_\Omega (1+|v|^3)F\dd x\dd v\dd t<\infty. \] For every \(\psi\in\{1,v_1,v_2,v_3,|v|^2/2\}\) and \(\phi\in C_c^\infty([0,\infty)\times\T^3)\), \begin{equation} \int_0^\infty\!\!\int_\Omega F\psi\D\phi\dd x\dd v\dd t +\int_\Omega F_0\psi\phi(0,x)\dd x\dd v=0. \end{equation} \end{enumerate}

definitions.name: Uniform sheet class
definitions.label: ker:sheet-class
definitions.text: Fix $L\geq1$. An elementary sheet in $\mathcal S_L$ is a product probability measure \begin{equation} c(\dd p)=\mathcal G_d(\dd\bar p)\rho(\dd p_3),\qquad 0\leq d\leq\tfrac18,\qquad \int_{\R}e^{8a^2}\rho(\dd a)\leq L. \end{equation} We also allow probability mixtures of elementary sheets. An upper bound by a sheet with amplitude $A_0$ means domination as measures by $A_0$ times such a mixture.

primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: There is a nonnegative density \(F_0\) on \(\T^3\times\R^3\), with bounded velocity support and \[ \int_{\T^3\times\R^3} F_0(1+|v|^2+|\log F_0|)\dd x\dd v<\infty, \] for which the hard-sphere Boltzmann equation has two distinct global admissible solutions, in the sense of Definition \ref{def:admissible}, with initial datum \(F_0\). On some common initial interval both solutions are strongly continuous in \(L^1\), and their collision gains and losses are integrable in space-time-velocity.

primaryStatements.name: Uniform cold control
primaryStatements.label: prop:cold-control
primaryStatements.text: There is a constant \(L\), depending on the fixed parameters, such that after imposing the additional condition \begin{equation} Ld_0\overline s^9\le1, \end{equation} the following statements hold at every time of existence of the finite approximation in \(0\le t\le\overline T\). \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item For every retained label \(i=(j,\sigma,n)\), \begin{equation} 0\le c_i\le f_i+\varepsilon_j m_i,\qquad \varepsilon_j=Ld_{s_j}/s_j . \end{equation} \item At each spatial point call the unique label with \(x\in\mathcal O_i(t)\), if one exists and is retained, the main label. Let \(c_{\mathrm{main}}\) be that color, or zero, and set \(e=c-c_{\mathrm{main}}\). For every \(A\ge0\), \begin{equation} 0\le e(t,x,v)\le C_A t^A e^{-4|v|^2}. \end{equation} The upper bound remains valid after restricting the escaped sum to any subset of its labels. \item If the main label has scale \(s\), its velocity measure is bounded by a fixed multiple of \((t+s)^{-1}\) times a sum of admissible probability sheets from Lemma \ref{lem:sheet-bound}. Its free-core contribution has the exact parameterization \eqref{eq:core-jacobian} below. The remainder has the smaller velocity-mass coefficient \(Cd_s/s^2\). In particular, for every fixed \(k\ge0\), \begin{equation} \int_{\R^3}\langle v\rangle^k c_{\mathrm{main}}\,\dd v \le\frac{C_k}{t+s},\qquad \int_{|v|>R}\langle v\rangle^k c_{\mathrm{main}}\,\dd v \le\frac{C_k e^{-c_kR^2}}{t+s}\quad(R\ge3). \end{equation} \item For the mixed-cold source in the hot equation, \begin{equation} \sum_{\substack{i,j\in\mathcal I_N\\i\ne j}} P^b(c_i,c_j)(t,x,v) \le C_A t^{A-1}H(v)\qquad (t>0) \end{equation} for every \(A\ge0\), with constants uniform in \(N\) and \(b\). \end{enumerate}

primaryStatements.name: Survival of a cold core under the cap
primaryStatements.label: jet:survival
primaryStatements.text: Suppose a finite approximation satisfies \[ 0\le h(t,x,v)\le(t+s_N)H(v) \] on an initial interval \([0,T]\subset[0,\overline T]\). All conclusions below concern times \(t\in[0,T]\). For every \(M\ge0\) there are constants \(C,C_M\), independent of \(T,N\), the cutoff, and the seed, such that \begin{equation} \begin{gathered} e^{-E_{s,N}(t)}f_i(t,x,v) \le c_i(t,x,v) \le f_i(t,x,v)+L(d_s/s)m_i(t,x,v),\\ E_{s,N}(t)=C(d_st/s+t^2+s_Nt)+C_Mt^{M+1} \end{gathered} \end{equation} for every label of scale \(s\). Consequently, if \(r\to0\), \(s_N\le r\), \(s/r\in[\epsilon,R]\) for fixed \(0<\epsilon<R<\infty\), and \(0\le t\le\min(T,Ar)\), then \[ E_{s,N}(t)\le C_{\epsilon,R,A}(d_s+r^2)+C_{M,A}r^{M+1}\longrightarrow0 \] uniformly in the label and in points of its free core. The transverse free displacement divided by the stripe period satisfies \begin{equation} \frac{td_s}{s^2}\le C_{\epsilon,R,A}r^9\longrightarrow0. \end{equation} On these scales the difference between cold and free-core velocity measures also satisfies, uniformly in position and time, \begin{equation} r\int_{\R^3}|c_i-f_i|(t,x,v)\,\dd v\longrightarrow0. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.label: prop:finite-cap
primaryStatements.text: There is a fixed \(T_0>0\) such that the following statements hold. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}] \item With \(\lambda=0\), the finite approximations exist on \([0,T_0]\) and satisfy \(0\le h\le t^2H\). \item There is a fixed finite \(L_0\) such that, for every \(0<T\le T_0\) and every \(N\), some \(\lambda\in[0,L_0]\) gives an approximation on \([0,T]\) with \begin{equation} 0\le h(t,x,v)\le(t+s_N)H(v),\qquad \max_{0\le t\le T}\frac{\|h(t)\|_H}{t+s_N}=1. \end{equation} \end{enumerate} In both cases all cold components obey Proposition \ref{prop:cold-control}.

primaryStatements.label: prop:admissible-limits
primaryStatements.text: Fix \(T\in(0,T_0]\). Either the zero-seed approximations of Proposition \ref{prop:finite-cap}, or any sequence of its cap shots on \([0,T]\), has a subsequence whose total densities \(F_N=c_N+h_N\) converge weakly in \(L^1([0,T]\times\Omega)\) to a nonnegative density \(F\). The subsequence can be chosen so that \(F_N(t)\rightharpoonup F(t)\) in \(L^1(\Omega)\) at every \(t\in[0,T]\), with uniformly small polynomially weighted velocity tails. The limit has the common initial datum \eqref{eq:datum}, and \[ Q^\pm(F,F)\in L^1([0,T]\times\Omega),\qquad F\in C([0,T];L^1(\Omega)). \] It satisfies every condition of Definition \ref{def:admissible} on this interval, including the inequalities at every time. Each such limit has an admissible global continuation. The dormant upper bound, consisting of the cold majorants of Proposition \ref{prop:cold-control} and \(t^2H\), passes to a zero-seed limit.

primaryStatements.label: prop:blowup-limit
primaryStatements.text: Every sequence \eqref{eq:rescaling} has a subsequence for which \(h_{r_N}\rightharpoonup g\) in local spacetime \(L^1\) on \((0,U)\times\R^3_x\times\R^3_v\), where \begin{equation} 0\leq g(t,x,v)\leq(t+l)H(v),\qquad \D g=2P(B,g)-g\nu_B. \end{equation} Here \(B\) is \eqref{eq:background}; its gain and loss are defined by integration against the velocity measure. Both terms on the right are locally integrable, with a velocity majorant uniform in position on each compact positive-time interval. Compactly supported velocity averages of \(h_{r_N}\) converge strongly in local \(L^1_{t,x}\). The limit has a locally strongly continuous \(L^1\) representative at positive times and obeys the integrating-factor formula \eqref{dil:mild} below. If \(l>0\), pass also to a limit \(\lambda_N\to\lambda_0\) of the shot parameters. The conclusion and its local continuity extend to time zero, with \begin{equation} g(0,x,v)=\lambda_0 l\,\chi(x/l,v). \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Nonvanishing of every cap limit
primaryStatements.label: prop:nonzero-limit
primaryStatements.text: Consider any sequence of cap shots with horizons \(T_n\to0\), approximation indices \(N_n\to\infty\), and \(s_{N_n}/T_n\to0\). Make the rescaling \eqref{eq:rescaling}, and pass to any subsequence supplied by Proposition \ref{prop:blowup-limit}. Its limit satisfies \[ g\not\equiv0\qquad\text{on }(0,U)\times\R^3_x\times\R^3_v. \] This conclusion includes \(l=1\), \(U=1\), and \(U=\infty\).

primaryStatements.label: prop:finite-dilated-horizon
primaryStatements.text: There are fixed positive choices of \(\eta,\alpha,\gamma,K\), with \(\eta,\alpha,\gamma\) small and \(K\) large, for which every limit in Propositions \ref{prop:blowup-limit} and \ref{prop:nonzero-limit} has \(U<\infty\). These parameters can be fixed before the final choices of \(s_0,d_0,T_0\). The same choices work for every limiting mesh and every \(l\in[0,1]\).

definitions.name: Entropy-class solution
definitions.label: def:admissible
definitions.text: For a nonnegative datum \(F_0\) satisfying \[ \int_\Omega F_0(1+|v|^2+|\log F_0|)\dd x\dd v<\infty, \] an admissible global solution is a nonnegative \(F\) with the following properties. \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}] \item \(F\in C_w([0,\infty);L^1(\Omega))\), with \(F(0)=F_0\), where weak continuity means continuity against every bounded measurable test. On each bounded time interval, \(\int_\Omega F(1+|v|^2+|\log F|)\) is uniformly bounded. \item \(Q^\pm(F,F)/(1+G)\) belong to \(L^1([0,T]\times\Omega)\) for every finite \(T\). For every \(\beta\in C^1([0,\infty))\) with \(\beta(0)=0\) and \(|\beta'(z)|\le C_\beta/(1+z)\), and every smooth test \(\varphi(t,x,v)\) periodic in \(x\) and compactly supported in \([0,\infty)\times\R^3_v\), \[ \begin{split} &\int_0^\infty\!\!\int_\Omega \bigl[M\beta(G)(\partial_t\varphi+v\cdot\nabla_x\varphi) +\beta'(G)Q(F,F)\varphi\bigr]\dd x\dd v\dd t\\ &\hspace{2cm} +\int_\Omega M\beta(F_0/M)\varphi(0,x,v)\dd x\dd v=0 . \end{split} \] \item With \(\rho=\int F\dd v\) and \(j=\int vF\dd v\), \(\partial_t\rho+\nabla_x\cdot j=0\) distributionally with the initial density \(\int F_0\dd v\). Total momentum is conserved. For every \(t\ge0\), \[ \int_\Omega |v|^2F(t)\le\int_\Omega |v|^2F_0,\qquad \mathcal H_M(F(t))+\int_0^t\mathcal D(F(s))\dd s \le\mathcal H_M(F_0). \] \end{enumerate}

definitions.name: Uniform sheet class
definitions.label: ker:sheet-class
definitions.text: Fix $L\geq1$. An elementary sheet in $\mathcal S_L$ is a product probability measure \begin{equation} c(\dd p)=\mathcal G_d(\dd\bar p)\rho(\dd p_3),\qquad 0\leq d\leq\tfrac18,\qquad \int_{\R}e^{8a^2}\rho(\dd a)\leq L. \end{equation} We also allow probability mixtures of elementary sheets. An upper bound by a sheet with amplitude $A_0$ means domination as measures by $A_0$ times such a mixture.

lean.scopeText:
The formalization proves nonuniqueness for the periodic hard-sphere Boltzmann equation by constructing two distinct global renormalized solutions on $\mathbb T^3\times\mathbb R^3$ with the same nonnegative initial density. The data have bounded velocity support and finite mass, energy, and absolute entropy. Both solutions conserve local mass and total momentum and satisfy the global energy and entropy-dissipation inequalities.

On a common initial interval they are strongly continuous in $L^1$, with integrable collision gains and losses. These are the conditions of the selected periodic result; later local-conservation refinements are outside it.

papers.title: The Boltzmann–Grad limit for stable radial potentials on regular kinetic intervals
papers.abstract: We derive the nonlinear Boltzmann equation from a grand-canonical Newtonian gas with initial pair exclusion. We treat stable, finite-range radial potentials that are C2 except for an allowed repulsive singularity at the origin, and C1 initial probability densities with spatially summable Gaussian bounds on the density and its spatial gradient. All fixed-order rescaled factorial marginals converge in L1, uniformly throughout every finite interval on which the classical kinetic solution has a uniform Gaussian bound. The result allows attractive wells and dynamically formed clusters, without restrictions on the differential scattering cross-section.
papers.familySummary: Derives the nonlinear Boltzmann equation from three-dimensional grand-canonical Newtonian gases throughout every regular kinetic interval with uniform Gaussian decay. Stable finite-range radial potentials may have attractive wells and a singular repulsive core; initial pair exclusion and spatially summable Gaussian density and gradient bounds are assumed. A companion gives finite-dimensional hard-sphere Gaussian fluctuations, centered at the exact microscopic expectation and governed by the linear fluctuating Boltzmann equation.

primaryStatements.name: Regular-lifespan kinetic limit
primaryStatements.label: thm:main
primaryStatements.text: Let $\Phi$ satisfy Assumption \ref{pre:potential}, and let $\beta>0$. Let $f_0\ge0$ be a $C^1$ probability density on $\R^3\times\R^3$ such that \begin{equation} \|f_0\|_{\mathrm{Bol},2\beta} +\|\nabla_xf_0\|_{\mathrm{Bol},2\beta}<\infty. \end{equation} Fix $0<T<\infty$ for which the equation \begin{equation} (\partial_t+v\cdot\nabla_x)f=Q_\Phi(f,f), \qquad f|_{t=0}=f_0, \end{equation} has a nonnegative classical probability-density solution satisfying \begin{equation} \sup_{0\le t\le T}\sup_{x,v} e^{2\beta|v|^2}f(t,x,v)<\infty. \end{equation} Start the exact Newtonian process from the grand-canonical law \eqref{pre:model}. For its scaled factorial densities $F_s^\varepsilon$, defined in \eqref{pre:factorial}, every fixed integer $s\ge1$ satisfies \begin{equation} \lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\; \sup_{0\le t\le T} \bigl\|F_s^\varepsilon(t)-f(t)^{\otimes s}\bigr\|_ {L^1((\R^3\times\R^3)^s)}=0. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Actual witnesses and layer remainders
primaryStatements.label: close:tails
primaryStatements.text: With the preceding schedule, for sufficiently small $\varepsilon$ and every $1\leq j\leq L$, \begin{equation} \mathbb P\bigl(\mathcal B_j(D_j)\bigr)\leq e^{-8D_j}, \qquad R_j\leq e^{-8K_j}. \end{equation} The estimates use the original Newtonian process, without conditioning it to stay in a good set.

primaryStatements.name: Empirical observables
primaryStatements.label: cor:empirical
primaryStatements.text: Under the hypotheses of Theorem \ref{thm:main}, let $a\in C_c^\infty(\R^3\times\R^3;\R)$ and $\eta>0$. Then \begin{equation} \lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\; \sup_{0\le t\le T} \PP\!\left( \left|\mu_\varepsilon^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{N}a(z_i(t)) -\int a(z)f(t,z)\,dz\right|>\eta\right)=0. \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Global finite-particle flow
primaryStatements.label: pre:flow
primaryStatements.text: For each fixed $\varepsilon>0$ and finite label set $R$, \eqref{pre:dynamics} has a unique global flow from every finite-energy initial state in its domain. The flow preserves phase volume and $\mathscr H_R$. In the singular case, every pair distance along a given trajectory is bounded away from zero. In the nonsingular case coincident positions are permitted.

primaryStatements.name: Initial insertion and centering
primaryStatements.label: pre:initial
primaryStatements.text: Put $\rho_0(x)=\int f_0(x,v)\,dv$, and assume $\|\rho_0\|_\infty<\infty$. At time zero, \begin{equation} \begin{split} \widetilde F_R^\varepsilon(0,Z_R) &=F_R^\varepsilon(0,Z_R)\\ &=f_0^{\otimes R}(Z_R)\mathbf1_{{\cal D}_R^\varepsilon}(Z_R) \mathbb E\prod_{i\in R}\mathbf1_{\{N(B_i)=0\}}, \qquad B_i=\overline B(x_i,\varepsilon). \end{split} \end{equation} The expectation is over an independent cloud with the original law, and $N(B)$ counts its positions in $B$. Consequently $0\leq F_R^\varepsilon(0)\leq f_0^{\otimes R}$. For $Z_R\in{\cal D}_R^\varepsilon$, define \begin{equation} E_R^\varepsilon(0,Z_R)= \sum_{S\subset R}(-1)^{|R\setminus S|} f_0^{\otimes(R\setminus S)}(Z_{R\setminus S}) \widetilde F_S^\varepsilon(0,Z_S). \end{equation} There are $c_0>0,C_0<\infty$, independent of $R,\varepsilon$, such that for sufficiently small $\varepsilon$, \begin{equation} |E_R^\varepsilon(0,Z_R)| \leq(C_0\varepsilon^{c_0})^{|R|}f_0^{\otimes R}(Z_R). \end{equation} One may take $c_0=1/125$. For fixed $r$, \begin{equation} 0\leq1-\int F_R^\varepsilon(0,Z_R)\,dZ_R \leq Cr\varepsilon+Cr^2\varepsilon^3, \qquad \int F_R^\varepsilon(t)=\int F_R^\varepsilon(0). \end{equation}

primaryStatements.name: Scattering nondegeneracy
primaryStatements.label: pre:scattering
primaryStatements.text: Outside a set of zero incoming flux, an encounter either is a straight force-free passage or satisfies \begin{equation} v'\ne v,\qquad v_*'\ne v . \end{equation} For $M<\infty$ and $\eta>0$, the non-free relative incoming data $(n,g)$ with $|g|\leq M$ can be restricted to a rotation-invariant compact set, losing at most $\eta$ relative incoming flux, on which the duration is bounded and $|g|$, $|v'-v|$, and $|v_*'-v|$ have positive lower bounds. For fixed radial scattering parameters, each of these nonzero increments has a uniform spherical directional marginal under common rotation. The two increments need not be independent.

primaryStatements.name: Known-solution envelopes
primaryStatements.label: pre:envelopes
primaryStatements.text: Suppose $f$ is the classical nonnegative solution in the statement, and \[ A=\sup_{0\leq t\leq T}\|f(t)\|_{\infty,2\beta}<\infty,\qquad B_0=\|f_0\|_{\mathrm{Bol},2\beta} +\|\nabla_xf_0\|_{\mathrm{Bol},2\beta}<\infty. \] Then \begin{equation} \sup_{0\leq t\leq T} \left(\|f(t)\|_{\mathrm{Bol},\beta} +\|\nabla_xf(t)\|_{\mathrm{Bol},\beta}\right) \leq C(A,B_0,\beta,T)<\infty. \end{equation} Fix, once and for all, \begin{equation} \beta_0=\beta/2. \end{equation} Thus all independent inputs $f(t)$ and their spatial Lipschitz envelopes have a common bound with the fixed margin $\beta-\beta_0$. Constants in \eqref{eq:pre-envelope} are independent of the subsequent time-layer subdivision.

primaryStatements.name: Exact cell expansion
primaryStatements.label: cell:expansion
primaryStatements.text: Let $R\subset S$ and let $A_0$ be the union of the blocks of $\pi_0(S)$ meeting $R$. For $R\ne\varnothing$, let $\mathcal P$ be the collection of the other blocks of $\pi_0(S)$. Then \begin{equation} \mathsf H^I_{R,S} =\sum_{\mathcal U\subset\mathcal P} \mathsf K^I_{R,A_0\cup\bigcup\mathcal U}, \end{equation} and, as an equality of signed measures, \begin{equation} \mathsf K^I_{R,A_0\cup\bigcup\mathcal U} =\sum_{\mathcal V\subset\mathcal U} (-1)^{|\mathcal U|-|\mathcal V|} \mathsf H^I_{R,A_0\cup\bigcup\mathcal V}. \end{equation} Every coefficient is evaluated on its displayed input coordinates. If $m=|S\setminus R|$, the number of diagrams in \eqref{eq:cell-K} is at most $(C(1+m))^{Cm}$, with a universal $C$. There is no partition of the roots in this count.

definitions.name: Potential class
definitions.label: pre:potential
definitions.text: Write $\Phi(q)=\phi(|q|)$, with $\Phi(q)=0$ for $|q|\geq1$. Assume either $\Phi\in C^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)$, or $\Phi\in C^2(\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\})$ with $\Phi(q)\to+\infty$ as $q\to0$. In the latter case set $\Phi(0)=+\infty$. Assume thermodynamic stability: for some $B\geq0$, \begin{equation} \sum_{\substack{i,j\in R\\i<j}}\Phi(q_i-q_j)\geq-B|R| \end{equation} for every finite configuration of distinct points. The potential is fixed independently of $\varepsilon$.

definitions.name: Exact initial ensemble
definitions.label: eq:pre-partition
definitions.text: Let $\mu=\varepsilon^{-2}$ and \[ {\cal D}_R^\varepsilon =\{Z_R:|x_i-x_j|>\varepsilon\text{ for all }i\ne j\in R\}. \] For the prescribed $C^1$ nonnegative probability density $f_0$, set \begin{align} {\cal Z}_\varepsilon &=\sum_{n=0}^\infty\frac{\mu^n}{n!} \int f_0^{\otimes n}(Z_n) \mathbf1_{{\cal D}_{[n]}^\varepsilon}(Z_n)\,dZ_n, \\ W_{0,n}(Z_n) &={\cal Z}_\varepsilon^{-1}\mu^n f_0^{\otimes n}(Z_n) \mathbf1_{{\cal D}_{[n]}^\varepsilon}(Z_n). \end{align} Here $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and empty products equal one. The probability law on ordered coordinates is \begin{equation} \mathbb P(N=n,Z_n\in dZ_n)=\frac1{n!}W_{0,n}(Z_n)\,dZ_n. \end{equation} Thereafter the cloud evolves by \eqref{pre:dynamics}.

definitions.name: The scattering collision operator
definitions.label: pre:collision
definitions.text: Write $c=(v+v_*)/2$, $g=v-v_*$, and, for almost every incoming datum, let $g_{\rm out}$ be the velocity after exit. Set \[ v'=c+\tfrac12g_{\rm out},\qquad v_*'=c-\tfrac12g_{\rm out}. \] For $\psi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$, define $Q_\Phi$ at each $x$ by \begin{equation} \begin{split} \int Q_\Phi(f,f)(x,v)\psi(v)\,dv =\frac12\int_{\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R^3} & f(x,v)f(x,v_*)|v-v_*|\\ {}\times\int_{\substack{b\in(v-v_*)^\perp\\|b|<1}} &[\,\psi(v')+\psi(v_*')-\psi(v)-\psi(v_*)\,]\, d^2b\,dv\,dv_* . \end{split} \end{equation} Here $d^2b$ is Euclidean area, and the $g=0$ contribution is zero. Null exceptional scattering data are ignored.

definitions.name: A cell diagram
definitions.label: def:cell-diagram
definitions.text: For $R\subset S$, with $R\ne\varnothing$, a cell diagram on $(R,S)$ is \[ \gamma=(A;\Gamma_1,\ldots,\Gamma_\ell). \] Here $R\subset A\subset S$; the nonempty sets in all the $\Gamma_g$ together partition $S\setminus A$; and each $\Gamma_g$ is a nonempty unordered collection of these sets. Put $\Gamma_0=\{A\}$. Different members of the diagram are different force groups. Let $\iota_0(\gamma)$ be the indicator that every force group in the diagram is a union of blocks of $\pi_0(S)$. Equivalently, all pairs in different force groups have distance greater than $\varepsilon$ at $a$. Define \begin{align} w_I(\gamma;Z_S) ={}&\iota_0(\gamma)c_I^R(A) \prod_{g=1}^{\ell} \left[ \prod_{B\in\Gamma_g}c_I(B)\tau_I(\Gamma_{g-1},B) \prod_{\{B,C\}\subset\Gamma_g}\alpha_I(B,C) \right], \\ \sigma(\gamma)={}&(-1)^{\sum_{g=1}^{\ell}|\Gamma_g|}. \end{align} Only the root group $A$ uses a joint flow containing roots. In particular, a contact between different generations is a condition on separate trajectories, not a force exerted between their groups. The empty list of generations is allowed when $S=A$.

definitions.name: A prescribed whole-cell history
definitions.label: cell:histories
definitions.text: A finite whole-cell history is a composition of the diagram kernels above on successive cells, together with any tensor products and singleton-slot deletions or independent insertions specified by the exact centered identities at layer cuts. Its discrete prescription records the following data: \begin{enumerate} \item every formal label and its lifetime, with a fresh label for each independent input and no reuse of an independent source; \item on each occupied cell, the required root labels $R$, the full set $S$, its root force group, and its detached groups and generations; \item all the indicators in \eqref{eq:cell-weight} and the endpoint isolation indicators, including the initial polymer restrictions restored at every deleted singleton slot; \item the signs, factorial weights, and any deterministic stopping marks and unexpanded factors. \end{enumerate} On an ordinary hierarchy cell, labels in $R$ persist through its upper endpoint; labels in $S\setminus R$ end their cell lifetime there. In the forward direction they were present throughout the cell, not created at a first-contact time. The root group is isolated from its departing members at the upper endpoint by $e_I^R(A)$. Detached groups have separate force systems; their geometric contacts with other generations at that endpoint are unrestricted. At the lower endpoint all force groups are unions of initial polymers. At a layer cut a nonsingleton polymer remains intact; independent singleton inputs are inserted only with the full polymer-pattern restrictions of the centered identity. The size $p$ is the number of distinct formal label lifetimes, not the number of their repeated appearances at cuts. All transport maps and indicators are defined on the full coordinates of these lifetimes. A history with a stopped factor can still depend on the unexpanded microscopic cloud through its last factor in $[0,1]$; its positive majorant drops that factor.

definitions.name: An unisolated terminal witness block
definitions.label: def:cell-terminal-witness
definitions.text: A terminal witness is permitted a different upper boundary condition from an ordinary hierarchy cell. For $R\subset A$ put \begin{equation} \mathsf J^I_{R,A}(Z_A;\dd Y_R) =\delta_{(X_i^A(\delta),V_i^A(\delta))_{i\in R}}(\dd Y_R), \end{equation} with no endpoint isolation factor. Its exact positive root-component decomposition is \begin{equation} \mathsf J^I_{R,S} =\sum_{\substack{R\subset A\subset S\\ A\text{ union of blocks of }\pi_0(S)}} c_I^R(A)\mathsf J^I_{R,A}\Xi_I(\{A\};S\setminus A). \end{equation} Indeed the unique actual union of rooted contact components is still the unique nonzero summand, and its root trajectories agree with the full ones. This proves the identity without asserting endpoint isolation. Integrating a nonnegative test and dropping its last avoidance factor gives the corresponding positive bound. For a terminal witness block, all selected force groups end their formal lifetimes together at the fixed upper endpoint $b$. The distinguished labels $R$---usually a single label---serve only for factorial normalization and spatial integration anchors. They do not persist as a force subsystem after that endpoint. All terminal coordinates of every selected group are retained in the integration and energy bookkeeping before any projection in \eqref{eq:cell-J}. In particular one keeps the full terminal group Hamiltonians; one does not split $R$ away from close companions. Geometric isolation of $R$ from $A\setminus R$ at $b$ is neither required nor inferred. A selected block may also carry a measurable nonnegative trajectory indicator $W_I(A;Z_A)\leq1$ specifying the witness. Such an indicator is evaluated on its isolated group flow. If the witness was identified at an earlier time inside the cell, keep that prefix condition and continue the isolated group to the fixed endpoint $b$ before using whole-cell coordinates. This is a finite prescription with an extra indicator, not a stopping-time change of phase-volume variables. Establishing that an actual bad event admits a selected witness of this form belongs to \Cref{close:witnesses}. At every earlier cut the ordinary rules of Definition \ref{cell:histories} remain in force. In particular, a selected union is initially externally isolated and its backward continuation across the preceding cell retains the usual endpoint isolation indicator. Only the final witness boundary uses \eqref{eq:cell-J}. These are formal operations in the witness integral; the microscopic evolution is not stopped or modified.

definitions.name: Patternwise centered marginal
definitions.label: cent:definition
definitions.text: The centered marginal on pattern $\pi$ is \begin{equation} E_\pi^\eps(t,Z_R)=\chi_\pi^\eps(Z_R) \sum_{A\subset S(\pi)}(-1)^{|S(\pi)\setminus A|} f_{S(\pi)\setminus A}(t,Z_{S(\pi)\setminus A}) \widetilde F_{B(\pi)\cup A}^\eps(t,Z_{B(\pi)\cup A}). \end{equation} We set $E_\varnothing^\eps=1$. A nonsingleton block is always retained as a whole; its individual labels are not centered.

definitions.name: Disjoint ownership
definitions.label: cent:ownership
definitions.text: Fix the labels, their order, and an original contact record for each occupied cell. At the top of a layer give each root label its own owner. Carry these owners backward through the cells. In a cell form the finite graph of physical and required virtual contacts of each original factor's displayed generation diagram, including initial-polymer edges. Take the disjoint union over tensor factors; contacts with other factors remain tests and marks below, and are not used to assign original parents. The selected original pin edges, together with internal contact trees of its pinned groups, connect every new label to the old array. For an internal tree choose the lexicographically first spanning tree of the finite contact graph. Root the resulting forest at the old array, retaining the prescribed original parent in the singleton case of Section \ref{cell:contact-records}. More explicitly, process the selected edges in their record order, with the internal-tree and label orders resolving ties: keep an edge joining two distinct components when at least one is rootless, and omit an edge within one component or between two components that already contain old labels. Orient the retained trees toward their old-label endpoints. If needed, process the remaining required contact edges in the same fixed order to finish this rooted forest. Connectivity guarantees that no new label remains rootless. Every new label inherits the owner of its old-label endpoint; an old label never changes owner. An omitted edge between two already owned components is still a displayed contact. If its endpoint owners differ, mark both endpoint lives. Likewise mark both endpoints of every other contact between different owners, whether or not the record selected that contact as a pin. A multiple addition marks every new label and each old label participating in its pins or contacts. The family of a root is the set of labels with that root as owner. This definition changes neither a force group nor a trajectory, and its families are disjoint by construction.

papers.title: Hard-sphere fluctuations on the regular Boltzmann lifespan
papers.abstract: We prove a finite-dimensional central limit theorem away from equilibrium for a deterministic grand-canonical hard-sphere gas in three dimensions. The initial probability density is smooth, with spatially summable Gaussian velocity bounds on the density and its spatial gradient. The limit holds on every finite interval on which the classical Boltzmann solution has uniform Gaussian velocity decay. The empirical measure is centered by its exact microscopic expectation. Its fluctuations converge to the Gaussian solution of the linear fluctuating Boltzmann equation.
